<h1 id="cloudflare-api">Cloudflare API v4.0.0</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

Welcome to Cloudflare's API documentation site. We are experimenting with an updated version of our API documentation - check out [developers.cloudflare.com/api-next/](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api-next/) to test out the new experience.

To get started using Cloudflare's products and services via the API, refer to [how to interact with Cloudflare](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/basic-tasks/interact-with-cloudflare/), which covers using tools like [Terraform](https://developers.cloudflare.com/terraform/#cloudflare-terraform) and the [official SDKs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/api/reference/sdks/) to maintain your Cloudflare resources.

Using the Cloudflare API requires authentication so that Cloudflare knows who is making requests and what permissions you have. Create an API token to grant access to the API to perform actions. You can also authenticate with [API keys](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/api/get-started/keys/), but these keys have [several limitations](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/api/get-started/keys/#limitations) that make them less secure than API tokens. Whenever possible, use API tokens to interact with the Cloudflare API.

To create an API token, from the Cloudflare dashboard, go to My Profile > API Tokens and select Create Token. For more information on how to create and troubleshoot API tokens, refer to
our [API fundamentals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/api/).

For information regarding rate limits, refer to our [API Rate Limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-for-platforms/workers-for-platforms/platform/limits/#api-rate-limits).

Totally new to Cloudflare? [Start here](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/get-started/).

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4">https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4</a> - Client API

License: <a href="https://opensource.org/licenses/BSD-3-Clause">BSD-3-Clause</a>

<a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/">Cloudflare Radar Documentation</a>

# Authentication

* API Key (api_email)
    - Parameter Name: **X-Auth-Email**, in: header.

* API Key (api_key)
    - Parameter Name: **X-Auth-Key**, in: header.

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer

* API Key (user_service_key)
    - Parameter Name: **X-Auth-User-Service-Key**, in: header.

## Create an Account

<a id="opIdaccount-creation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "standalone": true,
    "type": "standard",
    "unit": {
      "id": "f267e341f3dd4697bd3b9f71dd96247f"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /accounts`

Create an Account. To create the Account within an Organization, provide `unit.id` and omit `standalone`. To create a standalone Free Account, provide `standalone: true` and omit `unit`. Providing both fields is invalid. If you omit both fields, Cloudflare can determine the destination only when the User is an administrator of exactly one Organization. Cloudflare creates the Account in that Organization; otherwise, the request returns an error.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "standalone": true,
  "type": "standard",
  "unit": {
    "id": "f267e341f3dd4697bd3b9f71dd96247f"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|Optional key that identifies an Account-creation request. Free Account creation can require exactly one valid key, so API clients should send a key with every Account-creation request. Reuse the same key when retrying the same request.|
|body|body|[iam_create-account](#schemaiam_create-account)|true|Parameters for account creation|
|» name|body|string|true|Account name|
|» standalone|body|boolean|false|Set to `true` and omit `unit` to create a standalone Free Account. If provided, this field must be `true`.|
|» type|body|[iam_account-type](#schemaiam_account-type)|false|none|
|» unit|body|object|false|Information related to the tenant unit. Provide its ID and omit `standalone` to create the Account within an Organization. See https://developers.cloudflare.com/tenant/how-to/manage-accounts/.|
|» » id|body|string|false|Tenant unit ID|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» standalone|true|
|» type|standard|
|» type|enterprise|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "created_on": "2014-03-01T12:21:02Z",
    "id": "023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353",
    "managed_by": {
      "parent_org_id": "4536bcfad5faccb111b47003c79917fa",
      "parent_org_name": "Demo Parent Organization"
    },
    "name": "Demo Account",
    "settings": {
      "abuse_contact_email": "string",
      "enforce_twofactor": false
    },
    "type": "standard"
  }
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-account-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Account Creation Success Response|[iam_response_single_account](#schemaiam_response_single_account)|
|4XX|Client Error|Account Creation Failure Response|[iam_api-response-common-failure](#schemaiam_api-response-common-failure)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
api_email & api_key
</aside>

## Batch move accounts

<a id="opIdAccounts_batchMoveAccounts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/move \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
```

`POST /accounts/move`

## Move account to organization

<a id="opIdAccounts_moveAccounts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/move \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "destination_organization_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/move`

Move an account into a destination organization, either assigning a standalone account
to an organization or moving it between organizations in the same hierarchy. Availability
depends on the organization's capabilities.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "destination_organization_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="move-account-to-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|The ID of the account to move.|
|body|body|object|true|The destination organization ID is where the account is to be moved.|
|» destination_organization_id|body|string|true|The ID of the organization to move the account into.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [
    {
      "code": 0,
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "result": {
    "account_id": "string",
    "destination_organization_id": "string",
    "source_organization_id": "string"
  },
  "success": true
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 0,
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [
    {
      "code": 0,
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "result": {},
  "success": false
}
```

<h3 id="move-account-to-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The request has succeeded.|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|An unexpected error response.|[organizations-api_V4ErrorResponse](#schemaorganizations-api_v4errorresponse)|

## List account organizations

<a id="opIdAccounts_listAccountOrganizations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/organizations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/organizations`

Retrieve a list of the organizations that "contain" this account or are
managing it.

The returned list will be in order from "root" to "leaf", where the "leaf"
will be the organization that _immediately_ contains the specified
account.

## Get account profile

<a id="opIdAccounts_getAccountProfile"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/profile \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/profile`

Retrieves the business profile (name, email, phone, address, and external metadata)
associated with this account's parent organization customer record. Profiles can be shared
across accounts and organizations. Only available to members of an organization that
contains the account.

<h3 id="get-account-profile-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|The ID of the account whose business profile to retrieve.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [
    {
      "code": 0,
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "result": {
    "business_address": "string",
    "business_email": "string",
    "business_name": "string",
    "business_phone": "string",
    "external_metadata": "string"
  },
  "success": true
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 0,
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [
    {
      "code": 0,
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "result": {},
  "success": false
}
```

<h3 id="get-account-profile-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The request has succeeded.|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|An unexpected error response.|[organizations-api_V4ErrorResponse](#schemaorganizations-api_v4errorresponse)|

<h3 id="get-account-profile-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

`PUT /accounts/{account_id}/profile`

Updates the business profile (name, email, phone, address, and external metadata) associated
with this account's parent organization customer record. Changes apply to every account and
organization sharing that profile. Omitted or empty fields are left unchanged. Only
available to members of an organization that contains the account.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "business_address": "string",
  "business_email": "string",
  "business_name": "string",
  "business_phone": "string",
  "external_metadata": "string"
}
```

|» business_address|body|string|true|none|
|» business_email|body|string|true|none|
|» business_name|body|string|true|none|
|» business_phone|body|string|true|none|

## List abuse reports against the account

<a id="opIdListAbuseReports"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/abuse-reports \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/abuse-reports`

List abuse reports made against domains or other content associated with the account. To list reports that the account submitted, use the submitted abuse reports endpoint instead.

<h3 id="list-abuse-reports-against-the-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|Cloudflare Account ID|
|page|query|integer|false|Where in pagination to start listing abuse reports|
|per_page|query|integer|false|How many abuse reports per page to list|
|sort|query|string|false|A property to sort by, followed by the order (id, cdate, domain, type, status)|
|search|query|string|false|Free-text search. Returns reports whose report ID starts with the term or whose domain contains the term, both case-insensitively. Surrounding whitespace is ignored, and an empty value is treated as absent. Combined with the other filters using AND.|
|domain|query|string|false|Filter by domain name related to the abuse report|
|created_before|query|string|false|Returns reports created before the specified date|
|created_after|query|string|false|Returns reports created after the specified date|
|status|query|[abuse-reports_ReportStatus](#schemaabuse-reports_reportstatus)|false|Filter by the status of the report.|
|type|query|[abuse-reports_ReportType](#schemaabuse-reports_reporttype)|false|Filter by the type of the report.|
|mitigation_status|query|[abuse-reports_MitigationStatus](#schemaabuse-reports_mitigationstatus)|false|Filter reports that have any mitigations in the given status.|

## Check whether a report can be appealed

<a id="opIdCheckAppealEligibility"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/abuse-reports/string/appeals/eligibility \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/abuse-reports/{report_id}/appeals/eligibility`

Returns whether the report is currently appealable, along with the signals behind that decision: whether it already has an open appeal, how many appeals have been submitted against it, and whether it has at least one mitigation that an appeal could reverse.
Report-level appeals are currently available only for DMCA (copyright) reports. For other report types this operation returns the same `404 Report not found` response as a report that does not exist for the account.

<h3 id="check-whether-a-report-can-be-appealed-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|Cloudflare Account ID|
|report_id|path|string|true|Abuse Report ID|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],

    {
      "message": "string"
    }

    "appealable": true,
```

## Request review on mitigations

<a id="opIdRequestReview"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/abuse-reports/string/mitigations/appeal \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "appeals": [
      {
        "id": "string",
        "reason": "misclassified"
      }
    ],
    "data": {
      "city": "string",
      "company": "string",
      "counter_notice_response": "string",
      "country": "string",
      "email": "user@example.com",
      "full_name": "string",
      "jurisdiction_consent": true,
      "perjury_attestation": true,
      "phone_number": "string",
      "signature": "string",
      "state": "string",
      "street_address": "string",
      "urls": [
        "http://example.com"
      ],
      "zip_code": "string"
    },
    "explanation": "string",
    "type": "counter_notice"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/abuse-reports/{report_id}/mitigations/appeal`

Request a review of mitigations applied because of an abuse report, or submit a report-level appeal.

- To request a review of specific mitigations, send `appeals` with the mitigation IDs and reasons. Repeating a request for a mitigation with an unresolved appeal is idempotent and returns that mitigation in the in-review state.
- To submit a report-level appeal, send `type` and, for a `counter_notice`, the counter-notice details in `data`. Report-level appeals are currently available only for DMCA (copyright) reports.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "appeals": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "reason": "misclassified"
    }
  ],
  "data": {
    "city": "string",
    "company": "string",
    "counter_notice_response": "string",
    "country": "string",
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "full_name": "string",
    "jurisdiction_consent": true,
    "perjury_attestation": true,
    "phone_number": "string",
    "signature": "string",
    "state": "string",
    "street_address": "string",
    "urls": [
      "http://example.com"
    ],
    "zip_code": "string"
  },
  "explanation": "string",
  "type": "counter_notice"
}
```

<h3 id="request-review-on-mitigations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|Cloudflare Account ID|
|report_id|path|string|true|Abuse Report ID|
|body|body|[abuse-reports_MitigationAppealRequest](#schemaabuse-reports_mitigationappealrequest)|true|none|
|» appeals|body|[[abuse-reports_MitigationAppeal](#schemaabuse-reports_mitigationappeal)]|false|List of mitigations to appeal.|
|» data|body|[abuse-reports_DMCACounterNotice](#schemaabuse-reports_dmcacounternotice)|false|Counter-notice details supporting an appeal.|
|» explanation|body|string|false|Optional explanation for a "content_removed" appeal, such as how the content was removed. Not accepted for other appeal types.|
|» type|body|[abuse-reports_AppealType](#schemaabuse-reports_appealtype)|false|The type of appeal being submitted.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|

|» type|counter_notice|
|» type|content_removed|

## Submit an abuse report

<a id="opIdSubmitAbuseReport"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/abuse-reports/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "act": "abuse_dmca",
    "comments": "string",
    "company": "string",
    "email": "string",
    "email2": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "reported_country": "st",
    "reported_user_agent": "string",
    "tele": "string",
    "title": "string",
    "urls": "string",
    "address1": "string",
    "agent_name": "string",
    "agree": 1,
    "city": "string",
    "country": "string",
    "host_notification": "send",
    "original_work": "string",
    "owner_notification": "send",
    "signature": "string",
    "state": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/abuse-reports/{report_param}`

Submit an abuse report of a particular type.

Requires the abuse-reports entitlement on the account (Enterprise
accounts have it by default; other accounts must request access) and an
API token with the `Trust and Safety Write` permission. If the account
is not entitled, the request is rejected with an HTTP `401` response
(see below).

Delegated reports: In limited circumstances, Cloudflare works with
select customers who have established abuse-handling programs. For
these customers, Cloudflare may forward abuse reports directly and in
full—including reporter contact information, comments, and supporting
evidence—without redaction or preprocessing by Cloudflare. This allows
the customer to investigate and respond using their own policies and
processes. For delegated reports, the report—including contact
information and comments—will be forwarded to the customer in full
regardless of the `host_notification` and `owner_notification` values.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "act": "abuse_dmca",
  "comments": "string",
  "company": "string",
  "email": "string",
  "email2": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "reported_country": "st",
  "reported_user_agent": "string",
  "tele": "string",
  "title": "string",
  "urls": "string",
  "address1": "string",
  "agent_name": "string",
  "agree": 1,
  "city": "string",
  "country": "string",
  "host_notification": "send",
  "original_work": "string",
  "owner_notification": "send",
  "signature": "string",
  "state": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="submit-an-abuse-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|Cloudflare Account ID|
|report_param|path|[abuse-reports_SubmissionReportType](#schemaabuse-reports_submissionreporttype)|true|The report type to be submitted. Example: abuse_general|
|body|body|[abuse-reports_SubmitReportRequest](#schemaabuse-reports_submitreportrequest)|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[abuse-reports_DMCAReport](#schemaabuse-reports_dmcareport)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[abuse-reports_TrademarkReport](#schemaabuse-reports_trademarkreport)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[abuse-reports_GeneralReport](#schemaabuse-reports_generalreport)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[abuse-reports_PhishingReport](#schemaabuse-reports_phishingreport)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[abuse-reports_CSAMReport](#schemaabuse-reports_csamreport)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[abuse-reports_ThreatReport](#schemaabuse-reports_threatreport)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[abuse-reports_RegistrarWhoisReport](#schemaabuse-reports_registrarwhoisreport)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[abuse-reports_NCSEIReport](#schemaabuse-reports_ncseireport)|false|none|

<h3 id="submit-an-abuse-report-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Report submitted successfully|[abuse-reports_SubmitReportResponse](#schemaabuse-reports_submitreportresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Report submitted with an error|[abuse-reports_SubmitErrorResponse](#schemaabuse-reports_submiterrorresponse)|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized to submit abuse reports. Missing or<br>invalid credentials may be rejected with the standard Cloudflare API<br>authentication error. If credentials are valid, this is most commonly<br>because the account does not have the abuse-reports entitlement<br>(Enterprise accounts have it by default; other accounts must request<br>access), or because the API token is missing the<br>`Trust and Safety Write` permission. Entitlement failures<br>return the message `Not entitled to use feature: Abuse Report API`.|[abuse-reports_UnauthorizedErrorResponse](#schemaabuse-reports_unauthorizederrorresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|Cloudflare's API layer rejected the request because the API token or<br>OAuth grant does not have the required Trust and Safety permission for<br>this account. The response uses error code `10000`.|[abuse-reports_CloudflareAPIErrorResponse](#schemaabuse-reports_cloudflareapierrorresponse)|
|429|Too Many Requests|The submitter is over an enforced intake rate limit; the report was not created|[abuse-reports_RateLimitedErrorResponse](#schemaabuse-reports_ratelimitederrorresponse)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Report submitted with an error|[abuse-reports_SubmitErrorResponse](#schemaabuse-reports_submiterrorresponse)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|429|Retry-After|integer||Seconds to wait before the next submission can be accepted.|

## Create a new MCP Portal

<a id="opIdmcp-portals-api-create-portals"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/a86a8f5c339544d7bdc89926de14fb8c/access/ai-controls/mcp/portals \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "allow_code_mode": true,
    "code_mode": "opt_in",
    "description": "This is my custom MCP Portal",
    "hostname": "example.com",
    "id": "my-mcp-portal",
    "name": "My MCP Portal",
    "secure_web_gateway": false,
    "servers": [
      {
        "default_disabled": true,
        "on_behalf": true,
        "server_id": "my-mcp-server",
        "updated_prompts": [
          {
            "alias": "my-custom-alias",
            "description": "string",
            "enabled": true,
            "name": "string"
          }
        ],
        "updated_tools": [
          {
            "alias": "my-custom-alias",
            "description": "string",
            "enabled": true,
            "name": "string"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/access/ai-controls/mcp/portals`

Creates a new MCP portal for managing AI tool access through Cloudflare Access.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "allow_code_mode": true,
  "code_mode": "opt_in",
  "description": "This is my custom MCP Portal",
  "hostname": "example.com",
  "id": "my-mcp-portal",
  "name": "My MCP Portal",
  "secure_web_gateway": false,
  "servers": [
    {
      "default_disabled": true,
      "on_behalf": true,
      "server_id": "my-mcp-server",
      "updated_prompts": [
        {
          "alias": "my-custom-alias",
          "description": "string",
          "enabled": true,
          "name": "string"
        }
      ],
      "updated_tools": [
        {
          "alias": "my-custom-alias",
          "description": "string",
          "enabled": true,
          "name": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» allow_code_mode|body|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: use `code_mode` for new integrations. `true` maps to any non-off Code Mode policy; `false` maps to `code_mode: off`. If both fields are sent, they must be consistent or the request returns a 400.|
|» code_mode|body|string|false|Code Mode policy for this portal. `off`: Code Mode is unavailable; query parameters are ignored. `opt_in`: Code Mode is off by default; clients turn it on with `?codemode=search_and_execute`. `default_on`: Code Mode is on by default; clients can opt out with `?codemode=off`. `enforced`: Code Mode is always on; query parameters are ignored. Defaults to `opt_in` when omitted on create. If both `code_mode` and `allow_code_mode` are sent, they must be consistent or the request returns a 400.|

## Update an MCP Portal

<a id="opIdmcp-portals-api-update-portals"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/a86a8f5c339544d7bdc89926de14fb8c/access/ai-controls/mcp/portals/my-mcp-portal \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "allow_code_mode": true,
    "code_mode": "opt_in",
    "description": "This is my custom MCP Portal",
    "hostname": "example.com",
    "name": "My MCP Portal",
    "secure_web_gateway": false,
    "servers": [
      {
        "default_disabled": true,
        "on_behalf": true,
        "server_id": "my-mcp-server",
        "updated_prompts": [
          {
            "alias": "my-custom-alias",
            "description": "string",
            "enabled": true,
            "name": "string"
          }
        ],
        "updated_tools": [
          {
            "alias": "my-custom-alias",
            "description": "string",
            "enabled": true,
            "name": "string"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /accounts/{account_id}/access/ai-controls/mcp/portals/{id}`

Updates an MCP portal configuration.

## Resolve an MCP server OAuth redirect URI

<a id="opIdmcp-portals-api-effective-redirect-uri"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/a86a8f5c339544d7bdc89926de14fb8c/access/ai-controls/mcp/portals/my-mcp-portal/servers/my-mcp-server/effective-redirect-uri \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/access/ai-controls/mcp/portals/{portal_id}/servers/{server_id}/effective-redirect-uri`

Resolves the OAuth redirect URI to register for a portal and server based on the server's current shared callback setting. Use the returned value when setting up a new manual OAuth registration. This value is for display only: existing manual OAuth registrations continue using their stored redirect URI, so changing callback settings can make this result differ from the URI used at runtime.

<h3 id="resolve-an-mcp-server-oauth-redirect-uri-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|portal_id|path|string|true|none|
|server_id|path|string|true|none|
|account_id|path|string|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": {
    "redirect_uri": "http://example.com",
    "source": "per_portal"
  },
  "success": true
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7002,
      "message": "Not Found"
    }
  ],
  "success": false
}
```

<h3 id="resolve-an-mcp-server-oauth-redirect-uri-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns the effective redirect URI and its source.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|Inline|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|success|boolean|true|none|none|

## Create a new MCP Server

<a id="opIdmcp-portals-api-create-servers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/a86a8f5c339544d7bdc89926de14fb8c/access/ai-controls/mcp/servers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "auth_credentials": "sk-my-bearer-token",
    "auth_type": "unauthenticated",
    "client_secret": "string",
    "description": "This is one remote MCP server",
    "hostname": "https://example.com/mcp",
    "id": "my-mcp-server",
    "is_shared_oauth_callback_enabled": false,
    "name": "My MCP Server",
    "secure_web_gateway": false,
    "updated_prompts": [
      {
        "alias": "my-custom-alias",
        "description": "string",
        "enabled": true,
        "name": "string"
      }
    ],
    "updated_tools": [
      {
        "alias": "my-custom-alias",
        "description": "string",
        "enabled": true,
        "name": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/access/ai-controls/mcp/servers`

Creates a new MCP server for connecting to an upstream MCP endpoint.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "auth_credentials": "sk-my-bearer-token",
  "auth_type": "unauthenticated",
  "client_secret": "string",
  "description": "This is one remote MCP server",
  "hostname": "https://example.com/mcp",
  "id": "my-mcp-server",
  "is_shared_oauth_callback_enabled": false,
  "name": "My MCP Server",
  "secure_web_gateway": false,
  "updated_prompts": [
    {
      "alias": "my-custom-alias",
      "description": "string",
      "enabled": true,
      "name": "string"
    }
  ],
  "updated_tools": [
    {
      "alias": "my-custom-alias",
      "description": "string",
      "enabled": true,
      "name": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-mcp-server-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» auth_credentials|body|string|false|Credential configuration for the upstream MCP server. For auth_type "bearer", either a raw token string (e.g. "sk-abc123"), which is wrapped server-side as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or a JSON-encoded object of the form `{"headers":{"Header-Name":"value",...}}` for custom or multiple static headers (e.g. Cloudflare Access service tokens: `{"headers":{"cf-access-client-id":"...","cf-access-client-secret":"..."}}`). For auth_type "oauth" with a pre-registered client, send a JSON-encoded object containing `auth_mode:"manual"`, `config.authorization_endpoint`, `config.token_endpoint`, and `registration_info.client_id`. Also provide `registration_info.redirect_uris` unless `is_shared_oauth_callback_enabled` is true. Optional fields include `config.issuer`, `config.revocation_endpoint`, `registration_info.scope`, and `registration_info.token_endpoint_auth_method`. Send the client secret in the separate `client_secret` field. Omit `auth_credentials` on update to preserve the existing configuration.|
|» auth_type|body|string|true|Authentication method used to connect to the upstream MCP server.|
|» client_secret|body|string|false|Pre-registered OAuth client_secret. Write-only - accepted on create/update when auth_credentials.auth_mode is 'manual'. Required when creating a manual OAuth server or converting an existing server to manual mode. Omit it on update to preserve the existing secret; provide it to rotate the secret. Stored AES-GCM-encrypted in server_oauth_secrets; never returned by read endpoints.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Optional description of the MCP server.|
|» hostname|body|string(uri)|true|URL of the upstream MCP endpoint.|
|» id|body|string|true|Unique identifier for the MCP server.|
|» is_shared_oauth_callback_enabled|body|boolean|false|When true, the gateway worker uses the shared Cloudflare-owned OAuth callback endpoint as the redirect_uri for upstream on-behalf OAuth, instead of the customer portal hostname. Defaults to false (off); opt in per server by setting true.|
|» name|body|string|true|Display name for the MCP server.|
|» secure_web_gateway|body|boolean|false|Route outbound traffic to this MCP server through Zero Trust Secure Web Gateway.|
|» updated_prompts|body|[object]|false|Server-wide prompt capability overrides.|
|» » alias|body|string|false|Custom name exposed for the capability.|
|» » description|body|string|false|Custom description exposed for the capability.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether the capability is available through the MCP server.|
|» » name|body|string|true|Name of the tool or prompt capability to override.|
|» updated_tools|body|[object]|false|Server-wide tool capability overrides.|
|» » alias|body|string|false|Custom name exposed for the capability.|
|» » description|body|string|false|Custom description exposed for the capability.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether the capability is available through the MCP server.|
|» » name|body|string|true|Name of the tool or prompt capability to override.|

## Update an MCP Server

<a id="opIdmcp-portals-api-update-servers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/a86a8f5c339544d7bdc89926de14fb8c/access/ai-controls/mcp/servers/my-mcp-server \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "auth_credentials": "sk-my-bearer-token",
    "client_secret": "string",
    "description": "This is one remote MCP server",
    "is_shared_oauth_callback_enabled": false,
    "name": "My MCP Server",
    "secure_web_gateway": false,
    "updated_prompts": [
      {
        "alias": "my-custom-alias",
        "description": "string",
        "enabled": true,
        "name": "string"
      }
    ],
    "updated_tools": [
      {
        "alias": "my-custom-alias",
        "description": "string",
        "enabled": true,
        "name": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /accounts/{account_id}/access/ai-controls/mcp/servers/{id}`

Updates an MCP server's configuration and credentials.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "auth_credentials": "sk-my-bearer-token",
  "client_secret": "string",
  "description": "This is one remote MCP server",
  "is_shared_oauth_callback_enabled": false,
  "name": "My MCP Server",
  "secure_web_gateway": false,
  "updated_prompts": [
    {
      "alias": "my-custom-alias",
      "description": "string",
      "enabled": true,
      "name": "string"
    }
  ],
  "updated_tools": [
    {
      "alias": "my-custom-alias",
      "description": "string",
      "enabled": true,
      "name": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-mcp-server-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|account_id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» auth_credentials|body|string|false|Credential configuration for the upstream MCP server. For auth_type "bearer", either a raw token string (e.g. "sk-abc123"), which is wrapped server-side as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or a JSON-encoded object of the form `{"headers":{"Header-Name":"value",...}}` for custom or multiple static headers (e.g. Cloudflare Access service tokens: `{"headers":{"cf-access-client-id":"...","cf-access-client-secret":"..."}}`). For auth_type "oauth" with a pre-registered client, send a JSON-encoded object containing `auth_mode:"manual"`, `config.authorization_endpoint`, `config.token_endpoint`, and `registration_info.client_id`. Also provide `registration_info.redirect_uris` unless `is_shared_oauth_callback_enabled` is true. Optional fields include `config.issuer`, `config.revocation_endpoint`, `registration_info.scope`, and `registration_info.token_endpoint_auth_method`. Send the client secret in the separate `client_secret` field. Omit `auth_credentials` on update to preserve the existing configuration.|
|» client_secret|body|string|false|Pre-registered OAuth client_secret. Write-only - accepted on create/update when auth_credentials.auth_mode is 'manual'. Required when creating a manual OAuth server or converting an existing server to manual mode. Omit it on update to preserve the existing secret; provide it to rotate the secret. Stored AES-GCM-encrypted in server_oauth_secrets; never returned by read endpoints.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Optional description of the MCP server.|
|» is_shared_oauth_callback_enabled|body|boolean|false|When true, the gateway worker uses the shared Cloudflare-owned OAuth callback endpoint as the redirect_uri for upstream on-behalf OAuth, instead of the customer portal hostname. Defaults to false (off); opt in per server by setting true.|
|» name|body|string|false|Display name for the MCP server.|
|» secure_web_gateway|body|boolean|false|Route outbound traffic to this MCP server through Zero Trust Secure Web Gateway.|
|» updated_prompts|body|[object]|false|Server-wide prompt capability overrides.|
|» » alias|body|string|false|Custom name exposed for the capability.|
|» » description|body|string|false|Custom description exposed for the capability.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether the capability is available through the MCP server.|
|» » name|body|string|true|Name of the tool or prompt capability to override.|
|» updated_tools|body|[object]|false|Server-wide tool capability overrides.|
|» » alias|body|string|false|Custom name exposed for the capability.|
|» » description|body|string|false|Custom description exposed for the capability.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether the capability is available through the MCP server.|
|» » name|body|string|true|Name of the tool or prompt capability to override.|

## Sync MCP Server Capabilities

<a id="opIdmcp-portals-api-sync-server"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/a86a8f5c339544d7bdc89926de14fb8c/access/ai-controls/mcp/servers/my-mcp-server/sync \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/access/ai-controls/mcp/servers/{id}/sync`

Syncs an MCP server's capabilities and returns the updated server state, including any connection errors.

<h3 id="sync-mcp-server-capabilities-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|account_id|path|string|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": {
    "error": "string",
    "error_details": {
      "cause": "string",
      "is_upstream": true,
      "mcp_code": 0,
      "retryable": true,
      "status_code": 0
    },
    "status": "waiting"
  },
  "success": true
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7002,
      "message": "Not Found"
    }
  ],
  "success": false
}
```

<h3 id="sync-mcp-server-capabilities-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Sync completed. Check result.status and result.error_details for outcome.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|Inline|

<h3 id="sync-mcp-server-capabilities-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

|» » cause|string|false|none|Underlying error message|

|» » mcp_code|number|false|none|MCP protocol error code|
|» » retryable|boolean|false|none|Whether the error is transient and worth retrying|
|» » status_code|number|false|none|HTTP status code from the server|
|» status|string|false|none|none|
|success|boolean|true|none|none|

|» status|ready|
|» status|stale|
|» status|error|

## Add an Access application

<a id="opIdaccess-applications-add-an-application"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/access/apps \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "allowed_idps": [
      "699d98642c564d2e855e9661899b7252"
    ],
    "destinations": [
      {
        "overrides": [
          {
            "behavior": "public",
            "path_pattern": "/health/*"
          }
        ],
        "type": "public",
        "uri": "string"
      }
    ],
    "domain": "test.example.com/admin",
    "name": "Admin Site",
    "oauth_configuration": {
      "dynamic_client_registration": {
        "allow_any_on_localhost": true,
        "allow_any_on_loopback": true,
        "allowed_uris": [
          "https://example.com/callback",
          "com.example.app:/oauth/callback"
        ],
        "enabled": true
      },
      "enabled": true,
      "grant": {
        "access_token_lifetime": "5m",
        "session_duration": "24h"
      }
    },
    "self_hosted_domains": [
      "test.example.com/admin",
      "test.anotherexample.com/staff"
    ],
    "type": {},
    "user_populations": [
      "f174e90a-fafe-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415"
    ]
  }'
```

<h3 id="add-an-access-application-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Add an Access application response|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|Add an Access application response failure|[access_api-response-common-failure](#schemaaccess_api-response-common-failure)|

<h3 id="add-an-access-application-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **201**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[access_messages](#schemaaccess_messages)|true|none|none|
|messages|[access_messages](#schemaaccess_messages)|true|none|none|
|success|boolean|true|none|Whether the API call was successful.|
|result|[access_app_response](#schemaaccess_app_response)|false|none|none|
|result|[access_app_response](#schemaaccess_app_response)|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|success|true|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
api_token, api_email & api_key
</aside>

## Get an Access application

<a id="opIdaccess-applications-get-an-access-application"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/access/apps/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/access/apps/{app_id}`

Fetches information about an Access application.

<h3 id="get-an-access-application-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|app_id|path|[access_app_id](#schemaaccess_app_id)|true|none|
|account_id|path|[access_identifier](#schemaaccess_identifier)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "aud": "737646a56ab1df6ec9bddc7e5ca84eaf3b0768850f3ffb5d74f1534911fe3893",
    "created_at": {},
    "id": "f174e90a-fafe-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415",
    "updated_at": {},
    "allowed_idps": [
      "699d98642c564d2e855e9661899b7252"
    ],
    "destinations": [
      {
        "overrides": [
          {
            "behavior": "public",
            "path_pattern": "/health/*"
          }
        ],
        "type": "public",
        "uri": "string"
      }
    ],
    "domain": "test.example.com/admin",
    "name": "Admin Site",
    "oauth_configuration": {
      "dynamic_client_registration": {
        "allow_any_on_localhost": true,
        "allow_any_on_loopback": true,
        "allowed_uris": [
          "https://example.com/callback",
          "com.example.app:/oauth/callback"
        ],
        "enabled": true
      },
      "enabled": true,
      "grant": {
        "access_token_lifetime": "5m",
        "session_duration": "24h"
      }
    },
    "self_hosted_domains": [
      "test.example.com/admin",
      "test.anotherexample.com/staff"
    ],
    "type": {},
    "user_populations": [
      "f174e90a-fafe-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415"
    ]
  }
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

<h3 id="get-an-access-application-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Get an Access application response|[access_single_response-9](#schemaaccess_single_response-9)|
|4XX|Client Error|Get an Access application response failure|[access_api-response-common-failure](#schemaaccess_api-response-common-failure)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
api_token, api_email & api_key
</aside>

## Update an Access application

<a id="opIdaccess-applications-update-an-access-application"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/access/apps/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "allowed_idps": [
      "699d98642c564d2e855e9661899b7252"
    ],
    "destinations": [
      {
        "overrides": [
          {
            "behavior": "public",
            "path_pattern": "/health/*"
          }
        ],
        "type": "public",
        "uri": "string"
      }
    ],
    "domain": "test.example.com/admin",
    "name": "Admin Site",
    "oauth_configuration": {
      "dynamic_client_registration": {
        "allow_any_on_localhost": true,
        "allow_any_on_loopback": true,
        "allowed_uris": [
          "https://example.com/callback",
          "com.example.app:/oauth/callback"
        ],
        "enabled": true
      },
      "enabled": true,
      "grant": {
        "access_token_lifetime": "5m",
        "session_duration": "24h"
      }
    },
    "self_hosted_domains": [
      "test.example.com/admin",
      "test.anotherexample.com/staff"
    ],
    "type": {},
    "user_populations": [
      "f174e90a-fafe-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /accounts/{account_id}/access/apps/{app_id}`

Updates an Access application.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "allowed_idps": [
    "699d98642c564d2e855e9661899b7252"
  ],
  "destinations": [
    {
      "overrides": [
        {
          "behavior": "public",
          "path_pattern": "/health/*"
        }
      ],
      "type": "public",
      "uri": "string"
    }
  ],
  "domain": "test.example.com/admin",
  "name": "Admin Site",
  "oauth_configuration": {
    "dynamic_client_registration": {
      "allow_any_on_localhost": true,
      "allow_any_on_loopback": true,
      "allowed_uris": [
        "https://example.com/callback",
        "com.example.app:/oauth/callback"
      ],
      "enabled": true
    },
    "enabled": true,
    "grant": {
      "access_token_lifetime": "5m",
      "session_duration": "24h"
    }
  },
  "self_hosted_domains": [
    "test.example.com/admin",
    "test.anotherexample.com/staff"
  ],
  "type": {},
  "user_populations": [
    "f174e90a-fafe-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415"
  ]
}
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/access/custom_pages/validate`

Validate a Liquid template and return its errors and warnings without persisting it.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "template": "string",
  "type": "identity_denied",
  "version": 0
}
```

<h3 id="validate-a-custom-page-template-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[access_identifier](#schemaaccess_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[access_custom_page_validate](#schemaaccess_custom_page_validate)|false|none|
|» template|body|string|true|The Liquid template to validate.|
|» type|body|[access_type-2](#schemaaccess_type-2)|true|Custom page type.|
|» version|body|integer|false|Contract version to validate against; omit for the latest.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|identity_denied|
|» type|forbidden|
|» type|login|
|» type|interstitial|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "errors": [
      {
        "message": "string",
        "ref": "string",
        "tier": "string"
      }
    ],
    "page_type": "identity_denied",
    "version": 0,
    "warnings": [
      {
        "message": "string",
        "ref": "string",
        "tier": "string"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

<h3 id="validate-a-custom-page-template-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|200|OK|Validate a custom page template response|[access_validate_response](#schemaaccess_validate_response)|
|4XX|Client Error|Validate a custom page template response failure|[access_api-response-common-failure](#schemaaccess_api-response-common-failure)|

</aside>

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/access/groups \
```
```bash
  -X POST \
```
```bash
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

  -d '{
    "exclude": [

    "require": [

        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

## Create SAML encryption certificate for Identity Provider

<a id="opIdaccess-identity-providers-create-saml-certificate-for-identity-provider"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/access/identity_providers/f174e90a-fafe-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415/saml_certificate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/access/identity_providers/{identity_provider_id}/saml_certificate`

Creates a new SAML encryption certificate set and assigns it to the specified 
SAML Identity Provider. This endpoint is idempotent - if the IdP already has 
a certificate set assigned, the existing certificate set is returned with a 200 status.

**Workflow for enabling SAML encryption:**
1. Call this endpoint to create and assign a certificate set to the IdP
2. Update the IdP configuration (PUT `/identity_providers/{id}`) with:
   - `config.enable_encryption: true`
   - `saml_certificate_set_id: <uid from step 1>`
3. Configure the certificate's public key in your external SAML Identity Provider


<h3 id="create-saml-encryption-certificate-for-identity-provider-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[access_identifier](#schemaaccess_identifier)|true|none|
|identity_provider_id|path|[access_uuid](#schemaaccess_uuid)|true|none|

```bash
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/access/idp_federation_grants`

Creates an IdP federation grant for the specified identity provider, making it
available for federation to other accounts in the same Cloudflare organization.

The account must belong to a Cloudflare organization. One-time pin and
Cloudflare-managed identity providers cannot be federated. An account
can federate at most five identity providers at a time.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "idp_id": "a79de439-0e7f-4ebb-8a02-222222222222"
}
```

|» idp_id|body|string(uuid)|true|UID of the identity provider to federate. Must be an existing identity provider in this account. One-time pin and Cloudflare-managed identity providers cannot be federated.|

## Get Access authentication logs

<a id="opIdaccess-authentication-logs-get-access-authentication-logs"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/access/logs/access_requests \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/access/logs/access_requests`

Gets a list of Access authentication audit logs for an account.

<h3 id="get-access-authentication-logs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[access_identifier](#schemaaccess_identifier)|true|none|
|limit|query|integer|false|The maximum number of log entries to retrieve.|
|direction|query|string|false|The chronological sorting order for the logs.|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|The earliest event timestamp to query.|
|until|query|string(date-time)|false|The latest event timestamp to query.|
|page|query|integer|false|none|
|per_page|query|integer|false|none|
|email|query|[access_email-3](#schemaaccess_email-3)|false|Filter by user email. Match mode is controlled by `emailOp` (preferred) or the legacy `email_exact` flag.<br>- Default (no `emailOp`, `email_exact=false` or unset): substring match — `email=@example.com` returns all events with that domain.<br>- Exact match: set `emailOp=eq` (preferred) or `email_exact=true` — e.g. `email=user@example.com&email_exact=true` returns only that user.<br>- Explicit substring match: set `emailOp=contains` (without `email_exact=true`). When both are set, `email_exact=true` takes precedence and the match is exact.<br>- Exclusion: set `emailOp=neq`. With `email_exact=true` this is an exact-value exclusion; without it, a fuzzy substring exclusion.<br>|
|email_exact|query|boolean|false|When true, `email` is matched exactly instead of substring matching.|
|user_id|query|[access_user_id](#schemaaccess_user_id)|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated. Accepted for backward compatibility but no longer applied<br>as a filter. Use `email` instead.<br>|
|allowedOp|query|string|false|Operator for the `allowed` filter.|
|country_codeOp|query|string|false|Operator for the `country_code` filter.|
|app_typeOp|query|string|false|Operator for the `app_type` filter.|
|app_uidOp|query|string|false|Operator for the `app_uid` filter.|
|ray_idOp|query|string|false|Operator for the `ray_id` filter.|
|emailOp|query|string|false|Operator for the `email` filter.<br>`contains` performs a substring (case-sensitive) match. When `email_exact=true`<br>is also set, `email_exact` takes precedence and `contains` is ignored.<br>|
|idpOp|query|string|false|Operator for the `idp` filter.|
|non_identityOp|query|string|false|Operator for the `non_identity` filter.|
|user_idOp|query|string|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated. Accepted for backward compatibility but no longer applied<br>as a filter (the `user_id` parameter is itself deprecated).<br>|
|fields|query|string|false|Comma-separated list of fields to include in the response.<br>When omitted, all fields are returned.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|direction|desc|
|direction|asc|
|allowedOp|eq|
|allowedOp|neq|
|country_codeOp|eq|
|country_codeOp|neq|
|app_typeOp|eq|
|app_typeOp|neq|
|app_uidOp|eq|
|app_uidOp|neq|
|ray_idOp|eq|
|ray_idOp|neq|
|emailOp|eq|
|emailOp|neq|
|emailOp|contains|
|idpOp|eq|
|idpOp|neq|
|non_identityOp|eq|
|non_identityOp|neq|
|user_idOp|eq|
|user_idOp|neq|

<h3 id="update-your-zero-trust-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[access_identifier](#schemaaccess_identifier)|true|none|

|» allow_authenticate_via_warp|body|[access_allow_authenticate_via_warp](#schemaaccess_allow_authenticate_via_warp)|false|When set to true, users can authenticate via WARP for any application in your organization. Application settings will take precedence over this value.|
|» auth_domain|body|[access_auth_domain](#schemaaccess_auth_domain)|false|The unique subdomain assigned to your Zero Trust organization. If omitted on creation, a unique subdomain is auto-generated in the format `adjective-noun-hex4` (e.g. `frosty-moon-7a3b.cloudflareaccess.com`).|
|» auto_redirect_to_identity|body|[access_auto_redirect_to_identity](#schemaaccess_auto_redirect_to_identity)|false|When set to `true`, users skip the identity provider selection step during login.|
|» custom_pages|body|[access_custom_pages](#schemaaccess_custom_pages)|false|none|
|» deny_unmatched_requests|body|[access_deny_unmatched_requests](#schemaaccess_deny_unmatched_requests)|false|Determines whether to deny all requests to Cloudflare-protected resources that lack an associated Access application. If enabled, you must explicitly configure an Access application and policy to allow traffic to your Cloudflare-protected resources. For domains you want to be public across all subdomains, add the domain to the `deny_unmatched_requests_exempted_zone_names` array.|
|» deny_unmatched_requests_exempted_zone_names|body|[access_deny_unmatched_requests_exempted_zone_names](#schemaaccess_deny_unmatched_requests_exempted_zone_names)|false|Contains zone names to exempt from the `deny_unmatched_requests` feature. Requests to a subdomain in an exempted zone will block unauthenticated traffic by default if there is a configured Access application and policy that matches the request.|
|» disable_end_user_app_creation|body|[access_disable_end_user_app_creation](#schemaaccess_disable_end_user_app_creation)|false|Whether creation of end user applications is disabled for this organization.|
|» is_ui_read_only|body|[access_is_ui_read_only](#schemaaccess_is_ui_read_only)|false|Lock all settings as Read-Only in the Dashboard, regardless of user permission. Updates may only be made via the API or Terraform for this account when enabled.|
|» login_design|body|[access_login_design](#schemaaccess_login_design)|false|none|
|» mfa_config|body|[access_org_mfa_config](#schemaaccess_org_mfa_config)|false|Configures multi-factor authentication (MFA) settings for an organization.|
|» mfa_piv_key_requirements|body|[access_mfa_piv_key_requirements](#schemaaccess_mfa_piv_key_requirements)|false|Configures PIV key requirements for MFA using hardware security keys.|
|» mfa_required_for_all_apps|body|[access_mfa_required_for_all_apps](#schemaaccess_mfa_required_for_all_apps)|false|Determines whether global MFA settings apply to applications by default. The organization must have MFA enabled with at least one authentication method and a session duration configured. Note: 'allowed_authenticators' cannot contain only the infrastructure SSH authenticators ('piv_key' and 'ssh_fido2_key') if the organization has any non-infrastructure applications.|
|» name|body|[access_name](#schemaaccess_name)|false|The name of your Zero Trust organization. When omitted on creation, defaults to the provided auth_domain; when both are omitted, defaults to the auto-generated subdomain slug (e.g. frosty-moon-7a3b).|
|» service_token_inactivity|body|[access_service_token_inactivity](#schemaaccess_service_token_inactivity)|false|Configures automatic enforcement for inactive service tokens. A service token is inactive if no policy references it, and it has not successfully authenticated with an Access application during the selected inactivity period. This setting applies to every service token in your Zero Trust account.|
|» session_duration|body|[access_session_duration](#schemaaccess_session_duration)|false|The amount of time that tokens issued for applications will be valid. Must be in the format `300ms` or `2h45m`. Valid time units are: ns, us (or µs), ms, s, m, h.|
|» strict_service_token_auth|body|[access_strict_service_token_auth](#schemaaccess_strict_service_token_auth)|false|Enables new behaviors for requests made with Access service tokens. Unauthorized requests emit audit logs, and return a 401 or 403 status code in the response instead of redirecting to the login page. Successful requests no longer receive a CF_Authorization cookie in the response. Zero Trust organizations created on or after October 5, 2026 will have this setting enabled by default, and cannot disable it.|
|» ui_read_only_toggle_reason|body|[access_ui_read_only_toggle_reason](#schemaaccess_ui_read_only_toggle_reason)|false|A description of the reason why the UI read only field is being toggled.|
|» user_seat_expiration_inactive_time|body|[access_user_seat_expiration_inactive_time](#schemaaccess_user_seat_expiration_inactive_time)|false|The amount of time a user seat is inactive before it expires. When the user seat exceeds the set time of inactivity, the user is removed as an active seat and no longer counts against your Teams seat count.  Minimum value for this setting is 1 month (730h). Must be in the format `300ms` or `2h45m`. Valid time units are: `ns`, `us` (or `µs`), `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`.|
|» warp_auth_non_browser_401|body|[access_warp_auth_non_browser_401](#schemaaccess_warp_auth_non_browser_401)|false|When enabled, unsuccessful WARP authentication requests with a non-HTML Accept header return a 401 response instead of redirecting to the login page.|
|» warp_auth_session_duration|body|[access_warp_auth_session_duration](#schemaaccess_warp_auth_session_duration)|false|The amount of time that tokens issued for applications will be valid. Must be in the format `30m` or `2h45m`. Valid time units are: m, h.|

<h3 id="create-your-zero-trust-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[access_identifier](#schemaaccess_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» allow_authenticate_via_warp|body|[access_allow_authenticate_via_warp](#schemaaccess_allow_authenticate_via_warp)|false|When set to true, users can authenticate via WARP for any application in your organization. Application settings will take precedence over this value.|
|» auth_domain|body|[access_auth_domain](#schemaaccess_auth_domain)|false|The unique subdomain assigned to your Zero Trust organization. If omitted on creation, a unique subdomain is auto-generated in the format `adjective-noun-hex4` (e.g. `frosty-moon-7a3b.cloudflareaccess.com`).|
|» auto_redirect_to_identity|body|[access_auto_redirect_to_identity](#schemaaccess_auto_redirect_to_identity)|false|When set to `true`, users skip the identity provider selection step during login.|
|» deny_unmatched_requests|body|[access_deny_unmatched_requests](#schemaaccess_deny_unmatched_requests)|false|Determines whether to deny all requests to Cloudflare-protected resources that lack an associated Access application. If enabled, you must explicitly configure an Access application and policy to allow traffic to your Cloudflare-protected resources. For domains you want to be public across all subdomains, add the domain to the `deny_unmatched_requests_exempted_zone_names` array.|
|» deny_unmatched_requests_exempted_zone_names|body|[access_deny_unmatched_requests_exempted_zone_names](#schemaaccess_deny_unmatched_requests_exempted_zone_names)|false|Contains zone names to exempt from the `deny_unmatched_requests` feature. Requests to a subdomain in an exempted zone will block unauthenticated traffic by default if there is a configured Access application and policy that matches the request.|
|» disable_end_user_app_creation|body|[access_disable_end_user_app_creation](#schemaaccess_disable_end_user_app_creation)|false|Whether creation of end user applications is disabled for this organization.|
|» is_ui_read_only|body|[access_is_ui_read_only](#schemaaccess_is_ui_read_only)|false|Lock all settings as Read-Only in the Dashboard, regardless of user permission. Updates may only be made via the API or Terraform for this account when enabled.|
|» login_design|body|[access_login_design](#schemaaccess_login_design)|false|none|
|» mfa_config|body|[access_org_mfa_config](#schemaaccess_org_mfa_config)|false|Configures multi-factor authentication (MFA) settings for an organization.|
|» mfa_piv_key_requirements|body|[access_mfa_piv_key_requirements](#schemaaccess_mfa_piv_key_requirements)|false|Configures PIV key requirements for MFA using hardware security keys.|
|» mfa_required_for_all_apps|body|[access_mfa_required_for_all_apps](#schemaaccess_mfa_required_for_all_apps)|false|Determines whether global MFA settings apply to applications by default. The organization must have MFA enabled with at least one authentication method and a session duration configured. Note: 'allowed_authenticators' cannot contain only the infrastructure SSH authenticators ('piv_key' and 'ssh_fido2_key') if the organization has any non-infrastructure applications.|
|» name|body|[access_name](#schemaaccess_name)|false|The name of your Zero Trust organization. When omitted on creation, defaults to the provided auth_domain; when both are omitted, defaults to the auto-generated subdomain slug (e.g. frosty-moon-7a3b).|
|» service_token_inactivity|body|[access_service_token_inactivity](#schemaaccess_service_token_inactivity)|false|Configures automatic enforcement for inactive service tokens. A service token is inactive if no policy references it, and it has not successfully authenticated with an Access application during the selected inactivity period. This setting applies to every service token in your Zero Trust account.|
|» session_duration|body|[access_session_duration](#schemaaccess_session_duration)|false|The amount of time that tokens issued for applications will be valid. Must be in the format `300ms` or `2h45m`. Valid time units are: ns, us (or µs), ms, s, m, h.|
|» strict_service_token_auth|body|[access_strict_service_token_auth](#schemaaccess_strict_service_token_auth)|false|Enables new behaviors for requests made with Access service tokens. Unauthorized requests emit audit logs, and return a 401 or 403 status code in the response instead of redirecting to the login page. Successful requests no longer receive a CF_Authorization cookie in the response. Zero Trust organizations created on or after October 5, 2026 will have this setting enabled by default, and cannot disable it.|
|» ui_read_only_toggle_reason|body|[access_ui_read_only_toggle_reason](#schemaaccess_ui_read_only_toggle_reason)|false|A description of the reason why the UI read only field is being toggled.|
|» user_seat_expiration_inactive_time|body|[access_user_seat_expiration_inactive_time](#schemaaccess_user_seat_expiration_inactive_time)|false|The amount of time a user seat is inactive before it expires. When the user seat exceeds the set time of inactivity, the user is removed as an active seat and no longer counts against your Teams seat count.  Minimum value for this setting is 1 month (730h). Must be in the format `300ms` or `2h45m`. Valid time units are: `ns`, `us` (or `µs`), `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`.|
|» warp_auth_non_browser_401|body|[access_warp_auth_non_browser_401](#schemaaccess_warp_auth_non_browser_401)|false|When enabled, unsuccessful WARP authentication requests with a non-HTML Accept header return a 401 response instead of redirecting to the login page.|
|» warp_auth_session_duration|body|[access_warp_auth_session_duration](#schemaaccess_warp_auth_session_duration)|false|The amount of time that tokens issued for applications will be valid. Must be in the format `30m` or `2h45m`. Valid time units are: m, h.|

## Revoke all Access tokens for a user

<a id="opIdzero-trust-organization-revoke-all-access-tokens-for-a-user"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/access/organizations/revoke_user \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

  }'
```

<h3 id="create-an-access-reusable-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|body|body|[access_policy_req](#schemaaccess_policy_req)|true|none|
|» decision|body|[access_decision](#schemaaccess_decision)|true|The action Access will take if a user matches this policy. Infrastructure application policies can only use the Allow action.|
|» exclude|body|[access_exclude-2](#schemaaccess_exclude-2)|false|Rules evaluated with a NOT logical operator. To match the policy, a user cannot meet any of the Exclude rules.|
|» include|body|[access_include-2](#schemaaccess_include-2)|true|Rules evaluated with an OR logical operator. A user needs to meet only one of the Include rules.|
|» name|body|[access_name-9](#schemaaccess_name-9)|true|The name of the Access policy.|
|» policy_resolution_account_id|body|[access_policy_resolution_account_id](#schemaaccess_policy_resolution_account_id)|false|The account ID used to resolve policy resources and identity for cross-account WARP authentication. The account must be trusted by the account that owns this policy.|
|» require|body|[access_require-2](#schemaaccess_require-2)|false|Rules evaluated with an AND logical operator. To match the policy, a user must meet all of the Require rules.|
|» approval_groups|body|[access_approval_groups](#schemaaccess_approval_groups)|false|Administrators who can approve a temporary authentication request.|
|» approval_required|body|[access_approval_required](#schemaaccess_approval_required)|false|Requires the user to request access from an administrator at the start of each session.|
|» connection_rules|body|[access_connection_rules](#schemaaccess_connection_rules)|false|The rules that define how users may connect to targets secured by your application.|
|» isolation_required|body|[access_isolation_required](#schemaaccess_isolation_required)|false|Require this application to be served in an isolated browser for users matching this policy. 'Client Web Isolation' must be on for the account in order to use this feature.|
|» mfa_config|body|[access_mfa_config](#schemaaccess_mfa_config)|false|Configures multi-factor authentication (MFA) settings.|
|» purpose_justification_prompt|body|[access_purpose_justification_prompt](#schemaaccess_purpose_justification_prompt)|false|A custom message that will appear on the purpose justification screen.|
|» purpose_justification_required|body|[access_purpose_justification_required](#schemaaccess_purpose_justification_required)|false|Require users to enter a justification when they log in to the application.|
|» session_duration|body|[access_session_duration-3](#schemaaccess_session_duration-3)|false|The amount of time that tokens issued for the application will be valid. Must be in the format `300ms` or `2h45m`. Valid time units are: ns, us (or µs), ms, s, m, h.|

|» decision|allow|
|» decision|deny|
|» decision|non_identity|
|» decision|bypass|

## Rotate SAML certificate

<a id="opIdaccess-saml-certificates-rotate-certificate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/access/saml_certificates/f174e90a-fafe-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415/rotate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/access/saml_certificates/{saml_cert_set_id}/rotate`

Rotates the SAML encryption certificates within the specified certificate set. This generates a new
certificate and moves the current certificate to the previous slot. If a previous certificate exists,
it will be deactivated and removed.

This endpoint ensures zero-downtime rotation by maintaining both current and previous certificates 
during the transition period, allowing IdPs time to update their configurations. Automated rotation
happens 30 days before a current certificate's expiration.


<h3 id="rotate-saml-certificate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[access_identifier](#schemaaccess_identifier)|true|none|
|saml_cert_set_id|path|[access_uuid](#schemaaccess_uuid)|true|UID of the SAML certificate set to rotate.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "created_at": "2024-03-21T10:30:00Z",
    "current_certificate": {
      "is_current": true,
      "not_after": "2027-03-21T12:00:00Z",
      "public_certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIGAjCCA+qgAwIBAgIJAI7kymlF7CWT...\n...certificate content...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----\n",
      "uid": "f174e90a-fafe-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415"
    },
    "previous_certificate": {},
    "uid": "a5bb4b3f-c2d1-4e6a-8f9b-1d3e4f5a6b7c",
    "updated_at": "2024-03-21T10:30:00Z"

}
```

## Create a service token

<a id="opIdaccess-service-tokens-create-a-service-token"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/access/service_tokens \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "client_secret_version": 1,
    "duration": "60m",
    "enabled": true,
    "name": "CI/CD token",
    "previous_client_secret_expires_at": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/access/service_tokens`

Generates a new service token. **Note:** This is the only time you can get the Client Secret. If you lose the Client Secret, you will have to rotate the Client Secret or create a new service token.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_secret_version": 1,
  "duration": "60m",
  "enabled": true,
  "name": "CI/CD token",
  "previous_client_secret_expires_at": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-service-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[access_identifier](#schemaaccess_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» client_secret_version|body|[access_client_secret_version](#schemaaccess_client_secret_version)|false|A version number identifying the current `client_secret` associated with the service token. Incrementing it triggers a rotation; the previous secret will still be accepted until the time indicated by `previous_client_secret_expires_at`. If the service token was reported as leaked, `previous_client_secret_expires_at` is not required, may not be in the future, and the previous secret is discarded immediately.|
|» duration|body|[access_duration](#schemaaccess_duration)|false|The duration for how long the service token will be valid. Must be in the format `300ms` or `2h45m`, or the special value `forever` for non-expiring tokens. Valid time units are: ns, us (or µs), ms, s, m, h. The default is 1 year in hours (8760h).|
|» enabled|body|[access_enabled](#schemaaccess_enabled)|false|Whether the service token is enabled. A disabled service token cannot be used to authenticate; both its current and previous `client_secret` stop being accepted, but the token itself is preserved and can be re-enabled. A service token reported as leaked is disabled automatically and cannot be re-enabled until its secret is rotated; attempting to do so returns a 409. Defaults to enabled when omitted on create.|
|» name|body|[access_name-2](#schemaaccess_name-2)|true|The name of the service token.|
|» previous_client_secret_expires_at|body|[access_previous_client_secret_expires_at](#schemaaccess_previous_client_secret_expires_at)|false|The expiration of the previous `client_secret`. This can be modified at any point after a rotation. For example, you may extend it further into the future if you need more time to update services with the new secret; or move it into the past to immediately invalidate the previous token in case of compromise. Rotating a service token that was reported as leaked discards the previous secret entirely, so no grace period can be set.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "client_id": "88bf3b6d86161464f6509f7219099e57.access.example.com",
    "client_secret": "bdd31cbc4dec990953e39163fbbb194c93313ca9f0a6e420346af9d326b1d2a5",
    "created_at": {},
    "duration": "60m",
    "enabled": true,
    "id": "string",
    "name": "CI/CD token",
    "updated_at": {}
  }
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-service-token-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Create a service token response|[access_create_response](#schemaaccess_create_response)|

## Create Address Map

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/258def64c72dae45f3e4c8516e2111f2/addressing/address_maps \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "My Ecommerce zones",
    "enabled": true,
    "ips": [
      "192.0.2.1"
    ],
    "memberships": [
      {
        "identifier": "023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353",
        "kind": "zone"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/addressing/address_maps`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "My Ecommerce zones",
  "enabled": true,
  "ips": [
```

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/258def64c72dae45f3e4c8516e2111f2/addressing/prefixes/2af39739cc4e3b5910c918468bb89828/bgp/prefixes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/addressing/prefixes/{prefix_id}/bgp/prefixes`

List all BGP Prefixes within the specified IP Prefix. BGP Prefixes are used to control which specific subnets are advertised to the Internet. It is possible to advertise subnets more specific than an IP Prefix by creating more specific BGP Prefixes.

<h3 id="list-bgp-prefixes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[addressing_account_identifier](#schemaaddressing_account_identifier)|true|none|
|prefix_id|path|[addressing_prefix_identifier](#schemaaddressing_prefix_identifier)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": [
    {
      "asn": 13335,
      "asn_prepend_count": 2,
      "auto_advertise_withdraw": true,
      "bgp_signal_opts": {
        "enabled": false,
        "modified_at": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z"
      },
      "cidr": "192.0.2.0/24",
      "created_at": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z",
      "id": "7009ba364c7a5760798ceb430e603b74",
      "modified_at": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z",
      "on_demand": {
        "advertised": true,
        "advertised_modified_at": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z",
        "on_demand_enabled": true,
        "on_demand_locked": false
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "success": false,
  "result": null
}
```
