## Create a repository token

<a id="opIdartifacts_tokens_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/artifacts/namespaces/string/tokens \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "repo": "string",
    "scope": "read",
    "ttl": 60
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/artifacts/namespaces/{namespace}/tokens`

Creates a scoped Git token for a repository.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "repo": "string",
  "scope": "read",
  "ttl": 60
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-repository-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|Artifacts namespace name.|
|account_id|path|string|true|Cloudflare account ID.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» repo|body|string|true|none|
|» scope|body|string|false|none|
|» ttl|body|integer|false|none|

## Revoke a token

<a id="opIdartifacts_tokens_revoke"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/artifacts/namespaces/string/tokens/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /accounts/{account_id}/artifacts/namespaces/{namespace}/tokens/{id}`

Revokes an Artifacts repository token. Token IDs are resolved through an eventually consistent index, so revoking a token within about a second of creating it can return 404; retry after a short delay.

<h3 id="revoke-a-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|Artifacts namespace name.|
|id|path|string|true|Token ID. Must match /^[0-9a-z]{16}$/.|
|account_id|path|string|true|Cloudflare account ID.|

```json
      "documentation_url": "http://example.com",
      "message": "string",
```

## Get resource change history from an account audit log entry (Version 2)

<a id="opIdaudit-logs-v2-get-account-audit-log-history"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/a67e14daa5f8dceeb91fe5449ba496ef/logs/audit/f174be97-19b1-40d6-954d-70cd5fbd52db/history?action_time=2024-10-30T15%3A00%3A00Z&since=2024-10-30&before=2024-10-31' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/logs/audit/{id}/history`

Returns the chronological change history for the resource identified by the given audit log entry.

The endpoint first locates the source audit log entry by `id` (using `action_time` to narrow the lookup window), derives identifying filters from that entry, and then returns matching audit logs within the `since`/`before` window.

The `result_info.history_status` field indicates the quality of the resource identification used:
- `exact`: Resource was identified by the resource URI.
- `approximate`: Resource was identified without the resource URI.
- `unavailable`: The source audit log entry did not contain enough information to identify the resource; an empty result is returned.


<h3 id="get-resource-change-history-from-an-account-audit-log-entry-version-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|none|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|action_time|query|string(date-time)|true|RFC3339 timestamp of the source audit log entry's action time. Used to narrow the source-entry lookup window. Provide the `action.time` value from the audit log identified by `id`.|
|since|query|string(date)|true|Limits the returned results to logs newer than the specified date. This can be a date string 2019-04-30 (interpreted in UTC) or an absolute timestamp that conforms to RFC3339.|
|before|query|string(date)|true|Limits the returned results to logs older than the specified date. This can be a date string 2019-04-30 (interpreted in UTC) or an absolute timestamp that conforms to RFC3339.|
|direction|query|string|false|none|
|limit|query|number|false|none|
|cursor|query|string|false|none|

|---|---|
|direction|desc|
|direction|asc|

## Get resource change history from an organization audit log entry (Version 2)

<a id="opIdaudit-logs-v2-get-organization-audit-log-history"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/organizations/a67e14daa5f8dceeb91fe5449ba496ef/logs/audit/f174be97-19b1-40d6-954d-70cd5fbd52db/history?action_time=2024-10-30T15%3A00%3A00Z&since=2024-10-30&before=2024-10-31' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id}/logs/audit/{id}/history`

Returns the chronological change history for the resource identified by the given organization-scoped audit log entry.

The endpoint first locates the source audit log entry by `id` (using `action_time` to narrow the lookup window), derives identifying filters from that entry, and then returns matching audit logs within the `since`/`before` window.

The `result_info.history_status` field indicates the quality of the resource identification used:
- `exact`: Resource was identified by the resource URI.
- `approximate`: Resource was identified without the resource URI.
- `unavailable`: The source audit log entry did not contain enough information to identify the resource; an empty result is returned.


<h3 id="get-resource-change-history-from-an-organization-audit-log-entry-version-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|none|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|action_time|query|string(date-time)|true|RFC3339 timestamp of the source audit log entry's action time. Used to narrow the source-entry lookup window. Provide the `action.time` value from the audit log identified by `id`.|
|since|query|string(date)|true|Limits the returned results to logs newer than the specified date. This can be a date string 2019-04-30 (interpreted in UTC) or an absolute timestamp that conforms to RFC3339.|
|before|query|string(date)|true|Limits the returned results to logs older than the specified date. This can be a date string 2019-04-30 (interpreted in UTC) or an absolute timestamp that conforms to RFC3339.|
|direction|query|string|false|none|
|limit|query|number|false|none|
|cursor|query|string|false|none|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|direction|desc|
|direction|asc|

## Delete Basin Catalog metadata

<a id="opIdbasin-delete-catalog"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef/basin-catalog/my-data-bucket/delete \
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/basin-catalog/{bucket_name}/delete`

Removes the catalog from the control plane without deleting R2 bucket objects.
Set force=true to remove catalog namespaces, tables, views, and maintenance
metadata. Force deletion is limited to a configured catalog object count.

|force|query|boolean|false|Remove child metadata before deleting the catalog.|

## List namespaces in catalog

<a id="opIdbasin-list-namespaces"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef/basin-catalog/my-data-bucket/namespaces \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/basin-catalog/{bucket_name}/namespaces`

Returns a list of namespaces in the specified Basin Catalog.
Supports hierarchical filtering and pagination for efficient traversal
of large namespace hierarchies.


<h3 id="list-namespaces-in-catalog-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[r2-data-catalog_account-id](#schemar2-data-catalog_account-id)|true|Identifies the account.|
|bucket_name|path|[r2-data-catalog_bucket-name](#schemar2-data-catalog_bucket-name)|true|Specifies the R2 bucket name.|
|page_token|query|string|false|Opaque pagination token from a previous response.<br>Use this to fetch the next page of results.<br>|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Maximum number of namespaces to return per page.<br>Defaults to 100, maximum 1000.<br>|
|parent|query|string|false|Parent namespace to filter by. Only returns direct children of this namespace.<br>For nested namespaces, use %1F as separator (e.g., "bronze%1Fanalytics").<br>Omit this parameter to list top-level namespaces.<br>|
|return_uuids|query|boolean|false|Whether to include namespace UUIDs in the response.<br>Set to true to receive the namespace_uuids array.<br>|
|return_details|query|boolean|false|Whether to include additional metadata (timestamps).<br>When true, response includes created_at and updated_at arrays.<br>|

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef/basin-catalog/my-data-bucket/namespaces/bronze/tables \
```


`GET /accounts/{account_id}/basin-catalog/{bucket_name}/namespaces/{namespace}/tables`

Returns a list of tables in the specified namespace within a Basin Catalog.
Supports pagination for efficient traversal of large table collections.


<h3 id="list-tables-in-namespace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[r2-data-catalog_account-id](#schemar2-data-catalog_account-id)|true|Identifies the account.|
|bucket_name|path|[r2-data-catalog_bucket-name](#schemar2-data-catalog_bucket-name)|true|Specifies the R2 bucket name.|

## Get table details

<a id="opIdbasin-get-table"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef/basin-catalog/my-data-bucket/namespaces/bronze/tables/events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/basin-catalog/{bucket_name}/namespaces/{namespace}/tables/{table_name}`

Returns full Apache Iceberg metadata for a single table: schema,
partition specs, sort orders, properties, and recent snapshot history.
Designed for catalog introspection UIs that need per-table details
without holding R2 credentials.

The `metadata.snapshots`, `metadata.snapshot-log`, and
`metadata.metadata-log` arrays are pruned to the most recent 10
entries by `timestamp-ms`. Use `total_snapshots` and
`returned_snapshots` to surface the truncation to end users.


<h3 id="get-table-details-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[r2-data-catalog_account-id](#schemar2-data-catalog_account-id)|true|Identifies the account.|
|bucket_name|path|[r2-data-catalog_bucket-name](#schemar2-data-catalog_bucket-name)|true|Specifies the R2 bucket name.|
|namespace|path|string|true|The namespace identifier.<br>For nested namespaces, use %1F as separator (e.g., "bronze%1Fanalytics").<br>|
|table_name|path|string|true|The table name within the given namespace.|

> Example responses

## List tables in namespace

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/r2-catalog/{bucket_name}/namespaces/{namespace}/tables`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Returns a list of tables in the specified namespace within an R2 catalog.
Supports pagination for efficient traversal of large table collections.


<h3 id="list-tables-in-namespace-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|page_token|query|string|false|Opaque pagination token from a previous response.<br>Use this to fetch the next page of results.<br>|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Maximum number of tables to return per page.<br>Defaults to 100, maximum 1000.<br>|
|return_uuids|query|boolean|false|Whether to include table UUIDs in the response.<br>Set to true to receive the table_uuids array.<br>|
|return_details|query|boolean|false|Whether to include additional metadata (timestamps, locations).<br>When true, response includes created_at, updated_at, metadata_locations, and locations arrays.<br>|

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/basin-catalog/{bucket_name}/namespaces/{namespace}/tables/{table_name}/maintenance-configs`

including compaction settings.

## Get Account Billable Usage (Version 1, Alpha)

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/billable-usage`

Returns billable usage data for the account.
When no query parameters are provided, returns usage for the current
billing period.


<h3 id="get-account-billable-usage-version-1-alpha-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|from|query|string(date)|false|Start date for the usage query (ISO 8601). The provided time range must include the subscription billing cycle anchor day, otherwise no usage data is returned. Use the info endpoint to retrieve the subscription anchor day.|
|to|query|string(date)|false|End date for the usage query (ISO 8601).|

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-billable-usage-v2">Billable Usage V2</h1>

## Get Account Usage (Version 2, Alpha, Restricted)

<a id="opIdbillable-usage-v2-get-account-usage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/billable/usage \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/billable/usage`

Returns cost and usage data for a single Cloudflare account, aligned
with the [FinOps FOCUS v1.3](https://focus.finops.org/focus-specification/v1-3/)
Cost and Usage dataset specification.

Each record represents one billable metric for one account on one day.
This includes all metered usage, including usage that falls within
free-tier allowances and may result in zero cost.

**Note:** This endpoint serves `usage` records only; cost and pricing
fields are absent from responses. To retrieve rated costs, use `POST`
on the same path with `Metric: cost`.

When `from` and `to` are omitted, defaults to the start of the current
month through today. The maximum date range is 31 days.


<h3 id="get-account-usage-version-2-alpha-restricted-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[billable-usage-api_identifier](#schemabillable-usage-api_identifier)|true|Identifies the Cloudflare account.|
|from|query|string(date)|false|Start date for the usage query (ISO 8601). Required if `to` is set. When omitted along with `to`, defaults to the start of the current month. Filters by charge period (when consumption happened), not billing period. The maximum date range is 31 days.|
|to|query|string(date)|false|End date for the usage query (ISO 8601). Required if `from` is set. When omitted along with `from`, defaults to today. Filters by charge period (when consumption happened), not billing period. The maximum date range is 31 days.|

## Query Account Usage (Version 2, Alpha, Restricted)

<a id="opIdbillable-usage-v2-query-account-usage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/billable/usage \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "FilterBy": {
      "BillableMetricIds": [
        "workers_standard_requests",
        "http_transferred_bytes"
      ],
      "ProductFamilyIds": [
        "3f1b9c1e-0000-4000-8000-000000000000"
      ],
      "Tags": [
        {
          "Key": "team",
          "Values": [
            "fintech"
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    "GroupBy": [
      {
        "Key": "region",
        "Type": "DIMENSION"
      }
    ],
    "Metric": "usage",
    "TimePeriod": {
      "From": "2025-05-01T00:00:00Z",
      "To": "2025-05-31T00:00:00Z"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/billable/usage`

Returns cost and usage data for a single Cloudflare account, aligned
with the [FinOps FOCUS v1.3](https://focus.finops.org/focus-specification/v1-3/)
Cost and Usage dataset specification.

This is the filterable counterpart to `GET` on the same path. It is a
read-only operation and requires only the `#billing:read` permission;
`POST` is used so that filter criteria can be supplied in a request body
rather than in the query string.

Each record represents one billable metric for one account on one day.
This includes all metered usage, including usage that falls within
free-tier allowances and may result in zero cost.

**Note:** Cost and pricing fields are populated only when `Metric`
is `cost`; otherwise they are absent from responses.

The request body is optional. When it is omitted, or when `TimePeriod`
is omitted, the range defaults to the start of the current month through
today. The maximum date range is 31 days.

Filters of different kinds are combined with AND. Values within one tag
filter are combined with OR. Filter values that do not match usage
produce an empty result set.

Results can be grouped by up to two groups, in any combination of
dimension keys and resource-tag keys. Tag groups are returned in the
`Tags` field. Usage without a requested tag remains in an untagged
group, with that key omitted from `Tags`.

Requests that use tag filtering or tag grouping return HTTP 400 when the
underlying usage data source does not support tags.

Requests that use dimension grouping return HTTP 400 when the
underlying usage data source does not support dimensions.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "FilterBy": {
    "BillableMetricIds": [
      "workers_standard_requests",
      "http_transferred_bytes"
    ],
    "ProductFamilyIds": [
      "3f1b9c1e-0000-4000-8000-000000000000"
    ],
    "Tags": [
      {
        "Key": "team",
        "Values": [
          "fintech"
        ]
      }
    ]
  },
  "GroupBy": [
    {
      "Key": "region",
      "Type": "DIMENSION"
    }
  ],
  "Metric": "usage",
  "TimePeriod": {
    "From": "2025-05-01T00:00:00Z",
    "To": "2025-05-31T00:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="query-account-usage-version-2-alpha-restricted-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[billable-usage-api_identifier](#schemabillable-usage-api_identifier)|true|Identifies the Cloudflare account.|
|body|body|[billable-usage-api_v2_usage_query](#schemabillable-usage-api_v2_usage_query)|false|none|
|» FilterBy|body|[billable-usage-api_v2_filter_by](#schemabillable-usage-api_v2_filter_by)|false|Usage filters. Filters of different kinds are combined with AND, so a record must match every filter present to be returned.|
|» GroupBy|body|[[billable-usage-api_v2_group_by](#schemabillable-usage-api_v2_group_by)]|false|Grouping definitions used to split result rows. At most two unique keys may be supplied.|
|» Metric|body|string|false|Type of cost/usage records to retrieve. `usage` returns unrated usage quantities. `cost` returns rated usage with cost and pricing fields; it is available only on `POST` account usage and only when the underlying usage data source is ClickHouse (other sources return an empty result set). Requests that combine `cost` with `GroupBy` or `FilterBy.Tags` return HTTP 400. Unrelated to `FilterBy.BillableMetricIds`. Defaults to `usage` when omitted.|
|» TimePeriod|body|[billable-usage-api_v2_time_period](#schemabillable-usage-api_v2_time_period)|false|Charge period to query, i.e. when consumption happened, not when it was billed. `From` is inclusive and `To` is exclusive. `From` and `To` must be supplied together; supplying one without the other is an error. When both are omitted the range defaults to the start of the current month through today.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» Metric|usage|
|» Metric|cost|

## List Account Billable Metrics (Version 2, Alpha, Restricted)

<a id="opIdbillable-usage-v2-get-account-billable-metrics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/billable/usage/billable-metrics \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/billable/usage/billable-metrics`

Lists billable metrics available to the account through contracts and
subscriptions that overlap the requested period. Results are
deduplicated and ordered. If no qualifying contract exists, the
result is an empty array.

When `from` and `to` are omitted, the period defaults to the start of
the current month through today. The maximum date range is 31 days.


<h3 id="list-account-billable-metrics-version-2-alpha-restricted-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[billable-usage-api_identifier](#schemabillable-usage-api_identifier)|true|Identifies the Cloudflare account.|
|from|query|string(date)|false|Start date for the usage query (ISO 8601). Required if `to` is set. When omitted along with `to`, defaults to the start of the current month. Filters by charge period (when consumption happened), not billing period. The maximum date range is 31 days.|
|to|query|string(date)|false|End date for the usage query (ISO 8601). Required if `from` is set. When omitted along with `from`, defaults to today. Filters by charge period (when consumption happened), not billing period. The maximum date range is 31 days.|

## Get Organization Usage (Version 2, Alpha, Restricted)

<a id="opIdbillable-usage-v2-get-organization-usage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/organizations/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/billable/usage \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id}/billable/usage`

Returns cost and usage data for all accounts within an organization,
aligned with the [FinOps FOCUS v1.3](https://focus.finops.org/focus-specification/v1-3/)
Cost and Usage dataset specification.

Each record represents one billable metric for one account on one day.
This includes all metered usage, including usage that falls within
free-tier allowances and may result in zero cost. The response
includes usage for every account belonging to the specified
organization.

**Note:** This endpoint serves `usage` records only; cost and pricing
fields are absent from responses. Rated costs are available per
account via `POST /accounts/{account_id}/billable/usage` with
`Metric: cost`.

When `from` and `to` are omitted, defaults to the start of the current
month through today. The maximum date range is 31 days.

An organization with no accounts, or an organization ID that does not
exist, returns a successful response with an empty result set rather
than an error.


<h3 id="get-organization-usage-version-2-alpha-restricted-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|[billable-usage-api_identifier](#schemabillable-usage-api_identifier)|true|Identifies the Cloudflare organization.|
|from|query|string(date)|false|Start date for the usage query (ISO 8601). Required if `to` is set. When omitted along with `to`, defaults to the start of the current month. Filters by charge period (when consumption happened), not billing period. The maximum date range is 31 days.|
|to|query|string(date)|false|End date for the usage query (ISO 8601). Required if `from` is set. When omitted along with `from`, defaults to today. Filters by charge period (when consumption happened), not billing period. The maximum date range is 31 days.|

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-usage-analytics">Usage Analytics</h1>

## Get account billing usage

<a id="opIdusage-analytics-get-account-billing-usage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/billing/usage \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/billing/usage`

Retrieve billing usage analytics for an account. Returns time-series data for all billable product metrics including Stream, Media (Images), Rate Limiting, Load Balancing, Argo, Workers, Workers KV, Image Resizing, and Spectrum.


<h3 id="get-account-billing-usage-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[usage-analytics_identifier](#schemausage-analytics_identifier)|true|Standard Cloudflare hex account identifier. The API gateway translates this to an internal numeric ID before forwarding to the backend service.<br>|
|metrics|query|string|false|Comma-separated list of metrics to include in the response. Available metrics depend on the endpoint. Billing usage supports: streamMinutesViewed, rateLimitingRequestsAllowed, loadBalancingQueries, argoAcceleratedBytes, workersRequests, workersKVReads, imageResizingRequests, spectrumBytesTransferred, mediaUniqueTransformations. Stream/media usage supports: streamMinutesViewed.<br>|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|Start of the time range for the query (inclusive). ISO 8601 timestamp. Defaults to 6 hours before the current time.<br>|
|until|query|string(date-time)|false|End of the time range for the query (inclusive). ISO 8601 timestamp. Defaults to the current time.<br>|
|time_delta|query|string|false|Time unit to aggregate usage observations into. Data retention is approximately 18 months. The effective number of data points returned depends on the time range and granularity selected. For example, requesting hourly granularity over 18 months could produce up to ~13,000 data points; use the limit parameter to cap results and be aware that responses may be truncated.<br>|
|limit|query|integer|false|Maximum number of data points to return. The actual number of results depends on the interaction between the time range (since/until) and time_delta granularity. Results are truncated to this limit without error if the time range produces more data points than the limit allows.<br>|
|filters|query|string|false|Filter expressions to apply to the query. Format: field==value. Multiple filters can be combined.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|time_delta|hour|
|time_delta|day|
|time_delta|week|
|time_delta|month|
|time_delta|quarter|
|time_delta|year|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "result": [
    {
      "argoAcceleratedBytes": 5000000,
      "imageResizingRequests": 15000,
      "loadBalancingQueries": 10000,
      "mediaUniqueTransformations": 45000,
      "rateLimitingRequestsAllowed": 50000,
      "spectrumBytesTransferred": 8000000,
      "streamMinutesViewed": 125000,
      "ts": 1693526400,
      "workersKVReads": 30000,
      "workersRequests": 200000
    }
  ],
  "success": true
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 10010,
      "message": "Bad Request"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": [],
  "success": false
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 10000,
      "message": "Authentication required"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": [],
  "success": false
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 10001,
      "message": "Forbidden"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": [],
  "success": false
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Usage analytics response.|[usage-analytics_billing_usage_response](#schemausage-analytics_billing_usage_response)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid parameters or query.|[usage-analytics_error_response](#schemausage-analytics_error_response)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication required.|[usage-analytics_error_response](#schemausage-analytics_error_response)|
|403|Forbidden|Insufficient permissions to access this resource.|[usage-analytics_error_response](#schemausage-analytics_error_response)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
api_token, api_email & api_key
</aside>

|since|query|string(date-time)|false|Start of the time range for the query (inclusive). ISO 8601 timestamp. Defaults to 6 hours before the current time.<br>|
|until|query|string(date-time)|false|End of the time range for the query (inclusive). ISO 8601 timestamp. Defaults to the current time.<br>|
|time_delta|query|string|false|Time unit to aggregate usage observations into. Data retention is approximately 18 months. The effective number of data points returned depends on the time range and granularity selected. For example, requesting hourly granularity over 18 months could produce up to ~13,000 data points; use the limit parameter to cap results and be aware that responses may be truncated.<br>|
|limit|query|integer|false|Maximum number of data points to return. The actual number of results depends on the interaction between the time range (since/until) and time_delta granularity. Results are truncated to this limit without error if the time range produces more data points than the limit allows.<br>|
|filters|query|string|false|Filter expressions to apply to the query. Format: field==value. Multiple filters can be combined.<br>|

|time_delta|hour|
|time_delta|day|
|time_delta|week|
|time_delta|month|
|time_delta|quarter|
|time_delta|year|

Results are truncated to this limit without error if the time range produces more data points than the limit allows.<br>|

## Update saved string queries by ID

<a id="opIdpatchAccountsAccountIdBrandProtectionQueries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/brand-protection/queries \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "id": 0,
    "scan": true,
    "string_matches": [
      {
        "max_edit_distance": 0,
        "pattern": "string"
      }
    ],
    "tag": "string"
  }'
```

`PATCH /accounts/{account_id}/brand-protection/queries`

Update a saved query's tag, scan setting, or string_matches (pattern). When string_matches is provided, the query parameters and hash are updated. At least one of tag, scan, or string_matches is required.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": 0,
  "scan": true,
  "string_matches": [
    {
      "max_edit_distance": 0,
      "pattern": "string"
    }
  ],
  "tag": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="update-saved-string-queries-by-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» id|body|integer|false|The query ID to update (required when updating tag or scan).|
|» scan|body|boolean|false|Whether to scan matches.|
|» string_matches|body|[object]|false|Updated pattern match constraints. When provided, replaces the existing string_matches.|
|» » max_edit_distance|body|number|false|Maximum Levenshtein edit distance for fuzzy matching.|
|» » pattern|body|string|true|The pattern to match against.|
|» tag|body|string|false|Query tag. Required as identifier when updating string_matches.|

## Dismiss a match for a saved string query

<a id="opIdpostAccountsAccountIdBrandProtectionQueriesQueryIdMatchesDomainIdDismiss"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/brand-protection/queries/0/matches/0/dismiss \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

## Query browser extension event timeseries

<a id="opIdaccounts-browser-extension-config-extension-events-timeseries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/browser-extension/config/logs/extension-events/timeseries \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "filters": [
      {
        "field": "timestamp",
        "op": "eq",
        "value": "string"
      }
    ],
    "from": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "groupBy": [
      "eventName"
    ],
    "resolution": "1 hours",
    "stats": [
      "eventsTotal"
    ],
    "to": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/browser-extension/config/logs/extension-events/timeseries`

Returns browser extension event counts grouped by time bucket and the requested
`groupBy` fields. Accepts the same filters as event log search. When `resolution` is
omitted, ranges shorter than 10 days use `1 hours` buckets and ranges of 10 days or
more use `1 days`. Empty buckets are omitted. Results over 10000 slots return 400.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "field": "timestamp",
      "op": "eq",
      "value": "string"
    }
  ],
  "from": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "groupBy": [
    "eventName"
  ],
  "resolution": "1 hours",
  "stats": [
    "eventsTotal"
  ],
  "to": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="query-browser-extension-event-timeseries-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|Cloudflare account ID.|
|body|body|[brex_ExtensionEventsTimeseriesRequest](#schemabrex_extensioneventstimeseriesrequest)|true|none|
|» filters|body|[[brex_ExtensionEventFilter](#schemabrex_extensioneventfilter)]|false|none|
|» from|body|string(date-time)|true|Start of the query range (inclusive).|
|» groupBy|body|[string]|false|Fields to group each bucket by. Each requested field is returned on every slot.<br>An empty array returns one total per bucket.<br>|
|» resolution|body|string|false|Bucket size, for example `15 minutes`, `1 hours`, or `1 days`. Defaults to<br>`1 hours` for ranges shorter than 10 days and `1 days` otherwise. A request must not<br>produce more than 1440 buckets.<br>|
|» stats|body|[string]|false|none|
|» to|body|string(date-time)|true|End of the query range (exclusive). The range must not exceed 30 days.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» groupBy|eventName|
|» groupBy|action|
|» stats|eventsTotal|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [
    {
      "code": 0,
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "result": {
    "resolution": "1 hours",
    "slots": [
      {
        "action": "string",
        "eventName": "string",
        "eventsTotal": 0,
        "timestamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
      }
    ]
  },
  "success": true
}
```

```json
}
```

## List browser extension inventories

<a id="opIdaccounts-browser-extension-inventories-list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/browser-extension/config/inventories \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/browser-extension/config/inventories`

Returns the installed extension inventory for each registered browser
extension device in the account. Each device reports its inventory
periodically; this endpoint returns the latest known snapshot per device.

Results are paginated by cursor. Pass the `cursor` from a previous
response to fetch the next page. `per_page` controls page size
(default 50, max 200).


<h3 id="list-browser-extension-inventories-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cursor|query|string|false|Opaque cursor from a previous response to fetch the next page.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of results per page (default 50, max 200).|
|account_id|path|string|true|Cloudflare account ID.|

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-brapi">brapi</h1>

## Get accessibility tree page

<a id="opIdbrapi-post_AccessibilityTree"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/browser-rendering/accessibilityTree \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://www.example.com/"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/browser-rendering/accessibilityTree`

Returns the page's accessibility tree. Use `interestingOnly` to only return semantically meaningful nodes; use `root` to scope the tree to a CSS-selector-anchored subtree. Control page loading with `gotoOptions` and `waitFor*` options.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "url": "https://www.example.com/"
}
```

<h3 id="get-accessibility-tree-page-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

<h3 id="get-accessibility-tree-page-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns the requested formats information.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|The request contains errors or didn't properly encode content.|Inline|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Request failed due to site-related issues such as timeouts, SSL errors, or inaccessible content.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Request failed due to rate limiting. The Retry-After header indicates when the client should retry the request.|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error.|Inline|

## Get HTML content.

<a id="opIdbrapi-post_Content"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/browser-rendering/content \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://www.example.com/"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/browser-rendering/content`

Fetches rendered HTML content from provided URL or HTML. Check available options like `gotoOptions` and `waitFor*` to control page load behaviour.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "url": "https://www.example.com/"
}
```

<h3 id="get-html-content-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns the page's content.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|The request contains errors or didn't properly encode content.|Inline|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Request failed due to site-related issues such as timeouts, SSL errors, or inaccessible content.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Request failed due to rate limiting. The Retry-After header indicates when the client should retry the request.|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error.|Inline|

## Crawl websites.

<a id="opIdbrapi-post_Crawl"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/browser-rendering/crawl \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://www.example.com/"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/browser-rendering/crawl`

Starts a crawl job for the provided URL and its children. Check available options like `gotoOptions` and `waitFor*` to control page load behaviour.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "url": "https://www.example.com/"
}
```

## Get a browser session ID.

<a id="opIdbrapi-post_DevtoolsAcquire"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/browser-rendering/devtools/browser \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "guardrails": {
      "allowedDomainSets": [
        "string"
      ],
      "allowedDomains": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/browser-rendering/devtools/browser`

Acquires a browser and returns its session ID and websocket URL. Optionally accepts a JSON body with session guardrails to restrict outbound HTTP/S traffic.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "guardrails": {
    "allowedDomainSets": [
      "string"
    ],
    "allowedDomains": [
      "string"
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-a-browser-session-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|Account ID.|
|keep_alive|query|number|false|Keep-alive time in milliseconds.|
|lab|query|boolean|false|Use experimental browser.|
|targets|query|boolean|false|Include browser targets in response.|
|liveViewUrlExpiresInMs|query|number|false|How long the live view URL remains valid, in milliseconds (max 60 minutes). Only used when targets is true.|
|recording|query|boolean|false|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» guardrails|body|object|false|none|
|» » allowedDomainSets|body|[string]|false|Max 4 entries: curated preset names (common-cdns) and/or https URLs of newline-separated hostname lists.|
|» » allowedDomains|body|[string]|false|Hostname patterns, max 50. Supports exact hosts (example.com) or a single * wildcard anywhere. Prefer *.example.com (subdomain wildcard) over *example.com (prefix wildcard) to avoid matching overbroad lookalikes like evilexample.com.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "sessionId": "string",
  "webSocketDebuggerUrl": "string"
}
```

> 429 Response

```json

  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 0,
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "status": true
}
```

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns a session ID ready to be connected to.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Request failed due to rate limiting. The Retry-After header indicates when the client should retry the request.|Inline|

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

Status Code **429**

## Mint live view URLs for a browser session

<a id="opIdbrapi-post_DevtoolsLiveView"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/browser-rendering/devtools/browser/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/live_view \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "expiresInMs": 300000,
    "guardrails": {
      "mode": "readonly"
    },
    "mode": "devtools",
    "targetId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/browser-rendering/devtools/browser/{session_id}/live_view`

Generates time-limited URLs to view a remote browser session. Set `guardrails: { mode: 'readonly' }` to create a view-only link.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "expiresInMs": 300000,
  "guardrails": {
    "mode": "readonly"
  },
  "mode": "devtools",
  "targetId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="mint-live-view-urls-for-a-browser-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|Account ID.|
|session_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Browser session ID|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» expiresInMs|body|number|false|How long the live view URLs remain valid, in milliseconds. Default: 5 minutes. Max: 60 minutes.|
|» guardrails|body|object|false|Connection guardrails. Use `{ mode: 'readonly' }` to generate a view-only link.|
|» » mode|body|string|true|none|
|» mode|body|string|false|UI mode: 'devtools' (Chrome DevTools), 'tab' (single tab view), 'full' (multi-tab browser)|
|» targetId|body|string|false|Target ID (page) to connect to. If omitted, auto-resolves to the first active page.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » mode|readonly|
|» mode|devtools|
|» mode|tab|
|» mode|full|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "devtoolsFrontendUrl": "http://example.com",
  "id": "string",
  "options": {
    "guardrails": {
      "mode": "readonly"
    },
    "mode": "devtools"
  },
  "webSocketDebuggerUrl": "http://example.com"
}
```

```json
    }
  ],

}
```

```json
    {
      "code": 0,

    }
  ],
  "success": true
}
```

## Get markdown.

<a id="opIdbrapi-post_Markdown"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/browser-rendering/markdown \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://www.example.com/"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/browser-rendering/markdown`

Gets markdown of a webpage from provided URL or HTML. Control page loading with `gotoOptions` and `waitFor*` options.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "url": "https://www.example.com/"
}
```

## Get PDF.

<a id="opIdbrapi-post_Pdf"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/browser-rendering/pdf \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://www.example.com/"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/browser-rendering/pdf`

Fetches rendered PDF from provided URL or HTML. Check available options like `gotoOptions` and `waitFor*` to control page load behaviour.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "url": "https://www.example.com/"
}
```

```bash
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "elements": [
      {
        "selector": "h1"
      }
    ],
    "url": "https://www.example.com/"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/browser-rendering/scrape`

Get meta attributes like height, width, text and others of selected elements.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "elements": [
    {
      "selector": "h1"
    }
  ],
  "url": "https://www.example.com/"
}
```

## Get screenshot.

<a id="opIdbrapi-post_Screenshot"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/browser-rendering/screenshot \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://www.example.com/"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/browser-rendering/screenshot`

Takes a screenshot of a webpage from provided URL or HTML. Control page loading with `gotoOptions` and `waitFor*` options. Customize screenshots with `viewport`, `fullPage`, `clip` and others.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "url": "https://www.example.com/"
}
```

## Get HTML content and screenshot.

<a id="opIdbrapi-post_Snapshot"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/browser-rendering/snapshot \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "formats": [
      "content",
      "screenshot"
    ],
    "url": "https://www.example.com/"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/browser-rendering/snapshot`

Returns the page's HTML content and screenshot. Control page loading with `gotoOptions` and `waitFor*` options. Customize screenshots with `viewport`, `fullPage`, `clip` and others.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "formats": [
    "content",
    "screenshot"
  ],
  "url": "https://www.example.com/"
}
```

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-builds">Builds</h1>

## Get builds by Worker version

<a id="opIdgetBuildsByVersionIds"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/account-123/builds/builds?version_ids=123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000%2C223e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174001' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/builds/builds`

Retrieve builds associated with one or more Worker version IDs.

<h3 id="get-builds-by-worker-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

## Create a build trigger

<a id="opIdcreateTrigger"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/account-123/builds/triggers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "branch_excludes": [],
    "branch_includes": [
      "main"
    ],
    "build_caching_enabled": false,
    "build_command": "npm run build",
    "build_token_uuid": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "deploy_command": "npx wrangler deploy",
    "external_script_id": "dd7160bb9cef458093557736f4b9e75b",
    "path_excludes": [
      "*.md"
    ],
    "path_includes": [
      "*"
    ],
    "repo_connection_uuid": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "root_directory": "/",
    "trigger_name": "Production Deploy"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/builds/triggers`

Create a trigger defining the repository connection, Worker tag, commands, filters, cache setting, and build token.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "branch_excludes": [],
  "branch_includes": [
    "main"
  ],
  "build_caching_enabled": false,
  "build_command": "npm run build",
  "build_token_uuid": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "deploy_command": "npx wrangler deploy",
  "external_script_id": "dd7160bb9cef458093557736f4b9e75b",
  "path_excludes": [
    "*.md"
  ],
  "path_includes": [
    "*"
  ],
  "repo_connection_uuid": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "root_directory": "/",
  "trigger_name": "Production Deploy"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-build-trigger-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[builds_account_id](#schemabuilds_account_id)|true|none|
|body|body|[builds_CreateTriggerRequest](#schemabuilds_createtriggerrequest)|true|none|
|» branch_excludes|body|[builds_branch_excludes](#schemabuilds_branch_excludes)|true|Branch patterns that must not start builds.|
|» branch_includes|body|[builds_branch_includes](#schemabuilds_branch_includes)|true|Branch patterns that can start builds.|

## Start a Workers build

<a id="opIdcreateManualBuild"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/account-123/builds/triggers/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/builds \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "branch": {},
    "commit_hash": {},
    "seed_repo": {
      "branch": {},
      "files": [
        {
          "content": "name = \"my-worker\"\nmain = \"src/index.js\"\n",
          "filename": "wrangler.toml",
          "isBase64": false,
          "replace": "string"
        }
      ],
      "owner": "cloudflare",
      "path": "/",
      "provider": "github",
      "repository": "workers-sdk"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/builds/triggers/{trigger_uuid}/builds`

Start a build for a branch or commit using the selected trigger.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "branch": {},
  "commit_hash": {},
  "seed_repo": {
    "branch": {},
    "files": [
      {
        "content": "name = \"my-worker\"\nmain = \"src/index.js\"\n",
        "filename": "wrangler.toml",
        "isBase64": false,
        "replace": "string"
      }
    ],
    "owner": "cloudflare",
    "path": "/",
    "provider": "github",
    "repository": "workers-sdk"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="start-a-workers-build-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[builds_account_id](#schemabuilds_account_id)|true|none|
|trigger_uuid|path|[builds_trigger_uuid](#schemabuilds_trigger_uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[builds_CreateBuildRequest](#schemabuilds_createbuildrequest)|true|none|
|» branch|body|object|false|Git branch name (required if commit_hash not provided)|
|» commit_hash|body|object|false|Git commit hash (required if branch not provided)|
|» seed_repo|body|object|false|Optional repository and file overrides used to seed this build.|
|» » branch|body|object|false|Repository branch to seed.|
|» » files|body|[[builds_BuildSeedRepoInputFile](#schemabuilds_buildseedrepoinputfile)]|false|Files to add or replace for this build. Maximum 2.|
|» » owner|body|string|true|Repository owner or namespace.|
|» » path|body|string|false|Path within the repository to seed.|
|» » provider|body|string|true|Source control provider for the seed repository.|
|» » repository|body|string|true|Repository name.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|

|Parameter|Value|

## Set build variables

> Code samples


`PATCH /accounts/{account_id}/builds/triggers/{trigger_uuid}/environment_variables`

Add or replace build-time variables and secrets without changing unspecified keys.

```json
{
  "API_KEY": {
    "is_secret": true,
    "value": "secret-key"
  },
  "NODE_ENV": {
    "is_secret": false,
    "value": "production"
  }
```

## Update Worker build configuration

<a id="opIdupdateWorkerBuild"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/account-123/builds/workers/dd7160bb9cef458093557736f4b9e75b \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "production_settings": {
      "build_command": "npm run build:production",
      "deploy_command": "npx wrangler deploy --env production"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /accounts/{account_id}/builds/workers/{script_tag}`

Update the build configuration for a Worker script. Supports partial updates to git repository settings, production build settings, and Preview settings.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "production_settings": {
    "build_command": "npm run build:production",
    "deploy_command": "npx wrangler deploy --env production"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-worker-build-configuration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[builds_account_id](#schemabuilds_account_id)|true|none|
|script_tag|path|[builds_external_script_id](#schemabuilds_external_script_id)|true|The Worker script tag (external script ID)|
|patch_existing_previews|query|string|false|Apply a previews_base_config patch to every existing Preview of the Worker as well as to the base config.|
|body|body|[builds_UpdateWorkerRequest](#schemabuilds_updateworkerrequest)|true|none|
|» git_repository|body|object|false|Git repository settings to update|
|» » branch|body|string|false|New git branch to watch for builds|
|» previews_base_config|body|[builds_UpdateWorkerBuildSettingsInput](#schemabuilds_updateworkerbuildsettingsinput)|false|Partial build settings for updating a Worker build configuration|
|» previews_enabled|body|boolean|false|Enable or disable Previews for this Worker. Enabling requires previews_base_config to already exist or to be sent in the same request.|
|» production_settings|body|[builds_UpdateWorkerBuildSettingsInput](#schemabuilds_updateworkerbuildsettingsinput)|false|Partial build settings for updating a Worker build configuration|

`PUT /accounts/{account_id}/workers/workers/{worker_id}`

Perform a complete replacement of a Worker, where omitted properties are set to their default values. This is the exact same as the Create Worker endpoint, but operates on an existing Worker. To perform a partial update instead, use the Edit Worker endpoint.

<h3 id="update-worker-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|body|body|object|true|Worker update parameters.|
|» logpush|body|boolean|true|Whether logpush is enabled for the Worker.|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the Worker.|
|» observability|body|object|true|Observability settings for the Worker.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether observability is enabled for the Worker.|
|» » head_sampling_rate|body|number|false|The sampling rate for observability. From 0 to 1 (1 = 100%, 0.1 = 10%).|
|» » issues|body|object \| null|false|Real-time Issues settings for the Worker.|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether real-time Issues are enabled for the Worker.|
|» » logs|body|object|false|Log settings for the Worker.|
|» » » destinations|body|[string]|false|A list of destinations where logs will be exported to.|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether logs are enabled for the Worker.|
|» » » head_sampling_rate|body|number|false|The sampling rate for logs. From 0 to 1 (1 = 100%, 0.1 = 10%).|
|» » » invocation_logs|body|boolean|false|Whether [invocation logs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/logs/workers-logs/#invocation-logs) are enabled for the Worker.|
|» » » persist|body|boolean|false|Whether log persistence is enabled for the Worker.|
|» » redact_query_string|body|boolean|false|Whether query strings are removed from request URLs in logs and traces.|
|» » traces|body|object|false|Trace settings for the Worker.|
|» » » destinations|body|[string]|false|A list of destinations where traces will be exported to.|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether traces are enabled for the Worker.|
|» » » head_sampling_rate|body|number|false|The sampling rate for traces. From 0 to 1 (1 = 100%, 0.1 = 10%).|
|» » » persist|body|boolean|false|Whether trace persistence is enabled for the Worker.|
|» » » propagation_policy|body|string \| null|false|Controls how inbound trace context (traceparent/tracestate) headers on incoming requests are handled. "authenticated" honors inbound trace context only when accompanied by a valid trace auth token. "accept" unconditionally accepts inbound trace context. Requires the trace propagation feature to be enabled. Returns null when the trace propagation feature is not enabled for the account.|
|» previews_base_config|body|object|false|Template configuration used when creating new Previews for this Worker.|
|» » cache_options|body|object|false|Cache options used when creating new Previews.|
|» » » cross_version_cache|body|boolean|false|Whether cached responses are shared across Worker version<br>uploads. This is independent of `enabled`. It can stay true<br>while caching is off, so the preference survives turning<br>caching off and back on.<br>|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean|true|Whether caching is enabled for this Worker.|
|» » env|body|object|false|Bindings used when creating new Previews, keyed by binding name.|

## Delete Worker

<a id="opIddeleteWorker"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/workers/workers/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /accounts/{account_id}/workers/workers/{worker_id}`

Delete a Worker and all its associated resources (versions, deployments, etc.).

<h3 id="delete-worker-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[workers_identifier](#schemaworkers_identifier)|true|none|
|worker_id|path|string|true|none|
|force|query|boolean|false|If true, delete the Worker even when other Workers still reference it. Service bindings in those Workers may be left broken. Durable Object namespaces implemented by the deleted Worker are deleted even if other Workers reference them.|

## Create Subscriptions

<a id="opIdaccount-subscriptions-bulk-create-subscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/bulk/subscriptions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "coupon_code": "string",
    "payment_hold_id": 0,
    "subscriptions": [
      {
        "app": {
          "install_id": "string"
        },
        "component_values": [
          {
            "default": 5,
            "display_name": "Page Rules",
            "kind": "sum",
            "name": "page_rules",
            "price": 5,
            "value": 20
          }
        ],
        "frequency": "monthly",
        "rate_plan": {
          "currency": "USD",
          "externally_managed": false,
```

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/699d98642c564d2e855e9661899b7252/cfd_tunnel/f70ff985-a4ef-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415/token \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/cfd_tunnel/{tunnel_id}/token`

Retrieves the token used to run cloudflared and associate it with a specific Cloudflare Tunnel. Treat the token as a secret.

<h3 id="get-a-cloudflare-tunnel-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[tunnel_account_id](#schematunnel_account_id)|true|none|
|tunnel_id|path|[tunnel_tunnel_id](#schematunnel_tunnel_id)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "result": "eyJhIjoiNWFiNGU5Z...",
  "success": true
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

<h3 id="get-a-cloudflare-tunnel-token-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Get a Cloudflare Tunnel token response|[tunnel_tunnel_response_token](#schematunnel_tunnel_response_token)|
|4XX|Client Error|Get a Cloudflare Tunnel token response failure|Inline|

<h3 id="get-a-cloudflare-tunnel-token-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **4XX**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[tunnel_messages](#schematunnel_messages)|true|none|none|
|messages|[tunnel_messages](#schematunnel_messages)|true|none|none|
|result|object \| [object] \| string|true|none|none|
|» *anyOf*|object|false|none|none|
|» *anyOf*|[object]|false|none|none|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» *anyOf*|string|false|none|none|
|success|boolean|true|none|Whether the API call was successful|
|result|[tunnel_tunnel_token](#schematunnel_tunnel_token)|true|read-only|The Tunnel Token is used as a mechanism to authenticate the operation of a tunnel.|
|errors|object|true|none|none|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» code|integer|true|none|none|
|» context|object|false|none|Optional error-specific context.|
|» message|string|true|none|none|
|messages|object|true|none|none|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» code|integer|true|none|none|
|» context|object|false|none|Optional error-specific context.|
|» message|string|true|none|none|
|result|object \| null|true|none|none|

## Create a Mesh node

<a id="opIdcloudflare-tunnel-create-a-warp-connector-tunnel"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/699d98642c564d2e855e9661899b7252/warp_connector \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "ha": false,
    "name": "blog"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/warp_connector`

Creates a new Mesh node in an account.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ha": false,
  "name": "blog"
}
```

|body|body|object|true|none|

|» name|body|[tunnel_tunnel_name](#schematunnel_tunnel_name)|true|A user-friendly name for a tunnel.|

|» ha_mode|body|[tunnel_mesh_ha_mode](#schematunnel_mesh_ha_mode)|true|High-availability mode for the Mesh node. `none` means HA is enabled but no provider is configured yet (newly created nodes default to this). `disabled` means HA is explicitly turned off. `aws` uses AWS ENI move for failover. `local` uses virtual IPs (VIPs) on the local interface.|

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/challenges/widgets/{sitekey}/rotate_secret`

Generates a new secret key for this widget. If `invalidate_immediately`
is set to `false`, the previous secret remains valid for 2 hours.

Note that secrets cannot be rotated again during the grace period.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "invalidate_immediately": false
}
```

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /accounts/{account_id}/vuln_scanner/scans/{scan_id}`

Deletes a scan and all associated data. Only scans in a terminal state (`finished`, `failed`) may be deleted. Attempting to delete a scan that is still being created or executed (`created`, `scheduled`, `planning`, `running`) returns `400`.

<h3 id="delete-scan-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[vuln_scanner_identifier](#schemavuln_scanner_identifier)|true|Account identifier.|
|scan_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Scan identifier.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  },
  "result_info": {}
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

<h3 id="delete-scan-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response.|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|Client error.|[vuln_scanner_api-response-common-failure](#schemavuln_scanner_api-response-common-failure)|

<h3 id="delete-scan-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[vuln_scanner_messages](#schemavuln_scanner_messages)|true|none|none|
|messages|[vuln_scanner_messages](#schemavuln_scanner_messages)|true|none|none|
|success|boolean|true|none|Whether the API call was successful.|
|result|[vuln_scanner_delete-scan-response](#schemavuln_scanner_delete-scan-response)|false|none|Successful scan deletion result.|
|result_info|object \| null|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|success|true|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-bindb">BinDB</h1>

## Posts a file to Binary Storage

<a id="opIdpost_BinDBPost"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/cloudforce-one/binary \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/cloudforce-one/binary`

Uploads a binary file to Cloudforce One's binary database for malware analysis and threat intelligence correlation.

> Body parameter

```yaml
file: string
```

<h3 id="posts-a-file-to-binary-storage-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|Account ID.|
|body|body|object|true|Binary file to be uploaded to the database.|
|» file|body|string(binary)|true|The binary file content to upload.|

```json
  "content_type": "text/plain",
  "md5": "5d84ade76d2a8387c81175bb0cbe6492",

}
```

```json

  "errors": [

      "message": "An error occurred."

  "success": true
}
```

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-event">Event</h1>

## List events

<a id="opIdget_EventListGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/cloudforce-one/events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/cloudforce-one/events`

Lists events, with filters passed as query parameters. `datasetId` accepts dataset UUIDs or one scope value used alone: `all` (or `*`) and `operational` select the intelligence datasets you can read, and `analytics` selects the analytics datasets you can read. A scope value covers at most 50 datasets. Without `datasetId`, the default Cloudforce One Threat Events dataset is used. To send filters in a JSON body instead, use `threat-intel events search`.

|account_id|path|string|true|Account ID.|
|cursor|query|string|false|none|
|search|query|[object]|false|none|
|searchBranches|query|[[object]]|false|none|
|page|query|number|false|none|
|pageSize|query|number|false|none|
|orderBy|query|string|false|none|
|order|query|string|false|none|
|datasetId|query|[string]|false|none|
|forceRefresh|query|boolean|false|none|
|format|query|string|false|none|
|cache|query|string|false|none|

|order|desc|

|format|taxii|
|cache|from-graph|

## Search events

<a id="opIdpost_EventList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/cloudforce-one/events \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "cursor": "eyJ2ZXJzaW9uIjoxLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6eyJkYXRlIjoiMjAyNC0wMS0xMlQxMDowMDowMFoiLCJ1dWlkIjoiYWJjMTIzIn19",
    "datasetId": [
      "7632a037-fdef-4899-9b12-148470aae772"
    ],
    "order": "asc",
    "orderBy": "created",
    "page": 1,
    "pageSize": 100,
    "search": [],
    "searchBranches": [
      [
        {
          "field": "attacker",
          "op": "equals",
          "value": "string"
        }
      ]
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/cloudforce-one/events`

Lists events, with filters sent in a JSON request body. Accepts the same filters as `threat-intel events list` and suits long or complex `search` filters. `datasetId` accepts dataset UUIDs or one scope value used alone: `all` (or `*`) and `operational` select the intelligence datasets you can read, and `analytics` selects the analytics datasets you can read. A scope value covers at most 50 datasets. Without `datasetId`, the default Cloudforce One Threat Events dataset is used.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "cursor": "eyJ2ZXJzaW9uIjoxLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6eyJkYXRlIjoiMjAyNC0wMS0xMlQxMDowMDowMFoiLCJ1dWlkIjoiYWJjMTIzIn19",
  "datasetId": [
    "7632a037-fdef-4899-9b12-148470aae772"
  ],
  "order": "asc",
  "orderBy": "created",
  "page": 1,
  "pageSize": 100,
  "search": [],
  "searchBranches": [
    [
      {
        "field": "attacker",
        "op": "equals",
        "value": "string"
      }
    ]
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="search-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|Account ID.|
|forceRefresh|query|boolean|false|none|
|format|query|string|false|Output format for event data. 'json' returns the default format, 'stix2' returns STIX 2.1 Sighting SROs with linked Indicator SDOs, Observed Data SDOs, and SCOs, 'taxii' returns a TAXII 2.1 Envelope with Content-Type application/taxii+json;version=2.1.|
|cache|query|string|false|Cache strategy. 'from-graph' serves results from the graph-node KV cache when all requested UUIDs are cached; falls back to normal path on partial/zero hit.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» cursor|body|string|false|Cursor for pagination. When provided, filters are embedded in the cursor so you only need to pass cursor and pageSize.|
|» datasetId|body|[string]|false|Dataset UUIDs to query, or one standalone scope value: 'all'/'*' or 'operational' for readable intelligence datasets (isAnalytics=false), or 'analytics' for readable analytics datasets (isAnalytics=true). Scope values query at most 50 datasets. If not provided, uses the default dataset.|
|» order|body|string|false|none|

## Aggregate events

<a id="opIdget_EventAggregate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/cloudforce-one/events/aggregate?aggregateBy=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/cloudforce-one/events/aggregate`

Counts events grouped by one or more columns, such as `attacker` or `targetIndustry`. Optionally filter by date range and group the counts by day.

<h3 id="aggregate-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|Account ID.|
|aggregateBy|query|string|true|Column(s) to aggregate by - single column or comma-separated list (e.g., 'attacker', 'targetIndustry', 'attacker,targetIndustry'). With `tags`, an event counts once for each of its tags, in the bucket counts and in `total`, and events without tags count as `Unknown`; `tags` is not supported for analytics datasets.|
|datasetId|query|[string]|false|Dataset UUIDs to filter by, or one standalone scope value: 'all'/'*' or 'operational' for readable intelligence datasets (isAnalytics=false), or 'analytics' for readable analytics datasets (isAnalytics=true). Scope values query at most 50 datasets. If not provided, uses the default dataset.|
|startDate|query|string|false|Start date for filtering (ISO 8601 format, e.g., '2024-01-01')|
|endDate|query|string|false|End date for filtering (ISO 8601 format, e.g., '2024-12-31')|
|groupByDate|query|boolean|false|Whether to group results by date (daily aggregation)|
|limit|query|number|false|Maximum number of results to return|

```json
  "dateRange": {

    "startDate": "string"
  },
  "total": 0
}
```

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "An error occurred."
    }
  ],
  "result": {},
  "success": true
}
```

## List related events

<a id="opIdget_EventRelationships"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/cloudforce-one/events/by-id/string/relationships?datasetId=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/cloudforce-one/events/by-id/{event_id}/relationships`

Lists events related to an event by following its relationships. `datasetId` is required. Use `direction`, `maxDepth`, and `relationshipTypes` to control which relationships are followed.

<h3 id="list-related-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|Account ID.|
|event_id|path|string|true|Event UUID.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to traverse the graph. Defaults to 'both' to search all.|
|maxDepth|query|number|false|The maximum depth to traverse. Defaults to 5.|
|relationshipTypes|query|string \| [string]|false|An optional array of relationship types to filter by.|
|indicatorTypeIds|query|[string]|false|An optional array of indicator type IDs to filter the results by.|
|datasetId|query|string|true|The dataset ID to search within.|
|includeParent|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the starting event in the results. Defaults to true.|
|page|query|number|false|none|
|pageSize|query|number|false|none|

|---|---|
|direction|ancestors|
|direction|descendants|
|direction|both|

## Copy events to another dataset

<a id="opIdpost_EventCopyToNewDS"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/cloudforce-one/events/dataset/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/copy \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "destDatasetId": "12345678-1234-1234-1234-1234567890ab",
    "eventIds": [
      "7632a037-fdef-4899-9b12-148470aae772"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/cloudforce-one/events/dataset/{dataset_id}/copy`

Copies events to the dataset given by `destDatasetId` and leaves the originals in place. Raw event data is copied only when `keepRawData` is true.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "destDatasetId": "12345678-1234-1234-1234-1234567890ab",
  "eventIds": [
    "7632a037-fdef-4899-9b12-148470aae772"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="copy-events-to-another-dataset-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|Account ID.|
|dataset_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Dataset UUID.|
|keepRawData|query|boolean|false|If true, copies raw data to the destination dataset. Default is false (raw data is stripped/not copied).|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» destDatasetId|body|string|true|none|
|» eventIds|body|[string]|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "copied": 2,
  "indicatorsCopied": 5,
  "insertFailures": [
    {
      "index": 0,
      "reason": "string"
    }
  ],
  "relationshipsCopied": 3
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "An error occurred."
    }
  ],
  "result": {},
  "success": true
}
```

|---|---|---|---|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|indicatorsCopied|number|true|none|Number of indicators successfully copied|
|insertFailures|[object]|false|none|Array of events that failed to insert into destination|
|» index|number|true|none|Index of the event that failed to insert|
|» reason|string|true|none|Reason for the failure|
|relationshipsCopied|number|true|none|Number of relationships successfully copied|

Status Code **400**

## Move events to another dataset

<a id="opIdpost_EventMoveToNewDS"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/cloudforce-one/events/dataset/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/move \

    ]
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/cloudforce-one/events/dataset/{dataset_id}/move`

Moves events to the dataset given by `destDatasetId` and removes them from the source dataset. Raw event data is always removed from the source and is kept only when `keepRawData` is true.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "destDatasetId": "12345678-1234-1234-1234-1234567890ab",
  "eventIds": [
    "7632a037-fdef-4899-9b12-148470aae772"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="move-events-to-another-dataset-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|Account ID.|
|dataset_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Dataset UUID.|
|keepRawData|query|boolean|false|If true, copies raw data to the destination dataset. Default is false (raw data is stripped/not copied). Raw data is always deleted from the source.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» destDatasetId|body|string|true|none|
|» eventIds|body|[string]|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "deletionFailures": [
    {
      "datasetId": "string",
      "reason": "string"
    }

  "insertFailures": [
    {
      "index": 0,
      "reason": "string"
    }

  "moved": 2,

}
```

```json
}
```
