## Create account commands

<a id="opIdpost-commands"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/01a7362d577a6c3019a474fd6f485823/dex/commands \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "commands": [
      {
        "args": {
          "test-all-routes": true
        },
        "device_id": "string",
        "registration_id": "string",
        "type": "pcap",
        "user_email": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/dex/commands`

Initiate commands for up to 10 devices per account.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "commands": [
    {
      "args": {
        "test-all-routes": true
      },
      "device_id": "string",
      "registration_id": "string",
      "type": "pcap",
      "user_email": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-account-commands-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[digital-experience-monitoring_account_identifier](#schemadigital-experience-monitoring_account_identifier)|true|Unique Cloudflare account ID.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» commands|body|[object]|true|List of device-level commands to execute|
|» » args|body|object|false|Command arguments. Allowed fields depend on `type`.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » » test-all-routes|body|boolean|false|Test an IP address from all included or excluded ranges. Essentially the same as running 'route get <ip>' and collecting the results. This option may increase the time taken to collect the warp-diag.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » » max-file-size-mb|body|number|false|Maximum file size (in MB) for the capture file. If the capture artifact exceeds the specified max file size, it will NOT be uploaded.|
|» » » packet-size-bytes|body|number|false|Maximum number of bytes to save for each packet|
|» » » time-limit-min|body|number|false|Limit on capture duration (in minutes)|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » » interfaces|body|[string]|false|List of interfaces to run the speed test on|
|» » device_id|body|string|true|Unique identifier for the physical device|
|» » registration_id|body|string|false|Unique identifier for the device registration. Required for multi-user devices to target the correct user session.|
|» » type|body|string|true|Type of command to execute on the device|
|» » user_email|body|string|true|Email tied to the device|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » » interfaces|default|
|» » » interfaces|tunnel|
|» » type|pcap|
|» » type|speed-test|
|» » type|warp-diag|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result_info": {
    "count": 1,
```

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|

## Create a new dataset

<a id="opIddlp-datasets-create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/dlp/datasets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "case_sensitive": true,
    "description": "string",
    "encoding_version": 0,
    "name": "string",
    "secret": true
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/dlp/datasets`

Creates a new DLP (Data Loss Prevention) dataset for storing custom detection patterns. Datasets can contain exact match data, word lists, or EDM (Exact Data Match) configurations.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "case_sensitive": true,
  "description": "string",
  "encoding_version": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "secret": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-dataset-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[dlp_NewDataset](#schemadlp_newdataset)|true|Dataset description.|
|» case_sensitive|body|boolean|false|Only applies to custom word lists.<br>Determines if the words should be matched in a case-sensitive manner<br>Cannot be set to false if `secret` is true or undefined|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|The description of the dataset.|
|» encoding_version|body|integer(int32)|false|Dataset encoding version<br><br>Non-secret custom word lists with no header are always version 1.<br>Secret EDM lists with no header are version 1.<br>Multicolumn CSV with headers are version 2.<br>Omitting this field provides the default value 0, which is interpreted<br>the same as 1.|
|» name|body|string|true|none|
|» secret|body|boolean|false|Generate a secret dataset.<br><br>If true, the response will include a secret to use with the EDM encoder.<br>If false, the response has no secret and the dataset is uploaded in plaintext.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "dataset": {
      "case_sensitive": true,
      "columns": [
        {
          "entry_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
          "header_name": "string",
          "num_cells": 0,
          "upload_status": "empty"
        }
      ],
      "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "description": "string",
      "encoding_version": 0,
      "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
      "name": "string",
      "num_cells": 0,
      "secret": true,
      "status": "empty",
      "updated_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "uploads": [
        {
          "num_cells": 0,
          "status": "empty",
          "version": 0
        }
      ]
    },
    "encoding_version": 0,
    "max_cells": 0,
    "secret": "password",
    "version": 0
  }
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/dlp/datasets/{dataset_id}/upload/{version}`

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-dlp-settings">DLP Settings</h1>

## Fetch limits associated with DLP for account

<a id="opIddlp-limits-get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/dlp/limits \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/dlp/limits`

Retrieves current DLP usage limits and quotas for the account, including
maximum allowed counts and current usage for custom entries, dataset cells,
and document fingerprints.

<h3 id="fetch-limits-associated-with-dlp-for-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "max_custom_regex_entries": 0,
```

## Validate a DLP regex pattern

<a id="opIddlp-pattern-validate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/dlp/patterns/validate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "max_match_bytes": 0,
    "regex": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/dlp/patterns/validate`

Validates whether this pattern is a valid regular expression. Rejects it if
the regular expression is too complex or can match an unbounded-length
string. The regex will be rejected if it uses `*` or `+`. Bound the maximum
number of characters that can be matched using a range, e.g. `{1,100}`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "max_match_bytes": 0,
  "regex": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="validate-a-dlp-regex-pattern-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|Account ID.|
|body|body|[dlp_RegexValidationQuery](#schemadlp_regexvalidationquery)|true|Validation query.|
|» max_match_bytes|body|integer(int32) \| null|false|Maximum number of bytes that the regular expression can match.<br><br>If this is `null` then there is no limit on the length. Patterns can use<br>`*` and `+`. Otherwise repeats should use a range `{m,n}` to restrict<br>patterns to the length. If this field is missing, then a default length<br>limit is used.<br><br>Note that the length is specified in bytes. Since regular expressions<br>use UTF-8 the pattern `.` can match up to 4 bytes. Hence `.{1,256}`<br>has a maximum length of 1024 bytes.|
|» regex|body|string|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "valid": true
  }
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

<h3 id="validate-a-dlp-regex-pattern-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Validation response.|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|Failed to validate.|[dlp_api-response-common-failure](#schemadlp_api-response-common-failure)|

<h3 id="validate-a-dlp-regex-pattern-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[dlp_messages](#schemadlp_messages)|true|none|none|
|messages|[dlp_messages](#schemadlp_messages)|true|none|none|
|success|boolean|true|none|Whether the API call was successful.|
|result|[dlp_RegexValidationResult](#schemadlp_regexvalidationresult)|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|success|true|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
api_email & api_key & api_token
</aside>

## Delete integration profile

<a id="opIddlp-profiles-delete-integration-profile"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/dlp/profiles/integration/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /accounts/{account_id}/dlp/profiles/integration/{profile_id}`

Deletes a DLP integration profile whose integration no longer exists. If the profile owns
entries, `recursive=1` is required. This also deletes the entries and removes all references to
them, as listed by the references endpoint.

<h3 id="delete-integration-profile-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|recursive|query|integer(int32)|false|Set to `1` to also delete the entries owned by the profile and remove all references to<br>them, as listed by the references endpoint. Required if the profile owns any entries.<br>Defaults to `0`.|
|account_id|path|string|true|none|
|profile_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {}
}
```

```json

    }
  ],

  "success": false
}
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/dlp/profiles/integration/{profile_id}/references`

shows how each data class would change if the profile is deleted with `recursive=1`, and

```json
      }
```

```bash
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/dlp/validators/proximity_words`

Creates a reusable list of weighted words that detection entries can attach to in order to
refine their matches. An account may own at most 100 validators across all kinds.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "HIPAA context words",
  "words": [
    {
      "weight": "strong",
      "word": "social security number"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-proximity-word-validator-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[dlp_ProximityWordValidatorWrite](#schemadlp_proximitywordvalidatorwrite)|true|Attributes of the new validator.|
|» name|body|string|true|A name for this validator, at most 50 characters.|
|» words|body|[[dlp_ProximityWord](#schemadlp_proximityword)]|true|The words that raise confidence when found near a match, at most 100 per validator. Matching<br>ignores case, so the list may not contain the same word twice with different capitalisation.<br>Words are stored as sent.<br><br>For example, a validator for medical record numbers might use<br>`[{"word": "patient", "weight": "strong"}, {"word": "diagnosis", "weight": "moderate"},<br>{"word": "mrn", "weight": "weak"}]`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "name": "HIPAA context words",
    "referenced_by": {
      "entries": [
        {
          "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
          "name": "US Social Security Number",
          "type": "custom"
        }
      ],
      "entry_count": 3
    },
```

`DELETE /accounts/{account_id}/dlp/validators/worker/{validator_id}`

Deletes a `worker` validator. Fails with `409` while any detection entry is still attached to
it; detach it from those entries first.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|none|
|validator_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {}
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

## Create a DLS prefix binding

<a id="opIdpublicCreatePrefixBinding"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/dls/regional_services/prefix_bindings \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "cidr": "10.0.1.0/24",
    "prefix_id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
    "region_key": "eu"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/dls/regional_services/prefix_bindings`

Bind a CIDR from a BYOIP prefix to a region.

This requires the **IP Prefixes Write** permission in addition to **DLS Write**, because the binding is created against a BYOIP prefix in Addressing.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "cidr": "10.0.1.0/24",
  "prefix_id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
  "region_key": "eu"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-dls-prefix-binding-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[dls_account_identifier](#schemadls_account_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[dls_CreatePrefixBindingInput](#schemadls_createprefixbindinginput)|true|none|
|» cidr|body|string|true|IP prefix in CIDR notation to bind.|
|» prefix_id|body|string|true|The ID of the parent IP prefix that contains the CIDR.|
|» region_key|body|string|true|Region key from managed regions (e.g., "us", "eu").|

<a id="opIddns-firewall-create-dns-firewall-cluster"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/dns_firewall \

    "attack_mitigation": {

    },
    "deprecate_any_requests": true,
    "ecs_fallback": false,
    "maximum_cache_ttl": 900,
    "minimum_cache_ttl": 60,
    "name": "My Awesome DNS Firewall cluster",
    "negative_cache_ttl": 900,
    "ratelimit": 600,
    "retries": 2,
    "upstream_ips": [
      "192.0.2.1",
      "198.51.100.1",
      "2001:DB8:100::CF"
    ],
    "dns_firewall_ip_count": 2
  }'
```

```json
  "upstream_ips": [
    "192.0.2.1",
    "198.51.100.1",
    "2001:DB8:100::CF"
  ],

}
```

<h3 id="create-dns-firewall-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[dns-firewall_identifier](#schemadns-firewall_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[dns-firewall_dns-firewall-cluster-post](#schemadns-firewall_dns-firewall-cluster-post)|true|none|
|» attack_mitigation|body|[dns-firewall_attack_mitigation](#schemadns-firewall_attack_mitigation)|false|Attack mitigation settings|
|» deprecate_any_requests|body|[dns-firewall_deprecate_any_requests](#schemadns-firewall_deprecate_any_requests)|false|Whether to refuse to answer queries for the ANY type|
|» ecs_fallback|body|[dns-firewall_ecs_fallback](#schemadns-firewall_ecs_fallback)|false|Whether to forward client IP (resolver) subnet if no EDNS Client Subnet is sent|
|» maximum_cache_ttl|body|[dns-firewall_maximum_cache_ttl](#schemadns-firewall_maximum_cache_ttl)|false|By default, Cloudflare attempts to cache responses for as long as<br>indicated by the TTL received from upstream nameservers. This setting<br>sets an upper bound on this duration. For caching purposes, higher TTLs<br>will be decreased to the maximum value defined by this setting.<br><br>This setting does not affect the TTL value in the DNS response<br>Cloudflare returns to clients. Cloudflare will always forward the TTL<br>value received from upstream nameservers.<br>|
|» minimum_cache_ttl|body|[dns-firewall_minimum_cache_ttl](#schemadns-firewall_minimum_cache_ttl)|false|By default, Cloudflare attempts to cache responses for as long as<br>indicated by the TTL received from upstream nameservers. This setting<br>sets a lower bound on this duration. For caching purposes, lower TTLs<br>will be increased to the minimum value defined by this setting.<br><br>This setting does not affect the TTL value in the DNS response<br>Cloudflare returns to clients. Cloudflare will always forward the TTL<br>value received from upstream nameservers.<br><br>Note that, even with this setting, there is no guarantee that a<br>response will be cached for at least the specified duration. Cached<br>responses may be removed earlier for capacity or other operational<br>reasons.<br>|
|» name|body|[dns-firewall_name](#schemadns-firewall_name)|true|DNS Firewall cluster name|
|» negative_cache_ttl|body|[dns-firewall_negative_cache_ttl](#schemadns-firewall_negative_cache_ttl)|false|This setting controls how long DNS Firewall should cache negative<br>responses (e.g., NXDOMAIN) from the upstream servers.<br><br>This setting does not affect the TTL value in the DNS response<br>Cloudflare returns to clients. Cloudflare will always forward the TTL<br>value received from upstream nameservers.<br>|
|» ratelimit|body|[dns-firewall_ratelimit](#schemadns-firewall_ratelimit)|false|Maximum number of DNS queries per second that will be forwarded to your upstream nameservers. The limit is enforced per server, where each server receives a fraction of the configured value. The actual aggregate rate for a data center may vary depending on how many servers are present. Responses served from cache do not count toward this limit. Set to null to disable rate limiting.|
|» retries|body|[dns-firewall_retries](#schemadns-firewall_retries)|false|Number of retries for fetching DNS responses from upstream nameservers (not counting the initial attempt)|
|» upstream_ips|body|[dns-firewall_upstream_ips](#schemadns-firewall_upstream_ips)|true|none|
|» dns_firewall_ip_count|body|[dns-firewall_dns_firewall_ip_count](#schemadns-firewall_dns_firewall_ip_count)|false|Number of IPv4 addresses to assign to the DNS Firewall cluster. Only used during cluster creation and cannot be changed later.|

```json
      "198.51.100.1",
```

```bash
    ]
  }'
```

|body|body|[dns-firewall_dns-firewall-cluster-patch](#schemadns-firewall_dns-firewall-cluster-patch)|true|none|
|» attack_mitigation|body|[dns-firewall_attack_mitigation](#schemadns-firewall_attack_mitigation)|false|Attack mitigation settings|
|» deprecate_any_requests|body|[dns-firewall_deprecate_any_requests](#schemadns-firewall_deprecate_any_requests)|false|Whether to refuse to answer queries for the ANY type|
|» ecs_fallback|body|[dns-firewall_ecs_fallback](#schemadns-firewall_ecs_fallback)|false|Whether to forward client IP (resolver) subnet if no EDNS Client Subnet is sent|
|» maximum_cache_ttl|body|[dns-firewall_maximum_cache_ttl](#schemadns-firewall_maximum_cache_ttl)|false|By default, Cloudflare attempts to cache responses for as long as<br>indicated by the TTL received from upstream nameservers. This setting<br>sets an upper bound on this duration. For caching purposes, higher TTLs<br>will be decreased to the maximum value defined by this setting.<br><br>This setting does not affect the TTL value in the DNS response<br>Cloudflare returns to clients. Cloudflare will always forward the TTL<br>value received from upstream nameservers.<br>|
|» minimum_cache_ttl|body|[dns-firewall_minimum_cache_ttl](#schemadns-firewall_minimum_cache_ttl)|false|By default, Cloudflare attempts to cache responses for as long as<br>indicated by the TTL received from upstream nameservers. This setting<br>sets a lower bound on this duration. For caching purposes, lower TTLs<br>will be increased to the minimum value defined by this setting.<br><br>This setting does not affect the TTL value in the DNS response<br>Cloudflare returns to clients. Cloudflare will always forward the TTL<br>value received from upstream nameservers.<br><br>Note that, even with this setting, there is no guarantee that a<br>response will be cached for at least the specified duration. Cached<br>responses may be removed earlier for capacity or other operational<br>reasons.<br>|
|» name|body|[dns-firewall_name](#schemadns-firewall_name)|false|DNS Firewall cluster name|
|» negative_cache_ttl|body|[dns-firewall_negative_cache_ttl](#schemadns-firewall_negative_cache_ttl)|false|This setting controls how long DNS Firewall should cache negative<br>responses (e.g., NXDOMAIN) from the upstream servers.<br><br>This setting does not affect the TTL value in the DNS response<br>Cloudflare returns to clients. Cloudflare will always forward the TTL<br>value received from upstream nameservers.<br>|
|» ratelimit|body|[dns-firewall_ratelimit](#schemadns-firewall_ratelimit)|false|Maximum number of DNS queries per second that will be forwarded to your upstream nameservers. The limit is enforced per server, where each server receives a fraction of the configured value. The actual aggregate rate for a data center may vary depending on how many servers are present. Responses served from cache do not count toward this limit. Set to null to disable rate limiting.|
|» retries|body|[dns-firewall_retries](#schemadns-firewall_retries)|false|Number of retries for fetching DNS responses from upstream nameservers (not counting the initial attempt)|

## Create Custom Nameserver Set

<a id="opIddns-settings-for-an-account-create-custom-nameserver-set"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/dns_settings/nameserver_sets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "advanced": false,
    "ip_set": 1,
    "name": "Production nameservers",
    "nameservers": [
      {
        "ip_count": 1,
        "name": "ns1.example.com"
      },
      {
        "ip_count": 1,
        "name": "ns1.example.com"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/dns_settings/nameserver_sets`

Creates a named Custom Nameserver Set. Only the customer-defined name can be changed later. To change nameservers or addresses, create a new set, move any zone assignments, and delete the old set.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "advanced": false,
  "ip_set": 1,
  "name": "Production nameservers",
  "nameservers": [
    {
      "ip_count": 1,
      "name": "ns1.example.com"
    },
    {
      "ip_count": 1,
      "name": "ns1.example.com"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-custom-nameserver-set-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[dns-settings_identifier](#schemadns-settings_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[dns-settings_nameserver-set-create](#schemadns-settings_nameserver-set-create)|true|none|
|» advanced|body|boolean|false|Whether to allocate the nameservers from distinct Advanced anycast groups.|
|» ip_set|body|[dns-settings_nameserver-set-ip-set](#schemadns-settings_nameserver-set-ip-set)|false|Selects the account-specific IP set that supplies the nameserver addresses. Nameserver sets with the same `ip_set` and `advanced` value may reuse addresses; otherwise, they use disjoint address groups.|
|» name|body|[dns-settings_nameserver-set-name](#schemadns-settings_nameserver-set-name)|true|Customer-defined name, unique within the account by exact string equality (case-sensitive, with no Unicode normalization). Must be valid UTF-8 and at most 255 UTF-8 bytes, not 255 characters. Only graphical Unicode characters are allowed; leading or trailing whitespace is rejected. The name can be changed without changing the set's nameservers or addresses.|
|» nameservers|body|[[dns-settings_nameserver-set-create-member](#schemadns-settings_nameserver-set-create-member)]|true|Lists each nameserver and the number of addresses to allocate to it. Requires a unique name for each entry in the set.|

## Update Custom Nameserver Set

<a id="opIddns-settings-for-an-account-update-custom-nameserver-set"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/dns_settings/nameserver_sets/0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Production nameservers"
  }'
```

`PATCH /accounts/{account_id}/dns_settings/nameserver_sets/{nameserver_set_id}`

Renames a Custom Nameserver Set owned by the account. Only name may be supplied; immutable and unknown fields are rejected even if unchanged. An empty object or the existing name is a successful no-op. Requires the account-scoped creation entitlements for the existing set.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Production nameservers"
}
```

<h3 id="update-custom-nameserver-set-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[dns-settings_identifier](#schemadns-settings_identifier)|true|none|
|nameserver_set_id|path|[dns-settings_nameserver-set-id](#schemadns-settings_nameserver-set-id)|true|none|
|body|body|[dns-settings_nameserver-set-patch](#schemadns-settings_nameserver-set-patch)|true|none|
|» name|body|[dns-settings_nameserver-set-name](#schemadns-settings_nameserver-set-name)|false|Customer-defined name, unique within the account by exact string equality (case-sensitive, with no Unicode normalization). Must be valid UTF-8 and at most 255 UTF-8 bytes, not 255 characters. Only graphical Unicode characters are allowed; leading or trailing whitespace is rejected. The name can be changed without changing the set's nameservers or addresses.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "created_on": "2026-09-01T12:00:00Z",
    "id": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
    "ip_set": 1,
    "name": "Production nameservers",
    "advanced": false,
    "nameservers": [
      {
        "ipv4": [
          "192.0.2.1"
        ],
        "ipv6": [
          "2001:db8::1"
        ],
        "name": "ns1.example.com"
      },
      {
        "ipv4": [
          "192.0.2.1"
        ],
        "ipv6": [
          "2001:db8::1"
        ],
        "name": "ns1.example.com"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-email-security">Email Security</h1>

## Search email messages

<a id="opIdemail_security_investigate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/email-security/investigate \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/email-security/investigate`

Returns information for each email that matches the provided search parameters.

<h3 id="search-email-messages-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The beginning of the search date range. Defaults to `now - 30 days`. Must not be in the future.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the search date range. Defaults to `now`.|
|query|query|string|false|Space-delimited term matched case-insensitively against message metadata — sender, recipient, subject, attachment names and hashes, and message ID.|
|detections_only|query|boolean|false|Whether to include only detections in search results.|
|final_disposition|query|string|false|Dispositions to filter by.|
|metric|query|string|false|Metric to aggregate the results by.|
|message_action|query|string|false|Message actions to filter by.|
|recipient|query|string|false|Filter by recipient. Matches an email address or a domain.|
|sender|query|string|false|Filter by sender. Matches an email address or a domain.|
|smtp_helo_ip|query|string|false|Matches messages whose SMTP HELO server IP address equals this value.|
|alert_id|query|string|false|Filter by alert ID.|
|domain|query|string|false|Filter by a domain found in the email — sender domain, recipient domain, or a domain in a link.|
|message_id|query|string|false|Filter by the RFC 5322 Message-ID header.|
|subject|query|string|false|Search for messages containing individual keywords in any order within the subject.|
|delivery_status|query|[email-security_MessageDeliveryStatus](#schemaemail-security_messagedeliverystatus)|false|Delivery status to filter by.|
|cursor|query|string|false|Pagination cursor from the previous response's `result_info`.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page. Maximum value is 1000.|
|page|query|integer \| null|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: Use cursor pagination instead. End of life: November 1, 2026.|
|account_id|path|[email-security_identifier](#schemaemail-security_identifier)|true|Account identifier tag.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|final_disposition|MALICIOUS|
|final_disposition|SUSPICIOUS|
|final_disposition|SPOOF|
|final_disposition|SPAM|
|final_disposition|BULK|
|final_disposition|NONE|
|message_action|PREVIEW|
|message_action|QUARANTINE_RELEASED|
|message_action|MOVED|
|delivery_status|delivered|
|delivery_status|moved|
|delivery_status|quarantined|
|delivery_status|rejected|
|delivery_status|deferred|
|delivery_status|bounced|
|delivery_status|queued|
|delivery_status|move_failed|

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/email-security/investigate/bulk`

Creates a new bulk action job to move or release messages that match the provided search parameters. To move or release an explicit list of known messages instead of a search, use the move or release endpoints.

```json
}
```

```bash
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /accounts/{account_id}/email-security/investigate/bulk/{job_id}`

Deletes the job, removing it from all list and detail endpoints. Only jobs in a terminal state (`COMPLETED`, `CANCELLED`, or `FAILED`) can be deleted. To stop an in-progress job without removing it, use the cancel endpoint instead.

|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[email-security_identifier](#schemaemail-security_identifier)|true|Account identifier tag.|
|job_id|path|[email-security_BulkJobId](#schemaemail-security_bulkjobid)|true|Identifier of the bulk action job.|

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  }
}
```

```json
    {

    }

  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

## Move messages

<a id="opIdemail_security_post_bulk_move"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/email-security/investigate/move \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "destination": "Inbox",
    "expected_disposition": {},
    "ids": [
      "4Njp3P0STMz2c02Q-2024-01-05T10:00:00-12345678"
    ],
    "postfix_ids": [
      "4Njp3P0STMz2c02Q"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/email-security/investigate/move`

Moves one or more messages to a specified mailbox folder (Inbox, JunkEmail, DeletedItems, RecoverableItemsDeletions, or RecoverableItemsPurges). Requires active integration. Operates on an explicit list of messages; to move all messages matching a search, create a bulk action job instead.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "destination": "Inbox",
  "expected_disposition": {},
  "ids": [
    "4Njp3P0STMz2c02Q-2024-01-05T10:00:00-12345678"
  ],
  "postfix_ids": [
    "4Njp3P0STMz2c02Q"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="move-messages-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[email-security_identifier](#schemaemail-security_identifier)|true|Account identifier tag.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» destination|body|[email-security_MailboxDestination](#schemaemail-security_mailboxdestination)|true|The mailbox folder to move messages to.|
|» expected_disposition|body|string \| null|false|**Deprecated.** Nonfunctional field. End of life: December 1, 2026.|
|» ids|body|[[email-security_InvestigateId](#schemaemail-security_investigateid)]|true|List of message IDs to move.|
|» postfix_ids|body|[[email-security_PostfixId](#schemaemail-security_postfixid)]|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated, use `ids` instead. End of life: November 1, 2026.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» destination|Inbox|
|» destination|JunkEmail|
|» destination|DeletedItems|
|» destination|RecoverableItemsDeletions|
|» destination|RecoverableItemsPurges|

```json
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,

    {
```

## Generate preview for a non-detection message

<a id="opIdemail_security_post_preview"></a>

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/email-security/investigate/preview`

Generates a preview image for a message that was not flagged as a detection. The message is rendered from the copy in the recipient's mailbox, so this requires an active integration and only works while the message is still in the recipient's inbox. Returns a base64-encoded PNG screenshot of the email body. For messages with a detection, use the detection preview endpoint instead.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": "4Njp3P0STMz2c02Q-2024-01-05T10:00:00-12345678"
}
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/email-security/submissions`

Returns information for submissions made to reclassify emails. Shows the status, outcome, and disposition changes for reclassification requests made by users or the security team. Useful for tracking false positive/negative reports.

|type|query|string|false|Filter by who created the submission — `TEAM` for security team members or `USER` for end users.|
|submission_id|query|string|false|Filter by a specific submission ID.|
|original_disposition|query|[email-security_SubmissionDisposition](#schemaemail-security_submissiondisposition)|false|none|

## List email allow policies

<a id="opIdemail_security_list_allow_policies"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/email-security/settings/allow_policies \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/email-security/settings/allow_policies`

Returns a paginated list of email allow policies. These policies exempt matching emails from security detection, allowing them to bypass disposition actions. Supports filtering by pattern type and policy attributes.

<h3 id="list-email-allow-policies-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer|false|Current page within paginated list of results.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page. Maximum value is 1000.|
|search|query|string|false|Search term for filtering records. Behavior may change.|
|order|query|string|false|Field to sort by.|
|direction|query|string|false|The sorting direction.|
|is_exempt_recipient|query|boolean|false|Filter to show only policies where messages to the recipient bypass all detections.|
|is_trusted_sender|query|boolean|false|Filter to show only policies where messages from the sender bypass all detections and link following.|
|is_acceptable_sender|query|boolean|false|Filter to show only policies where messages from the sender are exempted from Spam, Spoof, and Bulk dispositions (not Malicious or Suspicious).|
|verify_sender|query|boolean|false|Filter to show only policies that enforce DMARC, SPF, or DKIM authentication.|
|pattern_type|query|object|false|Filter by pattern type.|
|pattern|query|string|false|Filter by exact pattern value.|
|expired|query|boolean|false|Filter to return only expired policies (`true`) or only policies that still apply (`false`). Omit to return both.|
|account_id|path|[email-security_identifier](#schemaemail-security_identifier)|true|Account identifier tag.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|pattern|
|order|created_at|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|

## Create email allow policy

<a id="opIdemail_security_create_allow_policy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/email-security/settings/allow_policies \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "comments": "Trust all messages send from test@example.com",
    "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "is_acceptable_sender": false,
    "is_exempt_recipient": false,
    "is_recipient": false,
    "is_regex": false,
    "is_sender": true,
    "is_spoof": false,
    "is_trusted_sender": true,
    "pattern": "test@example.com",
    "pattern_type": "EMAIL",
    "verify_sender": true
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/email-security/settings/allow_policies`

Creates a new allow policy that exempts matching emails from security detections. Use with caution as this bypasses email security scanning. Policies can match on sender patterns and apply to specific detections or all detections.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comments": "Trust all messages send from test@example.com",
  "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "is_acceptable_sender": false,
  "is_exempt_recipient": false,
  "is_recipient": false,
  "is_regex": false,
  "is_sender": true,
  "is_spoof": false,
  "is_trusted_sender": true,
  "pattern": "test@example.com",
  "pattern_type": "EMAIL",
  "verify_sender": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-email-allow-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[email-security_identifier](#schemaemail-security_identifier)|true|Account identifier tag.|
|body|body|[email-security_CreateAllowPolicy](#schemaemail-security_createallowpolicy)|true|none|
|» comments|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» expires_at|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|Timestamp at which the policy expires. After this time, Email Security ignores the policy. The value must lie in the future. Send `null` to clear the expiration.|
|» is_acceptable_sender|body|boolean|true|Exempts messages from this sender from Spam, Spoof and Bulk dispositions only; Malicious and Suspicious dispositions still apply.|
|» is_exempt_recipient|body|boolean|true|Bypasses all detections for messages to this recipient.|
|» is_recipient|body|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated as of July 1, 2025. Use `is_exempt_recipient` instead. End of life: July 1, 2026.|
|» is_regex|body|boolean|true|none|
|» is_sender|body|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated as of July 1, 2025. Use `is_trusted_sender` instead. End of life: July 1, 2026.|
|» is_spoof|body|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated as of July 1, 2025. Use `is_acceptable_sender` instead. End of life: July 1, 2026.|
|» is_trusted_sender|body|boolean|true|Bypasses all detections and link following for messages from this sender.|
|» pattern|body|string|true|The pattern value to match. The format depends on `pattern_type`: a valid email address for EMAIL (e.g. `user@example.com`), a valid domain name for DOMAIN (e.g. `example.com`), or a plain IPv4 or IPv6 address or CIDR block for IP (e.g. `1.2.3.4`, `1.2.3.0/24`, `2606:4700:4700::1111`, or `2606:4700:4700::/48`); the API rejects private or unique-local, loopback, link-local, unspecified, and IPv4 broadcast addresses, including their IPv4-mapped IPv6 equivalents.|
|» pattern_type|body|[email-security_PatternType](#schemaemail-security_patterntype)|true|Type of pattern matching.<br>- EMAIL: matches a full email address (e.g. `user@example.com`)<br>- DOMAIN: matches a domain name (e.g. `example.com`)<br>- IP: matches a plain IPv4 or IPv6 address (e.g. `1.2.3.4` or `2606:4700:4700::1111`) or CIDR block (e.g. `1.2.3.0/24` or `2606:4700:4700::/48`). The API rejects private or unique-local, loopback, link-local, unspecified, and IPv4 broadcast addresses, including their IPv4-mapped IPv6 equivalents.<br>- UNKNOWN: deprecated; you cannot use this when creating or updating policies, but it may appear on existing entries.<br>|
|» verify_sender|body|boolean|true|Enforce DMARC, SPF or DKIM authentication. When on, Email Security only honors policies that pass authentication.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» pattern_type|EMAIL|
|» pattern_type|DOMAIN|
|» pattern_type|IP|
|» pattern_type|UNKNOWN|

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/email-security/settings/allow_policies/batch`

Executes multiple allow policy operations atomically: delete, partially update,
replace, and create allow policies in a single request. All four operation arrays
(deletes, patches, puts, posts) are required and executed in order.
Send empty arrays for unused operations.

## Replace an email allow policy

<a id="opIdemail_security_replace_allow_policy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/email-security/settings/allow_policies/f174e90a-fafe-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "comments": "Trust all messages send from test@example.com",
    "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "is_acceptable_sender": false,
    "is_exempt_recipient": false,
    "is_recipient": false,
    "is_regex": false,
    "is_sender": true,
    "is_spoof": false,
    "is_trusted_sender": true,
    "pattern": "test@example.com",
    "pattern_type": "EMAIL",
    "verify_sender": true
  }'
```

`PUT /accounts/{account_id}/email-security/settings/allow_policies/{policy_id}`

Replaces an existing allow policy in full. Unlike PATCH, every field is taken from the request body, so optional fields that are omitted are reset rather than left untouched. Use this when managing policies declaratively.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comments": "Trust all messages send from test@example.com",
  "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "is_acceptable_sender": false,
  "is_exempt_recipient": false,
  "is_recipient": false,
  "is_regex": false,
  "is_sender": true,
  "is_spoof": false,
  "is_trusted_sender": true,
  "pattern": "test@example.com",

}
```

## Update an email allow policy

<a id="opIdemail_security_update_allow_policy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/email-security/settings/allow_policies/f174e90a-fafe-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415 \

  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

    "is_exempt_recipient": false,
    "is_recipient": false,
    "is_regex": false,
    "is_sender": true,
    "is_spoof": false,
    "is_trusted_sender": true,

    "pattern_type": "EMAIL",
    "verify_sender": true
  }'
```

`PATCH /accounts/{account_id}/email-security/settings/allow_policies/{policy_id}`

Updates an existing allow policy. Only provided fields will be modified. Changes take effect for new emails matching the pattern.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comments": "Trust all messages send from test@example.com",
  "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "is_acceptable_sender": false,
  "is_exempt_recipient": false,
  "is_recipient": false,
  "is_regex": false,
  "is_sender": true,
  "is_spoof": false,
  "is_trusted_sender": true,
  "pattern": "test@example.com",
  "pattern_type": "EMAIL",
  "verify_sender": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-email-allow-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[email-security_identifier](#schemaemail-security_identifier)|true|Account identifier tag.|
|policy_id|path|[email-security_AllowPolicyId](#schemaemail-security_allowpolicyid)|true|none|
|body|body|[email-security_UpdateAllowPolicy](#schemaemail-security_updateallowpolicy)|true|none|
|» comments|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» expires_at|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|Timestamp at which the policy expires. After this time, Email Security ignores the policy. The value must lie in the future. Send `null` to clear the expiration.|
|» is_acceptable_sender|body|boolean|false|Exempts messages from this sender from Spam, Spoof and Bulk dispositions only; Malicious and Suspicious dispositions still apply.|
|» is_exempt_recipient|body|boolean|false|Bypasses all detections for messages to this recipient.|
|» is_recipient|body|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated as of July 1, 2025. Use `is_exempt_recipient` instead. End of life: July 1, 2026.|
|» is_regex|body|boolean|false|none|
|» is_sender|body|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated as of July 1, 2025. Use `is_trusted_sender` instead. End of life: July 1, 2026.|
|» is_spoof|body|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated as of July 1, 2025. Use `is_acceptable_sender` instead. End of life: July 1, 2026.|
|» is_trusted_sender|body|boolean|false|Bypasses all detections and link following for messages from this sender.|
|» pattern|body|string|false|The pattern value to match. The format depends on `pattern_type`: a valid email address for EMAIL (e.g. `user@example.com`), a valid domain name for DOMAIN (e.g. `example.com`), or a plain IPv4 or IPv6 address or CIDR block for IP (e.g. `1.2.3.4`, `1.2.3.0/24`, `2606:4700:4700::1111`, or `2606:4700:4700::/48`); the API rejects private or unique-local, loopback, link-local, unspecified, and IPv4 broadcast addresses, including their IPv4-mapped IPv6 equivalents.|
|» pattern_type|body|[email-security_PatternType](#schemaemail-security_patterntype)|false|Type of pattern matching.<br>- EMAIL: matches a full email address (e.g. `user@example.com`)<br>- DOMAIN: matches a domain name (e.g. `example.com`)<br>- IP: matches a plain IPv4 or IPv6 address (e.g. `1.2.3.4` or `2606:4700:4700::1111`) or CIDR block (e.g. `1.2.3.0/24` or `2606:4700:4700::/48`). The API rejects private or unique-local, loopback, link-local, unspecified, and IPv4 broadcast addresses, including their IPv4-mapped IPv6 equivalents.<br>- UNKNOWN: deprecated; you cannot use this when creating or updating policies, but it may appear on existing entries.<br>|
|» verify_sender|body|boolean|false|Enforce DMARC, SPF or DKIM authentication. When on, Email Security only honors policies that pass authentication.|

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/email-security/settings/block_senders`

|pattern_type|query|object|false|Filter by pattern type.|

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/email-security/settings/block_senders`

<a id="opIdemail_security_batch_blocked_senders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "deletes": [
      {
        "id": "f174e90a-fafe-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415"
      }
    ],
    "patches": [
      {
        "comments": "Block sender with email test@example.com",
        "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "is_regex": false,
        "pattern": "test@example.com",
        "pattern_type": "EMAIL",
        "id": {}
      }
    ],
    "posts": [

        "comments": "Block sender with email test@example.com",
        "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "is_regex": false,
        "pattern": "test@example.com",
        "pattern_type": "EMAIL"
      }
    ],
    "puts": [
      {
        "comments": "Block sender with email test@example.com",
        "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "is_regex": false,
        "pattern": "test@example.com",
        "pattern_type": "EMAIL",
        "id": {}
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/email-security/settings/block_senders/batch`

Executes multiple blocked sender operations atomically: delete, partially update,
replace, and create blocked sender patterns in a single request. All four operation
arrays (deletes, patches, puts, posts) are required and executed in order.
Send empty arrays for unused operations.


> Body parameter

```json

  "deletes": [
    {
      "id": "f174e90a-fafe-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415"

      "is_regex": false,
      "pattern": "test@example.com",
      "pattern_type": "EMAIL",
      "id": {}

  ],
  "posts": [
    {
      "comments": "Block sender with email test@example.com",
      "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "is_regex": false,
      "pattern": "test@example.com",
      "pattern_type": "EMAIL"
    }
  ],
  "puts": [

}
```

## Replace a blocked email sender

<a id="opIdemail_security_replace_blocked_sender"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/email-security/settings/block_senders/f174e90a-fafe-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "comments": "Block sender with email test@example.com",
    "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "is_regex": false,
    "pattern": "test@example.com",
    "pattern_type": "EMAIL"
  }'
```

`PUT /accounts/{account_id}/email-security/settings/block_senders/{pattern_id}`

Replaces an existing blocked sender pattern in full. Unlike PATCH, every field is taken from the request body, so optional fields that are omitted are reset rather than left untouched. Use this when managing blocked senders declaratively.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comments": "Block sender with email test@example.com",
  "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "is_regex": false,
  "pattern": "test@example.com",
  "pattern_type": "EMAIL"
}
```

<h3 id="replace-a-blocked-email-sender-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[email-security_identifier](#schemaemail-security_identifier)|true|Account identifier tag.|
|pattern_id|path|[email-security_BlockedSenderId](#schemaemail-security_blockedsenderid)|true|none|
|body|body|[email-security_CreateBlockedSender](#schemaemail-security_createblockedsender)|true|none|
|» comments|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» expires_at|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|Timestamp at which the pattern expires. After this time, Email Security ignores the pattern. The value must lie in the future. Send `null` to clear the expiration.|
|» is_regex|body|boolean|true|Whether `pattern` is a regular expression instead of a literal value.|
|» pattern|body|string|true|The pattern value to match. The format depends on `pattern_type`: a valid email address for EMAIL (e.g. `user@example.com`), a valid domain name for DOMAIN (e.g. `example.com`), or a plain IPv4 or IPv6 address or CIDR block for IP (e.g. `1.2.3.4`, `1.2.3.0/24`, `2606:4700:4700::1111`, or `2606:4700:4700::/48`); the API rejects private or unique-local, loopback, link-local, unspecified, and IPv4 broadcast addresses, including their IPv4-mapped IPv6 equivalents.|
|» pattern_type|body|[email-security_PatternType](#schemaemail-security_patterntype)|true|Type of pattern matching.<br>- EMAIL: matches a full email address (e.g. `user@example.com`)<br>- DOMAIN: matches a domain name (e.g. `example.com`)<br>- IP: matches a plain IPv4 or IPv6 address (e.g. `1.2.3.4` or `2606:4700:4700::1111`) or CIDR block (e.g. `1.2.3.0/24` or `2606:4700:4700::/48`). The API rejects private or unique-local, loopback, link-local, unspecified, and IPv4 broadcast addresses, including their IPv4-mapped IPv6 equivalents.<br>- UNKNOWN: deprecated; you cannot use this when creating or updating policies, but it may appear on existing entries.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/email-security/settings/content_policies`

|direction|query|string|false|The sorting direction.|
|enabled|query|boolean|false|Filter by enabled status.|
|name|query|string|false|Filter by exact policy name.|
|expired|query|boolean|false|Filter to return only expired policies (`true`) or only policies that still apply (`false`). Omit to return both.|

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/email-security/settings/content_policies/batch`

Executes multiple content policy operations atomically: delete, partially update,
replace, and create content policies in a single request. All four operation arrays
(deletes, patches, puts, posts) are required and executed in order.
Send empty arrays for unused operations.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "deletes": [
    {
      "id": "f174e90a-fafe-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415"
    }
  ],
  "patches": [
    {
      "enabled": true,
      "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "name": "Block phishing keywords",
      "notes": "Blocks common phishing subject lines",
      "pattern": "urgent.*verify.*account",
      "targets": [
        "SUBJECT"
      ],
      "id": {}
    }
  ],
  "posts": [
    {
      "enabled": true,
      "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "name": "Block phishing keywords",
      "notes": "Blocks common phishing subject lines",
      "pattern": "urgent.*verify.*account",
      "targets": [
        "SUBJECT"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "puts": [
    {
      "enabled": true,
      "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "name": "Block phishing keywords",
      "notes": "Blocks common phishing subject lines",
      "pattern": "urgent.*verify.*account",
      "targets": [
        "SUBJECT"
      ],
      "id": {}
    }
  ]
}
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/email-security/settings/domains/batch`

Executes multiple domain operations in a single request. All four operation arrays
(deletes, patches, puts, posts) are required and executed in order.
Send empty arrays for unused operations.

## Get an email domain

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/email-security/settings/domains/{domain_id}`

Retrieves detailed information for a specific protected email domain including its delivery configuration, SPF/DMARC status, and authorization state.

<h3 id="get-an-email-domain-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|domain_id|path|[email-security_DomainId](#schemaemail-security_domainid)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/email-security/settings/impersonation_registry`

Returns a paginated list of protected identities in the impersonation registry. These entries define identities and email addresses to protect from impersonation attacks. Can be manually added or automatically synced from directory integrations.

|search|query|string|false|Search term for filtering records. Behavior may change.|
|order|query|string|false|Field to sort by.|
|direction|query|string|false|The sorting direction.|
|provenance|query|[email-security_Provenance](#schemaemail-security_provenance)|false|none|

## List trusted email domains

<a id="opIdemail_security_list_trusted_domains"></a>

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/email-security/settings/trusted_domains`

Returns a paginated list of trusted domain patterns. Trusted domains prevent false positives for recently registered domains and lookalike domain detections. Patterns can use regular expressions for flexible matching.

<h3 id="list-trusted-email-domains-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|search|query|string|false|Search term for filtering records. Behavior may change.|
|order|query|string|false|Field to sort by.|
|direction|query|string|false|The sorting direction.|
|is_recent|query|boolean|false|Filter to show only recently registered domains that are trusted to prevent triggering Suspicious or Malicious dispositions.|
|is_similarity|query|boolean|false|Filter to show only proximity domains (partner or approved domains with similar spelling to connected domains) that prevent Spoof dispositions.|
|pattern|query|string|false|none|
|account_id|path|[email-security_identifier](#schemaemail-security_identifier)|true|Account identifier tag.|

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/email-security/settings/trusted_domains`

Creates a new trusted domain pattern. Use for partner domains or approved senders that should bypass recent domain registration and similarity checks. Configure whether it prevents recent domain or spoof dispositions.

```json
  "comments": "Trusted partner domain",

  "is_regex": false,
  "is_similarity": false,
  "pattern": "example.com"
```

## Batch trusted domain operations

<a id="opIdemail_security_batch_trusted_domains"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/email-security/settings/trusted_domains/batch \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "deletes": [
      {
        "id": "f174e90a-fafe-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415"
      }
    ],
    "patches": [
      {
        "comments": "Trusted partner domain",
        "is_recent": true,
        "is_regex": false,
        "is_similarity": false,
        "pattern": "example.com",
        "id": {}
      }
    ],
    "posts": [
      {
        "comments": "Trusted partner domain",
        "is_recent": true,
        "is_regex": false,
        "is_similarity": false,
        "pattern": "example.com"
      }
    ],
    "puts": [
      {
        "comments": "Trusted partner domain",
        "is_recent": true,
        "is_regex": false,
        "is_similarity": false,
        "pattern": "example.com",
        "id": {}
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/email-security/settings/trusted_domains/batch`

Executes multiple trusted domain operations atomically: delete, partially update,
replace, and create trusted domain patterns in a single request. All four operation
arrays (deletes, patches, puts, posts) are required and executed in order.
Send empty arrays for unused operations.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "deletes": [
    {
      "id": "f174e90a-fafe-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415"
    }
  ],
  "patches": [
    {
      "comments": "Trusted partner domain",
      "is_recent": true,
      "is_regex": false,
      "is_similarity": false,
      "pattern": "example.com",
      "id": {}
    }
  ],
  "posts": [
    {
      "comments": "Trusted partner domain",
      "is_recent": true,
      "is_regex": false,
      "is_similarity": false,
      "pattern": "example.com"
    }
  ],
  "puts": [
    {
      "comments": "Trusted partner domain",
      "is_recent": true,
      "is_regex": false,
      "is_similarity": false,
      "pattern": "example.com",
      "id": {}
    }
  ]
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|account_id|path|[email-security_identifier](#schemaemail-security_identifier)|true|Account identifier tag.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» deletes|body|[object]|true|IDs of the trusted domain patterns to delete.|
|» » id|body|[email-security_TrustedDomainId](#schemaemail-security_trusteddomainid)|true|Trusted domain identifier.|

```bash
  }'
```

`PUT /accounts/{account_id}/email-security/settings/trusted_domains/{trusted_domain_id}`

Replaces an existing trusted domain in full. Unlike PATCH, every field is taken from the request body, so optional fields that are omitted are reset rather than left untouched. Use this when managing trusted domains declaratively.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comments": "Trusted partner domain",
  "is_recent": true,
  "is_regex": false,
  "is_similarity": false,
  "pattern": "example.com"

      }
```
```json
    ]
```
```bash
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/email-security/settings/url_ignore_patterns/batch`

Executes multiple operations atomically. All four operation arrays
(deletes, patches, puts, posts) are required and executed in order.
Send empty arrays for unused operations.

```json
      "comments": "Trusted internal redirect service",

    }
  ],

      "pattern": "https://example\\.com/.*",
      "id": {}
    }
  ]
}
```

## Create an Email Domain

<a id="opIdemail-domains-create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/email/domains \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "client_reference": "customer-42-enrollment-1",
    "hostname": "agents.customer.com"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/email/domains`

Creates a candidate and four DNS instructions. Rejects hostnames whose assigned Return-Path exceeds 201 ASCII characters. Creation follows read-only checks of the saved provider bundle and published exclusion. Hostnames inside an active full Cloudflare DNS zone return the generic hostname conflict error 2083. No per-domain provider DNS writes occur. Customer DNS observations remain pending and mail remains inactive. Unverified candidates may share a hostname. Supply an account-unique client_reference to retry the same enrollment safely; reuse with a different hostname returns error 2083. Final public-DNS, namespace protection and runtime readiness are separate gates. Available only to the configured OpenAI pilot account behind a default-off gate. Authentication failures may use the gateway error envelope.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_reference": "customer-42-enrollment-1",
  "hostname": "agents.customer.com"
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-email-domain-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[email_identifier](#schemaemail_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[email_email_domain_create](#schemaemail_email_domain_create)|true|none|
|» client_reference|body|string|false|Opaque reference for one customer enrollment. Reuse it with the same hostname to retry Create safely. Distinct references can enroll the same unverified hostname; a hostname alone never identifies a customer.|
|» hostname|body|string|true|Exact external hostname to enroll. After ASCII conversion, the assigned Return-Path hostname must be at most 201 characters (191 for the current cf-bounce. prefix). Wildcards, provider-zone names, and hostnames inside an existing Cloudflare-managed DNS zone are rejected.|

`DELETE /accounts/{account_id}/email/domains/{email_domain_id}`

Requires an empty body. Unclaimed unpublished candidates are purged immediately. Claimed domains persist deleting state and retain claims until the deletion worker acknowledges safe revocation and token retirement. Repeated requests while deleting are idempotent. Available only to the configured OpenAI pilot account behind a default-off gate. Authentication failures may use the gateway error envelope.

## Verify an Email Domain

<a id="opIdemail-domains-verify"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/email/domains/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/verify \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/email/domains/{email_domain_id}/verify`

Requires an empty body. Schedules an expedited check and coalesces queued or leased work. It does not accept verification results, bypass activation gates, or perform customer DNS checks synchronously. Follow the Location header after Retry-After seconds until verification.observed_at appears or advances beyond the value in this 202 response; status may remain unchanged. Candidate expiry returns 404. Available only to the configured OpenAI pilot account behind a default-off gate. Authentication failures may use the gateway error envelope.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[email_identifier](#schemaemail_identifier)|true|none|
|email_domain_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|

## Create routing rule

<a id="opIdemail-routing-routing-rules-create-routing-rule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/email/routing/rules \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "actions": [
      {
        "type": "forward",
        "value": [
          "destinationaddress@example.net"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "enabled": true,
    "matchers": [
      {
        "field": "to",
        "type": "literal",
        "value": "test@example.com"
      }
    ],
    "name": "Send to user@example.net rule.",
    "owner_worker_tag": "a7e6fb77503c41d8a7f3113c6918f10c",
    "priority": 0,
    "source": "api"
  }'
```

`POST /zones/{zone_id}/email/routing/rules`

Rules consist of a set of criteria for matching emails (such as an email being sent to a specific custom email address) plus a set of actions to take on the email (like forwarding it to a specific destination address). Forward actions require exactly one verified destination address.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "actions": [
    {
      "type": "forward",
      "value": [
        "destinationaddress@example.net"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "enabled": true,
  "matchers": [
    {
      "field": "to",
      "type": "literal",
      "value": "test@example.com"
    }
  ],
  "name": "Send to user@example.net rule.",
  "owner_worker_tag": "a7e6fb77503c41d8a7f3113c6918f10c",
  "priority": 0,
  "source": "api"
}
```

<h3 id="create-routing-rule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[email_identifier](#schemaemail_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[email_create_rule_properties](#schemaemail_create_rule_properties)|true|none|
|» actions|body|[email_rule_actions](#schemaemail_rule_actions)|true|List actions patterns.|
|» enabled|body|[email_rule_enabled](#schemaemail_rule_enabled)|false|Routing rule status.|
|» matchers|body|[email_rule_matchers](#schemaemail_rule_matchers)|true|Matching patterns to forward to your actions.|
|» name|body|[email_rule_name](#schemaemail_rule_name)|false|Routing rule name.|
|» owner_worker_tag|body|[email_rule_owner_worker_tag](#schemaemail_rule_owner_worker_tag)|false|Public tag (script_tag) of the Worker that owns this rule. Required when<br>`source` is `wrangler`.<br>|
|» priority|body|[email_rule_priority](#schemaemail_rule_priority)|false|Priority of the routing rule.|
|» source|body|[email_rule_source](#schemaemail_rule_source)|false|Who manages the rule. `api` covers dashboard, generic API, and Terraform;<br>`wrangler` means the rule is managed by a Worker's wrangler.jsonc. Defaults<br>to `api` when omitted on write.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» enabled|true|
|» enabled|false|
|» source|api|
|» source|wrangler|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "actions": [
      {
        "type": "forward",
        "value": [
          "destinationaddress@example.net"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "enabled": true,
    "id": "a7e6fb77503c41d8a7f3113c6918f10c",
    "matchers": [
      {
        "field": "to",
        "type": "literal",
        "value": "test@example.com"
      }
    ],
    "name": "Send to user@example.net rule.",
    "priority": 0,
    "source": "api",
    "tag": "a7e6fb77503c41d8a7f3113c6918f10c"
  }
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Create routing rule response|[email_rule_response_single](#schemaemail_rule_response_single)|
|400|Bad Request|Error 2054: Destination address is not verified. A forward action destination address must be verified before it can be used in a rule.|None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Error 2007: Invalid Input. Forward actions must contain exactly one destination address.|None|

`PUT /zones/{zone_id}/email/routing/rules/{rule_identifier}`

Update actions and matches, or enable/disable specific routing rules. Forward actions require exactly one verified destination address.

```json
    {

      "type": "literal",
      "value": "test@example.com"
    }
  ],
  "name": "Send to user@example.net rule.",
  "owner_worker_tag": "a7e6fb77503c41d8a7f3113c6918f10c",
  "priority": 0,
  "source": "api"
}
```

## Get sending limits

<a id="opIdemail-sending-get-sending-limits"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/email/sending/limits \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/email/sending/limits`

Returns the current daily sending quota for the account and, when a quota is resolved, the account's current usage against it. Quota is null when not yet available; usage is null when there is no resolved quota or usage is temporarily unavailable.

<h3 id="get-sending-limits-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[email_identifier](#schemaemail_identifier)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "quota": {
      "unit": "day",
      "value": 1000
    },
    "usage": {
      "over_quota": false,
      "resets_at": "2026-07-08T00:00:00Z",
      "sent": 42
    }
  }
}
```

## Send an email

<a id="opIdemail-sending-account-send-builder"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/email/sending/send \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "attachments": [
      {
        "content": "JVBERi0xLjQK...",
        "disposition": "attachment",
        "filename": "report.pdf",
        "type": "application/pdf"
      }
    ],
    "from": "sender@example.com",
    "html": "<h1>Hello</h1><p>Please find your report attached.</p>",
    "subject": "Monthly Report",
    "text": "Hello\n\nPlease find your report attached.",
    "to": [
      "recipient@example.com"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/email/sending/send`

Send an email for the specified account using the structured builder. Provide the sender, recipients, subject, and at least one of text or html; attachments are optional.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "attachments": [
    {
      "content": "JVBERi0xLjQK...",
      "disposition": "attachment",
      "filename": "report.pdf",
      "type": "application/pdf"
    }
  ],
  "from": "sender@example.com",
  "html": "<h1>Hello</h1><p>Please find your report attached.</p>",
  "subject": "Monthly Report",
  "text": "Hello\n\nPlease find your report attached.",
  "to": [
    "recipient@example.com"
  ]
}
```

## Send a raw MIME email

<a id="opIdemail-sending-account-send-raw-message"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/email/sending/send_raw \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "from": "sender@example.com",
    "mime_message": "From: sender@example.com\r\nTo: recipient@example.com\r\nSubject: Hello\r\nContent-Type: text/plain\r\n\r\nHello, World!",
    "recipients": [
      "recipient@example.com"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/email/sending/send_raw`

Send a raw RFC 5322 (MIME) email for the specified account. Provide the full MIME message plus the SMTP envelope (from and recipients).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "from": "sender@example.com",
  "mime_message": "From: sender@example.com\r\nTo: recipient@example.com\r\nSubject: Hello\r\nContent-Type: text/plain\r\n\r\nHello, World!",
  "recipients": [
    "recipient@example.com"
  ]
}
```

|» from|body|string|true|Sender email address.|
|» mime_message|body|string|true|The full MIME-encoded email message. Should include standard RFC 5322 headers such as From, To, Subject, and Content-Type. The from and recipients fields in the request body control SMTP envelope routing; the From and To headers in the MIME message control what the recipient's email client displays.|
|» recipients|body|[string]|true|List of recipient email addresses.|

## Create account Email Sending suppression

<a id="opIdpost_publicCreateSendingSuppression"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/12345678/email/sending/suppressions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

      "type": "sending_domain",
      "value": "mail.example.com"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/email/sending/suppressions`

Creates a suppression for every sending domain of the account (default) or for one sending domain (`scope.type = sending_domain`). Creating an existing active suppression returns its identifier. If a mutable legacy zone-linked account row already exists, it is promoted without changing its identifier.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "note": "Imported from CRM",
  "scope": {
    "type": "sending_domain",
    "value": "mail.example.com"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-account-email-sending-suppression-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» email|body|string(email)|true|The email address to suppress.|
|» expires_at|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|Expiration timestamp for the suppression. Omit or set to null for a permanent suppression that never expires.|
|» note|body|string|false|Advisory note for this suppression. Not enforced or validated beyond length.|
|» scope|body|object|false|Where the suppression applies. Omit for `{ "type": "account" }`, which blocks the recipient for every sending domain of the account.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » type|body|string|true|Blocks the recipient for every sending domain of the account.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » type|body|string|true|Blocks the recipient only for mail whose envelope MAIL FROM uses `value`.|
|» » value|body|string|true|The sending domain to suppress for: the domain part of the envelope MAIL FROM. It is lowercased and trailing dots are removed. Internationalized domains must use the ASCII (punycode) form. Ownership is not checked; a domain the account does not send from never matches.|

#### Enumerated Values

|» » type|sending_domain|

## Bulk import account Email Sending suppressions

<a id="opIdpost_publicBulkCreateSendingSuppressions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/12345678/email/sending/suppressions/bulk \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "items": [
      {
        "email": "user@example.com"
      },
      {
        "email": "other@example.com",
        "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "note": "Imported from CRM",
        "scope": {
          "type": "sending_domain",
          "value": "mail.example.com"
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/email/sending/suppressions/bulk`

Imports up to 1,000 Email Sending suppressions in one request. Each item applies to every sending domain of the account (default) or to one sending domain.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "email": "user@example.com"
    },
    {
      "email": "other@example.com",
      "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "note": "Imported from CRM",
      "scope": {
        "type": "sending_domain",
        "value": "mail.example.com"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-import-account-email-sending-suppressions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» items|body|[object]|true|Suppressions to import. Items with the same email address and scope are deduplicated before processing.|
|» » email|body|string|true|The email address to suppress.|
|» » expires_at|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|Expiration timestamp for the suppression. Omit or set to null for a permanent suppression that never expires.|
|» » note|body|string|false|Advisory note for this suppression. Not enforced or validated beyond length.|
|» » scope|body|object|false|Where the suppression applies. Omit for `{ "type": "account" }`, which blocks the recipient for every sending domain of the account.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » » type|body|string|true|Blocks the recipient for every sending domain of the account.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » » type|body|string|true|Blocks the recipient only for mail whose envelope MAIL FROM uses `value`.|
|» » » value|body|string|true|The sending domain to suppress for: the domain part of the envelope MAIL FROM. It is lowercased and trailing dots are removed. Internationalized domains must use the ASCII (punycode) form. Ownership is not checked; a domain the account does not send from never matches.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » » type|account|
|» » » type|sending_domain|

> 200 Response

```json

  "errors": [
    {}
  ],
  "messages": [
    {}
  ],
  "result": {
    "deduplicated": 1,
    "errors": 0,
    "invalid": 1,
    "items": [
      {
        "email": "user@example.com",
        "error": "Invalid email",
        "id": "396a5436-d4b0-42a6-b3fc-48e8fa522321",
        "index": 0,
        "scope": {
          "type": "sending_domain",
          "value": "mail.example.com"
        },
        "status": "processed"
      }
    ],
    "processed": 2,
    "skipped": 0,
    "total": 4
  },
  "success": true
}
```

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "invalid_scope_value",
      "message": "Suppression not found"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [
    {}
  ],
  "result": {},
  "success": false
}
```
