## Update account Email Sending suppression

<a id="opIdpatch_publicUpdateSendingSuppression"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/12345678/email/sending/suppressions/396a5436-d4b0-42a6-b3fc-48e8fa522321 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "note": "Customer re-confirmed opt-in",
    "scope": {
      "type": "account"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /accounts/{account_id}/email/sending/suppressions/{suppression_id}`

Updates expiry or advisory note fields without changing legacy internal zone memberships. Scope cannot be changed.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "note": "Customer re-confirmed opt-in",
  "scope": {
    "type": "account"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-account-email-sending-suppression-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|none|
|suppression_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» expires_at|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|New expiry. Send `null` to make the suppression permanent; omit to leave it unchanged.|
|» note|body|string|false|Replacement advisory note. Send an empty string to clear it; omit to leave it unchanged.|
|» scope|body|object|false|Not editable. Scope is fixed when the suppression is created; any value returns 400 with code `scope_immutable`. Delete and recreate the suppression to change it.|

```json
  "errors": [
    {}
  ],
  "messages": [
    {}
  ],
  "result": {
    "created_at": "2026-01-02T02:20:00Z",

    "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "id": "396a5436-d4b0-42a6-b3fc-48e8fa522321",
    "note": "Imported from CRM",
    "read_only": false,
    "reason": "hard_bounce",
    "scope": {
      "type": "sending_domain",
      "value": "mail.example.com"
    }
  },
  "success": true
}
```

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "invalid_scope_value",
      "message": "Suppression not found"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [
```

```bash
        "suffix": ".jpeg"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /accounts/{account_id}/event_notifications/r2/{bucket_name}/configuration/queues/{queue_id}`

Creates rules that send notifications for matching R2 object events to the specified Cloudflare Queue. Rules can filter objects by key prefix and suffix. New rules are added to any existing rules for the queue; a rule that overlaps an existing rule is rejected.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "rules": [
    {
      "actions": [
        "PutObject",
        "CopyObject"
      ],
      "description": "Notifications from source bucket to queue",
      "prefix": "img/",
      "suffix": ".jpeg"
    }
  ]
}
```

|cf-r2-jurisdiction|header|string|false|Jurisdiction where objects in this bucket are guaranteed to be stored.|

## Create Bucket (by name)

<a id="opIdr2-create-bucket-by-name"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/r2/buckets/example-bucket \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`PUT /accounts/{account_id}/r2/buckets/{bucket_name}`

Creates a new R2 bucket using the name from the URL path. Similar to `r2-create-bucket` (POST), but the bucket name comes from the path and the optional storage class is supplied via the `cf-r2-storage-class` header. There is no request body. Unlike the POST variant, this endpoint does not accept a location hint — the bucket is placed in the R2 region for the caller's edge colo. Use the POST variant if you need to set a `locationHint`.

## Create Bucket Job

<a id="opIdr2-create-bucket-job"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/r2/buckets/example-bucket/jobs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "jobType": "prefixDelete",
    "prefix": "logs/2026/"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/r2/buckets/{bucket_name}/jobs`

Creates a background job for an R2 bucket. The `jobType` field selects the job:

- **`prefixDelete`**: deletes every object whose key begins with `prefix`. A non-empty
  prefix must end in `/`. An empty prefix (`""`) empties the entire bucket.
- **`storageClassMigration`**: migrates every object in the bucket between storage
  classes. `sourceStorageClass` and `destinationStorageClass` must be provided together
  and must differ; omitting both migrates from `InfrequentAccess` to `Standard`.

Poll the returned `id` with the Get Bucket Job endpoint. Small prefix-delete jobs can
finish synchronously and return `COMPLETED`. Objects uploaded after a background job
starts are not affected by that job.

For prefix-delete jobs: abort active multipart uploads before submitting the request,
since a synchronously completed job does not abort them, and avoid writing objects or
starting multipart uploads while a bucket-emptying job is in progress. Each request
creates a distinct job, and the number of active prefix-delete jobs is limited per
bucket; wait for an existing job to finish before retrying a request rejected with
HTTP 429. A bucket cannot be emptied while event notifications are configured (HTTP 409
/ error code 10083). To protect a bucket with R2 Data Catalog enabled, send the
`cf-r2-data-catalog-check` header; a conflict is returned with HTTP 409 / error code
10081.

Prefix-delete jobs require permission to delete objects; storage-class migration jobs
require permission to write to the bucket.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "jobType": "prefixDelete",
  "prefix": "logs/2026/"
}
```

<h3 id="create-bucket-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[r2_account_identifier](#schemar2_account_identifier)|true|none|
|bucket_name|path|[r2_bucket_name](#schemar2_bucket_name)|true|none|
|cf-r2-jurisdiction|header|string|false|Jurisdiction where objects in this bucket are guaranteed to be stored.|
|cf-r2-data-catalog-check|header|string|false|For prefix-delete jobs, set this header to reject the request when R2 Data Catalog is enabled for the bucket.|
|body|body|[r2_create_prefix_delete_job_request](#schemar2_create_prefix_delete_job_request) \| [r2_create_storage_class_migration_job_request](#schemar2_create_storage_class_migration_job_request)|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[r2_create_prefix_delete_job_request](#schemar2_create_prefix_delete_job_request)|false|Request body that creates a prefix-delete job.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[r2_create_storage_class_migration_job_request](#schemar2_create_storage_class_migration_job_request)|false|Request body that creates a storage-class migration job.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|cf-r2-jurisdiction|default|
|cf-r2-jurisdiction|eu|
|cf-r2-jurisdiction|us|
|cf-r2-jurisdiction|fedramp|
|cf-r2-jurisdiction|fedramp-high|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "result": {
    "endTime": "2026-07-20T12:00:00Z",
    "id": "69f94626-a3fe-47bc-9615-e791b4d53c53",
    "jobType": "prefixDelete",
    "prefixDelete": {
      "deletedObjects": 0,
      "isBucketClear": true,
      "prefix": ""
    },
    "startTime": "2026-07-20T12:00:00Z",
    "status": "COMPLETED"
  },
  "success": true
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 10083,
      "message": "Remove all event notification rules from bucket (example-bucket) before emptying it (account 023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353)."
    }
  ],
  "messages": [
    "Request failed."
  ],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 10058,
      "message": "Too many concurrent prefix delete jobs for this bucket. Please wait for existing jobs to complete."
    }
  ],
  "messages": [
    "Request failed."
  ],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 1000,
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [
    "string"
  ],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|200|OK|The created job.|Inline|
|409|Conflict|Prefix-delete conflict. Event notification rules are still configured (error code<br>10083), or the Data Catalog check was requested and R2 Data Catalog is enabled for<br>the bucket (error code 10081). Remove the conflicting configuration before retrying.<br>|[r2_v4_response_failure](#schemar2_v4_response_failure)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many active prefix-delete or bucket-emptying jobs. Wait for an existing job to finish, then retry.|[r2_v4_response_failure](#schemar2_v4_response_failure)|
|4XX|Client Error|Create Bucket Job response failure. The request body may be invalid, the bucket may not exist, or the caller may not be authorized.|[r2_v4_response_failure](#schemar2_v4_response_failure)|

## Get Bucket Job

<a id="opIdr2-get-bucket-job"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/r2/buckets/example-bucket/jobs/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/r2/buckets/{bucket_name}/jobs/{job_id}`

Gets the current status of a background job of any type for an R2 bucket. Poll this
endpoint with the job identifier returned by Create Bucket Job until the status is
`COMPLETED`, `FAILED`, or `CANCELLED`.


<h3 id="get-bucket-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[r2_account_identifier](#schemar2_account_identifier)|true|none|

`PUT /accounts/{account_id}/r2/buckets/{bucket_name}/lifecycle`

Replaces the object lifecycle rules for an R2 bucket. Rules match object-key prefixes and can expire objects, abort incomplete multipart uploads, or transition objects to Infrequent Access storage.

```json
    {
      "abortMultipartUploadsTransition": {

          "type": "Age"
        }

      },

        "condition": {

          "type": "Age"
        }

      "storageClassTransitions": [
        {
          "condition": {
            "maxAge": 0,
            "type": "Age"
          },
          "storageClass": "InfrequentAccess"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Enable Sippy

<a id="opIdr2-put-bucket-sippy-config"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/r2/buckets/example-bucket/sippy \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "destination": {
      "accessKeyId": "string",
      "provider": "r2",
      "secretAccessKey": "string"
    },
    "source": {
      "accessKeyId": "string",
      "bucket": "string",
      "provider": "aws",
      "region": "string",
      "secretAccessKey": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /accounts/{account_id}/r2/buckets/{bucket_name}/sippy`

Configures and enables Sippy on-demand migration for an R2 bucket. When a requested object is missing from R2, Sippy serves it from the configured source storage provider and copies it to R2.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "destination": {
    "accessKeyId": "string",
    "provider": "r2",
    "secretAccessKey": "string"
  },
  "source": {
    "accessKeyId": "string",
    "bucket": "string",
    "provider": "aws",
    "region": "string",
    "secretAccessKey": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="enable-sippy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[r2_account_identifier](#schemar2_account_identifier)|true|none|
|bucket_name|path|[r2_bucket_name](#schemar2_bucket_name)|true|none|
|cf-r2-jurisdiction|header|string|false|Jurisdiction where objects in this bucket are guaranteed to be stored.|
|body|body|[r2_enable_sippy_aws](#schemar2_enable_sippy_aws) \| [r2_enable_sippy_gcs](#schemar2_enable_sippy_gcs) \| [r2_enable_sippy_s3](#schemar2_enable_sippy_s3) \| [r2_enable_sippy_azure](#schemar2_enable_sippy_azure)|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[r2_enable_sippy_aws](#schemar2_enable_sippy_aws)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[r2_enable_sippy_gcs](#schemar2_enable_sippy_gcs)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[r2_enable_sippy_s3](#schemar2_enable_sippy_s3)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[r2_enable_sippy_azure](#schemar2_enable_sippy_azure)|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|cf-r2-jurisdiction|default|
|cf-r2-jurisdiction|eu|
|cf-r2-jurisdiction|us|
|cf-r2-jurisdiction|fedramp|
|cf-r2-jurisdiction|fedramp-high|

> Example responses

```json
    {
      "code": 1000,

    }
  ],

    "string"
  ],

    "destination": {
```

## Disable Sippy

<a id="opIdr2-delete-bucket-sippy-config"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/r2/buckets/example-bucket/sippy \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /accounts/{account_id}/r2/buckets/{bucket_name}/sippy`

Disables Sippy on-demand migration for an R2 bucket. Requests no longer fetch missing objects from the source storage provider. Objects already copied to R2 remain in the bucket.

<h3 id="disable-sippy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bucket_name|path|[r2_bucket_name](#schemar2_bucket_name)|true|none|
|account_id|path|[r2_account_identifier](#schemar2_account_identifier)|true|none|
|cf-r2-jurisdiction|header|string|false|Jurisdiction where objects in this bucket are guaranteed to be stored.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|cf-r2-jurisdiction|default|
|cf-r2-jurisdiction|eu|
|cf-r2-jurisdiction|us|
|cf-r2-jurisdiction|fedramp|
|cf-r2-jurisdiction|fedramp-high|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 1000,
      "message": "string"
```

## Create Temporary Access Credentials

<a id="opIdr2-create-temp-access-credentials"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/r2/temp-access-credentials \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "bucket": "example-bucket",
    "objects": [
      "example-object"
    ],
    "parentAccessKeyId": "example-access-key-id",
    "permission": "object-read-write",
    "prefixes": [
      "example-prefix/"
    ],
    "ttlSeconds": 3600
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/r2/temp-access-credentials`

Creates temporary access credentials on a bucket that can be optionally scoped to prefixes or objects.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "bucket": "example-bucket",
  "objects": [
    "example-object"
  ],
  "parentAccessKeyId": "example-access-key-id",
  "permission": "object-read-write",
  "prefixes": [
    "example-prefix/"
  ],
  "ttlSeconds": 3600
}
```

<h3 id="create-temporary-access-credentials-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[r2_account_identifier](#schemar2_account_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[r2_temp_access_creds_request](#schemar2_temp_access_creds_request)|true|none|
|» bucket|body|string|true|Name of the R2 bucket.|
|» objects|body|[string]|false|Optional object paths to scope the credentials to.|
|» parentAccessKeyId|body|string|true|Access key ID of the parent R2 API token. The temporary credentials cannot exceed this token's permissions.|
|» permission|body|string|true|Permissions allowed on the credentials.|
|» prefixes|body|[string]|false|Optional prefix paths to scope the credentials to.|
|» ttlSeconds|body|number|true|Lifetime of the temporary credentials in seconds, up to 604800 seconds (7 days).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» permission|admin-read-write|
|» permission|admin-read-only|
|» permission|object-read-write|
|» permission|object-read-only|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 1000,
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [
    "string"
  ],
  "result": {
    "accessKeyId": "example-access-key-id",
    "secretAccessKey": "example-secret-key",
    "sessionToken": "example-session-token"
  },
  "success": true
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 1000,
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [
    "string"
  ],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-temporary-access-credentials-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Create temporary access credentials response.|Inline|

## Set the payload logging key

<a id="opIdpayload-logging-keys-for-an-account-set-the-payload-logging-key"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/firewall/payload_logging/key \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \

  }'
```

`PUT /accounts/{account_id}/firewall/payload_logging/key`

Creates or replaces the public key that payload logging uses to encrypt matched payloads for the account. It applies to every zone in the account that has no zone key. Requires a plan that includes payload logging (Enterprise); otherwise it returns 403.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "public_key": "Ycig/Zr/pZmklmFUN99nr+taURlYItL91g+NcHGYpB8="
}
```

<h3 id="set-the-payload-logging-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[firewall_account_identifier](#schemafirewall_account_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[firewall_payload_logging_key](#schemafirewall_payload_logging_key)|true|none|
|» public_key|body|string|true|Defines the X25519 public key, as standard base64 of exactly 32 bytes, that encrypts matched payloads. Cloudflare stores only the public key; keep the private key to decrypt logged payloads.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "result": {
    "public_key": "Ycig/Zr/pZmklmFUN99nr+taURlYItL91g+NcHGYpB8="
  },
  "success": true
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
    }
```

## Create flag

<a id="opIdflagship_create_flag"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/flagship/apps/string/flags \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "default_variation": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "enabled": true,
    "key": "string",
    "metadata": {
      "property1": true,
      "property2": true
    },
    "rules": [
      {
        "conditions": [
          {
            "attribute": "string",
            "operator": "equals",
            "value": "string"
          }
        ],
        "priority": 1,
        "rollout": {
          "attribute": "string",
          "percentage": 0
        },
        "serve_variation": "string"
      }
    ],
    "type": "boolean",
    "variations": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/flagship/apps/{app_id}/flags`

Creates a flag. Returns 409 if the key already exists. `type` is always inferred from variation values; legacy request-side values are ignored. Optional `metadata` can be attached at creation.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "default_variation": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "enabled": true,
  "key": "string",
  "metadata": {
    "property1": true,
    "property2": true
  },
  "rules": [
    {
      "conditions": [
        {
          "attribute": "string",
          "operator": "equals",
          "value": "string"
        }
      ],
      "priority": 1,
      "rollout": {
        "attribute": "string",
        "percentage": 0
      },
      "serve_variation": "string"
    }
  ],
  "type": "boolean",
  "variations": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-flag-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|Cloudflare account ID that owns the Flagship app.|
|app_id|path|string|true|Flagship app ID returned when the app was created.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» default_variation|body|string|true|Variation the API serves when the flag is off, or when it's on but no rule matches the context. Must be a key in `variations`.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Optional operator-facing description. It does not affect flag evaluation.|
|» enabled|body|boolean|true|When false, the flag bypasses all rules and always serves `default_variation`.|
|» key|body|string|true|Unique identifier for the flag within an app. Used in all evaluation and SDK calls.|
|» metadata|body|object \| null|false|Key-value metadata associated with the flag. `null` or an empty object clears existing metadata; omission semantics depend on the endpoint (PUT clears it, PATCH preserves it).|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|boolean \| string \| number|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» rules|body|[[flagship_Rule](#schemaflagship_rule)]|true|Targeting rules evaluated in ascending `priority`; the first matching rule wins. An empty array means the flag always serves `default_variation`.|
|» type|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated compatibility field. Omit it; the API ignores this value and infers the type from the flag's variations.|

`PUT /accounts/{account_id}/flagship/apps/{app_id}/flags/{flag_key}`

Replaces the entire flag definition. Omitted fields are cleared, not preserved — read before writing. The path key identifies the flag and cannot be renamed by changing the body `key`. A changelog entry is appended when the flag content actually changes; identical updates are no-ops.

> Body parameter

```json
  "description": "string",
  "enabled": true,
  "key": "string",
  "metadata": {
    "property1": true,
    "property2": true
  },

      "conditions": [

        "percentage": 0
      },
      "serve_variation": "string"
    }
  ],
  "type": "boolean",
  "variations": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  }
}
```

`PATCH /accounts/{account_id}/flagship/apps/{app_id}/flags/{flag_key}`

Applies a partial update to lightweight flag fields: `enabled`, `description`, `metadata`, and `default_variation`. Only fields present in the request body are modified; omitted fields are preserved. `metadata: null` or an empty object clears metadata. `default_variation` must exist in the current `variations`. Structural changes to `variations` and `rules` use PUT. A changelog entry is appended when the flag content actually changes.

```json
  "default_variation": "string",
  "description": "string",
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/flagship/apps/{app_id}/flags/{flag_key}/changelog`

|flag_key|path|string|true|Case-sensitive key identifying the flag within the app.|

## Create Zero Trust certificate

<a id="opIdzero-trust-certificates-create-zero-trust-certificate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/699d98642c564d2e855e9661899b7252/gateway/certificates \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "validity_period_days": 1826
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/gateway/certificates`

```json
  "validity_period_days": 1826
}
```

|» validity_period_days|body|integer|false|Sets the certificate validity period in days (range: 1-10,950 days / ~30 years). ## List Zero Trust lists

<a id="opIdzero-trust-lists-list-zero-trust-lists"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/699d98642c564d2e855e9661899b7252/gateway/lists \
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/gateway/lists`

Fetch all Zero Trust lists for an account.

<h3 id="list-zero-trust-lists-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[zero-trust-gateway_identifier-2](#schemazero-trust-gateway_identifier-2)|true|none|
|type|query|[zero-trust-gateway_type-2](#schemazero-trust-gateway_type-2)|false|**Deprecated.**|
|filter|query|[string]|false|Filter the returned lists by one or more `field:value` pairs.<br>Repeat the parameter to apply multiple filters; they are combined with<br>logical AND (a list must satisfy every filter to be returned).<br><br>Supported fields and their matching behaviour:<br>  * `name` — case-insensitive substring match on the list name.<br>  * `id` — substring match on the list ID (UUID), with or without dashes.<br>  * `type` — exact match on the list type. Supersedes the legacy `type` query<br>    parameter when both are supplied. Must be one of the valid type values.<br>  * `item_count` — exact integer match on the number of items in the list.<br><br>Each entry must match one of the per-field patterns below: the field must be<br>one of `name`, `id`, `type`, or `item_count`; `name`/`id` accept any value,<br>`type` is restricted to the valid list type values, and `item_count` must be<br>a non-negative integer.|
|search|query|string|false|Case-insensitive substring match on the list name or description. When<br>combined with `filter`, both must match (logical AND).|
|order_by|query|string|false|Field to sort the returned lists by. When omitted, results are ordered by<br>`created_at` in ascending order (i.e. creation order) for backwards<br>compatibility. Supported values:<br>  * `name` — sort alphabetically by list name.<br>  * `created_at` — sort by creation time; defaults to descending unless `direction` is set.<br>  * `updated_at` — sort by last-modified time; defaults to descending unless `direction` is set.<br>  * `item_count` — sort by number of items in the list.|
|direction|query|string|false|Sort direction. Applies to the field named in `order_by`; when `order_by`<br>is omitted it applies to the default `created_at` ordering. When<br>`direction` is omitted the default is field-specific: explicitly choosing<br>`created_at` or `updated_at` defaults to descending (newest first); `name`<br>and `item_count` default to ascending; and the default `created_at`<br>ordering used when `order_by` is omitted is ascending (for backwards<br>compatibility).<br>  * `asc` — ascending.<br>  * `desc` — descending.|

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-zero-trust-gateway-locations">Zero Trust Gateway locations</h1>

## List Zero Trust Gateway locations

<a id="opIdzero-trust-gateway-locations-list-zero-trust-gateway-locations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/699d98642c564d2e855e9661899b7252/gateway/locations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/gateway/locations`

List Zero Trust Gateway locations for an account.

<h3 id="list-zero-trust-gateway-locations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[zero-trust-gateway_identifier-2](#schemazero-trust-gateway_identifier-2)|true|none|
|filter|query|[string]|false|Filter the returned locations by one or more `field:value` pairs.<br>Repeat the parameter to apply multiple filters; they are combined with<br>logical AND (a location must satisfy every filter to be returned).<br><br>Supported fields and their matching behaviour:<br>  * `name` — case-insensitive substring match on the location name.<br>  * `id` — substring match on the location ID (UUID), with or without dashes.<br>  * `is_default` — whether it is the default for the account.<br><br>Each entry must match one of the per-field patterns below:<br>  * the field must be one of `name`, `id`, or `is_default`;<br>  * `name`/`id` accept any value;<br>  * `is_default` only accepts `true` or `false`; any other value returns `400`|
|search|query|string|false|Case-insensitive substring match on the location name. When combined<br>with `filter`, both must match (logical AND).|
|order_by|query|string|false|Field to sort the returned locations by. When omitted, the order of<br>results is unspecified. |direction|query|string|false|Sort direction. Only takes effect when `order_by` is also provided; it<br>is ignored otherwise. When `direction` is omitted the effective<br>direction is field-specific: `created_at` and `updated_at` default to<br>descending (newest first); `name` defaults to ascending.<br>  * `asc` — ascending.<br>  * `desc` — descending.|

<a id="opIdzero-trust-gateway-pacfiles-create-pacfile"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/699d98642c564d2e855e9661899b7252/gateway/pacfiles \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

  }'
```

<h3 id="list-proxy-endpoints-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[zero-trust-gateway_identifier-2](#schemazero-trust-gateway_identifier-2)|true|none|
|filter|query|[string]|false|Filter the returned proxy endpoints by one or more `field:value` pairs.<br>Repeat the parameter to apply multiple filters; they are combined with<br>logical AND (an endpoint must satisfy every filter to be returned).<br><br>Supported fields and their matching behaviour:<br>  * `name` — case-insensitive substring match on the endpoint name.<br>  * `id` — substring match on the endpoint ID (UUID), with or without dashes.<br>  * `kind` — exact match on the endpoint kind. The value must be `ip` or `identity`; any other value returns `400`.<br><br>Each entry must match one of the per-field patterns below: the field<br>must be one of `name`, `id`, or `kind`; `name`/`id` accept any value,<br>while `kind` only accepts `ip` or `identity`.|
|search|query|string|false|Case-insensitive substring match on the endpoint name. When combined<br>with `filter`, both must match (logical AND).|
|order_by|query|string|false|Field to sort the returned endpoints by. When omitted, the order of<br>results is unspecified. Supported values:<br>  * `name` — sort alphabetically by endpoint name.<br>  * `created_at` — sort by creation time; defaults to descending unless `direction` is set.<br>  * `updated_at` — sort by last-modified time; defaults to descending unless `direction` is set.|
|direction|query|string|false|Sort direction. Only takes effect when `order_by` is also provided; it<br>is ignored otherwise. When `direction` is omitted the effective<br>direction is field-specific: `created_at` and `updated_at` default to<br>descending (newest first); `name` defaults to ascending.<br>  * `asc` — ascending.<br>  * `desc` — descending.|

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/gateway/rules`

List Zero Trust Gateway rules for an account.

<h3 id="list-zero-trust-gateway-rules-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[zero-trust-gateway_identifier-2](#schemazero-trust-gateway_identifier-2)|true|none|
|filter|query|[string]|false|Filter the returned rules by one or more `field:value` pairs. Repeat the<br>parameter to combine filters with logical AND.<br><br>Supported fields are `name`, `id`, `action`, `enabled`, `source_account`,<br>`is_shared`, `filters`, and `expression` (max 1024 bytes). The `source_account`<br>value is matched as a normalized UUID substring. The `filters` value must<br>be one of the rule filter names and matches a member of the rule's `filters`<br>array. The `expression` filter performs a case-insensitive literal<br>substring match across traffic, identity, and device posture expressions.|
|search|query|string|false|Case-insensitive substring search across rule name and description.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Field to sort the returned rules by. Supported values are `name`,<br>`created_at`, `updated_at`, and `precedence`.|
|direction|query|string|false|Sort direction. When `order_by` is omitted, this controls the direction<br>of the existing precedence ordering. Shared rules remain first in either<br>direction. Accepted values are `asc` and `desc`.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order_by|name|
|order_by|created_at|
|order_by|updated_at|
|order_by|precedence|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|

<h3 id="create-a-zero-trust-gateway-rule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[zero-trust-gateway_identifier-2](#schemazero-trust-gateway_identifier-2)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» action|body|[zero-trust-gateway_action](#schemazero-trust-gateway_action)|true|Specify the action to perform when the associated traffic, identity, and device posture expressions either absent or evaluate to `true`.|
|» description|body|[zero-trust-gateway_description-2](#schemazero-trust-gateway_description-2)|false|Specify the rule description.|
|» device_posture|body|[zero-trust-gateway_device_posture](#schemazero-trust-gateway_device_posture)|false|Specify the wirefilter expression used for device posture check. The API automatically formats and sanitizes expressions before storing them. To prevent Terraform state drift, use the formatted expression returned in the API response.|
|» enabled|body|[zero-trust-gateway_enabled](#schemazero-trust-gateway_enabled)|false|Specify whether the rule is enabled.|
|» expiration|body|[zero-trust-gateway_expiration](#schemazero-trust-gateway_expiration)|false|Defines the expiration time stamp and default duration of a DNS policy. Takes precedence over the policy's `schedule` configuration, if any. This  does not apply to HTTP or network policies. Settable only for `dns` rules.|
|» filters|body|[zero-trust-gateway_filters](#schemazero-trust-gateway_filters)|false|Specify the protocol or layer to evaluate the traffic, identity, and device posture expressions. Can only contain a single value.|
|» identity|body|[zero-trust-gateway_identity](#schemazero-trust-gateway_identity)|false|Specify the wirefilter expression used for identity matching. The API automatically formats and sanitizes expressions before storing them. To prevent Terraform state drift, use the formatted expression returned in the API response.|
|» name|body|[zero-trust-gateway_name-3](#schemazero-trust-gateway_name-3)|true|Specify the rule name.|
|» precedence|body|[zero-trust-gateway_precedence](#schemazero-trust-gateway_precedence)|false|Set the order of your rules. Lower values indicate higher precedence. At each processing phase, evaluate applicable rules in ascending order of this value. Refer to [Order of enforcement](http://developers.cloudflare.com/learning-paths/secure-internet-traffic/understand-policies/order-of-enforcement/#manage-precedence-with-terraform) to manage precedence via Terraform.|
|» rule_settings|body|[zero-trust-gateway_rule-settings](#schemazero-trust-gateway_rule-settings)|false|Defines settings for this rule. Settings apply only to specific rule types and must use compatible selectors. If Terraform detects drift, confirm the setting supports your rule type and check whether the API modifies the value. Use API-returned values in your configuration to prevent drift.|
|» schedule|body|[zero-trust-gateway_schedule](#schemazero-trust-gateway_schedule)|false|Defines the schedule for activating DNS policies. Settable only for `dns` and `dns_resolver` rules.|
|» traffic|body|[zero-trust-gateway_traffic](#schemazero-trust-gateway_traffic)|false|Specify the wirefilter expression used for traffic matching. The API automatically formats and sanitizes expressions before storing them. To prevent Terraform state drift, use the formatted expression returned in the API response.|

## Patch multiple Zero Trust Gateway rules

<a id="opIdzero-trust-gateway-rules-patch-multiple-zero-trust-gateway-rules"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/699d98642c564d2e855e9661899b7252/gateway/rules \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '[
    {
      "description": "Block bad websites based on their host name.",
      "enabled": true,
      "id": "f174e90a-fafe-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415",
      "name": "block bad websites",
      "precedence": 0
    }
  ]'
```

`PATCH /accounts/{account_id}/gateway/rules`

Update select fields of multiple Zero Trust Gateway rules in a single request. This is commonly used to reorder rules by updating their precedence values. Only the fields provided for each rule are updated.

> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "description": "Block bad websites based on their host name.",
    "enabled": true,
    "id": "f174e90a-fafe-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415",
    "name": "block bad websites",
    "precedence": 0
  }
]
```

<h3 id="patch-multiple-zero-trust-gateway-rules-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[zero-trust-gateway_identifier-2](#schemazero-trust-gateway_identifier-2)|true|none|
|body|body|[object]|true|none|
|» description|body|[zero-trust-gateway_description-2](#schemazero-trust-gateway_description-2)|false|Specify the rule description.|
|» enabled|body|[zero-trust-gateway_enabled](#schemazero-trust-gateway_enabled)|false|Specify whether the rule is enabled.|
|» id|body|[zero-trust-gateway_uuid-4](#schemazero-trust-gateway_uuid-4)|true|Identify the API resource with a UUID.|
|» name|body|[zero-trust-gateway_name-3](#schemazero-trust-gateway_name-3)|false|Specify the rule name.|
|» precedence|body|[zero-trust-gateway_precedence](#schemazero-trust-gateway_precedence)|false|Set the order of your rules. Lower values indicate higher precedence. At each processing phase, evaluate applicable rules in ascending order of this value. Refer to [Order of enforcement](http://developers.cloudflare.com/learning-paths/secure-internet-traffic/understand-policies/order-of-enforcement/#manage-precedence-with-terraform) to manage precedence via Terraform.|

<h3 id="update-a-zero-trust-gateway-rule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|rule_id|path|[zero-trust-gateway_uuid-4](#schemazero-trust-gateway_uuid-4)|true|none|
|account_id|path|[zero-trust-gateway_identifier-2](#schemazero-trust-gateway_identifier-2)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» action|body|[zero-trust-gateway_action](#schemazero-trust-gateway_action)|true|Specify the action to perform when the associated traffic, identity, and device posture expressions either absent or evaluate to `true`.|
|» description|body|[zero-trust-gateway_description-2](#schemazero-trust-gateway_description-2)|false|Specify the rule description.|
|» device_posture|body|[zero-trust-gateway_device_posture](#schemazero-trust-gateway_device_posture)|false|Specify the wirefilter expression used for device posture check. The API automatically formats and sanitizes expressions before storing them. To prevent Terraform state drift, use the formatted expression returned in the API response.|
|» enabled|body|[zero-trust-gateway_enabled](#schemazero-trust-gateway_enabled)|false|Specify whether the rule is enabled.|
|» expiration|body|[zero-trust-gateway_expiration](#schemazero-trust-gateway_expiration)|false|Defines the expiration time stamp and default duration of a DNS policy. Takes precedence over the policy's `schedule` configuration, if any. This  does not apply to HTTP or network policies. Settable only for `dns` rules.|
|» filters|body|[zero-trust-gateway_filters](#schemazero-trust-gateway_filters)|false|Specify the protocol or layer to evaluate the traffic, identity, and device posture expressions. Can only contain a single value.|
|» identity|body|[zero-trust-gateway_identity](#schemazero-trust-gateway_identity)|false|Specify the wirefilter expression used for identity matching. The API automatically formats and sanitizes expressions before storing them. To prevent Terraform state drift, use the formatted expression returned in the API response.|
|» name|body|[zero-trust-gateway_name-3](#schemazero-trust-gateway_name-3)|true|Specify the rule name.|
|» precedence|body|[zero-trust-gateway_precedence](#schemazero-trust-gateway_precedence)|false|Set the order of your rules. Lower values indicate higher precedence. At each processing phase, evaluate applicable rules in ascending order of this value. Refer to [Order of enforcement](http://developers.cloudflare.com/learning-paths/secure-internet-traffic/understand-policies/order-of-enforcement/#manage-precedence-with-terraform) to manage precedence via Terraform.|
|» rule_settings|body|[zero-trust-gateway_rule-settings](#schemazero-trust-gateway_rule-settings)|false|Defines settings for this rule. Settings apply only to specific rule types and must use compatible selectors. If Terraform detects drift, confirm the setting supports your rule type and check whether the API modifies the value. Use API-returned values in your configuration to prevent drift.|
|» schedule|body|[zero-trust-gateway_schedule](#schemazero-trust-gateway_schedule)|false|Defines the schedule for activating DNS policies. Settable only for `dns` and `dns_resolver` rules.|
|» traffic|body|[zero-trust-gateway_traffic](#schemazero-trust-gateway_traffic)|false|Specify the wirefilter expression used for traffic matching. The API automatically formats and sanitizes expressions before storing them. To prevent Terraform state drift, use the formatted expression returned in the API response.|

## Patch a Zero Trust Gateway rule

<a id="opIdzero-trust-gateway-rules-patch-zero-trust-gateway-rule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/699d98642c564d2e855e9661899b7252/gateway/rules/f174e90a-fafe-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Block bad websites based on their host name.",
    "enabled": true,
    "name": "block bad websites",
    "precedence": 0
  }'
```

`PATCH /accounts/{account_id}/gateway/rules/{rule_id}`

Update select fields of an existing Zero Trust Gateway rule. Only the fields provided in the request body are updated. This endpoint supports a limited subset of fields (`name`, `description`, `precedence`, `enabled`). To update other fields such as `action`, `traffic`, `identity`, `device_posture`, `rule_settings`, `schedule`, or `expiration`, use the PUT endpoint for a full rule replacement.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Block bad websites based on their host name.",
  "enabled": true,
  "name": "block bad websites",
  "precedence": 0
}
```

<h3 id="patch-a-zero-trust-gateway-rule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|rule_id|path|[zero-trust-gateway_uuid-4](#schemazero-trust-gateway_uuid-4)|true|none|
|account_id|path|[zero-trust-gateway_identifier-2](#schemazero-trust-gateway_identifier-2)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» description|body|[zero-trust-gateway_description-2](#schemazero-trust-gateway_description-2)|false|Specify the rule description.|
|» enabled|body|[zero-trust-gateway_enabled](#schemazero-trust-gateway_enabled)|false|Specify whether the rule is enabled.|
|» name|body|[zero-trust-gateway_name-3](#schemazero-trust-gateway_name-3)|false|Specify the rule name.|
|» precedence|body|[zero-trust-gateway_precedence](#schemazero-trust-gateway_precedence)|false|Set the order of your rules. Lower values indicate higher precedence. At each processing phase, evaluate applicable rules in ascending order of this value. Refer to [Order of enforcement](http://developers.cloudflare.com/learning-paths/secure-internet-traffic/understand-policies/order-of-enforcement/#manage-precedence-with-terraform) to manage precedence via Terraform.|

## Reset the expiration of a Zero Trust Gateway Rule

<a id="opIdzero-trust-gateway-rules-reset-expiration-zero-trust-gateway-rule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/699d98642c564d2e855e9661899b7252/gateway/rules/f174e90a-fafe-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415/reset_expiration \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/gateway/rules/{rule_id}/reset_expiration`

Resets the expiration of a Zero Trust Gateway Rule if its duration elapsed and it has a default duration. The Zero Trust Gateway Rule must have values  for both `expiration.expires_at` and `expiration.duration`.

<h3 id="reset-the-expiration-of-a-zero-trust-gateway-rule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|rule_id|path|[zero-trust-gateway_uuid-4](#schemazero-trust-gateway_uuid-4)|true|none|
|account_id|path|[zero-trust-gateway_identifier-2](#schemazero-trust-gateway_identifier-2)|true|none|

`PUT /accounts/{account_id}/hyperdrive/configs/{hyperdrive_id}`

Replaces and returns the specified Hyperdrive configuration. The request must include the name and complete origin connection details. Omitted caching settings are reset to their defaults, while omitted mTLS settings and origin connection limits are preserved. The integration association is set only during creation and cannot be changed; omit the integration field even when replacing an integration-backed configuration. Use the update operation to modify only selected fields.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "caching": {
    "disabled": true
  },
  "mtls": {
    "ca_certificate_id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000",
    "mtls_certificate_id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000",
    "sslmode": "verify-full"
  },
  "name": "example-hyperdrive",
  "origin": {
    "database": "postgres",
    "password": "string",
    "scheme": "postgres",
    "user": "postgres",
    "host": "database.example.com",
    "port": 5432
  },
  "origin_connection_limit": 60
}
```

<h3 id="replace-hyperdrive-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[hyperdrive_identifier](#schemahyperdrive_identifier)|true|The Cloudflare account ID.|
|hyperdrive_id|path|[hyperdrive_identifier](#schemahyperdrive_identifier)|true|The unique identifier of the Hyperdrive configuration.|
|body|body|[hyperdrive_hyperdrive-config](#schemahyperdrive_hyperdrive-config)|true|none|
|» caching|body|[hyperdrive_hyperdrive-caching](#schemahyperdrive_hyperdrive-caching)|false|none|
|» mtls|body|[hyperdrive_hyperdrive-mtls](#schemahyperdrive_hyperdrive-mtls)|false|mTLS configuration for the origin connection. Cannot be used with VPC Service origins; TLS must be managed on the VPC Service.|
|» name|body|[hyperdrive_hyperdrive-name](#schemahyperdrive_hyperdrive-name)|true|The name of the Hyperdrive configuration. Used to identify the configuration in the Cloudflare dashboard and API.|
|» origin|body|[hyperdrive_hyperdrive-origin-full](#schemahyperdrive_hyperdrive-origin-full)|true|Combines database connection fields with exactly one supported network location.|
|» origin_connection_limit|body|[hyperdrive_hyperdrive-origin-connection-limit](#schemahyperdrive_hyperdrive-origin-connection-limit)|false|The (soft) maximum number of connections the Hyperdrive is allowed to make to the origin database.<br><br>Maximum allowed: 20 for free tier accounts, 100 for paid tier accounts.<br>If not specified, defaults to 20 for free tier and 60 for paid tier.<br>Certain Cloudflare-managed origins may be permitted a higher limit.<br>Contact Cloudflare if you need a higher limit.<br>|

|» » *anyOf*|body|[hyperdrive_internet-origin](#schemahyperdrive_internet-origin) \| [hyperdrive_over-access-origin](#schemahyperdrive_over-access-origin) \| [hyperdrive_vpc-service-origin](#schemahyperdrive_vpc-service-origin)|false|none|

|» » *oneOf*|body|[hyperdrive_vpc-service-origin](#schemahyperdrive_vpc-service-origin)|false|Connect to a database through a Workers VPC Service. TLS settings (mTLS, sslmode) cannot be configured on the Hyperdrive when using a VPC Service origin; TLS must be managed on the VPC Service itself.<br>|

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/hyperdrive/integrationsOperations/planetScale/createDatabaseSignature`

Returns a short-lived signed authorization for creating a database that is billed through Cloudflare. The caller passes these values to the integration partner's own CLI, which verifies the signature before creating the database. Requires the account to be entitled to Cloudflare-billed databases for the integration.

## Upload an image

<a id="opIdcloudflare-images-upload-an-image-via-url"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/images/v1 \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

  -F 'creator=string' \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file' \

  -F 'url=https://example.com/path/to/logo.png'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/images/v1`

Upload an image to CF Images. Images up to 10 Megabytes can be uploaded using a
single HTTP POST (multipart/form-data) request by sending an image file or
passing a URL accessible to the API.


> Body parameter

```yaml
creator: string
file: string
id: string
metadata: {}
requireSignedURLs: true
url: "https://example.com/path/to/logo.png"
```

<h3 id="upload-an-image-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[images_account_identifier](#schemaimages_account_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[images_image_basic_upload](#schemaimages_image_basic_upload)|true|none|
|» creator|body|string|false|Can set the creator field with an internal user ID.|
|» file|body|string(binary)|false|An image binary data. Only needed when type is uploading a file.|
|» id|body|string|false|An optional custom unique identifier for your image.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|User modifiable key-value store. Can use used for keeping references to another system of record for managing images.|
|» requireSignedURLs|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether the image requires a signature token for the access.|
|» url|body|string|false|A URL to fetch an image from origin. Only needed when type is uploading from a URL.|

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/images/v1/direct_upload`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Direct uploads allow users to upload images without API keys. A common use
case are web apps, client-side applications, or mobile devices where users
upload content directly to Cloudflare Images. This method creates a one-time
upload URL. Use the V2 endpoint for additional features such as custom IDs and
metadata.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "expiry": "2021-01-02T02:20:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="create-authenticated-direct-upload-url-v1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

## List images V2

<a id="opIdcloudflare-images-list-images-v2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/images/v2 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/images/v2`

List up to 10000 images from CF Images, with up to 1000 results per page. Use the optional parameters below to get a specific range of images.
Pagination is supported via continuation_token.

**Metadata Filtering (Optional):**

You can optionally filter images by custom metadata fields using the `meta.<field>[<operator>]=<value>` syntax.

**Supported Operators:**
- `eq` / `eq:string` / `eq:number` / `eq:boolean` - Exact match
- `gt` / `gt:number` - Greater than (number only)
- `gte` / `gte:number` - Greater than or equal (number only)
- `lt` / `lt:number` - Less than (number only)
- `lte` / `lte:number` - Less than or equal (number only)
- `in` / `in:string` / `in:number` - Match any value in list (pipe-separated)

**Metadata Filter Constraints:**
- Maximum 5 metadata filters per request
- Maximum 5 levels of nesting (e.g., `meta.first.second.third.fourth.fifth`)
- Maximum 10 elements for list operators (`in`)
- Supports string, number, and boolean value types
- Range operators (`gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`) only accept numeric values

**Filter Consistency:**
Filters are combined with AND logic. The system does not validate whether filter combinations are logically consistent. For example, `meta.priority[eq:number]=5&meta.priority[lte:number]=3` will return zero results because no value can satisfy both conditions simultaneously. It is the caller's responsibility to ensure filter combinations make sense.

**Examples:**
```
# List all images
/images/v2

# Filter by metadata [eq]
/images/v2?meta.status[eq:string]=active

# Filter by metadata [in]
/images/v2?meta.status[in]=pending|deleted|flagged

# Filter by metadata [in:number]
/images/v2?meta.ratings[in:number]=4|5

# Filter by metadata range [gte:number]
/images/v2?meta.priority[gte:number]=1

# Filter by bounded range
/images/v2?meta.priority[gte:number]=1&meta.priority[lte:number]=5

# Filter by nested metadata
/images/v2?meta.region.name[eq]=eu-west

# Combine metadata filters with creator
/images/v2?meta.status[eq]=active&creator=user123

# Multiple metadata filters (AND logic)
/images/v2?meta.status[eq]=active&meta.priority[eq:number]=5
```


<h3 id="list-images-v2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[images_account_identifier](#schemaimages_account_identifier)|true|none|
|continuation_token|query|[images_images_list_continuation_token](#schemaimages_images_list_continuation_token)|false|none|
|per_page|query|number|false|none|
|sort_order|query|string|false|none|
|creator|query|string \| null|false|none|
|meta.<field>[<operator>]|query|string|false|Optional metadata filter(s). Multiple filters can be combined with AND logic.<br><br>**Operators:**<br>- `eq`, `eq:string`, `eq:number`, `eq:boolean` - Exact match<br>- `gt`, `gt:number` - Greater than (number only)<br>- `gte`, `gte:number` - Greater than or equal (number only)<br>- `lt`, `lt:number` - Less than (number only)<br>- `lte`, `lte:number` - Less than or equal (number only)<br>- `in`, `in:string`, `in:number` - Match any value in pipe-separated list<br><br>**Examples:**<br>- `meta.status[eq]=active`<br>- `meta.priority[eq:number]=5`<br>- `meta.enabled[eq:boolean]=true`<br>- `meta.priority[gte:number]=1`<br>- `meta.score[lt:number]=100`<br>- `meta.region[in]=us-east\|us-west\|eu-west`<br><br>**Note:** Filter consistency is not validated. Contradictory filters (e.g., `meta.priority[eq:number]=5&meta.priority[lte:number]=3`) will return zero results.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort_order|asc|
|sort_order|desc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "result": {
    "images": [
      {
        "creator": "107b9558-dd06-4bbd-5fef-9c2c16bb7900",
        "filename": "logo.png",
        "id": "107b9558-dd06-4bbd-5fef-9c2c16bb7900",
        "meta": {
          "key": "value"
        },
        "requireSignedURLs": true,
        "uploaded": "2014-01-02T02:20:00.123Z",
        "variants": [
          "https://imagedelivery.net/MTt4OTd0b0w5aj/107b9558-dd06-4bbd-5fef-9c2c16bb7900/thumbnail",
          "https://imagedelivery.net/MTt4OTd0b0w5aj/107b9558-dd06-4bbd-5fef-9c2c16bb7900/hero",
          "https://imagedelivery.net/MTt4OTd0b0w5aj/107b9558-dd06-4bbd-5fef-9c2c16bb7900/original"
        ]
      }
    ]
  },
  "success": true
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
  "errors": [
    {

    }
```

## Create authenticated direct upload URL V2

<a id="opIdcloudflare-images-create-authenticated-direct-upload-url-v-2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/images/v2/direct_upload \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'creator=string' \
  -F 'expiry=2021-01-02T02:20:00Z' \
  -F 'id=this/is/my-customid' \
  -F 'metadata={}' \
  -F 'requireSignedURLs=true'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/images/v2/direct_upload`

Direct uploads allow users to upload images without API keys. A common use case are web apps, client-side applications, or mobile devices where users upload content directly to Cloudflare Images. This method creates a draft record for a future image. It returns an upload URL and an image identifier. To verify if the image itself has been uploaded, send an image details request (accounts/:account_identifier/images/v1/:identifier), and check that the `draft: true` property is not present.

> Body parameter

```yaml
creator: string
expiry: "2021-01-02T02:20:00Z"
id: this/is/my-customid
metadata: {}
requireSignedURLs: true
```

<h3 id="create-authenticated-direct-upload-url-v2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[images_account_identifier](#schemaimages_account_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[images_image_direct_upload_request_v2](#schemaimages_image_direct_upload_request_v2)|true|none|
|» creator|body|string|false|Can set the creator field with an internal user ID.|
|» expiry|body|string(date-time)|false|The date after which the upload will not be accepted. Minimum: Now + 2 minutes. Maximum: Now + 6 hours.|
|» id|body|string|false|Optional Image Custom ID. Up to 1024 chars. Can include any number of subpaths, and utf8 characters. Cannot start nor end with a / (forward slash). Cannot be a UUID.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|User modifiable key-value store. Can be used for keeping references to another system of record, for managing images.|
|» requireSignedURLs|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether the image requires a signature token to be accessed.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
```

## Create a variant

<a id="opIdcloudflare-images-variants-create-a-variant"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/images/v1/variants \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "id": "hero",
    "neverRequireSignedURLs": true,
    "options": {
      "fit": "scale-down",
      "height": 768,
      "metadata": "none",
      "width": 1366
    }
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/images/v1/variants`

Create a CF Images variant that allows you to resize images for different use cases.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": "hero",
  "neverRequireSignedURLs": true,
  "options": {
    "fit": "scale-down",
    "height": 768,
    "metadata": "none",
    "width": 1366
  }
}
```

|» neverRequireSignedURLs|body|[images_image_variant_neverRequireSignedURLs](#schemaimages_image_variant_neverrequiresignedurls)|false|Indicates whether the variant can access an image without a signature, regardless of image access control.|
|» options|body|[images_image_variant_options](#schemaimages_image_variant_options)|true|Allows you to define image resizing sizes for different use cases.|

```json
    }
```

## Create a sourcing kit migration

<a id="opIdcloudflare-images-sourcingkit-create-migration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/images/v2/sourcingkit/migrations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "conflictBehaviour": "skip",
    "excludedContentTypes": [
      "image/jpeg"
    ],
    "pathPrefix": "string",
    "rootDirectory": "string",
    "sourceId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/images/v2/sourcingkit/migrations`

Create a pending CF Images import from a configured source.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "conflictBehaviour": "skip",
  "excludedContentTypes": [
    "image/jpeg"
  ],
  "pathPrefix": "string",
  "rootDirectory": "string",
  "sourceId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-sourcing-kit-migration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[images_account_identifier](#schemaimages_account_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[images_sourcingkit_migration_create_request](#schemaimages_sourcingkit_migration_create_request)|true|none|
|» conflictBehaviour|body|[images_sourcingkit_conflict_behaviour](#schemaimages_sourcingkit_conflict_behaviour)|false|How to handle objects that already exist at the destination.|
|» excludedContentTypes|body|[[images_sourcingkit_acceptable_content_type](#schemaimages_sourcingkit_acceptable_content_type)]|false|Content types to skip during migration.|
|» pathPrefix|body|string|false|Prefix to prepend to image custom IDs.|
|» rootDirectory|body|string|false|Only import objects under this prefix in the source bucket.|
|» sourceId|body|string(uuid)|true|The identifier of the source to migrate from.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» conflictBehaviour|skip|
|» conflictBehaviour|overwrite|
|» excludedContentTypes|image/jpeg|
|» excludedContentTypes|image/png|
|» excludedContentTypes|image/webp|
|» excludedContentTypes|image/gif|
|» excludedContentTypes|image/avif|
|» excludedContentTypes|image/heic|
|» excludedContentTypes|image/svg+xml|

```json
  "messages": [],

      "image/jpeg"
    ],

    "logStopped": true,
    "pathPrefix": "string",
```

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-infrastructure-access-targets">Infrastructure Access Targets</h1>

## List all targets

<a id="opIdinfra-targets-list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/infrastructure/targets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/infrastructure/targets`

Lists and sorts an account's targets. Filters are optional and are ANDed
together.

<h3 id="list-all-targets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[infra_AccountTag](#schemainfra_accounttag)|true|none|
|hostname|query|string \| null|false|Hostname of a target|
|hostname_contains|query|string \| null|false|Partial match to the hostname of a target|
|virtual_network_id|query|string(uuid) \| null|false|Private virtual network identifier of the target|
|ip_v4|query|string \| null|false|IPv4 address of the target|
|ip_v6|query|string \| null|false|IPv6 address of the target|
|created_before|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Date and time at which the target was created before (inclusive)|
|created_after|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Date and time at which the target was created after (inclusive)|
|modified_before|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Date and time at which the target was modified before (inclusive)|
|modified_after|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Date and time at which the target was modified after (inclusive)|
|ips|query|[string]|false|Filters for targets that have any of the following IP addresses. Specify<br>`ips` multiple times in query parameter to build list of candidates.|
|target_ids|query|[string(uuid)]|false|Filters for targets that have any of the following UUIDs. Specify<br>`target_ids` multiple times in query parameter to build list of<br>candidates.|
|ip_like|query|string \| null|false|Filters for targets whose IP addresses look like the specified string.<br>Supports `*` as a wildcard character|
|ipv4_start|query|string \| null|false|Defines an IPv4 filter range's starting value (inclusive). Requires<br>`ipv4_end` to be specified as well.|
|ipv4_end|query|string \| null|false|Defines an IPv4 filter range's ending value (inclusive). Requires<br>`ipv4_start` to be specified as well.|
|ipv6_start|query|string \| null|false|Defines an IPv6 filter range's starting value (inclusive). Requires<br>`ipv6_end` to be specified as well.|
|ipv6_end|query|string \| null|false|Defines an IPv6 filter range's ending value (inclusive). Requires<br>`ipv6_start` to be specified as well.|
|tag|query|[string]|false|Filter by tag key:value pairs. Multiple `tag` params are AND'd.<br>Format: `tag=key:value` (e.g., `tag=environment:production`).<br>Key and value must both be non-empty; `tag=:value` and `tag=key:` return 400.|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|Current page in the response|
|per_page|query|integer(int32)|false|Max amount of entries returned per page|
|order|query|string|false|The field to sort by.|
|direction|query|object|false|The sorting direction.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|hostname|
|order|created_at|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
```

## Updates Security Center Insight Classification

<a id="opIdupdate-security-center-insight-classification"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

  }'
```

`PATCH /accounts/{account_id}/security-center/insights/{issue_id}/classification`

Updates the user classification for a Security Center insight. Valid values are 'false_positive' or 'accept_risk'. To reset, set classification to null. Cannot change directly between classification values - must reset to null first.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "classification": "false_positive",
  "rationale": "string"
}
```

|» classification|body|[security-center_userClassification](#schemasecurity-center_userclassification)|false|User-defined classification for the insight. Can be 'false_positive', 'accept_risk', 'other', or null.|
|» rationale|body|string|false|Rationale for the classification change. Required when classification is 'accept_risk' or 'other'.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» classification|false_positive|
|» classification|accept_risk|
|» classification|other|

`PATCH /zones/{zone_id}/security-center/insights/{issue_id}/classification`

Updates the user classification for a zone-specific Security Center insight. Valid values are 'false_positive' or 'accept_risk'. To reset, set classification to null. Cannot change directly between classification values - must reset to null first.

```json
  "rationale": "string"
```

|» classification|body|[security-center_userClassification](#schemasecurity-center_userclassification)|false|User-defined classification for the insight. Can be 'false_positive', 'accept_risk', 'other', or null.|
|» rationale|body|string|false|Rationale for the classification change. Required when classification is 'accept_risk' or 'other'.|

## Get Multiple Domain Details

<a id="opIddomain-intelligence-get-multiple-domain-details"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/intel/domain/bulk \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/intel/domain/bulk`

Returns security details and statistics about multiple domains in a
single request.

**Behavior change — domain ranking is becoming opt-in.** This endpoint
previously included domain ranking data in every response and accepted
a `skip_ranking=true` query parameter to opt out. That parameter is
being deprecated and ranking will no longer be returned by default.
Callers that want ranking data must pass `include_ranking=true`. The
`skip_ranking` parameter will be silently ignored once the change ships.


<h3 id="get-multiple-domain-details-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[intel_identifier](#schemaintel_identifier)|true|none|
|domain|query|[string]|false|Accepts multiple values like `?domain=cloudflare.com&domain=example.com`.|
|include_ranking|query|boolean|false|Whether to include domain ranking data in the response. Defaults to<br>`false` — ranking lookups are expensive at bulk scale and most<br>callers do not need them. Set to `true` to opt in. This parameter<br>replaces the deprecated `skip_ranking` (see below).<br>|
|skip_ranking|query|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** **Deprecated.** Previously controlled whether the ranking lookup<br>was skipped (defaulted to `false`, meaning ranking ran). The<br>endpoint's default behavior is being flipped — ranking is now<br>opt-in via `include_ranking=true` — and this parameter will be<br>silently ignored. Remove it from your callers and use<br>`include_ranking` instead.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "result": [
    {
      "additional_information": {
        "suspected_malware_family": ""
      },
      "application": {
        "id": 0,
        "name": "CLOUDFLARE"
      },
      "content_categories": [
        {
          "id": 155,
          "name": "Technology",
          "super_category_id": 26
        }
      ],
      "domain": "cloudflare.com",
      "inherited_content_categories": [],
      "inherited_from": "string",
      "inherited_risk_types": [],
      "popularity_rank": 0,
      "risk_score": 0,
      "risk_types": []
    }
  ],
  "success": true,
  "result_info": {
    "count": 1,
```

## Update indicator feed data

<a id="opIdcustom-indicator-feeds-update-indicator-feed-data"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/intel/indicator-feeds/12/snapshot \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -F 'source=@/Users/me/test.stix2.gz'
```

`PUT /accounts/{account_id}/intel/indicator-feeds/{feed_id}/snapshot`

Revises the raw data entries in a custom threat indicator feed.

Accepts both plain and gzipped STIX2/CRDF bodies. Gzip is
detected by RFC 1952 magic bytes (`0x1f 0x8b`) and/or a `.gz`
filename suffix (case-insensitive) — either signal alone is
sufficient to trigger the gzip path; if the body is not valid
gzip, the upload fails fast. Customers are encouraged to gzip
larger uploads — the api-gateway 500 MB body cap applies to
the on-the-wire (compressed) size, so gzip lets a single
upload carry several GiB of decompressed STIX.


> Body parameter

```yaml
source: "@/Users/me/test.stix2.gz"
```

<h3 id="update-indicator-feed-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[custom-indicator-feeds_identifier](#schemacustom-indicator-feeds_identifier)|true|none|
|feed_id|path|[custom-indicator-feeds_feed_id](#schemacustom-indicator-feeds_feed_id)|true|none|
|Cf-Async-Upload|header|string|false|Set to the literal value `1` to enqueue the upload and receive a<br>`202` response with a polling URL. Any other value uses the legacy<br>synchronous response.<br>|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» source|body|string|false|The file to upload. Either a plain STIX2/CRDF body<br>or a gzipped one (recognised by `0x1f 0x8b` magic<br>bytes or a `.gz` filename suffix).<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Cf-Async-Upload|1|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "file_id": 1,
    "filename": "snapshot_file.unified",
    "poll_url": "/intel/indicator-feeds/12/uploads/12345",
    "status": "Unifying",
    "upload_id": 12345
  }
}
```

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "poll_url": "/intel/indicator-feeds/12/uploads/12345",
    "status": "Queued",
    "upload_id": 0
  }
}
```

> 413 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

<h3 id="update-indicator-feed-data-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Get indicator feed metadata|[custom-indicator-feeds_update_feed_response](#schemacustom-indicator-feeds_update_feed_response)|
|202|Accepted|Upload accepted for asynchronous processing|[custom-indicator-feeds_enqueue_upload_response](#schemacustom-indicator-feeds_enqueue_upload_response)|
|413|Payload Too Large|Decompressed upload exceeds the maximum allowed size. The<br>server caps the decompressed body at a configured limit<br>(default 6 GiB) as a gzip-bomb defence; this response is<br>returned before any feed state changes. Resubmit a smaller<br>(or non-pathologically-compressed) body.<br>|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|Get indicator feeds response failure|Inline|

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-miscategorization">Miscategorization</h1>

## Create Miscategorization

<a id="opIdmiscategorization-create-miscategorization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/intel/miscategorization \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "content_adds": [
      82
    ],
    "content_removes": [
      155
    ],
    "indicator_type": "domain",
    "ip": "string",
    "security_adds": [
      117,
      131
    ],
    "security_removes": [
      83
    ],
    "url": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/intel/miscategorization`

Allows you to submit requests to change a domain’s category.

Requests that include category `169` (New Domains) or category `177` (Newly Seen)
in any of `content_adds`, `content_removes`, `security_adds`, or `security_removes`
will be rejected with a `400 Bad Request`. These categories are automatically
managed and fall off 30 days after they are applied.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "content_adds": [
    82
  ],
  "content_removes": [
    155
  ],
  "indicator_type": "domain",
  "ip": "string",
  "security_adds": [
    117,
    131
  ],
  "security_removes": [
    83
  ],
  "url": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-miscategorization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[intel_identifier](#schemaintel_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[intel_miscategorization](#schemaintel_miscategorization)|true|none|
|» content_adds|body|[integer]|false|Content category IDs to add.|
|» content_removes|body|[integer]|false|Content category IDs to remove.|
|» indicator_type|body|string|false|none|
|» ip|body|string \| null|false|Provide only if indicator_type is `ipv4` or `ipv6`.|
|» security_adds|body|[integer]|false|Security category IDs to add.|
|» security_removes|body|[integer]|false|Security category IDs to remove.|
|» url|body|string|false|Provide only if indicator_type is `domain` or `url`. Example if indicator_type is `domain`: `example.com`. Example if indicator_type is `url`: `https://example.com/news/`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|» indicator_type|domain|
|» indicator_type|ipv4|
|» indicator_type|ipv6|
|» indicator_type|url|

```json
}
```

```json
    }
  ],
```

`POST /zones/{zone_id}/intel/sinkholes/{sinkhole_id}/ingresses`

Create a new ingress rule for the specified sinkhole. The CIDR block must be a Cloudflare BYOIP associated with your account. The zone_id must be a zone with the ability to create Spectrum Apps. The sinkhole must belong to the same account as the zone.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "cidr": "string"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|sinkhole_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier for the sinkhole.|
|body|body|[intel-sinkholes_ingress_create_params](#schemaintel-sinkholes_ingress_create_params)|true|none|
|» cidr|body|string|true|The CIDR block for the ingress rule in IPv4 or IPv6 notation (e.g., 192.0.2.0/24). Provide a Cloudflare BYOIP CIDR that your account owns.|

```json
}
```

## Create K2 stream

<a id="opIdpostV4AccountsByAccount_idK2Streams"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/0123105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/k2/streams \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "http": {
      "enabled": false
    },
    "name": "my_k2_stream",
    "retention_seconds": 604800,
    "worker_binding": {
      "enabled": true
    }
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/k2/streams`

Create a new K2 stream. HTTP is disabled when `http` is omitted. Enabled HTTP requires authentication and allows all origins unless `authentication` or `cors` say otherwise. At least one input must be enabled.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "http": {
    "enabled": false
  },
  "name": "my_k2_stream",
  "retention_seconds": 604800,
  "worker_binding": {
    "enabled": true
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-k2-stream-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[cloudflare-k2_workers-k2-account-id](#schemacloudflare-k2_workers-k2-account-id)|true|none|
|body|body|[cloudflare-k2_CreateK2StreamRequest](#schemacloudflare-k2_createk2streamrequest)|true|none|
|» http|body|object|false|none|
|» » authentication|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether the HTTP endpoint requires an API token with K2 produce permission. When false, the endpoint accepts unauthenticated records. Defaults to true when HTTP is enabled without a stored value.|
|» » cors|body|[cloudflare-k2_K2StreamCorsOptions](#schemacloudflare-k2_k2streamcorsoptions)|false|none|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|true|Indicates whether the HTTP endpoint accepts records.|
|» name|body|string|true|Specifies the name of the K2 stream.|
|» retention_seconds|body|integer|false|Sets the record retention period from 1 hour (3600 seconds) to 30 days (2592000 seconds), inclusive.|
|» worker_binding|body|object|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|true|Indicates whether Workers bindings can produce records to the stream.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|true|Indicates whether Workers bindings can produce records to the stream.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » enabled|false|
|» » enabled|true|

```json
    {

    }
  ],

    }
  ],
  "result": {
    "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",

          "string"
        ]
      },

    },
```

`PATCH /accounts/{account_id}/k2/streams/{stream_id}`

Update a K2 stream. Omitted `http` settings, such as `authentication` and `cors`, keep their current values. Disabling HTTP keeps them, so enabling HTTP again restores them. At least one input must remain enabled.

```json
{

    "authentication": true,
    "cors": {
      "origins": [
        "string"
      ]
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/k2/streams/{stream_id}/subscriptions`

Lists every subscription on one stream, oldest first. Lag uses committed positions, not reserved read positions. A failed tail observation preserves subscription metadata and returns unavailable lag.

```json
    }
  ],

    {
      "code": 0,
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "result": [
    {
      "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "id": "string",
      "lag": {
        "records": "string",
        "status": "available"
      },
```
