## Produce records

<a id="opIdpostK2Produce"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/produce \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "records": [
      {
        "content": "eyJvcmRlcl9pZCI6MTAwMX0=",
        "headers": {
          "event-type": "order.created"
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /produce`

Send to the stream's `endpoint`, `https://<stream_id>.k2.cloudflarestorage.com`. Appends a batch of records to the stream. The batch is written atomically, so either every record is stored or none are. Requests are limited to 5 MB, compressed and decompressed, and each record to 1 MB. Gzip bodies are accepted when `Content-Encoding` is `gzip`. Requires an API token with K2 produce permission unless the stream's HTTP input sets `authentication` to false. Errors use a `success` and `error` body instead of the `errors` array.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "records": [
    {
      "content": "eyJvcmRlcl9pZCI6MTAwMX0=",
      "headers": {
        "event-type": "order.created"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="produce-records-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[cloudflare-k2_K2ProduceRequest](#schemacloudflare-k2_k2producerequest)|true|none|
|» records|body|[[cloudflare-k2_K2ProduceRecord](#schemacloudflare-k2_k2producerecord)]|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "success": true
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": 10211,
    "message": "K2 is temporarily unavailable",
    "retryable": true
  },
  "success": false
}
```

> 5XX Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": 10211,
    "message": "K2 is temporarily unavailable",
    "retryable": true
  },
  "success": false
}
```

<h3 id="produce-records-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Indicates that every record in the batch was stored.|[cloudflare-k2_K2ProduceResponse](#schemacloudflare-k2_k2produceresponse)|
|4XX|Client Error|Indicates an invalid request, a missing stream or HTTP input, or failed authorization. No records were stored.|[cloudflare-k2_K2ProduceError](#schemacloudflare-k2_k2produceerror)|
|5XX|Server Error|Indicates a server error. Retry with backoff when the error is retryable.|[cloudflare-k2_K2ProduceError](#schemacloudflare-k2_k2produceerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
api_token
</aside>

## Create subscription

<a id="opIdpostK2Subscriptions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/subscriptions \

    }
  }'
```

`POST /subscriptions`

Send to the stream's `endpoint`, `https://<stream_id>.k2.cloudflarestorage.com`. Create a subscription, which reads the stream from its own position. Creating a subscription with an existing name returns the existing subscription. A stream can have up to 100 subscriptions. Requires an API token with K2 consume permission.

```json
  "start_at": {
    "type": "earliest"
  }
}
```

|» start_at|body|object|true|none|
|» » type|body|string|true|Starts at the oldest retained record or at the end of the stream.|

`POST /subscriptions/{subscription_id}/batches/{batch_id}/ack`

|» worker_id|body|[cloudflare-k2_workers-k2-worker-id](#schemacloudflare-k2_workers-k2-worker-id)|true|Identifies the consumer process. Each worker holds at most one batch at a time.|

|4XX|Client Error|Indicates an invalid request, a missing stream or subscription, a lost lease, or failed authorization.|[cloudflare-k2_K2V4Error](#schemacloudflare-k2_k2v4error)|
|5XX|Server Error|Indicates a server error. Retry with backoff when the error is retryable.|[cloudflare-k2_K2V4Error](#schemacloudflare-k2_k2v4error)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
api_token
</aside>

## Consume records

<a id="opIdpostK2SubscriptionsBySubscription_idConsume"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/subscriptions/7c1e9b2a4d6f4e8a9b0c1d2e3f4a5b6c/consume \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "max_records": 100,
    "worker_id": "worker-1"
  }'
```

`POST /subscriptions/{subscription_id}/consume`

Send to the stream's `endpoint`, `https://<stream_id>.k2.cloudflarestorage.com`. Returns the next batch of records and leases it to the worker for 5 minutes. ACK the batch after processing it, NACK it to have it redelivered, or extend the lease if processing takes longer. When no records are available, the response has no records and a null `batch_id`. Returns 429 with code 10216 when every parallel read slot for the subscription is leased, and 409 with code 10217 while this worker has a read in progress; retry both. Requires an API token with K2 consume permission.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "max_records": 100,
  "worker_id": "worker-1"
}
```

<h3 id="consume-records-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscription_id|path|[cloudflare-k2_workers-k2-subscription-id](#schemacloudflare-k2_workers-k2-subscription-id)|true|none|
|body|body|[cloudflare-k2_K2ConsumeRequest](#schemacloudflare-k2_k2consumerequest)|true|none|
|» max_records|body|integer|true|Sets the maximum number of records to return.|
|» worker_id|body|[cloudflare-k2_workers-k2-worker-id](#schemacloudflare-k2_workers-k2-worker-id)|true|Identifies the consumer process. Each worker holds at most one batch at a time.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 0,
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [
    {
      "code": 0,
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "result": {
    "batch_id": "string",
    "leased_until_ms": 1759737900000,
    "records": [
      {
        "content": "eyJvcmRlcl9pZCI6MTAwMX0=",
        "headers": {
          "property1": "string",
          "property2": "string"
        },
        "timestamp_ms": 1759737600000
      }
    ]
  },
  "success": true
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 0,
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [
    {
      "code": 0,
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "result": {},
  "success": false
}
```

> 5XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 0,
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [
    {
      "code": 0,
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "result": {},
  "success": false
}
```

<h3 id="consume-records-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Indicates a leased batch, or no records.|[cloudflare-k2_K2ConsumeResponse](#schemacloudflare-k2_k2consumeresponse)|
|4XX|Client Error|Indicates an invalid request, a missing stream or subscription, a busy subscription or worker, or failed authorization.|[cloudflare-k2_K2V4Error](#schemacloudflare-k2_k2v4error)|
|5XX|Server Error|Indicates a server error. Retry with backoff when the error is retryable.|[cloudflare-k2_K2V4Error](#schemacloudflare-k2_k2v4error)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
api_token

<h3 id="create-account-load-balancer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[load-balancing_components-schemas-identifier](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» adaptive_routing|body|[load-balancing_adaptive_routing](#schemaload-balancing_adaptive_routing)|false|Controls features that modify the routing of requests to pools and origins in response to dynamic conditions, such as during the interval between active health monitoring requests. For example, zero-downtime failover occurs immediately when an origin becomes unavailable due to HTTP 521, 522, or 523 response codes. If there is another healthy origin in the same pool, the request is retried once against this alternate origin.|
|» country_pools|body|[load-balancing_country_pools](#schemaload-balancing_country_pools)|false|A mapping of country codes to a list of pool IDs (ordered by their failover priority) for the given country. Any country not explicitly defined will fall back to using the corresponding region_pool mapping if it exists else to default_pools.|
|» default_pools|body|[load-balancing_default_pools](#schemaload-balancing_default_pools)|true|A list of pool IDs ordered by their failover priority. Pools defined here are used by default, or when region_pools are not configured for a given region.|
|» description|body|[load-balancing_components-schemas-description](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-description)|false|Object description.|
|» enabled|body|[load-balancing_components-schemas-enabled](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-enabled)|false|Whether to enable (the default) this load balancer.|
|» fallback_pool|body|[load-balancing_fallback_pool](#schemaload-balancing_fallback_pool)|true|The pool ID to use when all other pools are detected as unhealthy.|
|» location_strategy|body|[load-balancing_location_strategy](#schemaload-balancing_location_strategy)|false|Controls location-based steering for non-proxied requests. See `steering_policy` to learn how steering is affected.|
|» name|body|[load-balancing_components-schemas-name](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-name)|true|The DNS hostname to associate with your Load Balancer. If this hostname already exists as a DNS record in Cloudflare's DNS, the Load Balancer will take precedence and the DNS record will not be used.|
|» networks|body|[load-balancing_networks](#schemaload-balancing_networks)|false|List of networks where Load Balancer or Pool is enabled.|
|» pop_pools|body|[load-balancing_pop_pools](#schemaload-balancing_pop_pools)|false|Enterprise only: A mapping of Cloudflare PoP identifiers to a list of pool IDs (ordered by their failover priority) for the PoP (datacenter). Any PoPs not explicitly defined will fall back to using the corresponding country_pool, then region_pool mapping if it exists else to default_pools.|
|» proxied|body|[load-balancing_proxied](#schemaload-balancing_proxied)|false|Whether the hostname should be gray clouded (false) or orange clouded (true).|
|» random_steering|body|[load-balancing_random_steering](#schemaload-balancing_random_steering)|false|Configures pool weights.<br>- `steering_policy="random"`: A random pool is selected with probability proportional to pool weights.<br>- `steering_policy="least_outstanding_requests"`: Use pool weights to scale each pool's outstanding requests.<br>- `steering_policy="least_connections"`: Use pool weights to scale each pool's open connections.|
|» region_pools|body|[load-balancing_region_pools](#schemaload-balancing_region_pools)|false|A mapping of region codes to a list of pool IDs (ordered by their failover priority) for the given region. Any regions not explicitly defined will fall back to using default_pools.|
|» rules|body|[load-balancing_rules](#schemaload-balancing_rules)|false|BETA Field Not General Access: A list of rules for this load balancer to execute.|
|» session_affinity|body|[load-balancing_session_affinity](#schemaload-balancing_session_affinity)|false|Specifies the type of session affinity the load balancer should use unless specified as `"none"`. The supported types are: - `"cookie"`: On the first request to a proxied load balancer, a cookie is generated, encoding information of which origin the request will be forwarded to. Subsequent requests, by the same client to the same load balancer, will be sent to the origin server the cookie encodes, for the duration of the cookie and as long as the origin server remains healthy. If the cookie has expired or the origin server is unhealthy, then a new origin server is calculated and used. - `"ip_cookie"`: Behaves the same as `"cookie"` except the initial origin selection is stable and based on the client's ip address. - `"header"`: On the first request to a proxied load balancer, a session key based on the configured HTTP headers (see `session_affinity_attributes.headers`) is generated, encoding the request headers used for storing in the load balancer session state which origin the request will be forwarded to. Subsequent requests to the load balancer with the same headers will be sent to the same origin server, for the duration of the session and as long as the origin server remains healthy. If the session has been idle for the duration of `session_affinity_ttl` seconds or the origin server is unhealthy, then a new origin server is calculated and used. See `headers` in `session_affinity_attributes` for additional required configuration.|
|» session_affinity_attributes|body|[load-balancing_session_affinity_attributes](#schemaload-balancing_session_affinity_attributes)|false|Configures attributes for session affinity.|
|» session_affinity_ttl|body|[load-balancing_session_affinity_ttl](#schemaload-balancing_session_affinity_ttl)|false|Time, in seconds, until a client's session expires after being created. Once the expiry time has been reached, subsequent requests may get sent to a different origin server. The accepted ranges per `session_affinity` policy are: - `"cookie"` / `"ip_cookie"`: The current default of 23 hours will be used unless explicitly set. The accepted range of values is between [1800, 604800]. - `"header"`: The current default of 1800 seconds will be used unless explicitly set. The accepted range of values is between [30, 3600]. Note: With session affinity by header, sessions only expire after they haven't been used for the number of seconds specified.|
|» steering_policy|body|[load-balancing_steering_policy](#schemaload-balancing_steering_policy)|false|Steering Policy for this load balancer.<br>- `"off"`: Use `default_pools`.<br>- `"geo"`: Use `region_pools`/`country_pools`/`pop_pools`. For non-proxied requests, the country for `country_pools` is determined by `location_strategy`.<br>- `"random"`: Select a pool randomly.<br>- `"dynamic_latency"`: Use round trip time to select the closest pool in default_pools (requires pool health checks).<br>- `"proximity"`: Use the pools' latitude and longitude to select the closest pool using the Cloudflare PoP location for proxied requests or the location determined by `location_strategy` for non-proxied requests.<br>- `"least_outstanding_requests"`: Select a pool by taking into consideration `random_steering` weights, as well as each pool's number of outstanding requests. Pools with more pending requests are weighted proportionately less relative to others.<br>- `"least_connections"`: Select a pool by taking into consideration `random_steering` weights, as well as each pool's number of open connections. Pools with more open connections are weighted proportionately less relative to others. Supported for HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 connections.<br>- `""`: Will map to `"geo"` if you use `region_pools`/`country_pools`/`pop_pools` otherwise `"off"`.|
|» ttl|body|[load-balancing_ttl](#schemaload-balancing_ttl)|false|Time to live (TTL) of the DNS entry for the IP address returned by this load balancer. This only applies to gray-clouded (unproxied) load balancers.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» session_affinity|none|
|» session_affinity|cookie|
|» session_affinity|ip_cookie|
|» session_affinity|header|
|» steering_policy|off|
|» steering_policy|geo|
|» steering_policy|random|
|» steering_policy|dynamic_latency|
|» steering_policy|proximity|
|» steering_policy|least_outstanding_requests|
|» steering_policy|least_connections|
|» steering_policy|""|

## List Load Balancer Usage

<a id="opIdaccount-load-balancers-list-load-balancer-usage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/load_balancers/usage \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/load_balancers/usage`

Get current load balancer resource usage counts for an account.

<h3 id="list-load-balancer-usage-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|account_id|path|[load-balancing_components-schemas-identifier](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-identifier)|true|none|

<h3 id="update-account-load-balancer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[load-balancing_components-schemas-identifier](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-identifier)|true|none|
|load_balancer_id|path|[load-balancing_load-balancer_components-schemas-identifier](#schemaload-balancing_load-balancer_components-schemas-identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» adaptive_routing|body|[load-balancing_adaptive_routing](#schemaload-balancing_adaptive_routing)|false|Controls features that modify the routing of requests to pools and origins in response to dynamic conditions, such as during the interval between active health monitoring requests. For example, zero-downtime failover occurs immediately when an origin becomes unavailable due to HTTP 521, 522, or 523 response codes. If there is another healthy origin in the same pool, the request is retried once against this alternate origin.|
|» country_pools|body|[load-balancing_country_pools](#schemaload-balancing_country_pools)|false|A mapping of country codes to a list of pool IDs (ordered by their failover priority) for the given country. Any country not explicitly defined will fall back to using the corresponding region_pool mapping if it exists else to default_pools.|
|» default_pools|body|[load-balancing_default_pools](#schemaload-balancing_default_pools)|true|A list of pool IDs ordered by their failover priority. Pools defined here are used by default, or when region_pools are not configured for a given region.|
|» description|body|[load-balancing_components-schemas-description](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-description)|false|Object description.|
|» enabled|body|[load-balancing_components-schemas-enabled](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-enabled)|false|Whether to enable (the default) this load balancer.|
|» fallback_pool|body|[load-balancing_fallback_pool](#schemaload-balancing_fallback_pool)|true|The pool ID to use when all other pools are detected as unhealthy.|
|» location_strategy|body|[load-balancing_location_strategy](#schemaload-balancing_location_strategy)|false|Controls location-based steering for non-proxied requests. See `steering_policy` to learn how steering is affected.|
|» name|body|[load-balancing_components-schemas-name](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-name)|true|The DNS hostname to associate with your Load Balancer. If this hostname already exists as a DNS record in Cloudflare's DNS, the Load Balancer will take precedence and the DNS record will not be used.|
|» networks|body|[load-balancing_networks](#schemaload-balancing_networks)|false|List of networks where Load Balancer or Pool is enabled.|
|» pop_pools|body|[load-balancing_pop_pools](#schemaload-balancing_pop_pools)|false|Enterprise only: A mapping of Cloudflare PoP identifiers to a list of pool IDs (ordered by their failover priority) for the PoP (datacenter). Any PoPs not explicitly defined will fall back to using the corresponding country_pool, then region_pool mapping if it exists else to default_pools.|
|» proxied|body|[load-balancing_proxied](#schemaload-balancing_proxied)|false|Whether the hostname should be gray clouded (false) or orange clouded (true).|
|» random_steering|body|[load-balancing_random_steering](#schemaload-balancing_random_steering)|false|Configures pool weights.<br>- `steering_policy="random"`: A random pool is selected with probability proportional to pool weights.<br>- `steering_policy="least_outstanding_requests"`: Use pool weights to scale each pool's outstanding requests.<br>- `steering_policy="least_connections"`: Use pool weights to scale each pool's open connections.|
|» region_pools|body|[load-balancing_region_pools](#schemaload-balancing_region_pools)|false|A mapping of region codes to a list of pool IDs (ordered by their failover priority) for the given region. Any regions not explicitly defined will fall back to using default_pools.|
|» rules|body|[load-balancing_rules](#schemaload-balancing_rules)|false|BETA Field Not General Access: A list of rules for this load balancer to execute.|
|» session_affinity|body|[load-balancing_session_affinity](#schemaload-balancing_session_affinity)|false|Specifies the type of session affinity the load balancer should use unless specified as `"none"`. The supported types are: - `"cookie"`: On the first request to a proxied load balancer, a cookie is generated, encoding information of which origin the request will be forwarded to. Subsequent requests, by the same client to the same load balancer, will be sent to the origin server the cookie encodes, for the duration of the cookie and as long as the origin server remains healthy. If the cookie has expired or the origin server is unhealthy, then a new origin server is calculated and used. - `"ip_cookie"`: Behaves the same as `"cookie"` except the initial origin selection is stable and based on the client's ip address. - `"header"`: On the first request to a proxied load balancer, a session key based on the configured HTTP headers (see `session_affinity_attributes.headers`) is generated, encoding the request headers used for storing in the load balancer session state which origin the request will be forwarded to. Subsequent requests to the load balancer with the same headers will be sent to the same origin server, for the duration of the session and as long as the origin server remains healthy. If the session has been idle for the duration of `session_affinity_ttl` seconds or the origin server is unhealthy, then a new origin server is calculated and used. See `headers` in `session_affinity_attributes` for additional required configuration.|
|» session_affinity_attributes|body|[load-balancing_session_affinity_attributes](#schemaload-balancing_session_affinity_attributes)|false|Configures attributes for session affinity.|
|» session_affinity_ttl|body|[load-balancing_session_affinity_ttl](#schemaload-balancing_session_affinity_ttl)|false|Time, in seconds, until a client's session expires after being created. Once the expiry time has been reached, subsequent requests may get sent to a different origin server. The accepted ranges per `session_affinity` policy are: - `"cookie"` / `"ip_cookie"`: The current default of 23 hours will be used unless explicitly set. The accepted range of values is between [1800, 604800]. - `"header"`: The current default of 1800 seconds will be used unless explicitly set. The accepted range of values is between [30, 3600]. Note: With session affinity by header, sessions only expire after they haven't been used for the number of seconds specified.|
|» steering_policy|body|[load-balancing_steering_policy](#schemaload-balancing_steering_policy)|false|Steering Policy for this load balancer.<br>- `"off"`: Use `default_pools`.<br>- `"geo"`: Use `region_pools`/`country_pools`/`pop_pools`. For non-proxied requests, the country for `country_pools` is determined by `location_strategy`.<br>- `"random"`: Select a pool randomly.<br>- `"dynamic_latency"`: Use round trip time to select the closest pool in default_pools (requires pool health checks).<br>- `"proximity"`: Use the pools' latitude and longitude to select the closest pool using the Cloudflare PoP location for proxied requests or the location determined by `location_strategy` for non-proxied requests.<br>- `"least_outstanding_requests"`: Select a pool by taking into consideration `random_steering` weights, as well as each pool's number of outstanding requests. Pools with more pending requests are weighted proportionately less relative to others.<br>- `"least_connections"`: Select a pool by taking into consideration `random_steering` weights, as well as each pool's number of open connections. Pools with more open connections are weighted proportionately less relative to others. Supported for HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 connections.<br>- `""`: Will map to `"geo"` if you use `region_pools`/`country_pools`/`pop_pools` otherwise `"off"`.|
|» ttl|body|[load-balancing_ttl](#schemaload-balancing_ttl)|false|Time to live (TTL) of the DNS entry for the IP address returned by this load balancer. This only applies to gray-clouded (unproxied) load balancers.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» session_affinity|none|
|» session_affinity|cookie|
|» session_affinity|ip_cookie|
|» session_affinity|header|
|» steering_policy|off|
|» steering_policy|geo|
|» steering_policy|random|
|» steering_policy|dynamic_latency|
|» steering_policy|proximity|
|» steering_policy|least_outstanding_requests|
|» steering_policy|least_connections|
|» steering_policy|""|

<h3 id="patch-account-load-balancer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[load-balancing_components-schemas-identifier](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-identifier)|true|none|
|load_balancer_id|path|[load-balancing_load-balancer_components-schemas-identifier](#schemaload-balancing_load-balancer_components-schemas-identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» adaptive_routing|body|[load-balancing_adaptive_routing](#schemaload-balancing_adaptive_routing)|false|Controls features that modify the routing of requests to pools and origins in response to dynamic conditions, such as during the interval between active health monitoring requests. For example, zero-downtime failover occurs immediately when an origin becomes unavailable due to HTTP 521, 522, or 523 response codes. If there is another healthy origin in the same pool, the request is retried once against this alternate origin.|
|» country_pools|body|[load-balancing_country_pools](#schemaload-balancing_country_pools)|false|A mapping of country codes to a list of pool IDs (ordered by their failover priority) for the given country. Any country not explicitly defined will fall back to using the corresponding region_pool mapping if it exists else to default_pools.|
|» default_pools|body|[load-balancing_default_pools](#schemaload-balancing_default_pools)|false|A list of pool IDs ordered by their failover priority. Pools defined here are used by default, or when region_pools are not configured for a given region.|
|» description|body|[load-balancing_components-schemas-description](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-description)|false|Object description.|
|» enabled|body|[load-balancing_components-schemas-enabled](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-enabled)|false|Whether to enable (the default) this load balancer.|
|» fallback_pool|body|[load-balancing_fallback_pool](#schemaload-balancing_fallback_pool)|false|The pool ID to use when all other pools are detected as unhealthy.|
|» location_strategy|body|[load-balancing_location_strategy](#schemaload-balancing_location_strategy)|false|Controls location-based steering for non-proxied requests. See `steering_policy` to learn how steering is affected.|
|» name|body|[load-balancing_components-schemas-name](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-name)|false|The DNS hostname to associate with your Load Balancer. If this hostname already exists as a DNS record in Cloudflare's DNS, the Load Balancer will take precedence and the DNS record will not be used.|
|» networks|body|[load-balancing_networks](#schemaload-balancing_networks)|false|List of networks where Load Balancer or Pool is enabled.|
|» pop_pools|body|[load-balancing_pop_pools](#schemaload-balancing_pop_pools)|false|Enterprise only: A mapping of Cloudflare PoP identifiers to a list of pool IDs (ordered by their failover priority) for the PoP (datacenter). Any PoPs not explicitly defined will fall back to using the corresponding country_pool, then region_pool mapping if it exists else to default_pools.|
|» proxied|body|[load-balancing_proxied](#schemaload-balancing_proxied)|false|Whether the hostname should be gray clouded (false) or orange clouded (true).|
|» random_steering|body|[load-balancing_random_steering](#schemaload-balancing_random_steering)|false|Configures pool weights.<br>- `steering_policy="random"`: A random pool is selected with probability proportional to pool weights.<br>- `steering_policy="least_outstanding_requests"`: Use pool weights to scale each pool's outstanding requests.<br>- `steering_policy="least_connections"`: Use pool weights to scale each pool's open connections.|
|» region_pools|body|[load-balancing_region_pools](#schemaload-balancing_region_pools)|false|A mapping of region codes to a list of pool IDs (ordered by their failover priority) for the given region. Any regions not explicitly defined will fall back to using default_pools.|
|» rules|body|[load-balancing_rules](#schemaload-balancing_rules)|false|BETA Field Not General Access: A list of rules for this load balancer to execute.|
|» session_affinity|body|[load-balancing_session_affinity](#schemaload-balancing_session_affinity)|false|Specifies the type of session affinity the load balancer should use unless specified as `"none"`. The supported types are: - `"cookie"`: On the first request to a proxied load balancer, a cookie is generated, encoding information of which origin the request will be forwarded to. Subsequent requests, by the same client to the same load balancer, will be sent to the origin server the cookie encodes, for the duration of the cookie and as long as the origin server remains healthy. If the cookie has expired or the origin server is unhealthy, then a new origin server is calculated and used. - `"ip_cookie"`: Behaves the same as `"cookie"` except the initial origin selection is stable and based on the client's ip address. - `"header"`: On the first request to a proxied load balancer, a session key based on the configured HTTP headers (see `session_affinity_attributes.headers`) is generated, encoding the request headers used for storing in the load balancer session state which origin the request will be forwarded to. Subsequent requests to the load balancer with the same headers will be sent to the same origin server, for the duration of the session and as long as the origin server remains healthy. If the session has been idle for the duration of `session_affinity_ttl` seconds or the origin server is unhealthy, then a new origin server is calculated and used. See `headers` in `session_affinity_attributes` for additional required configuration.|
|» session_affinity_attributes|body|[load-balancing_session_affinity_attributes](#schemaload-balancing_session_affinity_attributes)|false|Configures attributes for session affinity.|
|» session_affinity_ttl|body|[load-balancing_session_affinity_ttl](#schemaload-balancing_session_affinity_ttl)|false|Time, in seconds, until a client's session expires after being created. Once the expiry time has been reached, subsequent requests may get sent to a different origin server. The accepted ranges per `session_affinity` policy are: - `"cookie"` / `"ip_cookie"`: The current default of 23 hours will be used unless explicitly set. The accepted range of values is between [1800, 604800]. - `"header"`: The current default of 1800 seconds will be used unless explicitly set. The accepted range of values is between [30, 3600]. Note: With session affinity by header, sessions only expire after they haven't been used for the number of seconds specified.|
|» steering_policy|body|[load-balancing_steering_policy](#schemaload-balancing_steering_policy)|false|Steering Policy for this load balancer.<br>- `"off"`: Use `default_pools`.<br>- `"geo"`: Use `region_pools`/`country_pools`/`pop_pools`. For non-proxied requests, the country for `country_pools` is determined by `location_strategy`.<br>- `"random"`: Select a pool randomly.<br>- `"dynamic_latency"`: Use round trip time to select the closest pool in default_pools (requires pool health checks).<br>- `"proximity"`: Use the pools' latitude and longitude to select the closest pool using the Cloudflare PoP location for proxied requests or the location determined by `location_strategy` for non-proxied requests.<br>- `"least_outstanding_requests"`: Select a pool by taking into consideration `random_steering` weights, as well as each pool's number of outstanding requests. Pools with more pending requests are weighted proportionately less relative to others.<br>- `"least_connections"`: Select a pool by taking into consideration `random_steering` weights, as well as each pool's number of open connections. Pools with more open connections are weighted proportionately less relative to others. Supported for HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 connections.<br>- `""`: Will map to `"geo"` if you use `region_pools`/`country_pools`/`pop_pools` otherwise `"off"`.|
|» ttl|body|[load-balancing_ttl](#schemaload-balancing_ttl)|false|Time to live (TTL) of the DNS entry for the IP address returned by this load balancer. This only applies to gray-clouded (unproxied) load balancers.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» session_affinity|none|
|» session_affinity|cookie|
|» session_affinity|ip_cookie|
|» session_affinity|header|
|» steering_policy|off|
|» steering_policy|geo|
|» steering_policy|random|
|» steering_policy|dynamic_latency|
|» steering_policy|proximity|
|» steering_policy|least_outstanding_requests|
|» steering_policy|least_connections|
|» steering_policy|""|

```json
    ]
  },
```

```json
  "path": "/health",
  "port": 0,
  "probe_zone": "example.com",
  "retries": 2,
  "timeout": 5,
  "type": "https"
}
```

<h3 id="create-monitor-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[load-balancing_components-schemas-identifier](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» allow_insecure|body|[load-balancing_allow_insecure](#schemaload-balancing_allow_insecure)|false|Do not validate the certificate when monitor use HTTPS. This parameter is currently only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» consecutive_down|body|[load-balancing_consecutive_down](#schemaload-balancing_consecutive_down)|false|To be marked unhealthy the monitored origin must fail this healthcheck N consecutive times.|
|» consecutive_up|body|[load-balancing_consecutive_up](#schemaload-balancing_consecutive_up)|false|To be marked healthy the monitored origin must pass this healthcheck N consecutive times.|
|» description|body|[load-balancing_description](#schemaload-balancing_description)|false|Object description.|
|» expected_body|body|[load-balancing_expected_body](#schemaload-balancing_expected_body)|false|A case-insensitive sub-string to look for in the response body. If this string is not found, the origin will be marked as unhealthy. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» expected_codes|body|[load-balancing_expected_codes](#schemaload-balancing_expected_codes)|false|The expected HTTP response code or code range of the health check. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» follow_redirects|body|[load-balancing_follow_redirects](#schemaload-balancing_follow_redirects)|false|Follow redirects if returned by the origin. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» header|body|[load-balancing_header](#schemaload-balancing_header)|false|The HTTP request headers to send in the health check. It is recommended you set a Host header by default. The User-Agent header cannot be overridden. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» interval|body|[load-balancing_interval](#schemaload-balancing_interval)|false|The interval between each health check. Shorter intervals may improve failover time, but will increase load on the origins as we check from multiple locations.|
|» method|body|[load-balancing_method](#schemaload-balancing_method)|false|The method to use for the health check. This defaults to 'GET' for HTTP/HTTPS based checks and 'connection_established' for TCP based health checks.|
|» path|body|[load-balancing_path](#schemaload-balancing_path)|false|The endpoint path you want to conduct a health check against. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» port|body|[load-balancing_port](#schemaload-balancing_port)|false|The port number to connect to for the health check. Required for TCP, UDP, and SMTP checks. HTTP and HTTPS checks should only define the port when using a non-standard port (HTTP: default 80, HTTPS: default 443).|
|» probe_zone|body|[load-balancing_probe_zone](#schemaload-balancing_probe_zone)|false|Assign this monitor to emulate the specified zone while probing. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» retries|body|[load-balancing_retries](#schemaload-balancing_retries)|false|The number of retries to attempt in case of a timeout before marking the origin as unhealthy. Retries are attempted immediately.|
|» timeout|body|[load-balancing_timeout](#schemaload-balancing_timeout)|false|The timeout (in seconds) before marking the health check as failed.|
|» type|body|[load-balancing_type](#schemaload-balancing_type)|false|The protocol to use for the health check. Currently supported protocols are 'HTTP','HTTPS', 'TCP', 'ICMP-PING', 'UDP-ICMP', and 'SMTP'.|

|---|---|
|» type|http|
|» type|https|
|» type|tcp|
|» type|udp_icmp|
|» type|icmp_ping|
|» type|smtp|

<h3 id="create-pool-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[load-balancing_components-schemas-identifier](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» description|body|[load-balancing_schemas-description](#schemaload-balancing_schemas-description)|false|A human-readable description of the pool.|
|» enabled|body|[load-balancing_enabled](#schemaload-balancing_enabled)|false|Whether to enable (the default) or disable this pool. Disabled pools will not receive traffic and are excluded from health checks. Disabling a pool will cause any load balancers using it to failover to the next pool (if any).|
|» latitude|body|[load-balancing_latitude](#schemaload-balancing_latitude)|false|The latitude of the data center containing the origins used in this pool in decimal degrees. If this is set, longitude must also be set.|
|» load_shedding|body|[load-balancing_load_shedding](#schemaload-balancing_load_shedding)|false|Configures load shedding policies and percentages for the pool.|
|» longitude|body|[load-balancing_longitude](#schemaload-balancing_longitude)|false|The longitude of the data center containing the origins used in this pool in decimal degrees. If this is set, latitude must also be set.|
|» minimum_origins|body|[load-balancing_minimum_origins](#schemaload-balancing_minimum_origins)|false|The minimum number of origins that must be healthy for this pool to serve traffic. If the number of healthy origins falls below this number, the pool will be marked unhealthy and will failover to the next available pool.|
|» monitor|body|[load-balancing_monitor_id](#schemaload-balancing_monitor_id)|false|The ID of the Monitor to use for checking the health of origins within this pool.|
|» monitor_group|body|[load-balancing_monitor_group_id](#schemaload-balancing_monitor_group_id)|false|The ID of the Monitor Group to use for checking the health of origins within this pool.|
|» name|body|[load-balancing_name](#schemaload-balancing_name)|true|A short name (tag) for the pool. Only alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores are allowed.|
|» notification_email|body|[load-balancing_notification_email](#schemaload-balancing_notification_email)|false|This field is now deprecated. It has been moved to Cloudflare's Centralized Notification service https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/notifications/. The email address to send health status notifications to. This can be an individual mailbox or a mailing list. Multiple emails can be supplied as a comma delimited list.|
|» notification_filter|body|[load-balancing_notification_filter](#schemaload-balancing_notification_filter)|false|Filter pool and origin health notifications by resource type or health status. Use null to reset.|
|» origin_steering|body|[load-balancing_origin_steering](#schemaload-balancing_origin_steering)|false|Configures origin steering for the pool. Controls how origins are selected for new sessions and traffic without session affinity.|
|» origins|body|[load-balancing_origins](#schemaload-balancing_origins)|true|The list of origins within this pool. Traffic directed at this pool is balanced across all currently healthy origins, provided the pool itself is healthy.|

## Patch Pools

`PATCH /accounts/{account_id}/load_balancers/pools`

Apply changes to a number of existing pools, overwriting the supplied properties. Pools are ordered by ascending `name`. Returns the list of affected pools. Supports the standard pagination query parameters, either `limit`/`offset` or `per_page`/`page`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "notification_email": ""
}
```

This field is now deprecated in favor of Cloudflare Notifications for Load Balancing, so only resetting this field with an empty string `""` is accepted.|

<h3 id="update-pool-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|pool_id|path|[load-balancing_schemas-identifier](#schemaload-balancing_schemas-identifier)|true|none|

|body|body|object|true|none|
|» check_regions|body|[load-balancing_check_regions](#schemaload-balancing_check_regions)|false|A list of regions from which to run health checks. Null means every Cloudflare data center.|
|» description|body|[load-balancing_schemas-description](#schemaload-balancing_schemas-description)|false|A human-readable description of the pool.|
|» enabled|body|[load-balancing_enabled](#schemaload-balancing_enabled)|false|Whether to enable (the default) or disable this pool. Disabled pools will not receive traffic and are excluded from health checks. Disabling a pool will cause any load balancers using it to failover to the next pool (if any).|
|» health_sources|body|[load-balancing_health_sources](#schemaload-balancing_health_sources)|false|A list of health sources, ordered from highest to lowest priority, used to evaluate individual origin health and overall pool health. The load balancer uses the first source that has data and falls back to the next. Currently accepted values are null or the exact array ["regional", "global"]; any other combination is rejected. Null (the default) behaves like ["local", "global"]. ["regional", "global"] makes each region steer on its own health, falling back to the global decision when a region has no fresh data. Setting regional requires at least one region in check_regions.|
|» latitude|body|[load-balancing_latitude](#schemaload-balancing_latitude)|false|The latitude of the data center containing the origins used in this pool in decimal degrees. If this is set, longitude must also be set.|
|» load_shedding|body|[load-balancing_load_shedding](#schemaload-balancing_load_shedding)|false|Configures load shedding policies and percentages for the pool.|
|» longitude|body|[load-balancing_longitude](#schemaload-balancing_longitude)|false|The longitude of the data center containing the origins used in this pool in decimal degrees. If this is set, latitude must also be set.|
|» minimum_origins|body|[load-balancing_minimum_origins](#schemaload-balancing_minimum_origins)|false|The minimum number of origins that must be healthy for this pool to serve traffic. If the number of healthy origins falls below this number, the pool will be marked unhealthy and will failover to the next available pool.|

It has been moved to Cloudflare's Centralized Notification service https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/notifications/. The email address to send health status notifications to. This can be an individual mailbox or a mailing list. Multiple emails can be supplied as a comma delimited list.|
|» notification_filter|body|[load-balancing_notification_filter](#schemaload-balancing_notification_filter)|false|Filter pool and origin health notifications by resource type or health status. Use null to reset.|

<h3 id="patch-pool-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|» check_regions|body|[load-balancing_check_regions](#schemaload-balancing_check_regions)|false|A list of regions from which to run health checks. Null means every Cloudflare data center.|
|» description|body|[load-balancing_schemas-description](#schemaload-balancing_schemas-description)|false|A human-readable description of the pool.|
|» enabled|body|[load-balancing_enabled](#schemaload-balancing_enabled)|false|Whether to enable (the default) or disable this pool. Disabled pools will not receive traffic and are excluded from health checks. Disabling a pool will cause any load balancers using it to failover to the next pool (if any).|
|» health_sources|body|[load-balancing_health_sources](#schemaload-balancing_health_sources)|false|A list of health sources, ordered from highest to lowest priority, used to evaluate individual origin health and overall pool health. Null (the default) behaves like ["local", "global"]. ["regional", "global"] makes each region steer on its own health, falling back to the global decision when a region has no fresh data. Setting regional requires at least one region in check_regions.|

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/load_balancers/pools/{pool_id}/preview`

Preview pool health using provided monitor details. The returned preview_id can be used in the preview endpoint to retrieve the results.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "allow_insecure": true,
  "consecutive_down": 0,
  "consecutive_up": 0,
  "description": "Login page monitor",
  "expected_body": "alive",
  "expected_codes": "2xx",
  "follow_redirects": true,
  "header": {
    "Host": [
      "example.com"
    ],
    "X-App-ID": [
      "abc123"
    ]
  },
  "interval": 60,
  "method": "GET",
  "path": "/health",
  "port": 0,
  "probe_zone": "example.com",
  "retries": 2,
  "timeout": 5,
  "type": "https"
}
```

<h3 id="preview-pool-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pool_id|path|[load-balancing_schemas-identifier](#schemaload-balancing_schemas-identifier)|true|none|
|account_id|path|[load-balancing_components-schemas-identifier](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» allow_insecure|body|[load-balancing_allow_insecure](#schemaload-balancing_allow_insecure)|false|Do not validate the certificate when monitor use HTTPS. This parameter is currently only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» consecutive_down|body|[load-balancing_consecutive_down](#schemaload-balancing_consecutive_down)|false|To be marked unhealthy the monitored origin must fail this healthcheck N consecutive times.|
|» consecutive_up|body|[load-balancing_consecutive_up](#schemaload-balancing_consecutive_up)|false|To be marked healthy the monitored origin must pass this healthcheck N consecutive times.|
|» description|body|[load-balancing_description](#schemaload-balancing_description)|false|Object description.|
|» expected_body|body|[load-balancing_expected_body](#schemaload-balancing_expected_body)|false|A case-insensitive sub-string to look for in the response body. If this string is not found, the origin will be marked as unhealthy. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» expected_codes|body|[load-balancing_expected_codes](#schemaload-balancing_expected_codes)|false|The expected HTTP response code or code range of the health check. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» follow_redirects|body|[load-balancing_follow_redirects](#schemaload-balancing_follow_redirects)|false|Follow redirects if returned by the origin. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» header|body|[load-balancing_header](#schemaload-balancing_header)|false|The HTTP request headers to send in the health check. It is recommended you set a Host header by default. The User-Agent header cannot be overridden. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» interval|body|[load-balancing_interval](#schemaload-balancing_interval)|false|The interval between each health check. Shorter intervals may improve failover time, but will increase load on the origins as we check from multiple locations.|
|» method|body|[load-balancing_method](#schemaload-balancing_method)|false|The method to use for the health check. This defaults to 'GET' for HTTP/HTTPS based checks and 'connection_established' for TCP based health checks.|
|» path|body|[load-balancing_path](#schemaload-balancing_path)|false|The endpoint path you want to conduct a health check against. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» port|body|[load-balancing_port](#schemaload-balancing_port)|false|The port number to connect to for the health check. Required for TCP, UDP, and SMTP checks. HTTP and HTTPS checks should only define the port when using a non-standard port (HTTP: default 80, HTTPS: default 443).|
|» probe_zone|body|[load-balancing_probe_zone](#schemaload-balancing_probe_zone)|false|Assign this monitor to emulate the specified zone while probing. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» retries|body|[load-balancing_retries](#schemaload-balancing_retries)|false|The number of retries to attempt in case of a timeout before marking the origin as unhealthy. Retries are attempted immediately.|
|» timeout|body|[load-balancing_timeout](#schemaload-balancing_timeout)|false|The timeout (in seconds) before marking the health check as failed.|
|» type|body|[load-balancing_type](#schemaload-balancing_type)|false|The protocol to use for the health check. Currently supported protocols are 'HTTP','HTTPS', 'TCP', 'ICMP-PING', 'UDP-ICMP', and 'SMTP'.|

<h3 id="create-logpush-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[logpush_identifier](#schemalogpush_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» dataset|body|[logpush_dataset](#schemalogpush_dataset)|false|Name of the dataset. A list of supported datasets can be found on the [Developer Docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/reference/log-fields/).|
|» destination_conf|body|[logpush_destination_conf](#schemalogpush_destination_conf)|true|Uniquely identifies a resource (such as an s3 bucket) where data. will be pushed. Additional configuration parameters supported by the destination may be included.|
|» enabled|body|[logpush_enabled](#schemalogpush_enabled)|false|Flag that indicates if the job is enabled.|
|» filter|body|[logpush_filter](#schemalogpush_filter)|false|The filters to select the events to include and/or remove from your logs. For more information, refer to [Filters](https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/reference/filters/).|
|» filter_attack_traffic|body|[logpush_filter_attack_traffic](#schemalogpush_filter_attack_traffic)|false|When true, excludes DDoS attack traffic from logs. This option is supported for the `http_requests`, `firewall_events`, and `network_analytics_logs` datasets.|
|» frequency|body|[logpush_frequency](#schemalogpush_frequency)|false|**Deprecated.** This field is deprecated. Please use `max_upload_*` parameters instead. . The frequency at which Cloudflare sends batches of logs to your destination. Setting frequency to high sends your logs in larger quantities of smaller files. Setting frequency to low sends logs in smaller quantities of larger files.|
|» kind|body|[logpush_kind](#schemalogpush_kind)|false|The kind parameter (optional) is used to differentiate between Logpush and Edge Log Delivery jobs (when supported by the dataset).|
|» logpull_options|body|[logpush_logpull_options](#schemalogpush_logpull_options)|false|**Deprecated.** This field is deprecated. Use `output_options` instead. Configuration string. It specifies things like requested fields and timestamp formats. If migrating from the logpull api, copy the url (full url or just the query string) of your call here, and logpush will keep on making this call for you, setting start and end times appropriately.|
|» max_upload_bytes|body|[logpush_max_upload_bytes](#schemalogpush_max_upload_bytes)|false|The maximum uncompressed file size of a batch of logs. This setting value must be between `5 MB` and `1 GB`, or `0` to disable it. Note that you cannot set a minimum file size; this means that log files may be much smaller than this batch size.|
|» max_upload_interval_seconds|body|[logpush_max_upload_interval_seconds](#schemalogpush_max_upload_interval_seconds)|false|The maximum interval in seconds for log batches. This setting must be between 30 and 300 seconds (5 minutes), or `0` to disable it. Note that you cannot specify a minimum interval for log batches; this means that log files may be sent in shorter intervals than this.|
|» max_upload_records|body|[logpush_max_upload_records](#schemalogpush_max_upload_records)|false|The maximum number of log lines per batch. This setting must be between 1000 and 1,000,000 lines, or `0` to disable it. Note that you cannot specify a minimum number of log lines per batch; this means that log files may contain many fewer lines than this.|
|» name|body|[logpush_name](#schemalogpush_name)|false|Optional human readable job name. Not unique. Cloudflare suggests. that you set this to a meaningful string, like the domain name, to make it easier to identify your job.|
|» output_options|body|[logpush_output_options](#schemalogpush_output_options)|false|The structured replacement for `logpull_options`. When including this field, the `logpull_option` field will be ignored.|
|» ownership_challenge|body|[logpush_ownership_challenge](#schemalogpush_ownership_challenge)|false|Ownership challenge token to prove destination ownership.|

|» max_upload_interval_seconds|body|[logpush_max_upload_interval_seconds](#schemalogpush_max_upload_interval_seconds)|false|The maximum interval in seconds for log batches. This setting must be between 30 and 300 seconds (5 minutes), or `0` to disable it. Note that you cannot specify a minimum interval for log batches; this means that log files may be sent in shorter intervals than this.|
|» max_upload_records|body|[logpush_max_upload_records](#schemalogpush_max_upload_records)|false|The maximum number of log lines per batch. This setting must be between 1000 and 1,000,000 lines, or `0` to disable it. Note that you cannot specify a minimum number of log lines per batch; this means that log files may contain many fewer lines than this.|
|» name|body|[logpush_name](#schemalogpush_name)|false|Optional human readable job name. Not unique. Cloudflare suggests. that you set this to a meaningful string, like the domain name, to make it easier to identify your job.|
|» output_options|body|[logpush_output_options](#schemalogpush_output_options)|false|The structured replacement for `logpull_options`. When including this field, the `logpull_option` field will be ignored.|
|» ownership_challenge|body|[logpush_ownership_challenge](#schemalogpush_ownership_challenge)|false|Ownership challenge token to prove destination ownership.|

`PUT /accounts/{account_id}/logpush/transformers/{transformer_id}`

## Create an account dataset

<a id="opIdaccounts-logs-explorer-datasets-create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/logs/explorer/datasets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "dataset": "string",
    "fields": [
      {
        "enabled": true,
        "name": "string"
      }
    ],
    "filter": "string",
    "filter_attack_traffic": true
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/logs/explorer/datasets`

Create a new Log Explorer dataset for the account.

List available account datasets to see the dataset types and fields you
can use.

The `fields` property is optional. If not specified, all available fields
will be enabled.

For dataset field definitions, see: https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/logpush/logpush-job/datasets/


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "dataset": "string",
  "fields": [
    {
      "enabled": true,
      "name": "string"
    }
  ],
  "filter": "string",
  "filter_attack_traffic": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-account-dataset-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|Cloudflare account ID.|
|body|body|[lex_CreateDatasetRequest](#schemalex_createdatasetrequest)|true|none|
|» dataset|body|string|true|Dataset type name to create (e.g. `http_requests`).|
|» fields|body|[[lex_LogField](#schemalex_logfield)]|false|Controls which fields the API ingests. Defaults to all available<br>fields when absent.<br>|
|» filter|body|string|false|Optional Logpush filter predicate to restrict which events are ingested.<br>See [Logpush filters](https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/reference/filters/)<br>for syntax and examples.<br>|
|» filter_attack_traffic|body|boolean|false|Whether to filter attack traffic from the Logpush job. Defaults to<br>`true` for supported datasets when omitted. Supported datasets are<br>`http_requests`, `firewall_events`, and `network_analytics_logs`.<br>|

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/string/logs/explorer/datasets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

      }
    ],
    "filter": "string",
    "filter_attack_traffic": true
  }'
```

`POST /zones/{zone_id}/logs/explorer/datasets`

Create a new Log Explorer dataset for the zone.

List available zone datasets to see the dataset types and fields you
can use.

The `fields` property is optional. If not specified, all available fields
will be enabled.

For dataset field definitions, see: https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/logpush/logpush-job/datasets/


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "dataset": "string",
  "fields": [
    {
      "enabled": true,
      "name": "string"
    }
  ],
  "filter": "string",
  "filter_attack_traffic": true
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|

|» dataset|body|string|true|Dataset type name to create (e.g. `http_requests`).|
|» fields|body|[[lex_LogField](#schemalex_logfield)]|false|Controls which fields the API ingests. Defaults to all available<br>fields when absent.<br>|
|» filter|body|string|false|Optional Logpush filter predicate to restrict which events are ingested.<br>See [Logpush filters](https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/reference/filters/)<br>for syntax and examples.<br>|
|» filter_attack_traffic|body|boolean|false|Whether to filter attack traffic from the Logpush job. Defaults to<br>`true` for supported datasets when omitted. Supported datasets are<br>`http_requests`, `firewall_events`, and `network_analytics_logs`.<br>|

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/logs/explorer/query/sql`

Run a SQL query against account-level datasets.

Timestamp fields are RFC3339 strings. Filter with:
  WHERE {timestamp_field} >= now() - INTERVAL '30' DAY
  WHERE {timestamp_field} >= '2026-04-01T00:00:00Z'
  WHERE {timestamp_field} BETWEEN '2026-04-01T00:00:00Z' AND '2026-04-30T23:59:59Z'

List configured account datasets to see enabled account-level datasets.
Zone-level datasets will not appear here.
List available account datasets to inspect their schemas and timestamp fields.

For more information about the datasets, and the meaning of each field, check out https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/logpush/logpush-job/datasets/

```bash
curl 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/991fff3d2f1084b343f5a84db801fea8/logs/list?start=2022-06-06T16%3A00%3A00Z&end=2022-06-06T16%3A00%3A00Z&bucket=cloudflare-logs' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'R2-Access-Key-Id: 29a92f1a6e6887d79f3401a41' \
  -H 'R2-Secret-Access-Key: 869b6e19534a6715ab69a07d76492d673f8134d'
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/logs/list`

Lists R2 objects containing logs matching the provided query parameters.

<h3 id="list-log-files-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[logpull_AccountId](#schemalogpull_accountid)|true|Cloudflare account ID (32-character hex string).|
|R2-Access-Key-Id|header|[logpull_AccessKeyId](#schemalogpull_accesskeyid)|true|none|

|end|query|[logpull_TimestampRFC3339](#schemalogpull_timestamprfc3339)|true|End time in RFC3339 format.|

## Create DNS Protection rule.

<a id="opIdcreateDnsProtectionRule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/magic/advanced_dns_protection/configs/dns_protection/rules \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "block_any_queries": true,
    "burst_sensitivity": "string",
    "mode": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "profile_sensitivity": "string",
    "rate_sensitivity": "string",
    "scope": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/magic/advanced_dns_protection/configs/dns_protection/rules`

Create a DNS Protection rule for an account.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "block_any_queries": true,
  "burst_sensitivity": "string",
  "mode": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "profile_sensitivity": "string",
  "rate_sensitivity": "string",
  "scope": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-dns-protection-rule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[dos_identifier](#schemados_identifier)|true|The ID of the account.|
|body|body|[dos_NewDnsProtectionRule](#schemados_newdnsprotectionrule)|true|The new DNS Protection rule to add.|
|» block_any_queries|body|boolean|false|Whether to block DNS ANY queries. Optional. Defaults to true.|
|» burst_sensitivity|body|string|true|The burst sensitivity. Must be one of 'low', 'medium', 'high'.|
|» mode|body|string|true|The mode for DNS Protection. Must be one of 'enabled', 'disabled', 'monitoring'.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the DNS Protection rule. Value is relative to the 'scope' setting. For 'global' scope, name should be 'global'. For either the 'region' or 'datacenter' scope, name should be the actual name of the region or datacenter, e.g., 'wnam' or 'lax'.|
|» profile_sensitivity|body|string|true|The profile sensitivity. Recommended setting is 'low'. Must be one of 'low', 'medium', 'high', or 'very_high'.|
|» rate_sensitivity|body|string|true|The rate sensitivity. Must be one of 'low', 'medium', 'high'.|
|» scope|body|string|true|The scope for the DNS Protection rule. Must be one of 'global', 'region', or 'datacenter'.|

> Example responses

Each entry may carry an optional suffix that specifies which prefix lengths to match relative to the prefix length N: '{X,Y}' matches prefix lengths in the inclusive range [X, Y] where N <= X <= Y <= max (max is 32 for IPv4, 128 for IPv6), '{X}' matches exactly length X (equivalent to {X,X}), '+' is shorthand for {N, max} (the prefix and all more-specific subnets, including at length N itself; valid even when N is the maximum length). <h3 id="update-interconnect-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cf_interconnect_id|path|[magic_identifier](#schemamagic_identifier)|true|none|

|x-magic-new-hc-target|header|boolean|false|If true, the health check target in the request and response bodies will be presented using the new object format. Defaults to false.|
|body|body|[magic_interconnect_tunnel_update_request](#schemamagic_interconnect_tunnel_update_request)|true|none|
|» automatic_return_routing|body|[magic_automatic_return_routing](#schemamagic_automatic_return_routing)|false|True if automatic stateful return routing should be enabled for a tunnel, false otherwise. Requires the `coupler_integration` account flag to be enabled; requests setting this to `true` without that flag will be rejected.|
|» bgp|body|[magic_interconnect_bgp_config](#schemamagic_interconnect_bgp_config)|false|none|
|» description|body|[magic_interconnect_components-schemas-description](#schemamagic_interconnect_components-schemas-description)|false|An optional description of the interconnect.|
|» gre|body|object|false|none|
|» » cloudflare_endpoint|body|string|false|The IP address assigned to the Cloudflare side of the GRE tunnel created as part of the Interconnect.|
|» health_check|body|[magic_interconnect_health_check](#schemamagic_interconnect_health_check)|false|none|
|» interface_address|body|[magic_interface_address_interconnect](#schemamagic_interface_address_interconnect)|false|The IPv4 interface address for the interconnect. For MPLS Interconnects,<br>use a /30 or /31 prefix. For GRE Interconnects, a /30 or /31 prefix<br>may be used. Version 1.5 interconnects require a /31 prefix and may<br>also use a prefix from the account's authorized prefixes; otherwise,<br>select the subnet from RFC 1918 or the approved link-local ranges.<br>|
|» interface_address6|body|[magic_interface_address6](#schemamagic_interface_address6)|false|A 127 bit IPV6 prefix from within the virtual_subnet6 prefix space with the address being the first IP of the subnet and not same as the address of virtual_subnet6. Eg if virtual_subnet6 is 2606:54c1:7:0:a9fe:12d2::/127 , interface_address6 could be 2606:54c1:7:0:a9fe:12d2:1:200/127|
|» mtu|body|[magic_schemas-mtu](#schemamagic_schemas-mtu)|false|The Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) in bytes for the interconnect. The minimum value is 576.|
|» name|body|[magic_components-schemas-name](#schemamagic_components-schemas-name)|false|The name of the interconnect. The name cannot share a name with other tunnels.|

</aside>

## Create On-ramp

<a id="opIdonramps-create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/magic/cloud/onramps \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "adopted_hub_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "attached_hubs": [
      "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    ],
    "attached_vpcs": [
      "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    ],
    "cloud_asn": 0,
    "cloud_type": "AWS",
    "description": "string",
    "dynamic_routing": true,
    "hub_provider_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "install_routes_in_cloud": true,
    "install_routes_in_magic_wan": true,
    "manage_hub_to_hub_attachments": true,
    "manage_vpc_to_hub_attachments": true,
    "name": "string",
    "region": "string",
    "type": "OnrampTypeSingle",
    "vpc": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/magic/cloud/onramps`

Create a new On-ramp (Closed Beta).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "adopted_hub_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "attached_hubs": [
    "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  ],
  "attached_vpcs": [
    "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  ],
  "cloud_asn": 0,
  "cloud_type": "AWS",
  "description": "string",
  "dynamic_routing": true,
  "hub_provider_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "install_routes_in_cloud": true,
  "install_routes_in_magic_wan": true,
  "manage_hub_to_hub_attachments": true,
  "manage_vpc_to_hub_attachments": true,
  "name": "string",
  "region": "string",
  "type": "OnrampTypeSingle",
  "vpc": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
}
```

<h3 id="create-on-ramp-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[mcn_account_id](#schemamcn_account_id)|true|none|
|forwarded|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[mcn_create_onramp_request](#schemamcn_create_onramp_request)|true|none|
|» adopted_hub_id|body|[mcn_resource_id](#schemamcn_resource_id)|false|none|
|» attached_hubs|body|[[mcn_resource_id](#schemamcn_resource_id)]|false|none|
|» attached_vpcs|body|[[mcn_resource_id](#schemamcn_resource_id)]|false|none|
|» cloud_asn|body|integer(uint32)|false|Sets the cloud-side ASN. If unset or zero, the cloud's default ASN takes effect.|
|» cloud_type|body|[mcn_onramp_cloud_type](#schemamcn_onramp_cloud_type)|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|none|
|» dynamic_routing|body|boolean|true|Enables BGP routing. When enabling this feature, set both install_routes_in_cloud and install_routes_in_magic_wan to false.|
|» hub_provider_id|body|[mcn_provider_id](#schemamcn_provider_id)|false|none|
|» install_routes_in_cloud|body|boolean|true|none|
|» install_routes_in_magic_wan|body|boolean|true|none|
|» manage_hub_to_hub_attachments|body|boolean|false|none|
|» manage_vpc_to_hub_attachments|body|boolean|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|none|
|» region|body|string|false|none|
|» type|body|[mcn_onramp_type](#schemamcn_onramp_type)|true|none|
|» vpc|body|[mcn_resource_id](#schemamcn_resource_id)|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» cloud_type|AWS|
|» cloud_type|AZURE|
|» cloud_type|GOOGLE|
|» type|OnrampTypeSingle|
|» type|OnrampTypeHub|

## Update Magic WAN Address Space

<a id="opIdonramps-mwan-addr-space-update"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/magic/cloud/onramps/magic_wan_address_space \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "prefixes": [
      "192.168.0.0/16"
    ]
  }'
```

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
api_email & api_key & api_token
</aside>

## Update On-ramp

<a id="opIdonramps-update"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/magic/cloud/onramps/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "attached_hubs": [
      "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    ],
    "attached_vpcs": [
      "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    ],
    "description": "string",
    "install_routes_in_cloud": true,
    "install_routes_in_magic_wan": true,
    "manage_hub_to_hub_attachments": true,
    "manage_vpc_to_hub_attachments": true,
    "name": "string",
    "vpc": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  }'
```

`PUT /accounts/{account_id}/magic/cloud/onramps/{onramp_id}`

Update an On-ramp (Closed Beta).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "attached_hubs": [
    "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  ],
  "attached_vpcs": [
    "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  ],
  "description": "string",
  "install_routes_in_cloud": true,
  "install_routes_in_magic_wan": true,
  "manage_hub_to_hub_attachments": true,
  "manage_vpc_to_hub_attachments": true,
  "name": "string",
  "vpc": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[mcn_account_id](#schemamcn_account_id)|true|none|
|onramp_id|path|[mcn_onramp_id](#schemamcn_onramp_id)|true|none|
|body|body|[mcn_update_onramp_request](#schemamcn_update_onramp_request)|true|none|
|» attached_hubs|body|[[mcn_resource_id](#schemamcn_resource_id)]|false|none|
|» attached_vpcs|body|[[mcn_resource_id](#schemamcn_resource_id)]|false|none|
|» description|body|string|false|none|
|» install_routes_in_cloud|body|boolean|false|none|
|» install_routes_in_magic_wan|body|boolean|false|none|
|» manage_hub_to_hub_attachments|body|boolean|false|none|
|» manage_vpc_to_hub_attachments|body|boolean|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|none|
|» vpc|body|[mcn_resource_id](#schemamcn_resource_id)|false|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
api_email & api_key & api_token
</aside>

## Apply On-ramp

<a id="opIdonramps-apply"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/magic/cloud/onramps/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/apply \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/magic/cloud/onramps/{onramp_id}/apply`

Apply an On-ramp (Closed Beta).

<h3 id="apply-on-ramp-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[mcn_account_id](#schemamcn_account_id)|true|none|
|onramp_id|path|[mcn_onramp_id](#schemamcn_onramp_id)|true|none|

## Create Cloud Integration

<a id="opIdproviders-create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/magic/cloud/providers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{

    "description": "string",
    "friendly_name": "string"
  }'
```

## List GRE tunnels

<a id="opIdmagic-gre-tunnels-list-gre-tunnels"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/magic/gre_tunnels \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/magic/gre_tunnels`

<h3 id="create-an-ipsec-tunnel-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[magic_identifier](#schemamagic_identifier)|true|none|
|x-magic-new-hc-target|header|boolean|false|If true, the health check target in the request and response bodies will be presented using the new object format. Defaults to false.|
|body|body|[magic_ipsec_tunnel_add_request](#schemamagic_ipsec_tunnel_add_request)|true|none|
|» automatic_return_routing|body|[magic_automatic_return_routing](#schemamagic_automatic_return_routing)|false|True if automatic stateful return routing should be enabled for a tunnel, false otherwise. Requires the `coupler_integration` account flag to be enabled; requests setting this to `true` without that flag will be rejected.|
|» bgp|body|[magic_bgp_config](#schemamagic_bgp_config)|false|none|
|» cloudflare_endpoint|body|[magic_cloudflare_ipsec_endpoint](#schemamagic_cloudflare_ipsec_endpoint)|true|The IP address assigned to the Cloudflare side of the IPsec tunnel.|
|» custom_remote_identities|body|[magic_custom_remote_identities](#schemamagic_custom_remote_identities)|false|none|
|» customer_endpoint|body|[magic_customer_ipsec_endpoint](#schemamagic_customer_ipsec_endpoint)|false|The IP address assigned to the customer side of the IPsec tunnel. Not required, but must be set for proactive traceroutes to work.|
|» description|body|[magic_components-schemas-description](#schemamagic_components-schemas-description)|false|An optional description forthe IPsec tunnel.|
|» health_check|body|[magic_tunnel_health_check](#schemamagic_tunnel_health_check)|false|none|
|» interface_address|body|[magic_interface_address](#schemamagic_interface_address)|true|A 31-bit prefix (/31 in CIDR notation) supporting two hosts, one for each side of the tunnel. Select the subnet from the following private IP space: 10.0.0.0–10.255.255.255, 172.16.0.0–172.31.255.255, 192.168.0.0–192.168.255.255.|
|» interface_address6|body|[magic_interface_address6](#schemamagic_interface_address6)|false|A 127 bit IPV6 prefix from within the virtual_subnet6 prefix space with the address being the first IP of the subnet and not same as the address of virtual_subnet6. Eg if virtual_subnet6 is 2606:54c1:7:0:a9fe:12d2::/127 , interface_address6 could be 2606:54c1:7:0:a9fe:12d2:1:200/127|
|» name|body|[magic_ipsec_tunnel_name](#schemamagic_ipsec_tunnel_name)|true|The name of the IPsec tunnel. The name cannot share a name with other tunnels.|
|» psk|body|[magic_psk](#schemamagic_psk)|false|A randomly generated or provided string for use in the IPsec tunnel.|
|» replay_protection|body|[magic_replay_protection](#schemamagic_replay_protection)|false|If `true`, then IPsec replay protection will be supported in the Cloudflare-to-customer direction.|

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/magic/ipsec_tunnels/psk`

Sets Pre-Shared Keys for multiple IPsec tunnels associated with an account. Use `?validate_only=true` as an optional query parameter to only run validation without persisting changes. After PSKs are applied, they are immediately persisted to Cloudflare's edge and cannot be retrieved later. Store the PSKs in a safe place.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "psks": [
    {
      "id": {},
      "psk": "O3bwKSjnaoCxDoUxjcq4Rk8ZKkezQUiy"
    }
  ]
}
```

|» automatic_return_routing|body|[magic_automatic_return_routing](#schemamagic_automatic_return_routing)|false|True if automatic stateful return routing should be enabled for a tunnel, false otherwise. Requires the `coupler_integration` account flag to be enabled; requests setting this to `true` without that flag will be rejected.|
|» bgp|body|[magic_bgp_config](#schemamagic_bgp_config)|false|none|
|» cloudflare_endpoint|body|[magic_cloudflare_ipsec_endpoint](#schemamagic_cloudflare_ipsec_endpoint)|true|The IP address assigned to the Cloudflare side of the IPsec tunnel.|
|» custom_remote_identities|body|[magic_custom_remote_identities](#schemamagic_custom_remote_identities)|false|none|
|» customer_endpoint|body|[magic_customer_ipsec_endpoint](#schemamagic_customer_ipsec_endpoint)|false|The IP address assigned to the customer side of the IPsec tunnel. Not required, but must be set for proactive traceroutes to work.|
|» description|body|[magic_components-schemas-description](#schemamagic_components-schemas-description)|false|An optional description forthe IPsec tunnel.|
|» health_check|body|[magic_tunnel_health_check](#schemamagic_tunnel_health_check)|false|none|
|» interface_address|body|[magic_interface_address](#schemamagic_interface_address)|true|A 31-bit prefix (/31 in CIDR notation) supporting two hosts, one for each side of the tunnel. Select the subnet from the following private IP space: 10.0.0.0–10.255.255.255, 172.16.0.0–172.31.255.255, 192.168.0.0–192.168.255.255.|
|» interface_address6|body|[magic_interface_address6](#schemamagic_interface_address6)|false|A 127 bit IPV6 prefix from within the virtual_subnet6 prefix space with the address being the first IP of the subnet and not same as the address of virtual_subnet6. Eg if virtual_subnet6 is 2606:54c1:7:0:a9fe:12d2::/127 , interface_address6 could be 2606:54c1:7:0:a9fe:12d2:1:200/127|
|» name|body|[magic_ipsec_tunnel_name](#schemamagic_ipsec_tunnel_name)|true|The name of the IPsec tunnel. The name cannot share a name with other tunnels.|
|» psk|body|[magic_psk](#schemamagic_psk)|false|A randomly generated or provided string for use in the IPsec tunnel.|
|» replay_protection|body|[magic_replay_protection](#schemamagic_replay_protection)|false|If `true`, then IPsec replay protection will be supported in the Cloudflare-to-customer direction.|
