## List videos

<a id="opIdstream-videos-list-videos"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/stream \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/stream`

Lists up to 1000 videos from a single request. For a specific range, refer to the optional parameters.

<h3 id="list-videos-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[stream_account_identifier](#schemastream_account_identifier)|true|none|

|asc|query|[stream_asc](#schemastream_asc)|false|none|
|video_name|query|[stream_video_name](#schemastream_video_name)|false|none|
|search|query|[stream_search](#schemastream_search)|false|none|
|start|query|[stream_start](#schemastream_start)|false|none|
|end|query|[stream_end](#schemastream_end)|false|none|
|include_counts|query|[stream_include_counts](#schemastream_include_counts)|false|none|
|id|query|string|false|Filter by video ID(s). Can be a single ID or a comma-separated list of IDs.|
|name|query|string|false|Filter by video name/UID(s). Can be a single name or a comma-separated list.|
|live_input_id|query|string|false|Filter by live input ID to find videos associated with a specific live stream.|
|before|query|string(date-time)|false|Alias for 'end'. Returns videos created before this date/time (RFC 3339 format).|
|after|query|string(date-time)|false|Alias for 'start'. Returns videos created after this date/time (RFC 3339 format).|
|limit|query|integer|false|Maximum number of videos to return (default 1000, max 1000).|

## Initiate video uploads using TUS

<a id="opIdstream-videos-initiate-video-uploads-using-tus"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/stream \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'Tus-Resumable: 1.0.0' \
  -H 'Upload-Length: 0'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/stream`

Initiates a video upload using the TUS protocol. On success, the server responds with a status code 201 (created) and includes a `location` header to indicate where the content should be uploaded. Refer to https://tus.io for protocol details.

<h3 id="initiate-video-uploads-using-tus-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Tus-Resumable|header|[stream_tus_resumable](#schemastream_tus_resumable)|true|none|
|Upload-Creator|header|[stream_creator](#schemastream_creator)|false|none|
|Upload-Length|header|[stream_upload_length](#schemastream_upload_length)|true|none|
|Upload-Metadata|header|[stream_upload_metadata](#schemastream_upload_metadata)|false|none|
|account_id|path|[stream_account_identifier](#schemastream_account_identifier)|true|none|
|direct_user|query|[stream_direct_user](#schemastream_direct_user)|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Tus-Resumable|1.0.0|

> Example responses

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

<h3 id="initiate-video-uploads-using-tus-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Initiate video uploads using TUS response. Returns a 201 Created status with Location header for TUS uploads.|None|
|4XX|Client Error|Initiate video uploads using TUS response failure.|[stream_api-response-common-failure](#schemastream_api-response-common-failure)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|201|Location|string||The URL where the upload should be sent.|
|201|Stream-Media-ID|string||The unique identifier for the video being uploaded.|
|201|Tus-Resumable|string||The TUS protocol version.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
api_email & api_key & api_token
</aside>

## Upload videos from a URL

<a id="opIdstream-videos-upload-videos-from-a-url"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/stream/copy \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "allowedOrigins": [
      "example.com"
    ],
    "creator": "creator-id_abcde12345",
    "input": "https://example.com/myvideo.mp4",
    "meta": {
      "name": "video12345.mp4"
    },
    "name": "myvideo.mp4",
    "requireSignedURLs": true,
    "scheduledDeletion": "2014-01-02T02:20:00Z",
    "thumbnailTimestampPct": 0.529241,
    "url": "https://example.com/myvideo.mp4",
    "watermark": {
      "uid": "ea95132c15732412d22c1476fa83f27a"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/stream/copy`

Uploads a video to Stream from a provided URL.

> Body parameter

```json
{

    "example.com"
  ],

  },

  "requireSignedURLs": true,
  "scheduledDeletion": "2014-01-02T02:20:00Z",

  "url": "https://example.com/myvideo.mp4",
  "watermark": {
    "uid": "ea95132c15732412d22c1476fa83f27a"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="upload-videos-from-a-url-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[stream_account_identifier](#schemastream_account_identifier)|true|none|
|Upload-Creator|header|[stream_creator](#schemastream_creator)|false|none|
|body|body|[stream_video_copy_request](#schemastream_video_copy_request)|true|none|
|» allowedOrigins|body|[stream_allowedOrigins](#schemastream_allowedorigins)|false|Lists the origins allowed to display the video. Enter allowed origin domains in an array and use `*` for wildcard subdomains. Empty arrays allow the video to be viewed on any origin.|
|» creator|body|[stream_creator](#schemastream_creator)|false|A user-defined identifier for the media creator.|
|» input|body|string(uri)|false|A video's URL. The server must be publicly routable and support `HTTP HEAD` requests and `HTTP GET` range requests. The server should respond to `HTTP HEAD` requests with a `content-range` header that includes the size of the file. This is the preferred field over `url`.|
|» meta|body|[stream_media_metadata](#schemastream_media_metadata)|false|A user modifiable key-value store used to reference other systems of record for managing videos.|
|» name|body|string|false|A video's name. Used for legacy compatibility.|
|» requireSignedURLs|body|[stream_requireSignedURLs](#schemastream_requiresignedurls)|false|Indicates whether the video can be a accessed using the UID. When set to `true`, a signed token must be generated with a signing key to view the video.|
|» scheduledDeletion|body|[stream_scheduledDeletion](#schemastream_scheduleddeletion)|false|Indicates the date and time at which the video will be deleted. Omit the field to indicate no change, or include with a `null` value to remove an existing scheduled deletion. If specified, must be at least 30 days from upload time.|
|» thumbnailTimestampPct|body|[stream_thumbnailTimestampPct](#schemastream_thumbnailtimestamppct)|false|The timestamp for a thumbnail image calculated as a percentage value of the video's duration. To convert from a second-wise timestamp to a percentage, divide the desired timestamp by the total duration of the video.  If this value is not set, the default thumbnail image is taken from 0s of the video.|
|» url|body|string(uri)|false|A video's URL. The server must be publicly routable and support `HTTP HEAD` requests and `HTTP GET` range requests. The server should respond to `HTTP HEAD` requests with a `content-range` header that includes the size of the file. This field is deprecated in favor of `input`.|
|» watermark|body|[stream_watermark_at_upload](#schemastream_watermark_at_upload)|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|

|» scheduledDeletion|body|[stream_scheduledDeletion](#schemastream_scheduleddeletion)|false|Indicates the date and time at which the video will be deleted. Omit the field to indicate no change, or include with a `null` value to remove an existing scheduled deletion. If specified, must be at least 30 days from upload time.|
|» thumbnailTimestampPct|body|[stream_thumbnailTimestampPct](#schemastream_thumbnailtimestamppct)|false|The timestamp for a thumbnail image calculated as a percentage value of the video's duration. To convert from a second-wise timestamp to a percentage, divide the desired timestamp by the total duration of the video.  If this value is not set, the default thumbnail image is taken from 0s of the video.|
|» watermark|body|[stream_watermark_at_upload](#schemastream_watermark_at_upload)|false|none|

|» publicDetails|body|object|false|Public details for the video including title, share link, channel link, and logo.|

|» » logo|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » share_link|body|string \| null|false|none|

|» scheduledDeletion|body|[stream_scheduledDeletion](#schemastream_scheduleddeletion)|false|Indicates the date and time at which the video will be deleted. Omit the field to indicate no change, or include with a `null` value to remove an existing scheduled deletion. If specified, must be at least 30 days from upload time.|
|» thumbnailTimestampPct|body|[stream_thumbnailTimestampPct](#schemastream_thumbnailtimestamppct)|false|The timestamp for a thumbnail image calculated as a percentage value of the video's duration. To convert from a second-wise timestamp to a percentage, divide the desired timestamp by the total duration of the video.  If this value is not set, the default thumbnail image is taken from 0s of the video.|
|» uid|body|string|false|The unique identifier for the video. Can be used to verify the video being updated.|
|» uploadExpiry|body|[stream_oneTimeUploadExpiry](#schemastream_onetimeuploadexpiry)|false|The date and time when the video upload URL is no longer valid for direct user uploads.|

## Create signed URL tokens for videos

<a id="opIdstream-videos-create-signed-url-tokens-for-videos"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/stream/ea95132c15732412d22c1476fa83f27a/token \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "accessRules": [
      {
        "action": "block",
        "country": [
          "US",
          "MX"
        ],
        "type": "ip.geoip.country"
      },
      {
        "action": "allow",
        "ip": [
          "93.184.216.0/24",
          "2400:cb00::/32"
        ],
        "type": "ip.src"
      },
      {
        "action": "block",
        "type": "any"
      }
    ],
    "downloadable": false,
    "exp": 0,
    "flags": {
      "original": false
    },
    "id": "ab0d4ef71g4425f8dcba9041231813000",
    "nbf": 0,
    "pem": ""
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/stream/{identifier}/token`

Creates a signed URL token for a video. If a body is not provided in the request, a token is created with default values.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "accessRules": [
    {
      "action": "block",
      "country": [
        "US",
        "MX"
      ],
      "type": "ip.geoip.country"
    },
    {
      "action": "allow",
      "ip": [
        "93.184.216.0/24",
        "2400:cb00::/32"
      ],
      "type": "ip.src"
    },
    {
      "action": "block",
      "type": "any"
    }
  ],
  "downloadable": false,
  "exp": 0,
  "flags": {
    "original": false
  },
  "id": "ab0d4ef71g4425f8dcba9041231813000",
  "nbf": 0,
  "pem": ""
}
```

<h3 id="create-signed-url-tokens-for-videos-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|identifier|path|[stream_identifier](#schemastream_identifier)|true|none|
|account_id|path|[stream_account_identifier](#schemastream_account_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[stream_signed_token_request](#schemastream_signed_token_request)|true|none|
|» accessRules|body|[[stream_accessRules](#schemastream_accessrules)]|false|The optional list of access rule constraints on the token. Access can be blocked or allowed based on an IP, IP range, or by country. Access rules are evaluated from first to last. If a rule matches, the associated action is applied and no further rules are evaluated.|
|» downloadable|body|boolean|false|The optional boolean value that enables using signed tokens to access MP4 download links for a video.|
|» exp|body|integer|false|The optional unix epoch timestamp that specficies the time after a token is not accepted. The maximum time specification is 24 hours from issuing time. If this field is not set, the default is one hour after issuing.|
|» flags|body|object|false|Optional flags for the signed token.|
|» » original|body|boolean|false|Whether to return the original video without transformations.|
|» id|body|string|false|The optional ID of a Stream signing key. If present, the `pem` field is also required.|
|» nbf|body|integer|false|The optional unix epoch timestamp that specifies the time before a the token is not accepted. If this field is not set, the default is one hour before issuing.|
|» pem|body|string|false|The optional base64 encoded private key in PEM format associated with a Stream signing key. If present, the `id` field is also required.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
```

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-stream-video-clipping">Stream Video Clipping</h1>

## Clip videos given a start and end time

<a id="opIdstream-video-clipping-clip-videos-given-a-start-and-end-time"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/stream/clip \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "allowedOrigins": [
      "example.com"
    ],
    "clippedFromVideoUID": "023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353",
    "creator": "creator-id_abcde12345",
    "endTimeSeconds": 0,
    "input": "https://example.com/myvideo.mp4",
    "meta": {
      "name": "video12345.mp4"
    },
    "name": "myvideo.mp4",
    "requireSignedURLs": true,
    "scheduledDeletion": "2014-01-02T02:20:00Z",
    "startTimeSeconds": 0,
    "thumbnailTimestampPct": 0.529241,
    "url": "https://example.com/myvideo.mp4",
    "watermark": {
      "uid": "ea95132c15732412d22c1476fa83f27a"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/stream/clip`

Clips a video based on the specified start and end times provided in seconds.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "allowedOrigins": [
    "example.com"
  ],
  "clippedFromVideoUID": "023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353",
  "creator": "creator-id_abcde12345",
  "endTimeSeconds": 0,
  "input": "https://example.com/myvideo.mp4",
  "meta": {
    "name": "video12345.mp4"
  },
  "name": "myvideo.mp4",
  "requireSignedURLs": true,
  "scheduledDeletion": "2014-01-02T02:20:00Z",
  "startTimeSeconds": 0,
  "thumbnailTimestampPct": 0.529241,
  "url": "https://example.com/myvideo.mp4",
  "watermark": {
    "uid": "ea95132c15732412d22c1476fa83f27a"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="clip-videos-given-a-start-and-end-time-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[stream_account_identifier](#schemastream_account_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[stream_videoClipStandard](#schemastream_videoclipstandard)|true|none|
|» allowedOrigins|body|[stream_allowedOrigins](#schemastream_allowedorigins)|false|Lists the origins allowed to display the video. Enter allowed origin domains in an array and use `*` for wildcard subdomains. Empty arrays allow the video to be viewed on any origin.|
|» clippedFromVideoUID|body|[stream_clipped_from_video_uid](#schemastream_clipped_from_video_uid)|true|The unique video identifier (UID).|
|» creator|body|[stream_creator](#schemastream_creator)|false|A user-defined identifier for the media creator.|
|» endTimeSeconds|body|[stream_end_time_seconds](#schemastream_end_time_seconds)|true|Specifies the end time for the video clip in seconds.|
|» input|body|string(uri)|false|A video's URL. Preferred over 'url'.|
|» meta|body|[stream_media_metadata](#schemastream_media_metadata)|false|A user modifiable key-value store used to reference other systems of record for managing videos.|
|» name|body|string|false|A name for the video.|
|» requireSignedURLs|body|[stream_requireSignedURLs](#schemastream_requiresignedurls)|false|Indicates whether the video can be a accessed using the UID. When set to `true`, a signed token must be generated with a signing key to view the video.|
|» scheduledDeletion|body|[stream_scheduledDeletion](#schemastream_scheduleddeletion)|false|Indicates the date and time at which the video will be deleted. Omit the field to indicate no change, or include with a `null` value to remove an existing scheduled deletion. If specified, must be at least 30 days from upload time.|
|» startTimeSeconds|body|[stream_start_time_seconds](#schemastream_start_time_seconds)|true|Specifies the start time for the video clip in seconds.|
|» thumbnailTimestampPct|body|[stream_thumbnailTimestampPct](#schemastream_thumbnailtimestamppct)|false|The timestamp for a thumbnail image calculated as a percentage value of the video's duration. To convert from a second-wise timestamp to a percentage, divide the desired timestamp by the total duration of the video.  If this value is not set, the default thumbnail image is taken from 0s of the video.|
|» url|body|string(uri)|false|A video's URL (legacy field, use 'input' instead).|
|» watermark|body|[stream_watermarkAtUpload](#schemastream_watermarkatupload)|false|none|

> Example responses

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/stream/keys`

Creates an RSA private key in PEM and JWK formats. Key files are only displayed once after creation. Keys are created, used, and deleted independently of videos, and every key can sign any video.

## Create a live input

<a id="opIdstream-live-inputs-create-a-live-input"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/stream/live_inputs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "defaultCreator": "string",
    "deleteRecordingAfterDays": 45,
    "enabled": true,
    "meta": {
      "name": "test stream 1"
    },
    "preferLowLatency": true,
    "recording": {
      "hideLiveViewerCount": false,
      "mode": "off",
      "requireSignedURLs": false,
      "timeoutSeconds": 0
    }
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/stream/live_inputs`

Creates a live input, and returns credentials that you or your users can use to stream live video to Cloudflare Stream.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "defaultCreator": "string",
  "deleteRecordingAfterDays": 45,
  "enabled": true,
  "meta": {
    "name": "test stream 1"
  },
  "preferLowLatency": true,
  "recording": {
    "hideLiveViewerCount": false,
    "mode": "off",
    "requireSignedURLs": false,
    "timeoutSeconds": 0
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-live-input-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[stream_identifier-2](#schemastream_identifier-2)|true|none|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|Prevents duplicate live inputs from being created when retrying this request. The key is scoped to the account, may contain up to 255 bytes, and expires six hours after the live input is created. Reusing a key for a deleted input before expiry returns a 409 Conflict response.|
|body|body|[stream_create_input_request](#schemastream_create_input_request)|true|none|
|» defaultCreator|body|[stream_live_input_default_creator](#schemastream_live_input_default_creator)|false|Sets the creator ID asssociated with this live input.|
|» deleteRecordingAfterDays|body|[stream_live_input_recording_deletion](#schemastream_live_input_recording_deletion)|false|Indicates the number of days after which the live inputs recordings will be deleted. When a stream completes and the recording is ready, the value is used to calculate a scheduled deletion date for that recording. Omit the field to indicate no change, or include with a `null` value to remove an existing scheduled deletion.|
|» enabled|body|[stream_live_input_enabled](#schemastream_live_input_enabled)|false|Indicates whether the live input is enabled and can accept streams.|
|» meta|body|[stream_live_input_metadata](#schemastream_live_input_metadata)|false|A user modifiable key-value store used to reference other systems of record for managing live inputs.|
|» preferLowLatency|body|[stream_live_input_prefer_low_latency](#schemastream_live_input_prefer_low_latency)|false|When enabled, the live stream is delivered using Low-Latency HLS (LL-HLS), reducing glass-to-glass latency for viewers at the cost of reduced player compatibility.|
|» recording|body|[stream_live_input_recording_settings](#schemastream_live_input_recording_settings)|false|Records the input to a Cloudflare Stream video. Behavior depends on the mode. In most cases, the video will initially be viewable as a live video and transition to on-demand after a condition is satisfied.|

## Update a live input

<a id="opIdstream-live-inputs-update-a-live-input"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/stream/live_inputs/66be4bf738797e01e1fca35a7bdecdcd \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "defaultCreator": "string",
    "deleteRecordingAfterDays": 45,
    "enabled": true,
    "meta": {
      "name": "test stream 1"
    },
    "preferLowLatency": true,
    "recording": {
      "hideLiveViewerCount": false,
      "mode": "off",
      "requireSignedURLs": false,
      "timeoutSeconds": 0
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /accounts/{account_id}/stream/live_inputs/{live_input_identifier}`

Updates a specified live input.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "defaultCreator": "string",
  "deleteRecordingAfterDays": 45,
  "enabled": true,
  "meta": {
    "name": "test stream 1"
  },
  "preferLowLatency": true,
  "recording": {
    "hideLiveViewerCount": false,
    "mode": "off",
    "requireSignedURLs": false,
    "timeoutSeconds": 0
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-live-input-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|live_input_identifier|path|[stream_live_input_identifier](#schemastream_live_input_identifier)|true|none|
|account_id|path|[stream_identifier-2](#schemastream_identifier-2)|true|none|
|body|body|[stream_update_input_request](#schemastream_update_input_request)|true|none|
|» defaultCreator|body|[stream_live_input_default_creator](#schemastream_live_input_default_creator)|false|Sets the creator ID asssociated with this live input.|
|» deleteRecordingAfterDays|body|[stream_live_input_recording_deletion](#schemastream_live_input_recording_deletion)|false|Indicates the number of days after which the live inputs recordings will be deleted. When a stream completes and the recording is ready, the value is used to calculate a scheduled deletion date for that recording. Omit the field to indicate no change, or include with a `null` value to remove an existing scheduled deletion.|
|» enabled|body|[stream_live_input_enabled](#schemastream_live_input_enabled)|false|Indicates whether the live input is enabled and can accept streams.|
|» meta|body|[stream_live_input_metadata](#schemastream_live_input_metadata)|false|A user modifiable key-value store used to reference other systems of record for managing live inputs.|
|» preferLowLatency|body|[stream_live_input_prefer_low_latency](#schemastream_live_input_prefer_low_latency)|false|When enabled, the live stream is delivered using Low-Latency HLS (LL-HLS), reducing glass-to-glass latency for viewers at the cost of reduced player compatibility.|
|» recording|body|[stream_live_input_recording_settings](#schemastream_live_input_recording_settings)|false|Records the input to a Cloudflare Stream video. Behavior depends on the mode. In most cases, the video will initially be viewable as a live video and transition to on-demand after a condition is satisfied.|

```bash
    "streamKey": "uzya-f19y-g2g9-a2ee-51j2",
    "url": "rtmp://a.rtmp.youtube.com/live2"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/stream/live_inputs/{live_input_identifier}/outputs`

Creates a new output that can be used to simulcast or restream live video to other RTMP or SRT destinations. Outputs are always linked to a specific live input — one live input can have many outputs.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "streamKey": "uzya-f19y-g2g9-a2ee-51j2",
  "url": "rtmp://a.rtmp.youtube.com/live2"
}
```

|account_id|path|[stream_identifier-2](#schemastream_identifier-2)|true|none|
|body|body|[stream_create_output_request](#schemastream_create_output_request)|true|none|
|» enabled|body|[stream_output_enabled](#schemastream_output_enabled)|false|When enabled, live video streamed to the associated live input will be sent to the output URL. When disabled, live video will not be sent to the output URL, even when streaming to the associated live input. Use this to control precisely when you start and stop simulcasting to specific destinations like YouTube and Twitch.|
|» streamKey|body|[stream_output_streamKey](#schemastream_output_streamkey)|true|The streamKey used to authenticate against an output's target.|
|» url|body|[stream_output_url](#schemastream_output_url)|true|The URL an output uses to restream.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{

  "messages": [],
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/stream/live_inputs/{live_input_identifier}/rotate_keys`

Rotates the credentials for a live input without changing its identifier. Old credentials are revoked, broadcasts using stale credentials are automatically disconnected shortly after rotation, and the response returns refreshed credentials.

## Create watermark profiles via basic upload

<a id="opIdstream-watermark-profile-create-watermark-profiles-via-basic-upload"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/stream/watermarks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

  -d '{
    "name": "Marketing Videos",
    "opacity": 0.75,
    "padding": 0.1,
    "position": "center",
    "scale": 0.1,
    "url": "http://example.com"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/stream/watermarks`

Creates watermark profiles using a single `HTTP POST multipart/form-data` request.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Marketing Videos",
  "opacity": 0.75,
  "padding": 0.1,
  "position": "center",
  "scale": 0.1,
  "url": "http://example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="create-watermark-profiles-via-basic-upload-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[stream_account_identifier](#schemastream_account_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|[stream_name](#schemastream_name)|false|A short description of the watermark profile.|
|» opacity|body|[stream_opacity](#schemastream_opacity)|false|The translucency of the image. A value of `0.0` makes the image completely transparent, and `1.0` makes the image completely opaque. Note that if the image is already semi-transparent, setting this to `1.0` will not make the image completely opaque.|
|» padding|body|[stream_padding](#schemastream_padding)|false|The whitespace between the adjacent edges (determined by position) of the video and the image. `0.0` indicates no padding, and `1.0` indicates a fully padded video width or length, as determined by the algorithm.|
|» position|body|[stream_position](#schemastream_position)|false|The location of the image. Valid positions are: `upperRight`, `upperLeft`, `lowerLeft`, `lowerRight`, and `center`. Note that `center` ignores the `padding` parameter.|
|» scale|body|[stream_scale](#schemastream_scale)|false|The size of the image relative to the overall size of the video. This parameter will adapt to horizontal and vertical videos automatically. `0.0` indicates no scaling (use the size of the image as-is), and `1.0 `fills the entire video.|
|» url|body|string(uri)|false|URL of the watermark image to copy.|

> Example responses

```json
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {

    "height": 0,

  }
}
```

```json
    }
```

<h3 id="list-tagged-resources-parameters">Parameters</h3>

Lookups are limited to this page, at most five concurrently, with a shared two-second budget. |id|query|[[resource-tagging_resource_id](#schemaresource-tagging_resource_id)]|false|Filter by resource ID. Can be repeated up to 50 times to filter by multiple IDs. Example: ?id=abc&id=def|

## Delete a tunnel route (CIDR Endpoint)

<a id="opIdtunnel-route-delete-a-tunnel-route-with-cidr"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/699d98642c564d2e855e9661899b7252/teamnet/routes/network/172.16.0.0%252F16 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /accounts/{account_id}/teamnet/routes/network/{ip_network_encoded}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Deletes a private network route from an account. The CIDR in `ip_network_encoded` must be written in URL-encoded format. If no virtual_network_id is provided it will delete the route from the default vnet. If no tun_type is provided it will fetch the type from the tunnel_id or if that is missing it will assume Cloudflare Tunnel as default. If tunnel_id is provided it will delete the route from that tunnel, otherwise it will delete the route based on the vnet and tun_type.

|ip_network_encoded|path|[tunnel_ip_network_encoded](#schematunnel_ip_network_encoded)|true|none|
|account_id|path|[tunnel_account_id](#schematunnel_account_id)|true|none|
|virtual_network_id|query|[tunnel_virtual_network_id](#schematunnel_virtual_network_id)|false|none|
|tun_type|query|[tunnel_tunnel_type](#schematunnel_tunnel_type)|false|none|
|tunnel_id|query|[tunnel_tunnel_id](#schematunnel_tunnel_id)|false|none|

## Delete a concurrency key

<a id="opIdwor-delete-concurrency-key"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/workflows/concurrency/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /accounts/{account_id}/workflows/concurrency/{key_id}`

Deletes a concurrency key. Fails while any workflow’s latest version references the key. The key disappears immediately, but steps already holding it keep their slots until they finish and still count against a key re-created with the same name.

|key_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Identifier of the concurrency key.|

## Get full step output from instance

<a id="opIdwor-get-workflow-instance-step"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/workflows/string/instances/string/step?name=string&type=step' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/workflows/{workflow_name}/instances/{instance_id}/step`

Retrieves the full, untruncated output for a specific step on a workflow instance. Returns a flat status-shaped JSON body with step `status` ('running' | 'waiting' | 'complete' | 'errored'), `error` (nullable), and `output` (the step value, or null while running/waiting/errored). When the step returned a ReadableStream from step.do, the response is served as 'application/octet-stream' with the raw bytes as the body instead of JSON. A `status='running'` response with non-null `error` indicates the step is currently retrying after a prior attempt failed.

<h3 id="get-full-step-output-from-instance-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workflow_name|path|string|true|none|
|instance_id|path|string|true|Instance identifier. User-created instances match `^[a-zA-Z0-9_][a-zA-Z0-9-_]*$` (max 100 characters); cron-triggered instances can use a longer, system-generated id derived from the cron expression.|
|name|query|string|true|Exact step name from the instance logs response, including the generated counter suffix.|
|type|query|string|true|Step type to disambiguate step.do and waitForEvent entries that share the same name.|
|attempt|query|integer|false|Specific attempt number to retrieve output or error for.|
|account_id|path|string|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|step|
|type|waitForEvent|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [
    {
      "code": 0,
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "result": {
    "error": {
      "message": "string",
      "name": "string"
    },
    "event_type": "string",
    "output": {},
    "status": "queued"
  },
  "result_info": {
    "count": 0,
    "cursor": "string",
    "page": 0,
    "per_page": 0,
    "total_count": 0,
    "total_pages": 0
  },
  "success": true
}
```

> 400 Response

```json

    {
      "code": 0,

    }

  ],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

## Search URL scans

<a id="opIdurlscanner-search-scans"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/urlscanner/scan \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/urlscanner/scan`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Search scans by date and webpages' requests, including full URL (after redirects), hostname, and path. <br/> A successful scan will appear in search results a few minutes after finishing but may take much longer if the system in under load. By default, only successfully completed scans will appear in search results, unless searching by `scanId`. Please take into account that older scans may be removed from the search index at an unspecified time.

<h3 id="search-url-scans-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|Account ID.|
|scan_id|query|string(uuid)|false|Scan UUID.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limit the number of objects in the response.|
|next_cursor|query|string|false|Pagination cursor to get the next set of results.|
|date_start|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter scans requested after date (inclusive).|
|date_end|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter scans requested before date (inclusive).|
|url|query|string|false|Filter scans by URL of _any_ request made by the webpage|
|hostname|query|string|false|Filter scans by hostname of _any_ request made by the webpage.|
|path|query|string|false|Filter scans by url path of _any_ request made by the webpage.|
|ip|query|string|false|Filter scans by IP address (IPv4 or IPv6) of _any_ request made by the webpage.|
|hash|query|string|false|Filter scans by hash of any html/js/css request made by the webpage.|
|page_url|query|string|false|Filter scans by submitted or scanned URL|
|page_hostname|query|string|false|Filter scans by main page hostname (domain of effective URL).|
|page_path|query|string|false|Filter scans by exact match of effective URL path (also supports suffix search).|
|page_asn|query|string|false|Filter scans by main page Autonomous System Number (ASN).|
|page_ip|query|string|false|Filter scans by  main page IP address (IPv4 or IPv6).|
|account_scans|query|boolean|false|Return only scans created by account.|
|is_malicious|query|boolean|false|Filter scans by malicious verdict.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "Error"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [
    {
      "message": "OK"
    }
  ],
  "result": {
    "tasks": [
      {
        "country": "string",
        "success": true,
        "time": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "url": "https://www.example.com/",
        "uuid": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
        "visibility": "public"
      }
    ]
  },
  "success": true
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{

    {
      "message": "Scan ID is not a valid UUID."
    }
  ],
  "messages": [
    {
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "success": true
}
```

|404|Not Found|Scan not found.|Inline|

## Get URL scan's HAR

<a id="opIdurlscanner-get-scan-har"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/urlscanner/scan/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/har \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/urlscanner/scan/{scan_id}/har`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Get a URL scan's HAR file. See HAR spec at http://www.softwareishard.com/blog/har-12-spec/.

<h3 id="get-url-scans-har-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|scan_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Scan UUID.|
|account_id|path|string|true|Account ID.|

## Bulk create URL Scans

<a id="opIdurlscanner-create-scan-bulk-v2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/urlscanner/v2/bulk \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '[
    {
      "agentReadiness": true,
      "customHeaders": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      },
      "customagent": "string",
      "referer": "string",
      "screenshotsResolutions": [
        "desktop"
      ],
      "url": "https://www.example.com",
      "visibility": "Public"
    }
  ]'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/urlscanner/v2/bulk`

Submit URLs to scan. Check limits at https://developers.cloudflare.com/security-center/investigate/scan-limits/ and take into account scans submitted in bulk have lower priority and may take longer to finish.

> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "agentReadiness": true,
    "customHeaders": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "customagent": "string",
    "referer": "string",
    "screenshotsResolutions": [
      "desktop"
    ],
    "url": "https://www.example.com",
    "visibility": "Public"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="bulk-create-url-scans-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|Account ID.|
|body|body|[object]|false|none|
|» agentReadiness|body|boolean|false|Enable agent readiness checks.|
|» customHeaders|body|object|false|Set custom headers.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» customagent|body|string|false|none|
|» referer|body|string|false|none|
|» screenshotsResolutions|body|[string]|false|Take multiple screenshots targeting different device types.|
|» url|body|string|true|none|
|» visibility|body|string|false|The option `Public` means it will be included in listings like recent scans and search results. `Unlisted` means it will not be included in the aforementioned listings, users will need to have the scan's ID to access it. A a scan will be automatically marked as unlisted if it fails, if it contains potential PII or other sensitive material.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|

|» screenshotsResolutions|desktop|
|» screenshotsResolutions|mobile|
|» screenshotsResolutions|tablet|
|» visibility|Public|
|» visibility|Unlisted|

|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[object]|true|none|none|
|» detail|string|true|none|none|
|» status|integer|true|none|Status code.|
|» title|string|true|none|none|
|message|string|true|none|none|
|status|integer|true|none|Status code.|

Status Code **404**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[object]|true|none|none|
|» detail|string|true|none|none|
|» status|integer|true|none|Status code.|
|» title|string|true|none|none|
|message|string|true|none|Scan not found or in progress.|
|status|integer|true|none|Status code.|
|task|object|true|none|none|
|» status|string|true|none|none|
|» time|string|true|none|none|
|» url|string|true|none|none|
|» uuid|string|true|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
api_token, api_email & api_key
</aside>

## Get raw response

<a id="opIdurlscanner-get-response-v2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/urlscanner/v2/responses/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/urlscanner/v2/responses/{response_id}`

Returns the raw response of the network request. Find the `response_id` in the `data.requests.response.hash`.

<h3 id="get-raw-response-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|response_id|path|string|true|Response hash.|
|account_id|path|string|true|Account ID.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "string",
      "status": 400,
      "title": "Invalid url"
    }
  ],
  "message": "string",
  "status": 400
}
```

<h3 id="get-raw-response-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Get the raw response by its hash.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid input.|Inline|

<h3 id="get-raw-response-1-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[object]|true|none|none|
|» detail|string|true|none|none|
|» status|integer|true|none|Status code.|
|» title|string|true|none|none|
|message|string|true|none|none|
|status|integer|true|none|Status code.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
api_token, api_email & api_key
</aside>

## Get URL scan

<a id="opIdurlscanner-get-scan-v2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/urlscanner/v2/result/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/urlscanner/v2/result/{scan_id}`

Get URL scan by uuid

<h3 id="get-url-scan-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|scan_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Scan UUID.|
|account_id|path|string|true|Account ID.|

## Create URL Scan

<a id="opIdurlscanner-create-scan-v2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/urlscanner/v2/scan \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "agentReadiness": true,
    "country": "AE",
    "customHeaders": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "customagent": "string",
    "referer": "string",
    "screenshotsResolutions": [
      "desktop"
    ],
    "url": "https://www.example.com",
    "visibility": "Public"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/urlscanner/v2/scan`

Submit a URL to scan. Check limits at https://developers.cloudflare.com/security-center/investigate/scan-limits/.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "agentReadiness": true,
  "country": "AE",
  "customHeaders": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "customagent": "string",
  "referer": "string",
  "screenshotsResolutions": [
    "desktop"
  ],
  "url": "https://www.example.com",
  "visibility": "Public"
}
```

<h3 id="create-url-scan-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|Account ID.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» agentReadiness|body|boolean|false|Enable agent readiness checks.|
|» country|body|string|false|Country to geo egress from|
|» customHeaders|body|object|false|Set custom headers.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» customagent|body|string|false|none|
|» referer|body|string|false|none|
|» screenshotsResolutions|body|[string]|false|Take multiple screenshots targeting different device types.|
|» url|body|string|true|none|
|» visibility|body|string|false|The option `Public` means it will be included in listings like recent scans and search results. `Unlisted` means it will not be included in the aforementioned listings, users will need to have the scan's ID to access it. A a scan will be automatically marked as unlisted if it fails, if it contains potential PII or other sensitive material.|

## Search URL scans

<a id="opIdurlscanner-search-scans-v2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/urlscanner/v2/search \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/urlscanner/v2/search`

Use a subset of ElasticSearch Query syntax to filter scans. Some example queries:<br/> <br/>- 'path:"/bundles/jquery.js"': Searches for scans who requested resources with the given path.<br/>- 'page.asn:AS24940 AND hash:xxx': Websites hosted in AS24940 where a resource with the given hash was downloaded.<br/>- 'page.domain:microsoft* AND verdicts.malicious:true AND NOT page.domain:microsoft.com': malicious scans whose hostname starts with "microsoft".<br/>- 'apikey:me AND date:[2025-01 TO 2025-02]': my scans from 2025 January to 2025 February.

<h3 id="search-url-scans-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|Account ID.|
|size|query|integer|false|Limit the number of objects in the response.|
|q|query|string|false|Filter scans|

```json
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

## Query Vectors

<a id="opIdvectorize-query-vector"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/vectorize/v2/indexes/example-index/query \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "filter": {
      "has_viewed": {
        "$ne": true
      },
      "streaming_platform": "netflix"
    },
    "returnMetadata": "none",
    "returnValues": false,
    "topK": 5,
    "vector": [
      0.5,
      0.5,
      0.5
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/vectorize/v2/indexes/{index_name}/query`

Finds vectors closest to a given vector in an index.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "filter": {
    "has_viewed": {
      "$ne": true
    },
    "streaming_platform": "netflix"
  },
  "returnMetadata": "none",
  "returnValues": false,
  "topK": 5,
  "vector": [
    0.5,
    0.5,
    0.5
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="query-vectors-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[vectorize_identifier](#schemavectorize_identifier)|true|none|
|index_name|path|[vectorize_index-name](#schemavectorize_index-name)|true|none|
|body|body|[vectorize_index-query-v2-request](#schemavectorize_index-query-v2-request)|true|none|
|» filter|body|object|false|A metadata filter expression used to limit nearest neighbor results.|
|» returnMetadata|body|string|false|Whether to return no metadata, indexed metadata or all metadata associated with the closest vectors.|
|» returnValues|body|boolean|false|Whether to return the values associated with the closest vectors.|
|» topK|body|number|false|The number of nearest neighbors to find.|
|» vector|body|[number]|true|The search vector that will be used to find the nearest neighbors.|

|» returnMetadata|indexed|
|» returnMetadata|all|

<h3 id="create-waiting-room-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[waitingroom_identifier](#schemawaitingroom_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[waitingroom_query_waitingroom](#schemawaitingroom_query_waitingroom)|true|none|
|» additional_routes|body|[waitingroom_additional_routes](#schemawaitingroom_additional_routes)|false|Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. Additional hostname and path combinations to which this waiting room will be applied. There is an implied wildcard at the end of the path. The hostname and path combination must be unique to this and all other waiting rooms.|
|» cookie_attributes|body|[waitingroom_cookie_attributes](#schemawaitingroom_cookie_attributes)|false|Configures cookie attributes for the waiting room cookie. This encrypted cookie stores a user's status in the waiting room, such as queue position.|
|» cookie_suffix|body|[waitingroom_cookie_suffix](#schemawaitingroom_cookie_suffix)|false|Appends a '_' + a custom suffix to the end of Cloudflare Waiting Room's cookie name(__cf_waitingroom). If `cookie_suffix` is "abcd", the cookie name will be `__cf_waitingroom_abcd`. This field is required if using `additional_routes`.|
|» custom_page_html|body|[waitingroom_custom_page_html](#schemawaitingroom_custom_page_html)|false|Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. This is a template html file that will be rendered at the edge. If no custom_page_html is provided, the default waiting room will be used. The template is based on mustache ( https://mustache.github.io/ ). There are several variables that are evaluated by the Cloudflare edge:<br>1. {{`waitTimeKnown`}} Acts like a boolean value that indicates the behavior to take when wait time is not available, for instance when queue_all is **true**.<br>2. {{`waitTimeFormatted`}} Estimated wait time for the user. For example, five minutes. Alternatively, you can use:<br>3. {{`waitTime`}} Number of minutes of estimated wait for a user.<br>4. {{`waitTimeHours`}} Number of hours of estimated wait for a user (`Math.floor(waitTime/60)`).<br>5. {{`waitTimeHourMinutes`}} Number of minutes above the `waitTimeHours` value (`waitTime%60`).<br>6. {{`queueIsFull`}} Changes to **true** when no more people can be added to the queue.<br><br>To view the full list of variables, look at the `cfWaitingRoom` object described under the `json_response_enabled` property in other Waiting Room API calls.|
|» default_template_language|body|[waitingroom_default_template_language](#schemawaitingroom_default_template_language)|false|The language of the default page template. If no default_template_language is provided, then `en-US` (English) will be used.|
|» description|body|[waitingroom_description](#schemawaitingroom_description)|false|A note that you can use to add more details about the waiting room.|
|» disable_session_renewal|body|[waitingroom_disable_session_renewal](#schemawaitingroom_disable_session_renewal)|false|Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. Disables automatic renewal of session cookies. If `true`, an accepted user will have session_duration minutes to browse the site. After that, they will have to go through the waiting room again. If `false`, a user's session cookie will be automatically renewed on every request.|
|» enabled_origin_commands|body|[waitingroom_enabled_origin_commands](#schemawaitingroom_enabled_origin_commands)|false|A list of enabled origin commands.|
|» host|body|[waitingroom_host](#schemawaitingroom_host)|true|The host name to which the waiting room will be applied (no wildcards). Please do not include the scheme (http:// or https://). The host and path combination must be unique.|
|» json_response_enabled|body|[waitingroom_json_response_enabled](#schemawaitingroom_json_response_enabled)|false|Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. If `true`, requests to the waiting room with the header `Accept: application/json` will receive a JSON response object with information on the user's status in the waiting room as opposed to the configured static HTML page. This JSON response object has one property `cfWaitingRoom` which is an object containing the following fields:<br>1. `inWaitingRoom`: Boolean indicating if the user is in the waiting room (always **true**).<br>2. `waitTimeKnown`: Boolean indicating if the current estimated wait times are accurate. If **false**, they are not available.<br>3. `waitTime`: Valid only when `waitTimeKnown` is **true**. Integer indicating the current estimated time in minutes the user will wait in the waiting room. When `queueingMethod` is **random**, this is set to `waitTime50Percentile`.<br>4. `waitTime25Percentile`: Valid only when `queueingMethod` is **random** and `waitTimeKnown` is **true**. Integer indicating the current estimated maximum wait time for the 25% of users that gain entry the fastest (25th percentile).<br>5. `waitTime50Percentile`: Valid only when `queueingMethod` is **random** and `waitTimeKnown` is **true**. Integer indicating the current estimated maximum wait time for the 50% of users that gain entry the fastest (50th percentile). In other words, half of the queued users are expected to let into the origin website before `waitTime50Percentile` and half are expected to be let in after it.<br>6. `waitTime75Percentile`: Valid only when `queueingMethod` is **random** and `waitTimeKnown` is **true**. Integer indicating the current estimated maximum wait time for the 75% of users that gain entry the fastest (75th percentile).<br>7. `waitTimeFormatted`: String displaying the `waitTime` formatted in English for users. If `waitTimeKnown` is **false**, `waitTimeFormatted` will display **unavailable**.<br>8. `queueIsFull`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room's queue is currently full and not accepting new users at the moment.<br>9. `queueAll`: Boolean indicating if all users will be queued in the waiting room and no one will be let into the origin website.<br>10. `lastUpdated`: String displaying the timestamp as an ISO 8601 string of the user's last attempt to leave the waiting room and be let into the origin website. The user is able to make another attempt after `refreshIntervalSeconds` past this time. If the user makes a request too soon, it will be ignored and `lastUpdated` will not change.<br>11. `refreshIntervalSeconds`: Integer indicating the number of seconds after `lastUpdated` until the user is able to make another attempt to leave the waiting room and be let into the origin website. When the `queueingMethod` is `reject`, there is no specified refresh time —\_it will always be **zero**.<br>12. `queueingMethod`: The queueing method currently used by the waiting room. It is either **fifo**, **random**, **passthrough**, or **reject**.<br>13. `isFIFOQueue`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room uses a FIFO (First-In-First-Out) queue.<br>14. `isRandomQueue`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room uses a Random queue where users gain access randomly.<br>15. `isPassthroughQueue`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room uses a passthrough queue. Keep in mind that when passthrough is enabled, this JSON response will only exist when `queueAll` is **true** or `isEventPrequeueing` is **true** because in all other cases requests will go directly to the origin.<br>16. `isRejectQueue`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room uses a reject queue.<br>17. `isEventActive`: Boolean indicating if an event is currently occurring. Events are able to change a waiting room's behavior during a specified period of time. For additional information, look at the event properties `prequeue_start_time`, `event_start_time`, and `event_end_time` in the documentation for creating waiting room events. Events are considered active between these start and end times, as well as during the prequeueing period if it exists.<br>18. `isEventPrequeueing`: Valid only when `isEventActive` is **true**. Boolean indicating if an event is currently prequeueing users before it starts.<br>19. `timeUntilEventStart`: Valid only when `isEventPrequeueing` is **true**. Integer indicating the number of minutes until the event starts.<br>20. `timeUntilEventStartFormatted`: String displaying the `timeUntilEventStart` formatted in English for users. If `isEventPrequeueing` is **false**, `timeUntilEventStartFormatted` will display **unavailable**.<br>21. `timeUntilEventEnd`: Valid only when `isEventActive` is **true**. Integer indicating the number of minutes until the event ends.<br>22. `timeUntilEventEndFormatted`: String displaying the `timeUntilEventEnd` formatted in English for users. If `isEventActive` is **false**, `timeUntilEventEndFormatted` will display **unavailable**.<br>23. `shuffleAtEventStart`: Valid only when `isEventActive` is **true**. Boolean indicating if the users in the prequeue are shuffled randomly when the event starts.<br>24. `turnstile`: Empty when turnstile isn't enabled. String displaying an html tag to display the Turnstile widget. Please add the `{{{turnstile}}}` tag to the `custom_html` template to ensure the Turnstile widget appears.<br>25. `infiniteQueue`: Boolean indicating whether the response is for a user in the infinite queue.<br><br>An example cURL to a waiting room could be:<br><br>	curl -X GET "https://example.com/waitingroom" \<br>		-H "Accept: application/json"<br><br>If `json_response_enabled` is **true** and the request hits the waiting room, an example JSON response when `queueingMethod` is **fifo** and no event is active could be:<br><br>	{<br>		"cfWaitingRoom": {<br>			"inWaitingRoom": true,<br>			"waitTimeKnown": true,<br>			"waitTime": 10,<br>			"waitTime25Percentile": 0,<br>			"waitTime50Percentile": 0,<br>			"waitTime75Percentile": 0,<br>			"waitTimeFormatted": "10 minutes",<br>			"queueIsFull": false,<br>			"queueAll": false,<br>			"lastUpdated": "2020-08-03T23:46:00.000Z",<br>			"refreshIntervalSeconds": 20,<br>			"queueingMethod": "fifo",<br>			"isFIFOQueue": true,<br>			"isRandomQueue": false,<br>			"isPassthroughQueue": false,<br>			"isRejectQueue": false,<br>			"isEventActive": false,<br>			"isEventPrequeueing": false,<br>			"timeUntilEventStart": 0,<br>			"timeUntilEventStartFormatted": "unavailable",<br>			"timeUntilEventEnd": 0,<br>			"timeUntilEventEndFormatted": "unavailable",<br>			"shuffleAtEventStart": false<br>		}<br>	}<br><br>If `json_response_enabled` is **true** and the request hits the waiting room, an example JSON response when `queueingMethod` is **random** and an event is active could be:<br><br>	{<br>		"cfWaitingRoom": {<br>			"inWaitingRoom": true,<br>			"waitTimeKnown": true,<br>			"waitTime": 10,<br>			"waitTime25Percentile": 5,<br>			"waitTime50Percentile": 10,<br>			"waitTime75Percentile": 15,<br>			"waitTimeFormatted": "5 minutes to 15 minutes",<br>			"queueIsFull": false,<br>			"queueAll": false,<br>			"lastUpdated": "2020-08-03T23:46:00.000Z",<br>			"refreshIntervalSeconds": 20,<br>			"queueingMethod": "random",<br>			"isFIFOQueue": false,<br>			"isRandomQueue": true,<br>			"isPassthroughQueue": false,<br>			"isRejectQueue": false,<br>			"isEventActive": true,<br>			"isEventPrequeueing": false,<br>			"timeUntilEventStart": 0,<br>			"timeUntilEventStartFormatted": "unavailable",<br>			"timeUntilEventEnd": 15,<br>			"timeUntilEventEndFormatted": "15 minutes",<br>			"shuffleAtEventStart": true<br>		}<br>	}|
|» name|body|[waitingroom_name](#schemawaitingroom_name)|true|A unique name to identify the waiting room. Only alphanumeric characters, hyphens and underscores are allowed.|
|» new_users_per_minute|body|[waitingroom_new_users_per_minute](#schemawaitingroom_new_users_per_minute)|true|Sets the number of new users that will be let into the route every minute. This value is used as baseline for the number of users that are let in per minute. So it is possible that there is a little more or little less traffic coming to the route based on the traffic patterns at that time around the world.|
|» path|body|[waitingroom_path](#schemawaitingroom_path)|false|Sets the path within the host to enable the waiting room on. The waiting room will be enabled for all subpaths as well. If there are two waiting rooms on the same subpath, the waiting room for the most specific path will be chosen. Wildcards and query parameters are not supported.|
|» queue_all|body|[waitingroom_queue_all](#schemawaitingroom_queue_all)|false|If queue_all is `true`, all the traffic that is coming to a route will be sent to the waiting room. No new traffic can get to the route once this field is set and estimated time will become unavailable.|
|» queueing_method|body|[waitingroom_queueing_method](#schemawaitingroom_queueing_method)|false|Sets the queueing method used by the waiting room. Changing this parameter from the **default** queueing method is only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. Regardless of the queueing method, if `queue_all` is enabled or an event is prequeueing, users in the waiting room will not be accepted to the origin. These users will always see a waiting room page that refreshes automatically. The valid queueing methods are:<br>1. `fifo` **(default)**: First-In-First-Out queue where customers gain access in the order they arrived.<br>2. `random`: Random queue where customers gain access randomly, regardless of arrival time.<br>3. `passthrough`: Users will pass directly through the waiting room and into the origin website. As a result, any configured limits will not be respected while this is enabled. This method can be used as an alternative to disabling a waiting room (with `suspended`) so that analytics are still reported. This can be used if you wish to allow all traffic normally, but want to restrict traffic during a waiting room event, or vice versa.<br>4. `reject`: Users will be immediately rejected from the waiting room. As a result, no users will reach the origin website while this is enabled. This can be used if you wish to reject all traffic while performing maintenance, block traffic during a specified period of time (an event), or block traffic while events are not occurring. Consider a waiting room used for vaccine distribution that only allows traffic during sign-up events, and otherwise blocks all traffic. For this case, the waiting room uses `reject`, and its events override this with `fifo`, `random`, or `passthrough`. When this queueing method is enabled and neither `queueAll` is enabled nor an event is prequeueing, the waiting room page **will not refresh automatically**.|
|» queueing_status_code|body|[waitingroom_queueing_status_code](#schemawaitingroom_queueing_status_code)|false|HTTP status code returned to a user while in the queue.|
|» session_duration|body|[waitingroom_session_duration](#schemawaitingroom_session_duration)|false|Lifetime of a cookie (in minutes) set by Cloudflare for users who get access to the route. If a user is not seen by Cloudflare again in that time period, they will be treated as a new user that visits the route.|
|» suspended|body|[waitingroom_suspended](#schemawaitingroom_suspended)|false|Suspends or allows traffic going to the waiting room. If set to `true`, the traffic will not go to the waiting room.|
|» total_active_users|body|[waitingroom_total_active_users](#schemawaitingroom_total_active_users)|true|Sets the total number of active user sessions on the route at a point in time. A route is a combination of host and path on which a waiting room is available. This value is used as a baseline for the total number of active user sessions on the route. It is possible to have a situation where there are more or less active users sessions on the route based on the traffic patterns at that time around the world.|
|» turnstile_action|body|[waitingroom_turnstile_action](#schemawaitingroom_turnstile_action)|false|Which action to take when a bot is detected using Turnstile. `log` will<br>have no impact on queueing behavior, simply keeping track of how many<br>bots are detected in Waiting Room Analytics. `infinite_queue` will send<br>bots to a false queueing state, where they will never reach your<br>origin. `infinite_queue` requires Advanced Waiting Room.<br>|
|» turnstile_mode|body|[waitingroom_turnstile_mode](#schemawaitingroom_turnstile_mode)|false|Which Turnstile widget type to use for detecting bot traffic. See<br>[the Turnstile documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/turnstile/concepts/widget/#widget-types)<br>for the definitions of these widget types. Set to `off` to disable the<br>Turnstile integration entirely. Setting this to anything other than<br>`off` or `invisible` requires Advanced Waiting Room.<br>|

## Create a custom waiting room page preview

<a id="opIdwaiting-room-create-a-custom-waiting-room-page-preview"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/waiting_rooms/preview \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "custom_html": "{{#waitTimeKnown}} {{waitTime}} mins {{/waitTimeKnown}} {{^waitTimeKnown}} Queue all enabled {{/waitTimeKnown}}"
  }'
```

`POST /zones/{zone_id}/waiting_rooms/preview`

Creates a waiting room page preview. Upload a custom waiting room page for preview. You will receive a preview URL in the form `http://waitingrooms.dev/preview/<uuid>`. You can use the following query parameters to change the state of the preview:
1. `force_queue`: Boolean indicating if all users will be queued in the waiting room and no one will be let into the origin website (also known as queueAll).
2. `queue_is_full`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room's queue is currently full and not accepting new users at the moment.
3. `queueing_method`: The queueing method currently used by the waiting room.
	- **fifo** indicates a FIFO queue.
	- **random** indicates a Random queue.
	- **passthrough** indicates a Passthrough queue. Keep in mind that the waiting room page will only be displayed if `force_queue=true` or `event=prequeueing` — for other cases the request will pass through to the origin. For our preview, this will be a fake origin website returning \"Welcome\". 
	- **reject** indicates a Reject queue.
4. `event`: Used to preview a waiting room event.
	- **none** indicates no event is occurring.
	- **prequeueing** indicates that an event is prequeueing (between `prequeue_start_time` and `event_start_time`).
	- **started** indicates that an event has started (between `event_start_time` and `event_end_time`).
5. `shuffle_at_event_start`: Boolean indicating if the event will shuffle users in the prequeue when it starts. This can only be set to **true** if an event is active (`event` is not **none**).

For example, you can make a request to `http://waitingrooms.dev/preview/<uuid>?force_queue=false&queue_is_full=false&queueing_method=random&event=started&shuffle_at_event_start=true`
6. `waitTime`: Non-zero, positive integer indicating the estimated wait time in minutes. The default value is 10 minutes.

For example, you can make a request to `http://waitingrooms.dev/preview/<uuid>?waitTime=50` to configure the estimated wait time as 50 minutes.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "custom_html": "{{#waitTimeKnown}} {{waitTime}} mins {{/waitTimeKnown}} {{^waitTimeKnown}} Queue all enabled {{/waitTimeKnown}}"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-custom-waiting-room-page-preview-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[waitingroom_identifier](#schemawaitingroom_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[waitingroom_query_preview](#schemawaitingroom_query_preview)|true|none|
|» custom_html|body|[waitingroom_custom_page_html](#schemawaitingroom_custom_page_html)|true|Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. This is a template html file that will be rendered at the edge. If no custom_page_html is provided, the default waiting room will be used. The template is based on mustache ( https://mustache.github.io/ ). There are several variables that are evaluated by the Cloudflare edge:<br>1. {{`waitTimeKnown`}} Acts like a boolean value that indicates the behavior to take when wait time is not available, for instance when queue_all is **true**.<br>2. {{`waitTimeFormatted`}} Estimated wait time for the user. For example, five minutes. Alternatively, you can use:<br>3. {{`waitTime`}} Number of minutes of estimated wait for a user.<br>4. {{`waitTimeHours`}} Number of hours of estimated wait for a user (`Math.floor(waitTime/60)`).<br>5. {{`waitTimeHourMinutes`}} Number of minutes above the `waitTimeHours` value (`waitTime%60`).<br>6. {{`queueIsFull`}} Changes to **true** when no more people can be added to the queue.<br><br>To view the full list of variables, look at the `cfWaitingRoom` object described under the `json_response_enabled` property in other Waiting Room API calls.|

```json
  },
  "success": true
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
