|» additional_routes|body|[waitingroom_additional_routes](#schemawaitingroom_additional_routes)|false|Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. Additional hostname and path combinations to which this waiting room will be applied. There is an implied wildcard at the end of the path. The hostname and path combination must be unique to this and all other waiting rooms.|
|» cookie_attributes|body|[waitingroom_cookie_attributes](#schemawaitingroom_cookie_attributes)|false|Configures cookie attributes for the waiting room cookie. This encrypted cookie stores a user's status in the waiting room, such as queue position.|
|» cookie_suffix|body|[waitingroom_cookie_suffix](#schemawaitingroom_cookie_suffix)|false|Appends a '_' + a custom suffix to the end of Cloudflare Waiting Room's cookie name(__cf_waitingroom). If `cookie_suffix` is "abcd", the cookie name will be `__cf_waitingroom_abcd`. This field is required if using `additional_routes`.|
|» custom_page_html|body|[waitingroom_custom_page_html](#schemawaitingroom_custom_page_html)|false|Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. This is a template html file that will be rendered at the edge. If no custom_page_html is provided, the default waiting room will be used. The template is based on mustache ( https://mustache.github.io/ ). There are several variables that are evaluated by the Cloudflare edge:<br>1. {{`waitTimeKnown`}} Acts like a boolean value that indicates the behavior to take when wait time is not available, for instance when queue_all is **true**.<br>2. {{`waitTimeFormatted`}} Estimated wait time for the user. For example, five minutes. Alternatively, you can use:<br>3. {{`waitTime`}} Number of minutes of estimated wait for a user.<br>4. {{`waitTimeHours`}} Number of hours of estimated wait for a user (`Math.floor(waitTime/60)`).<br>5. {{`waitTimeHourMinutes`}} Number of minutes above the `waitTimeHours` value (`waitTime%60`).<br>6. {{`queueIsFull`}} Changes to **true** when no more people can be added to the queue.<br><br>To view the full list of variables, look at the `cfWaitingRoom` object described under the `json_response_enabled` property in other Waiting Room API calls.|
|» default_template_language|body|[waitingroom_default_template_language](#schemawaitingroom_default_template_language)|false|The language of the default page template. If no default_template_language is provided, then `en-US` (English) will be used.|
|» description|body|[waitingroom_description](#schemawaitingroom_description)|false|A note that you can use to add more details about the waiting room.|
|» disable_session_renewal|body|[waitingroom_disable_session_renewal](#schemawaitingroom_disable_session_renewal)|false|Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. Disables automatic renewal of session cookies. If `true`, an accepted user will have session_duration minutes to browse the site. After that, they will have to go through the waiting room again. If `false`, a user's session cookie will be automatically renewed on every request.|
|» enabled_origin_commands|body|[waitingroom_enabled_origin_commands](#schemawaitingroom_enabled_origin_commands)|false|A list of enabled origin commands.|
|» host|body|[waitingroom_host](#schemawaitingroom_host)|true|The host name to which the waiting room will be applied (no wildcards). Please do not include the scheme (http:// or https://). The host and path combination must be unique.|
|» json_response_enabled|body|[waitingroom_json_response_enabled](#schemawaitingroom_json_response_enabled)|false|Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. If `true`, requests to the waiting room with the header `Accept: application/json` will receive a JSON response object with information on the user's status in the waiting room as opposed to the configured static HTML page. This JSON response object has one property `cfWaitingRoom` which is an object containing the following fields:<br>1. `inWaitingRoom`: Boolean indicating if the user is in the waiting room (always **true**).<br>2. `waitTimeKnown`: Boolean indicating if the current estimated wait times are accurate. If **false**, they are not available.<br>3. `waitTime`: Valid only when `waitTimeKnown` is **true**. Integer indicating the current estimated time in minutes the user will wait in the waiting room. When `queueingMethod` is **random**, this is set to `waitTime50Percentile`.<br>4. `waitTime25Percentile`: Valid only when `queueingMethod` is **random** and `waitTimeKnown` is **true**. Integer indicating the current estimated maximum wait time for the 25% of users that gain entry the fastest (25th percentile).<br>5. `waitTime50Percentile`: Valid only when `queueingMethod` is **random** and `waitTimeKnown` is **true**. Integer indicating the current estimated maximum wait time for the 50% of users that gain entry the fastest (50th percentile). In other words, half of the queued users are expected to let into the origin website before `waitTime50Percentile` and half are expected to be let in after it.<br>6. `waitTime75Percentile`: Valid only when `queueingMethod` is **random** and `waitTimeKnown` is **true**. Integer indicating the current estimated maximum wait time for the 75% of users that gain entry the fastest (75th percentile).<br>7. `waitTimeFormatted`: String displaying the `waitTime` formatted in English for users. If `waitTimeKnown` is **false**, `waitTimeFormatted` will display **unavailable**.<br>8. `queueIsFull`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room's queue is currently full and not accepting new users at the moment.<br>9. `queueAll`: Boolean indicating if all users will be queued in the waiting room and no one will be let into the origin website.<br>10. `lastUpdated`: String displaying the timestamp as an ISO 8601 string of the user's last attempt to leave the waiting room and be let into the origin website. The user is able to make another attempt after `refreshIntervalSeconds` past this time. If the user makes a request too soon, it will be ignored and `lastUpdated` will not change.<br>11. `refreshIntervalSeconds`: Integer indicating the number of seconds after `lastUpdated` until the user is able to make another attempt to leave the waiting room and be let into the origin website. When the `queueingMethod` is `reject`, there is no specified refresh time —\_it will always be **zero**.<br>12. `queueingMethod`: The queueing method currently used by the waiting room. It is either **fifo**, **random**, **passthrough**, or **reject**.<br>13. `isFIFOQueue`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room uses a FIFO (First-In-First-Out) queue.<br>14. `isRandomQueue`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room uses a Random queue where users gain access randomly.<br>15. `isPassthroughQueue`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room uses a passthrough queue. Keep in mind that when passthrough is enabled, this JSON response will only exist when `queueAll` is **true** or `isEventPrequeueing` is **true** because in all other cases requests will go directly to the origin.<br>16. `isRejectQueue`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room uses a reject queue.<br>17. `isEventActive`: Boolean indicating if an event is currently occurring. Events are able to change a waiting room's behavior during a specified period of time. For additional information, look at the event properties `prequeue_start_time`, `event_start_time`, and `event_end_time` in the documentation for creating waiting room events. Events are considered active between these start and end times, as well as during the prequeueing period if it exists.<br>18. `isEventPrequeueing`: Valid only when `isEventActive` is **true**. Boolean indicating if an event is currently prequeueing users before it starts.<br>19. `timeUntilEventStart`: Valid only when `isEventPrequeueing` is **true**. Integer indicating the number of minutes until the event starts.<br>20. `timeUntilEventStartFormatted`: String displaying the `timeUntilEventStart` formatted in English for users. If `isEventPrequeueing` is **false**, `timeUntilEventStartFormatted` will display **unavailable**.<br>21. `timeUntilEventEnd`: Valid only when `isEventActive` is **true**. Integer indicating the number of minutes until the event ends.<br>22. `timeUntilEventEndFormatted`: String displaying the `timeUntilEventEnd` formatted in English for users. If `isEventActive` is **false**, `timeUntilEventEndFormatted` will display **unavailable**.<br>23. `shuffleAtEventStart`: Valid only when `isEventActive` is **true**. Boolean indicating if the users in the prequeue are shuffled randomly when the event starts.<br>24. `turnstile`: Empty when turnstile isn't enabled. String displaying an html tag to display the Turnstile widget. Please add the `{{{turnstile}}}` tag to the `custom_html` template to ensure the Turnstile widget appears.<br>25. `infiniteQueue`: Boolean indicating whether the response is for a user in the infinite queue.<br><br>An example cURL to a waiting room could be:<br><br>	curl -X GET "https://example.com/waitingroom" \<br>		-H "Accept: application/json"<br><br>If `json_response_enabled` is **true** and the request hits the waiting room, an example JSON response when `queueingMethod` is **fifo** and no event is active could be:<br><br>	{<br>		"cfWaitingRoom": {<br>			"inWaitingRoom": true,<br>			"waitTimeKnown": true,<br>			"waitTime": 10,<br>			"waitTime25Percentile": 0,<br>			"waitTime50Percentile": 0,<br>			"waitTime75Percentile": 0,<br>			"waitTimeFormatted": "10 minutes",<br>			"queueIsFull": false,<br>			"queueAll": false,<br>			"lastUpdated": "2020-08-03T23:46:00.000Z",<br>			"refreshIntervalSeconds": 20,<br>			"queueingMethod": "fifo",<br>			"isFIFOQueue": true,<br>			"isRandomQueue": false,<br>			"isPassthroughQueue": false,<br>			"isRejectQueue": false,<br>			"isEventActive": false,<br>			"isEventPrequeueing": false,<br>			"timeUntilEventStart": 0,<br>			"timeUntilEventStartFormatted": "unavailable",<br>			"timeUntilEventEnd": 0,<br>			"timeUntilEventEndFormatted": "unavailable",<br>			"shuffleAtEventStart": false<br>		}<br>	}<br><br>If `json_response_enabled` is **true** and the request hits the waiting room, an example JSON response when `queueingMethod` is **random** and an event is active could be:<br><br>	{<br>		"cfWaitingRoom": {<br>			"inWaitingRoom": true,<br>			"waitTimeKnown": true,<br>			"waitTime": 10,<br>			"waitTime25Percentile": 5,<br>			"waitTime50Percentile": 10,<br>			"waitTime75Percentile": 15,<br>			"waitTimeFormatted": "5 minutes to 15 minutes",<br>			"queueIsFull": false,<br>			"queueAll": false,<br>			"lastUpdated": "2020-08-03T23:46:00.000Z",<br>			"refreshIntervalSeconds": 20,<br>			"queueingMethod": "random",<br>			"isFIFOQueue": false,<br>			"isRandomQueue": true,<br>			"isPassthroughQueue": false,<br>			"isRejectQueue": false,<br>			"isEventActive": true,<br>			"isEventPrequeueing": false,<br>			"timeUntilEventStart": 0,<br>			"timeUntilEventStartFormatted": "unavailable",<br>			"timeUntilEventEnd": 15,<br>			"timeUntilEventEndFormatted": "15 minutes",<br>			"shuffleAtEventStart": true<br>		}<br>	}|
|» name|body|[waitingroom_name](#schemawaitingroom_name)|true|A unique name to identify the waiting room. Only alphanumeric characters, hyphens and underscores are allowed.|
|» new_users_per_minute|body|[waitingroom_new_users_per_minute](#schemawaitingroom_new_users_per_minute)|true|Sets the number of new users that will be let into the route every minute. This value is used as baseline for the number of users that are let in per minute. So it is possible that there is a little more or little less traffic coming to the route based on the traffic patterns at that time around the world.|
|» path|body|[waitingroom_path](#schemawaitingroom_path)|false|Sets the path within the host to enable the waiting room on. The waiting room will be enabled for all subpaths as well. If there are two waiting rooms on the same subpath, the waiting room for the most specific path will be chosen. Wildcards and query parameters are not supported.|
|» queue_all|body|[waitingroom_queue_all](#schemawaitingroom_queue_all)|false|If queue_all is `true`, all the traffic that is coming to a route will be sent to the waiting room. No new traffic can get to the route once this field is set and estimated time will become unavailable.|
|» queueing_method|body|[waitingroom_queueing_method](#schemawaitingroom_queueing_method)|false|Sets the queueing method used by the waiting room. Changing this parameter from the **default** queueing method is only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. Regardless of the queueing method, if `queue_all` is enabled or an event is prequeueing, users in the waiting room will not be accepted to the origin. These users will always see a waiting room page that refreshes automatically. The valid queueing methods are:<br>1. `fifo` **(default)**: First-In-First-Out queue where customers gain access in the order they arrived.<br>2. `random`: Random queue where customers gain access randomly, regardless of arrival time.<br>3. `passthrough`: Users will pass directly through the waiting room and into the origin website. As a result, any configured limits will not be respected while this is enabled. This method can be used as an alternative to disabling a waiting room (with `suspended`) so that analytics are still reported. This can be used if you wish to allow all traffic normally, but want to restrict traffic during a waiting room event, or vice versa.<br>4. `reject`: Users will be immediately rejected from the waiting room. As a result, no users will reach the origin website while this is enabled. This can be used if you wish to reject all traffic while performing maintenance, block traffic during a specified period of time (an event), or block traffic while events are not occurring. Consider a waiting room used for vaccine distribution that only allows traffic during sign-up events, and otherwise blocks all traffic. For this case, the waiting room uses `reject`, and its events override this with `fifo`, `random`, or `passthrough`. When this queueing method is enabled and neither `queueAll` is enabled nor an event is prequeueing, the waiting room page **will not refresh automatically**.|
|» queueing_status_code|body|[waitingroom_queueing_status_code](#schemawaitingroom_queueing_status_code)|false|HTTP status code returned to a user while in the queue.|
|» session_duration|body|[waitingroom_session_duration](#schemawaitingroom_session_duration)|false|Lifetime of a cookie (in minutes) set by Cloudflare for users who get access to the route. If a user is not seen by Cloudflare again in that time period, they will be treated as a new user that visits the route.|
|» suspended|body|[waitingroom_suspended](#schemawaitingroom_suspended)|false|Suspends or allows traffic going to the waiting room. If set to `true`, the traffic will not go to the waiting room.|
|» total_active_users|body|[waitingroom_total_active_users](#schemawaitingroom_total_active_users)|true|Sets the total number of active user sessions on the route at a point in time. A route is a combination of host and path on which a waiting room is available. This value is used as a baseline for the total number of active user sessions on the route. It is possible to have a situation where there are more or less active users sessions on the route based on the traffic patterns at that time around the world.|
|» turnstile_action|body|[waitingroom_turnstile_action](#schemawaitingroom_turnstile_action)|false|Which action to take when a bot is detected using Turnstile. `log` will<br>have no impact on queueing behavior, simply keeping track of how many<br>bots are detected in Waiting Room Analytics. `infinite_queue` will send<br>bots to a false queueing state, where they will never reach your<br>origin. `infinite_queue` requires Advanced Waiting Room.<br>|
|» turnstile_mode|body|[waitingroom_turnstile_mode](#schemawaitingroom_turnstile_mode)|false|Which Turnstile widget type to use for detecting bot traffic. See<br>[the Turnstile documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/turnstile/concepts/widget/#widget-types)<br>for the definitions of these widget types. Set to `off` to disable the<br>Turnstile integration entirely. Setting this to anything other than<br>`off` or `invisible` requires Advanced Waiting Room.<br>|

## Patch waiting room

<a id="opIdwaiting-room-patch-waiting-room"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/waiting_rooms/699d98642c564d2e855e9661899b7252 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "additional_routes": [
      {
        "host": "shop2.example.com",
        "path": "/shop2/checkout"
      }
    ],
    "cookie_attributes": {
      "samesite": "auto",
      "secure": "auto"
    },
    "cookie_suffix": "abcd",
    "custom_page_html": "{{#waitTimeKnown}} {{waitTime}} mins {{/waitTimeKnown}} {{^waitTimeKnown}} Queue all enabled {{/waitTimeKnown}}",
    "default_template_language": "es-ES",
    "description": "Production - DO NOT MODIFY",
    "disable_session_renewal": false,
    "enabled_origin_commands": [],
    "host": "shop.example.com",
    "json_response_enabled": false,
    "name": "production_webinar",
    "new_users_per_minute": 200,
    "path": "/shop/checkout",
    "queue_all": true,
    "queueing_method": "fifo",
    "queueing_status_code": 202,
    "session_duration": 5,
    "suspended": false,
    "total_active_users": 200,
    "turnstile_action": "log",
    "turnstile_mode": "invisible"
  }'
```

`PATCH /zones/{zone_id}/waiting_rooms/{waiting_room_id}`

<h3 id="patch-waiting-room-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|waiting_room_id|path|[waitingroom_waiting_room_id](#schemawaitingroom_waiting_room_id)|true|none|
|zone_id|path|[waitingroom_identifier](#schemawaitingroom_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[waitingroom_query_waitingroom](#schemawaitingroom_query_waitingroom)|true|none|
|» additional_routes|body|[waitingroom_additional_routes](#schemawaitingroom_additional_routes)|false|Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. Additional hostname and path combinations to which this waiting room will be applied. There is an implied wildcard at the end of the path. The hostname and path combination must be unique to this and all other waiting rooms.|
|» cookie_attributes|body|[waitingroom_cookie_attributes](#schemawaitingroom_cookie_attributes)|false|Configures cookie attributes for the waiting room cookie. This encrypted cookie stores a user's status in the waiting room, such as queue position.|
|» cookie_suffix|body|[waitingroom_cookie_suffix](#schemawaitingroom_cookie_suffix)|false|Appends a '_' + a custom suffix to the end of Cloudflare Waiting Room's cookie name(__cf_waitingroom). If `cookie_suffix` is "abcd", the cookie name will be `__cf_waitingroom_abcd`. This field is required if using `additional_routes`.|
|» custom_page_html|body|[waitingroom_custom_page_html](#schemawaitingroom_custom_page_html)|false|Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. This is a template html file that will be rendered at the edge. If no custom_page_html is provided, the default waiting room will be used. The template is based on mustache ( https://mustache.github.io/ ). There are several variables that are evaluated by the Cloudflare edge:<br>1. {{`waitTimeKnown`}} Acts like a boolean value that indicates the behavior to take when wait time is not available, for instance when queue_all is **true**.<br>2. {{`waitTimeFormatted`}} Estimated wait time for the user. For example, five minutes. Alternatively, you can use:<br>3. {{`waitTime`}} Number of minutes of estimated wait for a user.<br>4. {{`waitTimeHours`}} Number of hours of estimated wait for a user (`Math.floor(waitTime/60)`).<br>5. {{`waitTimeHourMinutes`}} Number of minutes above the `waitTimeHours` value (`waitTime%60`).<br>6. {{`queueIsFull`}} Changes to **true** when no more people can be added to the queue.<br><br>To view the full list of variables, look at the `cfWaitingRoom` object described under the `json_response_enabled` property in other Waiting Room API calls.|
|» default_template_language|body|[waitingroom_default_template_language](#schemawaitingroom_default_template_language)|false|The language of the default page template. If no default_template_language is provided, then `en-US` (English) will be used.|
|» description|body|[waitingroom_description](#schemawaitingroom_description)|false|A note that you can use to add more details about the waiting room.|
|» disable_session_renewal|body|[waitingroom_disable_session_renewal](#schemawaitingroom_disable_session_renewal)|false|Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. Disables automatic renewal of session cookies. If `true`, an accepted user will have session_duration minutes to browse the site. After that, they will have to go through the waiting room again. If `false`, a user's session cookie will be automatically renewed on every request.|
|» enabled_origin_commands|body|[waitingroom_enabled_origin_commands](#schemawaitingroom_enabled_origin_commands)|false|A list of enabled origin commands.|
|» host|body|[waitingroom_host](#schemawaitingroom_host)|true|The host name to which the waiting room will be applied (no wildcards). Please do not include the scheme (http:// or https://). The host and path combination must be unique.|
|» json_response_enabled|body|[waitingroom_json_response_enabled](#schemawaitingroom_json_response_enabled)|false|Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. If `true`, requests to the waiting room with the header `Accept: application/json` will receive a JSON response object with information on the user's status in the waiting room as opposed to the configured static HTML page. This JSON response object has one property `cfWaitingRoom` which is an object containing the following fields:<br>1. `inWaitingRoom`: Boolean indicating if the user is in the waiting room (always **true**).<br>2. `waitTimeKnown`: Boolean indicating if the current estimated wait times are accurate. If **false**, they are not available.<br>3. `waitTime`: Valid only when `waitTimeKnown` is **true**. Integer indicating the current estimated time in minutes the user will wait in the waiting room. When `queueingMethod` is **random**, this is set to `waitTime50Percentile`.<br>4. `waitTime25Percentile`: Valid only when `queueingMethod` is **random** and `waitTimeKnown` is **true**. Integer indicating the current estimated maximum wait time for the 25% of users that gain entry the fastest (25th percentile).<br>5. `waitTime50Percentile`: Valid only when `queueingMethod` is **random** and `waitTimeKnown` is **true**. Integer indicating the current estimated maximum wait time for the 50% of users that gain entry the fastest (50th percentile). In other words, half of the queued users are expected to let into the origin website before `waitTime50Percentile` and half are expected to be let in after it.<br>6. `waitTime75Percentile`: Valid only when `queueingMethod` is **random** and `waitTimeKnown` is **true**. Integer indicating the current estimated maximum wait time for the 75% of users that gain entry the fastest (75th percentile).<br>7. `waitTimeFormatted`: String displaying the `waitTime` formatted in English for users. If `waitTimeKnown` is **false**, `waitTimeFormatted` will display **unavailable**.<br>8. `queueIsFull`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room's queue is currently full and not accepting new users at the moment.<br>9. `queueAll`: Boolean indicating if all users will be queued in the waiting room and no one will be let into the origin website.<br>10. `lastUpdated`: String displaying the timestamp as an ISO 8601 string of the user's last attempt to leave the waiting room and be let into the origin website. The user is able to make another attempt after `refreshIntervalSeconds` past this time. If the user makes a request too soon, it will be ignored and `lastUpdated` will not change.<br>11. `refreshIntervalSeconds`: Integer indicating the number of seconds after `lastUpdated` until the user is able to make another attempt to leave the waiting room and be let into the origin website. When the `queueingMethod` is `reject`, there is no specified refresh time —\_it will always be **zero**.<br>12. `queueingMethod`: The queueing method currently used by the waiting room. It is either **fifo**, **random**, **passthrough**, or **reject**.<br>13. `isFIFOQueue`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room uses a FIFO (First-In-First-Out) queue.<br>14. `isRandomQueue`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room uses a Random queue where users gain access randomly.<br>15. `isPassthroughQueue`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room uses a passthrough queue. Keep in mind that when passthrough is enabled, this JSON response will only exist when `queueAll` is **true** or `isEventPrequeueing` is **true** because in all other cases requests will go directly to the origin.<br>16. `isRejectQueue`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room uses a reject queue.<br>17. `isEventActive`: Boolean indicating if an event is currently occurring. Events are able to change a waiting room's behavior during a specified period of time. For additional information, look at the event properties `prequeue_start_time`, `event_start_time`, and `event_end_time` in the documentation for creating waiting room events. Events are considered active between these start and end times, as well as during the prequeueing period if it exists.<br>18. `isEventPrequeueing`: Valid only when `isEventActive` is **true**. Boolean indicating if an event is currently prequeueing users before it starts.<br>19. `timeUntilEventStart`: Valid only when `isEventPrequeueing` is **true**. Integer indicating the number of minutes until the event starts.<br>20. `timeUntilEventStartFormatted`: String displaying the `timeUntilEventStart` formatted in English for users. If `isEventPrequeueing` is **false**, `timeUntilEventStartFormatted` will display **unavailable**.<br>21. `timeUntilEventEnd`: Valid only when `isEventActive` is **true**. Integer indicating the number of minutes until the event ends.<br>22. `timeUntilEventEndFormatted`: String displaying the `timeUntilEventEnd` formatted in English for users. If `isEventActive` is **false**, `timeUntilEventEndFormatted` will display **unavailable**.<br>23. `shuffleAtEventStart`: Valid only when `isEventActive` is **true**. Boolean indicating if the users in the prequeue are shuffled randomly when the event starts.<br>24. `turnstile`: Empty when turnstile isn't enabled. String displaying an html tag to display the Turnstile widget. Please add the `{{{turnstile}}}` tag to the `custom_html` template to ensure the Turnstile widget appears.<br>25. `infiniteQueue`: Boolean indicating whether the response is for a user in the infinite queue.<br><br>An example cURL to a waiting room could be:<br><br>	curl -X GET "https://example.com/waitingroom" \<br>		-H "Accept: application/json"<br><br>If `json_response_enabled` is **true** and the request hits the waiting room, an example JSON response when `queueingMethod` is **fifo** and no event is active could be:<br><br>	{<br>		"cfWaitingRoom": {<br>			"inWaitingRoom": true,<br>			"waitTimeKnown": true,<br>			"waitTime": 10,<br>			"waitTime25Percentile": 0,<br>			"waitTime50Percentile": 0,<br>			"waitTime75Percentile": 0,<br>			"waitTimeFormatted": "10 minutes",<br>			"queueIsFull": false,<br>			"queueAll": false,<br>			"lastUpdated": "2020-08-03T23:46:00.000Z",<br>			"refreshIntervalSeconds": 20,<br>			"queueingMethod": "fifo",<br>			"isFIFOQueue": true,<br>			"isRandomQueue": false,<br>			"isPassthroughQueue": false,<br>			"isRejectQueue": false,<br>			"isEventActive": false,<br>			"isEventPrequeueing": false,<br>			"timeUntilEventStart": 0,<br>			"timeUntilEventStartFormatted": "unavailable",<br>			"timeUntilEventEnd": 0,<br>			"timeUntilEventEndFormatted": "unavailable",<br>			"shuffleAtEventStart": false<br>		}<br>	}<br><br>If `json_response_enabled` is **true** and the request hits the waiting room, an example JSON response when `queueingMethod` is **random** and an event is active could be:<br><br>	{<br>		"cfWaitingRoom": {<br>			"inWaitingRoom": true,<br>			"waitTimeKnown": true,<br>			"waitTime": 10,<br>			"waitTime25Percentile": 5,<br>			"waitTime50Percentile": 10,<br>			"waitTime75Percentile": 15,<br>			"waitTimeFormatted": "5 minutes to 15 minutes",<br>			"queueIsFull": false,<br>			"queueAll": false,<br>			"lastUpdated": "2020-08-03T23:46:00.000Z",<br>			"refreshIntervalSeconds": 20,<br>			"queueingMethod": "random",<br>			"isFIFOQueue": false,<br>			"isRandomQueue": true,<br>			"isPassthroughQueue": false,<br>			"isRejectQueue": false,<br>			"isEventActive": true,<br>			"isEventPrequeueing": false,<br>			"timeUntilEventStart": 0,<br>			"timeUntilEventStartFormatted": "unavailable",<br>			"timeUntilEventEnd": 15,<br>			"timeUntilEventEndFormatted": "15 minutes",<br>			"shuffleAtEventStart": true<br>		}<br>	}|
|» name|body|[waitingroom_name](#schemawaitingroom_name)|true|A unique name to identify the waiting room. Only alphanumeric characters, hyphens and underscores are allowed.|
|» new_users_per_minute|body|[waitingroom_new_users_per_minute](#schemawaitingroom_new_users_per_minute)|true|Sets the number of new users that will be let into the route every minute. This value is used as baseline for the number of users that are let in per minute. So it is possible that there is a little more or little less traffic coming to the route based on the traffic patterns at that time around the world.|
|» path|body|[waitingroom_path](#schemawaitingroom_path)|false|Sets the path within the host to enable the waiting room on. The waiting room will be enabled for all subpaths as well. If there are two waiting rooms on the same subpath, the waiting room for the most specific path will be chosen. Wildcards and query parameters are not supported.|
|» queue_all|body|[waitingroom_queue_all](#schemawaitingroom_queue_all)|false|If queue_all is `true`, all the traffic that is coming to a route will be sent to the waiting room. No new traffic can get to the route once this field is set and estimated time will become unavailable.|
|» queueing_method|body|[waitingroom_queueing_method](#schemawaitingroom_queueing_method)|false|Sets the queueing method used by the waiting room. Changing this parameter from the **default** queueing method is only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. Regardless of the queueing method, if `queue_all` is enabled or an event is prequeueing, users in the waiting room will not be accepted to the origin. These users will always see a waiting room page that refreshes automatically. The valid queueing methods are:<br>1. `fifo` **(default)**: First-In-First-Out queue where customers gain access in the order they arrived.<br>2. `random`: Random queue where customers gain access randomly, regardless of arrival time.<br>3. `passthrough`: Users will pass directly through the waiting room and into the origin website. As a result, any configured limits will not be respected while this is enabled. This method can be used as an alternative to disabling a waiting room (with `suspended`) so that analytics are still reported. This can be used if you wish to allow all traffic normally, but want to restrict traffic during a waiting room event, or vice versa.<br>4. `reject`: Users will be immediately rejected from the waiting room. As a result, no users will reach the origin website while this is enabled. This can be used if you wish to reject all traffic while performing maintenance, block traffic during a specified period of time (an event), or block traffic while events are not occurring. Consider a waiting room used for vaccine distribution that only allows traffic during sign-up events, and otherwise blocks all traffic. For this case, the waiting room uses `reject`, and its events override this with `fifo`, `random`, or `passthrough`. When this queueing method is enabled and neither `queueAll` is enabled nor an event is prequeueing, the waiting room page **will not refresh automatically**.|
|» queueing_status_code|body|[waitingroom_queueing_status_code](#schemawaitingroom_queueing_status_code)|false|HTTP status code returned to a user while in the queue.|
|» session_duration|body|[waitingroom_session_duration](#schemawaitingroom_session_duration)|false|Lifetime of a cookie (in minutes) set by Cloudflare for users who get access to the route. If a user is not seen by Cloudflare again in that time period, they will be treated as a new user that visits the route.|
|» suspended|body|[waitingroom_suspended](#schemawaitingroom_suspended)|false|Suspends or allows traffic going to the waiting room. If set to `true`, the traffic will not go to the waiting room.|
|» total_active_users|body|[waitingroom_total_active_users](#schemawaitingroom_total_active_users)|true|Sets the total number of active user sessions on the route at a point in time. A route is a combination of host and path on which a waiting room is available. This value is used as a baseline for the total number of active user sessions on the route. It is possible to have a situation where there are more or less active users sessions on the route based on the traffic patterns at that time around the world.|
|» turnstile_action|body|[waitingroom_turnstile_action](#schemawaitingroom_turnstile_action)|false|Which action to take when a bot is detected using Turnstile. `log` will<br>have no impact on queueing behavior, simply keeping track of how many<br>bots are detected in Waiting Room Analytics. `infinite_queue` will send<br>bots to a false queueing state, where they will never reach your<br>origin. `infinite_queue` requires Advanced Waiting Room.<br>|
|» turnstile_mode|body|[waitingroom_turnstile_mode](#schemawaitingroom_turnstile_mode)|false|Which Turnstile widget type to use for detecting bot traffic. See<br>[the Turnstile documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/turnstile/concepts/widget/#widget-types)<br>for the definitions of these widget types. Set to `off` to disable the<br>Turnstile integration entirely. Setting this to anything other than<br>`off` or `invisible` requires Advanced Waiting Room.<br>|

## Create event

<a id="opIdwaiting-room-create-event"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/waiting_rooms/699d98642c564d2e855e9661899b7252/events \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "custom_page_html": "{{#waitTimeKnown}} {{waitTime}} mins {{/waitTimeKnown}} {{^waitTimeKnown}} Event is prequeueing / Queue all enabled {{/waitTimeKnown}}",
    "description": "Production event - DO NOT MODIFY",
    "disable_session_renewal": true,
    "event_end_time": "2021-09-28T17:00:00Z",
    "event_start_time": "2021-09-28T15:30:00Z",
    "name": "production_webinar_event",
    "new_users_per_minute": 200,
    "prequeue_start_time": "2021-09-28T15:00:00Z",
    "queueing_method": "random",
    "session_duration": 1,
    "shuffle_at_event_start": false,
    "suspended": false,
    "total_active_users": 200,
    "turnstile_action": "log",
    "turnstile_mode": "off"
  }'
```

`POST /zones/{zone_id}/waiting_rooms/{waiting_room_id}/events`

Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. Creates an event for a waiting room. An event takes place during a specified period of time, temporarily changing the behavior of a waiting room. While the event is active, some of the properties in the event's configuration may either override or inherit from the waiting room's configuration. Note that events cannot overlap with each other, so only one event can be active at a time.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "custom_page_html": "{{#waitTimeKnown}} {{waitTime}} mins {{/waitTimeKnown}} {{^waitTimeKnown}} Event is prequeueing / Queue all enabled {{/waitTimeKnown}}",
  "description": "Production event - DO NOT MODIFY",
  "disable_session_renewal": true,
  "event_end_time": "2021-09-28T17:00:00Z",
  "event_start_time": "2021-09-28T15:30:00Z",
  "name": "production_webinar_event",
  "new_users_per_minute": 200,
  "prequeue_start_time": "2021-09-28T15:00:00Z",
  "queueing_method": "random",
  "session_duration": 1,
  "shuffle_at_event_start": false,
  "suspended": false,
  "total_active_users": 200,
  "turnstile_action": "log",
  "turnstile_mode": "off"
}
```

<h3 id="create-event-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|waiting_room_id|path|[waitingroom_waiting_room_id](#schemawaitingroom_waiting_room_id)|true|none|
|zone_id|path|[waitingroom_identifier](#schemawaitingroom_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[waitingroom_query_event](#schemawaitingroom_query_event)|true|none|
|» custom_page_html|body|[waitingroom_event_custom_page_html](#schemawaitingroom_event_custom_page_html)|false|If set, the event will override the waiting room's `custom_page_html` property while it is active. If null, the event will inherit it.|
|» description|body|[waitingroom_event_description](#schemawaitingroom_event_description)|false|A note that you can use to add more details about the event.|
|» disable_session_renewal|body|[waitingroom_event_disable_session_renewal](#schemawaitingroom_event_disable_session_renewal)|false|If set, the event will override the waiting room's `disable_session_renewal` property while it is active. If null, the event will inherit it.|
|» event_end_time|body|[waitingroom_event_end_time](#schemawaitingroom_event_end_time)|true|An ISO 8601 timestamp that marks the end of the event.|
|» event_start_time|body|[waitingroom_event_start_time](#schemawaitingroom_event_start_time)|true|An ISO 8601 timestamp that marks the start of the event. At this time, queued users will be processed with the event's configuration. The start time must be at least one minute before `event_end_time`.|
|» name|body|[waitingroom_event_name](#schemawaitingroom_event_name)|true|A unique name to identify the event. Only alphanumeric characters, hyphens and underscores are allowed.|
|» new_users_per_minute|body|[waitingroom_event_new_users_per_minute](#schemawaitingroom_event_new_users_per_minute)|false|If set, the event will override the waiting room's `new_users_per_minute` property while it is active. If null, the event will inherit it. This can only be set if the event's `total_active_users` property is also set.|
|» prequeue_start_time|body|[waitingroom_event_prequeue_start_time](#schemawaitingroom_event_prequeue_start_time)|false|An ISO 8601 timestamp that marks when to begin queueing all users before the event starts. The prequeue must start at least five minutes before `event_start_time`.|
|» queueing_method|body|[waitingroom_event_queueing_method](#schemawaitingroom_event_queueing_method)|false|If set, the event will override the waiting room's `queueing_method` property while it is active. If null, the event will inherit it.|
|» session_duration|body|[waitingroom_event_session_duration](#schemawaitingroom_event_session_duration)|false|If set, the event will override the waiting room's `session_duration` property while it is active. If null, the event will inherit it.|
|» shuffle_at_event_start|body|[waitingroom_event_shuffle_at_event_start](#schemawaitingroom_event_shuffle_at_event_start)|false|If enabled, users in the prequeue will be shuffled randomly at the `event_start_time`. Requires that `prequeue_start_time` is not null. This is useful for situations when many users will join the event prequeue at the same time and you want to shuffle them to ensure fairness. Naturally, it makes the most sense to enable this feature when the `queueing_method` during the event respects ordering such as **fifo**, or else the shuffling may be unnecessary.|
|» suspended|body|[waitingroom_event_suspended](#schemawaitingroom_event_suspended)|false|Suspends or allows an event. If set to `true`, the event is ignored and traffic will be handled based on the waiting room configuration.|
|» total_active_users|body|[waitingroom_event_total_active_users](#schemawaitingroom_event_total_active_users)|false|If set, the event will override the waiting room's `total_active_users` property while it is active. If null, the event will inherit it. This can only be set if the event's `new_users_per_minute` property is also set.|
|» turnstile_action|body|[waitingroom_event_turnstile_action](#schemawaitingroom_event_turnstile_action)|false|If set, the event will override the waiting room's `turnstile_action` property while it is active. If null, the event will inherit it.|
|» turnstile_mode|body|[waitingroom_event_turnstile_mode](#schemawaitingroom_event_turnstile_mode)|false|If set, the event will override the waiting room's `turnstile_mode` property while it is active. If null, the event will inherit it.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» turnstile_action|log|
|» turnstile_action|infinite_queue|
|» turnstile_mode|off|
|» turnstile_mode|invisible|
|» turnstile_mode|visible_non_interactive|
|» turnstile_mode|visible_managed|

## Get waiting room status

<a id="opIdwaiting-room-get-waiting-room-status"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/waiting_rooms/699d98642c564d2e855e9661899b7252/status \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /zones/{zone_id}/waiting_rooms/{waiting_room_id}/status`

Fetches the status of a configured waiting room. Response fields include:
1. `status`: String indicating the status of the waiting room. The possible status are:
	- **not_queueing** indicates that the configured thresholds have not been met and all users are going through to the origin.
	- **queueing** indicates that the thresholds have been met and some users are held in the waiting room.
	- **event_prequeueing** indicates that an event is active and is currently prequeueing users before it starts.
	- **suspended** indicates that the room is suspended.
2. `event_id`: String of the current event's `id` if an event is active, otherwise an empty string.
3. `estimated_queued_users`: Integer of the estimated number of users currently waiting in the queue.
4. `estimated_total_active_users`: Integer of the estimated number of users currently active on the origin.
5. `max_estimated_time_minutes`: Integer of the maximum estimated time currently presented to the users.

<h3 id="get-waiting-room-status-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|waiting_room_id|path|[waitingroom_waiting_room_id](#schemawaitingroom_waiting_room_id)|true|none|
|zone_id|path|[waitingroom_identifier](#schemawaitingroom_identifier)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "result": {
    "estimated_queued_users": 0,
    "estimated_total_active_users": 0,
    "event_id": "25756b2dfe6e378a06b033b670413757",
    "max_estimated_time_minutes": 0,
    "status": "queueing"
  },
  "success": true
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

<a id="opIdworker-script-upload-worker-module"></a>

## Patch multiple Worker script secrets

<a id="opIdworker-patch-script-secrets-bulk"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/workers/scripts/this-is_my_script-01/secrets-bulk \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "secrets": {
      "property1": {
        "name": "myBinding",
        "text": "My secret.",
        "type": "secret_text"
      },
      "property2": {
        "name": "myBinding",
        "text": "My secret.",
        "type": "secret_text"
      }
    },
    "version_tags": {}
  }'
```

`PATCH /accounts/{account_id}/workers/scripts/{script_name}/secrets-bulk`

Create, update, or delete multiple secrets on a Worker script in a single operation using JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396).
This operation creates a single version with all changes included.
Prefer this API instead of changing many secrets individually.

Usage:

- To create or update a secret, set its value to a secret object.
- To delete a secret, set its value to `null`.
- Secrets not included in the request are left unchanged.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "secrets": {
    "property1": {
      "name": "myBinding",
      "text": "My secret.",
      "type": "secret_text"
    },
    "property2": {
      "name": "myBinding",
      "text": "My secret.",
      "type": "secret_text"
    }
  },
  "version_tags": {}
}
```

<h3 id="patch-multiple-worker-script-secrets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[workers_identifier](#schemaworkers_identifier)|true|none|
|script_name|path|[workers_script_name](#schemaworkers_script_name)|true|none|
|body|body|[workers_secret-patch-request](#schemaworkers_secret-patch-request)|true|none|
|» secrets|body|object|false|Map of secret names to secret values:<br>- Set to a secret object to create or update.<br>- Set to `null` to delete.<br>- Omit to leave unchanged.<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object \| null|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[workers_binding_kind_secret_text](#schemaworkers_binding_kind_secret_text)|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[workers_binding_kind_secret_key](#schemaworkers_binding_kind_secret_key)|false|none|
|» version_tags|body|object|false|Optional version tags to apply to the new script version.|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "property1": {
      "name": "myBinding",
      "type": "secret_text"
    },
    "property2": {
      "name": "myBinding",
      "type": "secret_text"
    }
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{

      "code": 7003,

    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
```

`PATCH /accounts/{account_id}/workers/scripts/{script_name}/settings`

Patch Worker script metadata or config, such as bindings or usage model.

> Body parameter

```yaml
settings:
  annotations:
    workers/message: Fixed bug.
    workers/tag: v1.0.1
  bindings: {}
  cache_options:
    cross_version_cache: true
    enabled: true
  compatibility_date: {}
  compatibility_flags: {}
  exports:
    Admin:
      cache:
        enabled: true
      type: worker
    Counter:
      storage: sqlite
      type: durable-object
    OldCounter:
      renamed_to: Counter
      state: renamed
      type: durable-object
    default:
      cache:
        enabled: false
      type: worker
  exports_reconciliation:
    created:
      - string
    deleted:
      - string
    info:
      -
        class: string
        message: string
        namespace_id: "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
        referencing_scripts:
          - string
        scenario: code_class_not_in_exports
    removable_entries:
      - string
    renamed:
      -
        from: string
        to: string
    transfer_pending:
      -
        class: string
        from: string
    transferred:
      -
        class: string
        phase: committed
        to: string
    updated:
      - string
    warnings:
      -
        class: string
        message: string
        namespace_id: "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
        scenario: code_class_not_in_exports
  limits:
    cpu_ms: 50
    subrequests: 1000
  logpush: false
  migrations:
    new_tag: v2
    old_tag: v1
    deleted_classes:
      - string
    new_classes:
      - string
    new_sqlite_classes:
      - string
    renamed_classes:
      -
        from: string
        to: string
    transferred_classes:
      -
        from: string
        from_script: string
        to: string
  observability:
    enabled: true
    head_sampling_rate: 0.1
    issues:
      enabled: true
    logs:
      destinations:
        - cloudflare
      enabled: true
      head_sampling_rate: 0.1
      invocation_logs: true
      persist: true
    redact_query_string: false
    traces:
      destinations:
        - cloudflare
      enabled: true
      head_sampling_rate: 0.1
      persist: true
      propagation_policy: authenticated
  placement:
    mode: smart
  tags: {}
  tail_consumers: {}
  usage_model: standard
```

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/workers/dispatch/namespaces/my-dispatch-namespace \
```

`PUT /accounts/{account_id}/workers/dispatch/namespaces/{dispatch_namespace}`

Update a Workers for Platforms dispatch namespace.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "my-dispatch-namespace",
  "trusted_workers": false
}
```

<h3 id="update-workers-for-platforms-dispatch-namespace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[workers_identifier](#schemaworkers_identifier)|true|none|

|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the dispatch namespace.|
|» trusted_workers|body|[workers_trusted_workers](#schemaworkers_trusted_workers)|false|Whether the Workers in the namespace are executed in a "trusted" manner. When a Worker is trusted, it has access to the shared caches for the zone in the Cache API, and has access to the `request.cf` object on incoming Requests. When a Worker is untrusted, caches are not shared across the zone, and `request.cf` is undefined. By default, Workers in a namespace are "untrusted".|

```json
    "namespace_name": "my-dispatch-namespace",
    "script_count": 800,
    "trusted_workers": false
  }
}
```

## Upload Workers for Platforms Script Module

<a id="opIdnamespace-worker-script-upload-worker-module"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/workers/dispatch/namespaces/my-dispatch-namespace/scripts/this-is_my_script-01 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'files=["export default {\n  async fetch(request, env, ctx) {\n    return new Response(\"Hello, world!\");\n  }\n};"]' \
  -F 'metadata={"compatibility_date":{},"compatibility_flags":["nodejs_compat"],"main_module":"worker.js"}'
```

`PUT /accounts/{account_id}/workers/dispatch/namespaces/{dispatch_namespace}/scripts/{script_name}`

Upload a Workers for Platforms script module to a dispatch namespace. You can find more about the multipart metadata on our docs: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/multipart-upload-metadata/.

> Body parameter

```yaml
files:
  - "export default {\n  async fetch(request, env, ctx) {\n    return new Response(\"Hello, world!\");\n  }\n};"
metadata:
  compatibility_date: {}
  compatibility_flags:
    - nodejs_compat
  main_module: worker.js
```

## Patch multiple Workers for Platforms script secrets

<a id="opIdnamespace-worker-patch-script-secrets-bulk"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/workers/dispatch/namespaces/my-dispatch-namespace/scripts/this-is_my_script-01/secrets-bulk \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "secrets": {
      "property1": {
        "name": "myBinding",
        "text": "My secret.",
        "type": "secret_text"
      },
      "property2": {
        "name": "myBinding",
        "text": "My secret.",
        "type": "secret_text"
      }
    },
    "version_tags": {}
  }'
```

`PATCH /accounts/{account_id}/workers/dispatch/namespaces/{dispatch_namespace}/scripts/{script_name}/secrets-bulk`

Create, update, or delete multiple secrets on a Workers for Platforms script in a single operation using JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396).
This operation creates a single version with all changes included.
Prefer this API instead of changing many secrets individually.

Usage:

- To create or update a secret, set its value to a secret object.
- To delete a secret, set its value to `null`.
- Secrets not included in the request are left unchanged.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "secrets": {
    "property1": {
      "name": "myBinding",
      "text": "My secret.",
      "type": "secret_text"
    },
    "property2": {
      "name": "myBinding",
      "text": "My secret.",
      "type": "secret_text"
    }
  },
  "version_tags": {}
}
```

<h3 id="patch-multiple-workers-for-platforms-script-secrets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[workers_identifier](#schemaworkers_identifier)|true|none|
|dispatch_namespace|path|[workers_dispatch_namespace_name](#schemaworkers_dispatch_namespace_name)|true|none|
|script_name|path|[workers_script_name](#schemaworkers_script_name)|true|none|
|body|body|[workers_secret-patch-request](#schemaworkers_secret-patch-request)|true|none|
|» secrets|body|object|false|Map of secret names to secret values:<br>- Set to a secret object to create or update.<br>- Set to `null` to delete.<br>- Omit to leave unchanged.<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object \| null|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[workers_binding_kind_secret_text](#schemaworkers_binding_kind_secret_text)|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[workers_binding_kind_secret_key](#schemaworkers_binding_kind_secret_key)|false|none|
|» version_tags|body|object|false|Optional version tags to apply to the new script version.|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "property1": {
      "name": "myBinding",
      "type": "secret_text"
    },
    "property2": {
      "name": "myBinding",
      "type": "secret_text"
    }
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],

  "success": false
}
```

```json
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
```

`DELETE /accounts/{account_id}/workers/dispatch/namespaces/{dispatch_namespace}/scripts/{script_name}/tags/{tag}`

Delete a tag from a script uploaded to a Workers for Platforms dispatch namespace.

On `api-version` dates on or after `2026-10-01`, `tag` identifies a key and the operation returns the complete updated tag map. Deleting a missing key succeeds. Earlier versions retain the legacy string-tag behavior and return a null result.

|api-version|header|string|false|Requested API compatibility date in `YYYY-MM-DD[.release]` format (UTC). The optional release suffix contains lowercase letters; for example, `2026-10-01.epoch`.<br><br>Typed Worker tag operations require a date on or after `2026-10-01`.<br>|

`PUT /accounts/{account_id}/workers/domains`

Attaches a domain that routes traffic to a Worker.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "hostname": "app.example.com",
  "previews_enabled": false,
  "service": "my-worker",
  "zone_id": "593c9c94de529bbbfaac7c53ced0447d",
  "zone_name": "example.com"
}
```

|body|body|object|true|none|
|» enabled|body|boolean|true|Whether the configured hostname is routable for the domain. If disabled, then requests to the configured hostname will not be routed to the configured Worker. If disabled, then preview routing must be enabled, and only subdomains of the configured hostname will be routable.|
|» hostname|body|string|true|Hostname of the domain. Can be either the zone apex or a subdomain of the zone. Requests to this hostname will be routed to the configured Worker.|
|» previews_enabled|body|boolean|true|Whether previews are routable for the domain. If enabled, previews will be routable as subdomains of the configured hostname. For example, if the configured hostname is `app.example.com`, then requests to `my-feature.app.example.com` will be routed to the preview with slug `my-feature`, if such a preview exists. If preview routing is disabled, then hostname routing must be enabled.|
|» service|body|string|true|Name of the Worker associated with the domain. Requests to the configured hostname will be routed to this Worker.|
|» zone_id|body|string|true|ID of the zone containing the domain hostname.|
|» zone_name|body|string|true|Name of the zone containing the domain hostname.|

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-agents">Agents</h1>

## List Agent sessions

<a id="opIdagents.sessions.list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/workers/observability/agents/sessions?service=string&agent=string&from=0&to=0' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/workers/observability/agents/sessions`

Lists sessions in which the specified agent participated, ordered by most recent activity. A session is identified by gen_ai.conversation.id and includes authorized activity from every agent in that conversation during the requested time range. Agent invocation and chat spans without a conversation ID are attributed only when their trace is associated with exactly one observed conversation.

<h3 id="list-agent-sessions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|service|query|string|true|Worker service name associated with the participating agent.|
|agent|query|string|true|Agent name reported in gen_ai.agent.name. The request is limited to conversations in which this service and agent participated.|
|from|query|integer|true|Start of the requested time range, as Unix epoch milliseconds. Values earlier than the 7-day retention boundary are clamped.|
|to|query|integer|true|End of the requested time range, as Unix epoch milliseconds. Must be later than from.|
|cursor|query|string|false|Opaque cursor from result_info.cursors.after in the previous response.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Maximum number of items to return. Defaults to 20 and cannot exceed 100.|
|account_id|path|string|true|Your Cloudflare account ID.|

## List Agent session runs

<a id="opIdagents.sessions.runs.list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/workers/observability/agents/sessions/string/runs?service=string&agent=string&from=0&to=0' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/workers/observability/agents/sessions/{conversationId}/runs`

Lists the traces associated with a session, ordered by most recent activity. The service and agent parameters must identify an agent that participated in the conversation. Results include every authorized trace containing an agent invocation in that conversation during the requested time range.

<h3 id="list-agent-session-runs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|conversationId|path|string|true|OpenTelemetry gen_ai.conversation.id value that identifies the session.|
|service|query|string|true|Worker service name associated with the participating agent.|
|agent|query|string|true|Agent name reported in gen_ai.agent.name. The request is limited to conversations in which this service and agent participated.|
|from|query|integer|true|Start of the requested time range, as Unix epoch milliseconds. Values earlier than the 7-day retention boundary are clamped.|
|to|query|integer|true|End of the requested time range, as Unix epoch milliseconds. Must be later than from.|
|cursor|query|string|false|Opaque cursor from result_info.cursors.after in the previous response.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Maximum number of items to return. Defaults to 20 and cannot exceed 100.|
|account_id|path|string|true|Your Cloudflare account ID.|

```bash
    "skipPreflightCheck": true
  }'
```

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-shared">Shared</h1>

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/workers/observability/shared/query`

Shared queries store the results of a previously run query, allowing you to share the results with others.

> Body parameter

```json
  "chartType": "timeseries_and_aggregate",
```

<h3 id="create-a-sharable-link-to-a-query-result-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|Your Cloudflare account ID.|
|body|body|object|true|Create a sharable link to a query result.|
|» chart|body|boolean|false|When true, includes time-series data in the response.|
|» chartType|body|string|false|Controls the SQL shape and response payload for the 'calculations' view. Omitted or 'timeseries_and_aggregate': current behaviour — both the time-series and aggregate queries. 'timeseries': time-series only. 'aggregate': aggregate only. 'distribution': a bucketed 2D histogram (time × value buckets) returned in 'distribution' instead of 'calculations'. 'distribution' is not compatible with 'compare' — combining them returns a 400.|
|» compare|body|boolean|false|When true, includes a comparison dataset from the previous time period of equal length.|
|» distributionScale|body|string|false|Value-axis bucketing for chartType 'distribution'. Omitted or 'log': geometric buckets, best for heavy-tailed latency. 'linear': fixed-width buckets, clearer for narrow or additive ranges. Ignored for other chartTypes. The response echoes the scheme used in distribution.bucketMode.|
|» dry|body|boolean|false|When true, executes the query without persisting the results. Useful for validation or previewing.|
|» granularity|body|number|false|Number of time-series buckets. Only used when view is 'calculations'. Omit to let the system auto-detect an appropriate granularity.|
|» ignoreSeries|body|boolean|false|When true, omits time-series data from the response and returns only aggregated values. Reduces response size when series are not needed.|
|» limit|body|number|false|Maximum number of events to return when view is 'events'. Also controls the number of group-by rows when view is 'calculations'.|
|» offset|body|string|false|Cursor for pagination in event, trace, invocation, and agent views. Pass the $metadata.id of the last event, the trace cursor, or AgentRun.id to fetch the next page.|
|» offsetBy|body|number|false|Numeric offset for paginating grouped/pattern results (top-N lists). Use together with limit. Not used by cursor-based pagination.|
|» offsetDirection|body|string|false|Pagination direction: 'next' for forward, 'prev' for backward.|
|» parameters|body|object|false|Query parameters defining what data to retrieve — filters, calculations, group-bys, and ordering. In practice this should always be provided for ad-hoc queries. Only omit when executing a previously saved query by queryId. Use the keys and values endpoints to discover available fields before building filters.|
|» » calculations|body|[object]|false|Aggregation calculations to compute (e.g. count, avg, p99). Each calculation produces aggregate values and optional time-series data.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » » alias|body|string|false|Custom label for this calculation in the results. Useful for distinguishing multiple calculations.|
|» » » key|body|string|false|Field name to calculate over. Must exist in the data. Verify with the keys endpoint. Required for every operator except `count`, which aggregates whole rows and may omit it.|
|» » » keyType|body|string|false|Data type of the key. Required when key is provided to ensure correct aggregation.|
|» » » operator|body|string|true|Aggregation operator to apply. Examples: count, avg, sum, min, max, median, p90, p95, p99, uniq, stddev, variance.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » » alias|body|string|false|Custom label for this calculation in the results. Useful for distinguishing multiple calculations.|
|» » » key|body|string|true|Field name to calculate over. Must exist in the data. Verify with the keys endpoint. Required for every operator except `count`, which aggregates whole rows and may omit it.|
|» » » keyType|body|string|false|Data type of the key. Required when key is provided to ensure correct aggregation.|
|» » » operator|body|string|true|Aggregation operator to apply. Examples: count, avg, sum, min, max, median, p90, p95, p99, uniq, stddev, variance.|
|» » datasets|body|[string]|false|Datasets to query. Leave empty to query all available datasets.|
|» » filterCombination|body|string|false|Logical operator for combining top-level filters: 'and' (all must match) or 'or' (any must match). Defaults to 'and'.|
|» » filters|body|[object]|false|Filters to narrow query results. Use the keys and values endpoints to discover available fields before building filters. Supports nested groups via kind: 'group'. Maximum nesting depth is 4.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » » filterCombination|body|string|true|none|
|» » » filters|body|[[workers-observability_filter_node](#schemaworkers-observability_filter_node)]|true|none|
|» » » kind|body|string|true|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|[workers-observability_filter_leaf](#schemaworkers-observability_filter_leaf)|false|A filter condition applied to query results. Use the keys and values endpoints to discover available fields and their values before constructing filters.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|object|false|A group node that nests child filters combined with a logical operator.|
|» » » filterCombination|body|string|true|Logical operator for combining child filters: 'and' (all must match) or 'or' (any must match).|
|» » » filters|body|[[workers-observability_filter_node](#schemaworkers-observability_filter_node)]|true|Child filter nodes. Each can be a leaf filter or another nested group.|
|» » » kind|body|string|true|Discriminator indicating this is a nested filter group.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|[workers-observability_filter_leaf](#schemaworkers-observability_filter_leaf)|false|A filter condition applied to query results. Use the keys and values endpoints to discover available fields and their values before constructing filters.|
|» » groupBys|body|[object]|false|Fields to group calculation results by. Only applicable when the query view is 'calculations'. Produces per-group aggregate values.|
|» » » type|body|string|true|Data type of the group-by field.|
|» » » value|body|string|true|Field name to group results by (e.g. $metadata.service, $metadata.statusCode).|
|» » havings|body|[object]|false|Post-aggregation filters applied to calculation results. Use to filter groups after aggregation (e.g. only groups where count > 100).|
|» » » key|body|string|true|Calculation alias or operator to filter on after aggregation.|
|» » » operation|body|string|true|Numeric comparison operator: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte.|
|» » » value|body|number|true|Threshold value to compare the calculation result against.|
|» » limit|body|integer|false|Maximum number of group-by rows to return in calculation results. A value of 10 is a sensible default for most use cases.|
|» » needle|body|object|false|Full-text search expression applied across all event fields. Matches events containing the specified text.|
|» » » isRegex|body|boolean|false|When true, treats the value as a regular expression (RE2 syntax).|
|» » » matchCase|body|boolean|false|When true, performs a case-sensitive search. Defaults to case-insensitive.|
|» » » value|body|object|true|The text or pattern to search for.|
|» » » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » *anyOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » » » *anyOf*|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » orderBy|body|object|false|Ordering for grouped calculation results. Only effective when a group-by is present.|
|» » » order|body|string|false|Sort direction: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.|
|» » » value|body|string|true|Alias of the calculation to order results by. Must match the alias (or operator) of a calculation in the query.|
|» queryId|body|string|true|Identifier for the query. When parameters are omitted, this ID is used to load a previously saved query's parameters. When providing parameters inline, pass any identifier (e.g. an ad-hoc ID).|
|» timeframe|body|object|true|Timeframe for the query using Unix timestamps in milliseconds. 'from' must be earlier than 'to'. Narrower timeframes produce faster responses and more specific results.|
|» » from|body|integer|true|Start timestamp for the query timeframe. Unix timestamp in milliseconds|
|» » to|body|integer|true|End timestamp for the query timeframe. Unix timestamp in milliseconds|
|» view|body|string|false|Controls the shape of the response. 'events': individual log lines matching the query. 'calculations': aggregated metrics (count, avg, p99, etc.) with optional group-by breakdowns and time-series. 'invocations': events grouped by request ID. 'traces': distributed trace summaries. 'agents': agent-specific trace summaries.|

## View a query that has been shared

<a id="opIdshared.query.get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/workers/observability/shared/query/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/workers/observability/shared/query/{id}`

Shared queries store the results of a previously run query, allowing you to share the results with others.

<h3 id="view-a-query-that-has-been-shared-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|Specify the ID of the shared query.|
|view|query|string|false|Select the view of the query result to return, defaults to events.|
|account_id|path|string|true|Your Cloudflare account ID.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|view|events|
|view|invocations|
|view|calculations|

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-keys">Keys</h1>

## List keys

<a id="opIdtelemetry.keys.list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/workers/observability/telemetry/keys \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "datasets": [],
    "filters": [],
    "from": 0,
    "keyNeedle": {
      "isRegex": true,
      "matchCase": true,
      "value": {}
    },
    "limit": 0,
    "needle": {
      "isRegex": true,
      "matchCase": true,
      "value": {}
    },
    "to": 0
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/workers/observability/telemetry/keys`

List all the keys in your telemetry events.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "datasets": [],
  "filters": [],
  "from": 0,
  "keyNeedle": {
    "isRegex": true,
    "matchCase": true,
    "value": {}
  },
  "limit": 0,
  "needle": {
    "isRegex": true,
    "matchCase": true,
    "value": {}
  },
  "to": 0
}
```

|» datasets|body|[string]|false|Leave this empty to use the default datasets|
|» filters|body|[object]|false|Apply filters to narrow key discovery. Supports nested groups via kind: 'group'. Maximum nesting depth is 4.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|

|» » filters|body|[[workers-observability_filter_node](#schemaworkers-observability_filter_node)]|true|none|

|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|A group node that nests child filters combined with a logical operator.|
|» » filterCombination|body|string|true|Logical operator for combining child filters: 'and' (all must match) or 'or' (any must match).|

|» » matchCase|body|boolean|false|When true, performs a case-sensitive search. Defaults to case-insensitive.|

|» needle|body|object|false|Search for a specific substring in any of the events|

<h3 id="run-a-query-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|Your Cloudflare account ID.|
|body|body|object|true|Query your observability events, requests, and traces to build visualizations and identify insights.|
|» chart|body|boolean|false|When true, includes time-series data in the response.|
|» chartType|body|string|false|Controls the SQL shape and response payload for the 'calculations' view. Omitted or 'timeseries_and_aggregate': current behaviour — both the time-series and aggregate queries. 'timeseries': time-series only. 'aggregate': aggregate only. 'distribution': a bucketed 2D histogram (time × value buckets) returned in 'distribution' instead of 'calculations'. 'distribution' is not compatible with 'compare' — combining them returns a 400.|
|» compare|body|boolean|false|When true, includes a comparison dataset from the previous time period of equal length.|
|» distributionScale|body|string|false|Value-axis bucketing for chartType 'distribution'. Omitted or 'log': geometric buckets, best for heavy-tailed latency. 'linear': fixed-width buckets, clearer for narrow or additive ranges. Ignored for other chartTypes. The response echoes the scheme used in distribution.bucketMode.|
|» dry|body|boolean|false|When true, executes the query without persisting the results. Useful for validation or previewing.|
|» granularity|body|number|false|Number of time-series buckets. Only used when view is 'calculations'. Omit to let the system auto-detect an appropriate granularity.|
|» ignoreSeries|body|boolean|false|When true, omits time-series data from the response and returns only aggregated values. Reduces response size when series are not needed.|
|» limit|body|number|false|Maximum number of events to return when view is 'events'. Also controls the number of group-by rows when view is 'calculations'.|
|» offset|body|string|false|Cursor for pagination in event, trace, invocation, and agent views. Pass the $metadata.id of the last event, the trace cursor, or AgentRun.id to fetch the next page.|
|» offsetBy|body|number|false|Numeric offset for paginating grouped/pattern results (top-N lists). Use together with limit. Not used by cursor-based pagination.|
|» offsetDirection|body|string|false|Pagination direction: 'next' for forward, 'prev' for backward.|
|» parameters|body|object|false|Query parameters defining what data to retrieve — filters, calculations, group-bys, and ordering. In practice this should always be provided for ad-hoc queries. Only omit when executing a previously saved query by queryId. Use the keys and values endpoints to discover available fields before building filters.|
|» » calculations|body|[object]|false|Aggregation calculations to compute (e.g. count, avg, p99). Each calculation produces aggregate values and optional time-series data.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » » alias|body|string|false|Custom label for this calculation in the results. Useful for distinguishing multiple calculations.|
|» » » key|body|string|false|Field name to calculate over. Must exist in the data. Verify with the keys endpoint. Required for every operator except `count`, which aggregates whole rows and may omit it.|
|» » » keyType|body|string|false|Data type of the key. Required when key is provided to ensure correct aggregation.|
|» » » operator|body|string|true|Aggregation operator to apply. Examples: count, avg, sum, min, max, median, p90, p95, p99, uniq, stddev, variance.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » » alias|body|string|false|Custom label for this calculation in the results. Useful for distinguishing multiple calculations.|
|» » » key|body|string|true|Field name to calculate over. Must exist in the data. Verify with the keys endpoint. Required for every operator except `count`, which aggregates whole rows and may omit it.|
|» » » keyType|body|string|false|Data type of the key. Required when key is provided to ensure correct aggregation.|
|» » » operator|body|string|true|Aggregation operator to apply. Examples: count, avg, sum, min, max, median, p90, p95, p99, uniq, stddev, variance.|
|» » datasets|body|[string]|false|Datasets to query. Leave empty to query all available datasets.|
|» » filterCombination|body|string|false|Logical operator for combining top-level filters: 'and' (all must match) or 'or' (any must match). Defaults to 'and'.|

|» » » filterCombination|body|string|true|Logical operator for combining child filters: 'and' (all must match) or 'or' (any must match).|
|» » » filters|body|[[workers-observability_filter_node](#schemaworkers-observability_filter_node)]|true|Child filter nodes. Each can be a leaf filter or another nested group.|
|» » » kind|body|string|true|Discriminator indicating this is a nested filter group.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|[workers-observability_filter_leaf](#schemaworkers-observability_filter_leaf)|false|A filter condition applied to query results. Use the keys and values endpoints to discover available fields and their values before constructing filters.|
|» » groupBys|body|[object]|false|Fields to group calculation results by. Only applicable when the query view is 'calculations'. Produces per-group aggregate values.|
|» » » type|body|string|true|Data type of the group-by field.|

|» » havings|body|[object]|false|Post-aggregation filters applied to calculation results. Use to filter groups after aggregation (e.g. only groups where count > 100).|
|» » » key|body|string|true|Calculation alias or operator to filter on after aggregation.|
|» » » operation|body|string|true|Numeric comparison operator: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte.|
|» » » value|body|number|true|Threshold value to compare the calculation result against.|
|» » limit|body|integer|false|Maximum number of group-by rows to return in calculation results. A value of 10 is a sensible default for most use cases.|
|» » needle|body|object|false|Full-text search expression applied across all event fields. Matches events containing the specified text.|
|» » » isRegex|body|boolean|false|When true, treats the value as a regular expression (RE2 syntax).|
|» » » matchCase|body|boolean|false|When true, performs a case-sensitive search. Defaults to case-insensitive.|

|» » » » *anyOf*|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » orderBy|body|object|false|Ordering for grouped calculation results. Only effective when a group-by is present.|
|» » » order|body|string|false|Sort direction: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.|
|» » » value|body|string|true|Alias of the calculation to order results by. Must match the alias (or operator) of a calculation in the query.|
|» queryId|body|string|true|Identifier for the query. When parameters are omitted, this ID is used to load a previously saved query's parameters. When providing parameters inline, pass any identifier (e.g. an ad-hoc ID).|
|» timeframe|body|object|true|Timeframe for the query using Unix timestamps in milliseconds. 'from' must be earlier than 'to'. Narrower timeframes produce faster responses and more specific results.|

|» » to|body|integer|true|End timestamp for the query timeframe. Unix timestamp in milliseconds|
|» view|body|string|false|Controls the shape of the response. 'events': individual log lines matching the query. 'calculations': aggregated metrics (count, avg, p99, etc.) with optional group-by breakdowns and time-series. 'invocations': events grouped by request ID. 'traces': distributed trace summaries. 'agents': agent-specific trace summaries.|
