<h1 id="cloudflare-api-values">Values</h1>

## List values

<a id="opIdtelemetry.values.list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/workers/observability/telemetry/values \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "datasets": [
      "string"
    ],
    "filters": [],
    "key": "string",
    "limit": 50,
    "needle": {
      "isRegex": true,
      "matchCase": true,
      "value": {}
    },
    "timeframe": {
      "from": 0,
      "to": 0
    },
    "type": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/workers/observability/telemetry/values`

List unique values found in your events.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "datasets": [
    "string"
  ],
  "filters": [],
  "key": "string",
  "limit": 50,
  "needle": {
    "isRegex": true,
    "matchCase": true,
    "value": {}
  },
  "timeframe": {
    "from": 0,
    "to": 0
  },
  "type": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="list-values-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|Your Cloudflare account ID.|
|body|body|object|true|Retrieve values from your telemetry events.|
|» datasets|body|[string]|true|Leave this empty to use the default datasets|
|» filters|body|[object]|false|Apply filters before listing values. Supports nested groups via kind: 'group'. Maximum nesting depth is 4.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » filterCombination|body|string|true|none|
|» » filters|body|[[workers-observability_filter_node](#schemaworkers-observability_filter_node)]|true|none|
|» » kind|body|string|true|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[workers-observability_filter_leaf](#schemaworkers-observability_filter_leaf)|false|A filter condition applied to query results. Use the keys and values endpoints to discover available fields and their values before constructing filters.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|A group node that nests child filters combined with a logical operator.|
|» » filterCombination|body|string|true|Logical operator for combining child filters: 'and' (all must match) or 'or' (any must match).|
|» » filters|body|[[workers-observability_filter_node](#schemaworkers-observability_filter_node)]|true|Child filter nodes. Each can be a leaf filter or another nested group.|
|» » kind|body|string|true|Discriminator indicating this is a nested filter group.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[workers-observability_filter_leaf](#schemaworkers-observability_filter_leaf)|false|A filter condition applied to query results. Use the keys and values endpoints to discover available fields and their values before constructing filters.|
|» key|body|string|true|none|
|» limit|body|number|false|none|
|» needle|body|object|false|Full-text search expression to match events containing the specified text or pattern.|
|» » isRegex|body|boolean|false|When true, treats the value as a regular expression (RE2 syntax).|
|» » matchCase|body|boolean|false|When true, performs a case-sensitive search. Defaults to case-insensitive.|
|» » value|body|object|true|The text or pattern to search for.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|boolean|false|none|
|» timeframe|body|object|true|none|
|» » from|body|number|true|none|
|» » to|body|number|true|none|
|» type|body|string|true|none|

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-usage">Usage</h1>

## Get event count

<a id="opIdusage.get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/string/workers/observability/usage?from=string&to=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/workers/observability/usage`

Event counts and sizes broken down by dataset and service, bucketed by day, for up to 90 days. The top-level events field is the sum of all breakdown counts.

<h3 id="get-event-count-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|from|query|string|true|Unix timestamp in milliseconds for the start of the range.|
|to|query|string|true|Unix timestamp in milliseconds for the end of the range.|
|tz|query|string|false|IANA timezone used to align daily bins to local midnight (e.g. 'America/Chicago'). Defaults to UTC.|
|account_id|path|string|true|Your Cloudflare account ID.|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
```

## Create Worker Deployment

<a id="opIdworker-deployments-create-deployment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/workers/scripts/this-is_my_script-01/deployments \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "annotations": {
      "workers/message": "Deploy bug fix."
    },
    "code_update_strategy": {
      "mode": "immediate"
    },
    "strategy": "percentage",
    "versions": [
      {
        "percentage": 100,
        "version_id": "023e105f-2a42-4f8b-a1c1-73f6a2a30c0f"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/workers/scripts/{script_name}/deployments`

Deployments configure how [Worker Versions](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/operations/worker-versions-list-versions) are deployed to traffic. A deployment can consist of multiple versions of a Worker.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "annotations": {
    "workers/message": "Deploy bug fix."
  },
  "code_update_strategy": {
    "mode": "immediate"
  },
  "strategy": "percentage",
  "versions": [
    {
      "percentage": 100,
      "version_id": "023e105f-2a42-4f8b-a1c1-73f6a2a30c0f"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-worker-deployment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[workers_identifier](#schemaworkers_identifier)|true|none|
|script_name|path|[workers_script_name](#schemaworkers_script_name)|true|none|
|force|query|boolean|false|If set to true, the deployment will be created even if normally blocked by something such rolling back to an older version when a secret has changed.|
|body|body|[workers_deployment](#schemaworkers_deployment)|true|none|
|» annotations|body|object|false|none|
|» » workers/message|body|string|false|Human-readable message about the deployment. Truncated to 1000 bytes if longer.|
|» code_update_strategy|body|[workers_code_update_strategy](#schemaworkers_code_update_strategy) \| object \| null|false|Choose whether to apply Durable Object code updates immediately or defer them. When omitted, the default strategy applies.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[workers_code_update_strategy](#schemaworkers_code_update_strategy)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object \| null|false|none|
|» strategy|body|string|true|none|
|» versions|body|[object]|true|Worker versions included in this deployment. Each object must contain a `version_id` UUID and a `percentage`; percentages across all objects must total 100. In the `cf` CLI, pass the entire array as one JSON value to `--versions`, either inline, for example `--versions '[{"version_id":"023e105f-2a42-4f8b-a1c1-73f6a2a30c0f","percentage":100}]'`, or from a JSON file with `--versions @versions.json`.|
|» » percentage|body|number|true|Percentage of traffic served by this version.|
|» » version_id|body|string(uuid)|true|Identifier of the Worker Version.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *oneOf*|null|
|» strategy|percentage|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "annotations": {
      "workers/message": "Deploy bug fix.",

    },

}
```

## Upload Version

<a id="opIdworker-versions-upload-version"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/workers/scripts/this-is_my_script-01/versions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'files=["string"]' \
  -F 'metadata={"annotations":{"workers/alias":"staging","workers/commit_sha":"8b6aeb38455e2f92e170deb46313b90166ccc1e5","workers/message":"Fixed worker code.","workers/pull_request_number":"14966","workers/pull_request_title":"Add a cool new feature","workers/pull_request_url":"https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/14966","workers/repository_url":"https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk","workers/tag":"any-identifier-from-external-system"},"bindings":[{"name":"MY_ENV_VAR","text":"my_data","type":"plain_text"}],"cache_options":{"cross_version_cache":true,"enabled":true},"compatibility_date":"2021-01-01T00:00:00Z","compatibility_flags":["nodejs_compat"],"exports":{"Admin":{"cache":{"enabled":true},"type":"worker"},"Counter":{"storage":"sqlite","type":"durable-object"},"OldCounter":{"renamed_to":"Counter","state":"renamed","type":"durable-object"},"default":{"cache":{"enabled":false},"type":"worker"}},"keep_bindings":["string"],"main_module":"worker.js","package_dependencies":[{"installedVersion":"4.17.22","name":"lodash","packageJsonVersion":"^4.17.21"}],"usage_model":"standard"}'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/workers/scripts/{script_name}/versions`

Upload a Worker Version without deploying to Cloudflare's network. You can find more about the multipart metadata on our docs: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/multipart-upload-metadata/.

> Body parameter

```yaml
files:
  - string
metadata:
  annotations:
    workers/alias: staging
    workers/commit_sha: "8b6aeb38455e2f92e170deb46313b90166ccc1e5"
    workers/message: Fixed worker code.
    workers/pull_request_number: "14966"
    workers/pull_request_title: Add a cool new feature
    workers/pull_request_url: "https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/14966"
    workers/repository_url: "https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk"
    workers/tag: any-identifier-from-external-system
  bindings:
    -
      name: MY_ENV_VAR
      text: my_data
      type: plain_text
  cache_options:
    cross_version_cache: true
    enabled: true
  compatibility_date: "2021-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  compatibility_flags:
    - nodejs_compat
  exports:
    Admin:
      cache:
        enabled: true
      type: worker
    Counter:
      storage: sqlite
      type: durable-object
    OldCounter:
      renamed_to: Counter
      state: renamed
      type: durable-object
    default:
      cache:
        enabled: false
      type: worker
  keep_bindings:
    - string
  main_module: worker.js
  package_dependencies:
    -
      installedVersion: "4.17.22"
      name: lodash
      packageJsonVersion: "^4.17.21"
  usage_model: standard
```

<h3 id="upload-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[workers_identifier](#schemaworkers_identifier)|true|none|
|script_name|path|[workers_script_name-2](#schemaworkers_script_name-2)|true|none|
|bindings_inherit|query|string|false|When set to "strict", the upload will fail with error 10057 if any `inherit` type bindings cannot be resolved against the latest uploaded version of the Worker, which may not be the deployed version. Without this, unresolvable inherit bindings are silently dropped.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» files|body|[string(binary)]|false|An array of modules (often JavaScript files) comprising a Worker script. At least one module must be present and referenced in the metadata as `main_module` or `body_part` by filename.<br/>Possible Content-Type(s) are: `application/javascript+module`, `text/javascript+module`, `application/javascript`, `text/javascript`, `text/x-python`, `text/x-python-requirement`, `application/wasm`, `text/plain`, `application/octet-stream`, `application/source-map`.|
|» metadata|body|object|true|JSON-encoded metadata about the uploaded parts and Worker configuration.|
|» » annotations|body|object|false|none|
|» » » workers/alias|body|string|false|Associated alias for a version.|
|» » » workers/commit_sha|body|string|false|Full commit SHA associated with the version, detected from the CI environment. Maximum 64 bytes.|
|» » » workers/message|body|string|false|Human-readable message about the version. Truncated to 1000 bytes if longer.|
|» » » workers/pull_request_number|body|string|false|Number of the pull or merge request associated with the version, detected from the CI environment. Maximum 20 bytes.|
|» » » workers/pull_request_title|body|string|false|Title of the pull or merge request associated with the version, detected from the CI environment. Maximum 512 bytes.|
|» » » workers/pull_request_url|body|string|false|URL of the pull or merge request associated with the version, detected from the CI environment. Maximum 512 bytes.|
|» » » workers/repository_url|body|string|false|URL of the source repository the version was built from, detected from the CI environment. Maximum 512 bytes.|
|» » » workers/tag|body|string|false|User-provided identifier for the version. Maximum 100 bytes.|
|» » bindings|body|[workers_bindings](#schemaworkers_bindings)|false|List of bindings attached to a Worker. You can find more about bindings on our docs: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/multipart-upload-metadata/#bindings.|
|» » cache_options|body|[workers_cache_options](#schemaworkers_cache_options)|false|Global CacheW configuration for the Worker. When caching is on,<br>the platform provisions a `cloudflare.app` zone for the Worker.<br>A `type: worker` entry in the `exports` map can override this<br>value for a single entrypoint.<br>|
|» » compatibility_date|body|[workers_compatibility_date](#schemaworkers_compatibility_date)|false|Date indicating targeted support in the Workers runtime. Backwards incompatible fixes to the runtime following this date will not affect this Worker.|
|» » compatibility_flags|body|[workers_compatibility_flags](#schemaworkers_compatibility_flags)|false|Flags that enable or disable certain features in the Workers runtime. Used to enable upcoming features or opt in or out of specific changes not included in a `compatibility_date`.|
|» » exports|body|object|false|Declarative exports for this version. Worker<br>entrypoint entries (`type: worker`) carry cache<br>configuration for that entrypoint.<br>|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|[workers_export_config](#schemaworkers_export_config)|false|A single entry in the `exports` map, keyed by export name (a<br>`WorkerEntrypoint` class name, a Durable Object class name, or<br>`default` for the Worker's default export). The `type`<br>discriminator selects the top-level shape: `worker` entrypoint<br>entries may carry `cache` configuration, while `durable-object`<br>entries are further refined by the optional `state` field<br>(default `created`). Tombstone states (`deleted`, `renamed`,<br>`transferred`) express destructive lifecycle operations<br>declaratively; `expecting-transfer` is the live target side of a<br>transfer. The server validates the exact per-(type, state) field<br>combinations; fields not listed for a variant are rejected.<br>|
|» » keep_bindings|body|[string]|false|List of binding types to keep from previous_upload.|
|» » main_module|body|string|true|Name of the uploaded file that contains the main module (e.g. the file exporting a `fetch` handler). Indicates a `module syntax` Worker, which is required for Version Upload.|

|» » » installedVersion|body|string|true|The exact version that was resolved and installed by the package manager.|
|» » » name|body|string|true|The npm package name.|
|» » » packageJsonVersion|body|string|true|The version constraint as written in package.json.|
|» » usage_model|body|[workers_usage_model](#schemaworkers_usage_model)|false|Usage model for the Worker invocations.|

## Replace Worker Environment Script Content

<a id="opIdworker-environment-put-script-content"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/workers/services/my-worker/environments/production/content \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'files=["string"]' \
  -F 'metadata={"body_part":"worker.js","main_module":"worker.js"}'
```

`PUT /accounts/{account_id}/workers/services/{service_name}/environments/{environment_name}/content`

Replace Worker script content for an environment.

> Body parameter

```yaml
files:
  - string
metadata:
  body_part: worker.js
  main_module: worker.js
```

<h3 id="replace-worker-environment-script-content-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[workers_identifier](#schemaworkers_identifier)|true|none|
|service_name|path|[workers_service](#schemaworkers_service)|true|none|
|environment_name|path|[workers_environment](#schemaworkers_environment)|true|none|
|CF-WORKER-BODY-PART|header|string|false|The multipart name of a script upload part containing script content in service worker format. Alternative to including in a metadata part.|
|CF-WORKER-MAIN-MODULE-PART|header|string|false|The multipart name of a script upload part containing script content in es module format. Alternative to including in a metadata part.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» files|body|[string(binary)]|false|An array of modules (often JavaScript files) comprising a Worker script. At least one module must be present and referenced in the metadata as `main_module` or `body_part` by filename.<br/>Possible Content-Type(s) are: `application/javascript+module`, `text/javascript+module`, `application/javascript`, `text/javascript`, `text/x-python`, `text/x-python-requirement`, `application/wasm`, `text/plain`, `application/octet-stream`, `application/source-map`.|
|» metadata|body|object|true|JSON-encoded metadata about the uploaded parts and Worker configuration.|
|» » body_part|body|string|false|Name of the part in the multipart request that contains the script (e.g. the file adding a listener to the `fetch` event). Indicates a `service worker syntax` Worker.|
|» » main_module|body|string|false|Name of the part in the multipart request that contains the main module (e.g. the file exporting a `fetch` handler). Indicates a `module syntax` Worker.|

<h3 id="create-preview-deployment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Create Preview Deployment success.|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|Create Preview Deployment failure. When the upload uses the<br>declarative `exports` field and one or more entries fail<br>reconciliation, the response is the exports reconciliation<br>error envelope (error code 100402) with per-class detail in<br>`errors[].meta.details`.<br>|Inline|

<h3 id="create-preview-deployment-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[workers_messages](#schemaworkers_messages)|true|none|none|
|messages|[workers_messages](#schemaworkers_messages)|true|none|none|
|success|boolean|true|none|Whether the API call was successful.|
|result|[workers_PreviewDeployment](#schemaworkers_previewdeployment)|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|success|true|

Status Code **4XX**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|[workers_api-response-common-failure](#schemaworkers_api-response-common-failure)|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|[workers_exports_reconciliation_error_response](#schemaworkers_exports_reconciliation_error_response)|false|none|The v4 error envelope returned with HTTP 400 when one or more<br>declared `exports` entries fail reconciliation (error code<br>100402). The top-level error `message` aggregates the per-class<br>failures as human-readable prose; the structured per-class payload<br>is carried in `errors[].meta.details`, sorted by class name.<br>|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
api_token, api_email & api_key

`PATCH /accounts/{account_id}/workers/workers/{worker_id}/previews/{preview_id}/deployments/latest`

Only `/deployments/latest` is supported. Creates a new preview deployment by applying a JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) to the latest deployment. Patching a specific deployment ID is not supported. Omitted fields are inherited from the latest deployment. Preview base config is used for the first deployment.

|» » subrequests|body|integer|false|Subrequest limit per request.|
|» main_module|body|string|false|The name of the module that exports a `fetch` handler. Multipart uploads reference the file part by filename.|
|» migrations|body|[workers_single_step_migrations](#schemaworkers_single_step_migrations) \| [workers_multiple_step_migrations](#schemaworkers_multiple_step_migrations)|false|Migrations for Durable Objects associated with the deployment. Migrations are applied when the deployment is created.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[workers_single_step_migrations](#schemaworkers_single_step_migrations)|false|A single set of migrations to apply.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[workers_multiple_step_migrations](#schemaworkers_multiple_step_migrations)|false|none|
|» placement|body|[workers_placement_info_no_status](#schemaworkers_placement_info_no_status)|false|Configuration for [Smart Placement](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/smart-placement). Specify mode='smart' for Smart Placement, or one of region/hostname/host.|
|» usage_model|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** Usage model for the deployment.|
|» modules|body|[object]|false|Code, sourcemaps, and other content used at runtime.|
|» » content_base64|body|string(byte)|true|The base64-encoded module content.|
|» » content_type|body|string|true|The content type of the module.|
|» » name|body|string|true|The name of the module.|

|» usage_model|standard|
|» usage_model|bundled|
|» usage_model|unbound|

The top-level error `message` aggregates the per-class<br>failures as human-readable prose; the structured per-class payload<br>is carried in `errors[].meta.details`, sorted by class name.<br>|

<h3 id="create-worker-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[workers_identifier](#schemaworkers_identifier)|true|none|
|worker_id|path|string|true|none|
|deploy|query|boolean|false|none|
|body|body|[workers_Version](#schemaworkers_version)|true|Version creation parameters.|
|» annotations|body|object|false|Metadata about the version.|
|» » workers/message|body|string|false|Human-readable message about the version. Truncated to 1000 bytes if longer.|
|» » workers/tag|body|string|false|User-provided identifier for the version. Maximum 100 bytes.|
|» assets|body|object|false|Configuration for assets within a Worker.<br><br>[`_headers`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/headers/#custom-headers) and<br>[`_redirects`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/redirects/) files should be<br>included as modules named `_headers` and `_redirects` with content type `text/plain`.<br>|
|» » config|body|object|false|Configuration for assets within a Worker.|
|» » » base_path|body|string \| null|false|The public URL path prefix under which assets are served. A null request value resets it to `/`; responses represent the root as `/`. All versions in a gradual deployment must use the same canonical value. To change it, first deploy the version containing the change at 100%.|
|» » » html_handling|body|string|false|Determines the redirects and rewrites of requests for HTML content.|
|» » » not_found_handling|body|string|false|Determines the response when a request does not match a static asset, and there is no Worker script.|
|» » » run_worker_first|body|[string] \| boolean|false|none|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|Contains a list path rules to control routing to either the Worker or assets. Glob (*) and negative (!) rules are supported. Rules must start with either '/' or '!/'. At least one non-negative rule must be provided, and negative rules have higher precedence than non-negative rules.|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|boolean|false|Enables routing to always invoke the Worker script ahead of all requests. When true, this is equivalent to `["/*"]` in the string array version of this field.|
|» » jwt|body|string|false|Token provided upon successful upload of all files from a registered manifest.|
|» bindings|body|[workers_bindings](#schemaworkers_bindings)|false|List of bindings attached to a Worker. You can find more about bindings on our docs: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/multipart-upload-metadata/#bindings.|
|» cache_options|body|[workers_cache_options](#schemaworkers_cache_options)|false|Global CacheW configuration for the Worker. When caching is on,<br>the platform provisions a `cloudflare.app` zone for the Worker.<br>A `type: worker` entry in the `exports` map can override this<br>value for a single entrypoint.<br>|
|» compatibility_date|body|[workers_compatibility_date](#schemaworkers_compatibility_date)|false|Date indicating targeted support in the Workers runtime. Backwards incompatible fixes to the runtime following this date will not affect this Worker.|
|» compatibility_flags|body|[workers_compatibility_flags](#schemaworkers_compatibility_flags)|false|Flags that enable or disable certain features in the Workers runtime. Used to enable upcoming features or opt in or out of specific changes not included in a `compatibility_date`.|
|» containers|body|[workers_containers](#schemaworkers_containers)|false|List of containers attached to a Worker. Containers can only be attached to Durable Object classes of this Worker script.|
|» exports|body|object|false|Declarative exports for the version, including Durable Object<br>classes (with their `storage` backend) and named Worker<br>entrypoints. On reads, tombstoned lifecycle entries are<br>omitted, so only live exports (`created` and<br>`expecting-transfer`) are returned. `exports` and `migrations`<br>are mutually exclusive on upload.<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[workers_export_config](#schemaworkers_export_config)|false|A single entry in the `exports` map, keyed by export name (a<br>`WorkerEntrypoint` class name, a Durable Object class name, or<br>`default` for the Worker's default export). The `type`<br>discriminator selects the top-level shape: `worker` entrypoint<br>entries may carry `cache` configuration, while `durable-object`<br>entries are further refined by the optional `state` field<br>(default `created`). Tombstone states (`deleted`, `renamed`,<br>`transferred`) express destructive lifecycle operations<br>declaratively; `expecting-transfer` is the live target side of a<br>transfer. The server validates the exact per-(type, state) field<br>combinations; fields not listed for a variant are rejected.<br>|
|» exports_reconciliation|body|object|false|Summary of the declarative exports reconciliation that ran on<br>this upload. Populated only when the uploaded metadata included<br>an `exports` block. Durable Object entries drive reconciliation;<br>`type: worker` entries do not contribute to this summary.<br>|
|» » created|body|[string]|true|Class names for which a new namespace was provisioned.|
|» » deleted|body|[string]|true|Class names whose namespace was deleted by a `deleted` tombstone.|
|» » info|body|[[workers_exports_reconciliation_info](#schemaworkers_exports_reconciliation_info)]|true|Non-blocking info entries (stale tombstones, tombstone applied<br>with class still in code). See `exports_reconciliation_info`.<br>|
|» » removable_entries|body|[string]|true|Source class names whose tombstone entry is now stale and safe<br>to delete from `exports` (no remaining referencing scripts).<br>|
|» » renamed|body|[[workers_exports_reconciliation_rename](#schemaworkers_exports_reconciliation_rename)]|true|Applied `renamed` tombstones.|
|» » transfer_pending|body|[[workers_exports_reconciliation_transfer_pending](#schemaworkers_exports_reconciliation_transfer_pending)]|true|Phase-1 transfer hints recorded on the target side.|
|» » transferred|body|[[workers_exports_reconciliation_transfer](#schemaworkers_exports_reconciliation_transfer)]|true|Committed `transferred` tombstones (phase-2).|
|» » updated|body|[string]|true|Class names whose provisioned namespace was mutated in place.|
|» » warnings|body|[[workers_exports_reconciliation_warning](#schemaworkers_exports_reconciliation_warning)]|true|Non-blocking warnings. See `exports_reconciliation_warning`.|
|» limits|body|object|false|Resource limits enforced at runtime.|
|» » cpu_ms|body|integer|false|CPU time limit in milliseconds.|
|» » subrequests|body|integer|false|Subrequest limit per request.|
|» main_module|body|string|false|The name of the main module in the `modules` array (e.g. the name of the module that exports a `fetch` handler).|
|» migrations|body|[workers_single_step_migrations](#schemaworkers_single_step_migrations) \| [workers_multiple_step_migrations](#schemaworkers_multiple_step_migrations)|false|Migrations for Durable Objects associated with the version. Migrations are applied when the version is deployed.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[workers_single_step_migrations](#schemaworkers_single_step_migrations)|false|A single set of migrations to apply.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[workers_multiple_step_migrations](#schemaworkers_multiple_step_migrations)|false|none|
|» modules|body|[object]|false|Code, sourcemaps, and other content used at runtime.<br><br>This includes [`_headers`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/headers/#custom-headers) and<br>[`_redirects`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/redirects/) files used to configure<br>[Static Assets](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/). `_headers` and `_redirects` files should be<br>included as modules named `_headers` and `_redirects` with content type `text/plain`.<br>|
|» » content_base64|body|string(byte)|true|The base64-encoded module content.|
|» » content_type|body|string|true|The content type of the module.|
|» » name|body|string|true|The name of the module.|
|» package_dependencies|body|[object]|false|The list of npm packages that were installed and used when this Worker<br>version was built.<br>|
|» » installedVersion|body|string|true|The exact version that was resolved and installed by the package manager.|
|» » name|body|string|true|The npm package name.|
|» » packageJsonVersion|body|string|true|The version constraint as written in package.json.|
|» placement|body|[workers_placement_info_no_status](#schemaworkers_placement_info_no_status)|false|Configuration for [Smart Placement](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/smart-placement). Specify mode='smart' for Smart Placement, or one of region/hostname/host.|
|» usage_model|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** Usage model for the version.|

<h3 id="create-worker-version-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Create version success.|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|Create version failure. When the upload uses the declarative<br>`exports` field and one or more entries fail reconciliation,<br>the response is the exports reconciliation error envelope<br>(error code 100402) with per-class detail in<br>`errors[].meta.details`.<br>|Inline|

<h3 id="create-worker-version-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[workers_messages](#schemaworkers_messages)|true|none|none|
|messages|[workers_messages](#schemaworkers_messages)|true|none|none|
|success|boolean|true|none|Whether the API call was successful.|
|result|[workers_Version](#schemaworkers_version)|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|success|true|

Status Code **4XX**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|[workers_api-response-common-failure](#schemaworkers_api-response-common-failure)|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|[workers_exports_reconciliation_error_response](#schemaworkers_exports_reconciliation_error_response)|false|none|The v4 error envelope returned with HTTP 400 when one or more<br>declared `exports` entries fail reconciliation (error code<br>100402). The top-level error `message` aggregates the per-class<br>failures as human-readable prose; the structured per-class payload<br>is carried in `errors[].meta.details`, sorted by class name.<br>|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
api_token, api_email & api_key
</aside>

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`PATCH /accounts/{account_id}/workers/workers/{worker_id}/versions/latest`

Only `/versions/latest` is supported. Creates a new Worker version by applying a JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) to the latest version. Patching a specific version ID is not supported. Omitted fields are inherited from the latest version.

<h3 id="patch-latest-worker-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[workers_identifier](#schemaworkers_identifier)|true|none|
|worker_id|path|string|true|none|
|deploy|query|boolean|false|none|
|body|body|object|false|JSON Merge Patch to apply to the latest version. An empty object creates a new version with no changes.|
|» annotations|body|object|false|Metadata about the version.|
|» » workers/message|body|string|false|Human-readable message about the version. Truncated to 1000 bytes if longer.|
|» » workers/tag|body|string|false|User-provided identifier for the version. Maximum 100 bytes.|
|» assets|body|object|false|Configuration for assets within a Worker.<br><br>[`_headers`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/headers/#custom-headers) and<br>[`_redirects`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/redirects/) files should be<br>included as modules named `_headers` and `_redirects` with content type `text/plain`.<br>|
|» » config|body|object|false|Configuration for assets within a Worker.|
|» » » base_path|body|string \| null|false|The public URL path prefix under which assets are served. A null request value resets it to `/`; responses represent the root as `/`. All versions in a gradual deployment must use the same canonical value. To change it, first deploy the version containing the change at 100%.|
|» » » html_handling|body|string|false|Determines the redirects and rewrites of requests for HTML content.|
|» » » not_found_handling|body|string|false|Determines the response when a request does not match a static asset, and there is no Worker script.|
|» » » run_worker_first|body|[string] \| boolean|false|none|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|Contains a list path rules to control routing to either the Worker or assets. Glob (*) and negative (!) rules are supported. Rules must start with either '/' or '!/'. At least one non-negative rule must be provided, and negative rules have higher precedence than non-negative rules.|
|» » » » *oneOf*|body|boolean|false|Enables routing to always invoke the Worker script ahead of all requests. When true, this is equivalent to `["/*"]` in the string array version of this field.|
|» » jwt|body|string|false|Token provided upon successful upload of all files from a registered manifest.|
|» bindings|body|[workers_bindings](#schemaworkers_bindings)|false|List of bindings attached to a Worker. You can find more about bindings on our docs: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/multipart-upload-metadata/#bindings.|
|» cache_options|body|[workers_cache_options](#schemaworkers_cache_options)|false|Global CacheW configuration for the Worker. When caching is on,<br>the platform provisions a `cloudflare.app` zone for the Worker.<br>A `type: worker` entry in the `exports` map can override this<br>value for a single entrypoint.<br>|
|» compatibility_date|body|[workers_compatibility_date](#schemaworkers_compatibility_date)|false|Date indicating targeted support in the Workers runtime. Backwards incompatible fixes to the runtime following this date will not affect this Worker.|
|» compatibility_flags|body|[workers_compatibility_flags](#schemaworkers_compatibility_flags)|false|Flags that enable or disable certain features in the Workers runtime. Used to enable upcoming features or opt in or out of specific changes not included in a `compatibility_date`.|
|» containers|body|[workers_containers](#schemaworkers_containers)|false|List of containers attached to a Worker. Containers can only be attached to Durable Object classes of this Worker script.|
|» exports|body|object|false|Declarative exports for the version, including Durable Object<br>classes (with their `storage` backend) and named Worker<br>entrypoints. On reads, tombstoned lifecycle entries are<br>omitted, so only live exports (`created` and<br>`expecting-transfer`) are returned. `exports` and `migrations`<br>are mutually exclusive on upload.<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[workers_export_config](#schemaworkers_export_config)|false|A single entry in the `exports` map, keyed by export name (a<br>`WorkerEntrypoint` class name, a Durable Object class name, or<br>`default` for the Worker's default export). The `type`<br>discriminator selects the top-level shape: `worker` entrypoint<br>entries may carry `cache` configuration, while `durable-object`<br>entries are further refined by the optional `state` field<br>(default `created`). Tombstone states (`deleted`, `renamed`,<br>`transferred`) express destructive lifecycle operations<br>declaratively; `expecting-transfer` is the live target side of a<br>transfer. The server validates the exact per-(type, state) field<br>combinations; fields not listed for a variant are rejected.<br>|
|» exports_reconciliation|body|object|false|Summary of the declarative exports reconciliation that ran on<br>this upload. Populated only when the uploaded metadata included<br>an `exports` block. Durable Object entries drive reconciliation;<br>`type: worker` entries do not contribute to this summary.<br>|
|» » created|body|[string]|true|Class names for which a new namespace was provisioned.|
|» » deleted|body|[string]|true|Class names whose namespace was deleted by a `deleted` tombstone.|
|» » info|body|[[workers_exports_reconciliation_info](#schemaworkers_exports_reconciliation_info)]|true|Non-blocking info entries (stale tombstones, tombstone applied<br>with class still in code). See `exports_reconciliation_info`.<br>|
|» » removable_entries|body|[string]|true|Source class names whose tombstone entry is now stale and safe<br>to delete from `exports` (no remaining referencing scripts).<br>|
|» » renamed|body|[[workers_exports_reconciliation_rename](#schemaworkers_exports_reconciliation_rename)]|true|Applied `renamed` tombstones.|
|» » transfer_pending|body|[[workers_exports_reconciliation_transfer_pending](#schemaworkers_exports_reconciliation_transfer_pending)]|true|Phase-1 transfer hints recorded on the target side.|
|» » transferred|body|[[workers_exports_reconciliation_transfer](#schemaworkers_exports_reconciliation_transfer)]|true|Committed `transferred` tombstones (phase-2).|
|» » updated|body|[string]|true|Class names whose provisioned namespace was mutated in place.|
|» » warnings|body|[[workers_exports_reconciliation_warning](#schemaworkers_exports_reconciliation_warning)]|true|Non-blocking warnings. See `exports_reconciliation_warning`.|
|» limits|body|object|false|Resource limits enforced at runtime.|
|» » cpu_ms|body|integer|false|CPU time limit in milliseconds.|
|» » subrequests|body|integer|false|Subrequest limit per request.|
|» main_module|body|string|false|The name of the main module in the `modules` array (e.g. the name of the module that exports a `fetch` handler).|
|» migrations|body|[workers_single_step_migrations](#schemaworkers_single_step_migrations) \| [workers_multiple_step_migrations](#schemaworkers_multiple_step_migrations)|false|Migrations for Durable Objects associated with the version. Migrations are applied when the version is deployed.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[workers_single_step_migrations](#schemaworkers_single_step_migrations)|false|A single set of migrations to apply.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[workers_multiple_step_migrations](#schemaworkers_multiple_step_migrations)|false|none|
|» modules|body|[object]|false|Code, sourcemaps, and other content used at runtime.<br><br>This includes [`_headers`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/headers/#custom-headers) and<br>[`_redirects`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/redirects/) files used to configure<br>[Static Assets](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/). `_headers` and `_redirects` files should be<br>included as modules named `_headers` and `_redirects` with content type `text/plain`.<br>|
|» » content_base64|body|string(byte)|true|The base64-encoded module content.|
|» » content_type|body|string|true|The content type of the module.|
|» » name|body|string|true|The name of the module.|
|» package_dependencies|body|[object]|false|The list of npm packages that were installed and used when this Worker<br>version was built.<br>|
|» » installedVersion|body|string|true|The exact version that was resolved and installed by the package manager.|
|» » name|body|string|true|The npm package name.|
|» » packageJsonVersion|body|string|true|The version constraint as written in package.json.|
|» placement|body|[workers_placement_info_no_status](#schemaworkers_placement_info_no_status)|false|Configuration for [Smart Placement](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/smart-placement). Specify mode='smart' for Smart Placement, or one of region/hostname/host.|
|» usage_model|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** Usage model for the version.|

<h3 id="patch-latest-worker-version-responses">Responses</h3>

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Patch version success.|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|Patch version failure. When the patch uses the declarative<br>`exports` field and one or more entries fail reconciliation,<br>the response is the exports reconciliation error envelope<br>(error code 100402) with per-class detail in<br>`errors[].meta.details`.<br>|Inline|

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-worker-profiling">Worker Profiling</h1>

## Profile Worker Version

<a id="opIdprofileWorkerVersion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/workers/workers/string/versions/string/profile \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "actor_id": "string",
    "duration_ms": 1000,
    "namespace_id": "string",
    "profile_type": "cpu"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/workers/workers/{worker_id}/versions/{version_id}/profile`

Captures a CPU or heap profile from a recently active isolate running the specified Worker version. This endpoint requires the Worker profiling feature to be enabled for the account.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "actor_id": "string",
  "duration_ms": 1000,
  "namespace_id": "string",
  "profile_type": "cpu"
}
```

<h3 id="profile-worker-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[workers_identifier](#schemaworkers_identifier)|true|none|
|worker_id|path|string|true|none|
|version_id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» actor_id|body|string|false|Identifies the exact Durable Object actor to profile. Must be specified together with namespace_id. The actor must currently be active and running the requested version.|
|» duration_ms|body|integer(int32)|true|Profile duration in milliseconds.|
|» namespace_id|body|string|false|Identifies the Durable Object namespace containing the actor to profile. Must be specified together with actor_id.|
|» profile_type|body|string|false|none|

|» profile_type|heap|

## Create WARP IP subnet

<a id="opIdzero-trust-networks-subnet-create-warp"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/699d98642c564d2e855e9661899b7252/zerotrust/subnets/warp \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "comment": "example comment",
    "is_default_network": false,
    "name": "IPv4 Cloudflare Source IPs",
    "network": "100.64.0.0/12"
  }'
```

`POST /accounts/{account_id}/zerotrust/subnets/warp`

Create a WARP IP assignment subnet. Currently, only IPv4 subnets can be created.

**Network constraints:**
- The network must be within one of the following private IP ranges:
  - `10.0.0.0/8` (RFC 1918)
  - `172.16.0.0/12` (RFC 1918)
  - `192.168.0.0/16` (RFC 1918)
  - `100.64.0.0/10` (RFC 6598 - CGNAT)
- The subnet must have a prefix length of `/24` or larger (e.g., `/16`, `/20`, `/24` are valid; `/25`, `/28` are not)


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comment": "example comment",
  "is_default_network": false,
  "name": "IPv4 Cloudflare Source IPs",
  "network": "100.64.0.0/12"
}
```

<h3 id="create-warp-ip-subnet-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|[tunnel_account_id](#schematunnel_account_id)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» comment|body|[tunnel_subnet_comment](#schematunnel_subnet_comment)|false|An optional description of the subnet.|
|» is_default_network|body|[tunnel_subnet_is_default_network](#schematunnel_subnet_is_default_network)|false|If `true`, this is the default subnet for the account. There can only be one default subnet per account.|
|» name|body|[tunnel_subnet_name](#schematunnel_subnet_name)|true|A user-friendly name for the subnet.|
|» network|body|[tunnel_subnet_ip_network](#schematunnel_subnet_ip_network)|true|The private IPv4 or IPv6 range defining the subnet, in CIDR notation.|

> Example responses

```json
    },

    "deleted_at": "2009-11-10T23:00:00Z",
    "id": "f70ff985-a4ef-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415",
    "is_default_network": false,
    "name": "IPv4 Cloudflare Source IPs",
```

`PATCH /accounts/{account_id}/zerotrust/subnets/warp/{subnet_id}`

Updates a WARP IP assignment subnet.

**Update constraints:**
- The `network` field cannot be modified for WARP subnets. Only `name`, `comment`, and `is_default_network` can be updated.
- IPv6 subnets cannot be updated

## Create Certificate

> Code samples

`POST /certificates`

Create an Origin CA certificate. You can use an Origin CA Key as your User Service Key or an API token when calling this endpoint ([see above](#requests)).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "csr": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE REQUEST-----\nMIICxzCCAa8CAQAwSDELMAkGA1UEBhMCVVMxFjAUBgNVBAgTDVNhbiBGcmFuY2lz\nY28xCzAJBgNVBAcTAkNBMRQwEgYDVQQDEwtleGFtcGxlLm5ldDCCASIwDQYJKoZI\nhvcNAQEBBQADggEPADCCAQoCggEBALxejtu4b+jPdFeFi6OUsye8TYJQBm3WfCvL\nHu5EvijMO/4Z2TImwASbwUF7Ir8OLgH+mGlQZeqyNvGoSOMEaZVXcYfpR1hlVak8\n4GGVr+04IGfOCqaBokaBFIwzclGZbzKmLGwIQioNxGfqFm6RGYGA3be2Je2iseBc\nN8GV1wYmvYE0RR+yWweJCTJ157exyRzu7sVxaEW9F87zBQLyOnwXc64rflXslRqi\ng7F7w5IaQYOl8yvmk/jEPCAha7fkiUfEpj4N12+oPRiMvleJF98chxjD4MH39c5I\nuOslULhrWunfh7GB1jwWNA9y44H0snrf+xvoy2TcHmxvma9Eln8CAwEAAaA6MDgG\nCSqGSIb3DQEJDjErMCkwJwYDVR0RBCAwHoILZXhhbXBsZS5uZXSCD3d3dy5leGFt\ncGxlLm5ldDANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQsFAAOCAQEAcBaX6dOnI8ncARrI9ZSF2AJX+8mx\npTHY2+Y2C0VvrVDGMtbBRH8R9yMbqWtlxeeNGf//LeMkSKSFa4kbpdx226lfui8/\nauRDBTJGx2R1ccUxmLZXx4my0W5iIMxunu+kez+BDlu7bTT2io0uXMRHue4i6quH\nyc5ibxvbJMjR7dqbcanVE10/34oprzXQsJ/VmSuZNXtjbtSKDlmcpw6To/eeAJ+J\nhXykcUihvHyG4A1m2R6qpANBjnA0pHexfwM/SgfzvpbvUg0T1ubmer8BgTwCKIWs\ndcWYTthM51JIqRBfNqy4QcBnX+GY05yltEEswQI55wdiS3CjTTA67sdbcQ==\n-----END CERTIFICATE REQUEST-----",
  "hostnames": [
    "example.com",
    "*.example.com",
    "sub.example.com"
  ],
  "request_type": "origin-rsa",
  "requested_validity": 5475
}
```

<h3 id="create-certificate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» csr|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_csr](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_csr)|true|The Certificate Signing Request (CSR). Must be newline-encoded.|
|» hostnames|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_hostnames](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_hostnames)|true|Array of hostnames or wildcard names bound to the certificate.<br>Hostnames must be fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) belonging to zones on your account (e.g., `example.com` or `sub.example.com`). Wildcards are supported only as a `*.` prefix for a single level (e.g., `*.example.com`). Double wildcards (`*.*.example.com`) and interior wildcards (`foo.*.example.com`) are not allowed. The wildcard suffix must be a multi-label domain (`*.example.com` is valid, but `*.com` is not). Unicode/IDN hostnames are accepted and automatically converted to punycode.|
|» request_type|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_request_type](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_request_type)|true|Signature type desired on certificate ("origin-rsa" (rsa), "origin-ecc" (ecdsa), or "keyless-certificate" (for Keyless SSL servers).|
|» requested_validity|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_requested_validity](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_requested_validity)|false|The number of days for which the certificate should be valid.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» request_type|origin-rsa|
|» request_type|origin-ecc|
|» request_type|keyless-certificate|
|» requested_validity|7|
|» requested_validity|30|
|» requested_validity|90|
|» requested_validity|365|
|» requested_validity|730|
|» requested_validity|1095|
|» requested_validity|5475|

## Get Certificate

<a id="opIdorigin-ca-get-certificate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/certificates/328578533902268680212849205732770752308931942346 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /certificates/{certificate_id}`

Get an existing Origin CA certificate by its serial number. You can use an Origin CA Key as your User Service Key or an API token when calling this endpoint ([see above](#requests)).

<h3 id="get-certificate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|certificate_id|path|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_origin_ca_certificate_identifier](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_origin_ca_certificate_identifier)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
```

## Revoke Certificate

<a id="opIdorigin-ca-revoke-certificate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /certificates/{certificate_id}`

Revoke an existing Origin CA certificate by its serial number. You can use an Origin CA Key as your User Service Key or an API token when calling this endpoint ([see above](#requests)).

```json
}
```

## List category APIs

<a id="opIdcws-list-category-apis"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/cws/categories/apis \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /cws/categories/apis`

Returns distinct active API names across every application or beneath an exact application name.

<h3 id="list-category-apis-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|name|query|string|false|Case-insensitive substring search over API names.|
|variants|query|boolean|false|Include the routing identities represented by each API name. Defaults to false.|

## List organizations the user has access to

<a id="opIdOrganization_listOrganizations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/organizations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations`

Retrieve a list of organizations a particular user has access to.

<h3 id="list-organizations-the-user-has-access-to-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|query|[[organizations-api_OrganizationID](#schemaorganizations-api_organizationid)]|false|Only return organizations with the specified IDs (ex. id=foo&id=bar). Send multiple elements<br>by repeating the query value.|
|name|query|string|false|(case-sensitive) Filter the list of organizations to where the name is equal to a<br>particular string.|
|name.startsWith|query|string|false|(case-insensitive) Filter the list of organizations to where the name starts with a<br>particular string.|
|name.endsWith|query|string|false|(case-insensitive) Filter the list of organizations to where the name ends with a particular<br>string.|
|name.contains|query|string|false|(case-insensitive) Filter the list of organizations to where the name contains a particular<br>string.|
|containing.account|query|string|false|Filter the list of organizations to the ones that contain this particular<br>account.|
|containing.user|query|string|false|Filter the list of organizations to the ones that contain this particular<br>user.<br><br>IMPORTANT: Just because an organization "contains" a user is not a<br>representation of any authorization or privilege to manage any resources<br>therein. An organization "containing" a user simply means the user is managed by<br>that organization.|
|containing.organization|query|string|false|Filter the list of organizations to the ones that contain this particular<br>organization.|
|parent.id|query|[organizations-api_OrganizationID](#schemaorganizations-api_organizationid) \| string|false|Filter the list of organizations to the ones that are a sub-organization<br>of the specified organization.<br><br>"null" is a valid value to provide for this parameter. It means "where<br>an organization has no parent (i.e. it is a 'root' organization)."|
|page_token|query|string|false|An opaque token returned from the last list response that when<br>provided will retrieve the next page.<br><br>Parameters used to filter the retrieved list must remain in subsequent<br>requests with a page token.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|The amount of items to return. Defaults to 10.|

`POST /pages/assets/upload`

Upload one or more files to the Pages asset store. Each file is
identified by its content hash and is uploaded using the same JSON shape
as the Cloudflare KV bulk write API. Used as part of the Pages Direct
Upload workflow.

Authenticate with the JWT obtained from the upload-token endpoint:
GET /accounts/{account_id}/pages/projects/{project_name}/upload-token


> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "base64": true,
    "key": "b026324c6904b2a9cb4b88d6d61c81d1",
    "metadata": {
      "contentType": "text/plain"
    },
    "value": "SGVsbG8sIFdvcmxkIQ=="
  }
]
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[pages_pages_assets_upload_request](#schemapages_pages_assets_upload_request)|true|none|
|» base64|body|boolean|true|Whether value is base64 encoded.|
|» key|body|string|true|File content hash used as the object key in the Pages asset store.|
|» metadata|body|object|true|none|
|» » contentType|body|string|true|MIME type for the uploaded file.|
|» value|body|string|true|File content. When base64 is true, this value is base64 encoded.|

`GET /radar/agent_readiness/summary/{dimension}`

`GET /radar/ai/bots/summary/user_agent`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of traffic by AI user agent.

<h3 id="get-ai-user-agents-summary-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|limitPerGroup|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

|format|JSON|
|format|CSV|

## Get AI bots HTTP requests distribution by dimension

<a id="opIdradar-get-ai-bots-summary"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/ai/bots/summary/USER_AGENT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/ai/bots/summary/{dimension}`

Retrieves an aggregated summary of AI bots HTTP requests grouped by the specified dimension.

<h3 id="get-ai-bots-http-requests-distribution-by-dimension-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dimension|path|string|true|Specifies the attribute by which to group the results.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|crawlPurpose|query|[string]|false|Filters results by bot crawl purpose.|
|userAgent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by user agent.|
|vertical|query|[string]|false|Filters results by vertical.|
|industry|query|[string]|false|Filters results by industry.|
|contentType|query|[string]|false|Filters results by content type category. When set, results can only be further filtered by location, continent, or Autonomous System.|
|responseStatus|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP response status code (e.g. 200, 403, 404). Only [IANA-registered codes](https://www.iana.org/assignments/http-status-codes/http-status-codes.xhtml) are accepted.|
|responseStatusCategory|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP response status code category.|
|limitPerGroup|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|


`GET /radar/ai/bots/timeseries_groups/user_agent`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of traffic by AI user agent over time.

<h3 id="get-ai-user-agents-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|limitPerGroup|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

`GET /radar/ai/inference/summary/task`

<aside class="warning">

</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of the number of inferences by task.

<h3 id="get-workers-ai-tasks-summary-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|limitPerGroup|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get Workers AI tasks time series

<a id="opIdradar-get-ai-inference-timeseries-group-by-task"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/ai/inference/timeseries_groups/task \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/ai/inference/timeseries_groups/task`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of the number of inferences by task over time.

<h3 id="get-workers-ai-tasks-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|limitPerGroup|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

|aggInterval|15m|
|aggInterval|1h|
|aggInterval|1d|
|aggInterval|1w|
|format|JSON|
|format|CSV|

## Get AI markdown for agents reduction ratio summary

<a id="opIdradar-get-ai-markdown-for-agents-summary"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/ai/markdown_for_agents/summary \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/ai/markdown_for_agents/summary`

Retrieves the overall median HTML-to-markdown reduction ratio for AI agent requests over the given date range.

<h3 id="get-ai-markdown-for-agents-reduction-ratio-summary-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get latest Internet outages and anomalies

<a id="opIdradar-get-annotations-outages"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/annotations/outages \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/annotations/outages`

Retrieves the latest Internet outages and anomalies.

<h3 id="get-latest-internet-outages-and-anomalies-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects returned in the response.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Skips the specified number of objects before fetching the results.|
|dateRange|query|string|false|Filters results by a relative date range ending at the current time. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`), e.g. `7d`. Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `3dcontrol` covers days -10 to -7, `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `28dcontrol` covers days -56 to -28, and `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). Mutually exclusive with `dateStart`/`dateEnd`.|
|dateStart|query|string(date-time)|false|Start of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`.|
|dateEnd|query|string(date-time)|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`.|
|dataSource|query|string|false|Filters results by data source.|
|outageType|query|string|false|Filters results by outage type.|
|outageCause|query|string|false|Filters results by outage cause.|
|tags|query|[string]|false|Filters results by annotation tag. Matches annotations carrying at least one of the given tags.|
|query|query|string|false|Filters results by a free-text match on the annotation description, id, or linked entities (location, ASN, origin).|
|asn|query|integer|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify a single Autonomous System Number (ASN) as integer.|
|location|query|string|false|Filters results by location. Specify an alpha-2 location code.|
|geoId|query|string|false|Filters results by geolocation. Refer to [GeoNames](https://download.geonames.org/export/dump/readme.txt).|
|origin|query|string|false|Filters results by origin.|
|tld|query|string|false|Filters results by top-level domain.|
|ca|query|string|false|Filters results by certificate authority.|
|log|query|string|false|Filters results by certificate log.|
|bot|query|string|false|Filters results by bot.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|
