
`GET /radar/as112/summary/dnssec`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of DNS queries to AS112 by DNSSEC (DNS Security Extensions) support.

<h3 id="get-as112-dns-queries-by-dnssec-summary-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|

|protocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS transport protocol.|
|responseCode|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS response code.|

## Get AS112 DNS queries by response code summary

<a id="opIdradar-get-dns-as112-timeseries-by-response-codes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/as112/summary/response_codes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/as112/summary/response_codes`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of AS112 DNS requests classified by response code.

<h3 id="get-as112-dns-queries-by-response-code-summary-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|queryType|query|[string \| null]|false|Filters results by DNS query type.|
|protocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS transport protocol.|
|limitPerGroup|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get AS112 DNS queries time series

<a id="opIdradar-get-dns-as112-timeseries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/as112/timeseries \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/as112/timeseries`

Retrieves the AS112 DNS queries over time.

<h3 id="get-as112-dns-queries-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|queryType|query|[string \| null]|false|Filters results by DNS query type.|
|protocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS transport protocol.|
|responseCode|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS response code.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get AS112 DNS queries by EDNS support summary

<a id="opIdradar-get-dns-as112-timeseries-group-by-edns"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/as112/timeseries_groups/edns \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/as112/timeseries_groups/edns`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of AS112 DNS queries by EDNS (Extension Mechanisms for DNS) support over time.

<h3 id="get-as112-dns-queries-by-edns-support-summary-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|queryType|query|[string \| null]|false|Filters results by DNS query type.|
|protocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS transport protocol.|
|responseCode|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS response code.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

<aside class="warning">

Retrieves the distribution of AS112 DNS requests classified by protocol over time.

<h3 id="get-as112-dns-queries-by-dns-protocol-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. |continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|

## Get AS112 DNS queries by response code time series

<a id="opIdradar-get-dns-as112-timeseries-group-by-response-codes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/as112/timeseries_groups/response_codes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/as112/timeseries_groups/response_codes`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of AS112 DNS requests classified by response code over time.

<h3 id="get-as112-dns-queries-by-response-code-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|queryType|query|[string \| null]|false|Filters results by DNS query type.|
|protocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS transport protocol.|
|limitPerGroup|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get top locations by AS112 DNS queries

<a id="opIdradar-get-dns-as112-top-locations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/as112/top/locations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/as112/top/locations`

Retrieves the top locations by AS112 DNS queries.

<h3 id="get-top-locations-by-as112-dns-queries-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects returned in the response.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|format|JSON|
|format|CSV|

## Get top locations by AS112 DNS queries for an IP version

<a id="opIdradar-get-dns-as112-top-locations-by-ip-version"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/as112/top/locations/ip_version/IPv4 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/as112/top/locations/ip_version/{ip_version}`

Retrieves the top locations of DNS queries to AS112 for an IP version.

<h3 id="get-top-locations-by-as112-dns-queries-for-an-ip-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ip_version|path|string|true|IP version.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects returned in the response.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|ip_version|IPv4|
|ip_version|IPv6|
|format|JSON|
|format|CSV|

|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|

|protocol|query|[string]|false|Filters the results by layer 3/4 protocol.|
|direction|query|string|false|Specifies whether the `location` filter applies to the source or target location.|
|limitPerGroup|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

`GET /radar/attacks/layer3/summary/{dimension}`

Retrieves the distribution of layer 3 attacks by the specified dimension.

<h3 id="get-layer-3-attacks-summary-by-dimension-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dimension|path|string|true|Specifies the attribute by which to group the results.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|
|protocol|query|[string]|false|Filters the results by layer 3/4 protocol.|
|direction|query|string|false|Specifies whether the `location` filter applies to the source or target location.|
|limitPerGroup|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.|

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/attacks/layer3/timeseries_groups/duration`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of layer 3 attacks by duration over time.

<h3 id="get-layer-3-attacks-by-duration-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|
|protocol|query|[string]|false|Filters the results by layer 3/4 protocol.|
|normalization|query|string|false|Normalization method applied to the results. Refer to [Normalization methods](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/normalization/).|
|direction|query|string|false|Specifies whether the `location` filter applies to the source or target location.|

<a id="opIdradar-get-attacks-layer3-timeseries-group-by-vertical"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/attacks/layer3/timeseries_groups/vertical \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/attacks/layer3/timeseries_groups/vertical`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of layer 3 attacks by targeted vertical over time.

<h3 id="get-layer-3-attacks-by-vertical-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|
|protocol|query|[string]|false|Filters the results by layer 3/4 protocol.|
|normalization|query|string|false|Normalization method applied to the results. Refer to [Normalization methods](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/normalization/).|
|direction|query|string|false|Specifies whether the `location` filter applies to the source or target location.|
|limitPerGroup|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get top layer 3 attack pairs (origin and target locations)

<a id="opIdradar-get-attacks-layer3-top-attacks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/attacks/layer3/top/attacks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/attacks/layer3/top/attacks`

Retrieves the top layer 3 attacks from origin to target location. Values are a percentage out of the total layer 3 attacks (with billing country). You can optionally limit the number of attacks by origin/target location (useful if all the top attacks are from or to the same location).

<h3 id="get-top-layer-3-attack-pairs-origin-and-target-locations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects returned in the response.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|
|protocol|query|[string]|false|Filters the results by layer 3/4 protocol.|
|limitDirection|query|string|false|Specifies whether the `limitPerLocation` applies to the source or target location.|
|limitPerLocation|query|integer|false|Limits the number of attacks per origin/target (refer to `limitDirection` parameter) location.|
|magnitude|query|string|false|Orders results based on attack magnitude, defined by total mitigated bytes or total mitigated attacks.|
|normalization|query|string|false|Normalization method applied to the results. Refer to [Normalization methods](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/normalization/).|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|ipVersion|IPv4|
|ipVersion|IPv6|
|protocol|UDP|
|protocol|TCP|
|protocol|ICMP|
|protocol|GRE|
|limitDirection|ORIGIN|
|limitDirection|TARGET|
|magnitude|MITIGATED_BYTES|
|magnitude|MITIGATED_ATTACKS|
|normalization|PERCENTAGE|
|normalization|MIN_MAX|
|format|JSON|
|format|CSV|

## Get top target locations of layer 3 attacks

<a id="opIdradar-get-attacks-layer3-top-target-locations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/attacks/layer3/top/locations/target \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/attacks/layer3/top/locations/target`

Retrieves the target locations of layer 3 attacks.

<h3 id="get-top-target-locations-of-layer-3-attacks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects returned in the response.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|
|protocol|query|[string]|false|Filters the results by layer 3/4 protocol.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

<h3 id="get-layer-7-attacks-by-http-version-summary-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|

|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|
|httpMethod|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP method.|

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/attacks/layer7/timeseries \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
```

```bash
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/attacks/layer7/timeseries`

Retrieves layer 7 attacks over time.

<h3 id="get-layer-7-attacks-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|normalization|query|string|false|Normalization method applied to the results. Refer to [Normalization methods](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/normalization/). `PERCENTAGE_CHANGE` requires exactly one comparison series (e.g. a `control` date range).|
|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|
|httpVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP version.|
|httpMethod|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP method.|
|mitigationProduct|query|[string]|false|Filters the results by layer 7 mitigation product.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of layer 7 attacks by HTTP version over time.

<h3 id="get-layer-7-attacks-by-http-version-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. |location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of layer 7 attacks by IP version used over time.

<h3 id="get-layer-7-attacks-by-ip-version-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|httpVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP version.|
|httpMethod|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP method.|
|mitigationProduct|query|[string]|false|Filters the results by layer 7 mitigation product.|
|normalization|query|string|false|Normalization method applied to the results. Refer to [Normalization methods](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/normalization/).|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/attacks/layer7/timeseries_groups/HTTP_METHOD \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/attacks/layer7/timeseries_groups/{dimension}`

Retrieves the distribution of layer 7 attacks grouped by dimension over time.

<h3 id="get-layer-7-attacks-time-series-grouped-by-dimension-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dimension|path|string|true|Specifies the attribute by which to group the results.|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|
|httpVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP version.|
|httpMethod|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP method.|
|mitigationProduct|query|[string]|false|Filters the results by layer 7 mitigation product.|
|normalization|query|string|false|Normalization method applied to the results. Refer to [Normalization methods](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/normalization/).|
|limitPerGroup|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get top layer 7 attack pairs (origin and target locations)

<a id="opIdradar-get-attacks-layer7-top-attacks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/attacks/layer7/top/attacks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/attacks/layer7/top/attacks`

Retrieves the top attacks from origin to target location. Values are percentages of the total layer 7 attacks (with billing country). The attack magnitude can be defined by the number of mitigated requests or by the number of zones affected. You can optionally limit the number of attacks by origin/target location (useful if all the top attacks are from or to the same location).

Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. ## Get top target locations of layer 7 attacks

<a id="opIdradar-get-attacks-layer7-top-target-location"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/attacks/layer7/top/locations/target \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/attacks/layer7/top/locations/target`

Retrieves the top target locations of and by layer 7 attacks. Values are a percentage out of the total layer 7 attacks. The target location is determined by the attacked zone's billing country, when available.

<h3 id="get-top-target-locations-of-layer-7-attacks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects returned in the response.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|mitigationProduct|query|[string]|false|Filters the results by layer 7 mitigation product.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

|mitigationProduct|WAF|
|mitigationProduct|BOT_MANAGEMENT|
|mitigationProduct|ACCESS_RULES|
|mitigationProduct|IP_REPUTATION|
|mitigationProduct|API_SHIELD|
|mitigationProduct|DATA_LOSS_PREVENTION|
|format|JSON|
|format|CSV|

`GET /radar/bgp/hijacks/events`

Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `3dcontrol` covers days -10 to -7, `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `28dcontrol` covers days -56 to -28, and `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). Mutually exclusive with `dateStart`/`dateEnd`.|
|dateStart|query|string(date-time)|false|Start of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`.|

## Get announced IP address space time series

<a id="opIdradar-get-bgp-ips-timeseries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/bgp/ips/timeseries \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/bgp/ips/timeseries`

Retrieves time series data for the announced IP space count, represented as the number of IPv4 /24s and IPv6 /48s, for a given ASN.

<h3 id="get-announced-ip-address-space-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 location codes.|
|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|
|includeDelay|query|boolean|false|Includes data delay meta information.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|ipVersion|IPv4|
|ipVersion|IPv6|
|format|JSON|
|format|CSV|

`GET /radar/bgp/ips/top/ases`

Returns the top-N autonomous systems by announced IP space at the nearest 8-hour RIB boundary at or before the requested date. The snapped boundary is returned as `anchor_ts`.

<h3 id="get-top-ases-by-announced-ip-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|date|query|string(date-time)|false|Filters results by the specified datetime (ISO 8601).|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects returned in the response.|
|metric|query|string|false|Ranking metric: IPv4 /24 count or IPv6 /48 count.|
|country|query|string|false|Optional ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country filter. Omit for global top-N.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

#### Enumerated Values

|metric|v6_48s|
|format|JSON|

## Get tier-1 path segments for an AS

<a id="opIdradar-get-bgp-routes-paths"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/bgp/routes/paths/174 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/bgp/routes/paths/{asn}`

Retrieves the paths an AS uses to reach the tier-1 clique, derived from RouteViews RIB snapshots. Each entry is an ordered AS-path segment (from the queried AS toward a tier-1) with the number of observed paths and peers, and the collectors that observed it. By default segments are merged across all active collectors; pass "collector" to scope to one. The response also includes an "asnInfo" map (keyed by ASN) with the name and country for every ASN in the returned segments plus the queried ASN (best-effort; null when unavailable).

<h3 id="get-tier-1-path-segments-for-an-as-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|asn|path|integer|true|Single Autonomous System Number (ASN) as integer.|
|ipVersion|query|string|false|Address family of the observed paths. Defaults to IPv4.|
|collector|query|string|false|Scope to a single RouteViews collector (e.g. "route-views3"). Omit to merge across all active collectors (identical path segments are deduplicated, observation counts summed, and every contributing collector listed).|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|ipVersion|IPv4|
|ipVersion|IPv6|
|format|JSON|
|format|CSV|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": {
    "asnInfo": {
      "13335": {
        "asn": 13335,
        "country": "US",
        "name": "Cloudflare"
      }
    },
    "collectors": [
      "string"
    ],
    "meta": {
      "dataTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "effectiveCollector": "string",
      "queryTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "stale": true
    },
    "paths": [
      {
        "collectors": [
          "string"
        ],
        "pathsCount": 0,
        "peersCount": 0,
        "segment": [
          0
        ]
      }
    ]
  },
  "success": true
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "result": {},
  "success": false
}
```

## Get upstream composition time series for an AS

<a id="opIdradar-get-bgp-routes-upstreams-timeseries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/bgp/routes/upstreams/174/timeseries \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/bgp/routes/upstreams/{asn}/timeseries`

Retrieves the share of an AS’s observed paths carried by each direct upstream over time, derived from RouteViews RIB snapshots across all collectors (the combined product). Each upstream ASN is returned as its own series of shares (0–1); the least-significant upstreams beyond the requested limit are grouped into an "OTHER" series. Series share a common set of timestamps.

<h3 id="get-upstream-composition-time-series-for-an-as-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|asn|path|integer|true|Single Autonomous System Number (ASN) as integer.|
|ipVersion|query|string|false|Address family of the observed paths. Defaults to IPv4.|
|dateStart|query|string(date-time)|false|Start of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`.|
|dateEnd|query|string(date-time)|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`.|

`GET /radar/bgp/rpki/roas/timeseries`

Retrieves RPKI ROA (Route Origin Authorization) validation ratios over time. Returns the selected metric as a time series. Supports filtering by ASN or location (country code) — multiple values of the same filter type produce one series per value. If no ASN or location is specified, returns the global aggregate.

|metric|query|string|false|Which RPKI ROA validation metric to return. validPfxsRatio = ratio of RPKI-valid prefixes (IPv4+IPv6 combined). validPfxsV4Ratio / validPfxsV6Ratio = same, split by IP version. validIpsRatio = ratio of RPKI-valid address space (IPv4 /24s + IPv6 /48s). validIpsV4Ratio / validIpsV6Ratio = same, split by IP version.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System Number. Specify one or more ASNs. Multiple values generate one series per ASN.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 location codes.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|
