## Get BGP time series

<a id="opIdradar-get-bgp-timeseries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/bgp/timeseries \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/bgp/timeseries`

Retrieves BGP updates over time. When requesting updates for an autonomous system, only BGP updates of type announcement are returned.

<h3 id="get-bgp-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|prefix|query|[string]|false|Filters results by BGP network prefix.|
|updateType|query|[string]|false|Filters results by BGP update type.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|aggInterval|15m|
|aggInterval|1h|
|aggInterval|1d|
|aggInterval|1w|
|updateType|ANNOUNCEMENT|
|updateType|WITHDRAWAL|
|format|JSON|
|format|CSV|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": {
    "meta": {
      "aggInterval": "15m",
      "confidenceInfo": {
        "annotations": [
          {
            "dataSource": "ALL",
            "description": "Cable cut in Tonga",
            "endDate": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
            "eventType": "GENERAL",
            "isInstantaneous": true,
            "linkedUrl": "http://example.com",
            "startDate": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
            "tags": [
              "BOT_CLASS"
            ]
          }
        ],
        "level": 0
      },
      "dateRange": [
        {
          "endTime": "2022-09-17T10:22:57.555Z",
          "startTime": "2022-09-16T10:22:57.555Z"
        }
      ],
      "lastUpdated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    },
    "serie_0": {
      "timestamps": [
        "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
      ],
      "values": [
        "10"
      ]
    }
  },
  "success": true
}
```

```json
    {
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
```

## Get top ASes by BGP updates

<a id="opIdradar-get-bgp-top-ases"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/bgp/top/ases \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/bgp/top/ases`

Retrieves the top autonomous systems by BGP updates (announcements only).

<h3 id="get-top-ases-by-bgp-updates-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects returned in the response.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|prefix|query|[string]|false|Filters results by BGP network prefix.|
|updateType|query|[string]|false|Filters results by BGP update type.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|updateType|ANNOUNCEMENT|
|updateType|WITHDRAWAL|
|format|JSON|
|format|CSV|

## Get bots HTTP requests time series

<a id="opIdradar-get-bots-timeseries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/bots/timeseries \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/bots/timeseries`

Retrieves bots HTTP request volume over time.

<h3 id="get-bots-http-requests-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|bot|query|[string]|false|Filters results by bot name.|
|botOperator|query|[string]|false|Filters results by bot operator.|
|botCategory|query|[string]|false|Filters results by bot category.|
|botKind|query|[string]|false|**Deprecated.** Filters results by bot kind. Deprecated: the Verified Bot / Signed Agent distinction is being removed.|
|botVerificationStatus|query|[string]|false|Filters results by bot verification status (Verified vs. Unverified).|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get time series distribution of bots HTTP requests by dimension.

<a id="opIdradar-get-bots-timeseries-group"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/bots/timeseries_groups/BOT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/bots/timeseries_groups/{dimension}`

Retrieves the distribution of HTTP requests from bots, grouped by the specified dimension over time.

<h3 id="get-time-series-distribution-of-bots-http-requests-by-dimension-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|limitPerGroup|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.|
|bot|query|[string]|false|Filters results by bot name.|
|botOperator|query|[string]|false|Filters results by bot operator.|

## Get crawler HTTP request distribution by dimension

<a id="opIdradar-get-crawlers-summary"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/bots/crawlers/summary/CLIENT_TYPE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/bots/crawlers/summary/{dimension}`

Retrieves an aggregated summary of HTTP requests from crawlers, grouped by the specified dimension.

<h3 id="get-crawler-http-request-distribution-by-dimension-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dimension|path|string|true|Specifies the attribute by which to group the results.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|limitPerGroup|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.|
|botOperator|query|[string]|false|Filters results by bot operator.|
|vertical|query|[string]|false|Filters results by vertical.|
|industry|query|[string]|false|Filters results by industry.|
|clientType|query|[string]|false|Filters results by agent type.|
|responseStatus|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP response status code (e.g. 200, 403, 404). Only [IANA-registered codes](https://www.iana.org/assignments/http-status-codes/http-status-codes.xhtml) are accepted.|
|responseStatusCategory|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP response status code category.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get certificate distribution by dimension

<a id="opIdradar-get-ct-summary"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/ct/summary/CA \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/ct/summary/{dimension}`

Retrieves an aggregated summary of certificates grouped by the specified dimension.

<h3 id="get-certificate-distribution-by-dimension-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dimension|path|string|true|Specifies the certificate attribute by which to group the results.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|limitPerGroup|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.|
|ca|query|[string]|false|Filters results by certificate authority.|
|caOwner|query|[string]|false|Filters results by certificate authority owner.|
|duration|query|[string]|false|Filters results by certificate duration.|
|entryType|query|[string]|false|Filters results by entry type (certificate vs. pre-certificate). Incompatible with the `tld` filter/dimension.|
|expirationStatus|query|[string]|false|Filters results by expiration status (expired vs. valid).|
|hasIps|query|[boolean]|false|Filters results based on whether the certificates are bound to specific IP addresses.|
|hasWildcards|query|[boolean]|false|Filters results based on whether the certificates contain wildcard domains.|
|log|query|[string]|false|Filters results by certificate log. Incompatible with the `tld` filter/dimension.|
|logApi|query|[string]|false|Filters results by certificate log API (RFC6962 vs. static). Incompatible with the `tld` filter/dimension.|
|logOperator|query|[string]|false|Filters results by certificate log operator. Incompatible with the `tld` filter/dimension.|
|publicKeyAlgorithm|query|[string]|false|Filters results by public key algorithm.|
|signatureAlgorithm|query|[string]|false|Filters results by signature algorithm.|
|tld|query|[string]|false|Filters results by top-level domain. Incompatible with the `log`, `logApi`, `logOperator`, and `entryType` filters/dimensions.|
|validationLevel|query|[string]|false|Filters results by validation level.|
|uniqueEntries|query|[string]|false|Specifies whether to filter out duplicate certificates and pre-certificates. Set to true for unique entries only.|
|normalization|query|string|false|Normalization method applied to the results. Refer to [Normalization methods](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/normalization/).|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get certificates time series

<a id="opIdradar-get-ct-timeseries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/ct/timeseries \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/ct/timeseries`

Retrieves certificate volume over time.

<h3 id="get-certificates-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|ca|query|[string]|false|Filters results by certificate authority.|
|caOwner|query|[string]|false|Filters results by certificate authority owner.|
|duration|query|[string]|false|Filters results by certificate duration.|
|entryType|query|[string]|false|Filters results by entry type (certificate vs. pre-certificate). Incompatible with the `tld` filter/dimension.|
|expirationStatus|query|[string]|false|Filters results by expiration status (expired vs. valid).|
|hasIps|query|[boolean]|false|Filters results based on whether the certificates are bound to specific IP addresses.|
|hasWildcards|query|[boolean]|false|Filters results based on whether the certificates contain wildcard domains.|
|log|query|[string]|false|Filters results by certificate log. Incompatible with the `tld` filter/dimension.|
|logApi|query|[string]|false|Filters results by certificate log API (RFC6962 vs. static). Incompatible with the `tld` filter/dimension.|
|logOperator|query|[string]|false|Filters results by certificate log operator. Incompatible with the `tld` filter/dimension.|
|publicKeyAlgorithm|query|[string]|false|Filters results by public key algorithm.|
|signatureAlgorithm|query|[string]|false|Filters results by signature algorithm.|
|tld|query|[string]|false|Filters results by top-level domain. Incompatible with the `log`, `logApi`, `logOperator`, and `entryType` filters/dimensions.|
|validationLevel|query|[string]|false|Filters results by validation level.|
|uniqueEntries|query|[string]|false|Specifies whether to filter out duplicate certificates and pre-certificates. Set to true for unique entries only.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## List datasets

<a id="opIdradar-get-reports-datasets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/datasets`

Retrieves a list of datasets.

|date|query|string(date)|false|Filters results by the specified date.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-radar-dns">Radar DNS</h1>

## Get DNS queries by cache status summary

<a id="opIdradar-get-dns-summary-by-cache-hit-status"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/dns/summary/cache_hit \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/dns/summary/cache_hit`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of DNS queries by cache status.

<h3 id="get-dns-queries-by-cache-status-summary-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|tld|query|[string]|false|Filters results by top-level domain. Incompatible with the `ipVersion`, `protocol`, `dnssecE2e`, `dnssecAware`, `responseTtl`, and `cacheHit` filters/dimensions; this restriction does not apply to country-code TLDs (2-letter, e.g. `uk`).|
|queryType|query|[string \| null]|false|Filters results by DNS query type.|
|protocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS transport protocol.|
|responseCode|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS response code.|
|nodata|query|[boolean]|false|Specifies whether the response includes empty DNS responses (NODATA).|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get DNS queries by DNSSEC support summary

<a id="opIdradar-get-dns-summary-by-dnssec"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/dns/summary/dnssec \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/dns/summary/dnssec`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of DNS responses by DNSSEC (DNS Security Extensions) support.

<h3 id="get-dns-queries-by-dnssec-support-summary-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|tld|query|[string]|false|Filters results by top-level domain. Incompatible with the `ipVersion`, `protocol`, `dnssecE2e`, `dnssecAware`, `responseTtl`, and `cacheHit` filters/dimensions; this restriction does not apply to country-code TLDs (2-letter, e.g. `uk`).|
|queryType|query|[string \| null]|false|Filters results by DNS query type.|
|protocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS transport protocol.|
|responseCode|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS response code.|
|nodata|query|[boolean]|false|Specifies whether the response includes empty DNS responses (NODATA).|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get DNS queries by DNSSEC end-to-end summary

<a id="opIdradar-get-dns-summary-by-dnssec-e2e-version"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/dns/summary/dnssec_e2e \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/dns/summary/dnssec_e2e`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of DNSSEC-validated answers by end-to-end security status.

<h3 id="get-dns-queries-by-dnssec-end-to-end-summary-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|tld|query|[string]|false|Filters results by top-level domain. Incompatible with the `ipVersion`, `protocol`, `dnssecE2e`, `dnssecAware`, `responseTtl`, and `cacheHit` filters/dimensions; this restriction does not apply to country-code TLDs (2-letter, e.g. `uk`).|
|queryType|query|[string \| null]|false|Filters results by DNS query type.|
|protocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS transport protocol.|
|responseCode|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS response code.|
|nodata|query|[boolean]|false|Specifies whether the response includes empty DNS responses (NODATA).|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get DNS queries by matching answer summary

<a id="opIdradar-get-dns-summary-by-matching-answer-status"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/dns/summary/matching_answer \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/dns/summary/matching_answer`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of DNS queries by matching answers.

<h3 id="get-dns-queries-by-matching-answer-summary-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|tld|query|[string]|false|Filters results by top-level domain. Incompatible with the `ipVersion`, `protocol`, `dnssecE2e`, `dnssecAware`, `responseTtl`, and `cacheHit` filters/dimensions; this restriction does not apply to country-code TLDs (2-letter, e.g. `uk`).|
|queryType|query|[string \| null]|false|Filters results by DNS query type.|
|protocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS transport protocol.|
|responseCode|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS response code.|
|nodata|query|[boolean]|false|Specifies whether the response includes empty DNS responses (NODATA).|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

<h3 id="get-dns-queries-by-type-summary-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|

|protocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS transport protocol.|

|nodata|query|[boolean]|false|Specifies whether the response includes empty DNS responses (NODATA).|

## Get DNS summary by dimension

<a id="opIdradar-get-dns-summary"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/dns/summary/AS \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/dns/summary/{dimension}`

Retrieves the distribution of DNS queries by the specified dimension.

<h3 id="get-dns-summary-by-dimension-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dimension|path|string|true|Specifies the attribute by which to group the results. Grouping by `TLD_DNS_MAGNITUDE` does not support sub-daily aggregation intervals; `15m` and `1h` are raised to `1d`.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|cacheHit|query|[boolean]|false|Filters results based on cache status.|
|nodata|query|[boolean]|false|Specifies whether the response includes empty DNS responses (NODATA).|
|protocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS transport protocol.|
|queryType|query|[string \| null]|false|Filters results by DNS query type.|
|responseCode|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS response code.|
|responseTtl|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS response TTL.|
|dnssec|query|[string]|false|Filters results based on DNSSEC (DNS Security Extensions) support.|
|dnssecAware|query|[string]|false|Filters results based on DNSSEC (DNS Security Extensions) client awareness.|
|dnssecE2e|query|[boolean]|false|Filters results based on DNSSEC-validated answers by end-to-end security status.|
|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|
|limitPerGroup|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.|
|matchingAnswer|query|[boolean]|false|Filters results based on whether the queries have a matching answer.|
|tld|query|[string]|false|Filters results by top-level domain. Incompatible with the `ipVersion`, `protocol`, `dnssecE2e`, `dnssecAware`, `responseTtl`, and `cacheHit` filters/dimensions; this restriction does not apply to country-code TLDs (2-letter, e.g. `uk`).|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get DNS queries time series

<a id="opIdradar-get-dns-timeseries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/dns/timeseries \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/dns/timeseries`

Retrieves normalized query volume to the 1.1.1.1 DNS resolver over time.

<h3 id="get-dns-queries-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|cacheHit|query|[boolean]|false|Filters results based on cache status.|
|nodata|query|[boolean]|false|Specifies whether the response includes empty DNS responses (NODATA).|
|protocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS transport protocol.|
|queryType|query|[string \| null]|false|Filters results by DNS query type.|
|responseCode|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS response code.|
|responseTtl|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS response TTL.|
|dnssec|query|[string]|false|Filters results based on DNSSEC (DNS Security Extensions) support.|
|dnssecAware|query|[string]|false|Filters results based on DNSSEC (DNS Security Extensions) client awareness.|
|dnssecE2e|query|[boolean]|false|Filters results based on DNSSEC-validated answers by end-to-end security status.|
|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|
|matchingAnswer|query|[boolean]|false|Filters results based on whether the queries have a matching answer.|
|tld|query|[string]|false|Filters results by top-level domain. Incompatible with the `ipVersion`, `protocol`, `dnssecE2e`, `dnssecAware`, `responseTtl`, and `cacheHit` filters/dimensions; this restriction does not apply to country-code TLDs (2-letter, e.g. `uk`).|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of DNS responses by DNSSEC (DNS Security Extensions) support over time.

<h3 id="get-dns-queries-by-dnssec-support-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. |location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|tld|query|[string]|false|Filters results by top-level domain. Incompatible with the `ipVersion`, `protocol`, `dnssecE2e`, `dnssecAware`, `responseTtl`, and `cacheHit` filters/dimensions; this restriction does not apply to country-code TLDs (2-letter, e.g. `uk`).|

## Get DNS queries by DNSSEC end-to-end time series

<a id="opIdradar-get-dns-timeseries-group-by-dnssec-e2e-version"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/dns/timeseries_groups/dnssec_e2e \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/dns/timeseries_groups/dnssec_e2e`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of DNSSEC-validated answers by end-to-end security status over time.

<h3 id="get-dns-queries-by-dnssec-end-to-end-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|tld|query|[string]|false|Filters results by top-level domain. Incompatible with the `ipVersion`, `protocol`, `dnssecE2e`, `dnssecAware`, `responseTtl`, and `cacheHit` filters/dimensions; this restriction does not apply to country-code TLDs (2-letter, e.g. `uk`).|
|queryType|query|[string \| null]|false|Filters results by DNS query type.|
|protocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS transport protocol.|
|responseCode|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS response code.|
|nodata|query|[boolean]|false|Specifies whether the response includes empty DNS responses (NODATA).|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get DNS queries by matching answer time series

<a id="opIdradar-get-dns-timeseries-group-by-matching-answer-status"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/dns/timeseries_groups/matching_answer \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/dns/timeseries_groups/matching_answer`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of DNS queries by matching answers over time.

<h3 id="get-dns-queries-by-matching-answer-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|tld|query|[string]|false|Filters results by top-level domain. Incompatible with the `ipVersion`, `protocol`, `dnssecE2e`, `dnssecAware`, `responseTtl`, and `cacheHit` filters/dimensions; this restriction does not apply to country-code TLDs (2-letter, e.g. `uk`).|
|queryType|query|[string \| null]|false|Filters results by DNS query type.|
|protocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS transport protocol.|
|responseCode|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS response code.|
|nodata|query|[boolean]|false|Specifies whether the response includes empty DNS responses (NODATA).|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get DNS queries by type time series

<a id="opIdradar-get-dns-timeseries-group-by-query-type"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/dns/timeseries_groups/query_type \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/dns/timeseries_groups/query_type`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of DNS queries by type over time.

<h3 id="get-dns-queries-by-type-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|tld|query|[string]|false|Filters results by top-level domain. Incompatible with the `ipVersion`, `protocol`, `dnssecE2e`, `dnssecAware`, `responseTtl`, and `cacheHit` filters/dimensions; this restriction does not apply to country-code TLDs (2-letter, e.g. `uk`).|
|protocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS transport protocol.|
|responseCode|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS response code.|
|nodata|query|[boolean]|false|Specifies whether the response includes empty DNS responses (NODATA).|
|limitPerGroup|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get DNS queries by response TTL time series

<a id="opIdradar-get-dns-timeseries-group-by-response-ttl"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/dns/timeseries_groups/response_ttl \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/dns/timeseries_groups/response_ttl`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of DNS queries by minimum answer TTL over time.

<h3 id="get-dns-queries-by-response-ttl-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|tld|query|[string]|false|Filters results by top-level domain. Incompatible with the `ipVersion`, `protocol`, `dnssecE2e`, `dnssecAware`, `responseTtl`, and `cacheHit` filters/dimensions; this restriction does not apply to country-code TLDs (2-letter, e.g. `uk`).|
|queryType|query|[string \| null]|false|Filters results by DNS query type.|
|protocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS transport protocol.|
|responseCode|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS response code.|
|nodata|query|[boolean]|false|Specifies whether the response includes empty DNS responses (NODATA).|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|
