## Get DNS time series grouped by dimension

<a id="opIdradar-get-dns-timeseries-group"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/dns/timeseries_groups/AS \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/dns/timeseries_groups/{dimension}`

Retrieves the distribution of DNS queries grouped by dimension over time.

<h3 id="get-dns-time-series-grouped-by-dimension-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dimension|path|string|true|Specifies the attribute by which to group the results. Grouping by `TLD_DNS_MAGNITUDE` does not support sub-daily aggregation intervals; `15m` and `1h` are raised to `1d`.|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|cacheHit|query|[boolean]|false|Filters results based on cache status.|
|nodata|query|[boolean]|false|Specifies whether the response includes empty DNS responses (NODATA).|
|protocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS transport protocol.|
|queryType|query|[string \| null]|false|Filters results by DNS query type.|
|responseCode|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS response code.|
|responseTtl|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS response TTL.|
|dnssec|query|[string]|false|Filters results based on DNSSEC (DNS Security Extensions) support.|
|dnssecAware|query|[string]|false|Filters results based on DNSSEC (DNS Security Extensions) client awareness.|
|dnssecE2e|query|[boolean]|false|Filters results based on DNSSEC-validated answers by end-to-end security status.|
|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|
|limitPerGroup|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.|
|matchingAnswer|query|[boolean]|false|Filters results based on whether the queries have a matching answer.|
|tld|query|[string]|false|Filters results by top-level domain. Incompatible with the `ipVersion`, `protocol`, `dnssecE2e`, `dnssecAware`, `responseTtl`, and `cacheHit` filters/dimensions; this restriction does not apply to country-code TLDs (2-letter, e.g. `uk`).|
|normalization|query|string|false|Normalization method applied to the results. Refer to [Normalization methods](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/normalization/). `RANK` is only meaningful with the `TLD_DNS_MAGNITUDE` dimension, where it ranks TLDs by DNS query magnitude at each timestamp; for other dimensions it has no effect.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get top ASes by DNS queries

<a id="opIdradar-get-dns-top-ases"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/dns/top/ases \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/dns/top/ases`

Retrieves the top autonomous systems by DNS queries made to 1.1.1.1 DNS resolver.

<h3 id="get-top-ases-by-dns-queries-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects returned in the response.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|domain|query|[string]|false|Filters results by domain name. When set, no other DNS filter may be used — only date filtering (`dateRange`, or `dateStart`/`dateEnd`) is allowed — and the date range cannot exceed 31 days.|
|cacheHit|query|[boolean]|false|Filters results based on cache status.|
|nodata|query|[boolean]|false|Specifies whether the response includes empty DNS responses (NODATA).|
|protocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS transport protocol.|
|queryType|query|[string \| null]|false|Filters results by DNS query type.|
|responseCode|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS response code.|
|responseTtl|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS response TTL.|
|dnssec|query|[string]|false|Filters results based on DNSSEC (DNS Security Extensions) support.|
|dnssecAware|query|[string]|false|Filters results based on DNSSEC (DNS Security Extensions) client awareness.|
|dnssecE2e|query|[boolean]|false|Filters results based on DNSSEC-validated answers by end-to-end security status.|
|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|
|matchingAnswer|query|[boolean]|false|Filters results based on whether the queries have a matching answer.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

<a id="opIdradar-get-dns-top-locations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/dns/top/locations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \

```

`GET /radar/dns/top/locations`

Retrieves the top locations by DNS queries made to 1.1.1.1 DNS resolver.

<h3 id="get-top-locations-by-dns-queries-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects returned in the response.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|domain|query|[string]|false|Filters results by domain name. When set, no other DNS filter may be used — only date filtering (`dateRange`, or `dateStart`/`dateEnd`) is allowed — and the date range cannot exceed 31 days.|
|cacheHit|query|[boolean]|false|Filters results based on cache status.|
|nodata|query|[boolean]|false|Specifies whether the response includes empty DNS responses (NODATA).|
|protocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS transport protocol.|
|queryType|query|[string \| null]|false|Filters results by DNS query type.|
|responseCode|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS response code.|
|responseTtl|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DNS response TTL.|
|dnssec|query|[string]|false|Filters results based on DNSSEC (DNS Security Extensions) support.|
|dnssecAware|query|[string]|false|Filters results based on DNSSEC (DNS Security Extensions) client awareness.|
|dnssecE2e|query|[boolean]|false|Filters results based on DNSSEC-validated answers by end-to-end security status.|
|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|
|matchingAnswer|query|[boolean]|false|Filters results based on whether the queries have a matching answer.|
|tld|query|[string]|false|Filters results by top-level domain. Incompatible with the `ipVersion`, `protocol`, `dnssecE2e`, `dnssecAware`, `responseTtl`, and `cacheHit` filters/dimensions; this restriction does not apply to country-code TLDs (2-letter, e.g. `uk`).|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|


`GET /radar/email/routing/summary/dmarc`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of emails by DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance) validation.

<h3 id="get-email-dmarc-validation-summary-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|arc|query|[string]|false|Filters results by ARC (Authenticated Received Chain) validation.|
|dkim|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) validation status.|
|spf|query|[string]|false|Filters results by SPF (Sender Policy Framework) validation status.|
|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|

Retrieves the distribution of emails by ARC (Authenticated Received Chain) validation over time.

<h3 id="get-email-arc-validation-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dkim|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) validation status.|
|dmarc|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance) validation status.|
|spf|query|[string]|false|Filters results by SPF (Sender Policy Framework) validation status.|
|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|
|encrypted|query|[string]|false|Filters results by encryption status (encrypted vs. not-encrypted).|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get email encryption status time series

<a id="opIdradar-get-email-routing-timeseries-group-by-encrypted"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/email/routing/timeseries_groups/encrypted \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/email/routing/timeseries_groups/encrypted`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of emails by encryption status (encrypted vs. not-encrypted) over time.

<h3 id="get-email-encryption-status-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|arc|query|[string]|false|Filters results by ARC (Authenticated Received Chain) validation.|
|dkim|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) validation status.|
|dmarc|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance) validation status.|
|spf|query|[string]|false|Filters results by SPF (Sender Policy Framework) validation status.|
|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get email routing time series grouped by dimension

<a id="opIdradar-get-email-routing-timeseries-group"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/email/routing/timeseries_groups/IP_VERSION \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/email/routing/timeseries_groups/{dimension}`

Retrieves the distribution of email routing metrics grouped by dimension over time.

<h3 id="get-email-routing-time-series-grouped-by-dimension-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dimension|path|string|true|Specifies the attribute by which to group the results.|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|arc|query|[string]|false|Filters results by ARC (Authenticated Received Chain) validation.|
|dkim|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) validation status.|
|dmarc|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance) validation status.|
|spf|query|[string]|false|Filters results by SPF (Sender Policy Framework) validation status.|
|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|
|encrypted|query|[string]|false|Filters results by encryption status (encrypted vs. not-encrypted).|
|limitPerGroup|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|

Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|arc|query|[string]|false|Filters results by ARC (Authenticated Received Chain) validation.|

<aside class="warning">

<h3 id="get-email-spam-classification-summary-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|arc|query|[string]|false|Filters results by ARC (Authenticated Received Chain) validation.|
|dkim|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) validation status.|

Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. ## Get email ARC validation time series

<a id="opIdradar-get-email-security-timeseries-group-by-arc"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/email/security/timeseries_groups/arc \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/email/security/timeseries_groups/arc`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of emails by ARC (Authenticated Received Chain) validation over time.

<h3 id="get-email-arc-validation-time-series-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dkim|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) validation status.|
|dmarc|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance) validation status.|
|spf|query|[string]|false|Filters results by SPF (Sender Policy Framework) validation status.|
|tlsVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by TLS version.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

<h3 id="get-email-dmarc-validation-time-series-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. ## Get email SPF validation time series

<a id="opIdradar-get-email-security-timeseries-group-by-spf"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/email/security/timeseries_groups/spf \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/email/security/timeseries_groups/spf`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of emails by SPF (Sender Policy Framework) validation over time.

<h3 id="get-email-spf-validation-time-series-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|arc|query|[string]|false|Filters results by ARC (Authenticated Received Chain) validation.|
|dkim|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) validation status.|
|dmarc|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance) validation status.|
|tlsVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by TLS version.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get top TLDs by email message volume

<a id="opIdradar-get-email-security-top-tlds-by-messages"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/email/security/top/tlds \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/email/security/top/tlds`

Retrieves the top TLDs by number of email messages.

<h3 id="get-top-tlds-by-email-message-volume-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects returned in the response.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|arc|query|[string]|false|Filters results by ARC (Authenticated Received Chain) validation.|
|dkim|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) validation status.|
|dmarc|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance) validation status.|
|spf|query|[string]|false|Filters results by SPF (Sender Policy Framework) validation status.|
|tlsVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by TLS version.|
|tldCategory|query|string|false|Filters results by TLD category.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get top TLDs by email spoof classification

<a id="opIdradar-get-email-security-top-tlds-by-spoof"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/email/security/top/tlds/spoof/SPOOF \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/email/security/top/tlds/spoof/{spoof}`

Retrieves the top TLDs by emails classified as spoof or not.

<h3 id="get-top-tlds-by-email-spoof-classification-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|spoof|path|string|true|Spoof classification.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects returned in the response.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|arc|query|[string]|false|Filters results by ARC (Authenticated Received Chain) validation.|
|dkim|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) validation status.|
|dmarc|query|[string]|false|Filters results by DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance) validation status.|
|spf|query|[string]|false|Filters results by SPF (Sender Policy Framework) validation status.|
|tlsVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by TLS version.|
|tldCategory|query|string|false|Filters results by TLD category.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

|spoof|NOT_SPOOF|

## Get AS rankings by botnet threat feed activity

<a id="opIdradar-get-as-botnet-threat-feed"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/entities/asns/botnet_threat_feed \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/entities/asns/botnet_threat_feed`

Retrieves a ranked list of Autonomous Systems based on their presence in the Cloudflare Botnet Threat Feed. Rankings can be sorted by offense count or number of bad IPs. Optionally compare to a previous date to see rank changes.

<h3 id="get-as-rankings-by-botnet-threat-feed-activity-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects returned in the response.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Skips the specified number of objects before fetching the results.|
|metric|query|string|false|Metric to rank ASNs by.|
|date|query|string(date)|false|The date to retrieve (YYYY-MM-DD format). If not specified, returns the most recent available data. Note: This is the date the report was generated. The report is generated from information collected from the previous day (e.g., the 2026-02-23 entry contains data from 2026-02-22).|
|compareDateRange|query|string|false|Relative date range for rank change comparison (e.g., "1d", "7d", "30d").|
|location|query|string|false|Filters results by location. Specify an alpha-2 location code.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|sortOrder|query|string|false|Sort order.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|metric|OFFENSE_COUNT|
|metric|NUMBER_OF_OFFENDING_IPS|
|sortOrder|ASC|
|sortOrder|DESC|
|format|JSON|
|format|CSV|

`GET /radar/geolocations`

Retrieves a list of geolocations. Geolocation names can be localized by sending an `Accept-Language` HTTP header with a BCP 47 language tag (e.g., `Accept-Language: pt-PT`). The full quality-value chain is supported (e.g., `pt-PT,pt;q=0.9,en;q=0.8`).

|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects returned in the response.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Skips the specified number of objects before fetching the results.|
|geoId|query|string|false|Filters results by geolocation. Specify a comma-separated list of GeoNames IDs.|
|location|query|string|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 location codes.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

|format|JSON|
|format|CSV|

```json
        "longitude": "10",
        "name": "Lisbon",
```

## Get Geolocation details

<a id="opIdradar-get-geolocation-details"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/geolocations/3190509 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/geolocations/{geo_id}`

Retrieves the requested Geolocation information. Geolocation names can be localized by sending an `Accept-Language` HTTP header with a BCP 47 language tag (e.g., `Accept-Language: pt-PT`). The full quality-value chain is supported (e.g., `pt-PT,pt;q=0.9,en;q=0.8`).

<h3 id="get-geolocation-details-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|geo_id|path|string|true|Geolocation ID. Refer to [GeoNames](https://download.geonames.org/export/dump/readme.txt)|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|format|JSON|
|format|CSV|

```json
  "result": {
    "geolocation": {
      "code": "PT-11",
      "geoId": "2267056",
      "latitude": "10",
      "locale": "pt-PT",
      "longitude": "10",
      "name": "Lisbon",
      "parent": {
        "code": "PT-11",
        "geoId": "2267056",
        "latitude": "10",
        "locale": "pt-PT",
        "longitude": "10",
        "name": "Lisbon",
        "parent": {
          "code": "PT-11",
          "geoId": "2267056",
          "latitude": "10",
          "locale": "pt-PT",
          "longitude": "10",
          "name": "Lisbon",
          "type": "CONTINENT"
        },
        "type": "CONTINENT"
      },
      "type": "CONTINENT"
    }
  },
  "success": true
}
```

> 404 Response

```json

  "error": "Not Found."
}
```

## Get HTTP requests by bot class summary

<a id="opIdradar-get-http-summary-by-bot-class"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/http/summary/bot_class \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/http/summary/bot_class`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of bot-generated HTTP requests to genuine human traffic, as classified by Cloudflare. Visit https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/bot-classes/ for more information.

<h3 id="get-http-requests-by-bot-class-summary-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|geoId|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Geolocation. Specify a comma-separated list of GeoNames IDs. Prefix with `-` to exclude geoIds from results. For example, `-2267056,360689` excludes results from the 2267056 (Lisbon), but includes results from 5128638 (New York).|
|deviceType|query|[string]|false|Filters results by device type.|
|httpProtocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP protocol (HTTP vs. HTTPS).|
|httpVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP version.|
|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|
|os|query|[string]|false|Filters results by operating system.|
|tlsVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by TLS version.|
|browserFamily|query|[string]|false|Filters results by browser family.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get HTTP requests by OS summary

<a id="opIdradar-get-http-summary-by-operating-system"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/http/summary/os \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/http/summary/os`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of HTTP requests by operating system (Windows, macOS, Android, iOS, and others).

<h3 id="get-http-requests-by-os-summary-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|geoId|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Geolocation. Specify a comma-separated list of GeoNames IDs. Prefix with `-` to exclude geoIds from results. For example, `-2267056,360689` excludes results from the 2267056 (Lisbon), but includes results from 5128638 (New York).|
|botClass|query|[string]|false|Filters results by bot class. Refer to [Bot classes](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/bot-classes/).|
|deviceType|query|[string]|false|Filters results by device type.|
|httpProtocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP protocol (HTTP vs. HTTPS).|
|httpVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP version.|
|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|
|tlsVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by TLS version.|
|browserFamily|query|[string]|false|Filters results by browser family.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|


`GET /radar/http/summary/tls_version`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of HTTP requests by TLS version.

<h3 id="get-http-requests-by-tls-version-summary-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series.
```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/http/timeseries_groups/bot_class \
```

```bash
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/http/timeseries_groups/bot_class`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of HTTP requests classified as automated or human over time. Visit https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/bot-classes/ for more information.

<h3 id="get-http-requests-by-bot-class-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|

## Get HTTP requests by user agent family time series

<a id="opIdradar-get-http-timeseries-group-by-browser-families"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/http/timeseries_groups/browser_family \

  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/http/timeseries_groups/browser_family`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of HTTP requests by user agent family over time.

<h3 id="get-http-requests-by-user-agent-family-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|

## Get HTTP requests by HTTP/HTTPS time series

<a id="opIdradar-get-http-timeseries-group-by-http-protocol"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/http/timeseries_groups/http_protocol \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/http/timeseries_groups/http_protocol`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of HTTP requests by HTTP protocol (HTTP vs. HTTPS) over time.

<h3 id="get-http-requests-by-httphttps-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|geoId|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Geolocation. Specify a comma-separated list of GeoNames IDs. Prefix with `-` to exclude geoIds from results. For example, `-2267056,360689` excludes results from the 2267056 (Lisbon), but includes results from 5128638 (New York).|
|botClass|query|[string]|false|Filters results by bot class. Refer to [Bot classes](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/bot-classes/).|
|deviceType|query|[string]|false|Filters results by device type.|
|httpVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP version.|
|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|
|os|query|[string]|false|Filters results by operating system.|
|tlsVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by TLS version.|
|browserFamily|query|[string]|false|Filters results by browser family.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get HTTP requests by IP version time series

<a id="opIdradar-get-http-timeseries-group-by-ip-version"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/http/timeseries_groups/ip_version \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/http/timeseries_groups/ip_version`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of HTTP requests by IP version over time.

<h3 id="get-http-requests-by-ip-version-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|geoId|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Geolocation. Specify a comma-separated list of GeoNames IDs. Prefix with `-` to exclude geoIds from results. For example, `-2267056,360689` excludes results from the 2267056 (Lisbon), but includes results from 5128638 (New York).|
|botClass|query|[string]|false|Filters results by bot class. Refer to [Bot classes](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/bot-classes/).|
|deviceType|query|[string]|false|Filters results by device type.|
|httpProtocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP protocol (HTTP vs. HTTPS).|
|httpVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP version.|
|os|query|[string]|false|Filters results by operating system.|
|tlsVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by TLS version.|
|browserFamily|query|[string]|false|Filters results by browser family.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/http/timeseries_groups/post_quantum \
```

```bash
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/http/timeseries_groups/post_quantum`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the distribution of HTTP requests by post-quantum support over time.

<h3 id="get-http-requests-by-post-quantum-support-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|geoId|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Geolocation. Specify a comma-separated list of GeoNames IDs. Prefix with `-` to exclude geoIds from results. For example, `-2267056,360689` excludes results from the 2267056 (Lisbon), but includes results from 5128638 (New York).|
|botClass|query|[string]|false|Filters results by bot class. Refer to [Bot classes](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/bot-classes/).|
|deviceType|query|[string]|false|Filters results by device type.|
