`GET /radar/http/timeseries_groups/{dimension}`

Retrieves the distribution of HTTP requests grouped by dimension.

<h3 id="get-http-requests-time-series-grouped-by-dimension-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dimension|path|string|true|Specifies the HTTP attribute by which to group the results.|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|geoId|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Geolocation. Specify a comma-separated list of GeoNames IDs. Prefix with `-` to exclude geoIds from results. For example, `-2267056,360689` excludes results from the 2267056 (Lisbon), but includes results from 5128638 (New York).|
|apiTraffic|query|[string]|false|Filters results by API traffic classification. API traffic is identified by JSON or XML response content types on dynamic (non-cacheable) HTTP requests. Incompatible with the `browserFamily`, `deviceType`, `httpProtocol`, `httpVersion`, `ipVersion`, `os`, and `tlsVersion` filters/dimensions. When set, results can only be further filtered by location, continent, or Autonomous System.|
|botClass|query|[string]|false|Filters results by bot class. Refer to [Bot classes](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/bot-classes/).|
|contentType|query|[string]|false|Filters results by content type category. When set, results can only be further filtered by location, continent, or Autonomous System.|
|limitPerGroup|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.|
|deviceType|query|[string]|false|Filters results by device type.|
|httpProtocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP protocol (HTTP vs. HTTPS).|
|httpVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP version.|
|normalization|query|string|false|Normalization method applied to the results. Refer to [Normalization methods](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/normalization/).|
|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|
|os|query|[string]|false|Filters results by operating system.|
|tlsVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by TLS version.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

`GET /radar/http/top/ases/browser_family/{browser_family}`

Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|

When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. ## Get top ASes by HTTP requests for an HTTP protocol

<a id="opIdradar-get-http-top-ases-by-http-protocol"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/http/top/ases/http_protocol/HTTP \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/http/top/ases/http_protocol/{http_protocol}`

Retrieves the top autonomous systems, by HTTP requests, of the requested HTTP protocol.

<h3 id="get-top-ases-by-http-requests-for-an-http-protocol-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|http_protocol|path|string|true|HTTP protocol (HTTP vs. HTTPS).|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects returned in the response.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|geoId|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Geolocation. Specify a comma-separated list of GeoNames IDs. Prefix with `-` to exclude geoIds from results. For example, `-2267056,360689` excludes results from the 2267056 (Lisbon), but includes results from 5128638 (New York).|
|botClass|query|[string]|false|Filters results by bot class. Refer to [Bot classes](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/bot-classes/).|
|deviceType|query|[string]|false|Filters results by device type.|
|httpVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP version.|
|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|
|os|query|[string]|false|Filters results by operating system.|
|tlsVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by TLS version.|
|browserFamily|query|[string]|false|Filters results by browser family.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get top user agents by HTTP requests

<a id="opIdradar-get-http-top-browsers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/http/top/browser \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/http/top/browser`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Retrieves the top user agents by HTTP requests.

<h3 id="get-top-user-agents-by-http-requests-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects returned in the response.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|geoId|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Geolocation. Specify a comma-separated list of GeoNames IDs. Prefix with `-` to exclude geoIds from results. For example, `-2267056,360689` excludes results from the 2267056 (Lisbon), but includes results from 5128638 (New York).|
|botClass|query|[string]|false|Filters results by bot class. Refer to [Bot classes](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/bot-classes/).|
|deviceType|query|[string]|false|Filters results by device type.|
|httpProtocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP protocol (HTTP vs. HTTPS).|
|httpVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP version.|
|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|
|os|query|[string]|false|Filters results by operating system.|
|tlsVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by TLS version.|
|browserFamily|query|[string]|false|Filters results by browser family.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

<a id="opIdradar-get-http-top-locations-by-http-requests"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/http/top/locations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/http/top/locations`

Retrieves the top locations by HTTP requests.

<h3 id="get-top-locations-by-http-requests-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects returned in the response.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|geoId|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Geolocation. Specify a comma-separated list of GeoNames IDs. Prefix with `-` to exclude geoIds from results. For example, `-2267056,360689` excludes results from the 2267056 (Lisbon), but includes results from 5128638 (New York).|
|botClass|query|[string]|false|Filters results by bot class. Refer to [Bot classes](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/bot-classes/).|
|deviceType|query|[string]|false|Filters results by device type.|

|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|

## Get top locations by HTTP requests for a device type

<a id="opIdradar-get-http-top-locations-by-device-type"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/http/top/locations/device_type/DESKTOP \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/http/top/locations/device_type/{device_type}`

Retrieves the top locations, by HTTP requests, of the requested device type.

<h3 id="get-top-locations-by-http-requests-for-a-device-type-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|device_type|path|string|true|Device type.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects returned in the response.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|geoId|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Geolocation. Specify a comma-separated list of GeoNames IDs. Prefix with `-` to exclude geoIds from results. For example, `-2267056,360689` excludes results from the 2267056 (Lisbon), but includes results from 5128638 (New York).|
|botClass|query|[string]|false|Filters results by bot class. Refer to [Bot classes](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/bot-classes/).|
|httpProtocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP protocol (HTTP vs. HTTPS).|

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/http/top/locations/http_version/HTTPv1 \
```

`GET /radar/http/top/locations/http_version/{http_version}`

<h3 id="get-top-locations-by-http-requests-for-an-http-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|

When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. ## Get top locations by HTTP requests for a TLS version

<a id="opIdradar-get-http-top-locations-by-tls-version"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/http/top/locations/tls_version/TLSv1_0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/http/top/locations/tls_version/{tls_version}`

Retrieves the top locations, by HTTP requests, of the requested TLS protocol version.

<h3 id="get-top-locations-by-http-requests-for-a-tls-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tls_version|path|string|true|TLS version.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects returned in the response.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|geoId|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Geolocation. Specify a comma-separated list of GeoNames IDs. Prefix with `-` to exclude geoIds from results. For example, `-2267056,360689` excludes results from the 2267056 (Lisbon), but includes results from 5128638 (New York).|
|botClass|query|[string]|false|Filters results by bot class. Refer to [Bot classes](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/bot-classes/).|
|deviceType|query|[string]|false|Filters results by device type.|
|httpProtocol|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP protocol (HTTP vs. HTTPS).|
|httpVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by HTTP version.|
|ipVersion|query|[string]|false|Filters results by IP version (Ipv4 vs. IPv6).|
|os|query|[string]|false|Filters results by operating system.|
|browserFamily|query|[string]|false|Filters results by browser family.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. <h3 id="get-http-authentication-requests-by-compromised-credential-status-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

```bash
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/leaked_credential_checks/timeseries_groups/{dimension}`

Retrieves the distribution of HTTP authentication requests, grouped by the specified dimension over time.

<h3 id="get-time-series-distribution-of-http-authentication-requests-by-dimension-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dimension|path|string|true|Specifies the attribute by which to group the results.|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|botClass|query|[string]|false|Filters results by bot class. Refer to [Bot classes](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/bot-classes/).|
|compromised|query|[string]|false|Filters results by compromised credential status (clean vs. compromised).|
|checkResult|query|[string]|false|Filters results by leaked credential check result.|
|limitPerGroup|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.|
|normalization|query|string|false|Normalization method applied to the results. Refer to [Normalization methods](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/normalization/). `PERCENTAGE_CHANGE` requires exactly one comparison series (e.g. a `control` date range).|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get network traffic distribution by dimension

<a id="opIdradar-get-netflows-summary"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/netflows/summary/ADM1 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/netflows/summary/{dimension}`

Retrieves the distribution of network traffic (NetFlows) by the specified dimension.

<h3 id="get-network-traffic-distribution-by-dimension-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dimension|path|string|true|Specifies the NetFlows attribute by which to group the results.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|geoId|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Geolocation. Specify a comma-separated list of GeoNames IDs. Prefix with `-` to exclude geoIds from results. For example, `-2267056,360689` excludes results from the 2267056 (Lisbon), but includes results from 5128638 (New York).|
|product|query|[string]|false|Filters the results by network traffic product types.|
|limitPerGroup|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

## Get time series distribution of network traffic by dimension

<a id="opIdradar-get-netflows-timeseries-group"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/netflows/timeseries_groups/ADM1 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/netflows/timeseries_groups/{dimension}`

Retrieves the distribution of NetFlows traffic, grouped by the specified dimension over time.

<h3 id="get-time-series-distribution-of-network-traffic-by-dimension-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dimension|path|string|true|Specifies the NetFlows attribute by which to group the results.|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|geoId|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Geolocation. Specify a comma-separated list of GeoNames IDs. Prefix with `-` to exclude geoIds from results. For example, `-2267056,360689` excludes results from the 2267056 (Lisbon), but includes results from 5128638 (New York).|
|limitPerGroup|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.|
|normalization|query|string|false|Normalization method applied to the results. Refer to [Normalization methods](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/normalization/). `PERCENTAGE_CHANGE` requires exactly one comparison series (e.g. a `control` date range).|
|product|query|[string]|false|Filters the results by network traffic product types.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

|dimension|PRODUCT|

## Get origin metrics distribution by dimension

<a id="opIdradar-get-origins-summary"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/origins/summary/ORIGIN?metric=REQUESTS' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/origins/summary/{dimension}`

Retrieves an aggregated summary of origin metrics grouped by the specified dimension.

<h3 id="get-origin-metrics-distribution-by-dimension-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dimension|path|string|true|Specifies the origin attribute by which to group the results. `ORIGIN` groups across all providers and does not accept an `origin` or `region`. `REGION` requires an `origin`. `SUCCESS_RATE` and `PERCENTILE` require both an `origin` and a `region` and constrain the `metric` (`SUCCESS_RATE` supports only `REQUESTS`; `PERCENTILE` supports any metric except `REQUESTS`). `limitPerGroup` is only supported on the `REGION` dimension.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|limitPerGroup|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.|
|origin|query|[string]|false|Filters results by origin. Required for every dimension except `ORIGIN`; must not be set on the `ORIGIN` dimension, which groups across all providers.|
|metric|query|string|true|Specifies the metric to retrieve. Allowed metrics depend on the selected dimension (see the `dimension` path parameter).|
|region|query|[string]|false|Filters results by origin region. Requires `origin` to be set and is validated against it.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|dimension|ORIGIN|
|dimension|REGION|
|dimension|SUCCESS_RATE|
|dimension|PERCENTILE|
|origin|AMAZON|
|origin|GOOGLE|
|origin|MICROSOFT|
|origin|ORACLE|
|metric|CONNECTION_FAILURES|
|metric|REQUESTS|
|metric|RESPONSE_HEADER_RECEIVE_DURATION|
|metric|TCP_HANDSHAKE_DURATION|
|metric|TCP_RTT|
|metric|TLS_HANDSHAKE_DURATION|
|format|JSON|
|format|CSV|

## Get origin metrics time series

<a id="opIdradar-get-origins-timeseries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/origins/timeseries?origin=AMAZON&metric=REQUESTS' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/origins/timeseries`

Retrieves the time series of origin metrics for the specified origin.

<h3 id="get-origin-metrics-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|origin|query|[string]|true|Filters results by origin.|
|metric|query|string|true|Specifies the metric to retrieve. Without a `region`, only `REQUESTS` or `CONNECTION_FAILURES` are available; specify a `region` to use the latency metrics.|
|region|query|[string]|false|Filters results by origin region. Requires `origin` to be set and is validated against it.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|
|aggInterval|15m|
|aggInterval|1h|
|aggInterval|1d|
|aggInterval|1w|
|origin|AMAZON|

## Get origin metrics time series grouped by dimension

<a id="opIdradar-get-origins-timeseries-group"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/origins/timeseries_groups/ORIGIN?metric=REQUESTS' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/origins/timeseries_groups/{dimension}`

Retrieves the distribution of origin metrics grouped by the specified dimension over time.

<h3 id="get-origin-metrics-time-series-grouped-by-dimension-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dimension|path|string|true|Specifies the origin attribute by which to group the results. `ORIGIN` groups across all providers and does not accept an `origin` or `region`. `REGION` requires an `origin`. `SUCCESS_RATE` and `PERCENTILE` require both an `origin` and a `region` and constrain the `metric` (`SUCCESS_RATE` supports only `REQUESTS`; `PERCENTILE` supports any metric except `REQUESTS`). `limitPerGroup` is only supported on the `REGION` dimension.|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|limitPerGroup|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.|
|origin|query|[string]|false|Filters results by origin. Required for every dimension except `ORIGIN`; must not be set on the `ORIGIN` dimension, which groups across all providers.|
|metric|query|string|true|Specifies the metric to retrieve. Allowed metrics depend on the selected dimension (see the `dimension` path parameter).|
|region|query|[string]|false|Filters results by origin region. Requires `origin` to be set and is validated against it.|
|normalization|query|string|false|Normalization method applied to the results. Refer to [Normalization methods](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/normalization/).|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|dimension|ORIGIN|
|dimension|REGION|
|dimension|SUCCESS_RATE|
|dimension|PERCENTILE|
|aggInterval|15m|
|aggInterval|1h|
|aggInterval|1d|
|aggInterval|1w|
|origin|AMAZON|

|normalization|PERCENTAGE|
|normalization|MIN0_MAX|
|format|JSON|
|format|CSV|

## Check Post-Quantum TLS support

<a id="opIdradar-get-post-quantum-tls-support"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/post_quantum/tls/support?host=cloudflare.com' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/post_quantum/tls/support`

Tests whether a hostname or IP address supports Post-Quantum (PQ) TLS key exchange. Returns information about the negotiated key exchange algorithm, whether it uses PQ cryptography, and any detected TLS implementation bugs (Split ClientHello, HRR failure, etc.).

<h3 id="check-post-quantum-tls-support-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|host|query|string|true|Hostname or IP address to test for Post-Quantum TLS support, optionally with port (defaults to 443).|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": {
    "bugs": {
      "hrrFailure": true,
      "splitClientHello": true,
      "unknownKeyshare": true
    },
    "host": "string",
    "kex": 0,
    "kexName": "string",
    "pq": true
  },
  "success": true
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "result": {},
  "success": false
}
```

<h3 id="check-post-quantum-tls-support-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request.|Inline|

<h3 id="check-post-quantum-tls-support-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|result|object|true|none|none|
|» bugs|object|true|none|none|
|» » hrrFailure|boolean|true|none|Server sends a HelloRetryRequest but fails to complete the handshake after the client sends the second ClientHello. Often caused by non-compliant TLS 1.3 implementations on shared hosting providers.|
|» » splitClientHello|boolean|true|none|Server rejects fragmented ClientHello caused by large PQ keyshare, but accepts classical (non-PQ) handshakes. Typically caused by middleboxes or firewalls that cannot reassemble split TLS ClientHello messages.|
|» » unknownKeyshare|boolean|true|none|Server cannot handle an unknown key exchange algorithm in the ClientHello keyshare extension. Compliant servers should respond with HelloRetryRequest for a supported algorithm.|
|» host|string|true|none|The host that was tested|
|» kex|number|true|none|TLS CurveID of the negotiated key exchange|
|» kexName|string|true|none|Human-readable name of the key exchange algorithm|
|» pq|boolean|true|none|Whether the negotiated key exchange uses Post-Quantum cryptography (specifically X25519MLKEM768)|
|success|boolean|true|none|none|

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[object]|true|none|none|
|» message|string|true|none|none|
|result|object|true|none|none|
|success|boolean|true|none|none|

## Get Internet Quality Index (IQI) summary

<a id="opIdradar-get-quality-index-summary"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/quality/iqi/summary?metric=latency' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/quality/iqi/summary`

Retrieves a summary (percentiles) of bandwidth, latency, or DNS response time from the Radar Internet Quality Index (IQI).

<h3 id="get-internet-quality-index-iqi-summary-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|metric|query|string|true|Defines which metric to return (bandwidth, latency, or DNS response time).|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|metric|BANDWIDTH|
|metric|DNS|
|metric|LATENCY|
|format|JSON|
|format|CSV|

## Get speed tests histogram

<a id="opIdradar-get-quality-speed-histogram"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/quality/speed/histogram \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/quality/speed/histogram`

Retrieves a histogram from the previous 90 days of Cloudflare Speed Test data, split into fixed bandwidth (Mbps), latency (ms), or jitter (ms) buckets.

<h3 id="get-speed-tests-histogram-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|bucketSize|query|integer|false|Specifies the width for every bucket in the histogram.|
|metricGroup|query|string|false|Metrics to be returned.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|metricGroup|BANDWIDTH|
|metricGroup|LATENCY|
|metricGroup|JITTER|
|format|JSON|
|format|CSV|

## Get top locations by speed test results

<a id="opIdradar-get-quality-speed-top-locations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/quality/speed/top/locations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/quality/speed/top/locations`

Retrieves the top locations by bandwidth, latency, jitter, or packet loss, from the previous 90 days of Cloudflare Speed Test data.

<h3 id="get-top-locations-by-speed-test-results-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects returned in the response.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|orderBy|query|string|false|Specifies the metric to order the results by.|
|reverse|query|boolean|false|Reverses the order of results.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

|orderBy|LATENCY_LOADED|
|orderBy|JITTER_IDLE|
|orderBy|JITTER_LOADED|
|format|JSON|
|format|CSV|

## Get domain rank details

<a id="opIdradar-get-ranking-domain-details"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/ranking/domain/google.com \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/ranking/domain/{domain}`

Retrieves domain rank details. Cloudflare provides an ordered rank for the top 100 domains, but for the remainder it only provides ranking buckets like top 200 thousand, top one million, etc.. These are available through Radar datasets endpoints.

<h3 id="get-domain-rank-details-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|domain|path|string|true|Domain name.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects returned in the response.|
|rankingType|query|string|false|The ranking type.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|includeTopLocations|query|boolean|false|Includes top locations in the response.|
|date|query|[string(date)]|false|Filters results by the specified array of dates.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|rankingType|POPULAR|
|rankingType|TRENDING_RISE|
|rankingType|TRENDING_STEADY|
|format|JSON|
|format|CSV|

## Get domains rank time series

<a id="opIdradar-get-ranking-domain-timeseries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/ranking/timeseries_groups \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/ranking/timeseries_groups`

Retrieves domains rank over time.

<h3 id="get-domains-rank-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects returned in the response.|
|rankingType|query|string|false|The ranking type.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 location codes.|
|domains|query|[string]|false|Filters results by domain name. Specify a comma-separated list of domain names.|
|domainCategory|query|[string]|false|Filters results by domain category.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|rankingType|POPULAR|
|rankingType|TRENDING_RISE|
|rankingType|TRENDING_STEADY|
|format|JSON|
|format|CSV|

```bash
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/ranking/top`

Retrieves the top or trending domains based on their rank. Popular domains are domains of broad appeal based on how people use the Internet. Trending domains are domains that are generating a surge in interest. For more information on top domains, see https://blog.cloudflare.com/radar-domain-rankings/.

|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 location codes.|
|domainCategory|query|[string]|false|Filters results by domain category.|
|date|query|[string(date)]|false|Filters results by the specified array of dates.|

<a id="opIdradar-get-ranking-internet-services-timeseries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/ranking/internet_services/timeseries_groups \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/ranking/internet_services/timeseries_groups`

Retrieves Internet Services rank update changes over time.

<h3 id="get-internet-services-rank-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|serviceCategory|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Internet service category.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects returned in the response.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-radar-search">Radar Search</h1>

## Search for locations, ASes, reports, and more

<a id="opIdradar-get-search-global"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/search/global?query=United' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/search/global`

Searches for locations, autonomous systems, reports, bots, certificate logs, certificate authorities, industries and verticals. Location names can be localized by sending an `Accept-Language` HTTP header with a BCP 47 language tag (e.g., `Accept-Language: pt-PT`). The full quality-value chain is supported (e.g., `pt-PT,pt;q=0.9,en;q=0.8`).

<h3 id="search-for-locations-ases-reports-and-more-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects returned in the response.|
|limitPerGroup|query|number|false|Limits the number of objects per search category.|
|query|query|string|true|String used to perform the search operation.|
|include|query|[string]|false|Search types included in results.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Search types excluded from results.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-radar-tcp-resets-and-timeouts">Radar TCP Resets and Timeouts</h1>

## Get TCP resets and timeouts summary

<a id="opIdradar-get-tcp-resets-timeouts-summary"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/tcp_resets_timeouts/summary \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/tcp_resets_timeouts/summary`

Retrieves the distribution of connection stage by TCP connections terminated within the first 10 packets by a reset or timeout.

<h3 id="get-tcp-resets-and-timeouts-summary-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|format|JSON|
|format|CSV|
