## Get TCP resets and timeouts time series

<a id="opIdradar-get-tcp-resets-timeouts-timeseries-group"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/tcp_resets_timeouts/timeseries_groups \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/tcp_resets_timeouts/timeseries_groups`

Retrieves the distribution of connection stage by TCP connections terminated within the first 10 packets by a reset or timeout over time.

<h3 id="get-tcp-resets-and-timeouts-time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggInterval|query|string|false|Aggregation interval of the results (e.g., in 15 minutes or 1 hour intervals). Refer to [Aggregation intervals](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/concepts/aggregation-intervals/). When omitted, the interval is auto-selected from the requested date range; finer intervals are only available for shorter ranges. If the requested interval is too granular for the date range, the request is rejected.|
|name|query|[string]|false|Array of names used to label the series in the response.|
|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|
|tld|query|[string]|false|Filters results by top-level domain.|
|nameserver|query|string|false|Filters results by nameserver hostname.|
|limitPerGroup|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

|aggInterval|1w|
|format|JSON|

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-radar-traffic-anomalies">Radar Traffic Anomalies</h1>

## Get latest Internet traffic anomalies

<a id="opIdradar-get-traffic-anomalies"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/traffic_anomalies \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /radar/traffic_anomalies`

Retrieves the latest Internet traffic anomalies, which are signals that might indicate an outage. These alerts are automatically detected by Radar and manually verified by our team.

<h3 id="get-latest-internet-traffic-anomalies-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of objects returned in the response.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Skips the specified number of objects before fetching the results.|
|dateRange|query|string|false|Filters results by a relative date range ending at the current time. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`), e.g. `7d`. Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `3dcontrol` covers days -10 to -7, `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `28dcontrol` covers days -56 to -28, and `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). Mutually exclusive with `dateStart`/`dateEnd`.|
|dateStart|query|string(date-time)|false|Start of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`.|
|dateEnd|query|string(date-time)|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`.|
|status|query|string|false|none|
|type|query|[string]|false|Filters results by entity type (LOCATION, AS, or ORIGIN).|
|dataSource|query|string|false|Filters results by data source.|
|asn|query|integer|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify a single Autonomous System Number (ASN) as integer.|
|location|query|string|false|Filters results by location. Specify an alpha-2 location code.|
|origin|query|string|false|Filters results by origin.|
|format|query|string|false|Format in which results will be returned.|

|dateRange|query|[string]|false|Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by the current window's length rounded up to a whole number of weeks, so it keeps the same weekday alignment and does not overlap the current window (e.g. `7dcontrol` covers days -14 to -7, `10dcontrol` covers days -24 to -14). For example, pass `7d` and `7dcontrol` to compare this week with the previous week. All series must resolve to the same duration as the main series; relative ranges (including `control`) satisfy this automatically. Use this parameter or set specific start and end dates (`dateStart` and `dateEnd` parameters).|
|dateStart|query|[string(date-time)]|false|Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|dateEnd|query|[string(date-time)]|false|End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations match only before alignment may be rejected.|
|asn|query|[string]|false|Filters results by Autonomous System. Specify one or more Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) as a comma-separated list. Prefix with `-` to exclude ASNs from results. For example, `-174, 3356` excludes results from AS174, but includes results from AS3356.|
|location|query|[string]|false|Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.|
|continent|query|[string]|false|Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.|

## Update communication preferences

<a id="opIduser-communication-preferences-update"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/user/communication_preferences \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "language-locale": "es-ES",
    "preferences": {
      "marketing": {
        "subscribed": true
      },
      "product_news": {
        "subscribed": true
      }
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /user/communication_preferences`

Set one or more communication preferences for the authenticated user. Supply a map of preference keys to subscription states, and an optional language locale. This endpoint does not modify email verification settings. Callers authenticate with standard Cloudflare API tokens or keys.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "language-locale": "es-ES",
  "preferences": {
    "marketing": {
      "subscribed": true
    },
    "product_news": {
      "subscribed": true
    }
  }
}
```

## Create Monitor

<a id="opIdload-balancer-monitors-create-monitor"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/user/load_balancers/monitors \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

    "expected_codes": "2xx",
    "follow_redirects": true,
    "header": {
      "Host": [
        "example.com"
      ],
      "X-App-ID": [
        "abc123"
      ]
    },

    "method": "GET",

  }'
```

`POST /user/load_balancers/monitors`

Create a configured monitor.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "allow_insecure": true,
  "consecutive_down": 0,
  "consecutive_up": 0,
  "description": "Login page monitor",
  "expected_body": "alive",
  "expected_codes": "2xx",
  "follow_redirects": true,
  "header": {
    "Host": [
      "example.com"
    ],
    "X-App-ID": [
      "abc123"
    ]
  },
  "interval": 60,
  "method": "GET",
  "path": "/health",
  "port": 0,
  "probe_zone": "example.com",
  "retries": 2,
  "timeout": 5,
  "type": "https"
}
```

<h3 id="create-monitor-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» allow_insecure|body|[load-balancing_allow_insecure](#schemaload-balancing_allow_insecure)|false|Do not validate the certificate when monitor use HTTPS. This parameter is currently only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» consecutive_down|body|[load-balancing_consecutive_down](#schemaload-balancing_consecutive_down)|false|To be marked unhealthy the monitored origin must fail this healthcheck N consecutive times.|
|» consecutive_up|body|[load-balancing_consecutive_up](#schemaload-balancing_consecutive_up)|false|To be marked healthy the monitored origin must pass this healthcheck N consecutive times.|
|» description|body|[load-balancing_description](#schemaload-balancing_description)|false|Object description.|
|» expected_body|body|[load-balancing_expected_body](#schemaload-balancing_expected_body)|false|A case-insensitive sub-string to look for in the response body. If this string is not found, the origin will be marked as unhealthy. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» expected_codes|body|[load-balancing_expected_codes](#schemaload-balancing_expected_codes)|false|The expected HTTP response code or code range of the health check. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» follow_redirects|body|[load-balancing_follow_redirects](#schemaload-balancing_follow_redirects)|false|Follow redirects if returned by the origin. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» header|body|[load-balancing_header](#schemaload-balancing_header)|false|The HTTP request headers to send in the health check. It is recommended you set a Host header by default. The User-Agent header cannot be overridden. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» interval|body|[load-balancing_interval](#schemaload-balancing_interval)|false|The interval between each health check. Shorter intervals may improve failover time, but will increase load on the origins as we check from multiple locations.|
|» method|body|[load-balancing_method](#schemaload-balancing_method)|false|The method to use for the health check. This defaults to 'GET' for HTTP/HTTPS based checks and 'connection_established' for TCP based health checks.|
|» path|body|[load-balancing_path](#schemaload-balancing_path)|false|The endpoint path you want to conduct a health check against. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» port|body|[load-balancing_port](#schemaload-balancing_port)|false|The port number to connect to for the health check. Required for TCP, UDP, and SMTP checks. HTTP and HTTPS checks should only define the port when using a non-standard port (HTTP: default 80, HTTPS: default 443).|
|» probe_zone|body|[load-balancing_probe_zone](#schemaload-balancing_probe_zone)|false|Assign this monitor to emulate the specified zone while probing. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» retries|body|[load-balancing_retries](#schemaload-balancing_retries)|false|The number of retries to attempt in case of a timeout before marking the origin as unhealthy. Retries are attempted immediately.|
|» timeout|body|[load-balancing_timeout](#schemaload-balancing_timeout)|false|The timeout (in seconds) before marking the health check as failed.|
|» type|body|[load-balancing_type](#schemaload-balancing_type)|false|The protocol to use for the health check. Currently supported protocols are 'HTTP','HTTPS', 'TCP', 'ICMP-PING', 'UDP-ICMP', and 'SMTP'.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|http|
|» type|https|
|» type|tcp|
|» type|udp_icmp|
|» type|icmp_ping|
|» type|smtp|

`POST /user/load_balancers/pools`

Create a new pool.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "check_regions": [
    "WEU",
    "ENAM"
  ],
  "description": "Primary data center - Provider XYZ",
  "enabled": false,
  "health_sources": [
    "regional",
    "global"
  ],
  "latitude": 0,
  "load_shedding": {
    "default_percent": 0,
    "default_policy": "random",
    "session_percent": 0,
    "session_policy": "hash"
  },
  "longitude": 0,
  "minimum_origins": 1,
  "monitor": "string",
  "monitor_group": "string",
  "name": "primary-dc-1",
  "networks": [
    "cloudflare",
    "jdcloud"
  ],
  "notification_email": "someone@example.com,sometwo@example.com",
  "notification_filter": {
    "origin": {
      "disable": true
    },
    "pool": {
      "healthy": false
    }
  },
  "origin_steering": {
    "policy": "random"
  },
  "origins": [
    {
      "address": "0.0.0.0",
      "enabled": true,
      "flatten_cname": true,
      "header": {
        "Host": [
          "example.com"
        ]
      },
      "name": "app-server-1",
      "port": 0,
      "virtual_network_id": "a5624d4e-044a-4ff0-b3e1-e2465353d4b4",
      "weight": 0.6
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-pool-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» check_regions|body|[load-balancing_check_regions](#schemaload-balancing_check_regions)|false|A list of regions from which to run health checks. Null means every Cloudflare data center.|
|» description|body|[load-balancing_schemas-description](#schemaload-balancing_schemas-description)|false|A human-readable description of the pool.|
|» enabled|body|[load-balancing_enabled](#schemaload-balancing_enabled)|false|Whether to enable (the default) or disable this pool. Disabled pools will not receive traffic and are excluded from health checks. Disabling a pool will cause any load balancers using it to failover to the next pool (if any).|
|» health_sources|body|[load-balancing_health_sources](#schemaload-balancing_health_sources)|false|A list of health sources, ordered from highest to lowest priority, used to evaluate individual origin health and overall pool health. The load balancer uses the first source that has data and falls back to the next. Currently accepted values are null or the exact array ["regional", "global"]; any other combination is rejected. Null (the default) behaves like ["local", "global"]. ["regional", "global"] makes each region steer on its own health, falling back to the global decision when a region has no fresh data. Setting regional requires at least one region in check_regions.|
|» latitude|body|[load-balancing_latitude](#schemaload-balancing_latitude)|false|The latitude of the data center containing the origins used in this pool in decimal degrees. If this is set, longitude must also be set.|
|» load_shedding|body|[load-balancing_load_shedding](#schemaload-balancing_load_shedding)|false|Configures load shedding policies and percentages for the pool.|
|» longitude|body|[load-balancing_longitude](#schemaload-balancing_longitude)|false|The longitude of the data center containing the origins used in this pool in decimal degrees. If this is set, latitude must also be set.|
|» minimum_origins|body|[load-balancing_minimum_origins](#schemaload-balancing_minimum_origins)|false|The minimum number of origins that must be healthy for this pool to serve traffic. If the number of healthy origins falls below this number, the pool will be marked unhealthy and will failover to the next available pool.|
|» monitor|body|[load-balancing_monitor_id](#schemaload-balancing_monitor_id)|false|The ID of the Monitor to use for checking the health of origins within this pool.|
|» monitor_group|body|[load-balancing_monitor_group_id](#schemaload-balancing_monitor_group_id)|false|The ID of the Monitor Group to use for checking the health of origins within this pool.|
|» name|body|[load-balancing_name](#schemaload-balancing_name)|true|A short name (tag) for the pool. Only alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores are allowed.|
|» networks|body|[load-balancing_networks](#schemaload-balancing_networks)|false|List of networks where Load Balancer or Pool is enabled.|
|» notification_email|body|[load-balancing_notification_email](#schemaload-balancing_notification_email)|false|This field is now deprecated. It has been moved to Cloudflare's Centralized Notification service https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/notifications/. The email address to send health status notifications to. This can be an individual mailbox or a mailing list. Multiple emails can be supplied as a comma delimited list.|
|» notification_filter|body|[load-balancing_notification_filter](#schemaload-balancing_notification_filter)|false|Filter pool and origin health notifications by resource type or health status. Use null to reset.|
|» origin_steering|body|[load-balancing_origin_steering](#schemaload-balancing_origin_steering)|false|Configures origin steering for the pool. Controls how origins are selected for new sessions and traffic without session affinity.|
|» origins|body|[load-balancing_origins](#schemaload-balancing_origins)|true|The list of origins within this pool. Traffic directed at this pool is balanced across all currently healthy origins, provided the pool itself is healthy.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» check_regions|WNAM|
|» check_regions|ENAM|
|» check_regions|WEU|
|» check_regions|EEU|
|» check_regions|NSAM|
|» check_regions|SSAM|
|» check_regions|OC|
|» check_regions|ME|
|» check_regions|NAF|
|» check_regions|SAF|
|» check_regions|SAS|
|» check_regions|SEAS|
|» check_regions|NEAS|
|» check_regions|CHINA|
|» check_regions|ALL_REGIONS|
|» health_sources|local|
|» health_sources|regional|
|» health_sources|global|

`PATCH /user/load_balancers/pools`

Apply changes to a number of existing pools, overwriting the supplied properties. Pools are ordered by ascending `name`. Returns the list of affected pools. Supports the standard pagination query parameters, either `limit`/`offset` or `per_page`/`page`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "notification_email": ""
}
```

<h3 id="update-pool-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pool_id|path|[load-balancing_schemas-identifier](#schemaload-balancing_schemas-identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» check_regions|body|[load-balancing_check_regions](#schemaload-balancing_check_regions)|false|A list of regions from which to run health checks. Null means every Cloudflare data center.|
|» description|body|[load-balancing_schemas-description](#schemaload-balancing_schemas-description)|false|A human-readable description of the pool.|
|» enabled|body|[load-balancing_enabled](#schemaload-balancing_enabled)|false|Whether to enable (the default) or disable this pool. Disabled pools will not receive traffic and are excluded from health checks. Disabling a pool will cause any load balancers using it to failover to the next pool (if any).|
|» health_sources|body|[load-balancing_health_sources](#schemaload-balancing_health_sources)|false|A list of health sources, ordered from highest to lowest priority, used to evaluate individual origin health and overall pool health. The load balancer uses the first source that has data and falls back to the next. Currently accepted values are null or the exact array ["regional", "global"]; any other combination is rejected. Null (the default) behaves like ["local", "global"]. ["regional", "global"] makes each region steer on its own health, falling back to the global decision when a region has no fresh data. Setting regional requires at least one region in check_regions.|
|» latitude|body|[load-balancing_latitude](#schemaload-balancing_latitude)|false|The latitude of the data center containing the origins used in this pool in decimal degrees. If this is set, longitude must also be set.|
|» load_shedding|body|[load-balancing_load_shedding](#schemaload-balancing_load_shedding)|false|Configures load shedding policies and percentages for the pool.|
|» longitude|body|[load-balancing_longitude](#schemaload-balancing_longitude)|false|The longitude of the data center containing the origins used in this pool in decimal degrees. If this is set, latitude must also be set.|
|» minimum_origins|body|[load-balancing_minimum_origins](#schemaload-balancing_minimum_origins)|false|The minimum number of origins that must be healthy for this pool to serve traffic. If the number of healthy origins falls below this number, the pool will be marked unhealthy and will failover to the next available pool.|
|» monitor|body|[load-balancing_monitor_id](#schemaload-balancing_monitor_id)|false|The ID of the Monitor to use for checking the health of origins within this pool.|
|» monitor_group|body|[load-balancing_monitor_group_id](#schemaload-balancing_monitor_group_id)|false|The ID of the Monitor Group to use for checking the health of origins within this pool.|
|» name|body|[load-balancing_name](#schemaload-balancing_name)|true|A short name (tag) for the pool. Only alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores are allowed.|
|» networks|body|[load-balancing_networks](#schemaload-balancing_networks)|false|List of networks where Load Balancer or Pool is enabled.|
|» notification_email|body|[load-balancing_notification_email](#schemaload-balancing_notification_email)|false|This field is now deprecated. It has been moved to Cloudflare's Centralized Notification service https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/notifications/. The email address to send health status notifications to. This can be an individual mailbox or a mailing list. Multiple emails can be supplied as a comma delimited list.|
|» notification_filter|body|[load-balancing_notification_filter](#schemaload-balancing_notification_filter)|false|Filter pool and origin health notifications by resource type or health status. Use null to reset.|
|» origin_steering|body|[load-balancing_origin_steering](#schemaload-balancing_origin_steering)|false|Configures origin steering for the pool. Controls how origins are selected for new sessions and traffic without session affinity.|
|» origins|body|[load-balancing_origins](#schemaload-balancing_origins)|true|The list of origins within this pool. Traffic directed at this pool is balanced across all currently healthy origins, provided the pool itself is healthy.|

## Preview Pool

<a id="opIdload-balancer-pools-preview-pool"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/user/load_balancers/pools/17b5962d775c646f3f9725cbc7a53df4/preview \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "allow_insecure": true,
    "consecutive_down": 0,
    "consecutive_up": 0,
    "description": "Login page monitor",
    "expected_body": "alive",
    "expected_codes": "2xx",
    "follow_redirects": true,
    "header": {
      "Host": [
        "example.com"
      ],
      "X-App-ID": [
        "abc123"
      ]
    },
    "interval": 60,
    "method": "GET",
    "path": "/health",
    "port": 0,
    "probe_zone": "example.com",
    "retries": 2,
    "timeout": 5,
    "type": "https"
  }'
```

`POST /user/load_balancers/pools/{pool_id}/preview`

Preview pool health using provided monitor details. The returned preview_id can be used in the preview endpoint to retrieve the results.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "allow_insecure": true,
  "consecutive_down": 0,
  "consecutive_up": 0,
  "description": "Login page monitor",
  "expected_body": "alive",
  "expected_codes": "2xx",
  "follow_redirects": true,
  "header": {
    "Host": [
      "example.com"
    ],
    "X-App-ID": [
      "abc123"
    ]
  },
  "interval": 60,
  "method": "GET",
  "path": "/health",
  "port": 0,
  "probe_zone": "example.com",
  "retries": 2,
  "timeout": 5,
  "type": "https"
}
```

<h3 id="preview-pool-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pool_id|path|[load-balancing_schemas-identifier](#schemaload-balancing_schemas-identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» allow_insecure|body|[load-balancing_allow_insecure](#schemaload-balancing_allow_insecure)|false|Do not validate the certificate when monitor use HTTPS. This parameter is currently only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» consecutive_down|body|[load-balancing_consecutive_down](#schemaload-balancing_consecutive_down)|false|To be marked unhealthy the monitored origin must fail this healthcheck N consecutive times.|
|» consecutive_up|body|[load-balancing_consecutive_up](#schemaload-balancing_consecutive_up)|false|To be marked healthy the monitored origin must pass this healthcheck N consecutive times.|
|» description|body|[load-balancing_description](#schemaload-balancing_description)|false|Object description.|
|» expected_body|body|[load-balancing_expected_body](#schemaload-balancing_expected_body)|false|A case-insensitive sub-string to look for in the response body. If this string is not found, the origin will be marked as unhealthy. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» expected_codes|body|[load-balancing_expected_codes](#schemaload-balancing_expected_codes)|false|The expected HTTP response code or code range of the health check. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» follow_redirects|body|[load-balancing_follow_redirects](#schemaload-balancing_follow_redirects)|false|Follow redirects if returned by the origin. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» header|body|[load-balancing_header](#schemaload-balancing_header)|false|The HTTP request headers to send in the health check. It is recommended you set a Host header by default. The User-Agent header cannot be overridden. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» interval|body|[load-balancing_interval](#schemaload-balancing_interval)|false|The interval between each health check. Shorter intervals may improve failover time, but will increase load on the origins as we check from multiple locations.|
|» method|body|[load-balancing_method](#schemaload-balancing_method)|false|The method to use for the health check. This defaults to 'GET' for HTTP/HTTPS based checks and 'connection_established' for TCP based health checks.|
|» path|body|[load-balancing_path](#schemaload-balancing_path)|false|The endpoint path you want to conduct a health check against. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» port|body|[load-balancing_port](#schemaload-balancing_port)|false|The port number to connect to for the health check. Required for TCP, UDP, and SMTP checks. HTTP and HTTPS checks should only define the port when using a non-standard port (HTTP: default 80, HTTPS: default 443).|
|» probe_zone|body|[load-balancing_probe_zone](#schemaload-balancing_probe_zone)|false|Assign this monitor to emulate the specified zone while probing. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|» retries|body|[load-balancing_retries](#schemaload-balancing_retries)|false|The number of retries to attempt in case of a timeout before marking the origin as unhealthy. Retries are attempted immediately.|
|» timeout|body|[load-balancing_timeout](#schemaload-balancing_timeout)|false|The timeout (in seconds) before marking the health check as failed.|
|» type|body|[load-balancing_type](#schemaload-balancing_type)|false|The protocol to use for the health check. Currently supported protocols are 'HTTP','HTTPS', 'TCP', 'ICMP-PING', 'UDP-ICMP', and 'SMTP'.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|http|
|» type|https|
|» type|tcp|
|» type|udp_icmp|
|» type|icmp_ping|
|» type|smtp|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "pools": {
      "abwlnp5jbqn45ecgxd03erbgtxtqai0d": "WNAM Datacenter",
      "ve8h9lrcip5n5bbga9yqmdws28ay5d0l": "EEU Datacenter"
    },
    "preview_id": "f1aba936b94213e5b8dca0c0dbf1f9cc"
  }
}
```

```json
}
```

## Create Zone

<a id="opIdzones-post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "account": {
      "id": "023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353"
    },
    "name": "example.com",
    "type": "full"
  }'
```

`POST /zones`

Creates a new zone (domain) in your Cloudflare account.

The zone is created in a pending state and must be activated by updating your domain's
nameservers to point to Cloudflare, or by completing the verification process for partial
(CNAME) setups.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "account": {
    "id": "023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353"
  },
  "name": "example.com",
  "type": "full"
}
```

<h3 id="create-zone-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» account|body|object|true|none|
|» » id|body|[zones_identifier](#schemazones_identifier)|false|Identifier|
|» name|body|[zones_name](#schemazones_name)|true|The domain name. Per [RFC 1035](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1035#section-2.3.4) the overall zone name can be up to 253 characters, with each segment ("label") not exceeding 63 characters.|
|» type|body|[zones_type](#schemazones_type)|false|A full zone implies that DNS is hosted with Cloudflare. A partial zone is<br>typically a partner-hosted zone or a CNAME setup.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|» type|full|
|» type|partial|
|» type|secondary|
|» type|internal|

## Invalidate Cached Content by Environment

<a id="opIdzone-environment-invalidate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/environments/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/invalidate_cache \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "tags": [
      "product-1234",
      "homepage"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /zones/{zone_id}/environments/{environment_id}/invalidate_cache`

Marks cached content as stale for one environment of the zone. Content cached for the zone's other environments, including production, is not affected. Otherwise this works like `POST /zones/{zone_id}/invalidate_cache`: the next request for invalidated content makes Cloudflare revalidate it with your origin, and the request body takes the same fields.

Environments are part of [Version Management](https://developers.cloudflare.com/version-management/). To delete the content instead, use `POST /zones/{zone_id}/environments/{environment_id}/purge_cache`.

Invalidating by URL (`files`) does not work for environments that select requests by IP address, country, ASN, or threat score, and fails with error `1136`. Use `tags`, `hosts`, `prefixes`, or `purge_everything` for those environments.

### Availability and limits

Rate limits and the number of items you can send in one request depend on your plan. See [Purge cache: availability and limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/purge-cache/#availability-and-limits).

## Invalidate Cached Content

<a id="opIdzone-invalidate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/invalidate_cache \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "tags": [
      "product-1234",
      "homepage"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /zones/{zone_id}/invalidate_cache`

Marks cached content as stale in every Cloudflare data center and cache tier, including Cache Reserve. The content stays in cache. The next request for it makes Cloudflare revalidate it with your origin, using the `ETag` and `Last-Modified` values it was cached with:

- If your origin answers `304 Not Modified`, Cloudflare serves the cached copy without downloading it again, and `CF-Cache-Status` is `REVALIDATED`.
- If your origin sends a full response, Cloudflare serves and caches the new content, and `CF-Cache-Status` is `EXPIRED`.

With Tiered Cache, each tier revalidates with the tier above it, so a visitor can see `EXPIRED` even when your origin answered `304`.

Until content is revalidated, your `stale-while-revalidate` and `stale-if-error` directives still apply, counted from the time you invalidated it. For example, if your origin fails during revalidation, Cloudflare can keep serving the stale copy for the `stale-if-error` window.

### Invalidate or purge?

- **Invalidate** when content may not have changed, for example after a deploy. Unchanged content costs your origin a `304` instead of a full response. That saving needs an origin that sends `ETag` or `Last-Modified` and answers conditional requests. Otherwise, every revalidation downloads the full response.
- **Purge**, with `POST /zones/{zone_id}/purge_cache`, when content must not be served again, for example content you removed for legal or security reasons.

Invalidating takes the same request bodies as purging, needs the same permission, and counts against the same rate limits. After a broad invalidation, such as `purge_everything`, expect more conditional requests to your origin while visitors request the invalidated content again.

### Choose what to invalidate

Send one of these fields in the request body:

- `files`: specific URLs. If your cache key includes request headers, send each URL with the header values it was cached with.
- `tags`: all content whose `Cache-Tag` response header contains one of the tags.
- `hosts`: all content cached for the hostnames.
- `prefixes`: all content whose URL starts with one of the prefixes.
- `purge_everything`: all cached content in the zone.

### Check the result

A `200` response with `success: true` means Cloudflare accepted the request. To check, request an invalidated URL and confirm that the `CF-Cache-Status` response header is `REVALIDATED` or `EXPIRED`.

### Availability and limits

Rate limits and the number of items you can send in one request depend on your plan. See [Purge cache: availability and limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/purge-cache/#availability-and-limits).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "tags": [
    "product-1234",
    "homepage"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="invalidate-cached-content-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[cache-purge_identifier](#schemacache-purge_identifier)|true|The zone ID.|
|body|body|[cache-purge_FlexPurgeByTags](#schemacache-purge_flexpurgebytags) \| [cache-purge_FlexPurgeByHostnames](#schemacache-purge_flexpurgebyhostnames) \| [cache-purge_FlexPurgeByPrefixes](#schemacache-purge_flexpurgebyprefixes) \| [cache-purge_Everything](#schemacache-purge_everything) \| [cache-purge_SingleFile](#schemacache-purge_singlefile) \| [cache-purge_SingleFileWithUrlAndHeaders](#schemacache-purge_singlefilewithurlandheaders)|true|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[cache-purge_FlexPurgeByTags](#schemacache-purge_flexpurgebytags)|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[cache-purge_FlexPurgeByHostnames](#schemacache-purge_flexpurgebyhostnames)|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[cache-purge_FlexPurgeByPrefixes](#schemacache-purge_flexpurgebyprefixes)|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[cache-purge_Everything](#schemacache-purge_everything)|false|none|

|» *anyOf*|body|[cache-purge_SingleFileWithUrlAndHeaders](#schemacache-purge_singlefilewithurlandheaders)|false|none|

```json
  },

```

## Get an Access application

<a id="opIdzone-level-access-applications-get-an-access-application"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/access/apps/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

<h3 id="create-an-access-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|app_id|path|[access_uuid](#schemaaccess_uuid)|true|none|

|body|body|object|true|none|
|» approval_groups|body|[access_approval_groups-2](#schemaaccess_approval_groups-2)|false|Administrators who can approve a temporary authentication request.|
|» approval_required|body|[access_approval_required-2](#schemaaccess_approval_required-2)|false|Requires the user to request access from an administrator at the start of each session.|
|» decision|body|[access_decision-2](#schemaaccess_decision-2)|true|The action Access will take if a user matches this policy.|
|» exclude|body|[access_exclude-3](#schemaaccess_exclude-3)|false|Rules evaluated with a NOT logical operator. To match the policy, a user cannot meet any of the Exclude rules.|
|» include|body|[access_include](#schemaaccess_include)|true|Rules evaluated with an OR logical operator. A user needs to meet only one of the Include rules.|
|» isolation_required|body|[access_isolation_required-2](#schemaaccess_isolation_required-2)|false|Require this application to be served in an isolated browser for users matching this policy.|
|» name|body|[access_name-9](#schemaaccess_name-9)|true|The name of the Access policy.|
|» precedence|body|[access_precedence-2](#schemaaccess_precedence-2)|false|The order of execution for this policy. Must be unique for each policy.|
|» purpose_justification_prompt|body|[access_purpose_justification_prompt](#schemaaccess_purpose_justification_prompt)|false|A custom message that will appear on the purpose justification screen.|
|» purpose_justification_required|body|[access_purpose_justification_required-2](#schemaaccess_purpose_justification_required-2)|false|Require users to enter a justification when they log in to the application.|
|» require|body|[access_require-3](#schemaaccess_require-3)|false|Rules evaluated with an AND logical operator. To match the policy, a user must meet all of the Require rules.|

|---|---|

|» decision|deny|
|» decision|non_identity|
|» decision|bypass|

## Create a service token

<a id="opIdzone-level-access-service-tokens-create-a-service-token"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/access/service_tokens \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "client_secret_version": 1,
    "duration": "60m",
    "enabled": true,
    "name": "CI/CD token",
    "previous_client_secret_expires_at": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z"
  }'
```

`POST /zones/{zone_id}/access/service_tokens`

Generates a new service token. **Note:** This is the only time you can get the Client Secret. If you lose the Client Secret, you will have to create a new service token.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_secret_version": 1,
  "duration": "60m",
  "enabled": true,
  "name": "CI/CD token",
  "previous_client_secret_expires_at": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-service-token-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[access_identifier](#schemaaccess_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» client_secret_version|body|[access_client_secret_version](#schemaaccess_client_secret_version)|false|A version number identifying the current `client_secret` associated with the service token. Incrementing it triggers a rotation; the previous secret will still be accepted until the time indicated by `previous_client_secret_expires_at`. If the service token was reported as leaked, `previous_client_secret_expires_at` is not required, may not be in the future, and the previous secret is discarded immediately.|
|» duration|body|[access_duration-2](#schemaaccess_duration-2)|false|The duration for how long the service token will be valid. Must be in the format `300ms` or `2h45m`, or the special value `forever` for non-expiring tokens. Valid time units are: ns, us (or µs), ms, s, m, h. The default is 1 year in hours (8760h).|
|» enabled|body|[access_enabled](#schemaaccess_enabled)|false|Whether the service token is enabled. A disabled service token cannot be used to authenticate; both its current and previous `client_secret` stop being accepted, but the token itself is preserved and can be re-enabled. A service token reported as leaked is disabled automatically and cannot be re-enabled until its secret is rotated; attempting to do so returns a 409. Defaults to enabled when omitted on create.|
|» name|body|[access_name-17](#schemaaccess_name-17)|true|The name of the service token.|
|» previous_client_secret_expires_at|body|[access_previous_client_secret_expires_at](#schemaaccess_previous_client_secret_expires_at)|false|The expiration of the previous `client_secret`. This can be modified at any point after a rotation. For example, you may extend it further into the future if you need more time to update services with the new secret; or move it into the past to immediately invalidate the previous token in case of compromise. Rotating a service token that was reported as leaked discards the previous secret entirely, so no grace period can be set.|

## Update a service token

<a id="opIdzone-level-access-service-tokens-update-a-service-token"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/access/service_tokens/f174e90a-fafe-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "client_secret_version": 1,
    "duration": "60m",
    "enabled": true,
    "name": "CI/CD token",
    "previous_client_secret_expires_at": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z"
  }'
```

`PUT /zones/{zone_id}/access/service_tokens/{service_token_id}`

Updates a configured service token.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_secret_version": 1,
  "duration": "60m",
  "enabled": true,
  "name": "CI/CD token",
  "previous_client_secret_expires_at": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-service-token-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|service_token_id|path|[access_uuid](#schemaaccess_uuid)|true|none|
|zone_id|path|[access_identifier](#schemaaccess_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» client_secret_version|body|[access_client_secret_version](#schemaaccess_client_secret_version)|false|A version number identifying the current `client_secret` associated with the service token. Incrementing it triggers a rotation; the previous secret will still be accepted until the time indicated by `previous_client_secret_expires_at`. If the service token was reported as leaked, `previous_client_secret_expires_at` is not required, may not be in the future, and the previous secret is discarded immediately.|
|» duration|body|[access_duration-2](#schemaaccess_duration-2)|false|The duration for how long the service token will be valid. Must be in the format `300ms` or `2h45m`, or the special value `forever` for non-expiring tokens. Valid time units are: ns, us (or µs), ms, s, m, h. The default is 1 year in hours (8760h).|
|» enabled|body|[access_enabled](#schemaaccess_enabled)|false|Whether the service token is enabled. A disabled service token cannot be used to authenticate; both its current and previous `client_secret` stop being accepted, but the token itself is preserved and can be re-enabled. A service token reported as leaked is disabled automatically and cannot be re-enabled until its secret is rotated; attempting to do so returns a 409. Defaults to enabled when omitted on create.|
|» name|body|[access_name-17](#schemaaccess_name-17)|false|The name of the service token.|
|» previous_client_secret_expires_at|body|[access_previous_client_secret_expires_at](#schemaaccess_previous_client_secret_expires_at)|false|The expiration of the previous `client_secret`. This can be modified at any point after a rotation. For example, you may extend it further into the future if you need more time to update services with the new secret; or move it into the past to immediately invalidate the previous token in case of compromise. Rotating a service token that was reported as leaked discards the previous secret entirely, so no grace period can be set.|

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-ai-security-for-apps">AI Security for Apps</h1>

## Get the AI Security for Apps custom topics of a zone.

<a id="opIdai-security-custom-topics-get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/ai-security/custom-topics \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /zones/{zone_id}/ai-security/custom-topics`

Get the custom topic categories defined for the zone. While AI Security for Apps is enabled, it scores every incoming prompt against these topics and writes the scores to the `cf.llm.prompt.custom_topic_categories` field, keyed by topic label. Topics can be configured while the detection is disabled, but no prompt is scored until you enable it.

<h3 id="get-the-ai-security-for-apps-custom-topics-of-a-zone-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[waf-product-api-bundle_zone_id](#schemawaf-product-api-bundle_zone_id)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "result": {
    "topics": [
      {
        "label": "credit-cards",
        "topic": "credit card numbers"
      }
    ]
  },
  "success": true
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 13900,
      "message": "internal server error"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

<h3 id="get-the-ai-security-for-apps-custom-topics-of-a-zone-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Get AI Security for Apps custom topics response.|[waf-product-api-bundle_response-custom-topics](#schemawaf-product-api-bundle_response-custom-topics)|
|4XX|Client Error|Get AI Security for Apps custom topics failure response.|Inline|

## Update the AI Security for Apps custom topics of a zone.

<a id="opIdai-security-custom-topics-put"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/ai-security/custom-topics \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "topics": [
      {
        "label": "credit-cards",
        "topic": "credit card numbers"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /zones/{zone_id}/ai-security/custom-topics`

Update the custom topic list of the zone, overwriting it entirely with the topics in the request, so include
every topic you want to keep. Changes can take up to a minute to propagate.

Each entry has a `label`, used to reference the topic in rule expressions and analytics, and a `topic`
description, which the classifier scores prompts against while AI Security for Apps is enabled. The following
rules apply:

- A zone can hold at most 20 topics.
- `label` must be 2–20 characters, using only lowercase letters (a–z), digits (0–9), and hyphens.
- `topic` must be 2–50 UTF-8 bytes. Text in any language is supported, including spaces, numbers,
  punctuation, and symbols. Tabs, line breaks, invalid text, and invisible formatting characters are not allowed.
- Labels must be unique within the zone, and so must topic descriptions.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "topics": [
    {
      "label": "credit-cards",
      "topic": "credit card numbers"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-the-ai-security-for-apps-custom-topics-of-a-zone-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[waf-product-api-bundle_zone_id](#schemawaf-product-api-bundle_zone_id)|true|none|
|body|body|[waf-product-api-bundle_custom-topics](#schemawaf-product-api-bundle_custom-topics)|true|none|
|» topics|body|[[waf-product-api-bundle_custom-topic](#schemawaf-product-api-bundle_custom-topic)]|false|Custom topic categories for AI Security for Apps content detection.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "result": {
    "topics": [
      {
        "label": "credit-cards",
        "topic": "credit card numbers"
      }
    ]
  },
  "success": true
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 13900,
      "message": "internal server error"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

<h3 id="update-the-ai-security-for-apps-custom-topics-of-a-zone-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

|4XX|Client Error|Update AI Security for Apps custom topics failure response.|Inline|

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-tiered-caching">Tiered Caching</h1>

## Get Tiered Caching setting

<a id="opIdtiered-caching-get-tiered-caching-setting"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/argo/tiered_caching \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /zones/{zone_id}/argo/tiered_caching`

Tiered Cache works by dividing Cloudflare's data centers into a hierarchy of lower-tiers and upper-tiers. If content is not cached in lower-tier data centers (generally the ones closest to a visitor), the lower-tier must ask an upper-tier to see if it has the content. If the upper-tier does not have the content, only the upper-tier can ask the origin for content. This practice improves bandwidth efficiency by limiting the number of data centers that can ask the origin for content, which reduces origin load and makes websites more cost-effective to operate. Additionally, Tiered Cache concentrates connections to origin servers so they come from a small number of data centers rather than the full set of network locations. This results in fewer open connections using server resources.

<h3 id="get-tiered-caching-setting-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[cache-settings_identifier](#schemacache-settings_identifier)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "id": "tiered_caching",
    "modified_on": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z",
    "value": "off"
  }
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

`PUT /zones/{zone_id}/bot_management`

Updates the Bot Management configuration for a zone.

This API is used to update:
- **Bot Fight Mode**
- **Super Bot Fight Mode**
- **Bot Management for Enterprise**

See [Bot Plans](https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/plans/) for more information on the different plans
\
If you recently upgraded or downgraded your plan, refer to the following examples to clean up old configurations.
Copy and paste the example body to remove old zone configurations based on your current plan.
#### Clean up configuration for Bot Fight Mode plan
```json
{
  "sbfm_likely_automated": "allow",
  "sbfm_definitely_automated": "allow",
  "sbfm_verified_bots": "allow",
  "sbfm_static_resource_protection": false,
  "optimize_wordpress": false,
  "suppress_session_score": false
}
```
#### Clean up configuration for SBFM Pro plan
```json
{
  "sbfm_likely_automated": "allow",
  "fight_mode": false
}
```
#### Clean up configuration for SBFM Biz plan
```json
{
  "fight_mode": false
}
```
#### Clean up configuration for BM Enterprise Subscription plan
It is strongly recommended that you ensure you have [custom rules](https://developers.cloudflare.com/waf/custom-rules/) in place to protect your zone before disabling the SBFM rules. Without these protections, your zone is vulnerable to attacks.
```json
{
  "sbfm_likely_automated": "allow",
  "sbfm_definitely_automated": "allow",
  "sbfm_verified_bots": "allow",
  "sbfm_static_resource_protection": false,
  "optimize_wordpress": false,
  "fight_mode": false
}
```


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ai_bots_migration_opt_out": false,
  "ai_bots_protection": "block",
  "ai_search": "block",
  "ai_training": "disallow",
  "ai_user": "only_on_ad_pages",
  "bot_preference_sync_enabled": true,
  "cf_robots_variant": "policy_only",
  "content_bots_protection": "disabled",
  "crawler_protection": "enabled",
  "enable_js": true,
  "is_robots_txt_managed": false,
  "jsd_api_results_enabled": true,
  "fight_mode": true
}
```

## Submit a feedback report

<a id="opIdbot-management-zone-feedback-create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/bot_management/feedback \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Automated scraping missed by detections",
    "expression": "http.host eq '\''www.example.com'\'' and http.request.uri.path starts_with '\''/products'\'' and cf.bot_management.score gt 25",
    "first_request_seen_at": "2025-09-29T00:00:00Z",
    "last_request_seen_at": "2025-09-29T06:00:00Z",
    "requests": 2000,
    "requests_by_attribute": {
      "topIPs": [
        {
          "metric": "203.0.113.55",
          "requests": 400
        }
      ],
      "topJA3Hashes": [
        {
          "metric": "ab12cd34ef56...",
          "requests": 900
        }
      ]
    },
    "requests_by_score": {
      "30": 800,
      "40": 700,
      "50": 500
    },
    "requests_by_score_src": {
      "heuristics": 200,
      "ml": 1800
    },
    "subtype": "Scraping",
    "type": "false_negative"
  }'
```

`POST /zones/{zone_id}/bot_management/feedback`

Submit a feedback report for the specified zone. Use `type` to indicate whether the report is a false positive (good traffic flagged as bot) or a false negative (bot traffic missed). Furthermore, you can also use `expression` as a wirefilter to identify the affected traffic sample.

See more accepted API fields and expression types at https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/concepts/feedback-loop/#api-fields and https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/concepts/feedback-loop/#expression-fields, respectively.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Automated scraping missed by detections",
  "expression": "http.host eq 'www.example.com' and http.request.uri.path starts_with '/products' and cf.bot_management.score gt 25",
  "first_request_seen_at": "2025-09-29T00:00:00Z",
  "last_request_seen_at": "2025-09-29T06:00:00Z",
  "requests": 2000,
  "requests_by_attribute": {
    "topIPs": [
      {
        "metric": "203.0.113.55",
        "requests": 400
      }
    ],
    "topJA3Hashes": [
      {
        "metric": "ab12cd34ef56...",
        "requests": 900
      }
    ]
  },
  "requests_by_score": {
    "30": 800,
    "40": 700,
    "50": 500
  },
  "requests_by_score_src": {
    "heuristics": 200,
    "ml": 1800
  },
  "subtype": "Scraping",
  "type": "false_negative"
}
```

<h3 id="submit-a-feedback-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[bot-management_identifier](#schemabot-management_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[bot-management_feedback_report](#schemabot-management_feedback_report)|true|none|
|» description|body|string|true|none|
|» expression|body|string|true|Wirefilter expression describing the traffic being reported.|
|» first_request_seen_at|body|string(date-time)|true|none|
|» last_request_seen_at|body|string(date-time)|true|none|
|» requests|body|integer(int64)|true|none|
|» requests_by_attribute|body|[bot-management_requests_by_attribute](#schemabot-management_requests_by_attribute)|true|Top attributes contributing to the feedback sample. Keys include topASNs, topCountries, topHosts, topIPs, topJA3Hashes, topJA4s, topPaths, topUserAgents.|
|» requests_by_score|body|[bot-management_requests_by_score](#schemabot-management_requests_by_score)|true|Map of bot scores (1-99) to request counts. Sum must equal `requests`.|

`GET /zones/{zone_id}/cache/cache_reserve`

Increase cache lifetimes by automatically storing all cacheable files into Cloudflare's persistent object storage buckets. Requires Cache Reserve subscription. `GET /zones/{zone_id}/cache/cache_reserve_clear`

You can use Cache Reserve Clear to clear your Cache Reserve, but you must first disable Cache Reserve. In most cases, this will be accomplished within 24 hours. You cannot re-enable Cache Reserve while this process is ongoing. Keep in mind that you cannot undo or cancel this operation.

```json
  "messages": [],

    "id": "cache_reserve_clear",
    "start_ts": "2023-10-02T10:00:00.12345Z",
    "state": "Completed"
  },
  "success": true
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 1142,
      "message": "Unable to retrieve cache_reserve_clear setting value. The zone setting does not exist because you never performed a Cache Reserve Clear operation."

}
```

`GET /zones/{zone_id}/cache/variants`

Variant support enables caching variants of images with certain file extensions in addition to the original. This only applies when the origin server sends the 'Vary: Accept' response header. If the origin server sends 'Vary: Accept' but does not serve the variant requested, the response will not be cached. This will be indicated with BYPASS cache status in the response headers.

```json
      ],

        "image/webp",
        "image/jpeg"
      ],

        "image/webp",

      ],

        "image/webp",
```

`GET /zones/{zone_id}/cache/origin_cloud_regions`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Returns all IP-to-cloud-region mappings configured for the zone. Each mapping tells Cloudflare which cloud vendor and region hosts the origin at that IP, enabling the edge to route via the nearest Tiered Cache upper-tier co-located with that cloud provider. Returns an empty array when no mappings exist.

## Create an origin cloud region mapping

<a id="opIdorigin-cloud-regions-create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/cache/origin_cloud_regions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ip": "192.0.2.1",
    "region": "us-east-1",
    "vendor": "aws"
  }'
```

`POST /zones/{zone_id}/cache/origin_cloud_regions`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Adds a single IP-to-cloud-region mapping for the zone. The IP must be a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address and is normalized to canonical form before storage (RFC 5952 for IPv6). Returns 400 (code 1145) if a mapping for that IP already exists — use PATCH to update an existing entry. The vendor and region are validated against the list from `GET /zones/{zone_id}/cache/origin_cloud_regions/supported_regions`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ip": "192.0.2.1",
  "region": "us-east-1",
  "vendor": "aws"
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-origin-cloud-region-mapping-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[cache-settings_identifier](#schemacache-settings_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[cache-settings_origin_cloud_region_request](#schemacache-settings_origin_cloud_region_request)|true|none|
|» ip|body|string|true|Origin IP address (IPv4 or IPv6). Normalized to canonical form before storage (RFC 5952 for IPv6).|
|» region|body|string|true|Cloud vendor region identifier. Must be a valid region for the specified vendor as returned by the supported_regions endpoint.|
|» vendor|body|string|true|Cloud vendor hosting the origin. Must be one of the supported vendors.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» vendor|aws|
|» vendor|azure|
|» vendor|gcp|
|» vendor|oci|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "result": {
    "editable": true,
    "id": "origin_public_cloud_region",
    "modified_on": "2026-03-01T12:00:00Z",
    "value": {
      "modified_on": "2026-03-01T12:00:00Z",
      "origin-ip": "192.0.2.1",
      "region": "us-east-1",
      "vendor": "aws"
    }
  },
  "success": true
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 1145,
      "message": "Unable to create new origin_public_cloud_region setting. The zone setting already exists."
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```


`PATCH /zones/{zone_id}/cache/origin_cloud_regions`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Adds or updates a single IP-to-cloud-region mapping for the zone. Unlike POST, this operation is idempotent — if a mapping for the IP already exists it is overwritten. Returns the complete updated list of all mappings for the zone. Returns 403 (code 1164) when the zone has reached the limit of 3,500 IP mappings.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ip": "2001:db8::1",
  "region": "us-central1",
  "vendor": "gcp"
}
```

|body|body|[cache-settings_origin_cloud_region_request](#schemacache-settings_origin_cloud_region_request)|true|none|
|» ip|body|string|true|Origin IP address (IPv4 or IPv6). Normalized to canonical form before storage (RFC 5952 for IPv6).|
|» region|body|string|true|Cloud vendor region identifier. Must be a valid region for the specified vendor as returned by the supported_regions endpoint.|
|» vendor|body|string|true|Cloud vendor hosting the origin. Must be one of the supported vendors.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» vendor|aws|
|» vendor|azure|
|» vendor|gcp|
|» vendor|oci|

## Batch create or replace origin cloud region mappings

<a id="opIdorigin-cloud-regions-v2-batch-upsert"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/origin/cloud_regions/batch \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '[
    {
      "origin_ip": "192.0.2.1",
      "region": "us-east-1",
      "vendor": "aws"
    },
    {
      "origin_ip": "2001:db8::1",
      "region": "us-central1",
      "vendor": "gcp"
    }
  ]'
```

`PUT /zones/{zone_id}/origin/cloud_regions/batch`

Upserts up to 100 IP-to-cloud-region mappings in a single request. Items in the request body are created or replaced; mappings not included in the request body are preserved unchanged (this is a merge operation, not a full collection replacement). Each item is validated independently — valid items are applied and invalid items are returned in the `failed` array. The vendor and region for every item are validated against the list from `GET /zones/{zone_id}/origin/cloud_regions/supported_regions`.

> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "origin_ip": "192.0.2.1",
    "region": "us-east-1",
    "vendor": "aws"
  },
  {
    "origin_ip": "2001:db8::1",
    "region": "us-central1",
    "vendor": "gcp"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="batch-create-or-replace-origin-cloud-region-mappings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[cache-settings_identifier](#schemacache-settings_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[[cache-settings_origin_cloud_region_v2_request](#schemacache-settings_origin_cloud_region_v2_request)]|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "result": {
    "failed": [],
    "succeeded": [
      {
        "origin_ip": "192.0.2.1",
        "region": "us-east-1",
        "vendor": "aws"
      },
      {
        "origin_ip": "2001:db8::1",
        "region": "us-central1",
        "vendor": "gcp"
      }
    ]
  },
  "success": true
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 1164,
      "message": "Maximum number of IP mappings configured for zone."
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

## Create or replace an origin cloud region mapping

<a id="opIdorigin-cloud-regions-v2-upsert"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/origin/cloud_regions/192.0.2.1 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "origin_ip": "192.0.2.1",
    "region": "us-east-1",
    "vendor": "aws"
  }'
```

`PUT /zones/{zone_id}/origin/cloud_regions/{origin_ip}`

Creates a new IP-to-cloud-region mapping or replaces the existing mapping for the specified IP. PUT is idempotent — calling it repeatedly with the same body produces the same result. The IP path parameter is normalized to canonical form (RFC 5952 for IPv6) before storage. The vendor and region are validated against the list from `GET /zones/{zone_id}/origin/cloud_regions/supported_regions`. Returns 400 if the `origin_ip` in the body does not match the URL path parameter. Returns 403 (code 1164) when the zone has reached the limit of 3,500 IP mappings.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "origin_ip": "192.0.2.1",
  "region": "us-east-1",
  "vendor": "aws"
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-replace-an-origin-cloud-region-mapping-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[cache-settings_identifier](#schemacache-settings_identifier)|true|none|
|origin_ip|path|string|true|Origin IP address to create or replace.|
|body|body|[cache-settings_origin_cloud_region_v2_request](#schemacache-settings_origin_cloud_region_v2_request)|true|none|
|» origin_ip|body|string|true|Origin IP address (IPv4 or IPv6). For the single PUT endpoint (`PUT /origin/cloud_regions/{origin_ip}`), this field must match the path parameter or the request will be rejected with a 400 error. For the batch PUT endpoint, this field identifies which mapping to upsert.|
|» region|body|string|true|Cloud vendor region identifier. Must be a valid region for the specified vendor as returned by the supported_regions endpoint.|
|» vendor|body|string|true|Cloud vendor hosting the origin. Must be one of the supported vendors.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» vendor|aws|
|» vendor|azure|
|» vendor|gcp|
|» vendor|oci|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "result": {
    "modified_on": "2026-03-01T12:00:00Z",
    "origin_ip": "192.0.2.1",
    "region": "us-east-1",
    "vendor": "aws"
  },
  "success": true
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 1157,
      "message": "The vendor provided doesn't exist or the region provided does not exist for the specified cloud vendor"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

## Get Origin Post-Quantum Encryption setting

<a id="opIdzone-cache-settings-get-origin-post-quantum-encryption-setting"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/cache/origin_post_quantum_encryption \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /zones/{zone_id}/cache/origin_post_quantum_encryption`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Instructs Cloudflare to use Post-Quantum (PQ) key agreement algorithms when connecting to your origin. Preferred instructs Cloudflare to opportunistically send a Post-Quantum keyshare in the first message to the origin (for fastest connections when the origin supports and prefers PQ), supported means that PQ algorithms are advertised but only used when requested by the origin, and off means that PQ algorithms are not advertised.

|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[cache-settings_identifier](#schemacache-settings_identifier)|true|none|

```json
  "messages": [],

  "result": {
    "id": "origin_pqe",
    "modified_on": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z",
    "value": "supported"
  }
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-smart-tiered-cache">Smart Tiered Cache</h1>

## Get Smart Tiered Cache setting

<a id="opIdsmart-tiered-cache-get-smart-tiered-cache-setting"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/cache/tiered_cache_smart_topology_enable \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /zones/{zone_id}/cache/tiered_cache_smart_topology_enable`

Smart Tiered Cache dynamically selects the single closest upper tier for each of your website’s origins with no configuration required, using our in-house performance and routing data. Cloudflare collects latency data for each request to an origin, and uses the latency data to determine how well any upper-tier data center is connected with an origin. As a result, Cloudflare can select the data center with the lowest latency to be the upper-tier for an origin.

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/cache/tiered_cache_smart_topology_enable \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "value": "on"
  }'
```

`PATCH /zones/{zone_id}/cache/tiered_cache_smart_topology_enable`

Smart Tiered Cache dynamically selects the single closest upper tier for each of your website’s origins with no configuration required, using our in-house performance and routing data. Cloudflare collects latency data for each request to an origin, and uses the latency data to determine how well any upper-tier data center is connected with an origin. As a result, Cloudflare can select the data center with the lowest latency to be the upper-tier for an origin.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "value": "on"
}
```

<h3 id="patch-smart-tiered-cache-setting-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[cache-settings_identifier](#schemacache-settings_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[cache-settings_smart_tiered_cache_patch](#schemacache-settings_smart_tiered_cache_patch)|true|none|
|» value|body|string|true|Enable or disable the Smart Tiered Cache.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» value|on|
|» value|off|

## Create Content Scanning custom expressions for a zone.

<a id="opIdwaf-content-scanning-add-custom-scan-expressions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/content-upload-scan/payloads \
  -X POST \

    }
  ]'
```

`POST /zones/{zone_id}/content-upload-scan/payloads`

Create one or more Content Scanning custom expressions, appending them to the existing list of the zone, and return the updated list. Each expression reaches content objects the scanner cannot find automatically, for example `lookup_json_string(http.request.body.raw, "file")`.

> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "payload": "lookup_json_string(http.request.body.raw, \"file\")"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="create-content-scanning-custom-expressions-for-a-zone-parameters">Parameters</h3>

## Update CT Alerting Subscription

<a id="opIdct-alerting-update-subscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/ct/alerting \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "emails": [
      "security@example.com",
      "admin@example.com"
    ],
    "enabled": true
  }'
```

`PATCH /zones/{zone_id}/ct/alerting`

Create or update the Certificate Transparency alerting subscription for a zone. Enables or disables email notifications when certificates are issued for the zone's domains.
The `enabled` field is required on every request and controls whether the subscription is active. The `emails` field is optional and, when provided, replaces the stored recipient list for the zone. When `emails` is omitted, the stored recipient list is preserved and only the enabled state is toggled. A maximum of 100 email addresses may be configured per zone.
Requests that omit `enabled` are rejected with error code 1008.
Subscribe and unsubscribe notification emails are only sent for recipients whose effective subscription state changes. Idempotent requests (no state change) send no notification email.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "emails": [
    "security@example.com",
    "admin@example.com"
  ],
  "enabled": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-ct-alerting-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_ct_alerting_subscription_update](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_ct_alerting_subscription_update)|true|none|
|» emails|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_ct_alerting_emails](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_ct_alerting_emails)|false|Email addresses that receive CT alert notifications for the zone. A maximum of 100 addresses may be configured. Each address must be a valid RFC 5322 email address and must not contain a comma.<br>|
|» enabled|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_ct_alerting_enabled](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_ct_alerting_enabled)|true|Whether CT alerting is enabled for the zone.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "emails": [
      "security@example.com",
      "admin@example.com"
    ],
    "enabled": true
  }
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "success": false,
  "result": null
}
```

<h3 id="update-ct-alerting-subscription-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Update CT Alerting Subscription response.|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_ct_alerting_subscription_response_single](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_ct_alerting_subscription_response_single)|

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /zones/{zone_id}/custom_certificates`

List, search, and filter all of your custom SSL certificates. The higher priority will break ties across overlapping 'legacy_custom' certificates, but 'legacy_custom' certificates will always supercede 'sni_custom' certificates.

<h3 id="list-ssl-configurations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier)|true|none|
|page|query|number|false|none|
|per_page|query|number|false|none|
|match|query|string|false|none|
|status|query|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|match|any|
|match|all|
|status|active|
|status|expired|
|status|deleted|
|status|pending|
|status|initializing|
