<h3 id="create-ssl-configuration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» bundle_method|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_bundle_method](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_bundle_method)|false|A ubiquitous bundle has the highest probability of being verified everywhere, even by clients using outdated or unusual trust stores. An optimal bundle uses the shortest chain and newest intermediates. And the force bundle verifies the chain, but does not otherwise modify it.|
|» certificate|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_certificate](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_certificate)|true|The zone's SSL certificate or certificate and the intermediate(s).|
|» custom_csr_id|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_csr_id](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_csr_id)|false|The identifier for the Custom CSR that was used.|
|» deploy|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_deploy](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_deploy)|false|The environment to deploy the certificate to, defaults to production.|
|» geo_restrictions|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_geo_restrictions](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_geo_restrictions)|false|Specify the region where your private key can be held locally for optimal TLS performance. HTTPS connections to any excluded data center will still be fully encrypted, but will incur some latency while Keyless SSL is used to complete the handshake with the nearest allowed data center. Options allow distribution to only to U.S. data centers, only to E.U. data centers, or only to highest security data centers. Default distribution is to all Cloudflare datacenters, for optimal performance.|
|» policy|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_policy](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_policy)|false|Specify the policy that determines the region where your private key will be held locally. HTTPS connections to any excluded data center will still be fully encrypted, but will incur some latency while Keyless SSL is used to complete the handshake with the nearest allowed data center. Any combination of countries, specified by their two letter country code (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2#Officially_assigned_code_elements) can be chosen, such as 'country: IN', as well as 'region: EU' which refers to the EU region. If there are too few data centers satisfying the policy, it will be rejected.<br>Note: The API accepts this field as either "policy" or "policy_restrictions" in requests. Responses return this field as "policy_restrictions".|
|» private_key|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_private_key](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_private_key)|false|The zone's private key. Not required if custom_csr_id is provided, in which case the private key is retrieved from the CSR record held by Cloudflare.|
|» type|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_type](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_type)|false|The type 'legacy_custom' enables support for legacy clients which do not include SNI in the TLS handshake.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» bundle_method|ubiquitous|
|» bundle_method|optimal|
|» bundle_method|force|
|» deploy|staging|
|» deploy|production|
|» type|legacy_custom|
|» type|sni_custom|

## Re-prioritize SSL Certificates

<a id="opIdcustom-ssl-for-a-zone-re-prioritize-ssl-certificates"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/custom_certificates/prioritize \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "certificates": [
      {
        "id": "5a7805061c76ada191ed06f989cc3dac",
        "priority": 2
      },
      {
        "id": "9a7806061c88ada191ed06f989cc3dac",
        "priority": 1
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /zones/{zone_id}/custom_certificates/prioritize`

If a zone has multiple SSL certificates, you can set the order in which they should be used during a request. The higher priority will break ties across overlapping 'legacy_custom' certificates.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "certificates": [
    {
      "id": "5a7805061c76ada191ed06f989cc3dac",
      "priority": 2
    },
    {
      "id": "9a7806061c88ada191ed06f989cc3dac",
      "priority": 1
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="re-prioritize-ssl-certificates-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» certificates|body|[object]|true|Array of ordered certificates.|
|» » priority|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_priority](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_priority)|false|The order/priority in which the certificate will be used in a request. The higher priority will break ties across overlapping 'legacy_custom' certificates, but 'legacy_custom' certificates will always supercede 'sni_custom' certificates.|

<h3 id="edit-ssl-configuration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|custom_certificate_id|path|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_certificate_identifier](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_certificate_identifier)|true|none|
|zone_id|path|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» bundle_method|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_bundle_method](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_bundle_method)|false|A ubiquitous bundle has the highest probability of being verified everywhere, even by clients using outdated or unusual trust stores. An optimal bundle uses the shortest chain and newest intermediates. And the force bundle verifies the chain, but does not otherwise modify it.|
|» certificate|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_certificate](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_certificate)|false|The zone's SSL certificate or certificate and the intermediate(s).|
|» custom_csr_id|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_csr_id](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_csr_id)|false|The identifier for the Custom CSR that was used.|
|» deploy|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_deploy](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_deploy)|false|The environment to deploy the certificate to, defaults to production.|
|» geo_restrictions|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_geo_restrictions](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_geo_restrictions)|false|Specify the region where your private key can be held locally for optimal TLS performance. HTTPS connections to any excluded data center will still be fully encrypted, but will incur some latency while Keyless SSL is used to complete the handshake with the nearest allowed data center. Options allow distribution to only to U.S. data centers, only to E.U. data centers, or only to highest security data centers. Default distribution is to all Cloudflare datacenters, for optimal performance.|
|» policy|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_policy](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_policy)|false|Specify the policy that determines the region where your private key will be held locally. HTTPS connections to any excluded data center will still be fully encrypted, but will incur some latency while Keyless SSL is used to complete the handshake with the nearest allowed data center. Any combination of countries, specified by their two letter country code (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2#Officially_assigned_code_elements) can be chosen, such as 'country: IN', as well as 'region: EU' which refers to the EU region. If there are too few data centers satisfying the policy, it will be rejected.<br>Note: The API accepts this field as either "policy" or "policy_restrictions" in requests. Responses return this field as "policy_restrictions".|
|» private_key|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_private_key](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_private_key)|false|The zone's private key. Not required if custom_csr_id is provided, in which case the private key is retrieved from the CSR record held by Cloudflare.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» bundle_method|ubiquitous|
|» bundle_method|optimal|
|» bundle_method|force|
|» deploy|staging|
|» deploy|production|

## Create Custom CSR

<a id="opIdcustom-csrs-for-a-zone-create-custom-csr"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/custom_csrs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "common_name": "example.com",
    "country": "US",
    "key_type": "rsa2048",
    "locality": "San Francisco",
    "organization": "Cloudflare, Inc.",
    "organizational_unit": "Engineering",
    "sans": [
      "example.com",
      "www.example.com"
    ],
    "state": "California"
  }'
```

`POST /zones/{zone_id}/custom_csrs`

Generate a new custom Certificate Signing Request (CSR) for a zone. Cloudflare generates and securely stores the private key associated with the CSR. The CSR can then be provided to a Certificate Authority for signing. Once signed, the certificate is uploaded via the Custom SSL endpoint using the CSR ID.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "common_name": "example.com",
  "country": "US",
  "key_type": "rsa2048",
  "locality": "San Francisco",
  "organization": "Cloudflare, Inc.",
  "organizational_unit": "Engineering",
  "sans": [
    "example.com",
    "www.example.com"
  ],
  "state": "California"
}
```

<h3 id="create-custom-csr-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_csr_create_request](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_csr_create_request)|true|none|
|» common_name|body|string|true|The common name (domain) for the CSR. Must be at most 64 characters.|
|» country|body|string|true|Two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.|

|» organization|body|string|true|Organization name.|
|» organizational_unit|body|string|false|Organizational unit name.|
|» sans|body|[string]|true|Subject Alternative Names for the CSR. At least one SAN is required. The list should include the common name.|
|» state|body|string|true|State or province name.|

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
```

`DELETE /zones/{zone_id}/custom_csrs/{custom_csr_id}`

Delete a custom Certificate Signing Request (CSR) and its associated private key. A CSR cannot be deleted if any custom certificates still reference it.

`POST /zones/{zone_id}/custom_hostnames`

Add a new custom hostname and request that an SSL certificate be issued for it. One of three validation methods—http, txt, email—should be used, with 'http' recommended if the CNAME is already in place (or will be soon). Specifying 'email' will send an email to the WHOIS contacts on file for the base domain plus hostmaster, postmaster, webmaster, admin, administrator. If http is used and the domain is not already pointing to the Managed CNAME host, the PATCH method must be used once it is (to complete validation).  Enable bundling of certificates using the custom_cert_bundle field. The bundling process requires the following condition One certificate in the bundle must use an RSA, and the other must use an ECDSA.

<h3 id="create-custom-hostname-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» custom_metadata|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_metadata](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_metadata)|false|Unique key/value metadata for this hostname. These are per-hostname (customer) settings.|
|» custom_origin_server|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_origin_server](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_origin_server)|false|a valid hostname that’s been added to your DNS zone as an A, AAAA, or CNAME record.|
|» custom_origin_sni|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_origin_sni](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_origin_sni)|false|A hostname that will be sent to your custom origin server as SNI for TLS handshake. This can be a valid subdomain of the zone or custom origin server name or the string ':request_host_header:' which will cause the host header in the request to be used as SNI. Not configurable with default/fallback origin server.|
|» hostname|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_hostname_post](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_hostname_post)|true|The custom hostname that will point to your hostname via CNAME.|
|» ssl|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_sslpost](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_sslpost)|false|SSL properties used when creating the custom hostname.|

## Get Custom Hostname Quota

<a id="opIdcustom-hostname-for-a-zone-get-custom-hostname-quota"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/custom_hostnames/quota \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /zones/{zone_id}/custom_hostnames/quota`

Returns custom hostname quota usage for a zone. The allocated quota is a soft limit; creating custom hostnames after usage exceeds this limit can still succeed until the hard cap is reached. Use the exceeded and hard_cap fields to track when usage is above the soft limit and when new custom hostname creation will be rejected.

<h3 id="get-custom-hostname-quota-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "allocated": 100,
    "exceeded": false,
    "hard_cap": 200,
    "used": 50
  }
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": {},
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

<h3 id="get-custom-hostname-quota-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Get Custom Hostname Quota response|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_hostname_quota_response](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_hostname_quota_response)|
|4XX|Client Error|Get Custom Hostname Quota response failure|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_hostname_api_response_failure](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_hostname_api_response_failure)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
api_token, api_email & api_key
</aside>

## Custom Hostname Details

<a id="opIdcustom-hostname-for-a-zone-custom-hostname-details"></a>

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /zones/{zone_id}/custom_hostnames/{custom_hostname_id}`

Retrieves detailed information about a specific custom hostname, including SSL certificate status, ownership verification, and origin configuration.

## Delete Custom Hostname (and any issued SSL certificates)

<a id="opIdcustom-hostname-for-a-zone-delete-custom-hostname-(-and-any-issued-ssl-certificates)"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/custom_hostnames/0d89c70d-ad9f-4843-b99f-6cc0252067e9 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /zones/{zone_id}/custom_hostnames/{custom_hostname_id}`

Permanently deletes a custom hostname and revokes any SSL certificates that were issued for it. This action cannot be undone.

<h3 id="delete-custom-hostname-and-any-issued-ssl-certificates-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|custom_hostname_id|path|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_hostname_identifier](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_hostname_identifier)|true|none|
|zone_id|path|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier)|true|none|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "id": "0d89c70d-ad9f-4843-b99f-6cc0252067e9"
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json

  "id": "0d89c70d-ad9f-4843-b99f-6cc0252067e9",
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
api_token, api_email & api_key
</aside>

`PATCH /zones/{zone_id}/custom_hostnames/{custom_hostname_id}`

Modify SSL configuration for a custom hostname. When sent with SSL config that matches existing config, used to indicate that hostname should pass domain control validation (DCV). Can also be used to change validation type, e.g., from 'http' to 'email'. Bundle an existing certificate with another certificate by using the "custom_cert_bundle" field. The bundling process supports combining certificates as long as the following condition is met. One certificate must use the RSA algorithm, and the other must use the ECDSA algorithm.

```json
  "custom_metadata": {
```

<h3 id="edit-custom-hostname-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|custom_hostname_id|path|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_hostname_identifier](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_hostname_identifier)|true|none|
|zone_id|path|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» custom_metadata|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_metadata](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_metadata)|false|Unique key/value metadata for this hostname. These are per-hostname (customer) settings.|
|» custom_origin_server|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_origin_server](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_origin_server)|false|a valid hostname that’s been added to your DNS zone as an A, AAAA, or CNAME record.|
|» custom_origin_sni|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_origin_sni](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_origin_sni)|false|A hostname that will be sent to your custom origin server as SNI for TLS handshake. This can be a valid subdomain of the zone or custom origin server name or the string ':request_host_header:' which will cause the host header in the request to be used as SNI. Not configurable with default/fallback origin server.|
|» ssl|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_sslpost](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_sslpost)|false|SSL properties used when creating the custom hostname.|

## Replace Custom Certificate and Custom Key In Custom Hostname

<a id="opIdcustom-hostname-for-a-zone-edit-custom-certificate-custom-hostname"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/custom_hostnames/0d89c70d-ad9f-4843-b99f-6cc0252067e9/certificate_pack/0d89c70d-ad9f-4843-b99f-6cc0252067e9/certificates/0d89c70d-ad9f-4843-b99f-6cc0252067e9 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "custom_certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIDdjCCAl6gAwIBAgIJAPnMg0Fs+/B0MA0GCSqGSIb3DQEBCwUAMFsx...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----\n",
    "custom_key": "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\nMIIEvQIBADANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAASCBKcwggSjAgEAAoIBAQC/SCB5...\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----\n"
  }'
```

`PUT /zones/{zone_id}/custom_hostnames/{custom_hostname_id}/certificate_pack/{certificate_pack_id}/certificates/{certificate_id}`

Replace a single custom certificate within a certificate pack that contains two bundled certificates. The replacement must adhere to the following constraints. You can only replace an RSA certificate with another RSA certificate or an ECDSA certificate with another ECDSA certificate.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "custom_certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIDdjCCAl6gAwIBAgIJAPnMg0Fs+/B0MA0GCSqGSIb3DQEBCwUAMFsx...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----\n",
  "custom_key": "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\nMIIEvQIBADANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAASCBKcwggSjAgEAAoIBAQC/SCB5...\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----\n"
}
```

<h3 id="replace-custom-certificate-and-custom-key-in-custom-hostname-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|custom_hostname_id|path|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_hostname_identifier](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_hostname_identifier)|true|none|
|certificate_pack_id|path|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_hostname_identifier](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_hostname_identifier)|true|none|
|certificate_id|path|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_hostname_identifier](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_hostname_identifier)|true|none|
|zone_id|path|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_cert_and_key](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_cert_and_key)|true|none|
|» custom_certificate|body|string|true|If a custom uploaded certificate is used.|
|» custom_key|body|string|true|The key for a custom uploaded certificate.|

## Delete Single Certificate And Key For Custom Hostname

<a id="opIdcustom-hostname-for-a-zone-delete_single_certificate_and_key_in_a_custom_hostname"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/custom_hostnames/0d89c70d-ad9f-4843-b99f-6cc0252067e9/certificate_pack/0d89c70d-ad9f-4843-b99f-6cc0252067e9/certificates/0d89c70d-ad9f-4843-b99f-6cc0252067e9 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /zones/{zone_id}/custom_hostnames/{custom_hostname_id}/certificate_pack/{certificate_pack_id}/certificates/{certificate_id}`

Delete a single custom certificate from a certificate pack that contains two bundled certificates. Deletion is subject to the following constraints. You cannot delete a certificate if it is the only remaining certificate in the pack. At least one certificate must remain in the pack.

`POST /zones/{zone_id}/custom_pages/preview_tokens`

Creates a signed JWT for previewing a zone-level custom page before it is published.

> Body parameter

```json
  "act": "preview",
  "target": "block:waf",
  "url": "https://example.com/error.html"
```

|body|body|[custom-pages_preview_request](#schemacustom-pages_preview_request)|true|none|
|» act|body|string|true|The preview action type. Required for request parsing but not used in token generation. Typically set to "preview".|
|» target|body|string|true|The target custom page type to preview (e.g. "block:waf"). Encoded as the "endpoint" claim in the resulting JWT.|

```json
      "ipv6_only": true
    },
    "tags": [],
```

```bash
    "content": "198.51.100.4",
    "private_routing": true,
    "type": "A"
  }'
```

`POST /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records`

Create a new DNS record for a zone.

Notes:
- A/AAAA records cannot exist on the same name as CNAME records.
- NS records cannot exist on the same name as any other record type.
- Domain names are always represented in Punycode, even if Unicode
  characters were used when creating the record.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comment": "Domain verification record",
  "name": "example.com",
  "proxied": true,

    "ipv4_only": true,

  },
  "tags": [],
  "ttl": 3600,

  "private_routing": true,

}
```

`POST /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records/batch`

Send a Batch of DNS Record API calls to be executed together.

Notes:
- Although Cloudflare will execute the batched operations in a single database transaction, Cloudflare's distributed KV store must treat each record change as a single key-value pair. This means that the propagation of changes is not atomic. See [the documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/how-to/batch-record-changes/ "Batch DNS records") for more information.
- The operations you specify within the /batch request body are always executed in the following order:

    - Deletes
    - Patches
    - Puts
    - Posts


> Body parameter

```json

  "deletes": [
    {
      "id": "023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353"
    }
  ],
```

## Import DNS Records

<a id="opIddns-records-for-a-zone-import-dns-records"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/dns_records/import \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'file=www.example.com. 300 IN  A 127.0.0.1' \
  -F 'proxied=true'
```

`POST /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records/import`

You can upload your [BIND config](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zone_file "Zone file") through this endpoint. It assumes that cURL is called from a location with bind_config.txt (valid BIND config) present.

See [the documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/how-to/import-and-export/ "Import and export records") for more information.

> Body parameter

```yaml
file: www.example.com. 300 IN  A 127.0.0.1
proxied: "true"
```

|body|body|object|true|none|
|» file|body|string|true|BIND config to import.<br><br>**Tip:** When using cURL, a file can be uploaded using `--form 'file=@bind_config.txt'`.<br>|
|» proxied|body|string|false|Whether or not proxiable records should receive the performance and security benefits of Cloudflare.<br><br>The value should be either `true` or `false`.|

`POST /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records/scan/trigger`

## Overwrite DNS Record

<a id="opIddns-records-for-a-zone-update-dns-record"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/dns_records/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "comment": "Domain verification record",
    "name": "example.com",
    "proxied": true,
    "settings": {
      "ipv4_only": true,
      "ipv6_only": true
    },
    "tags": [],
    "ttl": 3600,
    "content": "198.51.100.4",
    "private_routing": true,
    "type": "A"
  }'
```

`PUT /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records/{dns_record_id}`

Overwrite an existing DNS record.

Notes:
- A/AAAA records cannot exist on the same name as CNAME records.
- NS records cannot exist on the same name as any other record type.
- Domain names are always represented in Punycode, even if Unicode
  characters were used when creating the record.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comment": "Domain verification record",
  "name": "example.com",
  "proxied": true,
  "settings": {
    "ipv4_only": true,
    "ipv6_only": true
  },
  "tags": [],
  "ttl": 3600,
  "content": "198.51.100.4",
  "private_routing": true,
  "type": "A"
}
```

`PATCH /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records/{dns_record_id}`

Update an existing DNS record.

Notes:
- A/AAAA records cannot exist on the same name as CNAME records.
- NS records cannot exist on the same name as any other record type.
- Domain names are always represented in Punycode, even if Unicode
  characters were used when creating the record.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comment": "Domain verification record",
  "name": "example.com",
  "proxied": true,
  "settings": {
    "ipv4_only": true,
    "ipv6_only": true
  },
  "tags": [],
  "ttl": 3600,

}
```

## Edit DNSSEC Status

<a id="opIddnssec-edit-dnssec-status"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/dnssec \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "dnssec_multi_signer": false,
    "dnssec_presigned": true,
    "dnssec_use_nsec3": false,
    "status": "active"
  }'
```

`PATCH /zones/{zone_id}/dnssec`

Enable or disable DNSSEC.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "dnssec_multi_signer": false,
  "dnssec_presigned": true,
  "dnssec_use_nsec3": false,
  "status": "active"
}
```

<h3 id="edit-dnssec-status-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[dnssec_identifier](#schemadnssec_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» dnssec_multi_signer|body|[dnssec_dnssec_multi_signer](#schemadnssec_dnssec_multi_signer)|false|If true, multi-signer DNSSEC is enabled on the zone, allowing multiple<br>providers to serve a DNSSEC-signed zone at the same time.<br>This is required for DNSKEY records (except those automatically<br>generated by Cloudflare) to be added to the zone.<br><br>See [Multi-signer DNSSEC](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/dnssec/multi-signer-dnssec/) for details.|
|» dnssec_presigned|body|[dnssec_dnssec_presigned](#schemadnssec_dnssec_presigned)|false|If true, allows Cloudflare to transfer in a DNSSEC-signed zone<br>including signatures from an external provider, without requiring<br>Cloudflare to sign any records on the fly.<br><br>Note that this feature has some limitations.<br>See [Cloudflare as Secondary](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/zone-transfers/cloudflare-as-secondary/setup/#dnssec) for details.|
|» dnssec_use_nsec3|body|[dnssec_dnssec_use_nsec3](#schemadnssec_dnssec_use_nsec3)|false|If true, enables the use of NSEC3 together with DNSSEC on the zone.<br>Combined with setting dnssec_presigned to true, this enables the use of<br>NSEC3 records when transferring in from an external provider.<br>If dnssec_presigned is instead set to false (default), NSEC3 records will be<br>generated and signed at request time.<br><br>See [DNSSEC with NSEC3](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/dnssec/enable-nsec3/) for details.|
|» status|body|string|false|Status of DNSSEC, based on user-desired state and presence of necessary records.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|active|
|» status|disabled|

> Example responses

> 200 Response


## Configure DMARC Reports

<a id="opIdconfigure_dmarc_reports"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/email/auth/dmarc-reports \
```

`PATCH /zones/{zone_id}/email/auth/dmarc-reports`

Updates the DMARC report configuration for a zone.
At least one of `enabled` or `skip_wizard` must be provided.
When enabling, the handler will ensure the DMARC RUA record exists in DNS.

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "skip_wizard": false
}
```

|body|body|[email-auth_ConfigureDmarcReportsRequest](#schemaemail-auth_configuredmarcreportsrequest)|true|none|

## Inspect SPF Record

<a id="opIdinspect_spf"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/email/auth/spf/inspect?id=e5bb46707a802688812d5d1c9f7977d4' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /zones/{zone_id}/email/auth/spf/inspect`

Inspects a specific SPF TXT record and returns a parsed tree structure
in the spflimit-worker format.

The record ID must be provided via the `id` query parameter.

Returns a recursive tree showing:
- Parsed components with their qualifiers and types
- Nested includes recursively resolved within components
- Per-component and total lookup counts
- Detailed error information with context


<h3 id="inspect-spf-record-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[email-auth_identifier](#schemaemail-auth_identifier)|true|Zone identifier.|
|id|query|string|true|DNS record ID (rec_tag) to inspect|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{

  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "components": [

    ],

    "errors": [],
    "record": "v=spf1 ip4:203.0.113.1 include:spf.example.com -all",
    "total_lookups": 2
  }
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

<h3 id="inspect-spf-record-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|messages|[email-auth_messages](#schemaemail-auth_messages)|true|none|none|
|success|boolean|true|none|Whether the API call was successful.|
|result|[email-auth_SpfTree](#schemaemail-auth_spftree)|false|none|Recursive SPF inspection tree<br>|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|success|true|

## Create a sending subdomain

<a id="opIdemail-sending-subdomains-create-sending-subdomain"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/email/sending/subdomains \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "sub.example.com"
  }'
```

`POST /zones/{zone_id}/email/sending/subdomains`

Creates a new sending subdomain or re-enables sending on an existing subdomain that had it disabled. If zone-level Email Sending has not been enabled yet, the zone flag is automatically set when the entitlement is present. A leftmost wildcard such as `*.example.com` is accepted only for accounts with wildcard Email Sending enabled. Wildcard senders share the base domain's DKIM signing identity and `cf-bounce.<base>` return path.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "sub.example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-sending-subdomain-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[email_identifier](#schemaemail_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[email_create_sending_subdomain_properties](#schemaemail_create_sending_subdomain_properties)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The domain name within the zone. A wildcard is allowed only as the complete leftmost label (`*.example.com`) and requires the account wildcard Email Sending entitlement. The derived Return-Path hostname, including its bounce prefix, must be at most 201 characters after ASCII conversion; wildcards use the base hostname.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "created": "2014-01-02T02:20:00Z",
    "dkim_selector": "cf-bounce",
    "drop_suppressed_recipients": false,
    "enabled": true,
    "modified": "2014-01-02T02:20:00Z",
    "name": "sub.example.com",
    "preview_enabled": true,
    "return_path_domain": "cf-bounce.sub.example.com",
    "tag": "aabbccdd11223344aabbccdd11223344"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-sending-subdomain-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Create a sending subdomain response|[email_sending_subdomain_response_single](#schemaemail_sending_subdomain_response_single)|
|403|Forbidden|Error 2067: Wildcard Email Sending is not enabled for this account.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
api_token, api_email & api_key
</aside>

## Preview sending subdomain DNS

<a id="opIdemail-sending-subdomains-preview-sending-subdomain"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

  -d '{
    "name": "sub.example.com"
  }'
```

`POST /zones/{zone_id}/email/sending/subdomains/preview`

Returns the DNS records that would be created for a sending subdomain, flags which records are missing, and reports any conflicts with existing DNS records. This is a read-only dry-run — no records are created or modified. Use before or after creating a subdomain to check DNS status. A leftmost wildcard requires wildcard Email Sending to be enabled for the account and previews base-scoped DKIM and return-path records.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "sub.example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="preview-sending-subdomain-dns-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|» name|body|string|true|The domain name within the zone. A wildcard is allowed only as the complete leftmost label (`*.example.com`) and requires the account wildcard Email Sending entitlement. The derived Return-Path hostname, including its bounce prefix, must be at most 201 characters after ASCII conversion; wildcards use the base hostname.|

```json
        "ttl": 1,
        "type": "NS"
      }

}
```

`POST /zones/{zone_id}/email/sending/subdomains/{subdomain_id}/dns`

```json
          "ttl": 1,
```

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/filters \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '[
    {
      "description": "Restrict access from these browsers on this address range.",
      "expression": "(http.request.uri.path ~ \".*wp-login.php\" or http.request.uri.path ~ \".*xmlrpc.php\") and ip.addr ne 172.16.22.155",
      "paused": false,
      "ref": "FIL-100"
    }
  ]'
```

## Delete an IP Access rule

<a id="opIdip-access-rules-for-a-zone-delete-an-ip-access-rule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/firewall/access_rules/rules/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353 \

  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "cascade": "none"
  }'
```

`DELETE /zones/{zone_id}/firewall/access_rules/rules/{rule_id}`

Deletes an IP Access rule defined at the zone level.

Optionally, you can use the `cascade` property to specify that you wish to delete similar rules in other zones managed by the same zone owner.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "cascade": "none"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-an-ip-access-rule-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[firewall_identifier](#schemafirewall_identifier)|true|none|
|rule_id|path|[firewall_rule_identifier](#schemafirewall_rule_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» cascade|body|string|false|The level to attempt to delete similar rules defined for other zones with the same owner. The default value is `none`, which will only delete the current rule. Using `basic` will delete rules that match the same action (mode) and configuration, while using `aggressive` will delete rules that match the same configuration.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» cascade|none|
|» cascade|basic|
|» cascade|aggressive|

```json
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "result": {
    "id": "92f17202ed8bd63d69a66b86a49a8f6b"
  },
  "success": true
}
```

```json
}
```

`PATCH /zones/{zone_id}/firewall/access_rules/rules/{rule_id}`

Updates an IP Access rule defined at the zone level. You can only update the rule action (`mode` parameter) and notes.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "mode": {},
  "notes": "This rule is enabled because of an event that occurred on date X."
}
```

|rule_id|path|[firewall_rule_identifier](#schemafirewall_rule_identifier)|true|none|

`PUT /zones/{zone_id}/firewall/payload_logging/key`

## Update Fraud Detection Settings

<a id="opIdfraud-detection-zone-update-settings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/fraud_detection/settings \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "username_expressions": []
  }'
```

`PUT /zones/{zone_id}/fraud_detection/settings`

Update Fraud Detection settings for a zone.

Notes on `username_expressions` behavior:
- If omitted or set to null, expressions are not modified.
- If provided as an empty array `[]`, all expressions will be cleared.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "username_expressions": []
}
```

<h3 id="update-fraud-detection-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[fraud_identifier](#schemafraud_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[fraud_fraud_settings](#schemafraud_fraud_settings)|true|none|
|» authentication_settings|body|[fraud_authentication_settings](#schemafraud_authentication_settings)|false|Configuration for classifying login authentication outcomes based on the origin response.<br>Requires `user_profiles` to be enabled.<br><br>- Success and failure criteria are independently updatable — sending only `success_criteria`<br>  leaves failure codes untouched, and vice versa.<br>- Omit `authentication_settings` entirely to leave both unchanged.<br>- Status codes must not overlap between success and failure criteria.<br>|
|» user_profiles|body|[fraud_user_profiles_status](#schemafraud_user_profiles_status)|false|Whether Fraud User Profiles is enabled for the zone.|
|» username_expressions|body|[fraud_username_expressions](#schemafraud_username_expressions)|false|List of expressions to detect usernames in write HTTP requests.<br><br>- Maximum of 10 expressions.<br>- Omit or set to null to leave unchanged on update.<br>- Provide an empty array `[]` to clear all expressions on update.<br>- Invalid expressions will result in a 10400 Bad Request with details in the `messages` array.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» user_profiles|enabled|
|» user_profiles|disabled|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "authentication_settings": {
      "failure_criteria": {
        "kind": "status_code",
        "status_codes": [
          200,
          201
        ]
      },
      "success_criteria": {
        "kind": "status_code",
        "status_codes": [
          200,
          201
        ]
      }
    },
    "user_profiles": "disabled",
    "username_expressions": [
      "http.request.body.form[\"username\"][0]",
      "lookup_json_string(http.request.body.raw, \"username\")"
    ]
  }
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-health-check-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[healthchecks_identifier](#schemahealthchecks_identifier)|true|none|

|» address|body|[healthchecks_address](#schemahealthchecks_address)|true|The hostname or IP address of the origin server to run health checks on.|
|» check_regions|body|[healthchecks_check_regions](#schemahealthchecks_check_regions)|false|A list of regions from which to run health checks. Null means Cloudflare will pick a default region.|
|» consecutive_fails|body|[healthchecks_consecutive_fails](#schemahealthchecks_consecutive_fails)|false|The number of consecutive fails required from a health check before changing the health to unhealthy.|
|» consecutive_successes|body|[healthchecks_consecutive_successes](#schemahealthchecks_consecutive_successes)|false|The number of consecutive successes required from a health check before changing the health to healthy.|
|» description|body|[healthchecks_description](#schemahealthchecks_description)|false|A human-readable description of the health check.|
|» http_config|body|[healthchecks_http_config](#schemahealthchecks_http_config)|false|Parameters specific to an HTTP or HTTPS health check.|
|» interval|body|[healthchecks_interval](#schemahealthchecks_interval)|false|The interval between each health check. Shorter intervals may give quicker notifications if the origin status changes, but will increase load on the origin as we check from multiple locations.|
|» name|body|[healthchecks_name](#schemahealthchecks_name)|true|A short name to identify the health check. Only alphanumeric characters, hyphens and underscores are allowed.|

|» suspended|body|[healthchecks_suspended](#schemahealthchecks_suspended)|false|If suspended, no health checks are sent to the origin.|
|» tcp_config|body|[healthchecks_tcp_config](#schemahealthchecks_tcp_config)|false|Parameters specific to TCP health check.|
|» timeout|body|[healthchecks_timeout](#schemahealthchecks_timeout)|false|The timeout (in seconds) before marking the health check as failed.|
|» type|body|[healthchecks_type](#schemahealthchecks_type)|false|The protocol to use for the health check. Currently supported protocols are 'HTTP', 'HTTPS' and 'TCP'.|

## Remove Zone Hold

<a id="opIdzones-0-hold-delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/hold \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /zones/{zone_id}/hold`

Stop enforcement of a zone hold on the zone, permanently or temporarily, allowing the
creation and activation of zones with this zone's hostname.
Existing zone holds can be removed from CDN-only zones when `hold_after` is not provided.
Active holds are automatically disabled when a zone transitions to CDN-only mode.

<h3 id="remove-zone-hold-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[zones_identifier-2](#schemazones_identifier-2)|true|Zone ID|
|hold_after|query|string|false|If `hold_after` is provided, the hold will be temporarily disabled,<br>then automatically re-enabled by the system at the time specified<br>in this RFC3339-formatted timestamp. Otherwise, the hold will be<br>disabled indefinitely. `hold_after` cannot be provided for CDN-only zones.|

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "result": {
    "hold": false,
    "hold_after": "string",
    "include_subdomains": false
  },
  "success": true
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
    }

  "messages": [],

}
```

## Update Zone Hold

<a id="opIdzones-0-hold-patch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/hold \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "hold_after": "2023-01-31T15:56:36Z",
    "include_subdomains": true
  }'
```

`PATCH /zones/{zone_id}/hold`

Update the `hold_after` and/or `include_subdomains` values on an existing zone hold.
The hold is enabled if the `hold_after` date-time value is in the past.
Existing zone holds can be removed from CDN-only zones by setting `hold_after` to `null`.
Other zone hold updates cannot be made on CDN-only zones.
Active holds are automatically disabled when a zone transitions to CDN-only mode.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "hold_after": "2023-01-31T15:56:36Z",
  "include_subdomains": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-zone-hold-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[zones_identifier-2](#schemazones_identifier-2)|true|Zone ID|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» hold_after|body|string \| null|false|If `hold_after` is provided and future-dated, the hold will be temporarily disabled,<br>then automatically re-enabled by the system at the time specified<br>in this RFC3339-formatted timestamp. A past-dated `hold_after` value will have<br>no effect on an existing, enabled hold. Providing an empty string will set its value<br>to the current time. Providing `null` will disable the hold indefinitely.|
|» include_subdomains|body|boolean|false|If `true`, the zone hold will extend to block any subdomain of the given zone, as well<br>as SSL4SaaS Custom Hostnames. For example, a zone hold on a zone with the hostname<br>'example.com' and include_subdomains=true will block 'example.com',<br>'staging.example.com', 'api.staging.example.com', etc.|

## Get Zone Hold by Zone Name

<a id="opIdzones-0-hold-zone-name-get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/hold/subdomain.example.com \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /zones/{zone_id}/hold/{zone_name}`

Retrieve whether a given hostname is subject to a zone hold, and metadata about the hold.
This endpoint checks whether the given hostname (or any of its ancestor domains) is blocked
by an active zone hold. If a hold with `include_subdomains` is active on an ancestor domain,
that hold is returned. This endpoint is used internally by SSL/COMS to check hold status
during zone activation.

<h3 id="get-zone-hold-by-zone-name-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[zones_identifier-2](#schemazones_identifier-2)|true|Zone identifier. Consumed by the API gateway for routing; the backend<br>handler does not use this value directly.|
|zone_name|path|string|true|The hostname to check for a zone hold. May be a subdomain (e.g. `subdomain.example.com`)<br>or an apex domain (e.g. `example.com`). The service checks the hostname and its ancestor<br>domains for active holds with `include_subdomains` enabled.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "hold": true,
  "hold_after": "2023-01-31T15:56:36Z",
  "include_subdomains": false
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

<h3 id="get-zone-hold-by-zone-name-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful Response|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|Client Error|Inline|

<h3 id="get-zone-hold-by-zone-name-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|hold_after|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|The RFC3339-formatted timestamp at which the hold will be automatically<br>re-enabled, if the hold was temporarily disabled. Null if the hold is<br>permanently enabled or not set.|
|include_subdomains|boolean|false|none|Whether the hold extends to block subdomains of the held zone.|

`POST /zones/{zone_id}/keyless_certificates`

Creates a Keyless SSL configuration that allows SSL/TLS termination without exposing private keys to Cloudflare. Keys remain on your infrastructure.

> Body parameter


`POST /zones/{zone_id}/leaked-credential-checks/detections`

Create a detection location for credentials that the default scan locations do not cover, using Rules language expressions such as `lookup_json_string(http.request.body.raw, "user")`. Only the username expression is required, and Leaked Credential Checks must be enabled on the zone.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": "18a14bafaa8eb1df04ce683ec18c765e",
  "password": "lookup_json_string(http.request.body.raw, \"secret\")",
  "username": "lookup_json_string(http.request.body.raw, \"user\")"
```

## Delete a custom detection location from a zone.

<a id="opIdwaf-product-api-leaked-credentials-delete-detection"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/leaked-credential-checks/detections/18a14bafaa8eb1df04ce683ec18c765e \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /zones/{zone_id}/leaked-credential-checks/detections/{detection_id}`

Delete a user-defined detection location, identified by its detection ID. Incoming requests are then scanned using only the default scan locations and the detection locations that remain.

<h3 id="delete-a-custom-detection-location-from-a-zone-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[waf-product-api-bundle_identifier](#schemawaf-product-api-bundle_identifier)|true|none|
|detection_id|path|[waf-product-api-bundle_detection-id](#schemawaf-product-api-bundle_detection-id)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "result": {},
  "success": true
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 10100,
      "message": "Unknown error occured, please try again"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

<h3 id="delete-a-custom-detection-location-from-a-zone-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Delete Leaked Credential Checks custom detection location response.|[waf-product-api-bundle_api-response-common](#schemawaf-product-api-bundle_api-response-common)|
|4XX|Client Error|Delete Leaked Credential Checks custom detection location failure response.|[waf-product-api-bundle_api-response-common-failure](#schemawaf-product-api-bundle_api-response-common-failure)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
api_email & api_key & api_token
</aside>

<h3 id="create-load-balancer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[load-balancing_load-balancer_components-schemas-identifier](#schemaload-balancing_load-balancer_components-schemas-identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» adaptive_routing|body|[load-balancing_adaptive_routing](#schemaload-balancing_adaptive_routing)|false|Controls features that modify the routing of requests to pools and origins in response to dynamic conditions, such as during the interval between active health monitoring requests. For example, zero-downtime failover occurs immediately when an origin becomes unavailable due to HTTP 521, 522, or 523 response codes. If there is another healthy origin in the same pool, the request is retried once against this alternate origin.|
|» country_pools|body|[load-balancing_country_pools](#schemaload-balancing_country_pools)|false|A mapping of country codes to a list of pool IDs (ordered by their failover priority) for the given country. Any country not explicitly defined will fall back to using the corresponding region_pool mapping if it exists else to default_pools.|
|» default_pools|body|[load-balancing_default_pools](#schemaload-balancing_default_pools)|true|A list of pool IDs ordered by their failover priority. Pools defined here are used by default, or when region_pools are not configured for a given region.|
|» description|body|[load-balancing_components-schemas-description](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-description)|false|Object description.|
|» fallback_pool|body|[load-balancing_fallback_pool](#schemaload-balancing_fallback_pool)|true|The pool ID to use when all other pools are detected as unhealthy.|
|» location_strategy|body|[load-balancing_location_strategy](#schemaload-balancing_location_strategy)|false|Controls location-based steering for non-proxied requests. See `steering_policy` to learn how steering is affected.|
|» name|body|[load-balancing_components-schemas-name](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-name)|true|The DNS hostname to associate with your Load Balancer. If this hostname already exists as a DNS record in Cloudflare's DNS, the Load Balancer will take precedence and the DNS record will not be used.|
|» networks|body|[load-balancing_networks](#schemaload-balancing_networks)|false|List of networks where Load Balancer or Pool is enabled.|
|» pop_pools|body|[load-balancing_pop_pools](#schemaload-balancing_pop_pools)|false|Enterprise only: A mapping of Cloudflare PoP identifiers to a list of pool IDs (ordered by their failover priority) for the PoP (datacenter). Any PoPs not explicitly defined will fall back to using the corresponding country_pool, then region_pool mapping if it exists else to default_pools.|
|» proxied|body|[load-balancing_proxied](#schemaload-balancing_proxied)|false|Whether the hostname should be gray clouded (false) or orange clouded (true).|
|» random_steering|body|[load-balancing_random_steering](#schemaload-balancing_random_steering)|false|Configures pool weights.<br>- `steering_policy="random"`: A random pool is selected with probability proportional to pool weights.<br>- `steering_policy="least_outstanding_requests"`: Use pool weights to scale each pool's outstanding requests.<br>- `steering_policy="least_connections"`: Use pool weights to scale each pool's open connections.|
|» region_pools|body|[load-balancing_region_pools](#schemaload-balancing_region_pools)|false|A mapping of region codes to a list of pool IDs (ordered by their failover priority) for the given region. Any regions not explicitly defined will fall back to using default_pools.|
|» rules|body|[load-balancing_rules](#schemaload-balancing_rules)|false|BETA Field Not General Access: A list of rules for this load balancer to execute.|
|» session_affinity|body|[load-balancing_session_affinity](#schemaload-balancing_session_affinity)|false|Specifies the type of session affinity the load balancer should use unless specified as `"none"`. The supported types are: - `"cookie"`: On the first request to a proxied load balancer, a cookie is generated, encoding information of which origin the request will be forwarded to. Subsequent requests, by the same client to the same load balancer, will be sent to the origin server the cookie encodes, for the duration of the cookie and as long as the origin server remains healthy. If the cookie has expired or the origin server is unhealthy, then a new origin server is calculated and used. - `"ip_cookie"`: Behaves the same as `"cookie"` except the initial origin selection is stable and based on the client's ip address. - `"header"`: On the first request to a proxied load balancer, a session key based on the configured HTTP headers (see `session_affinity_attributes.headers`) is generated, encoding the request headers used for storing in the load balancer session state which origin the request will be forwarded to. Subsequent requests to the load balancer with the same headers will be sent to the same origin server, for the duration of the session and as long as the origin server remains healthy. If the session has been idle for the duration of `session_affinity_ttl` seconds or the origin server is unhealthy, then a new origin server is calculated and used. See `headers` in `session_affinity_attributes` for additional required configuration.|
|» session_affinity_attributes|body|[load-balancing_session_affinity_attributes](#schemaload-balancing_session_affinity_attributes)|false|Configures attributes for session affinity.|
|» session_affinity_ttl|body|[load-balancing_session_affinity_ttl](#schemaload-balancing_session_affinity_ttl)|false|Time, in seconds, until a client's session expires after being created. Once the expiry time has been reached, subsequent requests may get sent to a different origin server. The accepted ranges per `session_affinity` policy are: - `"cookie"` / `"ip_cookie"`: The current default of 23 hours will be used unless explicitly set. The accepted range of values is between [1800, 604800]. - `"header"`: The current default of 1800 seconds will be used unless explicitly set. The accepted range of values is between [30, 3600]. Note: With session affinity by header, sessions only expire after they haven't been used for the number of seconds specified.|
|» steering_policy|body|[load-balancing_steering_policy](#schemaload-balancing_steering_policy)|false|Steering Policy for this load balancer.<br>- `"off"`: Use `default_pools`.<br>- `"geo"`: Use `region_pools`/`country_pools`/`pop_pools`. For non-proxied requests, the country for `country_pools` is determined by `location_strategy`.<br>- `"random"`: Select a pool randomly.<br>- `"dynamic_latency"`: Use round trip time to select the closest pool in default_pools (requires pool health checks).<br>- `"proximity"`: Use the pools' latitude and longitude to select the closest pool using the Cloudflare PoP location for proxied requests or the location determined by `location_strategy` for non-proxied requests.<br>- `"least_outstanding_requests"`: Select a pool by taking into consideration `random_steering` weights, as well as each pool's number of outstanding requests. Pools with more pending requests are weighted proportionately less relative to others.<br>- `"least_connections"`: Select a pool by taking into consideration `random_steering` weights, as well as each pool's number of open connections. Pools with more open connections are weighted proportionately less relative to others. Supported for HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 connections.<br>- `""`: Will map to `"geo"` if you use `region_pools`/`country_pools`/`pop_pools` otherwise `"off"`.|
|» ttl|body|[load-balancing_ttl](#schemaload-balancing_ttl)|false|Time to live (TTL) of the DNS entry for the IP address returned by this load balancer. This only applies to gray-clouded (unproxied) load balancers.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» session_affinity|none|
|» session_affinity|cookie|
|» session_affinity|ip_cookie|
|» session_affinity|header|
|» steering_policy|off|
|» steering_policy|geo|
|» steering_policy|random|
|» steering_policy|dynamic_latency|
|» steering_policy|proximity|
|» steering_policy|least_outstanding_requests|
|» steering_policy|least_connections|
|» steering_policy|""|

## Update Load Balancer

<a id="opIdload-balancers-update-load-balancer"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/699d98642c564d2e855e9661899b7252/load_balancers/699d98642c564d2e855e9661899b7252 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "adaptive_routing": {
```

<h3 id="update-load-balancer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[load-balancing_load-balancer_components-schemas-identifier](#schemaload-balancing_load-balancer_components-schemas-identifier)|true|none|
|load_balancer_id|path|[load-balancing_load-balancer_components-schemas-identifier](#schemaload-balancing_load-balancer_components-schemas-identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» adaptive_routing|body|[load-balancing_adaptive_routing](#schemaload-balancing_adaptive_routing)|false|Controls features that modify the routing of requests to pools and origins in response to dynamic conditions, such as during the interval between active health monitoring requests. For example, zero-downtime failover occurs immediately when an origin becomes unavailable due to HTTP 521, 522, or 523 response codes. If there is another healthy origin in the same pool, the request is retried once against this alternate origin.|
|» country_pools|body|[load-balancing_country_pools](#schemaload-balancing_country_pools)|false|A mapping of country codes to a list of pool IDs (ordered by their failover priority) for the given country. Any country not explicitly defined will fall back to using the corresponding region_pool mapping if it exists else to default_pools.|
|» default_pools|body|[load-balancing_default_pools](#schemaload-balancing_default_pools)|true|A list of pool IDs ordered by their failover priority. Pools defined here are used by default, or when region_pools are not configured for a given region.|
|» description|body|[load-balancing_components-schemas-description](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-description)|false|Object description.|
|» enabled|body|[load-balancing_components-schemas-enabled](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-enabled)|false|Whether to enable (the default) this load balancer.|
|» fallback_pool|body|[load-balancing_fallback_pool](#schemaload-balancing_fallback_pool)|true|The pool ID to use when all other pools are detected as unhealthy.|
|» location_strategy|body|[load-balancing_location_strategy](#schemaload-balancing_location_strategy)|false|Controls location-based steering for non-proxied requests. See `steering_policy` to learn how steering is affected.|
|» name|body|[load-balancing_components-schemas-name](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-name)|true|The DNS hostname to associate with your Load Balancer. If this hostname already exists as a DNS record in Cloudflare's DNS, the Load Balancer will take precedence and the DNS record will not be used.|
|» networks|body|[load-balancing_networks](#schemaload-balancing_networks)|false|List of networks where Load Balancer or Pool is enabled.|
|» pop_pools|body|[load-balancing_pop_pools](#schemaload-balancing_pop_pools)|false|Enterprise only: A mapping of Cloudflare PoP identifiers to a list of pool IDs (ordered by their failover priority) for the PoP (datacenter). Any PoPs not explicitly defined will fall back to using the corresponding country_pool, then region_pool mapping if it exists else to default_pools.|
|» proxied|body|[load-balancing_proxied](#schemaload-balancing_proxied)|false|Whether the hostname should be gray clouded (false) or orange clouded (true).|
|» random_steering|body|[load-balancing_random_steering](#schemaload-balancing_random_steering)|false|Configures pool weights.<br>- `steering_policy="random"`: A random pool is selected with probability proportional to pool weights.<br>- `steering_policy="least_outstanding_requests"`: Use pool weights to scale each pool's outstanding requests.<br>- `steering_policy="least_connections"`: Use pool weights to scale each pool's open connections.|
|» region_pools|body|[load-balancing_region_pools](#schemaload-balancing_region_pools)|false|A mapping of region codes to a list of pool IDs (ordered by their failover priority) for the given region. Any regions not explicitly defined will fall back to using default_pools.|
|» rules|body|[load-balancing_rules](#schemaload-balancing_rules)|false|BETA Field Not General Access: A list of rules for this load balancer to execute.|
|» session_affinity|body|[load-balancing_session_affinity](#schemaload-balancing_session_affinity)|false|Specifies the type of session affinity the load balancer should use unless specified as `"none"`. The supported types are: - `"cookie"`: On the first request to a proxied load balancer, a cookie is generated, encoding information of which origin the request will be forwarded to. Subsequent requests, by the same client to the same load balancer, will be sent to the origin server the cookie encodes, for the duration of the cookie and as long as the origin server remains healthy. If the cookie has expired or the origin server is unhealthy, then a new origin server is calculated and used. - `"ip_cookie"`: Behaves the same as `"cookie"` except the initial origin selection is stable and based on the client's ip address. - `"header"`: On the first request to a proxied load balancer, a session key based on the configured HTTP headers (see `session_affinity_attributes.headers`) is generated, encoding the request headers used for storing in the load balancer session state which origin the request will be forwarded to. Subsequent requests to the load balancer with the same headers will be sent to the same origin server, for the duration of the session and as long as the origin server remains healthy. If the session has been idle for the duration of `session_affinity_ttl` seconds or the origin server is unhealthy, then a new origin server is calculated and used. See `headers` in `session_affinity_attributes` for additional required configuration.|
|» session_affinity_attributes|body|[load-balancing_session_affinity_attributes](#schemaload-balancing_session_affinity_attributes)|false|Configures attributes for session affinity.|
|» session_affinity_ttl|body|[load-balancing_session_affinity_ttl](#schemaload-balancing_session_affinity_ttl)|false|Time, in seconds, until a client's session expires after being created. Once the expiry time has been reached, subsequent requests may get sent to a different origin server. The accepted ranges per `session_affinity` policy are: - `"cookie"` / `"ip_cookie"`: The current default of 23 hours will be used unless explicitly set. The accepted range of values is between [1800, 604800]. - `"header"`: The current default of 1800 seconds will be used unless explicitly set. The accepted range of values is between [30, 3600]. Note: With session affinity by header, sessions only expire after they haven't been used for the number of seconds specified.|
|» steering_policy|body|[load-balancing_steering_policy](#schemaload-balancing_steering_policy)|false|Steering Policy for this load balancer.<br>- `"off"`: Use `default_pools`.<br>- `"geo"`: Use `region_pools`/`country_pools`/`pop_pools`. For non-proxied requests, the country for `country_pools` is determined by `location_strategy`.<br>- `"random"`: Select a pool randomly.<br>- `"dynamic_latency"`: Use round trip time to select the closest pool in default_pools (requires pool health checks).<br>- `"proximity"`: Use the pools' latitude and longitude to select the closest pool using the Cloudflare PoP location for proxied requests or the location determined by `location_strategy` for non-proxied requests.<br>- `"least_outstanding_requests"`: Select a pool by taking into consideration `random_steering` weights, as well as each pool's number of outstanding requests. Pools with more pending requests are weighted proportionately less relative to others.<br>- `"least_connections"`: Select a pool by taking into consideration `random_steering` weights, as well as each pool's number of open connections. Pools with more open connections are weighted proportionately less relative to others. Supported for HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 connections.<br>- `""`: Will map to `"geo"` if you use `region_pools`/`country_pools`/`pop_pools` otherwise `"off"`.|
|» ttl|body|[load-balancing_ttl](#schemaload-balancing_ttl)|false|Time to live (TTL) of the DNS entry for the IP address returned by this load balancer. This only applies to gray-clouded (unproxied) load balancers.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» session_affinity|none|
|» session_affinity|cookie|
|» session_affinity|ip_cookie|
|» session_affinity|header|
|» steering_policy|off|
|» steering_policy|geo|
|» steering_policy|random|
|» steering_policy|dynamic_latency|
|» steering_policy|proximity|
|» steering_policy|least_outstanding_requests|
|» steering_policy|least_connections|
|» steering_policy|""|

<h3 id="patch-load-balancer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[load-balancing_load-balancer_components-schemas-identifier](#schemaload-balancing_load-balancer_components-schemas-identifier)|true|none|
|load_balancer_id|path|[load-balancing_load-balancer_components-schemas-identifier](#schemaload-balancing_load-balancer_components-schemas-identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» adaptive_routing|body|[load-balancing_adaptive_routing](#schemaload-balancing_adaptive_routing)|false|Controls features that modify the routing of requests to pools and origins in response to dynamic conditions, such as during the interval between active health monitoring requests. For example, zero-downtime failover occurs immediately when an origin becomes unavailable due to HTTP 521, 522, or 523 response codes. If there is another healthy origin in the same pool, the request is retried once against this alternate origin.|
|» country_pools|body|[load-balancing_country_pools](#schemaload-balancing_country_pools)|false|A mapping of country codes to a list of pool IDs (ordered by their failover priority) for the given country. Any country not explicitly defined will fall back to using the corresponding region_pool mapping if it exists else to default_pools.|
|» default_pools|body|[load-balancing_default_pools](#schemaload-balancing_default_pools)|false|A list of pool IDs ordered by their failover priority. Pools defined here are used by default, or when region_pools are not configured for a given region.|
|» description|body|[load-balancing_components-schemas-description](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-description)|false|Object description.|
|» enabled|body|[load-balancing_components-schemas-enabled](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-enabled)|false|Whether to enable (the default) this load balancer.|
|» fallback_pool|body|[load-balancing_fallback_pool](#schemaload-balancing_fallback_pool)|false|The pool ID to use when all other pools are detected as unhealthy.|
|» location_strategy|body|[load-balancing_location_strategy](#schemaload-balancing_location_strategy)|false|Controls location-based steering for non-proxied requests. See `steering_policy` to learn how steering is affected.|
|» name|body|[load-balancing_components-schemas-name](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-name)|false|The DNS hostname to associate with your Load Balancer. If this hostname already exists as a DNS record in Cloudflare's DNS, the Load Balancer will take precedence and the DNS record will not be used.|
|» pop_pools|body|[load-balancing_pop_pools](#schemaload-balancing_pop_pools)|false|Enterprise only: A mapping of Cloudflare PoP identifiers to a list of pool IDs (ordered by their failover priority) for the PoP (datacenter). Any PoPs not explicitly defined will fall back to using the corresponding country_pool, then region_pool mapping if it exists else to default_pools.|
|» proxied|body|[load-balancing_proxied](#schemaload-balancing_proxied)|false|Whether the hostname should be gray clouded (false) or orange clouded (true).|
|» random_steering|body|[load-balancing_random_steering](#schemaload-balancing_random_steering)|false|Configures pool weights.<br>- `steering_policy="random"`: A random pool is selected with probability proportional to pool weights.<br>- `steering_policy="least_outstanding_requests"`: Use pool weights to scale each pool's outstanding requests.<br>- `steering_policy="least_connections"`: Use pool weights to scale each pool's open connections.|
|» region_pools|body|[load-balancing_region_pools](#schemaload-balancing_region_pools)|false|A mapping of region codes to a list of pool IDs (ordered by their failover priority) for the given region. Any regions not explicitly defined will fall back to using default_pools.|
|» rules|body|[load-balancing_rules](#schemaload-balancing_rules)|false|BETA Field Not General Access: A list of rules for this load balancer to execute.|
|» session_affinity|body|[load-balancing_session_affinity](#schemaload-balancing_session_affinity)|false|Specifies the type of session affinity the load balancer should use unless specified as `"none"`. The supported types are: - `"cookie"`: On the first request to a proxied load balancer, a cookie is generated, encoding information of which origin the request will be forwarded to. Subsequent requests, by the same client to the same load balancer, will be sent to the origin server the cookie encodes, for the duration of the cookie and as long as the origin server remains healthy. If the cookie has expired or the origin server is unhealthy, then a new origin server is calculated and used. - `"ip_cookie"`: Behaves the same as `"cookie"` except the initial origin selection is stable and based on the client's ip address. - `"header"`: On the first request to a proxied load balancer, a session key based on the configured HTTP headers (see `session_affinity_attributes.headers`) is generated, encoding the request headers used for storing in the load balancer session state which origin the request will be forwarded to. Subsequent requests to the load balancer with the same headers will be sent to the same origin server, for the duration of the session and as long as the origin server remains healthy. If the session has been idle for the duration of `session_affinity_ttl` seconds or the origin server is unhealthy, then a new origin server is calculated and used. See `headers` in `session_affinity_attributes` for additional required configuration.|
|» session_affinity_attributes|body|[load-balancing_session_affinity_attributes](#schemaload-balancing_session_affinity_attributes)|false|Configures attributes for session affinity.|
|» session_affinity_ttl|body|[load-balancing_session_affinity_ttl](#schemaload-balancing_session_affinity_ttl)|false|Time, in seconds, until a client's session expires after being created. Once the expiry time has been reached, subsequent requests may get sent to a different origin server. The accepted ranges per `session_affinity` policy are: - `"cookie"` / `"ip_cookie"`: The current default of 23 hours will be used unless explicitly set. The accepted range of values is between [1800, 604800]. - `"header"`: The current default of 1800 seconds will be used unless explicitly set. The accepted range of values is between [30, 3600]. Note: With session affinity by header, sessions only expire after they haven't been used for the number of seconds specified.|
|» steering_policy|body|[load-balancing_steering_policy](#schemaload-balancing_steering_policy)|false|Steering Policy for this load balancer.<br>- `"off"`: Use `default_pools`.<br>- `"geo"`: Use `region_pools`/`country_pools`/`pop_pools`. For non-proxied requests, the country for `country_pools` is determined by `location_strategy`.<br>- `"random"`: Select a pool randomly.<br>- `"dynamic_latency"`: Use round trip time to select the closest pool in default_pools (requires pool health checks).<br>- `"proximity"`: Use the pools' latitude and longitude to select the closest pool using the Cloudflare PoP location for proxied requests or the location determined by `location_strategy` for non-proxied requests.<br>- `"least_outstanding_requests"`: Select a pool by taking into consideration `random_steering` weights, as well as each pool's number of outstanding requests. Pools with more pending requests are weighted proportionately less relative to others.<br>- `"least_connections"`: Select a pool by taking into consideration `random_steering` weights, as well as each pool's number of open connections. Pools with more open connections are weighted proportionately less relative to others. Supported for HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 connections.<br>- `""`: Will map to `"geo"` if you use `region_pools`/`country_pools`/`pop_pools` otherwise `"off"`.|
|» ttl|body|[load-balancing_ttl](#schemaload-balancing_ttl)|false|Time to live (TTL) of the DNS entry for the IP address returned by this load balancer. This only applies to gray-clouded (unproxied) load balancers.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» session_affinity|none|
|» session_affinity|cookie|
|» session_affinity|ip_cookie|
|» session_affinity|header|
|» steering_policy|off|
|» steering_policy|geo|
|» steering_policy|random|
|» steering_policy|dynamic_latency|
|» steering_policy|proximity|
|» steering_policy|least_outstanding_requests|
|» steering_policy|least_connections|
|» steering_policy|""|
