## Create Logpush job

<a id="opIdpost-zones-zone_id-logpush-jobs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/logpush/jobs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "dataset": "http_requests",
    "destination_conf": "s3://mybucket/logs?region=us-west-2",
    "enabled": false,
    "filter": "{\"where\":{\"and\":[{\"key\":\"ClientRequestPath\",\"operator\":\"contains\",\"value\":\"/static\"},{\"key\":\"ClientRequestHost\",\"operator\":\"eq\",\"value\":\"example.com\"}]}}",
    "kind": "",
    "max_upload_bytes": 5000000,
    "max_upload_interval_seconds": 30,
    "max_upload_records": 1000,
    "name": "example.com",
    "output_options": {
      "CVE-2021-44228": false,
      "batch_prefix": "",
      "batch_suffix": "",
      "field_delimiter": ",",
      "field_names": [
        "RayID",
        "ClientIP",
        "EdgeStartTimestamp"
      ],
      "output_type": "ndjson",
      "record_delimiter": "",
      "record_prefix": "{",
      "record_suffix": "}\n",
      "sample_rate": 1,
      "timestamp_format": "unixnano"
    },
    "ownership_challenge": "00000000000000000000"
  }'
```

`POST /zones/{zone_id}/logpush/jobs`

> Body parameter

```json

  "dataset": "http_requests",

  "filter": "{\"where\":{\"and\":[{\"key\":\"ClientRequestPath\",\"operator\":\"contains\",\"value\":\"/static\"},{\"key\":\"ClientRequestHost\",\"operator\":\"eq\",\"value\":\"example.com\"}]}}",
  "kind": "",
```

<h3 id="create-logpush-job-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[logpush_identifier](#schemalogpush_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» dataset|body|[logpush_dataset](#schemalogpush_dataset)|false|Name of the dataset. A list of supported datasets can be found on the [Developer Docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/reference/log-fields/).|
|» destination_conf|body|[logpush_destination_conf](#schemalogpush_destination_conf)|true|Uniquely identifies a resource (such as an s3 bucket) where data. will be pushed. Additional configuration parameters supported by the destination may be included.|

## Get logs received

<a id="opIdget-zones-zone_id-logs-received"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/logs/received?end=2018-05-20T10%3A01%3A00Z' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /zones/{zone_id}/logs/received`

The `/received` api route allows customers to retrieve their edge HTTP logs. The basic access pattern is "give me all the logs for zone Z for minute M", where the minute M refers to the time records were received at Cloudflare's central data center. `start` is inclusive, and `end` is exclusive. Because of that, to get all data, at minutely cadence, starting at 10AM, the proper values are: `start=2018-05-20T10:00:00Z&end=2018-05-20T10:01:00Z`, then `start=2018-05-20T10:01:00Z&end=2018-05-20T10:02:00Z` and so on; the overlap will be handled properly.

<h3 id="get-logs-received-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[logshare_identifier](#schemalogshare_identifier)|true|none|
|start|query|[logshare_start](#schemalogshare_start)|false|none|
|end|query|[logshare_end](#schemalogshare_end)|true|none|
|fields|query|[logshare_fields](#schemalogshare_fields)|false|none|
|sample|query|[logshare_sample](#schemalogshare_sample)|false|none|
|count|query|[logshare_count](#schemalogshare_count)|false|none|
|timestamps|query|[logshare_timestamps](#schemalogshare_timestamps)|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|timestamps|unix|
|timestamps|unixnano|
|timestamps|rfc3339|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"ClientIP\":\"192.0.2.1\",\"RayID\":\"41ddf1740f67442d\",\"EdgeStartTimestamp\":1526810289280000000}\n{\"ClientIP\":\"192.0.2.1\",\"RayID\":\"41ddf1740f67442d\",\"EdgeStartTimestamp\":1526810289280000000}\n{\"ClientIP\":\"192.0.2.1\",\"RayID\":\"41ddf1740f67442d\",\"EdgeStartTimestamp\":1526810289280000000}"
```

```json
    {

}
```

`POST /zones/{zone_id}/origin_tls_client_auth`

Upload your own certificate you want Cloudflare to use for edge-to-origin communication to override the shared certificate. Please note that it is important to keep only one certificate active. Also, make sure to enable zone-level authenticated origin pulls by making a PUT call to settings endpoint to see the uploaded certificate in use.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» certificate|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_certificate-5](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_certificate-5)|true|The zone's leaf certificate.|
|» private_key|body|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_private_key-2](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_private_key-2)|true|The zone's private key.|

## Set Enablement for Zone

<a id="opIdzone-level-authenticated-origin-pulls-set-enablement-for-zone"></a>

## List Hostname Associations

<a id="opIdper-hostname-authenticated-origin-pull-list-hostname-associations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/origin_tls_client_auth/hostnames \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /zones/{zone_id}/origin_tls_client_auth/hostnames`

List certificate ID - hostname associations for the given zone. Shows which hostnames are associated to which certificates for authenticated origin pulls.

<h3 id="list-hostname-associations-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

## Enable or Disable a Hostname for Client Authentication

<a id="opIdper-hostname-authenticated-origin-pull-enable-or-disable-a-hostname-for-client-authentication"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/origin_tls_client_auth/hostnames \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "config": {}
  }'
```

`PUT /zones/{zone_id}/origin_tls_client_auth/hostnames`

Associate a hostname to a certificate and enable, disable or invalidate the association. If disabled, client certificate will not be sent to the hostname even if activated at the zone level. 100 maximum associations on a single certificate are allowed. Note: Use a null value for parameter *enabled* to invalidate the association.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "config": {}
}
```

<h3 id="enable-or-disable-a-hostname-for-client-authentication-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» config|body|object|true|none|

## List Certificates

<a id="opIdper-hostname-authenticated-origin-pull-list-certificates"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/origin_tls_client_auth/hostnames/certificates \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /zones/{zone_id}/origin_tls_client_auth/hostnames/certificates`

Lists all client certificates configured for per-hostname authenticated origin pulls on the zone.

## Delete Hostname Client Certificate

<a id="opIdper-hostname-authenticated-origin-pull-delete-hostname-client-certificate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/origin_tls_client_auth/hostnames/certificates/2458ce5a-0c35-4c7f-82c7-8e9487d3ff60 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /zones/{zone_id}/origin_tls_client_auth/hostnames/certificates/{certificate_id}`

Removes a client certificate used for authenticated origin pulls on a specific hostname.
Note: Before deleting the certificate, you must first invalidate the hostname for client authentication by sending a PUT request with `enabled` set to null. After invalidating the association, the certificate can be safely deleted.


<h3 id="delete-hostname-client-certificate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|certificate_id|path|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_hostname_aop_certificate_identifier](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_hostname_aop_certificate_identifier)|true|none|
|zone_id|path|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier)|true|none|

## Update Zone Precursor Config

<a id="opIdprecursor-for-a-zone-update-config"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/precursor \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'Cloudflare-Version: 1.0' \
  -d '{
    "mode": "monitor"
  }'
```

`PUT /zones/{zone_id}/precursor`

Updates the Precursor configuration for a zone.

`mode` controls whether Precursor detection is off, monitoring, or
armed. `show_interstitial` controls the zone-level response when armed.
`rules` is the ordered list of overrides for matching requests.

This is a partial update: only the fields present in the request body
are changed.

- Sending an empty array (`[]`) clears all rules.
- At least one of `mode`, `show_interstitial`, or `rules` must be
  present; an empty body (`{}`) is rejected with `400`.
- Rule `id` is read-only (assigned by Cloudflare) and ignored on input.
- Rule `show_interstitial` is required and controls the response for
  requests that match that rule.
- Rule `expression` is limited to 4000 characters. The limit applies to
  each rule individually, not to the combined size of all rules.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "mode": "monitor"
}
```

<h3 id="update-zone-precursor-config-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[precursor_identifier](#schemaprecursor_identifier)|true|none|
|Cloudflare-Version|header|string|true|Selects the split Precursor API schema.|
|body|body|[precursor_precursor_config](#schemaprecursor_precursor_config)|true|none|
|» mode|body|[precursor_precursor_mode](#schemaprecursor_precursor_mode)|false|Controls Precursor detection for the zone. `off` disables detection,<br>`monitor` records detections without affecting bot scores, and `arm`<br>allows detections to affect bot scores.<br>|
|» rules|body|[precursor_precursor_rules](#schemaprecursor_precursor_rules)|false|The ordered list of Precursor rules for the zone.|
|» show_interstitial|body|[precursor_show_interstitial](#schemaprecursor_show_interstitial)|false|Whether Precursor shows an interstitial when it takes action on a<br>request.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Cloudflare-Version|1.0|
|» mode|off|
|» mode|monitor|
|» mode|arm|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "mode": "arm",
    "rules": [
      {
        "description": "Show an interstitial on the shop page",
        "enabled": true,
        "expression": "http.request.uri.path eq \"/shop\"",
        "show_interstitial": true
      }
    ],
    "show_interstitial": false
  }
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
```

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-rate-limiting-analytics">Rate Limiting Analytics</h1>

## Get Rate Limiting Analytics

<a id="opIdrate-limit-analytics-get-zone-analytics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/rate_limit_analytics?since=2024-01-01T00%3A00%3A00Z&until=2024-01-02T00%3A00%3A00Z&time_delta=3600' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /zones/{zone_id}/rate_limit_analytics`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Returns rate limiting analytics for a zone over the specified time period.
The time period divides into time segments of a given length. Each segment
contains total action counts and action counts broken down by colo.

<h3 id="get-rate-limiting-analytics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|string|true|Identifier of the zone.|
|since|query|string(date-time)|true|The start of the queried time period. Time must be rounded to the time<br>segment boundary and formatted as RFC 3339.|
|until|query|string(date-time)|true|The exclusive end of the queried time period. Time must be rounded to the<br>time segment boundary and formatted as RFC 3339.|
|time_delta|query|integer|true|Length (in seconds) of each time segment dividing the entire time period.<br>Accepted values are 60 (minute), 3600 (hour), 86400 (day), and 2592000 (month).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|time_delta|60|
|time_delta|3600|
|time_delta|86400|
|time_delta|2592000|

## Create a rate limit

<a id="opIdrate-limits-for-a-zone-create-a-rate-limit"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/rate_limits \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "action": {
      "mode": "challenge",
      "response": {
        "body": "<error>This request has been rate-limited.</error>",
        "content_type": "text/xml"
      },
      "timeout": 86400
    },
    "match": {
      "headers": [
        {
          "name": "Cf-Cache-Status",
          "op": "ne",
          "value": "HIT"
        }
      ],
      "request": {
        "methods": [
          "GET",
          "POST"
        ],
        "schemes": [
          "HTTP",
          "HTTPS"
        ],
        "url": "*.example.org/path*"
      },
      "response": {
        "origin_traffic": true
      }
    },
    "period": 900,
    "threshold": 60
  }'
```

Full (Strict): SSL between the visitor and Cloudflare -- visitor sees HTTPS on your site, and SSL between Cloudflare and your web server. You'll need to have a valid SSL certificate installed on your web server. This certificate must be signed by a certificate authority, have an expiration date in the future, and respond for the request domain name (hostname). (https://support.cloudflare.com/hc/en-us/articles/200170416).|
|» *anyOf*|body|[zones_ssl_recommender](#schemazones_ssl_recommender)|false|Enrollment in the SSL/TLS Recommender service which tries to detect and recommend (by sending periodic emails) the most secure SSL/TLS setting your origin servers support.|
|» *anyOf*|body|[zones_tls_1_2_only](#schemazones_tls_1_2_only)|false|Only allows TLS1.2.|
|» *anyOf*|body|[zones_tls_1_3](#schemazones_tls_1_3)|false|Enables Crypto TLS 1.3 feature for a zone.|
|» *anyOf*|body|[zones_tls_client_auth](#schemazones_tls_client_auth)|false|TLS Client Auth requires Cloudflare to connect to your origin server using a client certificate (Enterprise Only).|
|» *anyOf*|body|[zones_true_client_ip_header-2](#schemazones_true_client_ip_header-2)|false|Allows customer to continue to use True Client IP (Akamai feature) in the headers we send to the origin. This is limited to Enterprise Zones.|
|» *anyOf*|body|[zones_waf-2](#schemazones_waf-2)|false|The WAF examines HTTP requests to your website.  It inspects both GET and POST requests and applies rules to help filter out illegitimate traffic from legitimate website visitors. The Cloudflare WAF inspects website addresses or URLs to detect anything out of the ordinary. If the Cloudflare WAF determines suspicious user behavior, then the WAF will 'challenge' the web visitor with a page that asks them to submit a CAPTCHA successfully  to continue their action. If the challenge is failed, the action will be stopped. What this means is that Cloudflare's WAF will block any traffic identified as illegitimate before it reaches your origin web server. (https://support.cloudflare.com/hc/en-us/articles/200172016).|
|» *anyOf*|body|[zones_webmcp_enabled](#schemazones_webmcp_enabled)|false|When enabled, Cloudflare injects the WebMCP bridge (bridge.js) into HTML<br>responses for this zone, exposing DOM and Content Credentials tools to an<br>in-browser AI agent via navigator.modelContext. No origin-side code<br>changes are required. This setting is currently in beta and its behavior<br>may change.|
|» *anyOf*|body|[zones_webmcp_mcp_url](#schemazones_webmcp_mcp_url)|false|Optional per-zone path of the site's own MCP server, used by the WebMCP<br>mcp-server-client tool pack to list and call the site's MCP tools from<br>the browser. The path is resolved against the page's origin, so it<br>applies to every hostname in the zone. Only takes effect when<br>webmcp_enabled is on and the mcp-server-client pack is active. Leave<br>empty to use /mcp. This setting is currently in beta and its behavior<br>may change.|
|» *anyOf*|body|[zones_webmcp_packs](#schemazones_webmcp_packs)|false|Optional per-zone override of which bundled WebMCP tool packs the<br>injected bridge.js activates. Only takes effect when webmcp_enabled is<br>on. Leave empty to use the bridge's default pack set. Unknown pack names<br>are ignored by the bridge. This setting is currently in beta and its<br>behavior may change.|
|» *anyOf*|body|[zones_webp](#schemazones_webp)|false|When the client requesting the image supports the WebP image codec, and WebP offers a performance advantage over the original image format, Cloudflare will serve a WebP version of the original image.|
|» *anyOf*|body|[zones_websockets](#schemazones_websockets)|false|WebSockets are open connections sustained between the client and the origin server. Inside a WebSockets connection, the client and the origin can pass data back and forth without having to reestablish sessions. This makes exchanging data within a WebSockets connection fast. WebSockets are often used for real-time applications such as live chat and gaming. For more information refer to [Can I use Cloudflare with Websockets](https://support.cloudflare.com/hc/en-us/articles/200169466-Can-I-use-Cloudflare-with-WebSockets-).|

`GET /zones/{zone_id}/settings/aegis`

Aegis provides dedicated egress IPs (from Cloudflare to your origin) for your layer 7 WAF and CDN services. The egress IPs are reserved exclusively for your account so that you can increase your origin security by only allowing traffic from a small list of IP addresses.

## Get Origin H2 Max Streams Setting

<a id="opIdzone-cache-settings-get-origin-h2-max-streams-setting"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/settings/origin_h2_max_streams \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /zones/{zone_id}/settings/origin_h2_max_streams`

Origin H2 Max Streams configures the max number of concurrent requests that Cloudflare will send within the same connection when communicating with the origin server, if the origin supports it. Note that if your origin does not support H2 multiplexing, 5xx errors may be observed, particularly 520s. Also note that the default value is `100` for all plan types except Enterprise where it is `1`. `1` means that H2 multiplexing is disabled.

<h3 id="get-origin-h2-max-streams-setting-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[cache-settings_identifier](#schemacache-settings_identifier)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "result": {
    "editable": true,
    "id": "origin_h2_max_streams",
    "value": 50
  },
  "success": true
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 12345,
      "message": "Some error message"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

<h3 id="get-origin-h2-max-streams-setting-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Get Origin H2 Max Streams setting response.|[cache-settings_origin_h2_max_streams_response_value](#schemacache-settings_origin_h2_max_streams_response_value)|

`GET /zones/{zone_id}/settings/origin_max_http_version`

Origin Max HTTP Setting Version sets the highest HTTP version Cloudflare will attempt to use with your origin. This setting allows Cloudflare to make HTTP/2 requests to your origin. ## Get Auto-Origin TLS KEX enrollment status for the given zone

<a id="opIdssl-detector-auto-origin-tls-kex-get-enrollment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/settings/auto_origin_tls_kex \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /zones/{zone_id}/settings/auto_origin_tls_kex`

When enabled, Cloudflare automatically selects the preferred TLS key-exchange algorithm to use when establishing the TLS connection to the zone's origin, picking from the algorithms permitted by the zone's `origin_tls_compliance_modes` setting. When disabled, the default key-exchange ordering is used.

|---|---|---|---|---|

```json
    "enabled": false,
    "id": "auto_origin_tls_kex",
    "modified_on": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z"
  },
  "success": true
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 1009,

    }
  ],
  "messages": [],

  },

}
```

`PATCH /zones/{zone_id}/settings/auto_origin_tls_kex`

Enable or disable Auto-Origin TLS KEX selection for the zone by sending `{"enabled": true}` or `{"enabled": false}`. When enabled, Cloudflare runs a periodic scan of the zone's origins to determine the preferred key-exchange algorithm and writes that preference to the edge so it is sent first in the TLS ClientHello to the origin.

```json
}
```

## Get Origin TLS Compliance Modes setting

<a id="opIdzone-cache-settings-get-origin-tls-compliance-modes-setting"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/settings/origin_tls_compliance_modes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /zones/{zone_id}/settings/origin_tls_compliance_modes`

Origin TLS Compliance Modes constrains the set of TLS key-exchange algorithms Cloudflare may use when establishing the TLS connection to the zone's origin. The value is a list of named compliance modes (currently `fips` and `pqh`). Multiple modes are combined as the intersection of their permitted algorithm lists. An empty list (or no rule configured) means no compliance constraint is applied.

<h3 id="get-origin-tls-compliance-modes-setting-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[cache-settings_identifier](#schemacache-settings_identifier)|true|none|

```json
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "id": "origin_tls_compliance_modes",
    "modified_on": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z",
    "value": [
      "fips",
      "pqh"
    ]
  }
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

|» modified_on|string(date-time) \| null|false|read-only|Last time this setting was modified.|
|» id|string|true|none|ID of the zone setting.|
|» value|[cache-settings_origin_tls_compliance_modes_value](#schemacache-settings_origin_tls_compliance_modes_value)|true|none|List of TLS compliance modes that constrain the key-exchange algorithms Cloudflare may use when establishing the TLS connection to the zone's origin. Currently supported values are `fips` (FIPS-approved curves) and `pqh` (post-quantum hybrid). Future modes (e.g. `cnsa2`) may be added; clients should treat unknown values as opaque strings. ## Replace Origin TLS Compliance Modes setting

<a id="opIdzone-cache-settings-replace-origin-tls-compliance-modes-setting"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/settings/origin_tls_compliance_modes \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "value": [
      "fips",
      "pqh"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /zones/{zone_id}/settings/origin_tls_compliance_modes`

Replace the entire set of TLS compliance modes for the zone with the list provided in the request body. PUT performs a full replace, not a merge — any modes not present in the request body are removed. The request body must be of the form `{"value": ["fips", "pqh"]}`. Currently supported modes are `fips` and `pqh`; an empty list clears the constraint. Future modes (e.g. `cnsa2`) may be added; clients should treat unknown values as opaque strings. Invalid mode values are rejected with a 4xx response.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "value": [
    "fips",
    "pqh"
  ]
}
```

|body|body|object|true|none|
|» value|body|[cache-settings_origin_tls_compliance_modes_value](#schemacache-settings_origin_tls_compliance_modes_value)|true|List of TLS compliance modes that constrain the key-exchange algorithms Cloudflare may use when establishing the TLS connection to the zone's origin. Currently supported values are `fips` (FIPS-approved curves) and `pqh` (post-quantum hybrid). Future modes (e.g. `cnsa2`) may be added; clients should treat unknown values as opaque strings. Multiple modes are combined as the intersection of their permitted algorithm lists; selections whose intersection is empty are rejected. An empty list clears the constraint.|

`PATCH /zones/{zone_id}/settings/origin_tls_compliance_modes`

Update the set of TLS compliance modes for the zone. PATCH performs a full replace of the modes list, not a merge — the request body is treated as the complete new list, and any modes not present in it are removed. Currently supported modes are `fips` and `pqh`; an empty list clears the constraint. Future modes (e.g. `cnsa2`) may be added; clients should treat unknown values as opaque strings. Invalid mode values are rejected with a 4xx response.

## Update CSAM Scanner setting

<a id="opIdcsam-scanner-update-setting"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/settings/csam_scanner_third_party \

      "resend_email": true,
      "sources": {
        "source1": true
      }
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /zones/{zone_id}/settings/csam_scanner_third_party`

Update the CSAM Scanner configuration for a zone. Allows enabling or
disabling CSAM scanning, updating the notification email, and
configuring scanning sources.

When a new email is provided, email verification is triggered
automatically. The `enabled` field is a toggle; the server may
adjust it based on whether the notification email is verified.

Returns 403 if the zone or account is locked by Trust & Safety.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": "csam_scanner",
  "value": {
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "enabled": true,
    "resend_email": true,
    "sources": {
      "source1": true
    }
  }
}
```

|» value|body|[csam-config-service_csam_scanner_third_party_update_value](#schemacsam-config-service_csam_scanner_third_party_update_value)|false|Writable CSAM Scanner feature configuration values.<br>|

`GET /zones/{zone_id}/settings/nel`

<h1 id="cloudflare-api-automatic-ssltls">Automatic SSL/TLS</h1>

## Get Automatic SSL/TLS enrollment status for the given zone

<a id="opIdssl-detector-automatic-mode-get-enrollment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/settings/ssl_automatic_mode \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /zones/{zone_id}/settings/ssl_automatic_mode`

If the system is enabled, the response will include next_scheduled_scan, representing the next time this zone will be scanned and the zone's ssl/tls encryption mode is potentially upgraded by the system. If the system is disabled, next_scheduled_scan will not be present in the response body.

<h3 id="get-automatic-ssltls-enrollment-status-for-the-given-zone-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[cache_identifier](#schemacache_identifier)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "result": {
    "editable": true,
    "id": "ssl_automatic_mode",
    "modified_on": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z",
    "next_scheduled_scan": "2014-02-01T05:20:00.12345Z",
    "value": "auto"
  },
  "success": true
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 1008,
      "message": "Invalid SSL/TLS encryption configuration value, only auto or custom accepted"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": {
    "editable": true,
    "id": "ssl_automatic_mode",
    "modified_on": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z",
    "value": "custom"
  },
  "success": false
}
```

## Get Zaraz configuration

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /zones/{zone_id}/settings/zaraz/config`

Gets latest Zaraz configuration for a zone. It can be preview or published configuration, whichever was the last updated. Secret variables values will not be included.

|zone_id|path|[zaraz_identifier](#schemazaraz_identifier)|true|none|

## Create Web3 Hostname

<a id="opIdweb3-hostname-create-web3-hostname"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353/web3/hostnames \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "This is my IPFS gateway.",
    "dnslink": "/ipns/onboarding.ipfs.cloudflare.com",
    "name": "gateway.example.com",
    "target": "ipfs"
  }'
```

```json
{
  "description": "This is my IPFS gateway.",

  "name": "gateway.example.com",
  "target": "ipfs"
}
```

```bash
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "pattern": "example.com/*",
    "script": "my-workers-script"
  }'
```

`POST /zones/{zone_id}/workers/routes`

Creates a route that maps a URL pattern to a Worker.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "pattern": "example.com/*",
  "script": "my-workers-script"
}
```

<h3 id="create-worker-route-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zone_id|path|[workers_identifier](#schemaworkers_identifier)|true|none|
|body|body|[workers_route](#schemaworkers_route)|true|none|
|» pattern|body|string|true|Pattern to match incoming requests against. [Learn more](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/routing/routes/#matching-behavior).|
|» script|body|string|false|Name of the script to run if the route matches.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [],
  "messages": [],
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "id": {},
    "pattern": "example.com/*",
    "script": "my-workers-script"
  }
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 7003,
      "message": "No route for the URI"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-worker-route-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Create Route response.|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|Create Route response failure.|[workers_api-response-common-failure](#schemaworkers_api-response-common-failure)|

<h3 id="create-worker-route-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[workers_messages](#schemaworkers_messages)|true|none|none|

|success|boolean|true|none|Whether the API call was successful.|
|result|[workers_route](#schemaworkers_route)|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|success|true|

<a id="tocsaaa_audit-logs"></a>

```json
{
  "action": {
    "result": true,
    "type": "change_setting"
  },
  "actor": {
    "email": "michelle@example.com",
    "id": "f6b5de0326bb5182b8a4840ee01ec774",
    "ip": "198.41.129.166",
    "type": "user"
  },
  "id": "d5b0f326-1232-4452-8858-1089bd7168ef",
  "interface": "API",
  "metadata": {
    "name": "security_level",
    "type": "firewall",
    "value": "high",
    "zone_name": "example.com"
  },
  "newValue": "low",
  "oldValue": "high",
  "owner": {
    "id": "023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353"
  },
  "resource": {
    "id": "023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353",
    "type": "zone"
  },
  "when": "2017-04-26T17:31:07Z"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|object|false|none|none|
|actor|object|false|none|none|
|id|string|false|none|A string that uniquely identifies the audit log.|
|interface|string|false|none|The source of the event.|
|metadata|object|false|none|An object which can lend more context to the action being logged. This is a flexible value and varies between different actions.|
|newValue|string|false|none|The new value of the resource that was modified.|
|oldValue|string|false|none|The value of the resource before it was modified.|
|owner|object|false|none|none|
|resource|object|false|none|none|
|when|string(date-time)|false|none|A UTC RFC3339 timestamp that specifies when the action being logged occured.|

```json
    "count": 1,
```

```json
  },
  "success": false
```

Returned when the source audit log entry referenced by `id` cannot be found within the `action_time` window. The `result_info.history_status` is always set to `unavailable` for this response.

|success|boolean|true|none|Indicates whether the API call was successful|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|success|false|

```json
  "history_status": "exact"
}
```

Provides information about the result of the request, including count, cursor, and identification quality.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|count|integer|true|none|The number of records returned in the response.|
|cursor|string|false|none|The cursor token used for pagination.|
|history_status|[aaa_history-status](#schemaaaa_history-status)|true|none|Indicates the quality of the resource identification used to derive the history.<br>- `exact`: Resource was identified by the resource URI.<br>- `approximate`: Resource was identified without the resource URI.<br>- `unavailable`: The source audit log entry did not contain enough information to identify the resource; result is empty.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|history_status|exact|
|history_status|approximate|
|history_status|unavailable|

Indicates the quality of the resource identification used to derive the history.

- `approximate`: Resource was identified without the resource URI.

The Abuse Reports API returns this HTTP 401 authorization error after credentials pass authentication but fail the required Trust and Safety permission check or, for report submission, the account entitlement check. Submission entitlement failures return "Not entitled to use feature: Abuse Report API". Enterprise accounts have the entitlement by default; other accounts must request access.

|result|string|true|none|The result is 'error' for an error response.|

<h2 id="tocS_abuse-reports_CloudflareAPIErrorResponse">abuse-reports_CloudflareAPIErrorResponse</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaabuse-reports_cloudflareapierrorresponse"></a>
<a id="schema_abuse-reports_CloudflareAPIErrorResponse"></a>
<a id="tocSabuse-reports_cloudflareapierrorresponse"></a>
<a id="tocsabuse-reports_cloudflareapierrorresponse"></a>

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 10000,
      "message": "Authentication error"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

Cloudflare's API layer uses this standard error envelope for requests that fail authentication or authorization before they reach the Abuse Reports API. The example shows error code `10000`, returned for missing or invalid credentials (HTTP 401) and for a token or OAuth grant that lacks the required Trust and Safety permission (HTTP 403).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[[abuse-reports_ErrorMessage](#schemaabuse-reports_errormessage)]|true|none|Cloudflare API error details.|
|messages|[[abuse-reports_Message](#schemaabuse-reports_message)]|true|none|Informational messages.|
|result|object \| null|true|none|Always null for this error response.|
|success|boolean|true|none|Whether the request succeeded.|

<h2 id="tocS_abuse-reports_MitigationAppealRequest">abuse-reports_MitigationAppealRequest</h2>

```json
{
  "appeals": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "reason": "misclassified"
    }
  ],
  "data": {
    "city": "string",
    "company": "string",
    "counter_notice_response": "string",
    "country": "string",
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "full_name": "string",
    "jurisdiction_consent": true,
    "perjury_attestation": true,
    "phone_number": "string",
    "signature": "string",
    "state": "string",
    "street_address": "string",
    "urls": [
      "http://example.com"
    ],
    "zip_code": "string"
  },
  "explanation": "string",
  "type": "counter_notice"
}
```

Submit an appeal for a report. Provide either a list of mitigations to appeal, or an appeal type with its supporting details, but not both. When type is "counter_notice", the counter-notice details are required. A "content_removed" appeal takes an optional explanation instead and is accepted only while the report is in its Notice and Takedown notice period (`has_pending_notice` on the eligibility response). Reports that allow a single appeal (`max_appeals` of 1) never have a notice period and accept it whenever `appealable` is true.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|appeals|[[abuse-reports_MitigationAppeal](#schemaabuse-reports_mitigationappeal)]|false|none|List of mitigations to appeal.|
|data|[abuse-reports_DMCACounterNotice](#schemaabuse-reports_dmcacounternotice)|false|none|Counter-notice details supporting an appeal.|
|explanation|string|false|none|Optional explanation for a "content_removed" appeal, such as how the content was removed. Not accepted for other appeal types.|
|type|[abuse-reports_AppealType](#schemaabuse-reports_appealtype)|false|none|The type of appeal being submitted.|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|counter_notice|
|type|content_removed|

<h2 id="tocS_abuse-reports_UnauthorizedErrorResponse">abuse-reports_UnauthorizedErrorResponse</h2>

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 10000,
      "message": "Authentication error"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [],
  "result": null,
  "success": false
}
```

For HTTP 401 responses, use one of these error shapes. Cloudflare's API layer rejects requests with missing or invalid credentials before they reach the Abuse Reports API and returns the standard Cloudflare API error envelope. The Abuse Reports API returns its authorization error shape when valid credentials fail the Trust and Safety permission check or the submission entitlement check.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[abuse-reports_CloudflareAPIErrorResponse](#schemaabuse-reports_cloudflareapierrorresponse)|false|none|Cloudflare's API layer uses this standard error envelope for requests that fail authentication or authorization before they reach the Abuse Reports API. The example shows error code `10000`, returned for missing or invalid credentials (HTTP 401) and for a token or OAuth grant that lacks the required Trust and Safety permission (HTTP 403).|
|*oneOf*|[abuse-reports_AuthErrorResponse](#schemaabuse-reports_autherrorresponse)|false|none|The Abuse Reports API returns this HTTP 401 authorization error after credentials pass authentication but fail the required Trust and Safety permission check or, for report submission, the account entitlement check. Submission entitlement failures return "Not entitled to use feature: Abuse Report API". Enterprise accounts have the entitlement by default; other accounts must request access.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|precedence|[access_precedence](#schemaaccess_precedence)|false|none|The order of execution for this policy. Must be unique for each policy within an app.<br>|
|decision|[access_decision](#schemaaccess_decision)|true|none|The action Access will take if a user matches this policy. Infrastructure application policies can only use the Allow action.|
|exclude|[access_exclude-2](#schemaaccess_exclude-2)|false|none|Rules evaluated with a NOT logical operator. To match the policy, a user cannot meet any of the Exclude rules.|
|include|[access_include-2](#schemaaccess_include-2)|true|none|Rules evaluated with an OR logical operator. A user needs to meet only one of the Include rules.|
|name|[access_name-9](#schemaaccess_name-9)|true|none|The name of the Access policy.|
|policy_resolution_account_id|[access_policy_resolution_account_id](#schemaaccess_policy_resolution_account_id)|false|none|The account ID used to resolve policy resources and identity for cross-account WARP authentication. The account must be trusted by the account that owns this policy.|
|require|[access_require-2](#schemaaccess_require-2)|false|none|Rules evaluated with an AND logical operator. To match the policy, a user must meet all of the Require rules.|
|approval_groups|[access_approval_groups](#schemaaccess_approval_groups)|false|none|Administrators who can approve a temporary authentication request.|
|approval_required|[access_approval_required](#schemaaccess_approval_required)|false|none|Requires the user to request access from an administrator at the start of each session.|
|connection_rules|[access_connection_rules](#schemaaccess_connection_rules)|false|none|The rules that define how users may connect to targets secured by your application.|
|isolation_required|[access_isolation_required](#schemaaccess_isolation_required)|false|none|Require this application to be served in an isolated browser for users matching this policy. 'Client Web Isolation' must be on for the account in order to use this feature.|
|mfa_config|[access_mfa_config](#schemaaccess_mfa_config)|false|none|Configures multi-factor authentication (MFA) settings.|
|purpose_justification_prompt|[access_purpose_justification_prompt](#schemaaccess_purpose_justification_prompt)|false|none|A custom message that will appear on the purpose justification screen.|
|purpose_justification_required|[access_purpose_justification_required](#schemaaccess_purpose_justification_required)|false|none|Require users to enter a justification when they log in to the application.|
|session_duration|[access_session_duration-3](#schemaaccess_session_duration-3)|false|none|The amount of time that tokens issued for the application will be valid. Must be in the format `300ms` or `2h45m`. Valid time units are: ns, us (or µs), ms, s, m, h.|

|decision|deny|

```json
    },
```

```json
        "operations": {
          "create": true,

        },
        "schema": "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User",
        "strictness": "strict",
        "transform_jsonata": "$merge([$, {'userName': $substringBefore($.userName, '@') & '+test@' & $substringAfter($.userName, '@')}])"
      }
    ],
    "remote_uri": "string"
  }
}
```

<h2 id="tocS_access_cf_resource_id">access_cf_resource_id</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaccess_cf_resource_id"></a>
<a id="schema_access_cf_resource_id"></a>
<a id="tocSaccess_cf_resource_id"></a>
<a id="tocsaccess_cf_resource_id"></a>

```json
[
  "a2abeb50-59c9-4c01-8c5c-963d3bf5700f"
]
```

The unique Cloudflare-generated Id of the SCIM Group resource; also known as the "Id".
Pass once for a single lookup (`?cf_resource_id=A`) or repeat the parameter
(`?cf_resource_id=A&cf_resource_id=B`) to look up multiple groups in one request,
up to 50 values. Mutually exclusive with `idp_resource_id`, `name`,
`search_contains`, and `search_starts_with`.

<h2 id="tocS_access_cf_resource_id-2">access_cf_resource_id-2</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaccess_cf_resource_id-2"></a>
<a id="schema_access_cf_resource_id-2"></a>
<a id="tocSaccess_cf_resource_id-2"></a>
<a id="tocsaccess_cf_resource_id-2"></a>

```json
[
  "bd97ef8d-7986-43e3-9ee0-c25dda33e4b0"
]
```

The unique Cloudflare-generated Id of the SCIM User resource; also known as the "Id".
Pass once for a single lookup (`?cf_resource_id=A`) or repeat the parameter
(`?cf_resource_id=A&cf_resource_id=B`) to look up multiple users in one request,
up to 50 values. Mutually exclusive with `idp_resource_id`, `username`, `email`,
`name`, `search_contains`, and `search_starts_with`.

<h2 id="tocS_access_client_secret_version">access_client_secret_version</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaccess_client_secret_version"></a>
<a id="schema_access_client_secret_version"></a>
<a id="tocSaccess_client_secret_version"></a>
<a id="tocsaccess_client_secret_version"></a>

```json
1
```

A version number identifying the current `client_secret` associated with the service token. Incrementing it triggers a rotation; the previous secret will still be accepted until the time indicated by `previous_client_secret_expires_at`. If the service token was reported as leaked, `previous_client_secret_expires_at` is not required, may not be in the future, and the previous secret is discarded immediately.

<h2 id="tocS_access_deny_unmatched_requests">access_deny_unmatched_requests</h2>

<a id="schemaaccess_deny_unmatched_requests"></a>
<a id="schema_access_deny_unmatched_requests"></a>
<a id="tocSaccess_deny_unmatched_requests"></a>
<a id="tocsaccess_deny_unmatched_requests"></a>

```json
"true"
```

Determines whether to deny all requests to Cloudflare-protected resources that lack an associated Access application. If enabled, you must explicitly configure an Access application and policy to allow traffic to your Cloudflare-protected resources. For domains you want to be public across all subdomains, add the domain to the `deny_unmatched_requests_exempted_zone_names` array.

```json
[
  "example.com"
]
```

Contains zone names to exempt from the `deny_unmatched_requests` feature. Requests to a subdomain in an exempted zone will block unauthenticated traffic by default if there is a configured Access application and policy that matches the request.

<h2 id="tocS_access_duration">access_duration</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaccess_duration"></a>
<a id="schema_access_duration"></a>
<a id="tocSaccess_duration"></a>
<a id="tocsaccess_duration"></a>

```json
"60m"
```

The duration for how long the service token will be valid. Must be in the format `300ms` or `2h45m`, or the special value `forever` for non-expiring tokens. Valid time units are: ns, us (or µs), ms, s, m, h. The default is 1 year in hours (8760h).

<h2 id="tocS_access_eager_redirect_cookie_setting">access_eager_redirect_cookie_setting</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaccess_eager_redirect_cookie_setting"></a>
<a id="schema_access_eager_redirect_cookie_setting"></a>
<a id="tocSaccess_eager_redirect_cookie_setting"></a>
<a id="tocsaccess_eager_redirect_cookie_setting"></a>

```json
true
```

Preemptively sets the Access session cookie on every hostname in a multi-hostname self-hosted application during the initial redirect chain, rather than setting it lazily on first visit. Defaults to true. Set to false to disable the eager redirect cookie behavior.

<h2 id="tocS_access_enabled">access_enabled</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaccess_enabled"></a>
<a id="schema_access_enabled"></a>
<a id="tocSaccess_enabled"></a>
<a id="tocsaccess_enabled"></a>

```json
true
```

Whether the service token is enabled. A disabled service token cannot be used to authenticate; both its current and previous `client_secret` stop being accepted, but the token itself is preserved and can be re-enabled. A service token reported as leaked is disabled automatically and cannot be re-enabled until its secret is rotated; attempting to do so returns a 409. Defaults to enabled when omitted on create.

```json
  "allowed_idps": [

      "overrides": [
        {

          "path_pattern": "/health/*"
        }
      ],
      "type": "public",
      "uri": "string"
    }
  ],
  "domain": "test.example.com/admin",
  "name": "Admin Site",
  "oauth_configuration": {
    "dynamic_client_registration": {
      "allow_any_on_localhost": true,
      "allow_any_on_loopback": true,
      "allowed_uris": [
        "https://example.com/callback",
        "com.example.app:/oauth/callback"
      ],
      "enabled": true
    },
    "enabled": true,

      "access_token_lifetime": "5m",
      "session_duration": "24h"
    }
  },
  "self_hosted_domains": [
    "test.example.com/admin",
    "test.anotherexample.com/staff"
  ],
  "type": {},
  "user_populations": [
    "f174e90a-fafe-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415"
  ]
}
```

An end user application is a public self-hosted application backed by exactly one organization-owned user population. End user applications use a canonical allow-everyone policy and do not support custom policies, SCIM configuration, MFA configuration, or private destinations.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|allowed_idps|[access_allowed_idps](#schemaaccess_allowed_idps)|false|none|The identity providers your users can select when connecting to this application. Defaults to all IdPs configured in your account.|
|destinations|[access_end_user_destinations](#schemaaccess_end_user_destinations)|false|none|Public hostname and Workers destinations secured by Access.|
|domain|[access_domain](#schemaaccess_domain)|false|none|The primary hostname and path secured by Access. This domain will be displayed if the app is visible in the App Launcher.|
|name|[access_name-8](#schemaaccess_name-8)|false|none|The name of the application.|
|oauth_configuration|[access_end_user_oauth_configuration](#schemaaccess_end_user_oauth_configuration)|true|none|none|
|self_hosted_domains|[access_self_hosted_domains](#schemaaccess_self_hosted_domains)|false|none|**Deprecated.** List of public domains that Access will secure. This field is deprecated in favor of `destinations` and will be supported until **November 21, 2025.** If `destinations` are provided, then `self_hosted_domains` will be ignored.<br>|
|type|object|true|none|none|
|user_populations|[[access_uuid](#schemaaccess_uuid)]|true|none|The single user population associated with this application.|

The IdP-generated Id of the SCIM Group resource; also known as the "external Id".
Pass once for a single lookup (`?idp_resource_id=A`) or repeat the parameter
(`?idp_resource_id=A&idp_resource_id=B`) to look up multiple groups in one request,
up to 50 values. Mutually exclusive with `cf_resource_id`, `name`,
`search_contains`, and `search_starts_with`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allowed_authenticators|[string]|false|none|Lists the MFA methods that users can authenticate with. For infrastructure applications, supported values are `piv_key` and `ssh_fido2_key`.|
|mfa_disabled|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether to disable MFA for this resource. This option is available at the application and policy level.|
|session_duration|string|false|none|Defines the duration of an MFA session. Must be in minutes (m) or hours (h). Minimum: 0m. Maximum: 720h (30 days). Examples: `5m` or `24h`.|

|allowed_authenticators|ssh_fido2_key|

|require|[access_require-2](#schemaaccess_require-2)|false|none|Rules evaluated with an AND logical operator. To match the policy, a user must meet all of the Require rules.|
|connection_rules|[access_connection_rules_infra](#schemaaccess_connection_rules_infra)|false|none|The rules that define how users may connect to the targets secured by your application.|

<h2 id="tocS_access_mfa_piv_key_requirements">access_mfa_piv_key_requirements</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaccess_mfa_piv_key_requirements"></a>

<a id="tocsaccess_mfa_piv_key_requirements"></a>

```json
{
  "pin_policy": "always",
  "require_fips_device": true,
  "ssh_key_size": [
    256,
    2048
  ],
  "ssh_key_type": [
    "ecdsa",
    "rsa"
  ],
  "touch_policy": "always"
}
```

Configures PIV key requirements for MFA using hardware security keys.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pin_policy|string|false|none|Defines when a PIN is required to use the SSH key. Valid values: `never` (no PIN required), `once` (PIN required once per session), `always` (PIN required for each use).|
|require_fips_device|boolean|false|none|Requires the PIV key to be stored on a FIPS 140-2 Level 1 or higher validated device.|
|ssh_key_size|[integer]|false|none|Specifies the allowed SSH key sizes in bits. Valid sizes depend on key type. Ed25519 has a fixed key size and does not accept this parameter.|
|ssh_key_type|[string]|false|none|Specifies the allowed SSH key types. Valid values are `ecdsa`, `ed25519`, and `rsa`.|
|touch_policy|string|false|none|Defines when physical touch is required to use the SSH key. Valid values: `never` (no touch required), `always` (touch required for each use), `cached` (touch cached for 15 seconds).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|pin_policy|never|
|pin_policy|once|
|pin_policy|always|
|ssh_key_size|256|
|ssh_key_size|384|
|ssh_key_size|521|
|ssh_key_size|2048|
|ssh_key_size|3072|
|ssh_key_size|4096|
|ssh_key_type|ecdsa|
|ssh_key_type|ed25519|
|ssh_key_type|rsa|
|touch_policy|never|
|touch_policy|always|
|touch_policy|cached|

```json
false
```

Determines whether global MFA settings apply to applications by default. The organization must have MFA enabled with at least one authentication method and a session duration configured. Note: 'allowed_authenticators' cannot contain only the infrastructure SSH authenticators ('piv_key' and 'ssh_fido2_key') if the organization has any non-infrastructure applications.

<a id="schema_access_oauth_configuration"></a>

<a id="tocsaccess_oauth_configuration"></a>

```json
{
  "dynamic_client_registration": {
    "allow_any_on_localhost": true,
    "allow_any_on_loopback": true,
    "allowed_uris": [
      "https://example.com/callback",
      "com.example.app:/oauth/callback"
    ],
    "enabled": true
  },
  "enabled": true,
  "grant": {
    "access_token_lifetime": "5m",
    "session_duration": "24h"
  }
}
```

**Beta:** Optional configuration for managing an OAuth authorization flow controlled by Access. When set, Access will act as the OAuth authorization server for this application. Only compatible with OAuth clients that support [RFC 8707](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8707) (Resource Indicators for OAuth 2.0). This feature is currently in beta.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dynamic_client_registration|object|false|none|Settings for OAuth dynamic client registration.|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether the OAuth configuration is enabled for this application. When set to `false`, Access will not handle OAuth for this application. Defaults to `true` if omitted.<br>|
|grant|object|false|none|Settings for OAuth grant behavior.|

```json
{
  "access_token_lifetime": "5m",
  "allow_pkce_without_client_secret": true,
  "app_launcher_url": "https://example.com/login",
  "auth_type": "oidc",
  "client_id": "oidc client id",
  "client_secret": "oidc client secret",
  "created_at": {},
  "custom_claims": [
    {
      "name": "family_name",
      "required": true,
      "scope": "profile",
      "source": {
        "name": "last_name",
        "name_by_idp": {
          "exampleIdPID1": "ClaimName1",
          "exampleIdPID2": "ClaimName2"
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "grant_types": [
    "authorization_code"
  ],
  "group_filter_regex": "^GROUP_FILTER-*$",
  "hybrid_and_implicit_options": {
    "return_access_token_from_authorization_endpoint": true,
    "return_id_token_from_authorization_endpoint": true
  },
  "public_key": "example unique name",
  "redirect_uris": [
    "https://example.com"
  ],
  "refresh_token_options": {
    "lifetime": "30d"
  },
  "scopes": [
    "openid",
    "groups",
    "email",
    "profile"
  ],
  "updated_at": {}
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|access_token_lifetime|string|false|none|The lifetime of the OIDC Access Token after creation. Valid units are m,h. Must be greater than or equal to 1m and less than or equal to 24h.|

|app_launcher_url|string|false|none|The URL where this applications tile redirects users|

|created_at|[access_created_at](#schemaaccess_created_at)|false|none|none|
|custom_claims|[object]|false|none|none|
|grant_types|[string]|false|none|The OIDC flows supported by this application|
|group_filter_regex|string|false|none|A regex to filter Cloudflare groups returned in ID token and userinfo endpoint|
|hybrid_and_implicit_options|object|false|none|none|
|public_key|string|false|none|The Access public certificate that will be used to verify your identity.|
|redirect_uris|[string]|false|none|The permitted URL's for Cloudflare to return Authorization codes and Access/ID tokens|
|refresh_token_options|object|false|none|none|
|scopes|[string]|false|none|Define the user information shared with access, "offline_access" scope will be automatically enabled if refresh tokens are enabled|
|updated_at|[access_updated_at](#schemaaccess_updated_at)|false|none|none|

```json
{
  "allowed_authenticators": [
    "totp",
    "biometrics",
    "security_key"
  ],
  "amr_matching_session_duration": "12h",
  "required_aaguids": "2fc0579f-8113-47ea-b116-bb5a8db9202a",
  "session_duration": "24h"
}
```

Configures multi-factor authentication (MFA) settings for an organization.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allowed_authenticators|[string]|false|none|Lists the MFA methods that users can authenticate with. The `piv_key` and `ssh_fido2_key` values are supported only for infrastructure applications.|
|amr_matching_session_duration|string|false|none|Allows a user to skip MFA via Authentication Method Reference (AMR) matching when the AMR claim provided by the IdP the user used to authenticate contains "mfa". Must be in minutes (m) or hours (h). Minimum: 0m. Maximum: 720h (30 days).|
|required_aaguids|string(uuid)|false|none|Specifies a Cloudflare List of required FIDO2 authenticator device AAGUIDs.|
|session_duration|string|false|none|Defines the duration of an MFA session. Must be in minutes (m) or hours (h). Minimum: 0m. Maximum: 720h (30 days). Examples:`5m` or `24h`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|allowed_authenticators|totp|
|allowed_authenticators|biometrics|
|allowed_authenticators|security_key|
|allowed_authenticators|piv_key|
|allowed_authenticators|ssh_fido2_key|

```json
  },

  "updated_at": {},
  "user_seat_expiration_inactive_time": "730h",
  "warp_auth_non_browser_401": false,
  "warp_auth_session_duration": "24h"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_authenticate_via_warp|[access_allow_authenticate_via_warp](#schemaaccess_allow_authenticate_via_warp)|false|none|When set to true, users can authenticate via WARP for any application in your organization. Application settings will take precedence over this value.|
|auth_domain|[access_auth_domain](#schemaaccess_auth_domain)|false|none|The unique subdomain assigned to your Zero Trust organization. If omitted on creation, a unique subdomain is auto-generated in the format `adjective-noun-hex4` (e.g. `frosty-moon-7a3b.cloudflareaccess.com`).|
|auto_redirect_to_identity|[access_auto_redirect_to_identity](#schemaaccess_auto_redirect_to_identity)|false|none|When set to `true`, users skip the identity provider selection step during login.|
|created_at|[access_created_at](#schemaaccess_created_at)|false|none|none|
|custom_pages|[access_custom_pages](#schemaaccess_custom_pages)|false|none|none|
|deny_unmatched_requests|[access_deny_unmatched_requests](#schemaaccess_deny_unmatched_requests)|false|none|Determines whether to deny all requests to Cloudflare-protected resources that lack an associated Access application. If enabled, you must explicitly configure an Access application and policy to allow traffic to your Cloudflare-protected resources. For domains you want to be public across all subdomains, add the domain to the `deny_unmatched_requests_exempted_zone_names` array.|
|deny_unmatched_requests_exempted_zone_names|[access_deny_unmatched_requests_exempted_zone_names](#schemaaccess_deny_unmatched_requests_exempted_zone_names)|false|none|Contains zone names to exempt from the `deny_unmatched_requests` feature. Requests to a subdomain in an exempted zone will block unauthenticated traffic by default if there is a configured Access application and policy that matches the request.|
|disable_end_user_app_creation|[access_disable_end_user_app_creation](#schemaaccess_disable_end_user_app_creation)|false|none|Whether creation of end user applications is disabled for this organization.|
|is_ui_read_only|[access_is_ui_read_only](#schemaaccess_is_ui_read_only)|false|none|Lock all settings as Read-Only in the Dashboard, regardless of user permission. Updates may only be made via the API or Terraform for this account when enabled.|
|login_design|[access_login_design](#schemaaccess_login_design)|false|none|none|
|mfa_config|[access_org_mfa_config](#schemaaccess_org_mfa_config)|false|none|Configures multi-factor authentication (MFA) settings for an organization.|
|mfa_piv_key_requirements|[access_mfa_piv_key_requirements](#schemaaccess_mfa_piv_key_requirements)|false|none|Configures PIV key requirements for MFA using hardware security keys.|
|mfa_required_for_all_apps|[access_mfa_required_for_all_apps](#schemaaccess_mfa_required_for_all_apps)|false|none|Determines whether global MFA settings apply to applications by default. The organization must have MFA enabled with at least one authentication method and a session duration configured. Note: 'allowed_authenticators' cannot contain only the infrastructure SSH authenticators ('piv_key' and 'ssh_fido2_key') if the organization has any non-infrastructure applications.|
|name|[access_name](#schemaaccess_name)|false|none|The name of your Zero Trust organization. When omitted on creation, defaults to the provided auth_domain; when both are omitted, defaults to the auto-generated subdomain slug (e.g. frosty-moon-7a3b).|
|service_token_inactivity|[access_service_token_inactivity](#schemaaccess_service_token_inactivity)|false|none|Configures automatic enforcement for inactive service tokens. A service token is inactive if no policy references it, and it has not successfully authenticated with an Access application during the selected inactivity period. This setting applies to every service token in your Zero Trust account.|
|session_duration|[access_session_duration](#schemaaccess_session_duration)|false|none|The amount of time that tokens issued for applications will be valid. Must be in the format `300ms` or `2h45m`. Valid time units are: ns, us (or µs), ms, s, m, h.|
|strict_service_token_auth|[access_strict_service_token_auth](#schemaaccess_strict_service_token_auth)|false|none|Enables new behaviors for requests made with Access service tokens. Unauthorized requests emit audit logs, and return a 401 or 403 status code in the response instead of redirecting to the login page. Successful requests no longer receive a CF_Authorization cookie in the response. Zero Trust organizations created on or after October 5, 2026 will have this setting enabled by default, and cannot disable it.|
|ui_read_only_toggle_reason|[access_ui_read_only_toggle_reason](#schemaaccess_ui_read_only_toggle_reason)|false|none|A description of the reason why the UI read only field is being toggled.|
|updated_at|[access_updated_at](#schemaaccess_updated_at)|false|none|none|
|user_seat_expiration_inactive_time|[access_user_seat_expiration_inactive_time](#schemaaccess_user_seat_expiration_inactive_time)|false|none|The amount of time a user seat is inactive before it expires. When the user seat exceeds the set time of inactivity, the user is removed as an active seat and no longer counts against your Teams seat count.  Minimum value for this setting is 1 month (730h). Must be in the format `300ms` or `2h45m`. Valid time units are: `ns`, `us` (or `µs`), `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`.|
|warp_auth_non_browser_401|[access_warp_auth_non_browser_401](#schemaaccess_warp_auth_non_browser_401)|false|none|When enabled, unsuccessful WARP authentication requests with a non-HTML Accept header return a 401 response instead of redirecting to the login page.|
|warp_auth_session_duration|[access_warp_auth_session_duration](#schemaaccess_warp_auth_session_duration)|false|none|The amount of time that tokens issued for applications will be valid. Must be in the format `30m` or `2h45m`. Valid time units are: m, h.|

<h2 id="tocS_access_previous_client_secret_expires_at">access_previous_client_secret_expires_at</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaccess_previous_client_secret_expires_at"></a>

<a id="tocSaccess_previous_client_secret_expires_at"></a>
<a id="tocsaccess_previous_client_secret_expires_at"></a>

```json
"2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z"
```

The expiration of the previous `client_secret`. This can be modified at any point after a rotation. For example, you may extend it further into the future if you need more time to update services with the new secret; or move it into the past to immediately invalidate the previous token in case of compromise. Rotating a service token that was reported as leaked discards the previous secret entirely, so no grace period can be set.

```json
"Authorization"
```

Allows matching Access Service Tokens passed HTTP in a single header with this name.
This works as an alternative to the (CF-Access-Client-Id, CF-Access-Client-Secret) pair of headers.
The header value will be interpreted as a json object similar to:
  {
    "cf-access-client-id": "88bf3b6d86161464f6509f7219099e57.access.example.com",
    "cf-access-client-secret": "bdd31cbc4dec990953e39163fbbb194c93313ca9f0a6e420346af9d326b1d2a5"
  }

```json
{
  "authentication": {
    "password": "string",
    "scheme": "httpbasic",
    "user": "string"
  },
  "deactivate_on_delete": true,
  "enabled": true,
  "idp_uid": "string",
  "mappings": [
    {
      "enabled": true,
      "filter": "title pr or userType eq \"Intern\"",
      "operations": {
        "create": true,
        "delete": true,
        "update": true
      },
      "schema": "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User",
      "strictness": "strict",
      "transform_jsonata": "$merge([$, {'userName': $substringBefore($.userName, '@') & '+test@' & $substringAfter($.userName, '@')}])"
    }
  ],
  "remote_uri": "string"
}
```

Configuration for provisioning to this application via SCIM. This is currently in closed beta.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|authentication|[access_scim_config_single_authentication](#schemaaccess_scim_config_single_authentication) \| [access_scim_config_multi_authentication](#schemaaccess_scim_config_multi_authentication)|false|none|none|
|deactivate_on_delete|boolean|false|none|If false, propagates DELETE requests to the target application for SCIM resources. If true, sets 'active' to false on the SCIM resource. Note: Some targets do not support DELETE operations.|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether SCIM provisioning is turned on for this application.|
|idp_uid|string|true|none|The UID of the IdP to use as the source for SCIM resources to provision to this application.|
|mappings|[[access_scim_config_mapping](#schemaaccess_scim_config_mapping)]|false|none|A list of mappings to apply to SCIM resources before provisioning them in this application. These can transform or filter the resources to be provisioned.|
|remote_uri|string|true|none|The base URI for the application's SCIM-compatible API.|

|auto_redirect_to_identity|[access_auto_redirect_to_identity-2](#schemaaccess_auto_redirect_to_identity-2)|false|none|When set to `true`, users skip the identity provider selection step during login. You must specify only one identity provider in allowed_idps.|

|custom_deny_message|[access_custom_deny_message](#schemaaccess_custom_deny_message)|false|none|The custom error message shown to a user when they are denied access to the application.|
|custom_deny_url|[access_custom_deny_url](#schemaaccess_custom_deny_url)|false|none|The custom URL a user is redirected to when they are denied access to the application when failing identity-based rules.|
|custom_non_identity_deny_url|[access_custom_non_identity_deny_url](#schemaaccess_custom_non_identity_deny_url)|false|none|The custom URL a user is redirected to when they are denied access to the application when failing non-identity rules.|
|custom_pages|[access_custom_pages-2](#schemaaccess_custom_pages-2)|false|none|The custom pages that will be displayed when applicable for this application|
|destinations|[access_destinations](#schemaaccess_destinations)|false|none|List of destinations secured by Access. ### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[access_client_id](#schemaaccess_client_id)|false|none|The Client ID for the service token. Access will check for this value in the `CF-Access-Client-ID` request header.|
|created_at|[access_created_at](#schemaaccess_created_at)|false|none|none|
|duration|[access_duration](#schemaaccess_duration)|false|none|The duration for how long the service token will be valid. Must be in the format `300ms` or `2h45m`, or the special value `forever` for non-expiring tokens. Valid time units are: ns, us (or µs), ms, s, m, h. The default is 1 year in hours (8760h).|
|enabled|[access_enabled](#schemaaccess_enabled)|false|none|Whether the service token is enabled. A disabled service token cannot be used to authenticate; both its current and previous `client_secret` stop being accepted, but the token itself is preserved and can be re-enabled. A service token reported as leaked is disabled automatically and cannot be re-enabled until its secret is rotated; attempting to do so returns a 409. Defaults to enabled when omitted on create.|
|expires_at|[access_timestamp](#schemaaccess_timestamp)|false|none|none|
|id|object|false|none|none|
|last_seen_at|object|false|none|none|
|leak_report_url|[access_leak_report_url](#schemaaccess_leak_report_url)|false|read-only|Where the leaked `client_secret` was found, if provided by the reporter. Omitted if the token has not been reported as leaked.|
|leak_reported_at|[access_leak_reported_at](#schemaaccess_leak_reported_at)|false|read-only|When a secret scanning partner reported this service token's `client_secret` as leaked. A leaked service token is disabled and must be rotated before it can be re-enabled. Cleared once the secret is rotated. Omitted if the token has not been reported as leaked.|
|leak_reporter|[access_leak_reporter](#schemaaccess_leak_reporter)|false|read-only|The secret scanning partner that reported the leak. Omitted if the token has not been reported as leaked.|
|name|[access_name-2](#schemaaccess_name-2)|false|none|The name of the service token.|
|updated_at|[access_updated_at](#schemaaccess_updated_at)|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_access_service_token_inactivity">access_service_token_inactivity</h2>

```json
{
  "action": "disable",
  "enabled": true,
  "inactivity_threshold_days": 30
}
```

Configures automatic enforcement for inactive service tokens. A service token is inactive if no policy references it, and it has not successfully authenticated with an Access application during the selected inactivity period. This setting applies to every service token in your Zero Trust account.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|string|true|none|The action applied to an inactive service token.|
|enabled|boolean|true|none|Whether automatic enforcement for inactive service tokens is enabled.|
|inactivity_threshold_days|integer|true|none|The number of days a service token must be inactive before the configured action is applied.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|action|disable|
|action|delete|

|same_site_cookie_attribute|[access_same_site_cookie_attribute](#schemaaccess_same_site_cookie_attribute)|false|none|Sets the SameSite cookie setting, which provides increased security against CSRF attacks.|
|scim_config|[access_scim_config](#schemaaccess_scim_config)|false|none|Configuration for provisioning to this application via SCIM. This is currently in closed beta.|
|self_hosted_domains|[access_self_hosted_domains](#schemaaccess_self_hosted_domains)|false|none|**Deprecated.** List of public domains that Access will secure. |tags|[access_tags](#schemaaccess_tags)|false|none|The tags you want assigned to an application. Tags are used to filter applications in the App Launcher dashboard.|

<h2 id="tocS_access_strict_service_token_auth">access_strict_service_token_auth</h2>

<a id="schemaaccess_strict_service_token_auth"></a>
<a id="schema_access_strict_service_token_auth"></a>
<a id="tocSaccess_strict_service_token_auth"></a>
<a id="tocsaccess_strict_service_token_auth"></a>

```json
true
```

Enables new behaviors for requests made with Access service tokens. Unauthorized requests emit audit logs, and return a 401 or 403 status code in the response instead of redirecting to the login page. Successful requests no longer receive a CF_Authorization cookie in the response. Zero Trust organizations created on or after October 5, 2026 will have this setting enabled by default, and cannot disable it.

<h2 id="tocS_access_user_seat_expiration_inactive_time">access_user_seat_expiration_inactive_time</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaccess_user_seat_expiration_inactive_time"></a>
<a id="schema_access_user_seat_expiration_inactive_time"></a>
<a id="tocSaccess_user_seat_expiration_inactive_time"></a>
<a id="tocsaccess_user_seat_expiration_inactive_time"></a>

```json
"730h"
```

The amount of time a user seat is inactive before it expires. When the user seat exceeds the set time of inactivity, the user is removed as an active seat and no longer counts against your Teams seat count.  Minimum value for this setting is 1 month (730h). Must be in the format `300ms` or `2h45m`. Valid time units are: `ns`, `us` (or `µs`), `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`.

```json
true
```

Determines if Cloudflare advertises a BYOIP BGP prefix even when there is no matching BGP prefix in the Magic routing table. When true, Cloudflare will automatically withdraw the BGP prefix when there are no matching BGP routes, and will resume advertising when there is at least one matching BGP route.


If you have legacy TLS clients which do not send the TLS server name indicator, then you can specify one default SNI on the map. If Cloudflare receives a TLS handshake from a client without an SNI, it will respond with the default SNI on those IPs. The default SNI can be any valid zone or subdomain owned by the account.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|asn|[addressing_asn-2](#schemaaddressing_asn-2)|false|none|Autonomous System Number (ASN) the prefix will be advertised under.|
|asn_prepend_count|[addressing_asn_prepend_count](#schemaaddressing_asn_prepend_count)|false|none|Number of times to prepend the Cloudflare ASN to the BGP AS-Path attribute|
|auto_advertise_withdraw|[addressing_auto_advertise_withdraw](#schemaaddressing_auto_advertise_withdraw)|false|none|Determines if Cloudflare advertises a BYOIP BGP prefix even when there is no matching BGP prefix in the Magic routing table. When true, Cloudflare will automatically withdraw the BGP prefix when there are no matching BGP routes, and will resume advertising when there is at least one matching BGP route.|
|bgp_signal_opts|[addressing_bgp_signal_opts](#schemaaddressing_bgp_signal_opts)|false|none|none|
|cidr|[addressing_cidr](#schemaaddressing_cidr)|false|none|IP Prefix in Classless Inter-Domain Routing format.|
|created_at|[addressing_timestamp](#schemaaddressing_timestamp)|false|none|none|
|id|[addressing_bgp_prefix_identifier](#schemaaddressing_bgp_prefix_identifier)|false|none|Identifier of BGP Prefix.|
|modified_at|[addressing_timestamp](#schemaaddressing_timestamp)|false|none|none|

```json
  "irr_validation_state": "pending",
```
