### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|[addressing_account_identifier](#schemaaddressing_account_identifier)|false|none|Identifier of a Cloudflare account.|
|advertised|[addressing_advertised](#schemaaddressing_advertised)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Prefix advertisement status to the Internet. This field is only not 'null' if on demand is enabled.|
|advertised_modified_at|[addressing_advertised_modified_at_nullable](#schemaaddressing_advertised_modified_at_nullable)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Last time the advertisement status was changed. This field is only not 'null' if on demand is enabled.|
|approved|[addressing_approved](#schemaaddressing_approved)|false|none|Approval state of the prefix (P = pending, V = active).|
|asn|[addressing_asn](#schemaaddressing_asn)|false|none|Autonomous System Number (ASN) the prefix will be advertised under.|
|cidr|[addressing_cidr](#schemaaddressing_cidr)|false|none|IP Prefix in Classless Inter-Domain Routing format.|
|created_at|[addressing_timestamp](#schemaaddressing_timestamp)|false|none|none|
|delegate_loa_creation|[addressing_delegate_loa_creation](#schemaaddressing_delegate_loa_creation)|false|none|Whether Cloudflare is allowed to generate the LOA document on behalf of the prefix owner.|
|description|[addressing_description](#schemaaddressing_description)|false|none|Description of the prefix.|
|id|[addressing_prefix_identifier](#schemaaddressing_prefix_identifier)|false|none|Identifier of an IP Prefix.|
|irr_validation_state|[addressing_validation_state](#schemaaddressing_validation_state)|false|none|State of one kind of validation for an IP prefix.|
|loa_document_id|[addressing_loa_document_identifier](#schemaaddressing_loa_document_identifier)|false|none|Identifier for the uploaded LOA document.|
|modified_at|[addressing_timestamp](#schemaaddressing_timestamp)|false|none|none|
|on_demand_enabled|[addressing_on_demand_enabled](#schemaaddressing_on_demand_enabled)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Whether advertisement of the prefix to the Internet may be dynamically enabled or disabled.|
|on_demand_locked|[addressing_on_demand_locked](#schemaaddressing_on_demand_locked)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Whether advertisement status of the prefix is locked, meaning it cannot be changed.|
|ownership_validation_state|[addressing_validation_state](#schemaaddressing_validation_state)|false|none|State of one kind of validation for an IP prefix.|
|ownership_validation_token|[addressing_ownership_validation_token](#schemaaddressing_ownership_validation_token)|false|none|Token provided to demonstrate ownership of the prefix.|
|rpki_validation_state|[addressing_validation_state](#schemaaddressing_validation_state)|false|none|State of one kind of validation for an IP prefix.|

```json
  ],
```

```json
  "version": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"
```


Describes one application in a list response. The response returns every property below unless `fields` narrows it. Treat all properties except `id` as optional.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|application_confidence_score|[alexandria_application_confidence_score](#schemaalexandria_application_confidence_score)|false|none|Confidence score for the application. Returns -1 when no score is available.|
|application_score_composition|[alexandria_application_score_composition](#schemaalexandria_application_score_composition)|false|none|Returns the score composition breakdown for the application.|
|application_source|[alexandria_application_source](#schemaalexandria_application_source)|false|none|Returns the application source.|
|application_type|[alexandria_application_type](#schemaalexandria_application_type)|false|none|Returns the application type.|
|application_type_description|[alexandria_application_type_description](#schemaalexandria_application_type_description)|false|none|Returns the application type description.|
|category_id|[alexandria_category_id](#schemaalexandria_category_id)|false|none|Numeric identifier for an application category.|
|created_at|[alexandria_application_created_at](#schemaalexandria_application_created_at)|false|none|Returns the application creation time.|
|gen_ai_score|[alexandria_application_gen_ai_score](#schemaalexandria_application_gen_ai_score)|false|none|GenAI score for the application. Returns -1 when no score is available.|
|hostnames|[alexandria_application_hostnames](#schemaalexandria_application_hostnames)|false|none|Hostnames matched by the application.|
|human_id|[alexandria_application_human_id](#schemaalexandria_application_human_id)|false|none|Human-readable identifier for the application.|
|id|[alexandria_application_id](#schemaalexandria_application_id)|true|none|Numeric identifier for the application.|
|ip_subnets|[alexandria_application_ip_subnets](#schemaalexandria_application_ip_subnets)|false|none|IP subnets for this application. Custom application create and update requests accept IPv4 prefix lengths /8 through /32 and IPv6 prefix lengths /32 through /128.|
|name|[alexandria_application_name](#schemaalexandria_application_name)|false|none|Application name.|
|port_protocols|[alexandria_application_port_protocols](#schemaalexandria_application_port_protocols)|false|none|Ports matched by the application, in `protocol/port` or inclusive `protocol/start-end` format (for example, `tcp/443` or `udp/10000-20000`). TCP and UDP ports must be between 0 and 65535.|
|review_status|string|false|none|The account-specific Gateway review status. Applications with no assigned review status are returned as `unreviewed`.|
|support_domains|[alexandria_application_support_domains](#schemaalexandria_application_support_domains)|false|none|Support domains matched by the application.|
|supported|[alexandria_application_supported](#schemaalexandria_application_supported)|false|none|Cloudflare products that support this application.|
|updated_at|[alexandria_application_updated_at](#schemaalexandria_application_updated_at)|false|none|Returns the application update time.|
|version|[alexandria_application_version](#schemaalexandria_application_version)|false|none|Returns the application version.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|review_status|approved|
|review_status|unapproved|
|review_status|in_review|
|review_status|unreviewed|
|supported|GATEWAY|
|supported|ACCESS|
|supported|CASB|

```json
  ],
```

```json
  ]
}
```

Defines a custom application. At least one hostname or IP subnet is required.
Support domains and port/protocol pairs do not satisfy this requirement.
A NUL character (U+0000) in any string value returns `400`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|category_id|[alexandria_category_id](#schemaalexandria_category_id)|true|none|Numeric identifier for an application category.|
|hostnames|[alexandria_application_hostnames](#schemaalexandria_application_hostnames)|false|none|Hostnames matched by the application.|
|human_id|[alexandria_application_human_id](#schemaalexandria_application_human_id)|true|none|Human-readable identifier for the application.|
|ip_subnets|[alexandria_application_ip_subnets](#schemaalexandria_application_ip_subnets)|false|none|IP subnets for this application. Custom application create and update requests accept IPv4 prefix lengths /8 through /32 and IPv6 prefix lengths /32 through /128.|
|name|[alexandria_application_name](#schemaalexandria_application_name)|true|none|Application name.|
|port_protocols|[alexandria_application_port_protocols](#schemaalexandria_application_port_protocols)|false|none|Ports matched by the application, in `protocol/port` or inclusive `protocol/start-end` format (for example, `tcp/443` or `udp/10000-20000`). TCP and UDP ports must be between 0 and 65535.|
|support_domains|[alexandria_application_support_domains](#schemaalexandria_application_support_domains)|false|none|Support domains matched by the application.|
|*anyOf*|object|false|none|none|
|hostnames|object|true|none|none|
|*anyOf*|object|false|none|none|
|ip_subnets|object|true|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_alexandria_update_application_request">alexandria_update_application_request</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaalexandria_update_application_request"></a>
<a id="schema_alexandria_update_application_request"></a>
<a id="tocSalexandria_update_application_request"></a>
<a id="tocsalexandria_update_application_request"></a>

```json
{
  "hostnames": [
    "example.com",
    "foo.com"
  ],
  "ip_subnets": [
    "192.168.1.0/24",
    "2001:db8::/48"
  ],
  "port_protocols": [
    "tcp/443",
    "udp/10000-20000"
  ],
  "support_domains": [
    "example.com",
    "foo.com"
  ]
}
```

Update the network matchers for the application. The service preserves omitted
matcher lists; send an empty array to clear a list. The resulting application must
contain at least one hostname or IP subnet. Support domains and port/protocol pairs
do not satisfy this requirement.
A NUL character (U+0000) in any string value returns `400`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|hostnames|[alexandria_application_hostnames](#schemaalexandria_application_hostnames)|false|none|Hostnames matched by the application.|
|ip_subnets|[alexandria_application_ip_subnets](#schemaalexandria_application_ip_subnets)|false|none|IP subnets for this application. Custom application create and update requests accept IPv4 prefix lengths /8 through /32 and IPv6 prefix lengths /32 through /128.|
|port_protocols|[alexandria_application_port_protocols](#schemaalexandria_application_port_protocols)|false|none|Ports matched by the application, in `protocol/port` or inclusive `protocol/start-end` format (for example, `tcp/443` or `udp/10000-20000`). TCP and UDP ports must be between 0 and 65535.|
|support_domains|[alexandria_application_support_domains](#schemaalexandria_application_support_domains)|false|none|Support domains matched by the application.|

```json
    ]
  }
```

What kind of dataset this is. Determines aggregation rules and sampling behavior. Exactly one of `events`, `states`, or `logs` is present.

### Properties

|events|object|false|none|Row-per-event analytics dataset. Aggregations describe the cumulative effect of those events.<br>|
|logs|object|false|none|Row-per-log dataset intended for record retrieval.|
|states|object|false|none|Snapshot/state dataset. Only `valid_aggregations` are valid aggregations for this dataset.<br>|

|selector|[api-shield_selector](#schemaapi-shield_selector)|true|none|Select operations covered by this rule.<br><br>For details on selectors, see the [Cloudflare Docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api-shield/security/jwt-validation/).<br>|

```json
      "alg": "RS256",
```

```json
      "kty": "RSA",
      "n": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

Request payload for PATCH credentials. Provided keys define the complete stored key set, and stored keys omitted from payload are removed. For each provided key identity (`{alg,kid}`), payload fields overwrite the stored key before validation and omitted fields inherit from the stored key. Key identities must be unique.


When set, this applies a mitigation action to this operation

  - `log` log request when request does not conform to schema for this operation
  - `block` deny access to the site when request does not conform to schema for this operation
  - `none` will skip mitigation for this operation
  - `null` indicates that no operation level mitigation is in place, see Zone Level Schema Validation Settings for mitigation action that will be applied

<h2 id="tocS_api-shield_old_validation_default_mitigation_action">api-shield_old_validation_default_mitigation_action</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaapi-shield_old_validation_default_mitigation_action"></a>
<a id="schema_api-shield_old_validation_default_mitigation_action"></a>
<a id="tocSapi-shield_old_validation_default_mitigation_action"></a>
<a id="tocsapi-shield_old_validation_default_mitigation_action"></a>

```json
"block"
```

The default mitigation action used when there is no mitigation action defined on the operation

Mitigation actions are as follows:

  * `log` - log request when request does not conform to schema
  * `block` - deny access to the site when request does not conform to schema

A special value of of `none` will skip running schema validation entirely for the request when there is no mitigation action defined on the operation

<h2 id="tocS_api-shield_old_validation_default_mitigation_action_patch">api-shield_old_validation_default_mitigation_action_patch</h2>

<a id="tocsapi-shield_old_validation_default_mitigation_action_patch"></a>

```json
"block"
```

The default mitigation action used when there is no mitigation action defined on the operation
Mitigation actions are as follows:

  * `log` - log request when request does not conform to schema
  * `block` - deny access to the site when request does not conform to schema

A special value of of `none` will skip running schema validation entirely for the request when there is no mitigation action defined on the operation

`null` will have no effect.

```json
  "selector": {

}
```

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|enabled|[api-shield_enabled](#schemaapi-shield_enabled)|false|none|Toggle rule on or off.|
|expression|[api-shield_expression](#schemaapi-shield_expression)|false|none|Rule expression. Requests that fail to match this expression will be subject to `action`.<br><br>For details on expressions, see the [Cloudflare Docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api-shield/security/jwt-validation/).<br>|
|selector|[api-shield_selector](#schemaapi-shield_selector)|false|none|Select operations covered by this rule.<br><br>For details on selectors, see the [Cloudflare Docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api-shield/security/jwt-validation/).<br>|

<a id="tocsapi-shield_selector-operation-state"></a>

```json
"included"
```

Details how `selector` interacted with an operation:
  - `included` operations are included by `selector` and will be covered by the Token Validation Rule
  - `excluded` operations are excluded by `selector` and will not be covered by the Token Validation Rule
  - `ignored` operations are not included by `selector` and will not be covered by the Token Validation Rule

```json
{
```

```json
    "team": "fintech"
  },

  "x_BillableMetricName": "Workers Standard Requests",

  "x_ZoneName": "example.com"

```

A single cost and usage record for a metered product within a specific charge period, aligned with the FinOps FOCUS v1.3 specification.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|BilledCost|number \| null|false|none|A charge serving as the basis for invoicing, inclusive of all reduced rates and discounts while excluding the amortization of upfront charges (one-time or recurring).|
|BillingAccountId|string|false|none|Public identifier of the Cloudflare account (account tag). Omitted when account is not part of the requested grouping, and always omitted for usage measured at contract level, even when grouping by account: that usage is returned as its own record with no account.|
|BillingAccountName|string|false|none|Display name of the Cloudflare account. Omitted when account is not part of the requested grouping, and for usage measured at contract level.|
|BillingCurrency|string \| null|false|none|Currency that a charge was billed in (ISO 4217).|
|BillingPeriodEnd|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Exclusive end of the billing cycle that contains this usage record.|
|BillingPeriodStart|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Inclusive start of the billing cycle that contains this usage record.|
|ChargeCategory|string|true|none|Highest-level classification of a charge based on the nature of how it gets billed. Currently only "Usage" is supported.|
|ChargeClass|string \| null|false|none|Indicates whether the row represents a correction to one or more charges invoiced in a previous billing period.|
|ChargeDescription|string|true|none|Self-contained summary of the charge's purpose and price.|
|ChargeFrequency|string|true|none|Indicates how often a charge occurs. Currently only "Usage-Based" is supported.|
|ChargePeriodEnd|string(date-time)|true|none|Exclusive end of the time interval during which the usage was consumed.|
|ChargePeriodStart|string(date-time)|true|none|Inclusive start of the time interval during which the usage was consumed.|
|ConsumedQuantity|number|false|none|Measured usage amount within the charge period. Reflects raw metered consumption before pricing transformations.|
|ConsumedUnit|string|true|none|Unit of measure for the consumed quantity (e.g., "GB", "Requests", "vCPU-Hours").|
|ContractedCost|number \| null|false|none|Cost calculated by multiplying ContractedUnitPrice and the corresponding PricingQuantity.|
|ContractedUnitPrice|number \| null|false|none|The agreed-upon unit price for a single PricingUnit of the associated billable metric, inclusive of negotiated discounts, if present, while excluding any other discounts.|
|EffectiveCost|number \| null|false|none|The amortized cost of the charge after applying all reduced rates, discounts, and the applicable portion of relevant, prepaid purchases (one-time or recurring) that covered the charge.|
|HostProviderName|string|true|none|Name of the entity providing the underlying infrastructure or platform.|
|InvoiceIssuerName|string|true|none|Name of the entity responsible for invoicing for the services consumed.|
|ListCost|number \| null|false|none|Cost calculated by multiplying ListUnitPrice and the corresponding PricingQuantity.|
|ListUnitPrice|number \| null|false|none|Suggested provider-published unit price for a single PricingUnit of the associated billable metric, exclusive of any discounts.|
|PricingQuantity|number \| null|false|none|Volume of a given service used or purchased, based on the PricingUnit.|
|PricingUnit|string \| null|false|none|Provider-specified measurement unit for determining unit prices, indicating how the provider rates measured usage after applying pricing rules like block pricing.|
|RegionId|string \| null|false|none|Provider-assigned identifier for an isolated geographic area where a service is provided.|
|RegionName|string \| null|false|none|Name of an isolated geographic area where a service is provided.|
|ServiceProviderName|string|true|none|Name of the entity that made the services available for purchase.|
|SubAccountId|string|false|none|Unique identifier assigned to a grouping of services. For Cloudflare, this is the subscription or contract ID.|
|SubAccountName|string|false|none|Name assigned to a grouping of services. For Cloudflare, this is the subscription or contract display name.|
|Tags|object|false|none|Tag values for the requested `GroupBy` keys. Omitted when `GroupBy` is not provided. Missing keys are omitted, and key-only tags are returned as boolean `true`. All other tag values are strings.|
|x_BillableMetricId|string|true|none|The unique identifier for the billable metric in the Cloudflare catalog. Cloudflare extension; replaces FOCUS SkuId.|
|x_BillableMetricName|string|false|none|The display name of the billable metric. Cloudflare extension; replaces FOCUS SkuMeter.|
|x_ProductCategoryName|string|false|none|The product category the charge belongs to (e.g., "Developer", "Cloudflare One"). Cloudflare extension; replaces FOCUS ServiceCategory.|
|x_ProductFamilyId|string|false|none|The unique identifier for the product family in the Cloudflare catalog. Cloudflare extension; replaces FOCUS ServiceId.|
|x_ProductFamilyName|string|false|none|The product family the charge belongs to (e.g., "R2", "Workers"). Cloudflare extension; replaces FOCUS ServiceName.|
|x_ZoneId|string \| null|false|none|The identifier for the Cloudflare zone (zone tag). Omitted when zone is not part of the requested grouping, and always omitted for usage measured at contract level, even when grouping by zone. Cloudflare extension.|
|x_ZoneName|string \| null|false|none|The display name of the Cloudflare zone. Omitted when zone is not part of the requested grouping, and for usage measured at contract level. Cloudflare extension.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|ChargeCategory|Usage|
|ChargeClass|Correction|
|ChargeFrequency|Usage-Based|

<h2 id="tocS_billable-usage-api_usage_record">billable-usage-api_usage_record</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabillable-usage-api_usage_record"></a>
<a id="schema_billable-usage-api_usage_record"></a>
<a id="tocSbillable-usage-api_usage_record"></a>
<a id="tocsbillable-usage-api_usage_record"></a>

```json
{
  "BilledCost": 0.75,
  "BillingAccountId": "023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353",
  "BillingAccountName": "Example Account",
  "BillingCurrency": "USD",
  "BillingPeriodStart": "2025-02-01T00:00:00Z",
  "ChargeCategory": "Usage",
  "ChargeClass": "string",
  "ChargeDescription": "Workers Standard usage measured in Count",
  "ChargePeriodEnd": "2025-02-02T00:00:00Z",
  "ChargePeriodStart": "2025-02-01T00:00:00Z",
  "ConsumedQuantity": 150000,
  "ConsumedUnit": "GB-months",
  "ContractedCost": 0.75,
  "CumulatedContractedCost": 2.25,
  "CumulatedPricingQuantity": 4500000,
  "EffectiveCost": 0.75,
  "HostProviderName": "Cloudflare, Inc.",
  "InvoiceIssuerName": "Cloudflare, Inc.",
  "ListCost": 0.75,
  "PricingQuantity": 150000,
  "PricingUnit": "Count",
  "ServiceFamilyName": "Workers",
  "ServiceName": "Workers Standard",
  "ServiceProviderName": "Cloudflare, Inc.",
  "SubscriptionId": "3F3CD4CQ6N7FXO7IK6NVFJBOYA",
  "ZoneId": "023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353",
  "ZoneName": "example.com"
}
```

Represents a single billable usage record.

This schema carries 19 of the 21 columns FOCUS 1.3 marks as mandatory. Mandatory columns are always present, using an explicit null when the value is unknown, so consumers can distinguish "unknown" from "not provided".

Known gap 1: `ServiceCategory` (FOCUS 1.3 section 3.1.55) is not yet implemented and does not appear in this schema. Cloudflare's product catalog does not yet have a stakeholder-approved mapping from product family to a FOCUS ServiceCategory value, so the column is omitted entirely rather than shipping unapproved values. It will be added once that mapping exists.

Known gap 2: `BillingPeriodEnd` (FOCUS 1.3 section 3.1.4) is not yet implemented and does not appear in this schema, because no authoritative source for it exists today. Deriving it by calendar arithmetic drifts for billing cycle anchors on day 29-31, and the billing provider's current period end describes only the current period, so it is wrong for backdated records. `BillingPeriodStart` is correctly sourced and is still reported, so records carry a billing period start with no corresponding end until an authoritative end date is available.

Per FOCUS 1.3 section 4.1.4.1, the columns that are not part of FOCUS (`ServiceFamilyName`, `CumulatedPricingQuantity`, `CumulatedContractedCost`, `ZoneId`, `ZoneName` and `SubscriptionId`) would normally carry an `x_` prefix. They are kept unprefixed here to avoid a breaking change for existing consumers.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|BilledCost|number|true|none|The amount invoiced for this charge. PayGo is billed directly by Cloudflare, so this equals ContractedCost.|
|BillingAccountId|string|true|none|The identifier of the account the charge is billed to (account tag).|
|BillingAccountName|string \| null|true|none|The display name of the billing account. Null when the name could not be resolved.|
|BillingCurrency|string|true|none|Specifies the billing currency code (ISO 4217).|
|BillingPeriodStart|string(date-time)|true|none|Indicates the start of the billing period. There is no `BillingPeriodEnd` counterpart; see the known gaps described on this schema.|
|ChargeCategory|string|true|none|Describes the nature of the charge. Always "Usage" for this endpoint, which only returns metered usage.|
|ChargeClass|string \| null|true|none|Indicates whether the row corrects a previously invoiced billing period. Always null for this endpoint, which does not return corrections.|
|ChargeDescription|string \| null|true|none|A human-readable summary of the charge.|
|ChargePeriodEnd|string(date-time)|true|none|Indicates the end of the charge period.|
|ChargePeriodStart|string(date-time)|true|none|Indicates the start of the charge period.|
|ConsumedQuantity|number|true|none|Specifies the quantity consumed during this charge period.|
|ConsumedUnit|string|true|none|A display name for the unit of measurement used for the product (for example, "GB-months", "GB-seconds"). May be empty when the unit is implicit in the service name.|
|ContractedCost|number|true|none|Specifies the cost for this charge period in the billing currency.|
|CumulatedContractedCost|number|true|none|Specifies the cumulated cost for the billing period in the billing currency.|
|CumulatedPricingQuantity|integer|true|none|Specifies the portion of usage that is actually subject to a unit price.|
|EffectiveCost|number|true|none|The amortized cost of the charge. PayGo has no upfront commitments, so this equals ContractedCost.|
|HostProviderName|string|true|none|The provider that hosts the infrastructure or platform the service runs on.|
|InvoiceIssuerName|string|true|none|The entity that issues the invoice for this charge.|
|ListCost|number|true|none|The cost at published list prices, before any discount. PayGo has no commitment discounts, so this equals ContractedCost.|
|PricingQuantity|integer|true|none|Specifies the pricing quantity for this charge period.|
|PricingUnit|string|true|none|The unit that PricingQuantity is expressed in. Unlike ConsumedUnit this is never empty; it falls back to "Count" when the service has no explicit unit.|
|ServiceFamilyName|string|false|none|Identifies the product family for the Cloudflare service.|
|ServiceName|string|true|none|Identifies the Cloudflare service.|
|ServiceProviderName|string|true|none|The provider of the purchased service.|
|SubscriptionId|string \| null|false|none|The identifier for the Cloudflare subscription.|
|ZoneId|string \| null|false|none|The identifier for the Cloudflare zone (zone tag).|
|ZoneName|string \| null|false|none|The display name of the Cloudflare zone.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|ChargeCategory|Usage|

<h2 id="tocS_billable-usage-api_v2_filter_by">billable-usage-api_v2_filter_by</h2>

Usage filters. Filters of different kinds are combined with AND, so a record must match every filter present to be returned.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|BillableMetricIds|[string]|false|none|Restrict results to rows whose `x_BillableMetricId` matches one of these billable metric ids (e.g. `workers_standard_requests`). Values must be unique.|
|ProductFamilyIds|[string(uuid)]|false|none|Restrict results to billable metrics belonging to these product families. Values must be unique UUIDs.|
|Tags|[[billable-usage-api_v2_tag_filter](#schemabillable-usage-api_v2_tag_filter)]|false|none|Restrict results by resource tags. Filters for different keys are combined with AND, while values within one filter are combined with OR. Keys must be unique and are case-sensitive.|

<h2 id="tocS_billable-usage-api_v2_group_by">billable-usage-api_v2_group_by</h2>

<a id="schemabillable-usage-api_v2_group_by"></a>

<a id="tocsbillable-usage-api_v2_group_by"></a>

```json
{
  "Key": "region",
  "Type": "DIMENSION"
}
```

A definition used to split result rows. TAG groups by a case-sensitive resource-tag key. DIMENSION groups by a usage dimension key — account_id, zone_id and region are the documented keys, and any other dimension key carried by the usage data is accepted and returned under that same key.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Key|string|true|none|Case-sensitive resource-tag key (for TAG) or dimension key (for DIMENSION), e.g. team, region, account_id or zone_id.|
|Type|string|true|none|Group category.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|Type|TAG|
|Type|DIMENSION|

<h2 id="tocS_billable-usage-api_v2_time_period">billable-usage-api_v2_time_period</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabillable-usage-api_v2_time_period"></a>

<a id="tocsbillable-usage-api_v2_time_period"></a>

```json
{
  "From": "2025-05-01T00:00:00Z",
  "To": "2025-05-31T00:00:00Z"
}
```

Charge period to query, i.e. when consumption happened, not when it was billed. `From` is inclusive and `To` is exclusive. `From` and `To` must be supplied together; supplying one without the other is an error. When both are omitted the range defaults to the start of the current month through today.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|From|string(date-time)|false|none|Start of the range (ISO 8601). Required if `To` is set.|
|To|string(date-time)|false|none|End of the range (ISO 8601). Required if `From` is set. Must be after `From` and no more than 31 days after it.|

|---|---|---|---|---|
|FilterBy|[billable-usage-api_v2_filter_by](#schemabillable-usage-api_v2_filter_by)|false|none|Usage filters. Filters of different kinds are combined with AND, so a record must match every filter present to be returned.|
|GroupBy|[[billable-usage-api_v2_group_by](#schemabillable-usage-api_v2_group_by)]|false|none|Grouping definitions used to split result rows. At most two unique keys may be supplied.|
|Metric|string|false|none|Type of cost/usage records to retrieve. `usage` returns unrated usage quantities. `cost` returns rated usage with cost and pricing fields; it is available only on `POST` account usage and only when the underlying usage data source is ClickHouse (other sources return an empty result set). Requests that combine `cost` with `GroupBy` or `FilterBy.Tags` return HTTP 400. Unrelated to `FilterBy.BillableMetricIds`. Defaults to `usage` when omitted.|
|TimePeriod|[billable-usage-api_v2_time_period](#schemabillable-usage-api_v2_time_period)|false|none|Charge period to query, i.e. when consumption happened, not when it was billed. `From` is inclusive and `To` is exclusive. `From` and `To` must be supplied together; supplying one without the other is an error. When both are omitted the range defaults to the start of the current month through today.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|Metric|usage|
|Metric|cost|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|read-only|none|
|description|string|true|none|none|
|expression|string|true|none|Wirefilter expression describing the traffic being reported.|
|first_request_seen_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|last_request_seen_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|requests|integer(int64)|true|none|none|
|requests_by_attribute|[bot-management_requests_by_attribute](#schemabot-management_requests_by_attribute)|true|none|Top attributes contributing to the feedback sample. Keys include topASNs, topCountries, topHosts, topIPs, topJA3Hashes, topJA4s, topPaths, topUserAgents.|
|requests_by_score|[bot-management_requests_by_score](#schemabot-management_requests_by_score)|true|none|Map of bot scores (1-99) to request counts. Sum must equal `requests`.|
|requests_by_score_src|[bot-management_requests_by_score_src](#schemabot-management_requests_by_score_src)|true|none|Map of score source to request counts. Sum must equal `requests`.|
|subtype|string|false|none|none|
|type|[bot-management_feedback_type](#schemabot-management_feedback_type)|true|none|Type of feedback report.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|type|false_negative|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|ai_search|[bot-management_ai_search](#schemabot-management_ai_search)|false|none|Configure robots.txt policy for AI search bots.|
|ai_training|[bot-management_ai_training](#schemabot-management_ai_training)|false|none|Configure robots.txt policy for AI model training bots.|
|ai_user|[bot-management_ai_user](#schemabot-management_ai_user)|false|none|Configure robots.txt policy for AI assistant and agent bots.|
|bot_preference_sync_enabled|[bot-management_bot_preference_sync_enabled](#schemabot-management_bot_preference_sync_enabled)|false|none|Enable Bot Preference Sync for this zone. When enabled, Cloudflare can serve robots.txt content derived from the zone's AI Search, AI User, and AI Training preferences.|
|cf_robots_variant|[bot-management_cf_robots_variant](#schemabot-management_cf_robots_variant)|false|none|Specifies the Robots Access Control License variant to use.|
|content_bots_protection|[bot-management_content_bots_protection](#schemabot-management_content_bots_protection)|false|none|Enable rule to block content bots. When enabled, blocks automated traffic with low bot scores, excluding safe verified bot categories. Exceptions should be managed via skip rules.|
|crawler_protection|[bot-management_crawler_protection](#schemabot-management_crawler_protection)|false|none|Enable rule to punish AI Scrapers and Crawlers via a link maze.|
|enable_js|[bot-management_enable_js](#schemabot-management_enable_js)|false|none|Use lightweight, invisible JavaScript detections to improve Bot Management. [Learn more about JavaScript Detections](https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/reference/javascript-detections/).|
|is_robots_txt_managed|[bot-management_is_robots_txt_managed](#schemabot-management_is_robots_txt_managed)|false|none|Enable cloudflare managed robots.txt. If an existing robots.txt is detected, then managed robots.txt will be prepended to the existing robots.txt.|
|jsd_api_results_enabled|[bot-management_jsd_api_results_enabled](#schemabot-management_jsd_api_results_enabled)|false|none|Whether to use JavaScript Detection results submitted through the API for this zone.|
|using_latest_model|[bot-management_using_latest_model](#schemabot-management_using_latest_model)|false|read-only|A read-only field that indicates whether the zone currently is running the latest ML model.<br>|
|optimize_wordpress|[bot-management_optimize_wordpress](#schemabot-management_optimize_wordpress)|false|none|Whether to optimize Super Bot Fight Mode protections for Wordpress.|
|sbfm_definitely_automated|[bot-management_sbfm_definitely_automated](#schemabot-management_sbfm_definitely_automated)|false|none|Super Bot Fight Mode (SBFM) action to take on definitely automated requests.|
|sbfm_static_resource_protection|[bot-management_sbfm_static_resource_protection](#schemabot-management_sbfm_static_resource_protection)|false|none|Super Bot Fight Mode (SBFM) to enable static resource protection.<br>Enable if static resources on your application need bot protection.<br>Note: Static resource protection can also result in legitimate traffic being blocked.<br>|
|sbfm_verified_bots|[bot-management_sbfm_verified_bots](#schemabot-management_sbfm_verified_bots)|false|none|Super Bot Fight Mode (SBFM) action to take on verified bots requests.|
|stale_zone_configuration|object|false|read-only|A read-only field that shows which unauthorized settings are currently active on the zone. These settings typically result from upgrades or downgrades.|

```json
    "https://www.example.com/css/styles.css",
    "https://www.example.com/js/index.js"
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

See [Purge by single-file](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/purge-cache/purge-by-single-file/).|

<h2 id="tocS_cache-purge_SingleFileWithUrlAndHeaders">cache-purge_SingleFileWithUrlAndHeaders</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacache-purge_singlefilewithurlandheaders"></a>
<a id="schema_cache-purge_SingleFileWithUrlAndHeaders"></a>
<a id="tocScache-purge_singlefilewithurlandheaders"></a>
<a id="tocscache-purge_singlefilewithurlandheaders"></a>

```json
{
  "files": [
    {
      "headers": {
        "Accept-Language": "zh-CN",
        "CF-Device-Type": "desktop",
        "CF-IPCountry": "US"
      },
      "url": "https://www.example.com/cat_picture.jpg"
    },
    {
      "headers": {
        "Accept-Language": "en-US",
        "CF-Device-Type": "mobile",
        "CF-IPCountry": "DE"
      },
      "url": "https://www.example.com/dog_picture.jpg"
    }
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|files|[object]|false|none|URLs with the request headers your cache key uses. Use this form when your cache key includes request headers, or the visitor's device type, country, or language: send the header values each URL was cached with, such as `CF-Device-Type`, `CF-IPCountry`, or `Accept-Language`.<br><br>When you send the `Origin` header, include the scheme and hostname. Include the port unless it is the default for the scheme: 80 for `http`, 443 for `https`.<br><br>See [Purge by single-file](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/purge-cache/purge-by-single-file/).<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_cache-settings_aegis">cache-settings_aegis</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacache-settings_aegis"></a>
<a id="schema_cache-settings_aegis"></a>

<a id="tocscache-settings_aegis"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "aegis",
  "modified_on": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z",
  "value": {
    "enabled": true,
    "pool_id": "pool-id"
  }
}
```

Aegis provides dedicated egress IPs (from Cloudflare to your origin) for your layer 7 WAF and CDN services. The egress IPs are reserved exclusively for your account so that you can increase your origin security by only allowing traffic from a small list of IP addresses.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|Identifier of the zone setting.|
|modified_on|string(date-time) \| null|false|read-only|Last time this setting was modified.|
|id|string|true|none|ID of the zone setting.|
|value|[cache-settings_aegis_value](#schemacache-settings_aegis_value)|false|none|Value of the zone setting.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|id|aegis|

<h2 id="tocS_cache-settings_cache_reserve">cache-settings_cache_reserve</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacache-settings_cache_reserve"></a>
<a id="schema_cache-settings_cache_reserve"></a>
<a id="tocScache-settings_cache_reserve"></a>
<a id="tocscache-settings_cache_reserve"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "cache_reserve",
  "modified_on": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z"
}
```

Increase cache lifetimes by automatically storing all cacheable files into Cloudflare's persistent object storage buckets. Requires Cache Reserve subscription. Note: using Tiered Cache with Cache Reserve is highly recommended to reduce Reserve operations costs. See the [developer docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/about/cache-reserve) for more information.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|Identifier of the zone setting.|
|modified_on|string(date-time) \| null|false|read-only|Last time this setting was modified.|
|id|string|true|none|ID of the zone setting.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|id|cache_reserve|

```json
{
  "id": "cache_reserve_clear",
  "modified_on": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z"
}
```

You can use Cache Reserve Clear to clear your Cache Reserve, but you must first disable Cache Reserve. In most cases, this will be accomplished within 24 hours. You cannot re-enable Cache Reserve while this process is ongoing. Keep in mind that you cannot undo or cancel this operation.

<h2 id="tocS_cache-settings_origin_h2_max_streams">cache-settings_origin_h2_max_streams</h2>

```json
{
  "id": "origin_h2_max_streams",
  "modified_on": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z",
  "value": 50
}
```

Origin H2 Max Streams configures the max number of concurrent requests that Cloudflare will send within the same connection when communicating with the origin server, if the origin supports it. Note that if your origin does not support H2 multiplexing, 5xx errors may be observed, particularly 520s. Also note that the default value is `100` for all plan types except Enterprise where it is `1`. `1` means that H2 multiplexing is disabled.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|Identifier of the zone setting.|
|modified_on|string(date-time) \| null|false|read-only|Last time this setting was modified.|
|id|string|true|none|Value of the zone setting.|
|value|[cache-settings_origin_h2_max_streams_value](#schemacache-settings_origin_h2_max_streams_value)|false|none|Value of the Origin H2 Max Streams Setting.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|id|origin_h2_max_streams|

<h2 id="tocS_cache-settings_origin_post_quantum_encryption">cache-settings_origin_post_quantum_encryption</h2>

<a id="schemacache-settings_origin_post_quantum_encryption"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "origin_pqe",
  "modified_on": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z"
}
```

Instructs Cloudflare to use Post-Quantum (PQ) key agreement algorithms when connecting to your origin. Preferred instructs Cloudflare to opportunistically send a Post-Quantum keyshare in the first message to the origin (for fastest connections when the origin supports and prefers PQ), supported means that PQ algorithms are advertised but only used when requested by the origin, and off means that PQ algorithms are not advertised.

|---|---|

```json
{
  "id": "origin_tls_compliance_modes",
  "modified_on": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z"
}
```

Origin TLS Compliance Modes constrains the set of TLS key-exchange algorithms Cloudflare may use when establishing the TLS connection to the zone's origin. The value is a list of named compliance modes (currently `fips` and `pqh`). Multiple modes are combined as the intersection of their permitted algorithm lists.

|id|string|true|none|Identifier of the zone setting.|

<h2 id="tocS_cache-settings_origin_tls_compliance_modes_value">cache-settings_origin_tls_compliance_modes_value</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacache-settings_origin_tls_compliance_modes_value"></a>
<a id="schema_cache-settings_origin_tls_compliance_modes_value"></a>
<a id="tocScache-settings_origin_tls_compliance_modes_value"></a>
<a id="tocscache-settings_origin_tls_compliance_modes_value"></a>

```json
[
  "fips",
  "pqh"
]
```

List of TLS compliance modes that constrain the key-exchange algorithms Cloudflare may use when establishing the TLS connection to the zone's origin. Currently supported values are `fips` (FIPS-approved curves) and `pqh` (post-quantum hybrid). Future modes (e.g. `cnsa2`) may be added; clients should treat unknown values as opaque strings. Multiple modes are combined as the intersection of their permitted algorithm lists; selections whose intersection is empty are rejected. An empty list clears the constraint.

<h2 id="tocS_cache-settings_variants">cache-settings_variants</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacache-settings_variants"></a>
<a id="schema_cache-settings_variants"></a>
<a id="tocScache-settings_variants"></a>
<a id="tocscache-settings_variants"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "variants",
  "modified_on": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z"
}
```

Variant support enables caching variants of images with certain file extensions in addition to the original. This only applies when the origin server sends the 'Vary: Accept' response header. If the origin server sends 'Vary: Accept' but does not serve the variant requested, the response will not be cached. This will be indicated with BYPASS cache status in the response headers.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|Identifier of the zone setting.|
|modified_on|string(date-time) \| null|false|read-only|Last time this setting was modified.|
|id|string|true|none|ID of the zone setting.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|id|variants|

```json
      ],

      ],
      "gif": [

      ],

      ],
      "png": [
        "image/webp",

        "image/webp",
        "image/avif"
      ],

        "image/webp",
        "image/avif"
      ],
      "webp": [
        "image/jpeg",
        "image/avif"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

```json
  "active": 0,
  "assigned": 0
}
```

Shows a count of application instance states.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|integer|true|none|Number of instances whose runtime reports the container as running (container_status = "running"). This is a subset of the placements that remain up: an instance that is already bound to a Durable Object and serving traffic is counted under "assigned" until its container_status catches up to "running", so container_status can briefly lag Durable Object attachment under churn. To estimate running, Durable-Object-bound instances, sum "active" + "assigned" rather than reading "active" alone.<br>|
|assigned|integer|true|none|Number of instances bound to a Durable Object with a running placement whose container_status remains behind "running". These count as live, serving instances; "active" + "assigned" approximates the running, Durable-Object-bound count.<br>|

Represents the status and metadata of a rollout process for an application.
For "rolling" strategy: includes steps and progress with instance counts.
For "new_instances" strategy: the response omits steps and progress. Use percentage,
version_distribution, and health.summary for status.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created_at|[cc_ISO8601Timestamp](#schemacc_iso8601timestamp)|true|none|UTC timestamp string in ISO 8601 format.|
|current_configuration|[cc_ModifyUserDeploymentConfiguration](#schemacc_modifyuserdeploymentconfiguration)|true|none|User-specified container configuration changes.|
|current_version|integer|true|none|Current application version before the rollout.|
|description|string|true|none|none|
|health|[cc_ApplicationHealth](#schemacc_applicationhealth)|true|none|none|
|id|[cc_RolloutID](#schemacc_rolloutid)|true|none|An identifier for a specific rollout within an application.|
|kind|string|true|none|Kind of the rollout process.<br> - "full_auto": For rolling rollouts, starts progressing steps upon rollout creation. For new_instances rollouts, advances percentage targets automatically after target-version health is observed.<br> - "full_manual": Requires manually progressing each step in the rollout using the UpdateRollout's action paramater.<br> - "durable_objects_auto": Default when the application is a DO application.<br>|
|last_updated_at|object|true|none|Timestamp of the most recent update to status, health, or progress.|
|percentage|integer|false|none|Current target version percentage (0-100). Only present for "new_instances" strategy.<br>|
|progress|[cc_ApplicationRolloutProgress](#schemacc_applicationrolloutprogress)|false|none|Progress details of an application rollout.|
|started_at|string(date-time)|false|none|Timestamp when the rollout started.|
|status|string|true|none|Current status of the rollout.|
|steps|[[cc_RolloutStep](#schemacc_rolloutstep)]|false|none|none|
|strategy|string|true|none|The rollout strategy.<br>- "rolling": Step-based rollout with health gates. Actively replaces instances to reach each step's target percentage. Response includes steps and progress.<br>- "new_instances": Percentage control over version distribution. Version sync actively replaces instances to match the configured percentage. "full_auto" ramps through fixed percentage targets after target-version health is observed. Response includes percentage, version_distribution, and health.summary.<br>|
|target_configuration|[cc_ModifyUserDeploymentConfiguration](#schemacc_modifyuserdeploymentconfiguration)|true|none|User-specified container configuration changes.|
|target_version|integer|true|none|Target application version after the rollout is complete and applied to all current instances.|
|version_distribution|object|false|none|Version percentage distribution. Only present for "new_instances" strategy.<br>For "rolling" strategy, see progress.version_distribution instead.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|kind|full_auto|
|kind|full_manual|
|kind|durable_objects_auto|
|status|pending|
|status|progressing|
|status|completed|
|status|reverted|
|status|replaced|
|strategy|rolling|
|strategy|new_instances|

scheduler-backed application with deployment configuration, instance counts,
constraints, versions, and rollouts. Set it to `durable_object` for a
Durable Object-managed application where each Durable Object creates and manages
the lifecycle of its container instance. For `durable_object` requests, supply
`name`, `scheduling_policy`, and `durable_objects`, with optional `configuration`
and top-level `observability` settings.

Each Durable Object<br>creates and manages the lifecycle of its container instance. Supply `name`,<br>`scheduling_policy`, and `durable_objects`, with optional `configuration` and<br>top-level `observability` settings. `constraints.jurisdiction` selects the<br>jurisdiction of the application's primary control-plane object at creation time.<br>Deployment configuration, instance counts, scaling, other placement constraints,<br>versions, and rollouts do not apply.<br>|

Request body to create a new rollout for a scheduler-backed application.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|string|true|none|Description of the rollout process.|
|kind|string|false|none|Kind of the rollout process. Defaults to "full_auto".<br> - "full_auto": For rolling rollouts, starts progressing steps upon rollout creation. For new_instances rollouts, advances percentage targets automatically after target-version health is observed.<br> - "full_manual": Requires manually progressing each step in the rollout using the UpdateRollout's action parameter.<br>|
|percentage|integer|false|none|Initial target version percentage (0-100). Version sync actively replaces instances to match.<br>Required when strategy is "new_instances" and kind is "full_manual". When strategy is "new_instances" and kind is "full_auto", omitted percentage starts at 10% or the smallest percentage that targets at least one instance. Unused for "rolling".<br>|
|step_percentage|integer|false|none|Percentage of rollout to increase in each step when "steps" is absent. Applicable values: 5, 10, 20, 25, 50, 100.<br>These create rollouts with 20, 10, 5, 4, 2, 1 steps respectively.<br>Only valid for "rolling" strategy.<br>|
|steps|[[cc_RolloutStepRequest](#schemacc_rolloutsteprequest)]|false|none|Steps defining the rollout process, used when "step_percentage" is absent.<br>Specify only one of "step_percentage" or "steps" when creating a rollout.<br>"steps" allow granular control over each step.<br>Only valid for "rolling" strategy.<br>|
|strategy|string|true|none|Strategy used for the rollout.<br>- "rolling": Step-based rollout with health gates. Actively replaces instances to reach each step's target percentage.<br>- "new_instances": Percentage control over version distribution. Version sync actively replaces instances to match the configured percentage. The "full_auto" kind advances through fixed percentage targets after target-version health is observed.<br>|
|target_configuration|[cc_ModifyUserDeploymentConfiguration](#schemacc_modifyuserdeploymentconfiguration)|true|none|User-specified container configuration changes.|

|step_percentage|20|
|step_percentage|25|
|step_percentage|50|
|step_percentage|100|

|strategy|new_instances|

Create a Durable Object-managed Containers application. Each Durable Object
creates and manages the lifecycle of its container instance. Supply `name`,
`scheduling_policy`, and `durable_objects`, with optional `configuration` and
top-level `observability` settings. `constraints.jurisdiction` selects the
jurisdiction of the application's primary control-plane object at creation time.
Deployment configuration, instance counts, scaling, other placement constraints,
versions, and rollouts do not apply.

|constraints|[cc_DurableObjectApplicationConstraints](#schemacc_durableobjectapplicationconstraints)|false|none|The jurisdiction of a Durable Object-managed application's primary control-plane object.<br>Set this when creating the application; it cannot be changed afterwards.<br>Other placement constraints are not supported by this scheduling policy.<br>|
|durable_objects|object|true|none|The customer-owned Durable Object namespace that owns this application and its instances.|
|name|string|true|none|The name for this application.|
|observability|[cc_DurableObjectApplicationObservability](#schemacc_durableobjectapplicationobservability)|false|none|Application-wide logging settings for a Durable Object-managed application.<br>The application publishes these settings to its runtime metadata. Updating<br>them does not create a deployment or rollout.<br>|
|scheduling_policy|object|true|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_cc_EventName">cc_EventName</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacc_eventname"></a>
<a id="schema_cc_EventName"></a>
<a id="tocScc_eventname"></a>
<a id="tocscc_eventname"></a>

```json
"SchedulerPlaced"
```

Name of the event that describes the kind event that happened.
  - SchedulerPlaced: It's the first event that creates a container placement. It happens when the Containers runtime was able to retrieve deployment resources and start verifying everything is correct.
  - NetworkingIPAssigned: It's sent when the Containers runtime maps the IP to the container.
  - VMStarted: It's sent when the Containers runtime starts the VM. The container might remain unhealthy at this point.
  - ImagePulled: It's sent when the Containers runtime pulls the image successfully.
  - ImagePullError: It's sent when the Containers runtime is having issues pulling the image. The message and details have more information on what happened for debugging.
  - VMFailedToStart: It's sent when the Containers runtime was unable to boot the VM.
  - VMStopping: It's sent when the scheduler is stopping the VM.
  - VMStopped: It's sent when the VM finally exits.
  - VMFailed: It's sent when the scheduling of the VM failed in the current location.
  - RuntimeStartFailed: It's sent when the runtime hits an internal error.
  - SSHStarted: It's sent when the container gains network connectivity and opens the SSH port. Containers only send this event when SSH keys exist.
  - CheckUpdate: Sent when the status of a health or readiness check changes. This may also affect the health status of the placement.
  - DurableObjectConnected: Sent when a durable object instance connects and gains control of the deployment.
    This event is only sent for durable object deployments. It is sent after VMStarted.
  - ContainerStarted: It's sent when the container starts running.

```json
{
  "commit_message": "Reduce false positives on legit CI workers.",
  "content": "rule example { condition: true }",
  "description": "Detects malicious proxy workers",
  "enabled": true,
  "is_public": false,
  "meta": [
    {
      "key": "string",
      "value": "string"
    }
  ],

  "namespaces": [
    "yara/workers"
  ],
  "path": "yara/workers"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|commit_message|string|false|none|Human-readable justification for this change. Required for internal-account submissions; optional for customer accounts and automated sync.|

|description|string|false|none|Human-readable description of the rule. Auto-extracted from YARA meta if present.|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether this rule is active for dice consumers.|
|is_public|boolean|false|none|Whether this rule is visible to other internal accounts.|
|meta|[[cloudforce-one_MetaInputEntry](#schemacloudforce-one_metainputentry)]|false|none|Adds YARA meta entries to the rule's meta block and stores them in rule_meta alongside content metadata. Use valid YARA identifiers for keys; exclude 'name', 'enabled', and 'description'. You may repeat keys.|
|name|string|false|none|none|
|namespaces|[string]|false|none|none|
|path|string|false|none|Path change goes through approval workflow.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created_on|string(date-time)|false|none|The date and time when the data entry was created|
|description|[custom-indicator-feeds_description](#schemacustom-indicator-feeds_description)|false|none|The description of the example test|
|id|[custom-indicator-feeds_id](#schemacustom-indicator-feeds_id)|false|none|The unique identifier for the indicator feed|
|is_attributable|[custom-indicator-feeds_is_attributable](#schemacustom-indicator-feeds_is_attributable)|false|none|Whether the indicator feed can be attributed to a provider|
|is_downloadable|[custom-indicator-feeds_is_downloadable](#schemacustom-indicator-feeds_is_downloadable)|false|none|Whether the indicator feed can be downloaded|
|is_public|[custom-indicator-feeds_is_public](#schemacustom-indicator-feeds_is_public)|false|none|Whether the indicator feed is exposed to customers|
|last_upload_summary|[custom-indicator-feeds_last_upload_summary](#schemacustom-indicator-feeds_last_upload_summary)|false|none|Summary of indicator counts from the last successful upload to this<br>feed. Populated by the custom-threat-feeds loader at the end of each<br>successful load. Absent (omitted) when no upload has completed<br>successfully or the upload errored before the summary write.<br>Surfaces silent-failure paths so operators can see when their<br>indicators were dropped (popularity allowlist, expired valid_until,<br>etc.) without reading loader logs.<br>|
|latest_upload_error|string|false|none|Human-readable error message describing why the latest upload<br>failed. Populated only when `latest_upload_status` is `Error`.<br>Returns one of a small fixed set of category-level messages<br>(invalid domain / IP / URL entries, malformed row or header,<br>invalid valid_until timestamp, etc.) or the generic<br>`Upload failed` for unknown or infrastructure-level errors.<br>Never echoes raw error text from the underlying loader.<br>Intel accounts receive the verbatim loader/API error text<br>(including specific offending values) instead of these<br>category-level messages.<br>|
|latest_upload_status|string|false|none|Status of the latest snapshot uploaded|
|modified_on|string(date-time)|false|none|The date and time when the data entry was last modified|
|name|[custom-indicator-feeds_name](#schemacustom-indicator-feeds_name)|false|none|The name of the indicator feed|
|provider_id|[custom-indicator-feeds_provider_id](#schemacustom-indicator-feeds_provider_id)|false|none|The unique identifier for the provider|
|provider_name|[custom-indicator-feeds_provider_name](#schemacustom-indicator-feeds_provider_name)|false|none|The provider of the indicator feed|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|latest_upload_status|Mirroring|
|latest_upload_status|Unifying|
|latest_upload_status|Loading|
|latest_upload_status|Provisioning|
|latest_upload_status|Complete|
|latest_upload_status|Error|

<h2 id="tocS_custom-indicator-feeds_last_upload_summary">custom-indicator-feeds_last_upload_summary</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacustom-indicator-feeds_last_upload_summary"></a>
<a id="schema_custom-indicator-feeds_last_upload_summary"></a>
<a id="tocScustom-indicator-feeds_last_upload_summary"></a>
<a id="tocscustom-indicator-feeds_last_upload_summary"></a>

```json
{
  "persisted": {
    "domains_added": 0,
    "domains_removed": 0,
    "ips_added": 0,
    "ips_removed": 0,
    "urls_added": 0,
    "urls_removed": 0
  },
  "skipped": {
    "allowlisted_domains": 0,
    "expired_indicators": 0,
    "invalid_indicators": 0
  },
  "uploaded": {
    "domains": 0,
    "ips": 0,
    "urls": 0
  }
}
```

Summary of indicator counts from the last successful upload to this
feed. Populated by the custom-threat-feeds loader at the end of each
successful load. Absent (omitted) when no upload has completed
successfully or the upload errored before the summary write.
Surfaces silent-failure paths so operators can see when their
indicators were dropped (popularity allowlist, expired valid_until,
etc.) without reading loader logs.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|persisted|object|false|none|Net delta applied to feed indicators by this upload. Snapshot<br>uploads emit both *_added and *_removed; delta-add emits only<br>*_added; delta-remove emits only *_removed.<br>|
|skipped|object|false|none|Counts of indicators that were uploaded but did not reach<br>QuickSilver, broken down by reason.<br>|
|uploaded|object|false|none|Indicator counts from the unified file the loader received|

```json
{
```

```json
  "status": "Unifying",
  "upload_id": 12345
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|integer|false|none|Feed id|
|filename|string|false|none|Name of the file unified in our system|
|poll_url|string|false|none|Account-relative polling path. Prepend `/accounts/{account_id}`<br>using the same account identifier and API host as the upload<br>request. The path omits the account segment because the service<br>does not have your account identifier in this context.<br>|
|status|string|false|none|Current status of the upload at the moment the request returned.<br>This is NOT a terminal state: the file is unified inline, but the<br>durable loader has only accepted it, so the upload is still<br>`Unifying`. Poll `poll_url` until the status reaches a terminal<br>value (`Unified` or `Error`).<br>|
|upload_id|integer(int64)|false|none|Identifier of the upload row, for polling this upload to a<br>terminal state via `poll_url`.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_d1_query-meta">d1_query-meta</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemad1_query-meta"></a>
<a id="schema_d1_query-meta"></a>
<a id="tocSd1_query-meta"></a>
<a id="tocsd1_query-meta"></a>

```json
{
  "changed_db": true,
  "changes": 0,
  "duration": 0,
  "last_row_id": 0,
  "rows_read": 0,
  "rows_written": 0,
  "served_by_colo": "LHR",
  "served_by_primary": true,
  "served_by_region": "EEUR",
  "size_after": 0,
  "timings": {
    "sql_duration_ms": 0
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|changed_db|boolean|false|none|Denotes if the database has been altered in some way, like deleting rows.|
|changes|number|false|none|Rough indication of how many rows were modified by the query, as provided by SQLite's `sqlite3_total_changes()`.|
|duration|number|false|none|The duration of the SQL query execution inside the database. Does not include any network communication.|
|last_row_id|number|false|none|The row ID of the last inserted row in a table with an `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` as provided by SQLite. Tables created with `WITHOUT ROWID` do not populate this.|
|rows_read|number|false|none|Number of rows read during the SQL query execution, including indices (not all rows are necessarily returned).|
|rows_written|number|false|none|Number of rows written during the SQL query execution, including indices.|
|served_by_colo|[d1_served-by-colo](#schemad1_served-by-colo)|false|none|The three letters airport code of the colo that handled the query.|
|served_by_primary|boolean|false|none|Denotes if the query has been handled by the database primary instance.|
|served_by_region|[d1_served-by-region](#schemad1_served-by-region)|false|none|Region location hint of the database instance that handled the query.|
|size_after|number|false|none|Size of the database after the query committed, in bytes.|
|timings|object|false|none|Various durations for the query.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|served_by_region|WNAM|
|served_by_region|ENAM|
|served_by_region|WEUR|
|served_by_region|EEUR|
|served_by_region|APAC|
|served_by_region|OC|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|interval|[digital-experience-monitoring_device-dex-test-schemas-interval](#schemadigital-experience-monitoring_device-dex-test-schemas-interval)|true|none|How often the test will run.|
|name|[digital-experience-monitoring_device-dex-test-schemas-name](#schemadigital-experience-monitoring_device-dex-test-schemas-name)|true|none|The name of the DEX test. Must be unique.|
|target_policies|object|false|none|none|
|targeted|boolean|false|none|none|
|test_id|[digital-experience-monitoring_schemas-test-id](#schemadigital-experience-monitoring_schemas-test-id)|false|read-only|The unique identifier for the test.|
|updated|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Date the test was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.|

<h2 id="tocS_digital-experience-monitoring_ip_info">digital-experience-monitoring_ip_info</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadigital-experience-monitoring_ip_info"></a>
<a id="schema_digital-experience-monitoring_ip_info"></a>
<a id="tocSdigital-experience-monitoring_ip_info"></a>
<a id="tocsdigital-experience-monitoring_ip_info"></a>

```json
{
  "address": "203.0.113.1",
  "asn": 13335,
  "aso": "CLOUDFLARENET",
  "location": {
    "city": "San Francisco",
    "country_iso": "US",
    "state_iso": "CA",
    "zip": "94107"
  },
  "name": "isp-gateway.example.com",
  "netmask": "255.255.255.0",
  "version": 1
}
```

IP address information for the ISP hop. Fields marked as PII-gated (`name`, `address`, `netmask`, and all `location` sub-fields) will be returned as the literal string `"REDACTED"` for callers that do not have the PII permission. `asn`, `aso`, and `version` are always returned regardless of PII access.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|address|string|false|none|IP address. Returned as `"REDACTED"` without PII permission.|
|asn|integer|false|none|Autonomous System Number.|
|aso|string|false|none|Autonomous System Organization name.|
|location|[digital-experience-monitoring_ip_location](#schemadigital-experience-monitoring_ip_location)|false|none|Geographic location information. All fields are returned as the literal string `"REDACTED"` for callers that do not have the PII permission.<br>|
|name|string|false|none|Named IP address (reverse DNS hostname when available). Returned as `"REDACTED"` without PII permission.|
|netmask|string|false|none|Network mask. Returned as `"REDACTED"` without PII permission.|
|version|integer|false|none|IP version (`1` for IPv4, `2` for IPv6, `0` if unknown).|

<h2 id="tocS_dlp_PayloadLogMaskingLevel">dlp_PayloadLogMaskingLevel</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadlp_payloadlogmaskinglevel"></a>
<a id="schema_dlp_PayloadLogMaskingLevel"></a>
<a id="tocSdlp_payloadlogmaskinglevel"></a>
<a id="tocsdlp_payloadlogmaskinglevel"></a>

```json
"full"
```

Masking level for payload logs.

- `full`: The entire payload is masked.
- `partial`: Only partial payload content is masked.
- `clear`: No masking is applied to the payload content.
- `default`: DLP uses its default masking behavior.

<h2 id="tocS_dlp_PayloadLogSettingUpdate">dlp_PayloadLogSettingUpdate</h2>

```json
{
  "masking_level": "default",
  "public_key": "string"
}
```

Request model for payload log settings within the DLP settings endpoint.
Unlike the legacy endpoint, null and missing are treated identically here
(both mean "not provided" for PATCH, "reset to default" for PUT).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|masking_level|object|false|none|none|
|public_key|string \| null|false|none|Base64-encoded public key for encrypting payload logs.<br><br>- Set to a non-empty base64 string to enable payload logging with the given key.<br>- Set to an empty string to disable payload logging.<br>- Omit or set to null to leave unchanged (PATCH) or reset to disabled (PUT).|

```json
{
  "masking_level": {},
  "public_key": "string"
}
```

Request model for the legacy payload log settings endpoint.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|masking_level|object|false|none|none|
|public_key|string \| null|false|none|Base64-encoded public key for encrypting payload logs.<br><br>- Set to null or empty string to disable payload logging.<br>- Set to a non-empty base64 string to enable payload logging with the given key.<br><br>For customers with configurable payload masking feature rolled out:<br>- If the field is missing, the existing setting will be kept. Note that this is different from setting to null or empty string.<br><br>For all other customers:<br>- If the field is missing, the existing setting will be cleared.|


How much a word contributes to a match's confidence when it is found nearby.

Separate from a profile's high/medium/low confidence threshold: this describes how telling the
word is, not how confident the resulting match is.

<h2 id="tocS_dlp_ProximityWordValidatorWrite">dlp_ProximityWordValidatorWrite</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadlp_proximitywordvalidatorwrite"></a>
<a id="schema_dlp_ProximityWordValidatorWrite"></a>
<a id="tocSdlp_proximitywordvalidatorwrite"></a>
<a id="tocsdlp_proximitywordvalidatorwrite"></a>

```json
{
  "name": "HIPAA context words",
  "words": [
    {
      "weight": "strong",
      "word": "social security number"
    }
  ]
}
```

The attributes of a proximity word validator.

A write replaces both fields in full, so `PUT` must send the complete word list, not just the
words that changed. The computed fields a `GET` returns (`id`, `kind`, `referenced_by`,
`created_at`, `updated_at`) are ignored if sent, so a response can be edited and submitted back
as-is.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|A name for this validator, at most 50 characters.|
|words|[[dlp_ProximityWord](#schemadlp_proximityword)]|true|none|The words that raise confidence when found near a match, at most 100 per validator. Matching<br>ignores case, so the list may not contain the same word twice with different capitalisation.<br>Words are stored as sent.<br><br>For example, a validator for medical record numbers might use<br>`[{"word": "patient", "weight": "strong"}, {"word": "diagnosis", "weight": "moderate"},<br>{"word": "mrn", "weight": "weak"}]`.|

|---|---|---|---|---|
|max_match_bytes|integer(int32) \| null|false|none|Maximum number of bytes that the regular expression can match.<br><br>If this is `null` then there is no limit on the length. Patterns can use<br>`*` and `+`. Otherwise repeats should use a range `{m,n}` to restrict<br>patterns to the length. If this field is missing, then a default length<br>limit is used.<br><br>Note that the length is specified in bytes. Since regular expressions<br>use UTF-8 the pattern `.` can match up to 4 bytes. Hence `.{1,256}`<br>has a maximum length of 1024 bytes.|
|regex|string|true|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_dns-firewall_dns-firewall-cluster">dns-firewall_dns-firewall-cluster</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadns-firewall_dns-firewall-cluster"></a>
<a id="schema_dns-firewall_dns-firewall-cluster"></a>
<a id="tocSdns-firewall_dns-firewall-cluster"></a>
<a id="tocsdns-firewall_dns-firewall-cluster"></a>

```json
{
  "attack_mitigation": {
    "enabled": true,
    "only_when_upstream_unhealthy": false
  },
  "deprecate_any_requests": true,
  "ecs_fallback": false,
  "maximum_cache_ttl": 900,
  "minimum_cache_ttl": 60,
  "name": "My Awesome DNS Firewall cluster",
  "negative_cache_ttl": 900,
  "ratelimit": 600,
  "retries": 2,
  "upstream_ips": [
    "192.0.2.1",
    "198.51.100.1",
    "2001:DB8:100::CF"
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|attack_mitigation|[dns-firewall_attack_mitigation](#schemadns-firewall_attack_mitigation)|false|none|Attack mitigation settings|
|deprecate_any_requests|[dns-firewall_deprecate_any_requests](#schemadns-firewall_deprecate_any_requests)|false|none|Whether to refuse to answer queries for the ANY type|
|ecs_fallback|[dns-firewall_ecs_fallback](#schemadns-firewall_ecs_fallback)|false|none|Whether to forward client IP (resolver) subnet if no EDNS Client Subnet is sent|
|maximum_cache_ttl|[dns-firewall_maximum_cache_ttl](#schemadns-firewall_maximum_cache_ttl)|false|none|By default, Cloudflare attempts to cache responses for as long as<br>indicated by the TTL received from upstream nameservers. This setting<br>sets an upper bound on this duration. For caching purposes, higher TTLs<br>will be decreased to the maximum value defined by this setting.<br><br>This setting does not affect the TTL value in the DNS response<br>Cloudflare returns to clients. Cloudflare will always forward the TTL<br>value received from upstream nameservers.<br>|
|minimum_cache_ttl|[dns-firewall_minimum_cache_ttl](#schemadns-firewall_minimum_cache_ttl)|false|none|By default, Cloudflare attempts to cache responses for as long as<br>indicated by the TTL received from upstream nameservers. This setting<br>sets a lower bound on this duration. For caching purposes, lower TTLs<br>will be increased to the minimum value defined by this setting.<br><br>This setting does not affect the TTL value in the DNS response<br>Cloudflare returns to clients. Cloudflare will always forward the TTL<br>value received from upstream nameservers.<br><br>Note that, even with this setting, there is no guarantee that a<br>response will be cached for at least the specified duration. Cached<br>responses may be removed earlier for capacity or other operational<br>reasons.<br>|
|name|[dns-firewall_name](#schemadns-firewall_name)|false|none|DNS Firewall cluster name|
|negative_cache_ttl|[dns-firewall_negative_cache_ttl](#schemadns-firewall_negative_cache_ttl)|false|none|This setting controls how long DNS Firewall should cache negative<br>responses (e.g., NXDOMAIN) from the upstream servers.<br><br>This setting does not affect the TTL value in the DNS response<br>Cloudflare returns to clients. Cloudflare will always forward the TTL<br>value received from upstream nameservers.<br>|
|ratelimit|[dns-firewall_ratelimit](#schemadns-firewall_ratelimit)|false|none|Maximum number of DNS queries per second that will be forwarded to your upstream nameservers. The limit is enforced per server, where each server receives a fraction of the configured value. The actual aggregate rate for a data center may vary depending on how many servers are present. Responses served from cache do not count toward this limit. Set to null to disable rate limiting.|
|retries|[dns-firewall_retries](#schemadns-firewall_retries)|false|none|Number of retries for fetching DNS responses from upstream nameservers (not counting the initial attempt)|
|upstream_ips|[dns-firewall_upstream_ips](#schemadns-firewall_upstream_ips)|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_dns-firewall_maximum_cache_ttl">dns-firewall_maximum_cache_ttl</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadns-firewall_maximum_cache_ttl"></a>
<a id="schema_dns-firewall_maximum_cache_ttl"></a>
<a id="tocSdns-firewall_maximum_cache_ttl"></a>
<a id="tocsdns-firewall_maximum_cache_ttl"></a>

```json
900
```

By default, Cloudflare attempts to cache responses for as long as
indicated by the TTL received from upstream nameservers. This setting
sets an upper bound on this duration. For caching purposes, higher TTLs
will be decreased to the maximum value defined by this setting.

This setting does not affect the TTL value in the DNS response
Cloudflare returns to clients. Cloudflare will always forward the TTL
value received from upstream nameservers.

<a id="tocsdns-firewall_minimum_cache_ttl"></a>

```json
60
```

By default, Cloudflare attempts to cache responses for as long as
indicated by the TTL received from upstream nameservers. This setting
sets a lower bound on this duration. For caching purposes, lower TTLs
will be increased to the minimum value defined by this setting.

This setting does not affect the TTL value in the DNS response
Cloudflare returns to clients. Cloudflare will always forward the TTL
value received from upstream nameservers.

Note that, even with this setting, there is no guarantee that a
response will be cached for at least the specified duration. Cached
responses may be removed earlier for capacity or other operational
reasons.

Settings for the DNS record.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ipv4_only|boolean|false|none|When enabled, only A records will be generated, and AAAA records will not be created. This setting is intended for exceptional cases. Note that this option only applies to proxied records and it has no effect on whether Cloudflare communicates with the origin using IPv4 or IPv6.|
|ipv6_only|boolean|false|none|When enabled, only AAAA records will be generated, and A records will not be created. This setting is intended for exceptional cases. Note that this option only applies to proxied records and it has no effect on whether Cloudflare communicates with the origin using IPv4 or IPv6.|

<h2 id="tocS_dns-settings_enforce_dns_only">dns-settings_enforce_dns_only</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadns-settings_enforce_dns_only"></a>
<a id="schema_dns-settings_enforce_dns_only"></a>
<a id="tocSdns-settings_enforce_dns_only"></a>
<a id="tocsdns-settings_enforce_dns_only"></a>

```json
false
```

When enabled, forces all proxied DNS records in the account to behave as DNS-only at the edge, regardless of each record's individual proxy setting. Note that this account-level override does not modify the records themselves; it only affects how they are served at the edge. See more on [Enforce DNS-only](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/enforce-dns-only).

<a id="tocsdns-settings_nameserver-set-patch"></a>

```json
{
  "name": "Production nameservers"
}
```

Updates only the customer-defined name. All other fields are rejected, even if unchanged. An empty object or the current name succeeds without changing the set. A null name is invalid. Requires the account-scoped creation entitlements, including eligibility for the set's current IP set and the Advanced entitlement for an Advanced set.

The name can be changed without changing the set's nameservers or addresses.|

Components of the zone's SOA record.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expire|number|false|none|Time in seconds of being unable to query the primary server after which secondary servers should stop serving the zone.|
|min_ttl|number|false|none|The time to live (TTL) for negative caching of records within the zone.|
|mname|string \| null|false|none|The primary nameserver, which may be used for outbound zone transfers. If null, a Cloudflare-assigned value will be used.|
|refresh|number|false|none|Time in seconds after which secondary servers should re-check the SOA record to see if the zone has been updated.|
|retry|number|false|none|Time in seconds after which secondary servers should retry queries after the primary server was unresponsive.|
|rname|string|false|none|The email address of the zone administrator, with the first label representing the local part of the email address.|
|ttl|number|false|none|The time to live (TTL) of the SOA record itself.|
