<h2 id="tocS_dnssec_dnssec_multi_signer">dnssec_dnssec_multi_signer</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadnssec_dnssec_multi_signer"></a>
<a id="schema_dnssec_dnssec_multi_signer"></a>
<a id="tocSdnssec_dnssec_multi_signer"></a>
<a id="tocsdnssec_dnssec_multi_signer"></a>

```json
false
```

If true, multi-signer DNSSEC is enabled on the zone, allowing multiple
providers to serve a DNSSEC-signed zone at the same time.
This is required for DNSKEY records (except those automatically
generated by Cloudflare) to be added to the zone.

See [Multi-signer DNSSEC](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/dnssec/multi-signer-dnssec/) for details.

<h2 id="tocS_dnssec_dnssec_presigned">dnssec_dnssec_presigned</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadnssec_dnssec_presigned"></a>
<a id="schema_dnssec_dnssec_presigned"></a>
<a id="tocSdnssec_dnssec_presigned"></a>
<a id="tocsdnssec_dnssec_presigned"></a>

```json
true
```

If true, allows Cloudflare to transfer in a DNSSEC-signed zone
including signatures from an external provider, without requiring
Cloudflare to sign any records on the fly.

Note that this feature has some limitations.
See [Cloudflare as Secondary](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/zone-transfers/cloudflare-as-secondary/setup/#dnssec) for details.

<h2 id="tocS_dnssec_dnssec_use_nsec3">dnssec_dnssec_use_nsec3</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadnssec_dnssec_use_nsec3"></a>
<a id="schema_dnssec_dnssec_use_nsec3"></a>
<a id="tocSdnssec_dnssec_use_nsec3"></a>
<a id="tocsdnssec_dnssec_use_nsec3"></a>

```json
false
```

If true, enables the use of NSEC3 together with DNSSEC on the zone.
Combined with setting dnssec_presigned to true, this enables the use of
NSEC3 records when transferring in from an external provider.
If dnssec_presigned is instead set to false (default), NSEC3 records will be
generated and signed at request time.

See [DNSSEC with NSEC3](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/dnssec/enable-nsec3/) for details.

```json
{
  "block_any_queries": true,
  "burst_sensitivity": "string",
  "created_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",

  "mode": "string",
  "modified_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "name": "string",
  "profile_sensitivity": "string",
  "rate_sensitivity": "string",
  "scope": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|block_any_queries|boolean|true|none|Whether to block DNS ANY queries. Defaults to true.|
|burst_sensitivity|string|true|none|The burst sensitivity. Must be one of 'low', 'medium', 'high'.|
|created_on|string(date-time)|true|none|The creation timestamp of the DNS Protection rule.|
|id|string|true|none|The unique ID of the DNS Protection rule.|
|mode|string|true|none|The mode for DNS Protection. Must be one of 'enabled', 'disabled', 'monitoring'.|
|modified_on|string(date-time)|true|none|The last modification timestamp of the DNS Protection rule.|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the DNS Protection rule. Value is relative to the 'scope' setting. For 'global' scope, name should be 'global'. For either the 'region' or 'datacenter' scope, name should be the actual name of the region or datacenter, e.g., 'wnam' or 'lax'.|
|profile_sensitivity|string|true|none|The profile sensitivity. Recommended setting is 'low'. Must be one of 'low', 'medium', 'high', or 'very_high'.|
|rate_sensitivity|string|true|none|The rate sensitivity. Must be one of 'low', 'medium', 'high'.|
|scope|string|true|none|The scope for the DNS Protection rule. Must be one of 'global', 'region', or 'datacenter'.|

<h2 id="tocS_email-auth_DmarcStatus">email-auth_DmarcStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaemail-auth_dmarcstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_email-auth_DmarcStatus"></a>
<a id="tocSemail-auth_dmarcstatus"></a>
<a id="tocsemail-auth_dmarcstatus"></a>

```json
"missing-dmarc-report"
```

DMARC configuration status. The API omits this field when DMARC is correctly configured. If the zone lacks a DMARC TXT record of its own, the API resolves _dmarc.{zone} recursively and evaluates whatever that lookup returns. A CNAME at _dmarc.{zone} that points to a valid DMARC record is therefore healthy; the cname-on-dmarc-record value means the CNAME resolves to no DMARC record at all.

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|content|string|false|none|Record content|
|id|string|false|none|DNS record ID|
|name|string|false|none|DNS record name|
|resolved|[string]|false|none|For a CNAME record, the TXT content(s) found by following the CNAME chain to its target. An empty array means the chain was resolved but nothing usable was found there; omitted/null means resolution was not attempted for this record (always the case for non-CNAME entries). A CNAME chain that terminates in more than one TXT value at the target yields multiple entries. Populated on entries in cname_dmarc_records, cname_spf_records, and cname_dkim_records.|
|ttl|integer|false|none|Time to live in seconds|
|type|string|false|none|Record type|

<h2 id="tocS_email-auth_InspectError">email-auth_InspectError</h2>

```json
}
```

An error encountered during SPF inspection

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|code|string|true|none|Error code. Known values:<br>- `lookup_failed` — DNS TXT lookup failed<br>- `spf_not_found` — no SPF record found<br>- `invalid_spf` — record does not start with `v=spf1`<br>- `invalid_domain` — PSL validation failed<br>- `loop_detected` — include/redirect cycle detected<br>- `invalid_mechanism` — unrecognised or malformed mechanism<br>- `resource_limit_exceeded` — internal resource protection limits exceeded (recursion depth or query budget)<br>- `max_lookups` — RFC 7208 10-lookup limit exceeded<br>|
|details|string|false|none|Additional error-specific details (optional).<br>- For `invalid_domain` errors: the invalid domain string<br>- For `invalid_mechanism` errors: the invalid mechanism text (e.g., "invalidmech123")<br>- For `loop_detected` errors: the domain that caused the loop<br>- For other error types: not present<br>|
|domain|string|true|none|Domain where the error occurred|
|message|string|true|none|Human-readable error message|

A DMARC TXT record that a recursive lookup of _dmarc.{zone} returned. Such a record usually lives in another zone outside this account's control, so this schema omits the DNS record ID. The API therefore treats such a record as read-only.

|name|string|false|none|The name the API queried.|

<h2 id="tocS_email-auth_SpfComponent">email-auth_SpfComponent</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaemail-auth_spfcomponent"></a>
<a id="schema_email-auth_SpfComponent"></a>
<a id="tocSemail-auth_spfcomponent"></a>
<a id="tocsemail-auth_spfcomponent"></a>

```json
{
  "lookup_count": 0,
  "nested": {
    "components": [
      {}
    ],
    "domain": "example.com",
    "errors": [],
    "record": "v=spf1 ip4:203.0.113.1 include:spf.example.com -all",
    "total_lookups": 2
  },
  "result": "pass",
  "type": "IP4",
  "value": "203.0.113.1"
}
```

A single SPF component (mechanism) in the inspection tree.

The `value` field includes the qualifier prefix (e.g., "-all", "~mx:example.com")
to match the raw SPF record syntax. The qualifier is also available separately
in the `result` field for programmatic access.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|lookup_count|integer|true|none|Number of DNS lookups this component requires (per RFC 7208).<br>- MX, A, EXISTS, INCLUDE, REDIRECT, PTR: 1<br>- IP4, IP6, ALL: 0<br>|
|nested|object|false|none|Nested SPF tree for INCLUDE or REDIRECT mechanisms.<br>Only present for INCLUDE/REDIRECT components.<br>|
|result|[email-auth_SpfResult](#schemaemail-auth_spfresult)|true|none|SPF mechanism result qualifier|
|type|string|true|none|Component type (UPPERCASE)|
|value|string|true|none|Component value with qualifier prefix.<br>For IP4/IP6, stores just the IP address (no "ip4:" or "ip6:" prefix).<br>Examples: "203.0.113.1", "203.0.113.0/24", "2001:db8::1/64", "-all", "~mx:example.com", "include:_spf.example.com"<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|result|pass|
|result|neutral|
|result|fail|
|result|soft_fail|
|result|none|
|result|temp_error|
|result|perm_error|
|type|ALL|
|type|A|
|type|MX|
|type|IP4|
|type|IP6|
|type|EXISTS|
|type|INCLUDE|
|type|PTR|
|type|REDIRECT|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|comments|string \| null|false|none|none|
|created_at|object|true|read-only|none|
|expires_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Timestamp at which the policy expires. After this time, Email Security ignores the policy. The value must lie in the future. Send `null` to clear the expiration.|
|id|object|true|read-only|none|
|is_acceptable_sender|boolean|false|none|Exempts messages from this sender from Spam, Spoof and Bulk dispositions only; Malicious and Suspicious dispositions still apply.|
|is_exempt_recipient|boolean|false|none|Bypasses all detections for messages to this recipient.|
|is_recipient|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated as of July 1, 2025. Use `is_exempt_recipient` instead. End of life: July 1, 2026.|
|is_regex|boolean|false|none|none|
|is_sender|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated as of July 1, 2025. Use `is_trusted_sender` instead. End of life: July 1, 2026.|
|is_spoof|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated as of July 1, 2025. Use `is_acceptable_sender` instead. End of life: July 1, 2026.|
|is_trusted_sender|boolean|false|none|Bypasses all detections and link following for messages from this sender.|
|last_modified|object|true|read-only|**Deprecated.** Deprecated, use `modified_at` instead. End of life: November 1, 2026.|
|modified_at|object|false|read-only|none|
|pattern|string|false|none|The pattern value to match. The format depends on `pattern_type`: a valid email address for EMAIL (e.g. `user@example.com`), a valid domain name for DOMAIN (e.g. `example.com`), or a plain IPv4 or IPv6 address or CIDR block for IP (e.g. `1.2.3.4`, `1.2.3.0/24`, `2606:4700:4700::1111`, or `2606:4700:4700::/48`); the API rejects private or unique-local, loopback, link-local, unspecified, and IPv4 broadcast addresses, including their IPv4-mapped IPv6 equivalents.|
|pattern_type|[email-security_PatternType](#schemaemail-security_patterntype)|false|none|Type of pattern matching.<br>- EMAIL: matches a full email address (e.g. `user@example.com`)<br>- DOMAIN: matches a domain name (e.g. `example.com`)<br>- IP: matches a plain IPv4 or IPv6 address (e.g. `1.2.3.4` or `2606:4700:4700::1111`) or CIDR block (e.g. `1.2.3.0/24` or `2606:4700:4700::/48`). The API rejects private or unique-local, loopback, link-local, unspecified, and IPv4 broadcast addresses, including their IPv4-mapped IPv6 equivalents.<br>- UNKNOWN: deprecated; you cannot use this when creating or updating policies, but it may appear on existing entries.<br>|
|verify_sender|boolean|false|none|Enforce DMARC, SPF or DKIM authentication. When on, Email Security only honors policies that pass authentication.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|comments|string \| null|false|none|none|

|expires_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Timestamp at which the policy expires. After this time, Email Security ignores the policy. The value must lie in the future. Send `null` to clear the expiration.|
|id|object|true|read-only|none|
|is_acceptable_sender|boolean|true|none|Exempts messages from this sender from Spam, Spoof and Bulk dispositions only; Malicious and Suspicious dispositions still apply.|
|is_exempt_recipient|boolean|true|none|Bypasses all detections for messages to this recipient.|
|is_recipient|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated as of July 1, 2025. Use `is_exempt_recipient` instead. End of life: July 1, 2026.|
|is_regex|boolean|true|none|none|

|is_spoof|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated as of July 1, 2025. Use `is_acceptable_sender` instead. End of life: July 1, 2026.|
|is_trusted_sender|boolean|true|none|Bypasses all detections and link following for messages from this sender.|
|last_modified|object|true|read-only|**Deprecated.** Deprecated, use `modified_at` instead. End of life: November 1, 2026.|
|modified_at|object|false|read-only|none|
|pattern|string|true|none|The pattern value to match. The format depends on `pattern_type`: a valid email address for EMAIL (e.g. `user@example.com`), a valid domain name for DOMAIN (e.g. `example.com`), or a plain IPv4 or IPv6 address or CIDR block for IP (e.g. `1.2.3.4`, `1.2.3.0/24`, `2606:4700:4700::1111`, or `2606:4700:4700::/48`); the API rejects private or unique-local, loopback, link-local, unspecified, and IPv4 broadcast addresses, including their IPv4-mapped IPv6 equivalents.|
|pattern_type|[email-security_PatternType](#schemaemail-security_patterntype)|true|none|Type of pattern matching.<br>- EMAIL: matches a full email address (e.g. `user@example.com`)<br>- DOMAIN: matches a domain name (e.g. `example.com`)<br>- IP: matches a plain IPv4 or IPv6 address (e.g. `1.2.3.4` or `2606:4700:4700::1111`) or CIDR block (e.g. `1.2.3.0/24` or `2606:4700:4700::/48`). The API rejects private or unique-local, loopback, link-local, unspecified, and IPv4 broadcast addresses, including their IPv4-mapped IPv6 equivalents.<br>- UNKNOWN: deprecated; you cannot use this when creating or updating policies, but it may appear on existing entries.<br>|
|verify_sender|boolean|true|none|Enforce DMARC, SPF or DKIM authentication. When on, Email Security only honors policies that pass authentication.|

<h2 id="tocS_email-security_PatternType">email-security_PatternType</h2>

<a id="schema_email-security_PatternType"></a>
<a id="tocSemail-security_patterntype"></a>
<a id="tocsemail-security_patterntype"></a>

```json
"EMAIL"
```

Type of pattern matching.
- EMAIL: matches a full email address (e.g. `user@example.com`)
- DOMAIN: matches a domain name (e.g. `example.com`)
- IP: matches a plain IPv4 or IPv6 address (e.g. `1.2.3.4` or `2606:4700:4700::1111`) or CIDR block (e.g. `1.2.3.0/24` or `2606:4700:4700::/48`). The API rejects private or unique-local, loopback, link-local, unspecified, and IPv4 broadcast addresses, including their IPv4-mapped IPv6 equivalents.
- UNKNOWN: deprecated; you cannot use this when creating or updating policies, but it may appear on existing entries.

|lookback_hops|integer \| null|false|none|Number of hops to trace back through received headers when reconstructing the original message (1-20).|
|regions|[[email-security_Region](#schemaemail-security_region)]|true|none|Regions that process messages for this domain, e.g. `["GLOBAL"]` or `["US"]`.|
|require_tls_inbound|boolean \| null|false|none|Require TLS on inbound connections.|
|require_tls_outbound|boolean \| null|false|none|Require TLS on outbound connections.|
|transport|string \| null|false|none|The mail transport hostname for MX/Inline delivery — the MX record Cloudflare delivers email to (e.g. `mx.example.com`).|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|comments|string \| null|false|none|none|

|id|object|true|read-only|none|
|is_acceptable_sender|boolean|false|none|Exempts messages from this sender from Spam, Spoof and Bulk dispositions only; Malicious and Suspicious dispositions still apply.|
|is_exempt_recipient|boolean|false|none|Bypasses all detections for messages to this recipient.|
|is_recipient|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated as of July 1, 2025. Use `is_exempt_recipient` instead. End of life: July 1, 2026.|
|is_regex|boolean|false|none|none|
|is_sender|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated as of July 1, 2025. Use `is_trusted_sender` instead. End of life: July 1, 2026.|
|is_spoof|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated as of July 1, 2025. Use `is_acceptable_sender` instead. End of life: July 1, 2026.|
|is_trusted_sender|boolean|false|none|Bypasses all detections and link following for messages from this sender.|
|last_modified|object|true|read-only|**Deprecated.** Deprecated, use `modified_at` instead. End of life: November 1, 2026.|
|modified_at|object|false|read-only|none|
|pattern|string|false|none|The pattern value to match. The format depends on `pattern_type`: a valid email address for EMAIL (e.g. `user@example.com`), a valid domain name for DOMAIN (e.g. `example.com`), or a plain IPv4 or IPv6 address or CIDR block for IP (e.g. `1.2.3.4`, `1.2.3.0/24`, `2606:4700:4700::1111`, or `2606:4700:4700::/48`); the API rejects private or unique-local, loopback, link-local, unspecified, and IPv4 broadcast addresses, including their IPv4-mapped IPv6 equivalents.|
|pattern_type|[email-security_PatternType](#schemaemail-security_patterntype)|false|none|Type of pattern matching.<br>- EMAIL: matches a full email address (e.g. `user@example.com`)<br>- DOMAIN: matches a domain name (e.g. `example.com`)<br>- IP: matches a plain IPv4 or IPv6 address (e.g. `1.2.3.4` or `2606:4700:4700::1111`) or CIDR block (e.g. `1.2.3.0/24` or `2606:4700:4700::/48`). The API rejects private or unique-local, loopback, link-local, unspecified, and IPv4 broadcast addresses, including their IPv4-mapped IPv6 equivalents.<br>- UNKNOWN: deprecated; you cannot use this when creating or updating policies, but it may appear on existing entries.<br>|
|verify_sender|boolean|false|none|Enforce DMARC, SPF or DKIM authentication. When on, Email Security only honors policies that pass authentication.|

|pattern_type|[email-security_PatternType](#schemaemail-security_patterntype)|false|none|Type of pattern matching.<br>- EMAIL: matches a full email address (e.g. `user@example.com`)<br>- DOMAIN: matches a domain name (e.g. `example.com`)<br>- IP: matches a plain IPv4 or IPv6 address (e.g. `1.2.3.4` or `2606:4700:4700::1111`) or CIDR block (e.g. `1.2.3.0/24` or `2606:4700:4700::/48`). The API rejects private or unique-local, loopback, link-local, unspecified, and IPv4 broadcast addresses, including their IPv4-mapped IPv6 equivalents.<br>- UNKNOWN: deprecated; you cannot use this when creating or updating policies, but it may appear on existing entries.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_email_sending_subdomain">email_sending_subdomain</h2>

<a id="schema_email_sending_subdomain"></a>
<a id="tocSemail_sending_subdomain"></a>
<a id="tocsemail_sending_subdomain"></a>

```json
{
  "created": "2014-01-02T02:20:00Z",
  "dkim_selector": "cf-bounce",
  "drop_suppressed_recipients": false,
  "enabled": true,
  "modified": "2014-01-02T02:20:00Z",
  "name": "sub.example.com",
  "preview_enabled": true,
  "return_path_domain": "cf-bounce.sub.example.com",
  "tag": "aabbccdd11223344aabbccdd11223344"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|[email_created](#schemaemail_created)|false|read-only|The date and time the destination address has been created.|
|dkim_selector|string|false|read-only|The DKIM selector used for email signing. Wildcard rows publish the selector and sign with `d=<base>`.|
|drop_suppressed_recipients|boolean|false|none|Whether a send request that includes a recipient suppressed on<br>this subdomain drops that recipient and still delivers to the<br>rest, instead of failing the entire request.<br>|
|enabled|boolean|true|read-only|Whether Email Sending is enabled on this subdomain.|
|modified|[email_modified](#schemaemail_modified)|false|read-only|The date and time the destination address was last modified.|
|name|string|true|none|The exact domain name or a leftmost wildcard such as `*.example.com`.|
|preview_enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether sent messages from this subdomain can be previewed in the activity log.|
|return_path_domain|string|false|read-only|The return-path domain used for bounce handling. Wildcard rows use `cf-bounce.<base>`.|
|tag|[email_sending_subdomain_identifier](#schemaemail_sending_subdomain_identifier)|true|read-only|Sending subdomain identifier.|

|code|string|true|none|Error code identifying the type of issue. `dkim.conflict` is<br>reported whenever 2+ TXT records exist at the DKIM selector,<br>even if one matches the canonical Cloudflare content — multi-record<br>DKIM can permerror at recipient verification regardless of which<br>entry is correct. `domainkey.delegated` indicates that<br>`_domainkey.<subdomain>` has NS records in the Cloudflare zone,<br>creating a zone cut that shadows the DKIM TXT record we publish;<br>the customer must remove the NS delegation for DKIM to verify.<br>`dmarc.incompatible` indicates that a wildcard sending row no longer<br>satisfies its DMARC safety requirements, such as relaxed alignment,<br>a valid governing policy, and the organizational-domain constraint.<br>The customer must correct the zone or policy configuration manually;<br>DNS Fix cannot resolve this error.<br>`sending_subdomain.conflict` is reported by preview when an enabled<br>explicit or wildcard sending row would give some senders a different<br>signing identity.<br>|
|conflicting_subdomain|string|false|none|The enabled sending-subdomain row that conflicts with the requested name.|
|existing|object|false|none|The conflicting DNS record found in the zone.|
|missing|object|false|none|The DNS record that must be added to resolve this error.|
|multiple|[[email_dns_record](#schemaemail_dns_record)]|false|none|Multiple conflicting DNS records found, for example more than one SPF or DMARC TXT record.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|code|mx.missing|
|code|mx.foreign|
|code|spf.missing|
|code|spf.foreign|
|code|spf.multiple|
|code|dkim.missing|
|code|dkim.conflict|
|code|dmarc.missing|
|code|dmarc.multiple|
|code|dmarc.incompatible|
|code|domainkey.delegated|
|code|sending_subdomain.conflict|

Represents the allocation value for an entitlement. The shape of `value` depends on `type`: `bool` uses a boolean, `max_count` uses an integer, `enum_number` uses an array of numbers, `range` uses an object with `min` and `max` integer fields, and `string` uses a string.

The action to perform when the threshold of matched traffic within the configured period is exceeded.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|object|false|none|none|

The custom response configured in this object will override the custom error for the zone. This object is optional.<br>Notes: If you omit this object, Cloudflare will use the default HTML error page. If "mode" is "challenge", "managed_challenge", or "js_challenge", Cloudflare will use the zone challenge pages and you should not provide the "response" object.|
|timeout|[firewall_timeout](#schemafirewall_timeout)|false|none|The time in seconds during which Cloudflare will perform the mitigation action. Must be an integer value greater than or equal to the period.<br>Notes: If "mode" is "challenge", "managed_challenge", or "js_challenge", Cloudflare will use the zone's Challenge Passage time and you should not provide this value.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|detection_mode|[firewall_detection_mode](#schemafirewall_detection_mode)|true|read-only|The mode that defines how rules within the package are evaluated during the course of a request. When a package uses anomaly detection mode (`anomaly` value), each rule is given a score when triggered. If the total score of all triggered rules exceeds the sensitivity defined in the WAF package, the action configured in the package will be performed. Traditional detection mode (`traditional` value) will decide the action to take when it is triggered by the request. If multiple rules are triggered, the action providing the highest protection will be applied (for example, a 'block' action will win over a 'challenge' action).|
|id|[firewall_identifier](#schemafirewall_identifier)|true|read-only|Defines an identifier.|
|name|[firewall_name](#schemafirewall_name)|true|read-only|The name of the WAF package.|
|status|[firewall_status](#schemafirewall_status)|false|read-only|When set to `active`, indicates that the WAF package will be applied to the zone.|
|zone_id|[firewall_identifier](#schemafirewall_identifier)|true|read-only|Defines an identifier.|
|action_mode|[firewall_action_mode](#schemafirewall_action_mode)|true|none|The default action performed by the rules in the WAF package.|
|description|[firewall_anomaly_description](#schemafirewall_anomaly_description)|true|read-only|A summary of the purpose/function of the WAF package.|
|detection_mode|[firewall_anomaly_detection_mode](#schemafirewall_anomaly_detection_mode)|true|read-only|When a WAF package uses anomaly detection, each rule is given a score when triggered. If the total score of all triggered rules exceeds the sensitivity defined on the WAF package, the action defined on the package will be taken.|
|name|[firewall_anomaly_name](#schemafirewall_anomaly_name)|true|read-only|The name of the WAF package.|

<h2 id="tocS_firewall_custom_response">firewall_custom_response</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemafirewall_custom_response"></a>
<a id="schema_firewall_custom_response"></a>
<a id="tocSfirewall_custom_response"></a>
<a id="tocsfirewall_custom_response"></a>

```json
{
  "body": "<error>This request has been rate-limited.</error>",
  "content_type": "text/xml"
}
```

A custom content type and reponse to return when the threshold is exceeded. The custom response configured in this object will override the custom error for the zone. This object is optional.
Notes: If you omit this object, Cloudflare will use the default HTML error page. If "mode" is "challenge", "managed_challenge", or "js_challenge", Cloudflare will use the zone challenge pages and you should not provide the "response" object.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|object|false|none|none|
|body|[firewall_body](#schemafirewall_body)|false|none|The response body to return. The value must conform to the configured content type.|
|content_type|[firewall_content_type](#schemafirewall_content_type)|false|none|The content type of the body. Must be one of the following: `text/plain`, `text/xml`, or `application/json`.|

<h2 id="tocS_firewall_detection_mode">firewall_detection_mode</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemafirewall_detection_mode"></a>
<a id="schema_firewall_detection_mode"></a>
<a id="tocSfirewall_detection_mode"></a>
<a id="tocsfirewall_detection_mode"></a>

```json
"traditional"
```

The mode that defines how rules within the package are evaluated during the course of a request. When a package uses anomaly detection mode (`anomaly` value), each rule is given a score when triggered. If the total score of all triggered rules exceeds the sensitivity defined in the WAF package, the action configured in the package will be performed. Traditional detection mode (`traditional` value) will decide the action to take when it is triggered by the request. If multiple rules are triggered, the action providing the highest protection will be applied (for example, a 'block' action will win over a 'challenge' action).

```json
true
```

When true, only the uncached traffic served from your origin servers will count towards rate limiting. In this case, any cached traffic served by Cloudflare will not count towards rate limiting. This field is optional.
Notes: This field is deprecated. Instead, use response headers and set "origin_traffic" to "false" to avoid legacy behaviour interacting with the "response_headers" property.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|description|[firewall_schemas-description](#schemafirewall_schemas-description)|true|read-only|A summary of the purpose/function of the WAF package.|
|detection_mode|[firewall_detection_mode](#schemafirewall_detection_mode)|true|read-only|The mode that defines how rules within the package are evaluated during the course of a request. When a package uses anomaly detection mode (`anomaly` value), each rule is given a score when triggered. If the total score of all triggered rules exceeds the sensitivity defined in the WAF package, the action configured in the package will be performed. Traditional detection mode (`traditional` value) will decide the action to take when it is triggered by the request. If multiple rules are triggered, the action providing the highest protection will be applied (for example, a 'block' action will win over a 'challenge' action).|
|id|[firewall_identifier](#schemafirewall_identifier)|true|read-only|Defines an identifier.|
|name|[firewall_name](#schemafirewall_name)|true|read-only|The name of the WAF package.|
|status|[firewall_status](#schemafirewall_status)|false|read-only|When set to `active`, indicates that the WAF package will be applied to the zone.|

An object that allows you to override the action of specific WAF rules. Each key of this object must be the ID of a WAF rule, and each value must be a valid WAF action. Unless you are disabling a rule, ensure that you also enable the rule group that this WAF rule belongs to. When creating a new URI-based WAF override, you must provide a `groups` object or a `rules` object.

<h2 id="tocS_flagship_Flag">flagship_Flag</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaflagship_flag"></a>
<a id="schema_flagship_Flag"></a>
<a id="tocSflagship_flag"></a>
<a id="tocsflagship_flag"></a>

```json
{
  "default_variation": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "enabled": true,
  "key": "string",
  "metadata": {
    "property1": true,
    "property2": true
  },
  "rules": [
    {
      "conditions": [
        {
          "attribute": "string",
          "operator": "equals",
          "value": "string"
        }
      ],
      "priority": 1,
      "rollout": {
        "attribute": "string",
        "percentage": 0
      },
      "serve_variation": "string"
    }
  ],
  "type": "boolean",
  "updated_at": "string",
  "updated_by": "string",
  "variations": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|default_variation|string|true|none|Variation the API serves when the flag is off, or when it's on but no rule matches the context. Must be a key in `variations`.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|Optional operator-facing description. It does not affect flag evaluation.|
|enabled|boolean|true|none|When false, the flag bypasses all rules and always serves `default_variation`.|
|key|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the flag within an app. Used in all evaluation and SDK calls.|
|metadata|object|false|none|Key-value metadata associated with the flag. Returned only when the flag has metadata.|
|rules|[[flagship_Rule](#schemaflagship_rule)]|true|none|Targeting rules evaluated in ascending `priority`; the first matching rule wins. An empty array means the flag always serves `default_variation`.|
|type|string|true|none|Server-inferred value type shared by all of the flag's variations.|
|updated_at|string|false|none|none|
|updated_by|string|false|none|none|
|variations|object|true|none|Map of variation name to value. All values share the same type (boolean, string, number, or JSON object/array), and each serialized value stays within 10KB.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|boolean|
|type|string|
|type|number|
|type|json|

<h2 id="tocS_fraud_auth_criteria">fraud_auth_criteria</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemafraud_auth_criteria"></a>
<a id="schema_fraud_auth_criteria"></a>
<a id="tocSfraud_auth_criteria"></a>
<a id="tocsfraud_auth_criteria"></a>

```json
{
  "kind": "status_code",
  "status_codes": [
    200,
    201
  ]
}
```

A criterion for determining authentication outcome. The `kind` field determines which
other fields are used for matching.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|kind|string|true|none|The type of criterion. Currently only `status_code` is supported.|
|status_codes|[integer]|false|none|HTTP status codes to match against the origin response.<br>- Maximum of 10 codes per criterion.<br>- Each code must be a valid HTTP status code (100-599).<br>- Codes are deduplicated and sorted on save.<br>- Omit to leave unchanged on update.<br>- Provide an empty array `[]` to clear codes on update.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|kind|status_code|

<h2 id="tocS_fraud_authentication_settings">fraud_authentication_settings</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemafraud_authentication_settings"></a>
<a id="schema_fraud_authentication_settings"></a>
<a id="tocSfraud_authentication_settings"></a>
<a id="tocsfraud_authentication_settings"></a>

```json
{
  "failure_criteria": {
    "kind": "status_code",
    "status_codes": [
      200,
      201
    ]
  },
  "success_criteria": {
    "kind": "status_code",
    "status_codes": [
      200,
      201
    ]
  }
}
```

Configuration for classifying login authentication outcomes based on the origin response.
Requires `user_profiles` to be enabled.

- Success and failure criteria are independently updatable — sending only `success_criteria`
  leaves failure codes untouched, and vice versa.
- Omit `authentication_settings` entirely to leave both unchanged.
- Status codes must not overlap between success and failure criteria.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|failure_criteria|object|false|none|Criterion for identifying failed login responses.|
|success_criteria|object|false|none|Criterion for identifying successful login responses.|

```json
{
```

```json
  "description": "Health check for www.example.com",
  "failure_reason": "",
  "http_config": {
    "allow_insecure": false,
    "expected_body": "success",
    "expected_codes": [
      "2xx",
      "302"
    ],
    "follow_redirects": false,
    "header": {
      "Host": [
        "example.com"
      ],
      "X-App-ID": [
        "abc123"
      ]
    },
    "method": "GET",
    "path": "/health",
    "port": 80
  },
  "id": "023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353",
  "interval": 60,
  "modified_on": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z",
  "name": "server-1",
  "retries": 2,
  "status": "healthy",
  "suspended": false,
  "tcp_config": {
    "method": "connection_established",
    "port": 80
  },
  "timeout": 5,
  "type": "HTTPS"
}
```

|consecutive_fails|[healthchecks_consecutive_fails](#schemahealthchecks_consecutive_fails)|false|none|The number of consecutive fails required from a health check before changing the health to unhealthy.|
|consecutive_successes|[healthchecks_consecutive_successes](#schemahealthchecks_consecutive_successes)|false|none|The number of consecutive successes required from a health check before changing the health to healthy.|

|id|[healthchecks_identifier](#schemahealthchecks_identifier)|false|read-only|Identifier|
|interval|[healthchecks_interval](#schemahealthchecks_interval)|false|none|The interval between each health check. Shorter intervals may give quicker notifications if the origin status changes, but will increase load on the origin as we check from multiple locations.|
|modified_on|[healthchecks_timestamp](#schemahealthchecks_timestamp)|false|read-only|none|
|name|[healthchecks_name](#schemahealthchecks_name)|false|none|A short name to identify the health check. Only alphanumeric characters, hyphens and underscores are allowed.|
|retries|[healthchecks_retries](#schemahealthchecks_retries)|false|none|The number of retries to attempt in case of a timeout before marking the origin as unhealthy. Retries are attempted immediately.|
|status|[healthchecks_status](#schemahealthchecks_status)|false|read-only|The current status of the origin server according to the health check.|
|suspended|[healthchecks_suspended](#schemahealthchecks_suspended)|false|none|If suspended, no health checks are sent to the origin.|
|tcp_config|[healthchecks_tcp_config](#schemahealthchecks_tcp_config)|false|none|Parameters specific to TCP health check.|
|timeout|[healthchecks_timeout](#schemahealthchecks_timeout)|false|none|The timeout (in seconds) before marking the health check as failed.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_insecure|boolean|false|none|Do not validate the certificate when the health check uses HTTPS.|
|expected_body|string|false|none|A case-insensitive sub-string to look for in the response body. If this string is not found, the origin will be marked as unhealthy.|
|expected_codes|[string]|false|none|The expected HTTP response codes (e.g. "200") or code ranges (e.g. "2xx" for all codes starting with 2) of the health check.|
|follow_redirects|boolean|false|none|Follow redirects if the origin returns a 3xx status code.|
|header|object \| null|false|none|The HTTP request headers to send in the health check. It is recommended you set a Host header by default. The User-Agent header cannot be overridden.|
|method|string|false|none|The HTTP method to use for the health check.|
|path|string|false|none|The endpoint path to health check against.|
|port|integer|false|none|Port number to connect to for the health check. Defaults to 80 if type is HTTP or 443 if type is HTTPS.|

```json
{
  "address": "www.example.com",
  "check_regions": [
    "WEU",
    "ENAM"
  ],
  "consecutive_fails": 1,
  "consecutive_successes": 1,
  "description": "Health check for www.example.com",
  "http_config": {
    "allow_insecure": false,
    "expected_body": "success",
    "expected_codes": [
      "2xx",
      "302"
    ],
    "follow_redirects": false,
    "header": {
      "Host": [
        "example.com"
      ],
      "X-App-ID": [
        "abc123"
      ]
    },
    "method": "GET",
    "path": "/health",
    "port": 80
  },
  "interval": 60,
  "name": "server-1",
  "retries": 2,
  "suspended": false,
  "tcp_config": {
    "method": "connection_established",
    "port": 80
  },
  "timeout": 5,
  "type": "HTTPS"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|address|[healthchecks_address](#schemahealthchecks_address)|true|none|The hostname or IP address of the origin server to run health checks on.|
|check_regions|[healthchecks_check_regions](#schemahealthchecks_check_regions)|false|none|A list of regions from which to run health checks. Null means Cloudflare will pick a default region.|
|consecutive_fails|[healthchecks_consecutive_fails](#schemahealthchecks_consecutive_fails)|false|none|The number of consecutive fails required from a health check before changing the health to unhealthy.|
|consecutive_successes|[healthchecks_consecutive_successes](#schemahealthchecks_consecutive_successes)|false|none|The number of consecutive successes required from a health check before changing the health to healthy.|
|description|[healthchecks_description](#schemahealthchecks_description)|false|none|A human-readable description of the health check.|
|http_config|[healthchecks_http_config](#schemahealthchecks_http_config)|false|none|Parameters specific to an HTTP or HTTPS health check.|
|interval|[healthchecks_interval](#schemahealthchecks_interval)|false|none|The interval between each health check. Shorter intervals may give quicker notifications if the origin status changes, but will increase load on the origin as we check from multiple locations.|
|name|[healthchecks_name](#schemahealthchecks_name)|true|none|A short name to identify the health check. Only alphanumeric characters, hyphens and underscores are allowed.|
|retries|[healthchecks_retries](#schemahealthchecks_retries)|false|none|The number of retries to attempt in case of a timeout before marking the origin as unhealthy. Retries are attempted immediately.|
|suspended|[healthchecks_suspended](#schemahealthchecks_suspended)|false|none|If suspended, no health checks are sent to the origin.|
|tcp_config|[healthchecks_tcp_config](#schemahealthchecks_tcp_config)|false|none|Parameters specific to TCP health check.|
|timeout|[healthchecks_timeout](#schemahealthchecks_timeout)|false|none|The timeout (in seconds) before marking the health check as failed.|
|type|[healthchecks_type](#schemahealthchecks_type)|false|none|The protocol to use for the health check. Currently supported protocols are 'HTTP', 'HTTPS' and 'TCP'.|

<a id="schemahyperdrive_internet-origin"></a>
<a id="schema_hyperdrive_internet-origin"></a>
<a id="tocShyperdrive_internet-origin"></a>
<a id="tocshyperdrive_internet-origin"></a>

```json
{
  "host": "database.example.com",
  "port": 5432
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|host|string|true|none|Defines the publicly reachable hostname or IP of your origin database. Private, loopback, and link-local IP addresses are not allowed.|
|port|integer|true|none|Defines the port of your origin database. Defaults to 5432 for PostgreSQL or 3306 for MySQL if not specified.|

<h2 id="tocS_hyperdrive_over-access-origin">hyperdrive_over-access-origin</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemahyperdrive_over-access-origin"></a>
<a id="schema_hyperdrive_over-access-origin"></a>
<a id="tocShyperdrive_over-access-origin"></a>
<a id="tocshyperdrive_over-access-origin"></a>

```json
{
  "access_client_id": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.access",
  "access_client_secret": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
  "host": "database.example.com"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|access_client_id|string|true|none|Defines the Client ID of the Access token to use when connecting to the origin database.|
|access_client_secret|string|true|write-only|Defines the Client Secret of the Access Token to use when connecting to the origin database. The API never returns this write-only value.|
|host|string|true|none|Defines the host (hostname or IP) of your origin database.|

```json
{
  "count": 1,
  "page": 1,
  "per_page": 20,
  "total_count": 2000
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|count|number|false|none|Defines the total number of results for the requested service.|
|page|number|false|none|Defines the current page within paginated list of results.|
|per_page|number|false|none|Defines the number of results per page of results.|
|total_count|number|false|none|Defines the total results available without any search parameters.|

<h2 id="tocS_hyperdrive_vpc-service-origin">hyperdrive_vpc-service-origin</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemahyperdrive_vpc-service-origin"></a>
<a id="schema_hyperdrive_vpc-service-origin"></a>
<a id="tocShyperdrive_vpc-service-origin"></a>
<a id="tocshyperdrive_vpc-service-origin"></a>

```json
{
  "service_id": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
}
```

Connect to a database through a Workers VPC Service. TLS settings (mTLS, sslmode) cannot be configured on the Hyperdrive when using a VPC Service origin; TLS must be managed on the VPC Service itself.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|service_id|string|true|none|The identifier of the Workers VPC Service to connect through. Hyperdrive will egress through the specified VPC Service to reach the origin database.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allowed_cors_origins|[string]|false|none|Array of allowed CORS origins.|
|client_name|string|false|none|Human-readable name of the OAuth client.|
|client_uri|string|false|none|URL of the home page of the client.|
|grant_types|[iam_oauth_client_grant_types](#schemaiam_oauth_client_grant_types)|false|none|Array of OAuth grant types the client is allowed to use. `authorization_code` is required; `refresh_token` may be included optionally.|
|logo_uri|string|false|none|URL of the client's logo.|
|optional_scopes|[string]|false|none|Scopes that the authorizing user may decline during consent. Each value must also appear in `scopes`. The scopes `openid`, `offline`, and `offline_access` cannot be optional.|
|policy_uri|string|false|none|URL that points to a privacy policy document.|
|post_logout_redirect_uris|[string]|false|none|Array of allowed post-logout redirect URIs.|
|redirect_uris|[string]|false|none|Array of allowed redirect URIs for the client.|
|response_types|[iam_oauth_client_response_types](#schemaiam_oauth_client_response_types)|false|none|Array of OAuth response types the client is allowed to use.|
|scopes|[string]|false|none|Array of OAuth scopes the client is allowed to request. Colon-delimited scopes are not accepted. Dot-delimited scopes are validated against available OAuth API scopes; simple identity scopes are allowed. Protocol scopes `offline_access` and `openid` are added or removed automatically based on `grant_types` and `response_types`.|
|token_endpoint_auth_method|[iam_oauth_client_token_endpoint_auth_method](#schemaiam_oauth_client_token_endpoint_auth_method)|false|none|The authentication method the client uses at the token endpoint.|

|emails|[[iam_scim_user_email_object](#schemaiam_scim_user_email_object)]|false|none|Email addresses for the user. If a primary email is provided, it must match `userName`.|
|externalId|string|false|none|An identifier for the user as defined by the provisioning client (IdP). This value is stored and returned but not interpreted by Cloudflare.|
|name|[iam_scim_user_name_object](#schemaiam_scim_user_name_object)|false|none|The components of the user's real name.|
|schemas|[string]|true|none|Must contain `urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User`.|
|userName|string(email)|true|none|Unique identifier for the user, equal to the user's email address.|

<h2 id="tocS_load-balancing_adaptive_routing">load-balancing_adaptive_routing</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaload-balancing_adaptive_routing"></a>
<a id="schema_load-balancing_adaptive_routing"></a>
<a id="tocSload-balancing_adaptive_routing"></a>
<a id="tocsload-balancing_adaptive_routing"></a>

```json
{
  "failover_across_pools": true
}
```

Controls features that modify the routing of requests to pools and origins in response to dynamic conditions, such as during the interval between active health monitoring requests. For example, zero-downtime failover occurs immediately when an origin becomes unavailable due to HTTP 521, 522, or 523 response codes. If there is another healthy origin in the same pool, the request is retried once against this alternate origin.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|failover_across_pools|boolean|false|none|Extends zero-downtime failover of requests to healthy origins from alternate pools, when no healthy alternate exists in the same pool, according to the failover order defined by traffic and origin steering. When set false (the default) zero-downtime failover will only occur between origins within the same pool. See `session_affinity_attributes` for control over when sessions are broken or reassigned.|

<h2 id="tocS_load-balancing_address">load-balancing_address</h2>

<a id="tocSload-balancing_address"></a>
<a id="tocsload-balancing_address"></a>

```json
"0.0.0.0"
```

The IP address (IPv4 or IPv6) of the origin, or its publicly addressable hostname. Hostnames entered here should resolve directly to the origin, and not be a hostname proxied by Cloudflare. To set an internal/reserved address, virtual_network_id must also be set.

<h2 id="tocS_load-balancing_health_sources">load-balancing_health_sources</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaload-balancing_health_sources"></a>
<a id="schema_load-balancing_health_sources"></a>
<a id="tocSload-balancing_health_sources"></a>
<a id="tocsload-balancing_health_sources"></a>

```json
[
  "regional",
  "global"
]
```

A list of health sources, ordered from highest to lowest priority, used to evaluate individual origin health and overall pool health. The load balancer uses the first source that has data and falls back to the next. Currently accepted values are null or the exact array ["regional", "global"]; any other combination is rejected. Null (the default) behaves like ["local", "global"]. ["regional", "global"] makes each region steer on its own health, falling back to the global decision when a region has no fresh data. Setting regional requires at least one region in check_regions.

If there is another healthy origin in the same pool, the request is retried once against this alternate origin.|

|description|[load-balancing_components-schemas-description](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-description)|false|none|Object description.|
|enabled|[load-balancing_components-schemas-enabled](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-enabled)|false|none|Whether to enable (the default) this load balancer.|
|fallback_pool|[load-balancing_fallback_pool](#schemaload-balancing_fallback_pool)|false|none|The pool ID to use when all other pools are detected as unhealthy.|
|id|[load-balancing_load-balancer_components-schemas-identifier](#schemaload-balancing_load-balancer_components-schemas-identifier)|false|none|none|
|location_strategy|[load-balancing_location_strategy](#schemaload-balancing_location_strategy)|false|none|Controls location-based steering for non-proxied requests. See `steering_policy` to learn how steering is affected.|
|modified_on|[load-balancing_timestamp](#schemaload-balancing_timestamp)|false|read-only|none|
|name|[load-balancing_components-schemas-name](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-name)|false|none|The DNS hostname to associate with your Load Balancer. If this hostname already exists as a DNS record in Cloudflare's DNS, the Load Balancer will take precedence and the DNS record will not be used.|
|networks|[load-balancing_networks](#schemaload-balancing_networks)|false|none|List of networks where Load Balancer or Pool is enabled.|
|pool_sets|[load-balancing_pool_sets](#schemaload-balancing_pool_sets)|false|none|An optional list of pool sets, evaluated in array order with first match wins. Pool sets are independent from the standard steering fields (`region_pools` / `country_pools` / `pop_pools` / `default_pools` / `steering_policy` / `random_steering` / `fallback_pool` / `rules`). On a PATCH, an empty array (`pool_sets: []`) clears all pool sets, while omitting the field leaves existing pool sets unchanged.|
|pop_pools|[load-balancing_pop_pools](#schemaload-balancing_pop_pools)|false|none|Enterprise only: A mapping of Cloudflare PoP identifiers to a list of pool IDs (ordered by their failover priority) for the PoP (datacenter). Any PoPs not explicitly defined will fall back to using the corresponding country_pool, then region_pool mapping if it exists else to default_pools.|
|proxied|[load-balancing_proxied](#schemaload-balancing_proxied)|false|none|Whether the hostname should be gray clouded (false) or orange clouded (true).|
|random_steering|[load-balancing_random_steering](#schemaload-balancing_random_steering)|false|none|Configures pool weights.<br>- `steering_policy="random"`: A random pool is selected with probability proportional to pool weights.<br>- `steering_policy="least_outstanding_requests"`: Use pool weights to scale each pool's outstanding requests.<br>- `steering_policy="least_connections"`: Use pool weights to scale each pool's open connections.|
|region_pools|[load-balancing_region_pools](#schemaload-balancing_region_pools)|false|none|A mapping of region codes to a list of pool IDs (ordered by their failover priority) for the given region. Any regions not explicitly defined will fall back to using default_pools.|
|rules|[load-balancing_rules](#schemaload-balancing_rules)|false|none|BETA Field Not General Access: A list of rules for this load balancer to execute.|
|session_affinity|[load-balancing_session_affinity](#schemaload-balancing_session_affinity)|false|none|Specifies the type of session affinity the load balancer should use unless specified as `"none"`. The supported types are: - `"cookie"`: On the first request to a proxied load balancer, a cookie is generated, encoding information of which origin the request will be forwarded to. Subsequent requests, by the same client to the same load balancer, will be sent to the origin server the cookie encodes, for the duration of the cookie and as long as the origin server remains healthy. If the cookie has expired or the origin server is unhealthy, then a new origin server is calculated and used. - `"ip_cookie"`: Behaves the same as `"cookie"` except the initial origin selection is stable and based on the client's ip address. - `"header"`: On the first request to a proxied load balancer, a session key based on the configured HTTP headers (see `session_affinity_attributes.headers`) is generated, encoding the request headers used for storing in the load balancer session state which origin the request will be forwarded to. Subsequent requests to the load balancer with the same headers will be sent to the same origin server, for the duration of the session and as long as the origin server remains healthy. If the session has been idle for the duration of `session_affinity_ttl` seconds or the origin server is unhealthy, then a new origin server is calculated and used. See `headers` in `session_affinity_attributes` for additional required configuration.|
|session_affinity_attributes|[load-balancing_session_affinity_attributes](#schemaload-balancing_session_affinity_attributes)|false|none|Configures attributes for session affinity.|
|session_affinity_ttl|[load-balancing_session_affinity_ttl](#schemaload-balancing_session_affinity_ttl)|false|none|Time, in seconds, until a client's session expires after being created. Once the expiry time has been reached, subsequent requests may get sent to a different origin server. The accepted ranges per `session_affinity` policy are: - `"cookie"` / `"ip_cookie"`: The current default of 23 hours will be used unless explicitly set. The accepted range of values is between [1800, 604800]. - `"header"`: The current default of 1800 seconds will be used unless explicitly set. The accepted range of values is between [30, 3600]. Note: With session affinity by header, sessions only expire after they haven't been used for the number of seconds specified.|
|steering_policy|[load-balancing_steering_policy](#schemaload-balancing_steering_policy)|false|none|Steering Policy for this load balancer.<br>- `"off"`: Use `default_pools`.<br>- `"geo"`: Use `region_pools`/`country_pools`/`pop_pools`. For non-proxied requests, the country for `country_pools` is determined by `location_strategy`.<br>- `"random"`: Select a pool randomly.<br>- `"dynamic_latency"`: Use round trip time to select the closest pool in default_pools (requires pool health checks).<br>- `"proximity"`: Use the pools' latitude and longitude to select the closest pool using the Cloudflare PoP location for proxied requests or the location determined by `location_strategy` for non-proxied requests.<br>- `"least_outstanding_requests"`: Select a pool by taking into consideration `random_steering` weights, as well as each pool's number of outstanding requests. Pools with more pending requests are weighted proportionately less relative to others.<br>- `"least_connections"`: Select a pool by taking into consideration `random_steering` weights, as well as each pool's number of open connections. Pools with more open connections are weighted proportionately less relative to others. Supported for HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 connections.<br>- `""`: Will map to `"geo"` if you use `region_pools`/`country_pools`/`pop_pools` otherwise `"off"`.|
|ttl|[load-balancing_ttl](#schemaload-balancing_ttl)|false|none|Time to live (TTL) of the DNS entry for the IP address returned by this load balancer. This only applies to gray-clouded (unproxied) load balancers.|
|zone_name|[load-balancing_components-schemas-zone-name](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-zone-name)|false|none|none|

The editable properties shared by load balancer create, update, and patch requests. Operations layer their own `required` constraints on top via `allOf`.

For example, zero-downtime failover occurs immediately when an origin becomes unavailable due to HTTP 521, 522, or 523 response codes. If there is another healthy origin in the same pool, the request is retried once against this alternate origin.|
|country_pools|[load-balancing_country_pools](#schemaload-balancing_country_pools)|false|none|A mapping of country codes to a list of pool IDs (ordered by their failover priority) for the given country. |default_pools|[load-balancing_default_pools](#schemaload-balancing_default_pools)|false|none|A list of pool IDs ordered by their failover priority. Pools defined here are used by default, or when region_pools are not configured for a given region.|
|description|[load-balancing_components-schemas-description](#schemaload-balancing_components-schemas-description)|false|none|Object description.|

<h2 id="tocS_load-balancing_load_shedding">load-balancing_load_shedding</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaload-balancing_load_shedding"></a>
<a id="schema_load-balancing_load_shedding"></a>
<a id="tocSload-balancing_load_shedding"></a>
<a id="tocsload-balancing_load_shedding"></a>

```json
{
  "default_percent": 0,
  "default_policy": "random",
  "session_percent": 0,
  "session_policy": "hash"
}
```

Configures load shedding policies and percentages for the pool.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|default_percent|number|false|none|The percent of traffic to shed from the pool, according to the default policy. Applies to new sessions and traffic without session affinity.|
|default_policy|string|false|none|The default policy to use when load shedding. A random policy randomly sheds a given percent of requests. A hash policy computes a hash over the CF-Connecting-IP address and sheds all requests originating from a percent of IPs.|
|session_percent|number|false|none|The percent of existing sessions to shed from the pool, according to the session policy.|
|session_policy|string|false|none|Only the hash policy is supported for existing sessions (to avoid exponential decay).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|default_policy|random|
|default_policy|hash|
|session_policy|hash|

<h2 id="tocS_load-balancing_location_strategy">load-balancing_location_strategy</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaload-balancing_location_strategy"></a>
<a id="schema_load-balancing_location_strategy"></a>
<a id="tocSload-balancing_location_strategy"></a>
<a id="tocsload-balancing_location_strategy"></a>

```json
{
  "mode": "resolver_ip",
  "prefer_ecs": "always"
}
```

Controls location-based steering for non-proxied requests. See `steering_policy` to learn how steering is affected.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|mode|string|false|none|Determines the authoritative location when ECS is not preferred, does not exist in the request, or its GeoIP lookup is unsuccessful.<br>- `"pop"`: Use the Cloudflare PoP location.<br>- `"resolver_ip"`: Use the DNS resolver GeoIP location. If the GeoIP lookup is unsuccessful, use the Cloudflare PoP location.|
|prefer_ecs|string|false|none|Whether the EDNS Client Subnet (ECS) GeoIP should be preferred as the authoritative location.<br>- `"always"`: Always prefer ECS.<br>- `"never"`: Never prefer ECS.<br>- `"proximity"`: Prefer ECS only when `steering_policy="proximity"`.<br>- `"geo"`: Prefer ECS only when `steering_policy="geo"`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|mode|pop|
|mode|resolver_ip|
|prefer_ecs|always|
|prefer_ecs|never|
|prefer_ecs|proximity|
|prefer_ecs|geo|

<h2 id="tocS_load-balancing_match">load-balancing_match</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaload-balancing_match"></a>
<a id="schema_load-balancing_match"></a>
<a id="tocSload-balancing_match"></a>
<a id="tocsload-balancing_match"></a>

```json
{
  "default": false,
  "topology": {
    "countries": [
      "string"
    ],
    "pops": [
      "string"
    ],
    "regions": [
      "string"
    ]
  }
}
```

Determines which requests a pool set applies to. Set `topology` to match by location or `default: true` to match all requests; the two are mutually exclusive. A pool set with no `match` matches all requests.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|default|boolean|false|none|When true, matches every request. Cannot be combined with `topology`.|
|topology|[load-balancing_topology_match](#schemaload-balancing_topology_match)|false|none|Matches requests by location. Set any combination of `pops`, `countries`, and `regions` (at least one is required); a request matches when its value appears in any populated list (e.g. `regions: ["WNAM"]` with `countries: ["US"]` matches a request in either WNAM or the US).|

<h2 id="tocS_load-balancing_minimum_origins">load-balancing_minimum_origins</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaload-balancing_minimum_origins"></a>
<a id="schema_load-balancing_minimum_origins"></a>
<a id="tocSload-balancing_minimum_origins"></a>
<a id="tocsload-balancing_minimum_origins"></a>

```json
1
```

The minimum number of origins that must be healthy for this pool to serve traffic. If the number of healthy origins falls below this number, the pool will be marked unhealthy and will failover to the next available pool.

<h2 id="tocS_load-balancing_monitor">load-balancing_monitor</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaload-balancing_monitor"></a>
<a id="schema_load-balancing_monitor"></a>
<a id="tocSload-balancing_monitor"></a>
<a id="tocsload-balancing_monitor"></a>

```json
{
  "allow_insecure": true,
  "consecutive_down": 0,
  "consecutive_up": 0,
  "description": "Login page monitor",
  "expected_body": "alive",
  "expected_codes": "2xx",
  "follow_redirects": true,
  "header": {
    "Host": [
      "example.com"
    ],
    "X-App-ID": [
      "abc123"
    ]
  },
  "interval": 60,
  "method": "GET",
  "path": "/health",
  "port": 0,
  "probe_zone": "example.com",
  "retries": 2,
  "timeout": 5,
  "type": "https",
  "created_on": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z",
  "id": "f1aba936b94213e5b8dca0c0dbf1f9cc",
  "modified_on": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_insecure|[load-balancing_allow_insecure](#schemaload-balancing_allow_insecure)|false|none|Do not validate the certificate when monitor use HTTPS. This parameter is currently only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|consecutive_down|[load-balancing_consecutive_down](#schemaload-balancing_consecutive_down)|false|none|To be marked unhealthy the monitored origin must fail this healthcheck N consecutive times.|
|consecutive_up|[load-balancing_consecutive_up](#schemaload-balancing_consecutive_up)|false|none|To be marked healthy the monitored origin must pass this healthcheck N consecutive times.|
|description|[load-balancing_description](#schemaload-balancing_description)|false|none|Object description.|
|expected_body|[load-balancing_expected_body](#schemaload-balancing_expected_body)|false|none|A case-insensitive sub-string to look for in the response body. If this string is not found, the origin will be marked as unhealthy. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|expected_codes|[load-balancing_expected_codes](#schemaload-balancing_expected_codes)|false|none|The expected HTTP response code or code range of the health check. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|follow_redirects|[load-balancing_follow_redirects](#schemaload-balancing_follow_redirects)|false|none|Follow redirects if returned by the origin. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|header|[load-balancing_header](#schemaload-balancing_header)|false|none|The HTTP request headers to send in the health check. It is recommended you set a Host header by default. The User-Agent header cannot be overridden. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|interval|[load-balancing_interval](#schemaload-balancing_interval)|false|none|The interval between each health check. Shorter intervals may improve failover time, but will increase load on the origins as we check from multiple locations.|
|method|[load-balancing_method](#schemaload-balancing_method)|false|none|The method to use for the health check. This defaults to 'GET' for HTTP/HTTPS based checks and 'connection_established' for TCP based health checks.|
|path|[load-balancing_path](#schemaload-balancing_path)|false|none|The endpoint path you want to conduct a health check against. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|port|[load-balancing_port](#schemaload-balancing_port)|false|none|The port number to connect to for the health check. Required for TCP, UDP, and SMTP checks. HTTP and HTTPS checks should only define the port when using a non-standard port (HTTP: default 80, HTTPS: default 443).|
|probe_zone|[load-balancing_probe_zone](#schemaload-balancing_probe_zone)|false|none|Assign this monitor to emulate the specified zone while probing. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|retries|[load-balancing_retries](#schemaload-balancing_retries)|false|none|The number of retries to attempt in case of a timeout before marking the origin as unhealthy. Retries are attempted immediately.|
|timeout|[load-balancing_timeout](#schemaload-balancing_timeout)|false|none|The timeout (in seconds) before marking the health check as failed.|
|type|[load-balancing_type](#schemaload-balancing_type)|false|none|The protocol to use for the health check. Currently supported protocols are 'HTTP','HTTPS', 'TCP', 'ICMP-PING', 'UDP-ICMP', and 'SMTP'.|
|created_on|[load-balancing_timestamp](#schemaload-balancing_timestamp)|false|read-only|none|
|id|[load-balancing_identifier](#schemaload-balancing_identifier)|false|none|none|
|modified_on|[load-balancing_timestamp](#schemaload-balancing_timestamp)|false|read-only|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|http|
|type|https|
|type|tcp|
|type|udp_icmp|
|type|icmp_ping|
|type|smtp|

|consecutive_down|[load-balancing_consecutive_down](#schemaload-balancing_consecutive_down)|false|none|To be marked unhealthy the monitored origin must fail this healthcheck N consecutive times.|
|consecutive_up|[load-balancing_consecutive_up](#schemaload-balancing_consecutive_up)|false|none|To be marked healthy the monitored origin must pass this healthcheck N consecutive times.|
|description|[load-balancing_description](#schemaload-balancing_description)|false|none|Object description.|
|expected_body|[load-balancing_expected_body](#schemaload-balancing_expected_body)|false|none|A case-insensitive sub-string to look for in the response body. If this string is not found, the origin will be marked as unhealthy. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|expected_codes|[load-balancing_expected_codes](#schemaload-balancing_expected_codes)|false|none|The expected HTTP response code or code range of the health check. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|follow_redirects|[load-balancing_follow_redirects](#schemaload-balancing_follow_redirects)|false|none|Follow redirects if returned by the origin. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|header|[load-balancing_header](#schemaload-balancing_header)|false|none|The HTTP request headers to send in the health check. It is recommended you set a Host header by default. The User-Agent header cannot be overridden. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|interval|[load-balancing_interval](#schemaload-balancing_interval)|false|none|The interval between each health check. Shorter intervals may improve failover time, but will increase load on the origins as we check from multiple locations.|
|method|[load-balancing_method](#schemaload-balancing_method)|false|none|The method to use for the health check. This defaults to 'GET' for HTTP/HTTPS based checks and 'connection_established' for TCP based health checks.|
|path|[load-balancing_path](#schemaload-balancing_path)|false|none|The endpoint path you want to conduct a health check against. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|port|[load-balancing_port](#schemaload-balancing_port)|false|none|The port number to connect to for the health check. Required for TCP, UDP, and SMTP checks. HTTP and HTTPS checks should only define the port when using a non-standard port (HTTP: default 80, HTTPS: default 443).|
|probe_zone|[load-balancing_probe_zone](#schemaload-balancing_probe_zone)|false|none|Assign this monitor to emulate the specified zone while probing. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors.|
|retries|[load-balancing_retries](#schemaload-balancing_retries)|false|none|The number of retries to attempt in case of a timeout before marking the origin as unhealthy. Retries are attempted immediately.|
|timeout|[load-balancing_timeout](#schemaload-balancing_timeout)|false|none|The timeout (in seconds) before marking the health check as failed.|
|type|[load-balancing_type](#schemaload-balancing_type)|false|none|The protocol to use for the health check. Currently supported protocols are 'HTTP','HTTPS', 'TCP', 'ICMP-PING', 'UDP-ICMP', and 'SMTP'.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|http|
|type|https|
|type|tcp|
|type|udp_icmp|
|type|icmp_ping|
|type|smtp|

<h2 id="tocS_load-balancing_origin">load-balancing_origin</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaload-balancing_origin"></a>
<a id="schema_load-balancing_origin"></a>
<a id="tocSload-balancing_origin"></a>
<a id="tocsload-balancing_origin"></a>

```json
{
  "address": "0.0.0.0",
  "disabled_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "enabled": true,
  "flatten_cname": true,
  "header": {
    "Host": [
      "example.com"
    ]
  },
  "name": "app-server-1",
  "port": 0,
  "virtual_network_id": "a5624d4e-044a-4ff0-b3e1-e2465353d4b4",
  "weight": 0.6
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|address|[load-balancing_address](#schemaload-balancing_address)|false|none|The IP address (IPv4 or IPv6) of the origin, or its publicly addressable hostname. Hostnames entered here should resolve directly to the origin, and not be a hostname proxied by Cloudflare. To set an internal/reserved address, virtual_network_id must also be set.|
|disabled_at|[load-balancing_disabled_at](#schemaload-balancing_disabled_at)|false|read-only|This field shows up only if the origin is disabled. This field is set with the time the origin was disabled.|
|enabled|[load-balancing_schemas-enabled](#schemaload-balancing_schemas-enabled)|false|none|Whether to enable (the default) this origin within the pool. Disabled origins will not receive traffic and are excluded from health checks. The origin will only be disabled for the current pool.|
|flatten_cname|[load-balancing_origin_flatten_cname](#schemaload-balancing_origin_flatten_cname)|false|none|Whether to flatten CNAME records for this origin, resolving them to A/AAAA records before returning to the client. When true (the default), the director resolves CNAME addresses to their underlying A/AAAA records. When false, the origin address is returned as a raw CNAME record without resolution. This setting mirrors the DNS API record flatten_cname setting.|
|header|[load-balancing_schemas-header](#schemaload-balancing_schemas-header)|false|none|The request header is used to pass additional information with an HTTP request. Currently supported header is 'Host'.|
|name|[load-balancing_schemas-name](#schemaload-balancing_schemas-name)|false|none|A human-identifiable name for the origin.|
|port|[load-balancing_origin_port](#schemaload-balancing_origin_port)|false|none|The port for upstream connections. A value of 0 means the default port for the protocol will be used.|
|virtual_network_id|[load-balancing_virtual_network_id](#schemaload-balancing_virtual_network_id)|false|none|The virtual network subnet ID the origin belongs in. Virtual network must also belong to the account.|
|weight|[load-balancing_weight](#schemaload-balancing_weight)|false|none|The weight of this origin relative to other origins in the pool. Based on the configured weight the total traffic is distributed among origins within the pool.<br>- `origin_steering.policy="least_outstanding_requests"`: Use weight to scale the origin's outstanding requests.<br>- `origin_steering.policy="least_connections"`: Use weight to scale the origin's open connections.|

<h2 id="tocS_load-balancing_origin_flatten_cname">load-balancing_origin_flatten_cname</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaload-balancing_origin_flatten_cname"></a>
<a id="schema_load-balancing_origin_flatten_cname"></a>
<a id="tocSload-balancing_origin_flatten_cname"></a>
<a id="tocsload-balancing_origin_flatten_cname"></a>

```json
true
```

Whether to flatten CNAME records for this origin, resolving them to A/AAAA records before returning to the client. When true (the default), the director resolves CNAME addresses to their underlying A/AAAA records. When false, the origin address is returned as a raw CNAME record without resolution. This setting mirrors the DNS API record flatten_cname setting.

<h2 id="tocS_load-balancing_origin_steering">load-balancing_origin_steering</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaload-balancing_origin_steering"></a>
<a id="schema_load-balancing_origin_steering"></a>
<a id="tocSload-balancing_origin_steering"></a>
<a id="tocsload-balancing_origin_steering"></a>

```json
{
  "policy": "random"
}
```

Configures origin steering for the pool. Controls how origins are selected for new sessions and traffic without session affinity.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|policy|string|false|none|The type of origin steering policy to use.<br>- `"random"`: Select an origin randomly.<br>- `"hash"`: Select an origin by computing a hash over the CF-Connecting-IP address.<br>- `"least_outstanding_requests"`: Select an origin by taking into consideration origin weights, as well as each origin's number of outstanding requests. Origins with more pending requests are weighted proportionately less relative to others.<br>- `"least_connections"`: Select an origin by taking into consideration origin weights, as well as each origin's number of open connections. Origins with more open connections are weighted proportionately less relative to others. Supported for HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 connections.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|policy|random|
|policy|hash|
|policy|least_outstanding_requests|
|policy|least_connections|
