<h2 id="tocS_load-balancing_pool">load-balancing_pool</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaload-balancing_pool"></a>
<a id="schema_load-balancing_pool"></a>
<a id="tocSload-balancing_pool"></a>
<a id="tocsload-balancing_pool"></a>

```json
{
  "check_regions": [
    "WEU",
    "ENAM"
  ],
  "created_on": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z",
  "description": "Primary data center - Provider XYZ",
  "disabled_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "enabled": false,
  "health_sources": [
    "regional",
    "global"
  ],
  "id": "17b5962d775c646f3f9725cbc7a53df4",
  "latitude": 0,
  "load_shedding": {
    "default_percent": 0,
    "default_policy": "random",
    "session_percent": 0,
    "session_policy": "hash"
  },
  "longitude": 0,
  "minimum_origins": 1,
  "modified_on": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z",
  "monitor": "string",
  "monitor_group": "string",
  "name": "primary-dc-1",
  "networks": [
    "cloudflare",
    "jdcloud"
  ],
  "notification_email": "someone@example.com,sometwo@example.com",
  "notification_filter": {
    "origin": {
      "disable": true
    },
    "pool": {
      "healthy": false
    }
  },
  "origin_steering": {
    "policy": "random"
  },
  "origins": [
    {
      "address": "0.0.0.0",
      "disabled_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "enabled": true,
      "flatten_cname": true,
      "header": {
        "Host": [
          "example.com"
        ]
      },
      "name": "app-server-1",
      "port": 0,
      "virtual_network_id": "a5624d4e-044a-4ff0-b3e1-e2465353d4b4",
      "weight": 0.6
    }
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|check_regions|[load-balancing_check_regions](#schemaload-balancing_check_regions)|false|none|A list of regions from which to run health checks. Null means every Cloudflare data center.|
|created_on|[load-balancing_timestamp](#schemaload-balancing_timestamp)|false|read-only|none|
|description|[load-balancing_schemas-description](#schemaload-balancing_schemas-description)|false|none|A human-readable description of the pool.|
|disabled_at|[load-balancing_schemas-disabled_at](#schemaload-balancing_schemas-disabled_at)|false|read-only|This field shows up only if the pool is disabled. This field is set with the time the pool was disabled at.|
|enabled|[load-balancing_enabled](#schemaload-balancing_enabled)|false|none|Whether to enable (the default) or disable this pool. Disabled pools will not receive traffic and are excluded from health checks. Disabling a pool will cause any load balancers using it to failover to the next pool (if any).|
|health_sources|[load-balancing_health_sources](#schemaload-balancing_health_sources)|false|none|A list of health sources, ordered from highest to lowest priority, used to evaluate individual origin health and overall pool health. The load balancer uses the first source that has data and falls back to the next. Currently accepted values are null or the exact array ["regional", "global"]; any other combination is rejected. Null (the default) behaves like ["local", "global"]. ["regional", "global"] makes each region steer on its own health, falling back to the global decision when a region has no fresh data. Setting regional requires at least one region in check_regions.|
|id|[load-balancing_schemas-identifier](#schemaload-balancing_schemas-identifier)|false|none|none|
|latitude|[load-balancing_latitude](#schemaload-balancing_latitude)|false|none|The latitude of the data center containing the origins used in this pool in decimal degrees. If this is set, longitude must also be set.|
|load_shedding|[load-balancing_load_shedding](#schemaload-balancing_load_shedding)|false|none|Configures load shedding policies and percentages for the pool.|
|longitude|[load-balancing_longitude](#schemaload-balancing_longitude)|false|none|The longitude of the data center containing the origins used in this pool in decimal degrees. If this is set, latitude must also be set.|
|minimum_origins|[load-balancing_minimum_origins](#schemaload-balancing_minimum_origins)|false|none|The minimum number of origins that must be healthy for this pool to serve traffic. If the number of healthy origins falls below this number, the pool will be marked unhealthy and will failover to the next available pool.|
|modified_on|[load-balancing_timestamp](#schemaload-balancing_timestamp)|false|read-only|none|
|monitor|[load-balancing_monitor_id](#schemaload-balancing_monitor_id)|false|none|The ID of the Monitor to use for checking the health of origins within this pool.|
|monitor_group|[load-balancing_monitor_group_id](#schemaload-balancing_monitor_group_id)|false|none|The ID of the Monitor Group to use for checking the health of origins within this pool.|
|name|[load-balancing_name](#schemaload-balancing_name)|false|none|A short name (tag) for the pool. Only alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores are allowed.|
|networks|[load-balancing_networks](#schemaload-balancing_networks)|false|none|List of networks where Load Balancer or Pool is enabled.|
|notification_email|[load-balancing_notification_email](#schemaload-balancing_notification_email)|false|none|This field is now deprecated. It has been moved to Cloudflare's Centralized Notification service https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/notifications/. The email address to send health status notifications to. This can be an individual mailbox or a mailing list. Multiple emails can be supplied as a comma delimited list.|
|notification_filter|[load-balancing_notification_filter](#schemaload-balancing_notification_filter)|false|none|Filter pool and origin health notifications by resource type or health status. Use null to reset.|
|origin_steering|[load-balancing_origin_steering](#schemaload-balancing_origin_steering)|false|none|Configures origin steering for the pool. Controls how origins are selected for new sessions and traffic without session affinity.|
|origins|[load-balancing_origins](#schemaload-balancing_origins)|false|none|The list of origins within this pool. Traffic directed at this pool is balanced across all currently healthy origins, provided the pool itself is healthy.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|check_regions|WNAM|
|check_regions|ENAM|
|check_regions|WEU|
|check_regions|EEU|
|check_regions|NSAM|
|check_regions|SSAM|
|check_regions|OC|
|check_regions|ME|
|check_regions|NAF|
|check_regions|SAF|
|check_regions|SAS|
|check_regions|SEAS|
|check_regions|NEAS|
|check_regions|CHINA|
|check_regions|ALL_REGIONS|
|health_sources|local|
|health_sources|regional|
|health_sources|global|

<h2 id="tocS_load-balancing_pool_set">load-balancing_pool_set</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaload-balancing_pool_set"></a>
<a id="schema_load-balancing_pool_set"></a>
<a id="tocSload-balancing_pool_set"></a>
<a id="tocsload-balancing_pool_set"></a>

```json
{
  "match": {
    "topology": {
      "regions": [
        "WNAM"
      ]
    }
  },
  "name": "wnam-primary",
  "overrides": {
    "fallback_pool": "9290f38c5d07c2e2f4df57b1f61d4196",
    "pools": [
      "17b5962d775c646f3f9725cbc7a53df4"
    ],
    "steering_policy": "random"
  }
}
```

One entry in a load balancer's `pool_sets`. Pool sets are evaluated in array order; the first whose `match` succeeds applies its `overrides` (or `fixed_response`), and evaluation stops there.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|disabled|boolean|false|none|Disable this specific pool set. It will no longer be evaluated.|
|fixed_response|[load-balancing_fixed_response](#schemaload-balancing_fixed_response)|false|none|A collection of fields used to directly respond to the client instead of routing to a pool. When supplied on a rule, that rule stops further rule evaluation.|
|match|[load-balancing_match](#schemaload-balancing_match)|false|none|Determines which requests a pool set applies to. Set `topology` to match by location or `default: true` to match all requests; the two are mutually exclusive. A pool set with no `match` matches all requests.|
|name|string|false|none|A human-readable name for this pool set.|
|overrides|[load-balancing_pool_set_overrides](#schemaload-balancing_pool_set_overrides)|false|none|The behavior a pool set applies when its `match` succeeds. A strict subset of a rule's `overrides`: a pool set replaces the topology wholesale with a flat pool list (`pools`), so only the declarative pool-routing fields plus `fallback_pool` and `steering_policy` are settable. All fields are optional.|

<h2 id="tocS_load-balancing_pool_set_overrides">load-balancing_pool_set_overrides</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaload-balancing_pool_set_overrides"></a>
<a id="schema_load-balancing_pool_set_overrides"></a>
<a id="tocSload-balancing_pool_set_overrides"></a>
<a id="tocsload-balancing_pool_set_overrides"></a>

```json
{
  "fallback_pool": "string",
  "pool_default_weight": 0.2,
  "pool_weights": {
    "9290f38c5d07c2e2f4df57b1f61d4196": 0.5,
    "de90f38ced07c2e2f4df50b1f61d4194": 0.3
  },
  "pools": [
    "17b5962d775c646f3f9725cbc7a53df4"
  ],
  "steering_policy": "dynamic_latency"
}
```

The behavior a pool set applies when its `match` succeeds. A strict subset of a rule's `overrides`: a pool set replaces the topology wholesale with a flat pool list (`pools`), so only the declarative pool-routing fields plus `fallback_pool` and `steering_policy` are settable. All fields are optional.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fallback_pool|[load-balancing_fallback_pool](#schemaload-balancing_fallback_pool)|false|none|The pool ID to use when all other pools are detected as unhealthy.|
|pool_default_weight|[load-balancing_pool_default_weight](#schemaload-balancing_pool_default_weight)|false|none|The default weight for pools not listed in `pool_weights`. The declarative alternative to `random_steering.default_weight`; mutually exclusive with `random_steering`.|
|pool_weights|[load-balancing_pool_weights](#schemaload-balancing_pool_weights)|false|none|A mapping of pool IDs to custom weights, relative to the other pools. The declarative alternative to `random_steering.pool_weights`; mutually exclusive with `random_steering`.|
|pools|[load-balancing_pools](#schemaload-balancing_pools)|false|none|A flat, ordered list of pool IDs to route the matched audience to. Replaces the resolved topology with exactly these pools. Mutually exclusive with `fixed_response`.|
|steering_policy|[load-balancing_steering_policy](#schemaload-balancing_steering_policy)|false|none|Steering Policy for this load balancer.<br>- `"off"`: Use `default_pools`.<br>- `"geo"`: Use `region_pools`/`country_pools`/`pop_pools`. For non-proxied requests, the country for `country_pools` is determined by `location_strategy`.<br>- `"random"`: Select a pool randomly.<br>- `"dynamic_latency"`: Use round trip time to select the closest pool in default_pools (requires pool health checks).<br>- `"proximity"`: Use the pools' latitude and longitude to select the closest pool using the Cloudflare PoP location for proxied requests or the location determined by `location_strategy` for non-proxied requests.<br>- `"least_outstanding_requests"`: Select a pool by taking into consideration `random_steering` weights, as well as each pool's number of outstanding requests. Pools with more pending requests are weighted proportionately less relative to others.<br>- `"least_connections"`: Select a pool by taking into consideration `random_steering` weights, as well as each pool's number of open connections. Pools with more open connections are weighted proportionately less relative to others. Supported for HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 connections.<br>- `""`: Will map to `"geo"` if you use `region_pools`/`country_pools`/`pop_pools` otherwise `"off"`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|steering_policy|off|
|steering_policy|geo|
|steering_policy|random|
|steering_policy|dynamic_latency|
|steering_policy|proximity|
|steering_policy|least_outstanding_requests|
|steering_policy|least_connections|
|steering_policy|""|

<h2 id="tocS_load-balancing_pool_sets">load-balancing_pool_sets</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaload-balancing_pool_sets"></a>
<a id="schema_load-balancing_pool_sets"></a>
<a id="tocSload-balancing_pool_sets"></a>
<a id="tocsload-balancing_pool_sets"></a>

```json
[
  {
    "match": {
      "topology": {
        "regions": [
          "WNAM"
        ]
      }
    },
    "name": "wnam-primary",
    "overrides": {
      "fallback_pool": "9290f38c5d07c2e2f4df57b1f61d4196",
      "pools": [
        "17b5962d775c646f3f9725cbc7a53df4"
      ],
      "steering_policy": "random"
    }
  }
]
```

An optional list of pool sets, evaluated in array order with first match wins. Pool sets are independent from the standard steering fields (`region_pools` / `country_pools` / `pop_pools` / `default_pools` / `steering_policy` / `random_steering` / `fallback_pool` / `rules`). On a PATCH, an empty array (`pool_sets: []`) clears all pool sets, while omitting the field leaves existing pool sets unchanged.

<h2 id="tocS_load-balancing_pop_pools">load-balancing_pop_pools</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaload-balancing_pop_pools"></a>
<a id="schema_load-balancing_pop_pools"></a>
<a id="tocSload-balancing_pop_pools"></a>
<a id="tocsload-balancing_pop_pools"></a>

```json
{
  "LAX": [
    "de90f38ced07c2e2f4df50b1f61d4194",
    "9290f38c5d07c2e2f4df57b1f61d4196"
  ],
```

<h2 id="tocS_load-balancing_random_steering">load-balancing_random_steering</h2>

```json
    "9290f38c5d07c2e2f4df57b1f61d4196": 0.5,
    "de90f38ced07c2e2f4df50b1f61d4194": 0.3
  }
}
```

Configures pool weights.
- `steering_policy="random"`: A random pool is selected with probability proportional to pool weights.
- `steering_policy="least_outstanding_requests"`: Use pool weights to scale each pool's outstanding requests.
- `steering_policy="least_connections"`: Use pool weights to scale each pool's open connections.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|default_weight|number|false|none|The default weight for pools in the load balancer that are not specified in the pool_weights map.|
|pool_weights|object|false|none|A mapping of pool IDs to custom weights. The weight is relative to other pools in the load balancer.|

```json
  "steering_policy": "dynamic_latency",
  "ttl": 30
}
```

A collection of overrides to apply when this rule's condition (or a pool set's `match`) is true. All fields are optional.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|adaptive_routing|[load-balancing_adaptive_routing](#schemaload-balancing_adaptive_routing)|false|none|Controls features that modify the routing of requests to pools and origins in response to dynamic conditions, such as during the interval between active health monitoring requests. For example, zero-downtime failover occurs immediately when an origin becomes unavailable due to HTTP 521, 522, or 523 response codes. If there is another healthy origin in the same pool, the request is retried once against this alternate origin.|
|country_pools|[load-balancing_country_pools](#schemaload-balancing_country_pools)|false|none|A mapping of country codes to a list of pool IDs (ordered by their failover priority) for the given country. Any country not explicitly defined will fall back to using the corresponding region_pool mapping if it exists else to default_pools.|
|default_pools|[load-balancing_default_pools](#schemaload-balancing_default_pools)|false|none|A list of pool IDs ordered by their failover priority. Pools defined here are used by default, or when region_pools are not configured for a given region.|
|fallback_pool|[load-balancing_fallback_pool](#schemaload-balancing_fallback_pool)|false|none|The pool ID to use when all other pools are detected as unhealthy.|
|location_strategy|[load-balancing_location_strategy](#schemaload-balancing_location_strategy)|false|none|Controls location-based steering for non-proxied requests. See `steering_policy` to learn how steering is affected.|
|pool_default_weight|[load-balancing_pool_default_weight](#schemaload-balancing_pool_default_weight)|false|none|The default weight for pools not listed in `pool_weights`. The declarative alternative to `random_steering.default_weight`; mutually exclusive with `random_steering`.|
|pool_weights|[load-balancing_pool_weights](#schemaload-balancing_pool_weights)|false|none|A mapping of pool IDs to custom weights, relative to the other pools. The declarative alternative to `random_steering.pool_weights`; mutually exclusive with `random_steering`.|
|pools|[load-balancing_pools](#schemaload-balancing_pools)|false|none|A flat, ordered list of pool IDs to route the matched audience to. Replaces the resolved topology with exactly these pools. Mutually exclusive with `fixed_response`.|
|pop_pools|[load-balancing_pop_pools](#schemaload-balancing_pop_pools)|false|none|Enterprise only: A mapping of Cloudflare PoP identifiers to a list of pool IDs (ordered by their failover priority) for the PoP (datacenter). Any PoPs not explicitly defined will fall back to using the corresponding country_pool, then region_pool mapping if it exists else to default_pools.|
|random_steering|[load-balancing_random_steering](#schemaload-balancing_random_steering)|false|none|Configures pool weights.<br>- `steering_policy="random"`: A random pool is selected with probability proportional to pool weights.<br>- `steering_policy="least_outstanding_requests"`: Use pool weights to scale each pool's outstanding requests.<br>- `steering_policy="least_connections"`: Use pool weights to scale each pool's open connections.|
|region_pools|[load-balancing_region_pools](#schemaload-balancing_region_pools)|false|none|A mapping of region codes to a list of pool IDs (ordered by their failover priority) for the given region. Any regions not explicitly defined will fall back to using default_pools.|
|session_affinity|[load-balancing_session_affinity](#schemaload-balancing_session_affinity)|false|none|Specifies the type of session affinity the load balancer should use unless specified as `"none"`. The supported types are: - `"cookie"`: On the first request to a proxied load balancer, a cookie is generated, encoding information of which origin the request will be forwarded to. Subsequent requests, by the same client to the same load balancer, will be sent to the origin server the cookie encodes, for the duration of the cookie and as long as the origin server remains healthy. If the cookie has expired or the origin server is unhealthy, then a new origin server is calculated and used. - `"ip_cookie"`: Behaves the same as `"cookie"` except the initial origin selection is stable and based on the client's ip address. - `"header"`: On the first request to a proxied load balancer, a session key based on the configured HTTP headers (see `session_affinity_attributes.headers`) is generated, encoding the request headers used for storing in the load balancer session state which origin the request will be forwarded to. Subsequent requests to the load balancer with the same headers will be sent to the same origin server, for the duration of the session and as long as the origin server remains healthy. If the session has been idle for the duration of `session_affinity_ttl` seconds or the origin server is unhealthy, then a new origin server is calculated and used. See `headers` in `session_affinity_attributes` for additional required configuration.|
|session_affinity_attributes|[load-balancing_session_affinity_attributes](#schemaload-balancing_session_affinity_attributes)|false|none|Configures attributes for session affinity.|
|session_affinity_ttl|[load-balancing_session_affinity_ttl](#schemaload-balancing_session_affinity_ttl)|false|none|Time, in seconds, until a client's session expires after being created. Once the expiry time has been reached, subsequent requests may get sent to a different origin server. The accepted ranges per `session_affinity` policy are: - `"cookie"` / `"ip_cookie"`: The current default of 23 hours will be used unless explicitly set. The accepted range of values is between [1800, 604800]. - `"header"`: The current default of 1800 seconds will be used unless explicitly set. The accepted range of values is between [30, 3600]. Note: With session affinity by header, sessions only expire after they haven't been used for the number of seconds specified.|
|steering_policy|[load-balancing_steering_policy](#schemaload-balancing_steering_policy)|false|none|Steering Policy for this load balancer.<br>- `"off"`: Use `default_pools`.<br>- `"geo"`: Use `region_pools`/`country_pools`/`pop_pools`. For non-proxied requests, the country for `country_pools` is determined by `location_strategy`.<br>- `"random"`: Select a pool randomly.<br>- `"dynamic_latency"`: Use round trip time to select the closest pool in default_pools (requires pool health checks).<br>- `"proximity"`: Use the pools' latitude and longitude to select the closest pool using the Cloudflare PoP location for proxied requests or the location determined by `location_strategy` for non-proxied requests.<br>- `"least_outstanding_requests"`: Select a pool by taking into consideration `random_steering` weights, as well as each pool's number of outstanding requests. Pools with more pending requests are weighted proportionately less relative to others.<br>- `"least_connections"`: Select a pool by taking into consideration `random_steering` weights, as well as each pool's number of open connections. Pools with more open connections are weighted proportionately less relative to others. Supported for HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 connections.<br>- `""`: Will map to `"geo"` if you use `region_pools`/`country_pools`/`pop_pools` otherwise `"off"`.|
|ttl|[load-balancing_ttl](#schemaload-balancing_ttl)|false|none|Time to live (TTL) of the DNS entry for the IP address returned by this load balancer. This only applies to gray-clouded (unproxied) load balancers.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|session_affinity|none|
|session_affinity|cookie|
|session_affinity|ip_cookie|
|session_affinity|header|
|steering_policy|off|
|steering_policy|geo|
|steering_policy|random|
|steering_policy|dynamic_latency|
|steering_policy|proximity|
|steering_policy|least_outstanding_requests|
|steering_policy|least_connections|
|steering_policy|""|

```json
        "00920f38ce07c2e2f4df50b1f61d4194"
      ],
      "fallback_pool": "string",
      "location_strategy": {
        "mode": "resolver_ip",
        "prefer_ecs": "always"
      },
      "pool_default_weight": 0.2,
```

<h2 id="tocS_load-balancing_session_affinity">load-balancing_session_affinity</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaload-balancing_session_affinity"></a>
<a id="schema_load-balancing_session_affinity"></a>
<a id="tocSload-balancing_session_affinity"></a>
<a id="tocsload-balancing_session_affinity"></a>

```json
"cookie"
```

Specifies the type of session affinity the load balancer should use unless specified as `"none"`. The supported types are: - `"cookie"`: On the first request to a proxied load balancer, a cookie is generated, encoding information of which origin the request will be forwarded to. Subsequent requests, by the same client to the same load balancer, will be sent to the origin server the cookie encodes, for the duration of the cookie and as long as the origin server remains healthy. If the cookie has expired or the origin server is unhealthy, then a new origin server is calculated and used. - `"ip_cookie"`: Behaves the same as `"cookie"` except the initial origin selection is stable and based on the client's ip address. - `"header"`: On the first request to a proxied load balancer, a session key based on the configured HTTP headers (see `session_affinity_attributes.headers`) is generated, encoding the request headers used for storing in the load balancer session state which origin the request will be forwarded to. Subsequent requests to the load balancer with the same headers will be sent to the same origin server, for the duration of the session and as long as the origin server remains healthy. If the session has been idle for the duration of `session_affinity_ttl` seconds or the origin server is unhealthy, then a new origin server is calculated and used. See `headers` in `session_affinity_attributes` for additional required configuration.

<h2 id="tocS_load-balancing_session_affinity_attributes">load-balancing_session_affinity_attributes</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaload-balancing_session_affinity_attributes"></a>
<a id="schema_load-balancing_session_affinity_attributes"></a>
<a id="tocSload-balancing_session_affinity_attributes"></a>
<a id="tocsload-balancing_session_affinity_attributes"></a>

```json
{
  "drain_duration": 100,
  "headers": [],
  "require_all_headers": false,
  "samesite": "Auto",
  "secure": "Auto",
  "zero_downtime_failover": "sticky"
}
```

Configures attributes for session affinity.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|drain_duration|number|false|none|Configures the drain duration in seconds. This field is only used when session affinity is enabled on the load balancer.|
|headers|[string]|false|none|Configures the names of HTTP headers to base session affinity on when header `session_affinity` is enabled. At least one HTTP header name must be provided. To specify the exact cookies to be used, include an item in the following format: `"cookie:<cookie-name-1>,<cookie-name-2>"` (example) where everything after the colon is a comma-separated list of cookie names. Providing only `"cookie"` will result in all cookies being used. The default max number of HTTP header names that can be provided depends on your plan: 5 for Enterprise, 1 for all other plans.|
|require_all_headers|boolean|false|none|When header `session_affinity` is enabled, this option can be used to specify how HTTP headers on load balancing requests will be used. The supported values are: - `"true"`: Load balancing requests must contain *all* of the HTTP headers specified by the `headers` session affinity attribute, otherwise sessions aren't created. - `"false"`: Load balancing requests must contain *at least one* of the HTTP headers specified by the `headers` session affinity attribute, otherwise sessions aren't created.|
|samesite|string|false|none|Configures the SameSite attribute on session affinity cookie. Value "Auto" will be translated to "Lax" or "None" depending if Always Use HTTPS is enabled. Note: when using value "None", the secure attribute can not be set to "Never".|
|secure|string|false|none|Configures the Secure attribute on session affinity cookie. Value "Always" indicates the Secure attribute will be set in the Set-Cookie header, "Never" indicates the Secure attribute will not be set, and "Auto" will set the Secure attribute depending if Always Use HTTPS is enabled.|
|zero_downtime_failover|string|false|none|Configures the zero-downtime failover between origins within a pool when session affinity is enabled. This feature is currently incompatible with Argo, Tiered Cache, and Bandwidth Alliance. The supported values are: - `"none"`: No failover takes place for sessions pinned to the origin (default). - `"temporary"`: Traffic will be sent to another other healthy origin until the originally pinned origin is available; note that this can potentially result in heavy origin flapping. - `"sticky"`: The session affinity cookie is updated and subsequent requests are sent to the new origin. Note: Zero-downtime failover with sticky sessions is currently not supported for session affinity by header.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|samesite|Auto|
|samesite|Lax|
|samesite|None|
|samesite|Strict|
|secure|Auto|
|secure|Always|
|secure|Never|
|zero_downtime_failover|none|
|zero_downtime_failover|temporary|
|zero_downtime_failover|sticky|

<h2 id="tocS_load-balancing_session_affinity_ttl">load-balancing_session_affinity_ttl</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaload-balancing_session_affinity_ttl"></a>
<a id="schema_load-balancing_session_affinity_ttl"></a>
<a id="tocSload-balancing_session_affinity_ttl"></a>
<a id="tocsload-balancing_session_affinity_ttl"></a>

```json
1800
```

Time, in seconds, until a client's session expires after being created. Once the expiry time has been reached, subsequent requests may get sent to a different origin server. The accepted ranges per `session_affinity` policy are: - `"cookie"` / `"ip_cookie"`: The current default of 23 hours will be used unless explicitly set. The accepted range of values is between [1800, 604800]. - `"header"`: The current default of 1800 seconds will be used unless explicitly set. The accepted range of values is between [30, 3600]. Note: With session affinity by header, sessions only expire after they haven't been used for the number of seconds specified.

<h2 id="tocS_load-balancing_steering_policy">load-balancing_steering_policy</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaload-balancing_steering_policy"></a>
<a id="schema_load-balancing_steering_policy"></a>
<a id="tocSload-balancing_steering_policy"></a>
<a id="tocsload-balancing_steering_policy"></a>

```json
"dynamic_latency"
```

Steering Policy for this load balancer.
- `"off"`: Use `default_pools`.
- `"geo"`: Use `region_pools`/`country_pools`/`pop_pools`. For non-proxied requests, the country for `country_pools` is determined by `location_strategy`.
- `"random"`: Select a pool randomly.
- `"dynamic_latency"`: Use round trip time to select the closest pool in default_pools (requires pool health checks).
- `"proximity"`: Use the pools' latitude and longitude to select the closest pool using the Cloudflare PoP location for proxied requests or the location determined by `location_strategy` for non-proxied requests.
- `"least_outstanding_requests"`: Select a pool by taking into consideration `random_steering` weights, as well as each pool's number of outstanding requests. Pools with more pending requests are weighted proportionately less relative to others.
- `"least_connections"`: Select a pool by taking into consideration `random_steering` weights, as well as each pool's number of open connections. Pools with more open connections are weighted proportionately less relative to others. Supported for HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 connections.
- `""`: Will map to `"geo"` if you use `region_pools`/`country_pools`/`pop_pools` otherwise `"off"`.

<h2 id="tocS_load-balancing_topology_match">load-balancing_topology_match</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaload-balancing_topology_match"></a>

```json
{
  "countries": [
    "string"
  ],
  "pops": [
    "string"
  ],
  "regions": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

Matches requests by location. Set any combination of `pops`, `countries`, and `regions` (at least one is required); a request matches when its value appears in any populated list (e.g. `regions: ["WNAM"]` with `countries: ["US"]` matches a request in either WNAM or the US).

### Properties

|---|---|---|---|---|
|countries|[string]|false|none|A list of ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes. Matches when the request's country is in this list.|
|pops|[string]|false|none|A list of Cloudflare PoP codes. Matches when the request's PoP is in this list.|
|regions|[string]|false|none|A list of Cloudflare region codes (e.g. `WNAM`, `ENAM`, `WEU`). Matches when the request's region is in this list.|

<h2 id="tocS_logpush_last_complete">logpush_last_complete</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalogpush_last_complete"></a>
<a id="schema_logpush_last_complete"></a>
<a id="tocSlogpush_last_complete"></a>
<a id="tocslogpush_last_complete"></a>

```json
"1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
```

Records the last time for which logs have been successfully pushed. If the last successful push was for logs range 2018-07-23T10:00:00Z to 2018-07-23T10:01:00Z then the value of this field will be 2018-07-23T10:01:00Z. If the job has never run or has just been enabled and hasn't run yet then the field will be empty.

<h2 id="tocS_logpush_last_error">logpush_last_error</h2>

<a id="tocSlogpush_last_error"></a>
<a id="tocslogpush_last_error"></a>

```json
"1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
```

Records the last time the job failed. If not null, the job is currently. failing. If null, the job has either never failed or has run successfully at least once since last failure. See also the error_message field.

If migrating from the logpull api, copy the url (full url or just the query string) of your call here, and logpush will keep on making this call for you, setting start and end times appropriately.

```json
    "timestamp_format": "unixnano"
  }
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|dataset|[logpush_dataset](#schemalogpush_dataset)|false|none|Name of the dataset. A list of supported datasets can be found on the [Developer Docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/reference/log-fields/).|
|destination_conf|[logpush_destination_conf](#schemalogpush_destination_conf)|false|none|Uniquely identifies a resource (such as an s3 bucket) where data. will be pushed. Additional configuration parameters supported by the destination may be included.|
|enabled|[logpush_enabled](#schemalogpush_enabled)|false|none|Flag that indicates if the job is enabled.|
|error_message|[logpush_error_message](#schemalogpush_error_message)|false|none|If not null, the job is currently failing. Failures are usually. repetitive (example: no permissions to write to destination bucket). Only the last failure is recorded. On successful execution of a job the error_message and last_error are set to null.|
|filter_attack_traffic|[logpush_filter_attack_traffic](#schemalogpush_filter_attack_traffic)|false|none|When true, excludes DDoS attack traffic from logs. This option is supported for the `http_requests`, `firewall_events`, and `network_analytics_logs` datasets.|
|frequency|[logpush_frequency](#schemalogpush_frequency)|false|none|**Deprecated.** This field is deprecated. Please use `max_upload_*` parameters instead. . The frequency at which Cloudflare sends batches of logs to your destination. Setting frequency to high sends your logs in larger quantities of smaller files. Setting frequency to low sends logs in smaller quantities of larger files.|
|id|[logpush_id](#schemalogpush_id)|false|none|Unique id of the job.|
|kind|[logpush_kind](#schemalogpush_kind)|false|none|The kind parameter (optional) is used to differentiate between Logpush and Edge Log Delivery jobs (when supported by the dataset).|
|last_complete|[logpush_last_complete](#schemalogpush_last_complete)|false|none|Records the last time for which logs have been successfully pushed. If the last successful push was for logs range 2018-07-23T10:00:00Z to 2018-07-23T10:01:00Z then the value of this field will be 2018-07-23T10:01:00Z. If the job has never run or has just been enabled and hasn't run yet then the field will be empty.|
|last_error|[logpush_last_error](#schemalogpush_last_error)|false|none|Records the last time the job failed. If not null, the job is currently. failing. If null, the job has either never failed or has run successfully at least once since last failure. See also the error_message field.|
|logpull_options|[logpush_logpull_options](#schemalogpush_logpull_options)|false|none|**Deprecated.** This field is deprecated. Use `output_options` instead. Configuration string. It specifies things like requested fields and timestamp formats. If migrating from the logpull api, copy the url (full url or just the query string) of your call here, and logpush will keep on making this call for you, setting start and end times appropriately.|
|max_upload_bytes|[logpush_max_upload_bytes](#schemalogpush_max_upload_bytes)|false|none|The maximum uncompressed file size of a batch of logs. This setting value must be between `5 MB` and `1 GB`, or `0` to disable it. Note that you cannot set a minimum file size; this means that log files may be much smaller than this batch size.|
|max_upload_interval_seconds|[logpush_max_upload_interval_seconds](#schemalogpush_max_upload_interval_seconds)|false|none|The maximum interval in seconds for log batches. This setting must be between 30 and 300 seconds (5 minutes), or `0` to disable it. Note that you cannot specify a minimum interval for log batches; this means that log files may be sent in shorter intervals than this.|
|max_upload_records|[logpush_max_upload_records](#schemalogpush_max_upload_records)|false|none|The maximum number of log lines per batch. This setting must be between 1000 and 1,000,000 lines, or `0` to disable it. Note that you cannot specify a minimum number of log lines per batch; this means that log files may contain many fewer lines than this.|
|name|[logpush_name](#schemalogpush_name)|false|none|Optional human readable job name. Not unique. Cloudflare suggests. that you set this to a meaningful string, like the domain name, to make it easier to identify your job.|
|output_options|[logpush_output_options](#schemalogpush_output_options)|false|none|The structured replacement for `logpull_options`. When including this field, the `logpull_option` field will be ignored.|

The structured replacement for `logpull_options`. When including this field, the `logpull_option` field will be ignored.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|CVE-2021-44228|boolean \| null|false|none|If set to true, will cause all occurrences of `${` in the generated files to be replaced with `x{`.|
|batch_prefix|string \| null|false|none|String to be prepended before each batch.|
|batch_suffix|string \| null|false|none|String to be appended after each batch.|
|field_delimiter|string \| null|false|none|String to join fields. This field be ignored when `record_template` is set.|
|field_names|[string]|false|none|List of field names to be included in the Logpush output. For the moment, there is no option to add all fields at once, so you must specify all the fields names you are interested in.|
|merge_subrequests|boolean \| null|false|none|If set to true, subrequests will be merged into the parent request. Only supported for the `http_requests` dataset.|
|output_type|string|false|none|Specifies the output type, such as `ndjson` or `csv`. This sets default values for the rest of the settings, depending on the chosen output type. Some formatting rules, like string quoting, are different between output types.|
|record_delimiter|string \| null|false|none|String to be inserted in-between the records as separator.|
|record_prefix|string \| null|false|none|String to be prepended before each record.|
|record_suffix|string \| null|false|none|String to be appended after each record.|
|record_template|string \| null|false|none|String to use as template for each record instead of the default json key value mapping. All fields used in the template must be present in `field_names` as well, otherwise they will end up as null. Format as a Go `text/template` without any standard functions, like conditionals, loops, sub-templates, etc.|
|sample_rate|number(float) \| null|false|none|Specifies the sampling rate as a floating number greater than 0 and at most 1. Sampling is applied on top of filtering, and regardless of the current `sample_interval` of the data.|
|timestamp_format|string|false|none|String to specify the format for timestamps, such as `unixnano`, `unix`, `rfc3339`, `rfc3339ms` or `rfc3339ns`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|

|output_type|csv|
|timestamp_format|unixnano|
|timestamp_format|unix|

|timestamp_format|rfc3339ms|
|timestamp_format|rfc3339ns|

<h2 id="tocS_logshare_count">logshare_count</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalogshare_count"></a>

<a id="tocSlogshare_count"></a>


When `?count=` is provided, the response will contain up to `count` results. Since results are not sorted, you are likely to get different data for repeated requests. `count` must be an integer > 0.

<h2 id="tocS_logshare_end">logshare_end</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalogshare_end"></a>
<a id="schema_logshare_end"></a>
<a id="tocSlogshare_end"></a>
<a id="tocslogshare_end"></a>

```json
"2018-05-20T10:01:00Z"
```

Sets the (exclusive) end of the requested time frame. This can be a unix timestamp (in seconds or nanoseconds), or an absolute timestamp that conforms to RFC 3339. `end` must be at least five minutes earlier than now and must be later than `start`. Difference between `start` and `end` must be not greater than one hour.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|string|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|integer|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_logshare_fields">logshare_fields</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalogshare_fields"></a>
<a id="schema_logshare_fields"></a>
<a id="tocSlogshare_fields"></a>
<a id="tocslogshare_fields"></a>

```json
"ClientIP,RayID,EdgeStartTimestamp"
```

The `/received` route by default returns a limited set of fields, and allows customers to override the default field set by specifying individual fields. The reasons for this are: 1. Most customers require only a small subset of fields, but that subset varies from customer to customer; 2. Flat schema is much easier to work with downstream (importing into BigTable etc); 3. Performance (time to process, file size). If `?fields=` is not specified, default field set is returned. This default field set may change at any time. When `?fields=` is provided, each record is returned with the specified fields. `fields` must be specified as a comma separated list without any whitespaces, and all fields must exist. The order in which fields are specified does not matter, and the order of fields in the response is not specified.

<h2 id="tocS_logshare_sample">logshare_sample</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalogshare_sample"></a>
<a id="schema_logshare_sample"></a>
<a id="tocSlogshare_sample"></a>
<a id="tocslogshare_sample"></a>

```json
0.1
```

When `?sample=` is provided, a sample of matching records is returned. If `sample=0.1` then 10% of records will be returned. Sampling is random: repeated calls will not only return different records, but likely will also vary slightly in number of returned records. When `?count=` is also specified, `count` is applied to the number of returned records, not the sampled records. So, with `sample=0.05` and `count=7`, when there is a total of 100 records available, approximately five will be returned. When there are 1000 records, seven will be returned. When there are 10,000 records, seven will be returned.

```json
"2018-05-20T10:00:00Z"
```

Sets the (inclusive) beginning of the requested time frame. This can be a unix timestamp (in seconds or nanoseconds), or an absolute timestamp that conforms to RFC 3339. At this point in time, it cannot exceed a time in the past greater than seven days.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|string|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|integer|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_logshare_timestamps">logshare_timestamps</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalogshare_timestamps"></a>
<a id="schema_logshare_timestamps"></a>
<a id="tocSlogshare_timestamps"></a>
<a id="tocslogshare_timestamps"></a>

```json
"unixnano"
```

By default, timestamps in responses are returned as Unix nanosecond integers. The `?timestamps=` argument can be set to change the format in which response timestamps are returned. Possible values are: `unix`, `unixnano`, `rfc3339`. Note that `unix` and `unixnano` return timestamps as integers; `rfc3339` returns timestamps as strings.

<h2 id="tocS_magic-visibility-mnm_mnm_rule">magic-visibility-mnm_mnm_rule</h2>

```json
{
  "automatic_advertisement": "false",
  "bandwidth_threshold": 1000,
  "duration": "300s",
  "id": "2890e6fa406311ed9b5a23f70f6fb8cf",
  "name": "my_rule_1",
  "packet_threshold": 10000,
  "prefix_match": "exact",
  "prefixes": [
    "203.0.113.1/32"
  ],
  "type": "zscore",
  "zscore_sensitivity": "high",
  "zscore_target": "bits"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|automatic_advertisement|[magic-visibility-mnm_mnm_rule_automatic_advertisement](#schemamagic-visibility-mnm_mnm_rule_automatic_advertisement)|true|none|Toggle on if you would like Cloudflare to automatically advertise the IP Prefixes within the rule via Magic Transit when the rule is triggered. Only available for users of Magic Transit.|
|bandwidth_threshold|[magic-visibility-mnm_mnm_rule_bandwidth_threshold](#schemamagic-visibility-mnm_mnm_rule_bandwidth_threshold)|false|none|The number of bits per second for the rule. When this value is exceeded for the set duration, an alert notification is sent. Minimum of 1 and no maximum.|
|duration|[magic-visibility-mnm_mnm_rule_duration](#schemamagic-visibility-mnm_mnm_rule_duration)|false|none|The amount of time that the rule threshold must be exceeded to send an alert notification. The final value must be equivalent to one of the following 8 values ["1m","5m","10m","15m","20m","30m","45m","60m"].|
|id|[magic-visibility-mnm_rule_identifier](#schemamagic-visibility-mnm_rule_identifier)|true|none|The id of the rule. Must be unique.|
|name|[magic-visibility-mnm_mnm_rule_name](#schemamagic-visibility-mnm_mnm_rule_name)|true|none|The name of the rule. Must be unique. Supports characters A-Z, a-z, 0-9, underscore (_), dash (-), period (.), and tilde (~). You can’t have a space in the rule name. Max 256 characters.|
|packet_threshold|[magic-visibility-mnm_mnm_rule_packet_threshold](#schemamagic-visibility-mnm_mnm_rule_packet_threshold)|false|none|The number of packets per second for the rule. When this value is exceeded for the set duration, an alert notification is sent. Minimum of 1 and no maximum.|
|prefix_match|[magic-visibility-mnm_mnm_rule_prefix_match](#schemamagic-visibility-mnm_mnm_rule_prefix_match)|false|none|Prefix match type to be applied for a prefix auto advertisement when using an advanced_ddos rule.|
|prefixes|[magic-visibility-mnm_mnm_rule_ip_prefixes](#schemamagic-visibility-mnm_mnm_rule_ip_prefixes)|true|none|none|
|type|[magic-visibility-mnm_mnm_rule_type](#schemamagic-visibility-mnm_mnm_rule_type)|true|none|MNM rule type.|
|zscore_sensitivity|[magic-visibility-mnm_mnm_rule_zscore_sensitivity](#schemamagic-visibility-mnm_mnm_rule_zscore_sensitivity)|false|none|Level of sensitivity set for zscore rules.|
|zscore_target|[magic-visibility-mnm_mnm_rule_zscore_target](#schemamagic-visibility-mnm_mnm_rule_zscore_target)|false|none|Target of the zscore rule analysis.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|duration|1m|
|duration|5m|
|duration|10m|
|duration|15m|
|duration|20m|
|duration|30m|
|duration|45m|
|duration|60m|
|prefix_match|exact|
|prefix_match|subnet|
|prefix_match|supernet|
|type|threshold|
|type|zscore|

<h2 id="tocS_magic_bgp_config">magic_bgp_config</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemamagic_bgp_config"></a>
<a id="schema_magic_bgp_config"></a>

<a id="tocsmagic_bgp_config"></a>

```json
{
  "customer_asn": 0,
  "export_filter_id": "a1b2c3d4e5f647890a1b2c3d4e5f6789",
  "extra_prefixes": [
    "string"
  ],
  "import_filter_id": "a1b2c3d4e5f647890a1b2c3d4e5f6789",
  "md5_key": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customer_asn|integer(int32)|true|none|ASN used on the customer end of the BGP session|
|export_filter_id|string|false|none|ID of the BGP filter profile applied to routes advertised to the customer.|
|extra_prefixes|[string(cidr)]|false|none|Prefixes in this list will be advertised to the customer device, in addition to the routes in the Magic routing table.<br>Each entry must be a network address in CIDR notation with no host bits set (for example `192.0.2.0/24`, not<br>`192.0.2.1/24`) and must not repeat another entry. IPv6 prefixes are accepted only when the tunnel has an<br>`interface_address6`.<br>|
|import_filter_id|string|false|none|ID of the BGP filter profile applied to routes received from the customer.|
|md5_key|string|false|none|MD5 key to use for session authentication.<br><br>Note that *this is not a security measure*. MD5 is not a valid security mechanism, and the<br>key is not treated as a secret value. This is *only* supported for preventing<br>misconfiguration, not for defending against malicious attacks.<br><br>The MD5 key, if set, must be of non-zero length and consist only of the following types of<br>character:<br><br>* ASCII alphanumerics: `[a-zA-Z0-9]`<br>* Special characters in the set `'!@#$%^&*()+[]{}<>/.,;:_-~`= \\|`<br><br>In other words, MD5 keys may contain any printable ASCII character aside from newline (0x0A),<br>quotation mark (`"`), vertical tab (0x0B), carriage return (0x0D), tab (0x09), form feed<br>(0x0C), and the question mark (`?`). Requests specifying an MD5 key with one or more of<br>these disallowed characters will be rejected.|

```json
  ]

```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|targets|[string]|true|none|List of CIDR prefixes. Each entry may carry an optional suffix that specifies which prefix lengths to match relative to the prefix length N: '{X,Y}' matches prefix lengths in the inclusive range [X, Y] where N <= X <= Y <= max (max is 32 for IPv4, 128 for IPv6), '{X}' matches exactly length X (equivalent to {X,X}), '+' is shorthand for {N, max} (the prefix and all more-specific subnets, including at length N itself; valid even when N is the maximum length). Omit the suffix to match the prefix exactly at length N.|

<h2 id="tocS_magic_create_bgp_filter_profile_request">magic_create_bgp_filter_profile_request</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemamagic_create_bgp_filter_profile_request"></a>
<a id="schema_magic_create_bgp_filter_profile_request"></a>
<a id="tocSmagic_create_bgp_filter_profile_request"></a>
<a id="tocsmagic_create_bgp_filter_profile_request"></a>

```json
{
  "description": "Allowed corporate subnets from on-premises",
  "match_action": "allow",
  "name": "Allowed On-Prem Imports",
  "targets": [
    "10.0.0.0/8{8,32}"
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|string|false|none|Description of the filter profile|
|match_action|[magic_bgp_filter_match_action](#schemamagic_bgp_filter_match_action)|true|none|Action to take when a route matches one of the targets in this profile|
|name|string|true|none|Friendly name for the filter profile|
|targets|[string]|true|none|List of CIDR prefixes. Each entry may carry an optional suffix that specifies which prefix lengths to match relative to the prefix length N: '{X,Y}' matches prefix lengths in the inclusive range [X, Y] where N <= X <= Y <= max (max is 32 for IPv4, 128 for IPv6), '{X}' matches exactly length X (equivalent to {X,X}), '+' is shorthand for {N, max} (the prefix and all more-specific subnets, including at length N itself; valid even when N is the maximum length). Omit the suffix to match the prefix exactly at length N.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|match_action|allow|
|match_action|deny|

```json
{

    "extra_prefixes": [
      "string"
    ],

    "md5_key": "string"
  },

  "customer_gre_endpoint": "203.0.113.1",
  "description": "Tunnel for ISP X",
  "health_check": {
    "enabled": true,
    "rate": "low",
    "target": {
      "effective": "203.0.113.1",
      "saved": "203.0.113.1"
    },
    "type": "request",
    "direction": "bidirectional"
  },
  "interface_address": "192.0.2.0/31",
  "interface_address6": "2606:54c1:7:0:a9fe:12d2:1:200/127",
  "mtu": 1476,
  "name": "GRE_1",
  "ttl": 64
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|automatic_return_routing|[magic_automatic_return_routing](#schemamagic_automatic_return_routing)|false|none|True if automatic stateful return routing should be enabled for a tunnel, false otherwise. Requires the `coupler_integration` account flag to be enabled; requests setting this to `true` without that flag will be rejected.|
|bgp|[magic_bgp_config](#schemamagic_bgp_config)|false|none|none|
|cloudflare_gre_endpoint|[magic_cloudflare_gre_endpoint](#schemamagic_cloudflare_gre_endpoint)|true|none|The IP address assigned to the Cloudflare side of the GRE tunnel.|
|customer_gre_endpoint|[magic_customer_gre_endpoint](#schemamagic_customer_gre_endpoint)|true|none|The IP address assigned to the customer side of the GRE tunnel.|
|description|[magic_schemas-description](#schemamagic_schemas-description)|false|none|An optional description of the GRE tunnel.|
|health_check|[magic_tunnel_health_check](#schemamagic_tunnel_health_check)|false|none|none|
|interface_address|[magic_interface_address](#schemamagic_interface_address)|true|none|A 31-bit prefix (/31 in CIDR notation) supporting two hosts, one for each side of the tunnel. Select the subnet from the following private IP space: 10.0.0.0–10.255.255.255, 172.16.0.0–172.31.255.255, 192.168.0.0–192.168.255.255.|
|interface_address6|[magic_interface_address6](#schemamagic_interface_address6)|false|none|A 127 bit IPV6 prefix from within the virtual_subnet6 prefix space with the address being the first IP of the subnet and not same as the address of virtual_subnet6. Eg if virtual_subnet6 is 2606:54c1:7:0:a9fe:12d2::/127 , interface_address6 could be 2606:54c1:7:0:a9fe:12d2:1:200/127|
|mtu|[magic_mtu](#schemamagic_mtu)|false|none|Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) in bytes for the GRE tunnel. The minimum value is 576.|
|name|[magic_gre_tunnel_name](#schemamagic_gre_tunnel_name)|true|none|The name of the tunnel. The name cannot contain spaces or special characters, must be 15 characters or less, and cannot share a name with another GRE tunnel.|
|ttl|[magic_ttl](#schemamagic_ttl)|false|none|Time To Live (TTL) in number of hops of the GRE tunnel.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|[magic_description](#schemamagic_description)|false|none|An optional human provided description of the static route.|
|nexthop|[magic_nexthop](#schemamagic_nexthop)|true|none|The next-hop IP Address for the static route.|
|prefix|[magic_prefix](#schemamagic_prefix)|true|none|IP Prefix in Classless Inter-Domain Routing format.|
|priority|[magic_priority](#schemamagic_priority)|true|none|Priority of the static route.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|type|string|true|none|The type of the option value. text: a string (max 255 bytes). hex: colon-separated hex bytes (e.g. "01:04:aa:bb:cc", max 255 bytes). ip: an IPv4 address (e.g. "10.20.30.40"). byte: an unsigned integer 0-255 (1 byte). short: an unsigned integer 0-65535 (2 bytes). integer: an unsigned integer 0-4294967295 (4 bytes).<br>|
|value|string|true|none|The option value, interpreted according to the type field.|

|type|hex|
|type|ip|
|type|byte|

This field is ignored for bidirectional healthchecks as the interface_address (not assigned to the Cloudflare side of the tunnel) is used as the target. Must be in object form if the x-magic-new-hc-target header is set to true and string form if x-magic-new-hc-target is absent or set to false.|
|type|string|false|none|The type of healthcheck to run, reply or request. The default value is `reply`.|

```json
}
```

The destination address in a request type health check. After the healthcheck is decapsulated at the customer end of the tunnel, the ICMP echo will be forwarded to this address. This field defaults to `customer_gre_endpoint address`. This field is ignored for bidirectional healthchecks as the interface_address (not assigned to the Cloudflare side of the tunnel) is used as the target.

|saved|string|false|none|The saved health check target. Setting the value to the empty string indicates that the calculated default value will be used.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|as_no|integer(int32)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated. Use customer_asn.|
|cloudflare_endpoint|string(ipv4)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Read-only for v1.5; derived from interface_address.|
|customer_asn|integer(int32)|false|none|ASN used on the customer end of the BGP session.|
|customer_endpoint|string(ipv4)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Read-only for v1.5; derived from interface_address.|
|export_filter_id|string|false|none|ID of the BGP filter profile applied to routes advertised to the customer.|
|extra_prefixes|[string(cidr)]|false|none|IPv4 prefixes in this list will be advertised to the customer device, in addition to the routes in the Magic<br>routing table. Each entry must be a network address in CIDR notation with no host bits set (for example<br>`192.0.2.0/24`, not `192.0.2.1/24`) and must not repeat another entry.<br>|
|import_filter_id|string|false|none|ID of the BGP filter profile applied to routes received from the customer.|
|md5_key|string|false|none|MD5 key to use for session authentication.<br><br>Note that *this is not a security measure*. MD5 is not a valid security mechanism, and the<br>key is not treated as a secret value. This is *only* supported for preventing<br>misconfiguration, not for defending against malicious attacks.<br><br>The MD5 key, if set, must be of non-zero length and consist only of the following types of<br>character:<br><br>* ASCII alphanumerics: `[a-zA-Z0-9]`<br>* Special characters in the set `'!@#$%^&*()+[]{}<>/.,;:_-~`= \\|`<br><br>In other words, MD5 keys may contain any printable ASCII character aside from newline (0x0A),<br>quotation mark (`"`), vertical tab (0x0B), carriage return (0x0D), tab (0x09), form feed<br>(0x0C), and the question mark (`?`). Requests specifying an MD5 key with one or more of<br>these disallowed characters will be rejected.|

```json
  "rate": "low",
  "target": {
    "effective": "203.0.113.1",
    "saved": "203.0.113.1"
  },

  "source": "198.41.199.225"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|Determines whether to run healthchecks for a tunnel.|
|rate|string|false|none|How frequent the health check is run. The default value is `mid`.|
|target|[magic_health_check_target](#schemamagic_health_check_target) \| string|false|none|The destination address in a request type health check. After the healthcheck is decapsulated at the customer end of the tunnel, the ICMP echo will be forwarded to this address. This field defaults to `customer_gre_endpoint address`. This field is ignored for bidirectional healthchecks as the interface_address (not assigned to the Cloudflare side of the tunnel) is used as the target. Must be in object form if the x-magic-new-hc-target header is set to true and string form if x-magic-new-hc-target is absent or set to false.|
|type|string|false|none|The type of healthcheck to run, reply or request. The default value is `reply`.|
|direction|string|false|none|The direction of the flow of the healthcheck. Either unidirectional, where the probe comes to you via the interconnect and the result comes back to Cloudflare via the open Internet, or bidirectional where both the probe and result come and go via the interconnect.|
|source|string|false|none|The source IPv4 address used for bidirectional health checks. Supported only for version 1.5 interconnects. It is required when `direction` is `bidirectional` and must be omitted (and is cleared) when `direction` is `unidirectional`. The address must be within RFC1918 space, the approved link-local range 169.254.240.0/20, or the Cloudflare reserved range 198.41.199.224/27.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|rate|low|
|rate|mid|
|rate|high|
|type|reply|
|type|request|
|direction|unidirectional|
|direction|bidirectional|

|automatic_return_routing|[magic_automatic_return_routing](#schemamagic_automatic_return_routing)|false|none|True if automatic stateful return routing should be enabled for a tunnel, false otherwise. Requires the `coupler_integration` account flag to be enabled; requests setting this to `true` without that flag will be rejected.|
|bgp|[magic_bgp_config](#schemamagic_bgp_config)|false|none|none|
|cloudflare_endpoint|[magic_cloudflare_ipsec_endpoint](#schemamagic_cloudflare_ipsec_endpoint)|true|none|The IP address assigned to the Cloudflare side of the IPsec tunnel.|
|custom_remote_identities|[magic_custom_remote_identities](#schemamagic_custom_remote_identities)|false|none|none|
|customer_endpoint|[magic_customer_ipsec_endpoint](#schemamagic_customer_ipsec_endpoint)|false|none|The IP address assigned to the customer side of the IPsec tunnel. Not required, but must be set for proactive traceroutes to work.|
|description|[magic_components-schemas-description](#schemamagic_components-schemas-description)|false|none|An optional description forthe IPsec tunnel.|
|health_check|[magic_tunnel_health_check](#schemamagic_tunnel_health_check)|false|none|none|
|interface_address|[magic_interface_address](#schemamagic_interface_address)|true|none|A 31-bit prefix (/31 in CIDR notation) supporting two hosts, one for each side of the tunnel. Select the subnet from the following private IP space: 10.0.0.0–10.255.255.255, 172.16.0.0–172.31.255.255, 192.168.0.0–192.168.255.255.|
|interface_address6|[magic_interface_address6](#schemamagic_interface_address6)|false|none|A 127 bit IPV6 prefix from within the virtual_subnet6 prefix space with the address being the first IP of the subnet and not same as the address of virtual_subnet6. Eg if virtual_subnet6 is 2606:54c1:7:0:a9fe:12d2::/127 , interface_address6 could be 2606:54c1:7:0:a9fe:12d2:1:200/127|
|name|[magic_ipsec_tunnel_name](#schemamagic_ipsec_tunnel_name)|true|none|The name of the IPsec tunnel. The name cannot share a name with other tunnels.|
|psk|[magic_psk](#schemamagic_psk)|false|none|A randomly generated or provided string for use in the IPsec tunnel.|
|replay_protection|[magic_replay_protection](#schemamagic_replay_protection)|false|none|If `true`, then IPsec replay protection will be supported in the Cloudflare-to-customer direction.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|ports|[[magic_port](#schemamagic_port)]|false|none|Array of ports on the provided LAN that will be included in the ACL. If no ports or port ranges are provided, communication on any port on this LAN is allowed.|
|subnets|[[magic_acl-subnet](#schemamagic_acl-subnet)]|false|none|Array of subnet IPs within the LAN that will be included in the ACL. If no subnets are provided, communication on any subnets on this LAN are allowed.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|Determines whether to run healthchecks for a tunnel.|
|rate|string|false|none|How frequent the health check is run. The default value is `mid`.|
|target|[magic_health_check_target](#schemamagic_health_check_target) \| string|false|none|The destination address in a request type health check. After the healthcheck is decapsulated at the customer end of the tunnel, the ICMP echo will be forwarded to this address. This field defaults to `customer_gre_endpoint address`. This field is ignored for bidirectional healthchecks as the interface_address (not assigned to the Cloudflare side of the tunnel) is used as the target. Must be in object form if the x-magic-new-hc-target header is set to true and string form if x-magic-new-hc-target is absent or set to false.|
|type|string|false|none|The type of healthcheck to run, reply or request. The default value is `reply`.|
|direction|string|false|none|The direction of the flow of the healthcheck. Either unidirectional, where the probe comes to you via the tunnel and the result comes back to Cloudflare via the open Internet, or bidirectional where both the probe and result come and go via the tunnel.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|rate|low|
|rate|mid|
|rate|high|
|type|reply|
|type|request|
|direction|unidirectional|
|direction|bidirectional|

<h2 id="tocS_magic_update_bgp_filter_profile_request">magic_update_bgp_filter_profile_request</h2>

<a id="tocsmagic_update_bgp_filter_profile_request"></a>

```json
{
  "description": "Allowed corporate subnets from on-premises",
  "match_action": "allow",
  "name": "Allowed On-Prem Imports",
  "targets": [
    "10.0.0.0/8{8,32}"
  ]
}
```

Partial update for a BGP filter profile. At least one property must be provided; omitted properties are left unchanged. To clear an existing description send `description: ""`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|string|false|none|Description of the filter profile|
|match_action|[magic_bgp_filter_match_action](#schemamagic_bgp_filter_match_action)|false|none|Action to take when a route matches one of the targets in this profile|
|name|string|false|none|Friendly name for the filter profile|
|targets|[string]|false|none|List of CIDR prefixes. Each entry may carry an optional suffix that specifies which prefix lengths to match relative to the prefix length N: '{X,Y}' matches prefix lengths in the inclusive range [X, Y] where N <= X <= Y <= max (max is 32 for IPv4, 128 for IPv6), '{X}' matches exactly length X (equivalent to {X,X}), '+' is shorthand for {N, max} (the prefix and all more-specific subnets, including at length N itself; valid even when N is the maximum length). Omit the suffix to match the prefix exactly at length N.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|match_action|allow|
|match_action|deny|

<h2 id="tocS_mconn-telemetry_event">mconn-telemetry_event</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemamconn-telemetry_event"></a>
<a id="schema_mconn-telemetry_event"></a>
<a id="tocSmconn-telemetry_event"></a>
<a id="tocsmconn-telemetry_event"></a>

```json
{
  "k": "Init"
}
```

Event kind plus event-specific payload fields.

Event kinds:
- `Init`: Initialized process
- `Leave`: Stopped process
- `StartAttestation`: Started attestation
- `FinishAttestationSuccess`: Finished attestation
- `FinishAttestationFailure`: Failed attestation
- `StartRotateCryptKey`: Started crypt key rotation
- `FinishRotateCryptKeySuccess`: Finished crypt key rotation
- `FinishRotateCryptKeyFailure`: Failed crypt key rotation
- `StartRotatePki`: Started PKI rotation
- `FinishRotatePkiSuccess`: Finished PKI rotation
- `FinishRotatePkiFailure`: Failed PKI rotation
- `StartUpgrade`: Started upgrade
- `FinishUpgradeSuccess`: Finished upgrade
- `FinishUpgradeFailure`: Failed upgrade
- `BlessSlotSuccess`: Blessed boot entry slot
- `BlessSlotPending`: Boot entry slot is not yet blessed
- `BlessSlotFailure`: Failed to bless boot entry slot
- `Reconcile`: Reconciled
- `ConfigureCloudflaredTunnel`: Configured Cloudflared tunnel
- `RekeyInstallBoth`: Installed initial inbound and outbound keys
- `RekeyStart`: Installed new inbound key, kept old outbound
- `RekeyRestart`: Restarted in-progress rekey with newer key material
- `RekeyAdvance`: Confirmed traffic on new inbound key, swapped outbound to new
- `RekeyComplete`: Deleted old keys
- `RekeyReset`: Deleted all keys after receiving an unexpected key
- `HaTransition`: Completed HA state transition
- `HaError`: Received unexpected HA error
- `HaInit`: Initialized HA subsystem
- `HaLeave`: Stopped HA subsystem

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|k|string|true|none|Event kind|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|k|Init|
|k|Leave|
|k|StartAttestation|
|k|FinishAttestationSuccess|
|k|FinishAttestationFailure|
|k|StartRotateCryptKey|
|k|FinishRotateCryptKeySuccess|
|k|FinishRotateCryptKeyFailure|
|k|StartRotatePki|
|k|FinishRotatePkiSuccess|
|k|FinishRotatePkiFailure|
|k|StartUpgrade|
|k|FinishUpgradeSuccess|
|k|FinishUpgradeFailure|
|k|BlessSlotSuccess|

|k|BlessSlotFailure|
|k|Reconcile|
|k|ConfigureCloudflaredTunnel|

|k|RekeyStart|
|k|RekeyRestart|

Recorded Event

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|e|[mconn-telemetry_event](#schemamconn-telemetry_event)|true|none|Event kind plus event-specific payload fields.<br><br>Event kinds:<br>- `Init`: Initialized process<br>- `Leave`: Stopped process<br>- `StartAttestation`: Started attestation<br>- `FinishAttestationSuccess`: Finished attestation<br>- `FinishAttestationFailure`: Failed attestation<br>- `StartRotateCryptKey`: Started crypt key rotation<br>- `FinishRotateCryptKeySuccess`: Finished crypt key rotation<br>- `FinishRotateCryptKeyFailure`: Failed crypt key rotation<br>- `StartRotatePki`: Started PKI rotation<br>- `FinishRotatePkiSuccess`: Finished PKI rotation<br>- `FinishRotatePkiFailure`: Failed PKI rotation<br>- `StartUpgrade`: Started upgrade<br>- `FinishUpgradeSuccess`: Finished upgrade<br>- `FinishUpgradeFailure`: Failed upgrade<br>- `BlessSlotSuccess`: Blessed boot entry slot<br>- `BlessSlotPending`: Boot entry slot is not yet blessed<br>- `BlessSlotFailure`: Failed to bless boot entry slot<br>- `Reconcile`: Reconciled<br>- `ConfigureCloudflaredTunnel`: Configured Cloudflared tunnel<br>- `RekeyInstallBoth`: Installed initial inbound and outbound keys<br>- `RekeyStart`: Installed new inbound key, kept old outbound<br>- `RekeyRestart`: Restarted in-progress rekey with newer key material<br>- `RekeyAdvance`: Confirmed traffic on new inbound key, swapped outbound to new<br>- `RekeyComplete`: Deleted old keys<br>- `RekeyReset`: Deleted all keys after receiving an unexpected key<br>- `HaTransition`: Completed HA state transition<br>- `HaError`: Received unexpected HA error<br>- `HaInit`: Initialized HA subsystem<br>- `HaLeave`: Stopped HA subsystem|
|n|number|true|none|Sequence number, used to order events with the same timestamp|
|t|number|true|none|Time the Event was recorded (seconds since the Unix epoch)|
|v|string|false|none|Version|

<h2 id="tocS_monetization_monetization-price">monetization_monetization-price</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemamonetization_monetization-price"></a>
<a id="schema_monetization_monetization-price"></a>
<a id="tocSmonetization_monetization-price"></a>
<a id="tocsmonetization_monetization-price"></a>

```json
"250000"
```

Price in the smallest indivisible unit of the configured payment token, encoded as a decimal string. Must be a canonical decimal integer in [1000, 100000000]: no leading zeros, and a bare JSON number is rejected. The price is required for the fixed-price schemes ("exact" and "upto") and must be at least 1000, the smallest amount the payment facilitator can settle ($0.001 for a 6-decimal token such as USDC), and at most 100000000 ($100 for a 6-decimal token). When the scheme is "origin_controlled" the origin server sets pricing dynamically and the rule carries no price: the field must be omitted — any provided value, including "0", is rejected because it would not be enforced. Responses always encode this as a string and omit it for "origin_controlled" rules; the pattern matches exactly the set of values the server accepts.

The rule carries no price and the price field must be omitted — any provided value, including "0", is rejected because it would not be enforced.|
|id|object|true|none|The server-assigned unique ID of the payment rule. Stable across full-ruleset replacements.|


Payment rule with a fixed price set at configuration time.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|address|string|true|none|0x-prefixed 20-byte hexadecimal Ethereum address. Mixed-case addresses must carry a valid EIP-55 checksum; all-lowercase or all-uppercase addresses are also accepted. The address must pass wallet screening whenever its rule is deployed or patched.|
|description|string|false|none|none|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|expression|string|true|none|Wirefilter expression identifying the requests that require payment. Forwarded verbatim to the Rulesets API, which validates its syntax.|
|id|object|false|none|Optional on input. Include the ID of an existing payment rule to update it in place, preserving its stable identity across the full-ruleset replacement; omit it to create a new rule. An ID that does not match an existing payment rule in the zone is rejected. Rules omitted from the request are deleted.|
|price|[monetization_monetization-price](#schemamonetization_monetization-price)|true|none|Price in the smallest indivisible unit of the configured payment token, encoded as a decimal string. Must be a canonical decimal integer in [1000, 100000000]: no leading zeros, and a bare JSON number is rejected. The price is required for the fixed-price schemes ("exact" and "upto") and must be at least 1000, the smallest amount the payment facilitator can settle ($0.001 for a 6-decimal token such as USDC), and at most 100000000 ($100 for a 6-decimal token). When the scheme is "origin_controlled" the origin server sets pricing dynamically and the rule carries no price: the field must be omitted — any provided value, including "0", is rejected because it would not be enforced. Responses always encode this as a string and omit it for "origin_controlled" rules; the pattern matches exactly the set of values the server accepts.|
|scheme|string|true|none|X402 payment scheme. "exact" requires the specified payment amount; "upto" permits a payment up to the specified amount. Both fixed-price schemes require the price field.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|scheme|exact|
|scheme|upto|

```json
{
  "created": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "expires": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "jti": "f3a1b2c3d4e5f67890a1b2c3d4e5f678",
  "label": "primary-encoder",
  "operations": [
    "publish",
    "subscribe"
  ],
  "secret": "eyJhbGciOiJFZDI1NTE5..."
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|expires|string(date-time)|true|none|Mandatory; no more than 1 year after `created`.|
|jti|string|true|none|Token identity and registry key (32 hex chars).|
|label|string|false|none|Optional, customer-set.|
|operations|[string]|true|none|Signed allowlist of what the token may do. V1 coarse roles; the array<br>form extends to fine-grained MoQT message names later without a<br>breaking change.<br>|
|secret|string|false|none|The signed JWT. Present ONLY in create / auto-create responses (shown<br>once); never returned by list, never stored.<br>|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|operations|publish|
|operations|subscribe|

```json
  "issuers": [

      "cloudflare_tokens": [
        {
          "created": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
```

|issuers|[[moq_issuer](#schemamoq_issuer)]|true|none|Token collection (discriminated union on `type`). On create this<br>holds the auto-created default pair, each including its one-time<br>secret.<br>|
|modified|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|name|string|true|none|none|
|uid|string|true|none|Server-generated unique identifier (32 hex chars).|

<h2 id="tocS_moq_tokens_envelope">moq_tokens_envelope</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemamoq_tokens_envelope"></a>
<a id="schema_moq_tokens_envelope"></a>
<a id="tocSmoq_tokens_envelope"></a>
<a id="tocsmoq_tokens_envelope"></a>

```json
{
  "issuers": [
    {
      "cloudflare_tokens": [
        {
          "created": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
          "expires": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
          "jti": "f3a1b2c3d4e5f67890a1b2c3d4e5f678",
          "label": "primary-encoder",
          "operations": [
            "publish",
            "subscribe"
          ],
          "secret": "eyJhbGciOiJFZDI1NTE5..."
        }
      ],
      "issuer": "cloudflare",
      "type": "cloudflare_jwt"
    }
  ]
}
```

A relay's token collection, keyed on issuer `type` (a discriminated
union). V1 ships exactly one arm (`cloudflare_jwt`). Clients iterate
`issuers`, switch on `type`, and ignore unknown types — that contract is
what makes adding or removing an arm non-breaking.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issuers|[[moq_issuer](#schemamoq_issuer)]|true|none|none|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

<h2 id="tocS_nsc_BgpControl">nsc_BgpControl</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemansc_bgpcontrol"></a>
<a id="schema_nsc_BgpControl"></a>
<a id="tocSnsc_bgpcontrol"></a>
<a id="tocsnsc_bgpcontrol"></a>

```json
{
  "customer_asn": 0,
  "extra_prefixes": [
    "192.168.3.4/31"
  ],
  "md5_key": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customer_asn|integer(int32)|true|none|ASN used on the customer end of the BGP session|
|extra_prefixes|[string(A.B.C.D/N)]|true|none|Extra set of static prefixes to advertise to the customer's end of the session<br>Prefixes containing host bits will be normalized to contain network bits only.<br>Duplicates are not allowed.|
|md5_key|string \| null|false|none|MD5 key to use for session authentication.<br><br>Note that *this is not a security measure*. MD5 is not a valid security mechanism, and the<br>key is not treated as a secret value. This is *only* supported for preventing<br>misconfiguration, not for defending against malicious attacks.<br><br>The MD5 key, if set, must be of non-zero length and consist only of the following types of<br>character:<br><br>* ASCII alphanumerics: `[a-zA-Z0-9]`<br>* Special characters in the set `'!@#$%^&*()+[]{}<>/.,;:_-~`= \\|`<br><br>In other words, MD5 keys may contain any printable ASCII character aside from newline<br>(0x0A), quotation mark (`"`), vertical tab (0x0B), carriage return (0x0D), tab (0x09),<br>form feed (0x0C), and the question mark (`?`). Requests specifying an MD5 key with one<br>or more of these disallowed characters will be rejected.|

|framework|string|true|read-only|Framework the project is using.|

|id|string|true|read-only|ID of the project.|
|latest_deployment|object|true|none|none|
|name|[pages_project_name](#schemapages_project_name)|true|none|Name of the Pages project. Must begin with a lowercase letter or digit and contain only lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens.|
|preview_script_name|string|true|read-only|Name of the preview script.|
|production_branch|string|true|none|Production branch of the project. Used to identify production deployments.|
|production_script_name|string|true|read-only|Name of the production script.|
|source|[pages_source](#schemapages_source)|false|none|Configs for the project source control.|
|subdomain|string|false|read-only|The Cloudflare subdomain associated with the project.|
|uses_functions|boolean \| null|true|read-only|Whether the project uses functions.|

|pr_comments_enabled|boolean|true|none|Whether to enable PR comments.|
|preview_branch_excludes|[string]|true|none|A list of branches that should not trigger a preview deployment. Wildcard syntax (`*`) is supported. Must be used with `preview_deployment_setting` set to `custom`.|
|preview_branch_includes|[string]|true|none|A list of branches that should trigger a preview deployment. Wildcard syntax (`*`) is supported. Must be used with `preview_deployment_setting` set to `custom`.|
|preview_deployment_setting|string|true|none|Controls whether commits to preview branches trigger a preview deployment.|
|production_branch|string|true|none|The production branch of the repository.|
|production_deployments_enabled|boolean|true|none|Whether to trigger a production deployment on commits to the production branch.|
|repo_id|string|true|none|The ID of the repository.|
|repo_name|string|true|none|The name of the repository.|

Zone-wide grace is represented by the zone configuration expires_at instead.|

|---|---|---|---|---|
