```json
[
  "count",
  "bytesIngress"
]
```

One or more metrics to compute. Options are:

Metric                    | Name                                | Example                  | Unit
--------------------------|-------------------------------------|--------------------------|--------------------------
count                     | Count of total events               | 1000                     | Count
bytesIngress              | Sum of ingress bytes                | 1000                     | Sum
bytesEgress               | Sum of egress bytes                 | 1000                     | Sum
durationAvg               | Average connection duration         | 1.0                      | Time in milliseconds
durationMedian            | Median connection duration          | 1.0                      | Time in milliseconds
duration90th              | 90th percentile connection duration | 1.0                      | Time in milliseconds
duration99th              | 99th percentile connection duration | 1.0                      | Time in milliseconds.

```json
  ],
```

```json
  },
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created_on|[spectrum-config_created](#schemaspectrum-config_created)|true|read-only|When the Application was created.|
|id|[spectrum-config_app_identifier](#schemaspectrum-config_app_identifier)|true|read-only|App identifier.|
|modified_on|[spectrum-config_modified](#schemaspectrum-config_modified)|true|read-only|When the Application was last modified.|
|argo_smart_routing|[spectrum-config_argo_smart_routing](#schemaspectrum-config_argo_smart_routing)|false|none|Enables Argo Smart Routing for this application.<br>Notes: Only available for TCP or UDP applications with traffic_type set to "direct".|
|dns|[spectrum-config_dns](#schemaspectrum-config_dns)|true|none|The name and type of DNS record for the Spectrum application.|
|edge_ips|[spectrum-config_edge_ips](#schemaspectrum-config_edge_ips)|false|none|The anycast edge IP configuration for the hostname of this application.|
|ip_firewall|[spectrum-config_ip_firewall](#schemaspectrum-config_ip_firewall)|false|none|Enables IP Access Rules for this application.<br>Notes: Only available for TCP applications.|
|origin_direct|[spectrum-config_origin_direct](#schemaspectrum-config_origin_direct)|false|none|List of origin IP addresses. Array may contain multiple IP addresses for load balancing.|
|origin_dns|[spectrum-config_origin_dns](#schemaspectrum-config_origin_dns)|false|none|The name and type of DNS record for the Spectrum application.|
|origin_port|[spectrum-config_origin_port](#schemaspectrum-config_origin_port)|false|none|The destination port at the origin. Only specified in conjunction with origin_dns. May use an integer to specify a single origin port, for example `1000`, or a string to specify a range of origin ports, for example `"1000-2000"`.<br>Notes: If specifying a port range, the number of ports in the range must match the number of ports specified in the "protocol" field.|
|origin_worker_id|[spectrum-config_origin_worker_id](#schemaspectrum-config_origin_worker_id)|false|none|Optional Worker script tag (worker ID) to use as the application's origin. Only supported for TCP applications with traffic_type "worker"; mutually exclusive with origin_direct, origin_dns, origin_port, proxy_protocol, and argo_smart_routing. tls may only be "off" or "flexible".|
|protocol|[spectrum-config_protocol](#schemaspectrum-config_protocol)|true|none|The port configuration at Cloudflare's edge. May specify a single port, for example `"tcp/1000"`, or a range of ports, for example `"tcp/1000-2000"`.|
|proxy_protocol|[spectrum-config_proxy_protocol](#schemaspectrum-config_proxy_protocol)|false|none|Enables Proxy Protocol to the origin. Refer to [Enable Proxy protocol](https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/getting-started/proxy-protocol/) for implementation details on PROXY Protocol V1, PROXY Protocol V2, and Simple Proxy Protocol.|
|tls|[spectrum-config_tls](#schemaspectrum-config_tls)|false|none|The type of TLS termination associated with the application.|
|traffic_type|[spectrum-config_traffic_type](#schemaspectrum-config_traffic_type)|true|none|Determines how data travels from the edge to your origin. When set to "direct", Spectrum will send traffic directly to your origin, and the application's type is derived from the `protocol`. When set to "http" or "https", Spectrum will apply Cloudflare's HTTP/HTTPS features as it sends traffic to your origin, and the application type matches this property exactly. When set to "worker", traffic is sent to the Worker specified by `origin_worker_id`.|
|virtual_network_id|[spectrum-config_virtual_network_id](#schemaspectrum-config_virtual_network_id)|false|none|Optional UUID of a virtual network for routing origin traffic through tunnel virtual networks.|

<h2 id="tocS_spectrum-config_traffic_type">spectrum-config_traffic_type</h2>

<a id="tocSspectrum-config_traffic_type"></a>
<a id="tocsspectrum-config_traffic_type"></a>

```json
"direct"
```

Determines how data travels from the edge to your origin. When set to "direct", Spectrum will send traffic directly to your origin, and the application's type is derived from the `protocol`. When set to "http" or "https", Spectrum will apply Cloudflare's HTTP/HTTPS features as it sends traffic to your origin, and the application type matches this property exactly. When set to "worker", traffic is sent to the Worker specified by `origin_worker_id`.

```json
{
  "action": "allow",
  "country": [
    "string"
  ],
  "ip": [
    "string"
  ],
  "type": "ip.src"
}
```

Defines rules for fine-grained control over content than signed URL tokens alone. Access rules primarily make tokens conditionally valid based on user information. Access Rules are specified on token payloads as the `accessRules` property containing an array of Rule objects.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|string|false|none|The action to take when a request matches a rule. If the action is `block`, the signed token blocks views for viewers matching the rule.|
|country|[string]|false|none|An array of 2-letter country codes in ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 format used to match requests.|
|ip|[string]|false|none|An array of IPv4 or IPV6 addresses or CIDRs used to match requests.|
|type|string|false|none|Lists available rule types to match for requests. An `any` type matches all requests and can be used as a wildcard to apply default actions after other rules.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|action|allow|
|action|block|

|recording|[stream_live_input_recording_settings](#schemastream_live_input_recording_settings)|false|none|Records the input to a Cloudflare Stream video. Behavior depends on the mode. |meta|[stream_media_metadata](#schemastream_media_metadata)|false|none|A user modifiable key-value store used to reference other systems of record for managing videos.|
|requireSignedURLs|[stream_requireSignedURLs](#schemastream_requiresignedurls)|false|none|Indicates whether the video can be a accessed using the UID. When set to `true`, a signed token must be generated with a signing key to view the video.|
|scheduledDeletion|[stream_scheduledDeletion](#schemastream_scheduleddeletion)|false|none|Indicates the date and time at which the video will be deleted. Omit the field to indicate no change, or include with a `null` value to remove an existing scheduled deletion. If specified, must be at least 30 days from upload time.|
|thumbnailTimestampPct|[stream_thumbnailTimestampPct](#schemastream_thumbnailtimestamppct)|false|none|The timestamp for a thumbnail image calculated as a percentage value of the video's duration. To convert from a second-wise timestamp to a percentage, divide the desired timestamp by the total duration of the video.  If this value is not set, the default thumbnail image is taken from 0s of the video.|
|watermark|[stream_watermark_at_upload](#schemastream_watermark_at_upload)|false|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

Enter allowed origin domains in an array and use `*` for wildcard subdomains. An empty array allows videos to be viewed on any origin.|
|hideLiveViewerCount|[stream_live_input_recording_hideLiveViewerCount](#schemastream_live_input_recording_hideliveviewercount)|false|none|Disables reporting the number of live viewers when this property is set to `true`.|
|mode|[stream_live_input_recording_mode](#schemastream_live_input_recording_mode)|false|none|Specifies the recording behavior for the live input. Set this value to `off` to prevent a recording. Set the value to `automatic` to begin a recording and transition to on-demand after Stream Live stops receiving input.|
|requireSignedURLs|[stream_live_input_recording_requireSignedURLs](#schemastream_live_input_recording_requiresignedurls)|false|none|Indicates if a video using the live input has the `requireSignedURLs` property set. Also enforces access controls on any video recording of the livestream with the live input.|
|timeoutSeconds|[stream_live_input_recording_timeoutSeconds](#schemastream_live_input_recording_timeoutseconds)|false|none|Determines the amount of time a live input configured in `automatic` mode should wait before a recording transitions from live to on-demand. `0` is recommended for most use cases and indicates the platform default should be used.|

<h2 id="tocS_stream_media_status">stream_media_status</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemastream_media_status"></a>
<a id="schema_stream_media_status"></a>
<a id="tocSstream_media_status"></a>
<a id="tocsstream_media_status"></a>

```json
{
  "errorReasonCode": "ERR_NON_VIDEO",
  "errorReasonText": "The file was not recognized as a valid video file.",
  "pctComplete": "45",
  "state": "inprogress"
}
```

Specifies a detailed status for a video. If the `state` is `inprogress` or `error`, the `step` field returns `encoding` or `manifest`. If the `state` is `inprogress`, `pctComplete` returns a number between 0 and 100 to indicate the approximate percent of completion. If the `state` is `error`, `errorReasonCode` and `errorReasonText` provide additional details.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errorReasonCode|[stream_errorReasonCode](#schemastream_errorreasoncode)|false|none|Specifies why the video failed to encode. This field is empty if the video is not in an `error` state. Preferred for programmatic use.|
|errorReasonText|[stream_errorReasonText](#schemastream_errorreasontext)|false|none|Specifies why the video failed to encode using a human readable error message in English. This field is empty if the video is not in an `error` state.|
|pctComplete|[stream_pctComplete](#schemastream_pctcomplete)|false|none|Indicates the progress as a percentage between 0 and 100.|
|state|[stream_media_state](#schemastream_media_state)|false|none|Specifies the processing status for all quality levels for a video.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|state|pendingupload|
|state|downloading|

<h2 id="tocS_stream_signed_token_request">stream_signed_token_request</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemastream_signed_token_request"></a>
<a id="schema_stream_signed_token_request"></a>
<a id="tocSstream_signed_token_request"></a>
<a id="tocsstream_signed_token_request"></a>

```json
{
  "accessRules": [
    {
      "action": "block",
      "country": [
        "US",
        "MX"
      ],
      "type": "ip.geoip.country"
    },
    {
      "action": "allow",
      "ip": [
        "93.184.216.0/24",
        "2400:cb00::/32"
      ],
      "type": "ip.src"
    },
    {
      "action": "block",
      "type": "any"
    }
  ],
  "downloadable": false,
  "exp": 0,
  "flags": {
    "original": false
  },
  "id": "ab0d4ef71g4425f8dcba9041231813000",
  "nbf": 0,
  "pem": ""
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accessRules|[[stream_accessRules](#schemastream_accessrules)]|false|none|The optional list of access rule constraints on the token. Access can be blocked or allowed based on an IP, IP range, or by country. Access rules are evaluated from first to last. If a rule matches, the associated action is applied and no further rules are evaluated.|
|downloadable|boolean|false|none|The optional boolean value that enables using signed tokens to access MP4 download links for a video.|
|exp|integer|false|none|The optional unix epoch timestamp that specficies the time after a token is not accepted. The maximum time specification is 24 hours from issuing time. If this field is not set, the default is one hour after issuing.|
|flags|object|false|none|Optional flags for the signed token.|
|id|string|false|none|The optional ID of a Stream signing key. If present, the `pem` field is also required.|
|nbf|integer|false|none|The optional unix epoch timestamp that specifies the time before a the token is not accepted. If this field is not set, the default is one hour before issuing.|
|pem|string|false|none|The optional base64 encoded private key in PEM format associated with a Stream signing key. If present, the `id` field is also required.|

To convert from a second-wise timestamp to a percentage, divide the desired timestamp by the total duration of the video. If this value is not set, the default thumbnail image is taken from 0s of the video.|
|url|string(uri)|false|none|A video's URL. The server must be publicly routable and support `HTTP HEAD` requests and `HTTP GET` range requests. The server should respond to `HTTP HEAD` requests with a `content-range` header that includes the size of the file. This field is deprecated in favor of `input`.|

|disable_auto_fallback|[teams-devices_disable_auto_fallback](#schemateams-devices_disable_auto_fallback)|false|none|If the `dns_server` field of a fallback domain is not present, the client will fall back to a best guess of the default/system DNS resolvers unless this policy option is set to `true`.|

<h2 id="tocS_teams-devices_global_acceleration">teams-devices_global_acceleration</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemateams-devices_global_acceleration"></a>

```json
{
  "allow_manual_override": true,
  "api_endpoints": [
    "198.51.100.1:443"
  ],
  "autoswitch": true,
  "enabled": true,
  "masque_endpoints": [
    "198.51.100.1:443"
  ],
  "wireguard_endpoints": [
    "198.51.100.1:2408"
  ]
}
```

Global Acceleration settings for China. When configured, WARP clients connect to the Global Accelerator addresses instead of the default ones. Please contact your account representative to enable this feature on your account. See https://developers.cloudflare.com/china-network/concepts/global-acceleration/.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_manual_override|boolean|false|none|Whether WARP users may manually override the automatic Global Acceleration decision. Defaults to true when not provided.|
|api_endpoints|[string]|true|none|IP:port entries for the API endpoints.|
|autoswitch|boolean|false|none|Automatically switch Global Acceleration regions based on device location. Defaults to false when not provided.|
|enabled|boolean|true|none|Global acceleration settings are used only when "enabled".|
|masque_endpoints|[string]|true|none|IP:port entries for the MASQUE tunnel endpoints. Either wireguard_endpoints or masque_endpoints must be provided.|
|wireguard_endpoints|[string]|true|none|IP:port entries for the WireGuard tunnel endpoints. Either wireguard_endpoints or masque_endpoints must be provided.|

<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemateams-devices_physical_device"></a>
<a id="schema_teams-devices_physical_device"></a>
<a id="tocSteams-devices_physical_device"></a>
<a id="tocsteams-devices_physical_device"></a>

```json
{
  "active_registrations": 1,
  "client_version": "1.0.0",
  "created_at": "2025-02-14T13:17:00Z",
  "deleted_at": "2025-02-14T13:17:00Z",
  "device_type": "linux",
  "hardware_id": "string",
  "id": "fc9ab6ab-3b94-4319-9941-459462b3d73e",
  "last_seen_at": "2025-02-14T13:17:00Z",
  "last_seen_registration": {
    "policy": {
      "default": true,
      "deleted": true,
      "id": "11ffb86f-3f0c-4306-b4a2-e62f872b166a",
      "name": "string",
      "updated_at": "2025-02-14T13:17:00Z"
    }
  },
  "last_seen_user": {
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "id": "f174e90a-fafe-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415",
    "name": "John Appleseed"
  },
  "mac_address": "f5:01:73:cf:12:23",
  "manufacturer": "ACME",
  "model": "Mark VII",
  "multiuser": true,
  "name": "My Device",
  "os_version": "string",
  "os_version_extra": "string",
  "public_ip": "1.1.1.1",
  "serial_number": "ABS765ASD8A",
  "tags": {
    "environment": "production",
    "fleet": "warehouse"
  },
  "updated_at": "2025-02-14T13:17:00Z"
}
```

A WARP Device.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active_registrations|integer|true|none|The number of active registrations for the device. Active registrations are those which haven't been revoked or deleted.|
|client_version|string \| null|false|none|Version of the WARP client.|
|created_at|string|true|none|The RFC3339 timestamp when the device was created.|
|deleted_at|string \| null|false|none|The RFC3339 timestamp when the device was deleted.|
|device_type|string \| null|false|none|The device operating system.|
|hardware_id|string \| null|false|none|A string that uniquely identifies the hardware or virtual machine (VM).|
|id|string|true|none|The unique ID of the device.|
|last_seen_at|string \| null|true|none|The RFC3339 timestamp when the device was last seen.|
|last_seen_registration|object \| null|false|none|The last seen registration for the device.|
|last_seen_user|object \| null|false|none|The last user to use the WARP device.|
|mac_address|string \| null|false|none|The device MAC address.|
|manufacturer|string \| null|false|none|The device manufacturer.|
|model|string \| null|false|none|The model name of the device.|
|multiuser|boolean|false|none|True if this device is in [multi-user mode](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/connections/connect-devices/warp/deployment/mdm-deployment/windows-multiuser/).|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the device.|
|os_version|string \| null|false|none|The device operating system version number.|
|os_version_extra|string \| null|false|none|Additional operating system version details. For Windows, the UBR (Update Build Revision). For Mac or iOS, the Product Version Extra. For Linux, the distribution name and version.|
|public_ip|string \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** **Deprecated**: IP information is provided by DEX - see https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/zero_trust/subresources/dex/subresources/fleet_status/subresources/devices/methods/list/<br>|
|serial_number|string \| null|false|none|The device serial number.|
|tags|object|true|none|Tags assigned to the device. An empty object if the device has no tags.|
|updated_at|string|true|none|The RFC3339 timestamp when the device was last updated.|

<h2 id="tocS_teams-devices_registration">teams-devices_registration</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemateams-devices_registration"></a>
<a id="schema_teams-devices_registration"></a>
<a id="tocSteams-devices_registration"></a>
<a id="tocsteams-devices_registration"></a>

```json
{
  "created_at": "2025-02-14T13:17:00Z",
  "deleted_at": "2025-02-14T13:17:00Z",
  "device": {
    "client_version": "1.0.0",
    "id": "32aa0404-78f1-49a4-99e0-97f575081356",
    "name": "My Device"
  },
  "id": "11ffb86f-3f0c-4306-b4a2-e62f872b166a",
  "key": "U+QTP50RsWfeLGHF4tlGDnmGeuwtsz46KCHr5OyhWq00Rsdfl45mgnQAuEJ6CO0YrkyTl9FUf5iB0bwYR3g4EEFEHhtu6jFaqfMrBMBSz6itv9HQXkaR9OieKQ==",
  "key_type": "secp256r1",
  "last_seen_at": "2025-02-14T13:17:00Z",
  "policy": {
    "default": true,
    "deleted": true,
    "id": "11ffb86f-3f0c-4306-b4a2-e62f872b166a",
    "name": "string",
    "updated_at": "2025-02-14T13:17:00Z"
  },
  "registration_type": "warp",
  "revoked_at": "2025-02-14T13:17:00Z",
  "tunnel_type": "masque",
  "updated_at": "2025-02-14T13:17:00Z",
  "user": {
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "id": "f174e90a-fafe-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415",
    "name": "John Appleseed"
  },
  "virtual_ipv4": "100.96.0.1",
  "virtual_ipv6": "2606:4700:0cf1:1000::1"
}
```

A WARP configuration tied to a single user. Multiple registrations can be created from a single WARP device.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created_at|string|true|none|The RFC3339 timestamp when the registration was created.|
|deleted_at|string \| null|false|none|The RFC3339 timestamp when the registration was deleted.|
|device|[teams-devices_registration_device_details](#schemateams-devices_registration_device_details)|true|none|Device details embedded inside of a registration.|
|id|string|true|none|The ID of the registration.|
|key|string|true|none|The public key used to connect to the Cloudflare network.|
|key_type|string \| null|false|none|The type of encryption key used by the WARP client for the active key. Currently 'curve25519' for WireGuard and 'secp256r1' for MASQUE.|
|last_seen_at|string|true|none|The RFC3339 timestamp when the registration was last seen.|
|policy|[teams-devices_policy_summary](#schemateams-devices_policy_summary)|false|none|The device settings profile assigned to this registration.|
|registration_type|[teams-devices_registration_type](#schemateams-devices_registration_type)|true|none|The registration client type, derived from device_type.|
|revoked_at|string \| null|false|none|The RFC3339 timestamp when the registration was revoked.|
|tunnel_type|string \| null|false|none|Type of the tunnel - wireguard or masque.|
|updated_at|string|true|none|The RFC3339 timestamp when the registration was last updated.|
|user|[teams-devices_user](#schemateams-devices_user)|false|none|none|
|virtual_ipv4|string \| null|false|none|The virtual IPv4 address assigned to the network interface of the tunnel for this registration.|
|virtual_ipv6|string \| null|false|none|The virtual IPv6 address assigned to the network interface of the tunnel for this registration.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|registration_type|warp|
|registration_type|browser_extension|

<a id="tocsteams-devices_zero-trust-account-device-settings"></a>

```json
{
  "disable_for_time": 0,
  "external_emergency_signal_enabled": true,
  "external_emergency_signal_fingerprint": "abcd1234567890abcd1234567890abcd1234567890abcd1234567890abcd1234",
  "external_emergency_signal_interval": "5m",
  "external_emergency_signal_url": "https://192.0.2.1/signal",
  "gateway_proxy_enabled": true,
  "gateway_udp_proxy_enabled": true,
  "root_certificate_installation_enabled": true,
  "use_zt_virtual_ip": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|disable_for_time|number|false|none|Sets the time limit, in seconds, that a user can use an override code to bypass WARP.|
|external_emergency_signal_enabled|boolean|false|none|Controls whether the external emergency disconnect feature is enabled.|
|external_emergency_signal_fingerprint|string|false|none|The SHA256 fingerprint (64 hexadecimal characters) of the HTTPS server certificate for the external_emergency_signal_url. If provided, the WARP client will use this value to verify the server's identity. The device will ignore any response if the server's certificate fingerprint does not exactly match this value.|
|external_emergency_signal_interval|string|false|none|The interval at which the WARP client fetches the emergency disconnect signal, formatted as a duration string (e.g., "5m", "2m30s", "1h"). Minimum 30 seconds.|
|external_emergency_signal_url|string|false|none|The HTTPS URL from which to fetch the emergency disconnect signal. Must use HTTPS and have an IPv4 or IPv6 address as the host.|
|gateway_proxy_enabled|boolean|false|none|Enable gateway proxy filtering on TCP.|
|gateway_udp_proxy_enabled|boolean|false|none|Enable gateway proxy filtering on UDP.|
|root_certificate_installation_enabled|boolean|false|none|Enable installation of cloudflare managed root certificate.|
|use_zt_virtual_ip|boolean|false|none|Enable using CGNAT virtual IPv4.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|name|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_name](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_name)|true|read-only|The keyless SSL name.|
|permissions|[string]|true|read-only|Available permissions for the Keyless SSL for the current user requesting the item.|
|port|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_port](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_port)|true|none|The keyless SSL port used to communicate between Cloudflare and the client's Keyless SSL server.|
|status|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_status-2](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_status-2)|true|read-only|Status of the Keyless SSL.|

<h2 id="tocS_tls-certificates-and-hostnames_bundle_method">tls-certificates-and-hostnames_bundle_method</h2>

<a id="schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_bundle_method"></a>

<a id="tocStls-certificates-and-hostnames_bundle_method"></a>
<a id="tocstls-certificates-and-hostnames_bundle_method"></a>

```json
"ubiquitous"
```

A ubiquitous bundle has the highest probability of being verified everywhere, even by clients using outdated or unusual trust stores. An optimal bundle uses the shortest chain and newest intermediates. And the force bundle verifies the chain, but does not otherwise modify it.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bundle_method|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_bundle_method](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_bundle_method)|false|none|A ubiquitous bundle has the highest probability of being verified everywhere, even by clients using outdated or unusual trust stores. An optimal bundle uses the shortest chain and newest intermediates. And the force bundle verifies the chain, but does not otherwise modify it.|
|custom_csr_id|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_csr_id](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_csr_id)|false|none|The identifier for the Custom CSR that was used.|
|expires_on|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_expires_on](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_expires_on)|false|read-only|When the certificate from the authority expires.|
|geo_restrictions|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_geo_restrictions](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_geo_restrictions)|false|none|Specify the region where your private key can be held locally for optimal TLS performance. HTTPS connections to any excluded data center will still be fully encrypted, but will incur some latency while Keyless SSL is used to complete the handshake with the nearest allowed data center. Options allow distribution to only to U.S. data centers, only to E.U. data centers, or only to highest security data centers. Default distribution is to all Cloudflare datacenters, for optimal performance.|
|hosts|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_hosts](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_hosts)|false|none|none|
|id|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_certificate_identifier](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_certificate_identifier)|true|read-only|Custom certificate identifier tag.|
|issuer|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_issuer](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_issuer)|false|read-only|The certificate authority that issued the certificate.|
|keyless_server|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_keyless-certificate](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_keyless-certificate)|false|none|none|
|modified_on|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_modified_on](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_modified_on)|false|read-only|When the certificate was last modified.|
|policy_restrictions|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_policy_restrictions](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_policy_restrictions)|false|read-only|The policy restrictions returned by the API. This field is returned in responses<br>when a policy has been set. The API accepts the "policy" field in requests but<br>returns this field as "policy_restrictions" in responses.<br><br>Specifies the region(s) where your private key can be held locally for optimal<br>TLS performance. Format is a boolean expression, for example:<br>"(country: US) or (region: EU)"<br>|
|priority|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_priority](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_priority)|false|none|The order/priority in which the certificate will be used in a request. The higher priority will break ties across overlapping 'legacy_custom' certificates, but 'legacy_custom' certificates will always supercede 'sni_custom' certificates.|
|signature|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_signature](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_signature)|false|read-only|The type of hash used for the certificate.|
|status|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_status](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_status)|false|read-only|Status of the zone's custom SSL.|
|uploaded_on|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_uploaded_on](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_uploaded_on)|false|read-only|When the certificate was uploaded to Cloudflare.|
|zone_id|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_identifier)|true|none|Identifier.|

|bundle_method|optimal|
|bundle_method|force|

|status|expired|

<h2 id="tocS_tls-certificates-and-hostnames_enabled-2">tls-certificates-and-hostnames_enabled-2</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_enabled-2"></a>
<a id="schema_tls-certificates-and-hostnames_enabled-2"></a>
<a id="tocStls-certificates-and-hostnames_enabled-2"></a>
<a id="tocstls-certificates-and-hostnames_enabled-2"></a>

```json
true
```

Disabling Universal SSL removes any currently active Universal SSL certificates for your zone from the edge and prevents any future Universal SSL certificates from being ordered. If there are no advanced certificates or custom certificates uploaded for the domain, visitors will be unable to access the domain over HTTPS.

By disabling Universal SSL, you understand that the following Cloudflare settings and preferences will result in visitors being unable to visit your domain unless you have uploaded a custom certificate or purchased an advanced certificate.

* HSTS
* Always Use HTTPS
* Opportunistic Encryption
* Onion Routing
* Any Page Rules redirecting traffic to HTTPS

Similarly, any HTTP redirect to HTTPS at the origin while the Cloudflare proxy is enabled will result in users being unable to visit your site without a valid certificate at Cloudflare's edge.

If you do not have a valid custom or advanced certificate at Cloudflare's edge and are unsure if any of the above Cloudflare settings are enabled, or if any HTTP redirects exist at your origin, we advise leaving Universal SSL enabled for your domain.

<h2 id="tocS_tls-certificates-and-hostnames_geo_restrictions">tls-certificates-and-hostnames_geo_restrictions</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_geo_restrictions"></a>
<a id="schema_tls-certificates-and-hostnames_geo_restrictions"></a>
<a id="tocStls-certificates-and-hostnames_geo_restrictions"></a>
<a id="tocstls-certificates-and-hostnames_geo_restrictions"></a>

```json
{
  "label": "us"
}
```

Specify the region where your private key can be held locally for optimal TLS performance. HTTPS connections to any excluded data center will still be fully encrypted, but will incur some latency while Keyless SSL is used to complete the handshake with the nearest allowed data center. Options allow distribution to only to U.S. data centers, only to E.U. data centers, or only to highest security data centers. Default distribution is to all Cloudflare datacenters, for optimal performance.

|---|---|---|---|---|
|label|string|false|none|none|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|label|eu|
|label|highest_security|

<h2 id="tocS_tls-certificates-and-hostnames_hostnames">tls-certificates-and-hostnames_hostnames</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_hostnames"></a>
<a id="schema_tls-certificates-and-hostnames_hostnames"></a>
<a id="tocStls-certificates-and-hostnames_hostnames"></a>
<a id="tocstls-certificates-and-hostnames_hostnames"></a>

```json
[
  "example.com",
  "*.example.com",
  "sub.example.com"
]
```

Array of hostnames or wildcard names bound to the certificate.
Hostnames must be fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) belonging to zones on your account (e.g., `example.com` or `sub.example.com`). Wildcards are supported only as a `*.` prefix for a single level (e.g., `*.example.com`). Double wildcards (`*.*.example.com`) and interior wildcards (`foo.*.example.com`) are not allowed. The wildcard suffix must be a multi-label domain (`*.example.com` is valid, but `*.com` is not). Unicode/IDN hostnames are accepted and automatically converted to punycode.

<h2 id="tocS_tls-certificates-and-hostnames_policy">tls-certificates-and-hostnames_policy</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_policy"></a>
<a id="schema_tls-certificates-and-hostnames_policy"></a>
<a id="tocStls-certificates-and-hostnames_policy"></a>
<a id="tocstls-certificates-and-hostnames_policy"></a>

```json
"(country: US) or (region: EU)"
```

Specify the policy that determines the region where your private key will be held locally. HTTPS connections to any excluded data center will still be fully encrypted, but will incur some latency while Keyless SSL is used to complete the handshake with the nearest allowed data center. Any combination of countries, specified by their two letter country code (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2#Officially_assigned_code_elements) can be chosen, such as 'country: IN', as well as 'region: EU' which refers to the EU region. If there are too few data centers satisfying the policy, it will be rejected.
Note: The API accepts this field as either "policy" or "policy_restrictions" in requests. Responses return this field as "policy_restrictions".

<h2 id="tocS_tls-certificates-and-hostnames_policy_restrictions">tls-certificates-and-hostnames_policy_restrictions</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_policy_restrictions"></a>
<a id="schema_tls-certificates-and-hostnames_policy_restrictions"></a>
<a id="tocStls-certificates-and-hostnames_policy_restrictions"></a>
<a id="tocstls-certificates-and-hostnames_policy_restrictions"></a>

```json
"(country: US) or (region: EU)"
```

The policy restrictions returned by the API. This field is returned in responses
when a policy has been set. The API accepts the "policy" field in requests but
returns this field as "policy_restrictions" in responses.

Specifies the region(s) where your private key can be held locally for optimal
TLS performance. Format is a boolean expression, for example:
"(country: US) or (region: EU)"

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

<h2 id="tocS_tls-certificates-and-hostnames_setting_id">tls-certificates-and-hostnames_setting_id</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_setting_id"></a>

<a id="tocStls-certificates-and-hostnames_setting_id"></a>
<a id="tocstls-certificates-and-hostnames_setting_id"></a>

```json
"ciphers"
```

The TLS Setting name.
The value type depends on the setting:
- `ciphers`: value is an array of cipher suite strings (e.g., `["ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256", "AES128-GCM-SHA256"]`).
- `min_tls_version`: value is a TLS version string (`"1.0"`, `"1.1"`, `"1.2"`, or `"1.3"`).
- `http2`: value is `"on"` or `"off"`.

SSL properties used when creating the custom hostname.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|bundle_method|string|false|none|A ubiquitous bundle has the highest probability of being verified everywhere, even by clients using outdated or unusual trust stores. An optimal bundle uses the shortest chain and newest intermediates. And the force bundle verifies the chain, but does not otherwise modify it.|
|certificate_authority|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_certificate_authority](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_certificate_authority)|false|none|The Certificate Authority that will issue the certificate.|
|cloudflare_branding|boolean|false|none|Whether or not to add Cloudflare Branding for the order.  This will add a subdomain of sni.cloudflaressl.com as the Common Name if set to true.|
|custom_cert_bundle|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_cert_bundle](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_custom_cert_bundle)|false|none|Array of custom certificate and key pairs (1 or 2 pairs allowed).|
|custom_certificate|string|false|none|If a custom uploaded certificate is used.|
|custom_csr_id|string|false|none|The identifier for the Custom CSR that was used.|
|custom_key|string|false|none|The key for a custom uploaded certificate.|
|method|string|false|none|Domain control validation (DCV) method used for this hostname.|
|settings|[tls-certificates-and-hostnames_sslsettings](#schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_sslsettings)|false|none|SSL specific settings.|
|type|string|false|none|Level of validation to be used for this hostname. Domain validation (dv) must be used.|
|wildcard|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether the certificate covers a wildcard.|

<h2 id="tocS_tls-certificates-and-hostnames_value">tls-certificates-and-hostnames_value</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematls-certificates-and-hostnames_value"></a>
<a id="schema_tls-certificates-and-hostnames_value"></a>
<a id="tocStls-certificates-and-hostnames_value"></a>
<a id="tocstls-certificates-and-hostnames_value"></a>

```json
[
  "ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256",
  "AES128-GCM-SHA256"
]
```

The TLS setting value.
The type depends on the `setting_id` used in the request path:
- `ciphers`: an array of allowed cipher suite strings in BoringSSL format (e.g., `["ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256", "AES128-GCM-SHA256"]`).
- `min_tls_version`: a string indicating the minimum TLS version — one of `"1.0"`, `"1.1"`, `"1.2"`, or `"1.3"` (e.g., `"1.2"`).
- `http2`: a string indicating whether HTTP/2 is enabled — `"on"` or `"off"` (e.g., `"on"`).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[string]|false|none|Used when `setting_id` is `ciphers`. An array of allowed cipher suite strings.|
|*oneOf*|string|false|none|Used when `setting_id` is `min_tls_version`. The minimum TLS version.|
|*oneOf*|string|false|none|Used when `setting_id` is `http2`. Whether HTTP/2 is enabled.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|*oneOf*|1.0|
|*oneOf*|1.1|
|*oneOf*|1.2|
|*oneOf*|1.3|
|*oneOf*|on|
|*oneOf*|off|

<h2 id="tocS_tunnel_originRequest">tunnel_originRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematunnel_originrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_tunnel_originRequest"></a>
<a id="tocStunnel_originrequest"></a>
<a id="tocstunnel_originrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "access": {
    "audTag": [
      "string"
    ],
    "required": false,
    "teamName": "zero-trust-organization-name"
  },
  "caPool": "string",
  "connectTimeout": 10,
  "disableChunkedEncoding": true,
  "http2Origin": true,
  "httpHostHeader": "string",
  "keepAliveConnections": 100,
  "keepAliveTimeout": 90,
  "matchSNItoHost": false,
  "noHappyEyeballs": false,
  "noTLSVerify": false,
  "originServerName": "string",
  "proxyType": "string",
  "tcpKeepAlive": 30,
  "tlsTimeout": 10
}
```

Configuration parameters for the public hostname specific connection settings between cloudflared and origin server.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|access|object|false|none|For all L7 requests to this hostname, cloudflared will validate each request's Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion request header.|
|caPool|string|false|none|Path to the certificate authority (CA) for the certificate of your origin. This option should be used only if your certificate is not signed by Cloudflare.|
|connectTimeout|integer|false|none|Timeout for establishing a new TCP connection to your origin server. This excludes the time taken to establish TLS, which is controlled by tlsTimeout.|
|disableChunkedEncoding|boolean|false|none|Disables chunked transfer encoding. Useful if you are running a WSGI server.|
|http2Origin|boolean|false|none|Attempt to connect to origin using HTTP2. Origin must be configured as https.|
|httpHostHeader|string|false|none|Sets the HTTP Host header on requests sent to the local service.|
|keepAliveConnections|integer|false|none|Maximum number of idle keepalive connections between Tunnel and your origin. This does not restrict the total number of concurrent connections.|
|keepAliveTimeout|integer|false|none|Timeout after which an idle keepalive connection can be discarded.|
|matchSNItoHost|boolean|false|none|Auto configure the Hostname on the origin server certificate.|
|noHappyEyeballs|boolean|false|none|Disable the “happy eyeballs” algorithm for IPv4/IPv6 fallback if your local network has misconfigured one of the protocols.|
|noTLSVerify|boolean|false|none|Disables TLS verification of the certificate presented by your origin. Will allow any certificate from the origin to be accepted.|
|originServerName|string|false|none|Hostname that cloudflared should expect from your origin server certificate.|
|proxyType|string|false|none|cloudflared starts a proxy server to translate HTTP traffic into TCP when proxying, for example, SSH or RDP. This configures what type of proxy will be started. Valid options are: "" for the regular proxy and "socks" for a SOCKS5 proxy.<br>|
|tcpKeepAlive|integer|false|none|The timeout after which a TCP keepalive packet is sent on a connection between Tunnel and the origin server.|
|tlsTimeout|integer|false|none|Timeout for completing a TLS handshake to your origin server, if you have chosen to connect Tunnel to an HTTPS server.|

<h2 id="tocS_tunnel_status">tunnel_status</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematunnel_status"></a>
<a id="schema_tunnel_status"></a>
<a id="tocStunnel_status"></a>
<a id="tocstunnel_status"></a>

```json
"healthy"
```

The status of the tunnel. Valid values are `inactive` (tunnel has never been run), `degraded` (tunnel is active and able to serve traffic but in an unhealthy state), `healthy` (tunnel is active and able to serve traffic), or `down` (tunnel can not serve traffic as it has no connections to the Cloudflare Edge).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_tag|[tunnel_account_id](#schematunnel_account_id)|false|read-only|Cloudflare account ID|

|conns_active_at|[tunnel_conns_active_at](#schematunnel_conns_active_at)|false|none|Timestamp of when the tunnel established at least one connection to Cloudflare's edge. If `null`, the tunnel is inactive.|
|conns_inactive_at|[tunnel_conns_inactive_at](#schematunnel_conns_inactive_at)|false|none|Timestamp of when the tunnel became inactive (no connections to Cloudflare's edge). If `null`, the tunnel is active.|
|created_at|[tunnel_created_at](#schematunnel_created_at)|false|read-only|Timestamp of when the resource was created.|
|deleted_at|[tunnel_deleted_at](#schematunnel_deleted_at)|false|read-only|Timestamp of when the resource was deleted. If `null`, the resource has not been deleted.|
|id|[tunnel_tunnel_id](#schematunnel_tunnel_id)|false|read-only|UUID of the tunnel.|
|metadata|[tunnel_metadata](#schematunnel_metadata)|false|none|Metadata associated with the tunnel.|
|name|[tunnel_tunnel_name](#schematunnel_tunnel_name)|false|none|A user-friendly name for a tunnel.|
|status|[tunnel_status](#schematunnel_status)|false|none|The status of the tunnel. Valid values are `inactive` (tunnel has never been run), `degraded` (tunnel is active and able to serve traffic but in an unhealthy state), `healthy` (tunnel is active and able to serve traffic), or `down` (tunnel can not serve traffic as it has no connections to the Cloudflare Edge).|
|tun_type|[tunnel_tunnel_type](#schematunnel_tunnel_type)|false|none|The type of tunnel.|

<h2 id="tocS_vuln_scanner_bola-credential-role">vuln_scanner_bola-credential-role</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemavuln_scanner_bola-credential-role"></a>
<a id="schema_vuln_scanner_bola-credential-role"></a>
<a id="tocSvuln_scanner_bola-credential-role"></a>
<a id="tocsvuln_scanner_bola-credential-role"></a>

```json
"owner"
```

Identifies the role a request was made with. The credential set governs this role. `owner` is the resource owner, `attacker` attempts to access resources.

<h2 id="tocS_vuln_scanner_bola-credential-sets">vuln_scanner_bola-credential-sets</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemavuln_scanner_bola-credential-sets"></a>
<a id="schema_vuln_scanner_bola-credential-sets"></a>
<a id="tocSvuln_scanner_bola-credential-sets"></a>
<a id="tocsvuln_scanner_bola-credential-sets"></a>

```json
{
  "attacker": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "owner": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
}
```

Credential set references for a BOLA scan. The scanner uses the
`owner` credentials for legitimate requests and the `attacker`
credentials to attempt unauthorized access.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|attacker|string(uuid)|true|none|Credential set ID for the attacker.|
|owner|string(uuid)|true|none|Credential set ID for the resource owner.|

<h2 id="tocS_vuln_scanner_bola-outcome">vuln_scanner_bola-outcome</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemavuln_scanner_bola-outcome"></a>
<a id="schema_vuln_scanner_bola-outcome"></a>
<a id="tocSvuln_scanner_bola-outcome"></a>
<a id="tocsvuln_scanner_bola-outcome"></a>

```json
"ok"
```

Outcome of an assertion. `ok` means the assertion passed, `fail` means the assertion failed, `inconclusive` means the scanner could not evaluate the assertion.

```json
          }

                "description": "string",

                    "min": 0
                  },
                  "type": "http_status_within_range"
                },
                "observed": 0,
                "outcome": {}
              }
            ],
            "errors": [
              {
                "description": "string",
                "error_code": 0
              }
            ],
            "request": {
              "body": {},
              "credential_set": {
                "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
                "role": {}
              },
              "header_names": [
                "string"
              ],
              "method": {},
              "url": "http://example.com",
              "variable_captures": [
                {
                  "json_path": "string",
                  "name": "string"
                }
              ]
            },
            "response": {
              "body": {
                "kind": "not_found"
              },
              "header_names": [
                "string"
              ],
              "status": 0,
              "status_text": "string"

          }
        ],

      }
    ]

}
```

```json
{
  "description": "SQL injection prevention for SELECT statements",
  "group": {
    "id": "de677e5818985db1285d0e80225f06e5",
    "name": "Project Honey Pot"

  ],
```

When triggered, anomaly detection WAF rules contribute to an overall threat score that will determine if a request is considered malicious. You can configure the total scoring threshold through the 'sensitivity' property of the WAF package.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|[waf-managed-rules_schemas-description](#schemawaf-managed-rules_schemas-description)|true|read-only|Defines the public description of the WAF rule.|

|id|[waf-managed-rules_rule_components-schemas-identifier](#schemawaf-managed-rules_rule_components-schemas-identifier)|true|read-only|Defines the unique identifier of the WAF rule.|
|package_id|[waf-managed-rules_identifier](#schemawaf-managed-rules_identifier)|true|read-only|Defines the unique identifier of a WAF package.|
|priority|[waf-managed-rules_priority](#schemawaf-managed-rules_priority)|true|read-only|Defines the order in which the individual WAF rule is executed within its rule group.|
|allowed_modes|[waf-managed-rules_allowed_modes_anomaly](#schemawaf-managed-rules_allowed_modes_anomaly)|true|read-only|Defines the available modes for the current WAF rule. Applies to anomaly detection WAF rules.|
|mode|[waf-managed-rules_mode_anomaly](#schemawaf-managed-rules_mode_anomaly)|true|none|Defines the mode anomaly. When set to `on`, the current WAF rule will be used when evaluating the request. Applies to anomaly detection WAF rules.|

|Property|Value|

|allowed_modes|off|

|mode|off|

<h2 id="tocS_waf-managed-rules_traditional_allow_rule">waf-managed-rules_traditional_allow_rule</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawaf-managed-rules_traditional_allow_rule"></a>
<a id="schema_waf-managed-rules_traditional_allow_rule"></a>
<a id="tocSwaf-managed-rules_traditional_allow_rule"></a>
<a id="tocswaf-managed-rules_traditional_allow_rule"></a>

```json
{
  "description": "SQL injection prevention for SELECT statements",
  "group": {
    "id": "de677e5818985db1285d0e80225f06e5",
    "name": "Project Honey Pot"
  },
  "id": "f939de3be84e66e757adcdcb87908023",
  "package_id": "a25a9a7e9c00afc1fb2e0245519d725b",
  "priority": "string",
  "allowed_modes": [
    "on",
    "off"
  ],
  "mode": "on"
}
```

When triggered, traditional WAF rules cause the firewall to immediately act on the request based on the rule configuration. An 'allow' rule will immediately allow the request and no other rules will be processed.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|[waf-managed-rules_schemas-description](#schemawaf-managed-rules_schemas-description)|true|read-only|Defines the public description of the WAF rule.|
|group|object|true|read-only|Defines the rule group to which the current WAF rule belongs.|
|id|[waf-managed-rules_rule_components-schemas-identifier](#schemawaf-managed-rules_rule_components-schemas-identifier)|true|read-only|Defines the unique identifier of the WAF rule.|
|package_id|[waf-managed-rules_identifier](#schemawaf-managed-rules_identifier)|true|read-only|Defines the unique identifier of a WAF package.|
|priority|[waf-managed-rules_priority](#schemawaf-managed-rules_priority)|true|read-only|Defines the order in which the individual WAF rule is executed within its rule group.|
|allowed_modes|[waf-managed-rules_allowed_modes_allow_traditional](#schemawaf-managed-rules_allowed_modes_allow_traditional)|true|read-only|Defines the available modes for the current WAF rule.|
|mode|[waf-managed-rules_mode_allow_traditional](#schemawaf-managed-rules_mode_allow_traditional)|true|none|When set to `on`, the current rule will be used when evaluating the request. Applies to traditional (allow) WAF rules.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|allowed_modes|on|
|allowed_modes|off|
|mode|on|
|mode|off|

<h2 id="tocS_waf-managed-rules_traditional_deny_rule">waf-managed-rules_traditional_deny_rule</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawaf-managed-rules_traditional_deny_rule"></a>
<a id="schema_waf-managed-rules_traditional_deny_rule"></a>
<a id="tocSwaf-managed-rules_traditional_deny_rule"></a>
<a id="tocswaf-managed-rules_traditional_deny_rule"></a>

```json
{
  "description": "SQL injection prevention for SELECT statements",
  "group": {
    "id": "de677e5818985db1285d0e80225f06e5",
    "name": "Project Honey Pot"
  },
  "id": "f939de3be84e66e757adcdcb87908023",
  "package_id": "a25a9a7e9c00afc1fb2e0245519d725b",
  "priority": "string",
  "allowed_modes": [
    "default",
    "disable",
    "simulate",
    "block",
    "challenge"
  ],
  "default_mode": "block",
  "mode": "block"
}
```

When triggered, traditional WAF rules cause the firewall to immediately act upon the request based on the configuration of the rule. A 'deny' rule will immediately respond to the request based on the configured rule action/mode (for example, 'block') and no other rules will be processed.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|[waf-managed-rules_schemas-description](#schemawaf-managed-rules_schemas-description)|true|read-only|Defines the public description of the WAF rule.|
|group|object|true|read-only|Defines the rule group to which the current WAF rule belongs.|
|id|[waf-managed-rules_rule_components-schemas-identifier](#schemawaf-managed-rules_rule_components-schemas-identifier)|true|read-only|Defines the unique identifier of the WAF rule.|
|package_id|[waf-managed-rules_identifier](#schemawaf-managed-rules_identifier)|true|read-only|Defines the unique identifier of a WAF package.|
|priority|[waf-managed-rules_priority](#schemawaf-managed-rules_priority)|true|read-only|Defines the order in which the individual WAF rule is executed within its rule group.|
|allowed_modes|[waf-managed-rules_allowed_modes_deny_traditional](#schemawaf-managed-rules_allowed_modes_deny_traditional)|true|read-only|Defines the list of possible actions of the WAF rule when it is triggered.|
|default_mode|[waf-managed-rules_default_mode](#schemawaf-managed-rules_default_mode)|true|read-only|Defines the default action/mode of a rule.|
|mode|[waf-managed-rules_mode_deny_traditional](#schemawaf-managed-rules_mode_deny_traditional)|true|none|Defines the action that the current WAF rule will perform when triggered. Applies to traditional (deny) WAF rules.|

|allowed_modes|disable|
|allowed_modes|simulate|
|allowed_modes|block|
|allowed_modes|challenge|
|default_mode|disable|
|default_mode|simulate|
|default_mode|block|
|default_mode|challenge|
|mode|default|
|mode|disable|
|mode|simulate|
|mode|block|
|mode|challenge|

<h2 id="tocS_waitingroom_cookie_attributes">waitingroom_cookie_attributes</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawaitingroom_cookie_attributes"></a>
<a id="schema_waitingroom_cookie_attributes"></a>
<a id="tocSwaitingroom_cookie_attributes"></a>
<a id="tocswaitingroom_cookie_attributes"></a>

```json
{
  "samesite": "auto",
  "secure": "auto"
}
```

Configures cookie attributes for the waiting room cookie. This encrypted cookie stores a user's status in the waiting room, such as queue position.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|samesite|string|false|none|Configures the SameSite attribute on the waiting room cookie. Value `auto` will be translated to `lax` or `none` depending if **Always Use HTTPS** is enabled. Note that when using value `none`, the secure attribute cannot be set to `never`.|
|secure|string|false|none|Configures the Secure attribute on the waiting room cookie. Value `always` indicates that the Secure attribute will be set in the Set-Cookie header, `never` indicates that the Secure attribute will not be set, and `auto` will set the Secure attribute depending if **Always Use HTTPS** is enabled.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|samesite|auto|
|samesite|lax|
|samesite|none|
|samesite|strict|
|secure|auto|
|secure|always|
|secure|never|

<h2 id="tocS_waitingroom_cookie_suffix">waitingroom_cookie_suffix</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawaitingroom_cookie_suffix"></a>
<a id="schema_waitingroom_cookie_suffix"></a>
<a id="tocSwaitingroom_cookie_suffix"></a>
<a id="tocswaitingroom_cookie_suffix"></a>

```json
"abcd"
```

Appends a '_' + a custom suffix to the end of Cloudflare Waiting Room's cookie name(__cf_waitingroom). If `cookie_suffix` is "abcd", the cookie name will be `__cf_waitingroom_abcd`. This field is required if using `additional_routes`.

<h2 id="tocS_waitingroom_custom_page_html">waitingroom_custom_page_html</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawaitingroom_custom_page_html"></a>
<a id="schema_waitingroom_custom_page_html"></a>
<a id="tocSwaitingroom_custom_page_html"></a>
<a id="tocswaitingroom_custom_page_html"></a>

```json
"{{#waitTimeKnown}} {{waitTime}} mins {{/waitTimeKnown}} {{^waitTimeKnown}} Queue all enabled {{/waitTimeKnown}}"
```

Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. This is a template html file that will be rendered at the edge. If no custom_page_html is provided, the default waiting room will be used. The template is based on mustache ( https://mustache.github.io/ ). There are several variables that are evaluated by the Cloudflare edge:
1. {{`waitTimeKnown`}} Acts like a boolean value that indicates the behavior to take when wait time is not available, for instance when queue_all is **true**.
2. {{`waitTimeFormatted`}} Estimated wait time for the user. For example, five minutes. Alternatively, you can use:
3. {{`waitTime`}} Number of minutes of estimated wait for a user.
4. {{`waitTimeHours`}} Number of hours of estimated wait for a user (`Math.floor(waitTime/60)`).
5. {{`waitTimeHourMinutes`}} Number of minutes above the `waitTimeHours` value (`waitTime%60`).
6. {{`queueIsFull`}} Changes to **true** when no more people can be added to the queue.

To view the full list of variables, look at the `cfWaitingRoom` object described under the `json_response_enabled` property in other Waiting Room API calls.

```json
false
```

Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. Disables automatic renewal of session cookies. If `true`, an accepted user will have session_duration minutes to browse the site. After that, they will have to go through the waiting room again. If `false`, a user's session cookie will be automatically renewed on every request.

<h2 id="tocS_waitingroom_event_shuffle_at_event_start">waitingroom_event_shuffle_at_event_start</h2>

<a id="tocswaitingroom_event_shuffle_at_event_start"></a>

```json
false
```

If enabled, users in the prequeue will be shuffled randomly at the `event_start_time`. Requires that `prequeue_start_time` is not null. This is useful for situations when many users will join the event prequeue at the same time and you want to shuffle them to ensure fairness. Naturally, it makes the most sense to enable this feature when the `queueing_method` during the event respects ordering such as **fifo**, or else the shuffling may be unnecessary.

<h2 id="tocS_waitingroom_json_response_enabled">waitingroom_json_response_enabled</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawaitingroom_json_response_enabled"></a>
<a id="schema_waitingroom_json_response_enabled"></a>
<a id="tocSwaitingroom_json_response_enabled"></a>
<a id="tocswaitingroom_json_response_enabled"></a>

```json
false
```

Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. If `true`, requests to the waiting room with the header `Accept: application/json` will receive a JSON response object with information on the user's status in the waiting room as opposed to the configured static HTML page. This JSON response object has one property `cfWaitingRoom` which is an object containing the following fields:
1. `inWaitingRoom`: Boolean indicating if the user is in the waiting room (always **true**).
2. `waitTimeKnown`: Boolean indicating if the current estimated wait times are accurate. If **false**, they are not available.
3. `waitTime`: Valid only when `waitTimeKnown` is **true**. Integer indicating the current estimated time in minutes the user will wait in the waiting room. When `queueingMethod` is **random**, this is set to `waitTime50Percentile`.
4. `waitTime25Percentile`: Valid only when `queueingMethod` is **random** and `waitTimeKnown` is **true**. Integer indicating the current estimated maximum wait time for the 25% of users that gain entry the fastest (25th percentile).
5. `waitTime50Percentile`: Valid only when `queueingMethod` is **random** and `waitTimeKnown` is **true**. Integer indicating the current estimated maximum wait time for the 50% of users that gain entry the fastest (50th percentile). In other words, half of the queued users are expected to let into the origin website before `waitTime50Percentile` and half are expected to be let in after it.
6. `waitTime75Percentile`: Valid only when `queueingMethod` is **random** and `waitTimeKnown` is **true**. Integer indicating the current estimated maximum wait time for the 75% of users that gain entry the fastest (75th percentile).
7. `waitTimeFormatted`: String displaying the `waitTime` formatted in English for users. If `waitTimeKnown` is **false**, `waitTimeFormatted` will display **unavailable**.
8. `queueIsFull`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room's queue is currently full and not accepting new users at the moment.
9. `queueAll`: Boolean indicating if all users will be queued in the waiting room and no one will be let into the origin website.
10. `lastUpdated`: String displaying the timestamp as an ISO 8601 string of the user's last attempt to leave the waiting room and be let into the origin website. The user is able to make another attempt after `refreshIntervalSeconds` past this time. If the user makes a request too soon, it will be ignored and `lastUpdated` will not change.
11. `refreshIntervalSeconds`: Integer indicating the number of seconds after `lastUpdated` until the user is able to make another attempt to leave the waiting room and be let into the origin website. When the `queueingMethod` is `reject`, there is no specified refresh time —\_it will always be **zero**.
12. `queueingMethod`: The queueing method currently used by the waiting room. It is either **fifo**, **random**, **passthrough**, or **reject**.
13. `isFIFOQueue`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room uses a FIFO (First-In-First-Out) queue.
14. `isRandomQueue`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room uses a Random queue where users gain access randomly.
15. `isPassthroughQueue`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room uses a passthrough queue. Keep in mind that when passthrough is enabled, this JSON response will only exist when `queueAll` is **true** or `isEventPrequeueing` is **true** because in all other cases requests will go directly to the origin.
16. `isRejectQueue`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room uses a reject queue.
17. `isEventActive`: Boolean indicating if an event is currently occurring. Events are able to change a waiting room's behavior during a specified period of time. For additional information, look at the event properties `prequeue_start_time`, `event_start_time`, and `event_end_time` in the documentation for creating waiting room events. Events are considered active between these start and end times, as well as during the prequeueing period if it exists.
18. `isEventPrequeueing`: Valid only when `isEventActive` is **true**. Boolean indicating if an event is currently prequeueing users before it starts.
19. `timeUntilEventStart`: Valid only when `isEventPrequeueing` is **true**. Integer indicating the number of minutes until the event starts.
20. `timeUntilEventStartFormatted`: String displaying the `timeUntilEventStart` formatted in English for users. If `isEventPrequeueing` is **false**, `timeUntilEventStartFormatted` will display **unavailable**.
21. `timeUntilEventEnd`: Valid only when `isEventActive` is **true**. Integer indicating the number of minutes until the event ends.
22. `timeUntilEventEndFormatted`: String displaying the `timeUntilEventEnd` formatted in English for users. If `isEventActive` is **false**, `timeUntilEventEndFormatted` will display **unavailable**.
23. `shuffleAtEventStart`: Valid only when `isEventActive` is **true**. Boolean indicating if the users in the prequeue are shuffled randomly when the event starts.
24. `turnstile`: Empty when turnstile isn't enabled. String displaying an html tag to display the Turnstile widget. Please add the `{{{turnstile}}}` tag to the `custom_html` template to ensure the Turnstile widget appears.
25. `infiniteQueue`: Boolean indicating whether the response is for a user in the infinite queue.

An example cURL to a waiting room could be:

	curl -X GET "https://example.com/waitingroom" \
		-H "Accept: application/json"

If `json_response_enabled` is **true** and the request hits the waiting room, an example JSON response when `queueingMethod` is **fifo** and no event is active could be:

	{
		"cfWaitingRoom": {
			"inWaitingRoom": true,
			"waitTimeKnown": true,
			"waitTime": 10,
			"waitTime25Percentile": 0,
			"waitTime50Percentile": 0,
			"waitTime75Percentile": 0,
			"waitTimeFormatted": "10 minutes",
			"queueIsFull": false,
			"queueAll": false,
			"lastUpdated": "2020-08-03T23:46:00.000Z",
			"refreshIntervalSeconds": 20,
			"queueingMethod": "fifo",
			"isFIFOQueue": true,
			"isRandomQueue": false,
			"isPassthroughQueue": false,
			"isRejectQueue": false,
			"isEventActive": false,
			"isEventPrequeueing": false,
			"timeUntilEventStart": 0,
			"timeUntilEventStartFormatted": "unavailable",
			"timeUntilEventEnd": 0,
			"timeUntilEventEndFormatted": "unavailable",
			"shuffleAtEventStart": false
		}
	}

If `json_response_enabled` is **true** and the request hits the waiting room, an example JSON response when `queueingMethod` is **random** and an event is active could be:

	{
		"cfWaitingRoom": {
			"inWaitingRoom": true,
			"waitTimeKnown": true,
			"waitTime": 10,
			"waitTime25Percentile": 5,
			"waitTime50Percentile": 10,
			"waitTime75Percentile": 15,
			"waitTimeFormatted": "5 minutes to 15 minutes",
			"queueIsFull": false,
			"queueAll": false,
			"lastUpdated": "2020-08-03T23:46:00.000Z",
			"refreshIntervalSeconds": 20,
			"queueingMethod": "random",
			"isFIFOQueue": false,
			"isRandomQueue": true,
			"isPassthroughQueue": false,
			"isRejectQueue": false,
			"isEventActive": true,
			"isEventPrequeueing": false,
			"timeUntilEventStart": 0,
			"timeUntilEventStartFormatted": "unavailable",
			"timeUntilEventEnd": 15,
			"timeUntilEventEndFormatted": "15 minutes",
			"shuffleAtEventStart": true
		}
	}

|prequeue_start_time|[waitingroom_event_prequeue_start_time](#schemawaitingroom_event_prequeue_start_time)|false|none|An ISO 8601 timestamp that marks when to begin queueing all users before the event starts. The prequeue must start at least five minutes before `event_start_time`.|
|queueing_method|[waitingroom_event_queueing_method](#schemawaitingroom_event_queueing_method)|false|none|If set, the event will override the waiting room's `queueing_method` property while it is active. If null, the event will inherit it.|
|session_duration|[waitingroom_event_session_duration](#schemawaitingroom_event_session_duration)|false|none|If set, the event will override the waiting room's `session_duration` property while it is active. If null, the event will inherit it.|
|shuffle_at_event_start|[waitingroom_event_shuffle_at_event_start](#schemawaitingroom_event_shuffle_at_event_start)|false|none|If enabled, users in the prequeue will be shuffled randomly at the `event_start_time`. Requires that `prequeue_start_time` is not null. This is useful for situations when many users will join the event prequeue at the same time and you want to shuffle them to ensure fairness. Naturally, it makes the most sense to enable this feature when the `queueing_method` during the event respects ordering such as **fifo**, or else the shuffling may be unnecessary.|
|suspended|[waitingroom_event_suspended](#schemawaitingroom_event_suspended)|false|none|Suspends or allows an event. If set to `true`, the event is ignored and traffic will be handled based on the waiting room configuration.|
|total_active_users|[waitingroom_event_total_active_users](#schemawaitingroom_event_total_active_users)|false|none|If set, the event will override the waiting room's `total_active_users` property while it is active. If null, the event will inherit it. This can only be set if the event's `new_users_per_minute` property is also set.|
|turnstile_action|[waitingroom_event_turnstile_action](#schemawaitingroom_event_turnstile_action)|false|none|If set, the event will override the waiting room's `turnstile_action` property while it is active. If null, the event will inherit it.|
|turnstile_mode|[waitingroom_event_turnstile_mode](#schemawaitingroom_event_turnstile_mode)|false|none|If set, the event will override the waiting room's `turnstile_mode` property while it is active. If null, the event will inherit it.|

```json

  "custom_html": "{{#waitTimeKnown}} {{waitTime}} mins {{/waitTimeKnown}} {{^waitTimeKnown}} Queue all enabled {{/waitTimeKnown}}"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|custom_html|[waitingroom_custom_page_html](#schemawaitingroom_custom_page_html)|true|none|Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. This is a template html file that will be rendered at the edge. If no custom_page_html is provided, the default waiting room will be used. The template is based on mustache ( https://mustache.github.io/ ). There are several variables that are evaluated by the Cloudflare edge:<br>1. {{`waitTimeKnown`}} Acts like a boolean value that indicates the behavior to take when wait time is not available, for instance when queue_all is **true**.<br>2. {{`waitTimeFormatted`}} Estimated wait time for the user. For example, five minutes. Alternatively, you can use:<br>3. {{`waitTime`}} Number of minutes of estimated wait for a user.<br>4. {{`waitTimeHours`}} Number of hours of estimated wait for a user (`Math.floor(waitTime/60)`).<br>5. {{`waitTimeHourMinutes`}} Number of minutes above the `waitTimeHours` value (`waitTime%60`).<br>6. {{`queueIsFull`}} Changes to **true** when no more people can be added to the queue.<br><br>To view the full list of variables, look at the `cfWaitingRoom` object described under the `json_response_enabled` property in other Waiting Room API calls.|

```json
  "path": "/shop/checkout",

  "session_duration": 5,
  "suspended": false,
  "total_active_users": 200,
  "turnstile_action": "log",
  "turnstile_mode": "invisible"
```
