### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|additional_routes|[waitingroom_additional_routes](#schemawaitingroom_additional_routes)|false|none|Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. Additional hostname and path combinations to which this waiting room will be applied. There is an implied wildcard at the end of the path. The hostname and path combination must be unique to this and all other waiting rooms.|
|cookie_attributes|[waitingroom_cookie_attributes](#schemawaitingroom_cookie_attributes)|false|none|Configures cookie attributes for the waiting room cookie. This encrypted cookie stores a user's status in the waiting room, such as queue position.|
|cookie_suffix|[waitingroom_cookie_suffix](#schemawaitingroom_cookie_suffix)|false|none|Appends a '_' + a custom suffix to the end of Cloudflare Waiting Room's cookie name(__cf_waitingroom). If `cookie_suffix` is "abcd", the cookie name will be `__cf_waitingroom_abcd`. This field is required if using `additional_routes`.|
|custom_page_html|[waitingroom_custom_page_html](#schemawaitingroom_custom_page_html)|false|none|Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. This is a template html file that will be rendered at the edge. If no custom_page_html is provided, the default waiting room will be used. The template is based on mustache ( https://mustache.github.io/ ). There are several variables that are evaluated by the Cloudflare edge:<br>1. {{`waitTimeKnown`}} Acts like a boolean value that indicates the behavior to take when wait time is not available, for instance when queue_all is **true**.<br>2. {{`waitTimeFormatted`}} Estimated wait time for the user. For example, five minutes. Alternatively, you can use:<br>3. {{`waitTime`}} Number of minutes of estimated wait for a user.<br>4. {{`waitTimeHours`}} Number of hours of estimated wait for a user (`Math.floor(waitTime/60)`).<br>5. {{`waitTimeHourMinutes`}} Number of minutes above the `waitTimeHours` value (`waitTime%60`).<br>6. {{`queueIsFull`}} Changes to **true** when no more people can be added to the queue.<br><br>To view the full list of variables, look at the `cfWaitingRoom` object described under the `json_response_enabled` property in other Waiting Room API calls.|
|default_template_language|[waitingroom_default_template_language](#schemawaitingroom_default_template_language)|false|none|The language of the default page template. If no default_template_language is provided, then `en-US` (English) will be used.|
|description|[waitingroom_description](#schemawaitingroom_description)|false|none|A note that you can use to add more details about the waiting room.|
|disable_session_renewal|[waitingroom_disable_session_renewal](#schemawaitingroom_disable_session_renewal)|false|none|Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. Disables automatic renewal of session cookies. If `true`, an accepted user will have session_duration minutes to browse the site. After that, they will have to go through the waiting room again. If `false`, a user's session cookie will be automatically renewed on every request.|
|enabled_origin_commands|[waitingroom_enabled_origin_commands](#schemawaitingroom_enabled_origin_commands)|false|none|A list of enabled origin commands.|
|host|[waitingroom_host](#schemawaitingroom_host)|true|none|The host name to which the waiting room will be applied (no wildcards). Please do not include the scheme (http:// or https://). The host and path combination must be unique.|
|json_response_enabled|[waitingroom_json_response_enabled](#schemawaitingroom_json_response_enabled)|false|none|Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. If `true`, requests to the waiting room with the header `Accept: application/json` will receive a JSON response object with information on the user's status in the waiting room as opposed to the configured static HTML page. This JSON response object has one property `cfWaitingRoom` which is an object containing the following fields:<br>1. `inWaitingRoom`: Boolean indicating if the user is in the waiting room (always **true**).<br>2. `waitTimeKnown`: Boolean indicating if the current estimated wait times are accurate. If **false**, they are not available.<br>3. `waitTime`: Valid only when `waitTimeKnown` is **true**. Integer indicating the current estimated time in minutes the user will wait in the waiting room. When `queueingMethod` is **random**, this is set to `waitTime50Percentile`.<br>4. `waitTime25Percentile`: Valid only when `queueingMethod` is **random** and `waitTimeKnown` is **true**. Integer indicating the current estimated maximum wait time for the 25% of users that gain entry the fastest (25th percentile).<br>5. `waitTime50Percentile`: Valid only when `queueingMethod` is **random** and `waitTimeKnown` is **true**. Integer indicating the current estimated maximum wait time for the 50% of users that gain entry the fastest (50th percentile). In other words, half of the queued users are expected to let into the origin website before `waitTime50Percentile` and half are expected to be let in after it.<br>6. `waitTime75Percentile`: Valid only when `queueingMethod` is **random** and `waitTimeKnown` is **true**. Integer indicating the current estimated maximum wait time for the 75% of users that gain entry the fastest (75th percentile).<br>7. `waitTimeFormatted`: String displaying the `waitTime` formatted in English for users. If `waitTimeKnown` is **false**, `waitTimeFormatted` will display **unavailable**.<br>8. `queueIsFull`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room's queue is currently full and not accepting new users at the moment.<br>9. `queueAll`: Boolean indicating if all users will be queued in the waiting room and no one will be let into the origin website.<br>10. `lastUpdated`: String displaying the timestamp as an ISO 8601 string of the user's last attempt to leave the waiting room and be let into the origin website. The user is able to make another attempt after `refreshIntervalSeconds` past this time. If the user makes a request too soon, it will be ignored and `lastUpdated` will not change.<br>11. `refreshIntervalSeconds`: Integer indicating the number of seconds after `lastUpdated` until the user is able to make another attempt to leave the waiting room and be let into the origin website. When the `queueingMethod` is `reject`, there is no specified refresh time —\_it will always be **zero**.<br>12. `queueingMethod`: The queueing method currently used by the waiting room. It is either **fifo**, **random**, **passthrough**, or **reject**.<br>13. `isFIFOQueue`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room uses a FIFO (First-In-First-Out) queue.<br>14. `isRandomQueue`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room uses a Random queue where users gain access randomly.<br>15. `isPassthroughQueue`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room uses a passthrough queue. Keep in mind that when passthrough is enabled, this JSON response will only exist when `queueAll` is **true** or `isEventPrequeueing` is **true** because in all other cases requests will go directly to the origin.<br>16. `isRejectQueue`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room uses a reject queue.<br>17. `isEventActive`: Boolean indicating if an event is currently occurring. Events are able to change a waiting room's behavior during a specified period of time. For additional information, look at the event properties `prequeue_start_time`, `event_start_time`, and `event_end_time` in the documentation for creating waiting room events. Events are considered active between these start and end times, as well as during the prequeueing period if it exists.<br>18. `isEventPrequeueing`: Valid only when `isEventActive` is **true**. Boolean indicating if an event is currently prequeueing users before it starts.<br>19. `timeUntilEventStart`: Valid only when `isEventPrequeueing` is **true**. Integer indicating the number of minutes until the event starts.<br>20. `timeUntilEventStartFormatted`: String displaying the `timeUntilEventStart` formatted in English for users. If `isEventPrequeueing` is **false**, `timeUntilEventStartFormatted` will display **unavailable**.<br>21. `timeUntilEventEnd`: Valid only when `isEventActive` is **true**. Integer indicating the number of minutes until the event ends.<br>22. `timeUntilEventEndFormatted`: String displaying the `timeUntilEventEnd` formatted in English for users. If `isEventActive` is **false**, `timeUntilEventEndFormatted` will display **unavailable**.<br>23. `shuffleAtEventStart`: Valid only when `isEventActive` is **true**. Boolean indicating if the users in the prequeue are shuffled randomly when the event starts.<br>24. `turnstile`: Empty when turnstile isn't enabled. String displaying an html tag to display the Turnstile widget. Please add the `{{{turnstile}}}` tag to the `custom_html` template to ensure the Turnstile widget appears.<br>25. `infiniteQueue`: Boolean indicating whether the response is for a user in the infinite queue.<br><br>An example cURL to a waiting room could be:<br><br>	curl -X GET "https://example.com/waitingroom" \<br>		-H "Accept: application/json"<br><br>If `json_response_enabled` is **true** and the request hits the waiting room, an example JSON response when `queueingMethod` is **fifo** and no event is active could be:<br><br>	{<br>		"cfWaitingRoom": {<br>			"inWaitingRoom": true,<br>			"waitTimeKnown": true,<br>			"waitTime": 10,<br>			"waitTime25Percentile": 0,<br>			"waitTime50Percentile": 0,<br>			"waitTime75Percentile": 0,<br>			"waitTimeFormatted": "10 minutes",<br>			"queueIsFull": false,<br>			"queueAll": false,<br>			"lastUpdated": "2020-08-03T23:46:00.000Z",<br>			"refreshIntervalSeconds": 20,<br>			"queueingMethod": "fifo",<br>			"isFIFOQueue": true,<br>			"isRandomQueue": false,<br>			"isPassthroughQueue": false,<br>			"isRejectQueue": false,<br>			"isEventActive": false,<br>			"isEventPrequeueing": false,<br>			"timeUntilEventStart": 0,<br>			"timeUntilEventStartFormatted": "unavailable",<br>			"timeUntilEventEnd": 0,<br>			"timeUntilEventEndFormatted": "unavailable",<br>			"shuffleAtEventStart": false<br>		}<br>	}<br><br>If `json_response_enabled` is **true** and the request hits the waiting room, an example JSON response when `queueingMethod` is **random** and an event is active could be:<br><br>	{<br>		"cfWaitingRoom": {<br>			"inWaitingRoom": true,<br>			"waitTimeKnown": true,<br>			"waitTime": 10,<br>			"waitTime25Percentile": 5,<br>			"waitTime50Percentile": 10,<br>			"waitTime75Percentile": 15,<br>			"waitTimeFormatted": "5 minutes to 15 minutes",<br>			"queueIsFull": false,<br>			"queueAll": false,<br>			"lastUpdated": "2020-08-03T23:46:00.000Z",<br>			"refreshIntervalSeconds": 20,<br>			"queueingMethod": "random",<br>			"isFIFOQueue": false,<br>			"isRandomQueue": true,<br>			"isPassthroughQueue": false,<br>			"isRejectQueue": false,<br>			"isEventActive": true,<br>			"isEventPrequeueing": false,<br>			"timeUntilEventStart": 0,<br>			"timeUntilEventStartFormatted": "unavailable",<br>			"timeUntilEventEnd": 15,<br>			"timeUntilEventEndFormatted": "15 minutes",<br>			"shuffleAtEventStart": true<br>		}<br>	}|
|name|[waitingroom_name](#schemawaitingroom_name)|true|none|A unique name to identify the waiting room. Only alphanumeric characters, hyphens and underscores are allowed.|
|new_users_per_minute|[waitingroom_new_users_per_minute](#schemawaitingroom_new_users_per_minute)|true|none|Sets the number of new users that will be let into the route every minute. This value is used as baseline for the number of users that are let in per minute. So it is possible that there is a little more or little less traffic coming to the route based on the traffic patterns at that time around the world.|
|path|[waitingroom_path](#schemawaitingroom_path)|false|none|Sets the path within the host to enable the waiting room on. The waiting room will be enabled for all subpaths as well. If there are two waiting rooms on the same subpath, the waiting room for the most specific path will be chosen. Wildcards and query parameters are not supported.|
|queue_all|[waitingroom_queue_all](#schemawaitingroom_queue_all)|false|none|If queue_all is `true`, all the traffic that is coming to a route will be sent to the waiting room. No new traffic can get to the route once this field is set and estimated time will become unavailable.|
|queueing_method|[waitingroom_queueing_method](#schemawaitingroom_queueing_method)|false|none|Sets the queueing method used by the waiting room. Changing this parameter from the **default** queueing method is only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. Regardless of the queueing method, if `queue_all` is enabled or an event is prequeueing, users in the waiting room will not be accepted to the origin. These users will always see a waiting room page that refreshes automatically. The valid queueing methods are:<br>1. `fifo` **(default)**: First-In-First-Out queue where customers gain access in the order they arrived.<br>2. `random`: Random queue where customers gain access randomly, regardless of arrival time.<br>3. `passthrough`: Users will pass directly through the waiting room and into the origin website. As a result, any configured limits will not be respected while this is enabled. This method can be used as an alternative to disabling a waiting room (with `suspended`) so that analytics are still reported. This can be used if you wish to allow all traffic normally, but want to restrict traffic during a waiting room event, or vice versa.<br>4. `reject`: Users will be immediately rejected from the waiting room. As a result, no users will reach the origin website while this is enabled. This can be used if you wish to reject all traffic while performing maintenance, block traffic during a specified period of time (an event), or block traffic while events are not occurring. Consider a waiting room used for vaccine distribution that only allows traffic during sign-up events, and otherwise blocks all traffic. For this case, the waiting room uses `reject`, and its events override this with `fifo`, `random`, or `passthrough`. When this queueing method is enabled and neither `queueAll` is enabled nor an event is prequeueing, the waiting room page **will not refresh automatically**.|
|queueing_status_code|[waitingroom_queueing_status_code](#schemawaitingroom_queueing_status_code)|false|none|HTTP status code returned to a user while in the queue.|
|session_duration|[waitingroom_session_duration](#schemawaitingroom_session_duration)|false|none|Lifetime of a cookie (in minutes) set by Cloudflare for users who get access to the route. If a user is not seen by Cloudflare again in that time period, they will be treated as a new user that visits the route.|
|suspended|[waitingroom_suspended](#schemawaitingroom_suspended)|false|none|Suspends or allows traffic going to the waiting room. If set to `true`, the traffic will not go to the waiting room.|
|total_active_users|[waitingroom_total_active_users](#schemawaitingroom_total_active_users)|true|none|Sets the total number of active user sessions on the route at a point in time. A route is a combination of host and path on which a waiting room is available. This value is used as a baseline for the total number of active user sessions on the route. It is possible to have a situation where there are more or less active users sessions on the route based on the traffic patterns at that time around the world.|
|turnstile_action|[waitingroom_turnstile_action](#schemawaitingroom_turnstile_action)|false|none|Which action to take when a bot is detected using Turnstile. `log` will<br>have no impact on queueing behavior, simply keeping track of how many<br>bots are detected in Waiting Room Analytics. `infinite_queue` will send<br>bots to a false queueing state, where they will never reach your<br>origin. `infinite_queue` requires Advanced Waiting Room.<br>|
|turnstile_mode|[waitingroom_turnstile_mode](#schemawaitingroom_turnstile_mode)|false|none|Which Turnstile widget type to use for detecting bot traffic. See<br>[the Turnstile documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/turnstile/concepts/widget/#widget-types)<br>for the definitions of these widget types. Set to `off` to disable the<br>Turnstile integration entirely. Setting this to anything other than<br>`off` or `invisible` requires Advanced Waiting Room.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_waitingroom_queue_all">waitingroom_queue_all</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawaitingroom_queue_all"></a>
<a id="schema_waitingroom_queue_all"></a>
<a id="tocSwaitingroom_queue_all"></a>
<a id="tocswaitingroom_queue_all"></a>

```json
true
```

If queue_all is `true`, all the traffic that is coming to a route will be sent to the waiting room. No new traffic can get to the route once this field is set and estimated time will become unavailable.

<h2 id="tocS_waitingroom_queueing_method">waitingroom_queueing_method</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawaitingroom_queueing_method"></a>
<a id="schema_waitingroom_queueing_method"></a>
<a id="tocSwaitingroom_queueing_method"></a>
<a id="tocswaitingroom_queueing_method"></a>

```json
"fifo"
```

Sets the queueing method used by the waiting room. Changing this parameter from the **default** queueing method is only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. Regardless of the queueing method, if `queue_all` is enabled or an event is prequeueing, users in the waiting room will not be accepted to the origin. These users will always see a waiting room page that refreshes automatically. The valid queueing methods are:
1. `fifo` **(default)**: First-In-First-Out queue where customers gain access in the order they arrived.
2. `random`: Random queue where customers gain access randomly, regardless of arrival time.
3. `passthrough`: Users will pass directly through the waiting room and into the origin website. As a result, any configured limits will not be respected while this is enabled. This method can be used as an alternative to disabling a waiting room (with `suspended`) so that analytics are still reported. This can be used if you wish to allow all traffic normally, but want to restrict traffic during a waiting room event, or vice versa.
4. `reject`: Users will be immediately rejected from the waiting room. As a result, no users will reach the origin website while this is enabled. This can be used if you wish to reject all traffic while performing maintenance, block traffic during a specified period of time (an event), or block traffic while events are not occurring. Consider a waiting room used for vaccine distribution that only allows traffic during sign-up events, and otherwise blocks all traffic. For this case, the waiting room uses `reject`, and its events override this with `fifo`, `random`, or `passthrough`. When this queueing method is enabled and neither `queueAll` is enabled nor an event is prequeueing, the waiting room page **will not refresh automatically**.

<a id="tocswaitingroom_total_active_users"></a>

```json
200
```

Sets the total number of active user sessions on the route at a point in time. A route is a combination of host and path on which a waiting room is available. This value is used as a baseline for the total number of active user sessions on the route. It is possible to have a situation where there are more or less active users sessions on the route based on the traffic patterns at that time around the world.

```json
"log"
```

Which action to take when a bot is detected using Turnstile. `log` will
have no impact on queueing behavior, simply keeping track of how many
bots are detected in Waiting Room Analytics. `infinite_queue` will send
bots to a false queueing state, where they will never reach your
origin. `infinite_queue` requires Advanced Waiting Room.

```json
"invisible"
```

Which Turnstile widget type to use for detecting bot traffic. See
[the Turnstile documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/turnstile/concepts/widget/#widget-types)
for the definitions of these widget types. Set to `off` to disable the
Turnstile integration entirely. Setting this to anything other than
`off` or `invisible` requires Advanced Waiting Room.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|additional_routes|[waitingroom_additional_routes](#schemawaitingroom_additional_routes)|false|none|Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. Additional hostname and path combinations to which this waiting room will be applied. There is an implied wildcard at the end of the path. The hostname and path combination must be unique to this and all other waiting rooms.|
|cookie_attributes|[waitingroom_cookie_attributes](#schemawaitingroom_cookie_attributes)|false|none|Configures cookie attributes for the waiting room cookie. This encrypted cookie stores a user's status in the waiting room, such as queue position.|
|cookie_suffix|[waitingroom_cookie_suffix](#schemawaitingroom_cookie_suffix)|false|none|Appends a '_' + a custom suffix to the end of Cloudflare Waiting Room's cookie name(__cf_waitingroom). If `cookie_suffix` is "abcd", the cookie name will be `__cf_waitingroom_abcd`. This field is required if using `additional_routes`.|
|created_on|[waitingroom_timestamp](#schemawaitingroom_timestamp)|false|read-only|none|
|custom_page_html|[waitingroom_custom_page_html](#schemawaitingroom_custom_page_html)|false|none|Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. This is a template html file that will be rendered at the edge. If no custom_page_html is provided, the default waiting room will be used. The template is based on mustache ( https://mustache.github.io/ ). There are several variables that are evaluated by the Cloudflare edge:<br>1. {{`waitTimeKnown`}} Acts like a boolean value that indicates the behavior to take when wait time is not available, for instance when queue_all is **true**.<br>2. {{`waitTimeFormatted`}} Estimated wait time for the user. For example, five minutes. Alternatively, you can use:<br>3. {{`waitTime`}} Number of minutes of estimated wait for a user.<br>4. {{`waitTimeHours`}} Number of hours of estimated wait for a user (`Math.floor(waitTime/60)`).<br>5. {{`waitTimeHourMinutes`}} Number of minutes above the `waitTimeHours` value (`waitTime%60`).<br>6. {{`queueIsFull`}} Changes to **true** when no more people can be added to the queue.<br><br>To view the full list of variables, look at the `cfWaitingRoom` object described under the `json_response_enabled` property in other Waiting Room API calls.|
|default_template_language|[waitingroom_default_template_language](#schemawaitingroom_default_template_language)|false|none|The language of the default page template. If no default_template_language is provided, then `en-US` (English) will be used.|
|description|[waitingroom_description](#schemawaitingroom_description)|false|none|A note that you can use to add more details about the waiting room.|
|disable_session_renewal|[waitingroom_disable_session_renewal](#schemawaitingroom_disable_session_renewal)|false|none|Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. Disables automatic renewal of session cookies. If `true`, an accepted user will have session_duration minutes to browse the site. After that, they will have to go through the waiting room again. If `false`, a user's session cookie will be automatically renewed on every request.|
|enabled_origin_commands|[waitingroom_enabled_origin_commands](#schemawaitingroom_enabled_origin_commands)|false|none|A list of enabled origin commands.|
|host|[waitingroom_host](#schemawaitingroom_host)|false|none|The host name to which the waiting room will be applied (no wildcards). Please do not include the scheme (http:// or https://). The host and path combination must be unique.|
|id|[waitingroom_waiting_room_id](#schemawaitingroom_waiting_room_id)|false|none|none|
|json_response_enabled|[waitingroom_json_response_enabled](#schemawaitingroom_json_response_enabled)|false|none|Only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. If `true`, requests to the waiting room with the header `Accept: application/json` will receive a JSON response object with information on the user's status in the waiting room as opposed to the configured static HTML page. This JSON response object has one property `cfWaitingRoom` which is an object containing the following fields:<br>1. `inWaitingRoom`: Boolean indicating if the user is in the waiting room (always **true**).<br>2. `waitTimeKnown`: Boolean indicating if the current estimated wait times are accurate. If **false**, they are not available.<br>3. `waitTime`: Valid only when `waitTimeKnown` is **true**. Integer indicating the current estimated time in minutes the user will wait in the waiting room. When `queueingMethod` is **random**, this is set to `waitTime50Percentile`.<br>4. `waitTime25Percentile`: Valid only when `queueingMethod` is **random** and `waitTimeKnown` is **true**. Integer indicating the current estimated maximum wait time for the 25% of users that gain entry the fastest (25th percentile).<br>5. `waitTime50Percentile`: Valid only when `queueingMethod` is **random** and `waitTimeKnown` is **true**. Integer indicating the current estimated maximum wait time for the 50% of users that gain entry the fastest (50th percentile). In other words, half of the queued users are expected to let into the origin website before `waitTime50Percentile` and half are expected to be let in after it.<br>6. `waitTime75Percentile`: Valid only when `queueingMethod` is **random** and `waitTimeKnown` is **true**. Integer indicating the current estimated maximum wait time for the 75% of users that gain entry the fastest (75th percentile).<br>7. `waitTimeFormatted`: String displaying the `waitTime` formatted in English for users. If `waitTimeKnown` is **false**, `waitTimeFormatted` will display **unavailable**.<br>8. `queueIsFull`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room's queue is currently full and not accepting new users at the moment.<br>9. `queueAll`: Boolean indicating if all users will be queued in the waiting room and no one will be let into the origin website.<br>10. `lastUpdated`: String displaying the timestamp as an ISO 8601 string of the user's last attempt to leave the waiting room and be let into the origin website. The user is able to make another attempt after `refreshIntervalSeconds` past this time. If the user makes a request too soon, it will be ignored and `lastUpdated` will not change.<br>11. `refreshIntervalSeconds`: Integer indicating the number of seconds after `lastUpdated` until the user is able to make another attempt to leave the waiting room and be let into the origin website. When the `queueingMethod` is `reject`, there is no specified refresh time —\_it will always be **zero**.<br>12. `queueingMethod`: The queueing method currently used by the waiting room. It is either **fifo**, **random**, **passthrough**, or **reject**.<br>13. `isFIFOQueue`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room uses a FIFO (First-In-First-Out) queue.<br>14. `isRandomQueue`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room uses a Random queue where users gain access randomly.<br>15. `isPassthroughQueue`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room uses a passthrough queue. Keep in mind that when passthrough is enabled, this JSON response will only exist when `queueAll` is **true** or `isEventPrequeueing` is **true** because in all other cases requests will go directly to the origin.<br>16. `isRejectQueue`: Boolean indicating if the waiting room uses a reject queue.<br>17. `isEventActive`: Boolean indicating if an event is currently occurring. Events are able to change a waiting room's behavior during a specified period of time. For additional information, look at the event properties `prequeue_start_time`, `event_start_time`, and `event_end_time` in the documentation for creating waiting room events. Events are considered active between these start and end times, as well as during the prequeueing period if it exists.<br>18. `isEventPrequeueing`: Valid only when `isEventActive` is **true**. Boolean indicating if an event is currently prequeueing users before it starts.<br>19. `timeUntilEventStart`: Valid only when `isEventPrequeueing` is **true**. Integer indicating the number of minutes until the event starts.<br>20. `timeUntilEventStartFormatted`: String displaying the `timeUntilEventStart` formatted in English for users. If `isEventPrequeueing` is **false**, `timeUntilEventStartFormatted` will display **unavailable**.<br>21. `timeUntilEventEnd`: Valid only when `isEventActive` is **true**. Integer indicating the number of minutes until the event ends.<br>22. `timeUntilEventEndFormatted`: String displaying the `timeUntilEventEnd` formatted in English for users. If `isEventActive` is **false**, `timeUntilEventEndFormatted` will display **unavailable**.<br>23. `shuffleAtEventStart`: Valid only when `isEventActive` is **true**. Boolean indicating if the users in the prequeue are shuffled randomly when the event starts.<br>24. `turnstile`: Empty when turnstile isn't enabled. String displaying an html tag to display the Turnstile widget. Please add the `{{{turnstile}}}` tag to the `custom_html` template to ensure the Turnstile widget appears.<br>25. `infiniteQueue`: Boolean indicating whether the response is for a user in the infinite queue.<br><br>An example cURL to a waiting room could be:<br><br>	curl -X GET "https://example.com/waitingroom" \<br>		-H "Accept: application/json"<br><br>If `json_response_enabled` is **true** and the request hits the waiting room, an example JSON response when `queueingMethod` is **fifo** and no event is active could be:<br><br>	{<br>		"cfWaitingRoom": {<br>			"inWaitingRoom": true,<br>			"waitTimeKnown": true,<br>			"waitTime": 10,<br>			"waitTime25Percentile": 0,<br>			"waitTime50Percentile": 0,<br>			"waitTime75Percentile": 0,<br>			"waitTimeFormatted": "10 minutes",<br>			"queueIsFull": false,<br>			"queueAll": false,<br>			"lastUpdated": "2020-08-03T23:46:00.000Z",<br>			"refreshIntervalSeconds": 20,<br>			"queueingMethod": "fifo",<br>			"isFIFOQueue": true,<br>			"isRandomQueue": false,<br>			"isPassthroughQueue": false,<br>			"isRejectQueue": false,<br>			"isEventActive": false,<br>			"isEventPrequeueing": false,<br>			"timeUntilEventStart": 0,<br>			"timeUntilEventStartFormatted": "unavailable",<br>			"timeUntilEventEnd": 0,<br>			"timeUntilEventEndFormatted": "unavailable",<br>			"shuffleAtEventStart": false<br>		}<br>	}<br><br>If `json_response_enabled` is **true** and the request hits the waiting room, an example JSON response when `queueingMethod` is **random** and an event is active could be:<br><br>	{<br>		"cfWaitingRoom": {<br>			"inWaitingRoom": true,<br>			"waitTimeKnown": true,<br>			"waitTime": 10,<br>			"waitTime25Percentile": 5,<br>			"waitTime50Percentile": 10,<br>			"waitTime75Percentile": 15,<br>			"waitTimeFormatted": "5 minutes to 15 minutes",<br>			"queueIsFull": false,<br>			"queueAll": false,<br>			"lastUpdated": "2020-08-03T23:46:00.000Z",<br>			"refreshIntervalSeconds": 20,<br>			"queueingMethod": "random",<br>			"isFIFOQueue": false,<br>			"isRandomQueue": true,<br>			"isPassthroughQueue": false,<br>			"isRejectQueue": false,<br>			"isEventActive": true,<br>			"isEventPrequeueing": false,<br>			"timeUntilEventStart": 0,<br>			"timeUntilEventStartFormatted": "unavailable",<br>			"timeUntilEventEnd": 15,<br>			"timeUntilEventEndFormatted": "15 minutes",<br>			"shuffleAtEventStart": true<br>		}<br>	}|
|modified_on|[waitingroom_timestamp](#schemawaitingroom_timestamp)|false|read-only|none|
|name|[waitingroom_name](#schemawaitingroom_name)|false|none|A unique name to identify the waiting room. Only alphanumeric characters, hyphens and underscores are allowed.|
|new_users_per_minute|[waitingroom_new_users_per_minute](#schemawaitingroom_new_users_per_minute)|false|none|Sets the number of new users that will be let into the route every minute. This value is used as baseline for the number of users that are let in per minute. So it is possible that there is a little more or little less traffic coming to the route based on the traffic patterns at that time around the world.|
|next_event_prequeue_start_time|[waitingroom_next_event_prequeue_start_time](#schemawaitingroom_next_event_prequeue_start_time)|false|none|An ISO 8601 timestamp that marks when the next event will begin queueing.|
|next_event_start_time|[waitingroom_next_event_start_time](#schemawaitingroom_next_event_start_time)|false|none|An ISO 8601 timestamp that marks when the next event will start.|
|path|[waitingroom_path](#schemawaitingroom_path)|false|none|Sets the path within the host to enable the waiting room on. The waiting room will be enabled for all subpaths as well. If there are two waiting rooms on the same subpath, the waiting room for the most specific path will be chosen. Wildcards and query parameters are not supported.|
|queue_all|[waitingroom_queue_all](#schemawaitingroom_queue_all)|false|none|If queue_all is `true`, all the traffic that is coming to a route will be sent to the waiting room. No new traffic can get to the route once this field is set and estimated time will become unavailable.|
|queueing_method|[waitingroom_queueing_method](#schemawaitingroom_queueing_method)|false|none|Sets the queueing method used by the waiting room. Changing this parameter from the **default** queueing method is only available for the Waiting Room Advanced subscription. Regardless of the queueing method, if `queue_all` is enabled or an event is prequeueing, users in the waiting room will not be accepted to the origin. These users will always see a waiting room page that refreshes automatically. The valid queueing methods are:<br>1. `fifo` **(default)**: First-In-First-Out queue where customers gain access in the order they arrived.<br>2. `random`: Random queue where customers gain access randomly, regardless of arrival time.<br>3. `passthrough`: Users will pass directly through the waiting room and into the origin website. As a result, any configured limits will not be respected while this is enabled. This method can be used as an alternative to disabling a waiting room (with `suspended`) so that analytics are still reported. This can be used if you wish to allow all traffic normally, but want to restrict traffic during a waiting room event, or vice versa.<br>4. `reject`: Users will be immediately rejected from the waiting room. As a result, no users will reach the origin website while this is enabled. This can be used if you wish to reject all traffic while performing maintenance, block traffic during a specified period of time (an event), or block traffic while events are not occurring. Consider a waiting room used for vaccine distribution that only allows traffic during sign-up events, and otherwise blocks all traffic. For this case, the waiting room uses `reject`, and its events override this with `fifo`, `random`, or `passthrough`. When this queueing method is enabled and neither `queueAll` is enabled nor an event is prequeueing, the waiting room page **will not refresh automatically**.|
|queueing_status_code|[waitingroom_queueing_status_code](#schemawaitingroom_queueing_status_code)|false|none|HTTP status code returned to a user while in the queue.|
|session_duration|[waitingroom_session_duration](#schemawaitingroom_session_duration)|false|none|Lifetime of a cookie (in minutes) set by Cloudflare for users who get access to the route. If a user is not seen by Cloudflare again in that time period, they will be treated as a new user that visits the route.|
|suspended|[waitingroom_suspended](#schemawaitingroom_suspended)|false|none|Suspends or allows traffic going to the waiting room. If set to `true`, the traffic will not go to the waiting room.|
|total_active_users|[waitingroom_total_active_users](#schemawaitingroom_total_active_users)|false|none|Sets the total number of active user sessions on the route at a point in time. A route is a combination of host and path on which a waiting room is available. This value is used as a baseline for the total number of active user sessions on the route. It is possible to have a situation where there are more or less active users sessions on the route based on the traffic patterns at that time around the world.|
|turnstile_action|[waitingroom_turnstile_action](#schemawaitingroom_turnstile_action)|false|none|Which action to take when a bot is detected using Turnstile. `log` will<br>have no impact on queueing behavior, simply keeping track of how many<br>bots are detected in Waiting Room Analytics. `infinite_queue` will send<br>bots to a false queueing state, where they will never reach your<br>origin. `infinite_queue` requires Advanced Waiting Room.<br>|
|turnstile_mode|[waitingroom_turnstile_mode](#schemawaitingroom_turnstile_mode)|false|none|Which Turnstile widget type to use for detecting bot traffic. See<br>[the Turnstile documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/turnstile/concepts/widget/#widget-types)<br>for the definitions of these widget types. Set to `off` to disable the<br>Turnstile integration entirely. Setting this to anything other than<br>`off` or `invisible` requires Advanced Waiting Room.<br>|

### Properties

|elapsed|number|true|none|Time in seconds for the query to run.|
|rows_read|number|true|none|Number of rows scanned from the table.|

Complete results of a query run. The populated fields depend on the requested view type (events, calculations, invocations, traces, or agents).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|agents|[object]|false|none|Agent run summaries. Present when the query view is 'agents'. Each entry represents one trace containing at least one agent invocation.|
|calculations|[object]|false|none|Aggregated calculation results. Present when the query view is 'calculations'. Contains computed metrics (count, avg, p99, etc.) with optional group-by breakdowns and time-series data.|
|compare|[object]|false|none|Comparison calculation results from the previous time period. Present when the compare option is enabled. Same structure as calculations.|
|distribution|[workers-observability_distribution_result](#schemaworkers-observability_distribution_result)|false|none|Bucketed 2D histogram of a numeric field over time. Present when chartType is 'distribution'.|
|events|object|false|none|Individual event results. Present when the query view is 'events'. Contains the matching log lines and their metadata.|
|invocations|object|false|none|Events grouped by invocation (request ID). Present when the query view is 'invocations'. Each key is a request ID mapping to all events from that invocation.|
|run|[workers-observability_query_run](#schemaworkers-observability_query_run)|true|none|Represents a single execution of a query against Workers Observability data, including the query definition, execution status, and performance statistics.|
|statistics|[workers-observability_performance_information](#schemaworkers-observability_performance_information)|true|none|Query performance statistics from the database. Includes execution time, rows scanned, and bytes read. Does not include network latency.|
|traces|[object]|false|none|Trace summaries matching the query. Present when the query view is 'traces'. Each entry represents a distributed trace with its spans, duration, and services involved.|

Represents a single execution of a query against Workers Observability data, including the query definition, execution status, and performance statistics.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accountId|string|true|none|Cloudflare account ID that owns this query run.|
|created|string|false|none|ISO-8601 timestamp when the query run was created.|
|dry|boolean|true|none|Whether this was a dry run (results not persisted).|
|granularity|number|true|none|Number of time-series buckets used for the query. Higher values produce more detailed series data.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for this query run.|
|query|object|true|none|A saved query definition with its parameters, metadata, and ownership information.|
|statistics|object|false|none|Query performance statistics from the database (does not include network latency).|
|status|string|true|none|Current execution status of the query run.|
|timeframe|object|true|none|Time range for the query execution. 'from' must be earlier than 'to'. No fractional milliseconds.|
|updated|string|false|none|ISO-8601 timestamp when the query run was last updated.|
|userId|string|true|none|ID of the user who initiated the query run.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|STARTED|
|status|COMPLETED|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|$containers|object|false|none|Cloudflare Containers event information that enriches your logs for identifying and debugging issues.|
|$metadata|object|true|none|Structured metadata extracted from the event. These fields are indexed and available for filtering and aggregation.|
|$workers|object|false|none|Cloudflare Workers event information that enriches your logs for identifying and debugging issues.|
|dataset|string|true|none|The dataset this event belongs to (e.g. cloudflare-workers).|
|source|string \| object|true|none|Raw log payload. May be a string or a structured object depending on how the log was emitted.|
|timestamp|integer|true|none|Event timestamp as a Unix epoch in milliseconds.|

|enabled|boolean|true|none|Whether the configured hostname is routable for the domain. If disabled, then requests to the configured hostname will not be routed to the configured Worker. If disabled, then preview routing must be enabled, and only subdomains of the configured hostname will be routable.|
|environment|string|true|read-only|**Deprecated.** Worker environment associated with the domain.|
|hostname|string|true|none|Hostname of the domain. Can be either the zone apex or a subdomain of the zone. Requests to this hostname will be routed to the configured Worker.|
|id|string|true|read-only|Immutable ID of the domain.|
|previews_enabled|boolean|true|none|Whether previews are routable for the domain. If enabled, previews will be routable as subdomains of the configured hostname. For example, if the configured hostname is `app.example.com`, then requests to `my-feature.app.example.com` will be routed to the preview with slug `my-feature`, if such a preview exists. If preview routing is disabled, then hostname routing must be enabled.|
|service|string|true|none|Name of the Worker associated with the domain. Requests to the configured hostname will be routed to this Worker.|
|zone_id|string|true|none|ID of the zone containing the domain hostname.|
|zone_name|string|true|none|Name of the zone containing the domain hostname.|

|bindings|object|false|none|Bindings attached to the deployment, as an array of objects<br>that each name themselves. An upload can send `env` or<br>`bindings`, and a read returns both. Uploads to a Preview whose<br>parent Worker has a previews base config must use `env`.<br>|
|cache_options|[workers_cache_options](#schemaworkers_cache_options)|false|none|Global CacheW configuration for the Worker. When caching is on,<br>the platform provisions a `cloudflare.app` zone for the Worker.<br>A `type: worker` entry in the `exports` map can override this<br>value for a single entrypoint.<br>|
|compatibility_date|[workers_compatibility_date](#schemaworkers_compatibility_date)|false|none|Date indicating targeted support in the Workers runtime. Backwards incompatible fixes to the runtime following this date will not affect this Worker.|
|compatibility_flags|[workers_compatibility_flags](#schemaworkers_compatibility_flags)|false|none|Flags that enable or disable certain features in the Workers runtime. Used to enable upcoming features or opt in or out of specific changes not included in a `compatibility_date`.|
|containers|[workers_containers](#schemaworkers_containers)|false|none|List of containers attached to a Worker. Containers can only be attached to Durable Object classes of this Worker script.|
|env|object|false|none|Bindings attached to the deployment, keyed by binding name. An<br>upload can send `env` or `bindings`, and a read returns both.<br>|
|exports|object|false|none|Declarative exports for the deployment, including Durable<br>Object classes (with their `storage` backend) and named Worker<br>entrypoints. On reads, tombstoned lifecycle entries are<br>omitted, so only live exports (`created` and<br>`expecting-transfer`) are returned. `exports` and `migrations`<br>are mutually exclusive on upload.<br>|
|limits|object|false|none|Resource limits enforced at runtime.|
|main_module|string|false|none|The name of the module that exports a `fetch` handler. Multipart uploads reference the file part by filename.|
|migrations|[workers_single_step_migrations](#schemaworkers_single_step_migrations) \| [workers_multiple_step_migrations](#schemaworkers_multiple_step_migrations)|false|none|Migrations for Durable Objects associated with the deployment. Migrations are applied when the deployment is created.|
|placement|[workers_placement_info_no_status](#schemaworkers_placement_info_no_status)|false|none|Configuration for [Smart Placement](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/smart-placement). Specify mode='smart' for Smart Placement, or one of region/hostname/host.|
|usage_model|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** Usage model for the deployment.|
|modules|[object]|false|none|Code, sourcemaps, and other content used at runtime.|
|author_email|string|true|read-only|Email of the user who created the deployment. May be empty for deployments created using an API token.|
|author_id|string|true|read-only|Identifier of the user who created the deployment.|
|created_on|string(date-time)|true|read-only|When the deployment was created.|
|exports_reconciliation|object|false|none|Summary of the declarative exports reconciliation that ran on<br>this upload. Populated only when the uploaded metadata included<br>an `exports` block. Durable Object entries drive reconciliation;<br>`type: worker` entries do not contribute to this summary.<br>|
|id|string(uuid)|true|read-only|Deployment identifier.|
|migration_tag|string|false|read-only|Durable Object migration tag. Omitted if the Preview does not use Durable Objects.|
|number|integer|true|read-only|The integer deployment number, starting from one.|
|source|string|false|read-only|The client used to create the deployment.|
|startup_time_ms|integer|false|read-only|Time in milliseconds spent on Worker startup.|
|urls|[string(uri)]|true|read-only|All routable URLs that always point to this deployment.|

```json
      }
```

```json
  "tags": [
```

|references|object|true|read-only|Other resources that reference the Worker and depend on it existing.|
|subdomain|object|true|none|Subdomain settings for the Worker.|
|tags|[string]|true|none|Tags associated with the Worker.|
|tail_consumers|[object]|true|none|Other Workers that should consume logs from the Worker.|
|updated_on|string(date-time)|true|read-only|When the Worker was most recently updated.|

<h2 id="tocS_workers_durable_object_expecting_transfer_export">workers_durable_object_expecting_transfer_export</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaworkers_durable_object_expecting_transfer_export"></a>
<a id="schema_workers_durable_object_expecting_transfer_export"></a>
<a id="tocSworkers_durable_object_expecting_transfer_export"></a>
<a id="tocsworkers_durable_object_expecting_transfer_export"></a>

```json
{
  "container": "my-container",
  "state": "expecting-transfer",
  "storage": "sqlite",
  "transfer_from": "source-worker",
  "type": "durable-object"
}
```

The target side of a two-phase transfer (`state:
expecting-transfer`). Declares that this script expects to receive
a namespace for this class from the `transfer_from` script. This
is a live entry, not a tombstone: bindings resolve through the
source's namespace until the source commits with a `transferred`
tombstone. `storage` and `transfer_from` are required; `renamed_to`
and `transferred_to` are not allowed.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|container|string|false|none|Name of the container (declared in the upload's<br>`metadata.containers`) that backs this Durable Object once the<br>transfer settles. Valid only on live entries.<br>|
|state|string|true|none|Target side of a two-phase transfer.|
|storage|[workers_export_storage](#schemaworkers_export_storage)|true|none|Durable Object storage backend. `sqlite` is the recommended (and<br>only) backend for new namespaces. `legacy-kv` is accepted only for<br>a class whose namespace already exists as KV-backed; the `exports`<br>flow never provisions a new `legacy-kv` namespace.<br>|
|transfer_from|string|true|none|The source script name to receive the namespace from. Must be<br>in the same account and dispatch-namespace context. Present on<br>reads for `expecting-transfer` entries.<br>|
|type|string|true|none|Marks this entry as a Durable Object export.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|state|expecting-transfer|
|storage|sqlite|
|storage|legacy-kv|
|type|durable-object|

<h2 id="tocS_workers_durable_object_export">workers_durable_object_export</h2>

```json

  "container": "my-container",
  "state": "created",
  "storage": "sqlite",
  "type": "durable-object"
}
```

A live Durable Object export (`state: created`, the default). The
platform auto-provisions the namespace on first deploy, matches it
on subsequent deploys, and never mutates or deletes it as a side
effect of a code-only change. `storage` is required; `renamed_to`,
`transferred_to` and `transfer_from` are not allowed on a live
entry.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|container|string|false|none|Name of the container (declared in the upload's<br>`metadata.containers`) that backs this Durable Object. When<br>set, the namespace is container-enabled. Valid only on live<br>entries.<br>|
|state|string|false|none|Live export. May be omitted; defaults to `created`.|
|storage|[workers_export_storage](#schemaworkers_export_storage)|true|none|Durable Object storage backend. `sqlite` is the recommended (and<br>only) backend for new namespaces. `legacy-kv` is accepted only for<br>a class whose namespace already exists as KV-backed; the `exports`<br>flow never provisions a new `legacy-kv` namespace.<br>|
|type|string|true|none|Marks this entry as a Durable Object export.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|state|created|
|storage|sqlite|
|storage|legacy-kv|
|type|durable-object|

<h2 id="tocS_workers_durable_object_export_variants">workers_durable_object_export_variants</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaworkers_durable_object_export_variants"></a>
<a id="schema_workers_durable_object_export_variants"></a>
<a id="tocSworkers_durable_object_export_variants"></a>
<a id="tocsworkers_durable_object_export_variants"></a>

```json
{
  "container": "my-container",
  "state": "created",
  "storage": "sqlite",
  "type": "durable-object"
}
```

Any Durable Object export entry (`type: durable-object`), across
all lifecycle states. The optional `state` field selects the
variant (default `created`); the tombstone states (`deleted`,
`renamed`, `transferred`) and the live transfer target
(`expecting-transfer`) are the alternatives. The server validates
the exact per-state field combinations; fields not listed for a
variant are rejected.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[workers_durable_object_export](#schemaworkers_durable_object_export)|false|none|A live Durable Object export (`state: created`, the default). The<br>platform auto-provisions the namespace on first deploy, matches it<br>on subsequent deploys, and never mutates or deletes it as a side<br>effect of a code-only change. `storage` is required; `renamed_to`,<br>`transferred_to` and `transfer_from` are not allowed on a live<br>entry.<br>|
|*oneOf*|[workers_durable_object_deleted_export](#schemaworkers_durable_object_deleted_export)|false|none|A `deleted` tombstone: retires the provisioned namespace for this<br>class and all of its data. The class must be absent from the<br>uploaded code and no other Worker in the account may bind to the<br>namespace, otherwise the deploy is rejected. No other fields are<br>allowed. Deletion is irreversible.<br>|
|*oneOf*|[workers_durable_object_renamed_export](#schemaworkers_durable_object_renamed_export)|false|none|A `renamed` tombstone: rewrites the provisioned namespace's class<br>name from this map key to `renamed_to`. The source class may stay<br>in code during the rollout window (an info notice is emitted).<br>`storage`, `transferred_to` and `transfer_from` are not allowed.<br>|
|*oneOf*|[workers_durable_object_transferred_export](#schemaworkers_durable_object_transferred_export)|false|none|A `transferred` tombstone (source side of a two-phase transfer):<br>hands ownership of the provisioned namespace to another script in<br>the same account, named by `transferred_to`. The target must have<br>already deployed a matching `expecting-transfer` entry. The source<br>class may stay in code during the rollout window (an info notice<br>is emitted). `storage`, `renamed_to` and `transfer_from` are not<br>allowed.<br>|
|*oneOf*|[workers_durable_object_expecting_transfer_export](#schemaworkers_durable_object_expecting_transfer_export)|false|none|The target side of a two-phase transfer (`state:<br>expecting-transfer`). Declares that this script expects to receive<br>a namespace for this class from the `transfer_from` script. This<br>is a live entry, not a tombstone: bindings resolve through the<br>source's namespace until the source commits with a `transferred`<br>tombstone. `storage` and `transfer_from` are required; `renamed_to`<br>and `transferred_to` are not allowed.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_workers_durable_object_renamed_export">workers_durable_object_renamed_export</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaworkers_durable_object_renamed_export"></a>

<a id="tocsworkers_durable_object_renamed_export"></a>

```json
{
  "renamed_to": "NewName",
  "state": "renamed",
  "type": "durable-object"
}
```

A `renamed` tombstone: rewrites the provisioned namespace's class
name from this map key to `renamed_to`. The source class may stay
in code during the rollout window (an info notice is emitted).
`storage`, `transferred_to` and `transfer_from` are not allowed.

|renamed_to|string|true|write-only|The destination class name. Must differ from the source class<br>(the map key) and must be declared as a live (`created`) entry<br>in the same `exports` map. Write-only: never present in GET<br>responses.<br>|
|state|string|true|none|Tombstone that renames the namespace's class.|
|type|string|true|none|Marks this entry as a Durable Object export.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|state|renamed|
|type|durable-object|

```json
{
  "state": "transferred",
  "transferred_to": "target-worker",
  "type": "durable-object"
}
```

A `transferred` tombstone (source side of a two-phase transfer):
hands ownership of the provisioned namespace to another script in
the same account, named by `transferred_to`. The target must have
already deployed a matching `expecting-transfer` entry. The source
class may stay in code during the rollout window (an info notice
is emitted). `storage`, `renamed_to` and `transfer_from` are not
allowed.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|state|string|true|none|Tombstone that transfers the namespace to another script.|
|transferred_to|string|true|write-only|The destination script name. Must be in the same account and<br>the same dispatch-namespace context (or both non-dispatch).<br>Cross-dispatch-namespace transfers are rejected. Write-only:<br>never present in GET responses.<br>|
|type|string|true|none|Marks this entry as a Durable Object export.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|state|transferred|
|type|durable-object|

```json

}
```

CacheW configuration for a single `type: worker` entrypoint.
When present it overrides the Worker's global
`cache_options.enabled` for that entrypoint, so a Worker can turn

<h2 id="tocS_workers_export_config">workers_export_config</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaworkers_export_config"></a>
<a id="schema_workers_export_config"></a>
<a id="tocSworkers_export_config"></a>
<a id="tocsworkers_export_config"></a>

```json
{
  "cache": {
    "enabled": true
  },
  "state": "created",
  "type": "worker"
}
```

A single entry in the `exports` map, keyed by export name (a
`WorkerEntrypoint` class name, a Durable Object class name, or
`default` for the Worker's default export). The `type`
discriminator selects the top-level shape: `worker` entrypoint
entries may carry `cache` configuration, while `durable-object`
entries are further refined by the optional `state` field
(default `created`). Tombstone states (`deleted`, `renamed`,
`transferred`) express destructive lifecycle operations
declaratively; `expecting-transfer` is the live target side of a
transfer. The server validates the exact per-(type, state) field
combinations; fields not listed for a variant are rejected.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[workers_worker_export](#schemaworkers_worker_export)|false|none|A named Worker entrypoint export (`type: worker`). Worker<br>entrypoints are always live (`state: created`) and carry no<br>storage or lifecycle fields. The optional `cache` block overrides<br>the Worker's global `cache_options.enabled` for this entrypoint.<br>|
|*oneOf*|[workers_durable_object_export_variants](#schemaworkers_durable_object_export_variants)|false|none|Any Durable Object export entry (`type: durable-object`), across<br>all lifecycle states. The optional `state` field selects the<br>variant (default `created`); the tombstone states (`deleted`,<br>`renamed`, `transferred`) and the live transfer target<br>(`expecting-transfer`) are the alternatives. The server validates<br>the exact per-state field combinations; fields not listed for a<br>variant are rejected.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_workers_export_storage">workers_export_storage</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaworkers_export_storage"></a>
<a id="schema_workers_export_storage"></a>
<a id="tocSworkers_export_storage"></a>
<a id="tocsworkers_export_storage"></a>

```json
"sqlite"
```

Durable Object storage backend. `sqlite` is the recommended (and
only) backend for new namespaces. `legacy-kv` is accepted only for
a class whose namespace already exists as KV-backed; the `exports`
flow never provisions a new `legacy-kv` namespace.

<h2 id="tocS_workers_exports_config_map">workers_exports_config_map</h2>

```json
{
  "Admin": {
    "cache": {
      "enabled": true
    },
    "type": "worker"
  },
  "Counter": {
    "storage": "sqlite",
    "type": "durable-object"
  },
  "OldCounter": {
    "renamed_to": "Counter",
    "state": "renamed",
    "type": "durable-object"
  },
  "default": {
    "cache": {
      "enabled": false
    },
    "type": "worker"
  }
}
```

Declarative exports for the Worker, keyed by export name. Worker
entrypoint entries (`type: worker`) carry cache configuration for
that entrypoint. Durable Object entries (`type: durable-object`)
are also configured here and drive namespace reconciliation. At
most 100 entries; class names are at most 128 characters.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|**additionalProperties**|[workers_export_config](#schemaworkers_export_config)|false|none|A single entry in the `exports` map, keyed by export name (a<br>`WorkerEntrypoint` class name, a Durable Object class name, or<br>`default` for the Worker's default export). The `type`<br>discriminator selects the top-level shape: `worker` entrypoint<br>entries may carry `cache` configuration, while `durable-object`<br>entries are further refined by the optional `state` field<br>(default `created`). Tombstone states (`deleted`, `renamed`,<br>`transferred`) express destructive lifecycle operations<br>declaratively; `expecting-transfer` is the live target side of a<br>transfer. The server validates the exact per-(type, state) field<br>combinations; fields not listed for a variant are rejected.<br>|

```json
{
  "created": [
    "string"
  ],
  "deleted": [
    "string"
  ],

    {
      "class": "string",
      "message": "string",

      "referencing_scripts": [
        "string"
      ],
      "scenario": "code_class_not_in_exports"
    }
  ],
  "removable_entries": [
    "string"
  ],
  "renamed": [
    {
      "from": "string",
      "to": "string"
    }
  ],
  "transfer_pending": [

      "class": "string",
      "from": "string"
    }

      "phase": "committed",
      "to": "string"
    }
  ],

      "class": "string",
      "message": "string",
      "namespace_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
      "scenario": "code_class_not_in_exports"
    }
  ]
}
```

Summary of what the declarative exports reconciliation did on this
upload. Present only on uploads that included an `exports` block.
Reconciliation acts on Durable Object entries; `type: worker`
entries in the same map do not participate. Every array is always
present (possibly empty) so clients can iterate unconditionally.
Clients should surface `warnings` prominently, render `info` at
lower visibility, and use `removable_entries` as the "safe to
delete from your config" hint.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|[string]|true|none|Class names for which a new namespace was provisioned.|
|deleted|[string]|true|none|Class names whose namespace was deleted by a `deleted` tombstone.|
|info|[[workers_exports_reconciliation_info](#schemaworkers_exports_reconciliation_info)]|true|none|Non-blocking info entries (stale tombstones, tombstone applied<br>with class still in code). See `exports_reconciliation_info`.<br>|
|removable_entries|[string]|true|none|Source class names whose tombstone entry is now stale and safe<br>to delete from `exports` (no remaining referencing scripts).<br>|
|renamed|[[workers_exports_reconciliation_rename](#schemaworkers_exports_reconciliation_rename)]|true|none|Applied `renamed` tombstones.|
|transfer_pending|[[workers_exports_reconciliation_transfer_pending](#schemaworkers_exports_reconciliation_transfer_pending)]|true|none|Phase-1 transfer hints recorded on the target side.|
|transferred|[[workers_exports_reconciliation_transfer](#schemaworkers_exports_reconciliation_transfer)]|true|none|Committed `transferred` tombstones (phase-2).|
|updated|[string]|true|none|Class names whose provisioned namespace was mutated in place.|
|warnings|[[workers_exports_reconciliation_warning](#schemaworkers_exports_reconciliation_warning)]|true|none|Non-blocking warnings. See `exports_reconciliation_warning`.|

|compatibility_date|object|false|none|none|
|compatibility_flags|object|false|none|none|
|exports|object|false|write-only|Declarative exports for the Worker. Worker entrypoint entries<br>(`type: worker`) carry cache configuration for that entrypoint.<br>|
|exports_reconciliation|object|false|none|Summary of the declarative exports reconciliation that ran on<br>this upload. Populated only when the uploaded metadata included<br>an `exports` block. Durable Object entries drive reconciliation;<br>`type: worker` entries do not contribute to this summary.<br>|
|limits|[workers_limits](#schemaworkers_limits)|false|none|Limits to apply for this Worker.|
|logpush|[workers_logpush](#schemaworkers_logpush)|false|none|Whether Logpush is turned on for the Worker.|

|observability|[workers_observability-2](#schemaworkers_observability-2)|false|none|Observability settings for the Worker.|
|placement|object|false|none|none|
|tags|object|false|none|none|
|tail_consumers|object|false|none|none|
|usage_model|[workers_usage_model](#schemaworkers_usage_model)|false|none|Usage model for the Worker invocations.|

<h2 id="tocS_workers_trusted_workers">workers_trusted_workers</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaworkers_trusted_workers"></a>
<a id="schema_workers_trusted_workers"></a>
<a id="tocSworkers_trusted_workers"></a>
<a id="tocsworkers_trusted_workers"></a>

```json
false
```

Whether the Workers in the namespace are executed in a "trusted" manner. When a Worker is trusted, it has access to the shared caches for the zone in the Cache API, and has access to the `request.cf` object on incoming Requests. When a Worker is untrusted, caches are not shared across the zone, and `request.cf` is undefined. By default, Workers in a namespace are "untrusted".

<h2 id="tocS_workers_worker_export">workers_worker_export</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaworkers_worker_export"></a>
<a id="schema_workers_worker_export"></a>
<a id="tocSworkers_worker_export"></a>
<a id="tocsworkers_worker_export"></a>

```json
{
  "cache": {
    "enabled": true
  },
  "state": "created",
  "type": "worker"
}
```

A named Worker entrypoint export (`type: worker`). Worker
entrypoints are always live (`state: created`) and carry no
storage or lifecycle fields. The optional `cache` block overrides
the Worker's global `cache_options.enabled` for this entrypoint.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cache|object|false|none|Cache override for this entrypoint. Overrides the Worker's<br>global `cache_options.enabled` for this entrypoint only.<br>|
|state|string|false|none|Live export. May be omitted; defaults to `created`.|
|type|string|true|none|Marks this entry as a Worker entrypoint export.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|state|created|
|type|worker|

```json
  "name": "string",
  "vendorName": "string",
  "vendorPolicyUrl": "string",
  "actions": {
    "property1": {
      "actionType": "string",
      "blockingTriggers": [
        "string"
      ],
      "data": {},
      "firingTriggers": [
        "string"
      ]
    },
    "property2": {
      "actionType": "string",
      "blockingTriggers": [
        "string"
      ],
      "data": {},
      "firingTriggers": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  },
  "component": "string",
  "neoEvents": [
    {
      "actionType": "string",
      "blockingTriggers": [
        "string"
      ],
      "data": {},
```

```json
        "string"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "permissions": [
    "string"
  ],
  "settings": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "type": "component"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|blockingTriggers|[string]|true|none|List of blocking trigger IDs.|
|defaultFields|object|true|none|Default fields for tool's actions.|
|defaultPurpose|string|false|none|Default consent purpose ID.|
|enabled|boolean|true|none|Whether tool is enabled.|
|name|string|true|none|Tool's name defined by the user.|
|vendorName|string|false|none|Vendor name for TCF compliant consent modal, required for Custom Managed Components and Custom HTML tool with a defaultPurpose assigned.|
|vendorPolicyUrl|string|false|none|Vendor's Privacy Policy URL for TCF compliant consent modal, required for Custom Managed Components and Custom HTML tool with a defaultPurpose assigned.|
|actions|object|false|none|Actions configured on a tool. Either this or neoEvents field is required.|
|component|string|true|none|Tool's internal name.|
|neoEvents|[object]|false|none|DEPRECATED - List of actions configured on a tool. Either this or actions field is required. If both are present, actions field will take precedence.|
|permissions|[string]|true|none|List of permissions granted to the component.|
|settings|object|true|none|Tool's settings.|
|type|string|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|component|

```json
{
  "consent": {
    "cookieName": "zaraz-consent",
    "customIntroDisclaimerDismissed": true,
    "enabled": false
  },
  "dataLayer": true,
  "debugKey": "my-debug-key",
  "settings": {
    "autoInjectScript": true,
    "ecommerce": true,
    "initPath": "/i"
  },
  "tools": {
    "aJvt": {
      "actions": {
        "hrnc": {
          "actionType": "pageview",
          "blockingTriggers": [],
          "data": {
            "__zaraz_setting_name": "Page view",
            "ev": "PageView"
          },
          "firingTriggers": [
            "Pageview"
          ]
        }
      },
      "component": "facebook-pixel",
      "defaultFields": {
        "testKey": "TEST123456"
      },
      "enabled": true,
      "name": "Facebook Pixel",
      "permissions": [
        "access_client_kv"
      ],
      "settings": {
        "accessToken": "ABcdEFg",
        "ecommerce": true,
        "property": "12345"
      },
      "type": "component"
    }
  },
  "triggers": {
    "ktBn": {
      "Pageview": {
        "clientRules": [],
        "description": "All page loads",
        "excludeRules": [],
        "loadRules": [
          {
            "match": "{{ client.__zarazTrack }}",
            "op": "EQUALS",
            "value": "Pageview"
          }
        ],
        "name": "Pageview",
        "system": "pageload"
      }
    }
  },
  "variables": {
    "Autd": {
      "name": "ip",
      "type": "string",
      "value": "{{ system.device.ip }}"
    }
  },
  "zarazVersion": 43
}
```

Zaraz configuration.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|analytics|object|false|none|Cloudflare Monitoring settings.|
|consent|object|false|none|Consent management configuration.|
|dataLayer|boolean|true|none|Data layer compatibility mode enabled.|
|debugKey|string|true|none|The key for Zaraz debug mode.|
|historyChange|boolean|false|none|Single Page Application support enabled.|
|settings|object|true|none|General Zaraz settings.|
|triggers|object|true|none|Triggers set up under Zaraz configuration, where key is the trigger alpha-numeric ID and value is the trigger configuration.|
|variables|object|true|none|Variables set up under Zaraz configuration, where key is the variable alpha-numeric ID and value is the variable configuration. Values of variables of type secret are not included.|
|zarazVersion|integer|true|none|Zaraz internal version of the config.|

```json
{
  "binding_status": "pending_deployment",
  "certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\\\\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----\\n",
  "created_at": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z",
  "expires_on": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z",
  "fingerprint": "E9:19:49:AA:DD:D8:1E:C1:20:2A:D8:22:BF:A5:F8:FC:1A:F7:10:9F:C7:5B:69:AB:0:31:91:8B:61:B4:BF:1C",
  "id": "f174e90a-fafe-4643-bbbc-4a0ed4fc8415",
  "in_use": true,
  "issuer_org": "Example Inc.",
  "issuer_raw": "O=Example Inc.,L=California,ST=San Francisco,C=US",
  "region": "wnam",
  "type": "gateway_managed",
  "updated_at": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z",
  "uploaded_on": "2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|binding_status|[zero-trust-gateway_binding_status](#schemazero-trust-gateway_binding_status)|false|read-only|Indicate the read-only deployment status of the certificate on Cloudflare's edge. Gateway TLS interception can use certificates in the 'available' (previously called 'active') state.|
|certificate|string|false|read-only|Provide the CA certificate (read-only).|
|created_at|[zero-trust-gateway_read_only_timestamp](#schemazero-trust-gateway_read_only_timestamp)|false|read-only|none|
|expires_on|[zero-trust-gateway_read_only_timestamp](#schemazero-trust-gateway_read_only_timestamp)|false|read-only|none|
|fingerprint|string|false|read-only|Provide the SHA256 fingerprint of the certificate (read-only).|
|id|[zero-trust-gateway_uuid](#schemazero-trust-gateway_uuid)|false|none|Identify the certificate with a UUID.|
|in_use|boolean|false|read-only|Indicate whether Gateway TLS interception uses this certificate (read-only). You cannot set this value directly. To configure interception, use the Gateway configuration setting named `certificate` (read-only).|
|issuer_org|string|false|read-only|Indicate the organization that issued the certificate (read-only).|
|issuer_raw|string|false|read-only|Provide the entire issuer field of the certificate (read-only).|
|region|[zero-trust-gateway_region](#schemazero-trust-gateway_region)|false|read-only|Indicate the read-only region the certificate authority's key material is pinned to. Omitted for certificates that were created without a region.|
|type|[zero-trust-gateway_type](#schemazero-trust-gateway_type)|false|read-only|Indicate the read-only certificate type, BYO-PKI (custom) or Gateway-managed.|
|updated_at|[zero-trust-gateway_read_only_timestamp](#schemazero-trust-gateway_read_only_timestamp)|false|read-only|none|
|uploaded_on|[zero-trust-gateway_read_only_timestamp](#schemazero-trust-gateway_read_only_timestamp)|false|read-only|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|binding_status|pending_deployment|
|binding_status|available|
|binding_status|pending_deletion|
|binding_status|inactive|
|type|custom|
|type|gateway_managed|

```json
{
  "duration": 10,
  "expired": false,
  "expires_at": {}
}
```

Defines the expiration time stamp and default duration of a DNS policy. Takes precedence over the policy's `schedule` configuration, if any. This  does not apply to HTTP or network policies. Settable only for `dns` rules.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|duration|integer|false|none|Defines the default duration a policy active in minutes. Must set in order to use the `reset_expiration` endpoint on this rule.|
|expired|boolean|false|read-only|Indicates whether the policy is expired.|
|expires_at|object|true|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_zero-trust-gateway_extended-email-matching">zero-trust-gateway_extended-email-matching</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemazero-trust-gateway_extended-email-matching"></a>
<a id="schema_zero-trust-gateway_extended-email-matching"></a>
<a id="tocSzero-trust-gateway_extended-email-matching"></a>
<a id="tocszero-trust-gateway_extended-email-matching"></a>

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "read_only": true,
  "source_account": "string",
  "version": 1
}
```

Configures user email settings for firewall policies. When you enable this, the system standardizes email addresses in the identity portion of the rule to match extended email variants in firewall policies. When you disable this setting, the system matches email addresses exactly as you provide them. Enable this setting if your email uses `.` or `+` modifiers.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|boolean \| null|false|none|Specify whether to match all variants of user emails (with + or . modifiers) used as criteria in Firewall policies.|
|read_only|boolean|false|read-only|Indicate that this setting was shared via the Orgs API and read only for the current account.|
|source_account|string|false|read-only|Indicate the account tag of the account that shared this setting.|
|version|integer|false|read-only|Indicate the version number of the setting.|

|networks|[zero-trust-gateway_ipv4_networks](#schemazero-trust-gateway_ipv4_networks)|false|none|Specify the list of network ranges from which requests at this location originate. The list takes effect only if it is non-empty and the IPv4 endpoint is enabled for this location.|

<h2 id="tocS_zero-trust-gateway_max-ttl">zero-trust-gateway_max-ttl</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemazero-trust-gateway_max-ttl"></a>
<a id="schema_zero-trust-gateway_max-ttl"></a>
<a id="tocSzero-trust-gateway_max-ttl"></a>
<a id="tocszero-trust-gateway_max-ttl"></a>

```json
{
  "mode": "inherit"
}
```

Controls how DNS response TTLs are capped for this location relative to the account `max_ttl_secs` setting. Omitting `max_ttl` on update resets it to `inherit`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|mode|string|true|none|`inherit` uses the account `max_ttl_secs`. `override` uses this location's `ttl_secs`. `disabled` leaves returned TTLs unchanged.|
|ttl_secs|integer \| null|false|none|Location-specific cap on DNS response TTLs, in seconds. Required when `mode` is `override`. Must be omitted when `mode` is `inherit` or `disabled`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|mode|inherit|
|mode|override|
|mode|disabled|

<h2 id="tocS_zero-trust-gateway_max-ttl-secs">zero-trust-gateway_max-ttl-secs</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemazero-trust-gateway_max-ttl-secs"></a>

<a id="tocSzero-trust-gateway_max-ttl-secs"></a>
<a id="tocszero-trust-gateway_max-ttl-secs"></a>

```json
3600
```

Account-level cap on DNS response TTLs, in seconds. Gateway rewrites DNS responses so returned record TTLs do not exceed this value. Null means no cap. Each DNS location can inherit, override, or disable it through the location `max_ttl` setting.
